# KFX — C-9 fix + minimal G-59 processed-frontier for `Effectful`

Kernel-lane chunk **KFX**, milestone plan §1 (kernel lane: *"C-9 fix + minimal G-59
processed-frontier for `Effectful`; depends on CHA2 failing tests; unblocks CON1"*), §4
position **3** (*"small; CON1 hard-blocked; CHA2 hands it failing tests"*), §5 row 18
(*"CON1 — hard-blocked on KFX"*).

Filed under **KHYG — Kernel structural hygiene** (`computenet-yh6`). KHYG's stated
criteria are: work that takes a kernel-lane slot and serializes against KX/KE1/KFX/KAGG-R
under the single kernel SCC (G-63); work that completes or restructures an existing
mechanism rather than inventing semantics; and work that *"carries a latent correctness
finding that the structural work either pins as current behaviour or fixes outright"*.
KFX is the third pattern in its purest form. **One honest qualification**: KHYG says its
children are "behaviour-preserving *in intent*". KFX is not behaviour-preserving on the
recovery path — it deliberately changes what fires after a crash. It belongs under KHYG on
the "fixes the latent correctness finding outright" clause, and this ticket says so rather
than letting the epic's framing imply a smaller blast radius than the change has.

## The audit that must be done before any code — the frontier is already landed

The milestone plan describes KFX as building *"a minimal G-59 processed-frontier for
`Effectful`"*. **A pre-ticket inspection of `main` shows that mechanism is already
merged.** Building it again would be the single most expensive possible reading of this
ticket.

| Landed | Where |
|---|---|
| `interface Effectful` | `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/evolve/Evolution.kt:22` |
| Per-`(cellRef, portName)` processed-frontier, last applied `Timestamp` per source | `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/HostDurability.kt:100-106` |
| `alreadyProcessed(cellRef, portName, timestamp)` — at-or-behind test | `HostDurability.kt:253-258` |
| `advanceAndJournalFrontier(...)` — advance in memory, then journal, in that order | `HostDurability.kt:266-276` |
| Durable frontier record type `RECORD_FRONTIER` + `FrontierRecord` | `HostDurability.kt:21,34-39,192-199,247-250` |
| Frontier carried in the checkpoint atomically with cell state | `HostDurability.kt:41-45,209-235,237-245` |
| The suppression itself, consulted by **both** replay and post-recovery live delivery | `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/ManagedHost.kt:790-813` |
| Kernel test | `kernel/src/test/kotlin/civictech/cell/durability/EffectfulRecoveryTest.kt` |
| Conformance scenario, genuinely exercised | `concord/corpus/15-durability/DUR-REPLAY-01.yaml` (`covers: [24-DUR-01, 24-DUR-02, 24-DUR-05]`, `effect-count(esink, exactly: 1)`) |
| Normative requirement | `[24-DUR-05]` (`doc/spec/20-dataflow-semantics/24-data-cells.md`), restated in `doc/spec/30-execution-model/31-hosts.md` and `doc/spec/50-development-process/52-verification.md`, all marked *"G-59 resolved (in part), W2.6, closes C-9"* |

### The documentation divergence this ticket must record, not fix

`doc/spec/90-roadmap/91-gap-analysis.md:18`, the C-9 row, still reads *"code diverges; fix
pending"*. Three normative sections (`20/24`, `30/31`, `50/52`) and
`concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` all say the frontier landed. **The gap table is stale, not the
code.** Per `AGENTS.md`, plan and gap documents are not edited except under an explicit
documentation-maintenance authorization, and per §6 of the milestone plan only the periodic
integration pass writes the gap table. KFX therefore **files this as a finding** in the
kernel lane's findings file and does not touch `91-gap-analysis.md`.

## What is actually still broken — the two real residuals

`concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` records the boundary honestly, and it is the ticket's real
scope:

### Residual A — the outlet's `sourceId` is not replay-stable

`FanOutlet` mints its emission-epoch `sourceId` with `UUID.randomUUID()`
(`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/port/FanOutlet.kt:127`, re-minted at `:235` by
`mintFreshEpoch`). The processed-frontier keys on `MessageContext.timestamp.sourceId`
(`HostDurability.kt:257-258`, `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/MessageContext.kt:16-17`).
`OutletWaveState(sourceId, highWater)`
(`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/port/OutletWaveState.kt:15`) is **not** part of any
`Stateful.snapshot`, and durability recovery does not adopt it.

Consequence, verified by construction in `DISPUTES.md` and reproducible: **a journaled
source feeding an `Effectful` sink double-fires on recovery** — the replayed re-emission
carries a fresh `sourceId` the sink's restored frontier cannot match. Exactly-once effect
delivery is drivable today *only* when the effect subgraph's source is volatile, which is
why `DUR-REPLAY-01` deliberately keeps the data-recovery path and the effect-once path as
two independent subgraphs.

This is not merely a G-59 residual; it is a direct instance of `[24-DUR-04]`, which
requires that *"a recovered instance MUST re-mint the identities the network already
observed … derived from the cell's ref (never `randomUUID`)"*. That requirement is
currently satisfied for the **tag plane** (set tags, PN source slots, tag counter in
snapshot state) and **not** for the **outlet wave plane**. Closing that asymmetry is the
core of KFX.

**The mechanism to carry an epoch across a continuation already exists and is the natural
fix.** `FanOutlet.waveState()` (`FanOutlet.kt:216`) and `adoptWaveState(state)`
(`FanOutlet.kt:223`) are exactly a preserved-epoch handover, used today by promotion state
transfer (`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/evolve/Evolution.kt:198`) and, per
`OutletWaveState`'s KDoc, by drain and migration. Durable recovery is the one preserved-epoch
continuation that does not use it — it falls through to the cold-start default and mints
fresh.

### Residual B — a null-timestamp frame at an `Effectful` inlet is never deduped

`ManagedHost.kt:790-794` reads
`hostedInvocation.invocation.context?.timestamp` and applies the frontier check **only when
that timestamp is non-null**. A frame carrying no `MessageContext` — the externally-driven
root case, precisely the shape a CON1 connector ingress produces — is therefore **never
deduped and always re-fires on replay**. `[24-DUR-05]` is written unconditionally
(*"IF an invocation at an `Effectful` inlet is at or behind that inlet's processed-frontier
… THEN it SHALL be suppressed"*), and a frame with no timestamp has no defined position
relative to any frontier. The gap is real; the ticket's job is to *decide* it, not to
discover it at CON1 time.

### The decided-rule question the ticket must answer explicitly

Is durable recovery a **preserved-epoch** continuation (adopt the `sourceId`) or a
**fresh-epoch succession** (mint, and announce via the `ReBaseline` supersession notice)?
Both are defensible against decided text and the ticket must choose one **in writing**,
against the sources, rather than by whichever is easier to code:

- **Preserved-epoch** is supported by `31-hosts.md`: *"Durability subsumes RESTART: a
  durable cell's RESTART MUST restore its latest snapshot + journal tail instead of the
  spawn-time checkpoint — same mechanism, richer checkpoint source"*, and by `[24-DUR-04]`'s
  "re-mint the identities the network already observed". It is also what makes the sink's
  restored frontier work at all.
- **Fresh-epoch** is supported by 93 I-14 Rule S1 as encoded in `OutletWaveState`'s KDoc:
  *"Every other transition (cold start, **RESTART**, replica/candidate spawn, a fallback
  promotion swap) mints a fresh `sourceId`"* — and I-14 Rule S5 / I-22 require such a
  succession to be wave-observable via `ReBaseline` (`FanOutlet.reBaseline`, `:243`) so a
  glitch-free consumer recomputes its per-source completeness set.

If they conflict, `AGENTS.md`'s authority order applies — cited spec text, then
`93-feature-interactions.md`, then the corpus — and the divergence is made explicit in tests
and in the final report, not silently resolved.

## What we build

1. **The audit record**: the frontier is landed; `91-gap-analysis.md:18` is stale; filed as
   a finding, gap table untouched.
2. **CHA2's failing tests turned green** — CHA2 delivers the C-9 reproduction suite, and
   KFX is the fix those tests are waiting for. KFX does not re-derive the reproductions.
3. **Replay-stable outlet wave identity** so a journaled source's replayed emissions carry
   the identity the sink's restored frontier already recorded — closing Residual A and the
   outlet-plane half of `[24-DUR-04]`.
4. **A decided, tested answer for the null-timestamp `Effectful` frame** — closing
   Residual B, or recording it as an explicit, bounded limit if the decision is that it
   cannot be closed here.
5. **The corpus consequence**: if Residual A closes, `DUR-REPLAY-01`'s two-subgraph
   construction is no longer forced, and the corresponding `DISPUTES.md` entry is retired
   or narrowed — the DISPUTES "Resolves" bullet already names this exact outcome.

## How, using ComputeNet

**Residual A.** The checkpoint payload already carries cell state and the processed-frontier
atomically together (`CheckpointRecord`, `HostDurability.kt:41-45`, written at `:209-235`,
restored at `:237-245`). Outlet wave state joins it by the same route, captured through the
existing `FanOutlet.waveState()` and restored through the existing `adoptWaveState()` — the
same pair promotion already uses at `Evolution.kt:198`. No new mechanism, no new record
type if the checkpoint record carries it; if a per-outlet durable record is needed between
checkpoints, it follows the `FrontierRecord`/`RECORD_FRONTIER` shape already established
(`HostDurability.kt:34-39,192-199`).

The alternative shape — deriving the `sourceId` from the cell's ref and the port, the way
set tags and PN slots already are per `[24-DUR-04]` — is the more literal reading of that
requirement and avoids a durable record entirely, at the cost of interacting with
`mintFreshEpoch`'s epoch-rotation semantics (`FanOutlet.kt:229-238`). The ticket picks one
and argues it against `[24-DUR-04]` and I-14 Rule S1; both are in scope, the choice is not
pre-made here.

**Residual B.** The decision point is `ManagedHost.kt:790`. The candidate answers, all
expressible with existing machinery:
- stamp a `Timestamp` at the ingress boundary so every frame reaching an `Effectful` inlet
  has a frontier position;
- refuse to journal an `Effectful`-bound frame that carries no timestamp, making the hole
  impossible rather than silent;
- keep the current behaviour and state it as a bounded limit — with the external-idempotency
  ceiling that 93 I-7 already names as a stated limit — recorded in `DISPUTES.md` against
  `[24-DUR-05]`.
The third is an acceptable outcome; **silently keeping the current behaviour is not.**

**Glitch-freedom and replication must not regress.** `Effectful` is also read by
`Replication` (`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/replication/Replication.kt:190`) and
`SingleWriterReplication` (`.../SingleWriterReplication.kt:285,309`), where PN-17's
effect-authority rule suppresses follower inlets through `Shadow.suppress`
(`Evolution.kt:62,77-86`). A change to `sourceId` stability touches the per-source
completeness sets that glitch-free consumers maintain, and the replayed-cone baseline logic
at `FanOutlet.kt:~228` (PN-2). Both are regression surfaces, not scope.

## Scope boundaries

- **Not the processed-frontier itself** — landed; do not rebuild.
- **Not CHA2.** CHA2 owns the reproduction suite for C-9/C-11/C-12. KFX consumes its C-9
  failing tests and fixes them; it does not build the rig.
- **Not C-11 or C-12.** CHA2 reproduces all three decided-but-divergent rules; KFX fixes
  only the C-9 one. C-11 (shadow drops exclusives) is noted in KHYG's findings and is
  SEC1-adjacent; C-12 was adjudicated (D-C12) as stale prose, not divergent code.
- **Not the whole of G-59.** G-59 names five unhandled classes: wall-clock/random logic,
  spontaneously-emitting sources, `Effectful` sinks without idempotency keys, glitch-free
  partial-wave buffers, and cross-host recovery-frontier drift. KFX addresses the
  **source-identity** and **`Effectful`-sink** slices. The determinism marker/lint, the
  emitted-delta log format, partial-wave-buffer reconstruction, cross-host frontier drift,
  and the opt-in coordinated checkpoint are **not** in scope — several are research-gated.
- **No edit to `91-gap-analysis.md`, `CONCORDANCE.md`, or any plan document.**
- **No journal record-format break** beyond an additive field/record, and no change to
  `recoverFrom`'s ordering or its `RecoveryIncomplete` shape
  (`HostDurability.kt:120-174,30`).
- **No new normative spec id** without explicit documentation-maintenance authorization;
  `[24-DUR-04]` and `[24-DUR-05]` already state the rules.
- **Not CON1.** CON1's Postgres-CDC/Kafka connector pair with idempotency keys is the
  consumer; KFX is its unblock.

## Functional requirements (EARS)

### Audit band

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KFX-01]` The ticket SHALL produce a findings record stating that the
`Effectful` processed-frontier is landed, citing the implementing sites, and stating that
the C-9 row of the gap analysis is stale relative to the normative sections and the
corpus. *(`[24-DUR-05]`)*

*(Unwanted behaviour)* `[KFX-02]` IF the audit finds the frontier present, THEN no second
processed-frontier mechanism SHALL be introduced. *(`[24-DUR-05]`)*

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KFX-03]` The ticket SHALL NOT edit `doc/spec/90-roadmap/91-gap-analysis.md`,
`doc/spec/CONCORDANCE.md`, or any plan document. *(`AGENTS.md`; milestone plan §6)*

### The existing guarantee must not regress

*(Event-driven)* `[KFX-04]` WHEN a host recovers from a journal, an invocation at an
`Effectful` inlet at or behind that inlet's processed-frontier SHALL be suppressed as
already-acted rather than re-driving the sink. *(`[24-DUR-05]`)*

*(Event-driven)* `[KFX-05]` WHEN post-recovery live delivery presents an invocation at or
behind an `Effectful` inlet's frontier, it SHALL be suppressed by the same rule as replay —
one frontier, consulted on both paths. *(`[24-DUR-05]`)*

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KFX-06]` An `Effectful` inlet's frontier advance SHALL remain durable
together with the cell state it accompanies, so a restored cell and its restored frontier
are always from the same point. *(`[24-DUR-05]`, `[24-DUR-02]`)*

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KFX-07]` A journal SHALL continue to hold only its own cells' records, so
replay re-delivers nothing to a co-hosted cell mapped elsewhere. *(`[24-DUR-03]`)*

### Residual A — replay-stable source identity

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KFX-08]` A recovered cell's outlet emission identity SHALL be the identity
its emissions already carried before the crash — it SHALL NOT be freshly minted at random
by the recovery path. *(`[24-DUR-04]`)*

*(Event-driven)* `[KFX-09]` WHEN a **journaled** source feeds an `Effectful` sink and the
host crashes and recovers, each logical delta SHALL fire its external effect exactly once
across the crash — not zero times, and not twice. *(`[24-DUR-05]`, `[24-DUR-04]`)*

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KFX-10]` The outlet's counter high-water SHALL be restored together with
its identity, so a recovered outlet's next emission does not reuse a counter value the
network already observed. *(`[24-DUR-04]`)*

*(Unwanted behaviour)* `[KFX-11]` IF a recovered outlet's identity were reused while its
counter restarted from zero, THEN a downstream frontier would suppress live post-recovery
traffic as already-acted; this SHALL NOT occur. *(`[24-DUR-04]`, `[24-DUR-05]`)*

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KFX-12]` The ticket SHALL state, in writing and against the cited sources,
whether durable recovery is a preserved-epoch continuation or a fresh-epoch succession, and
SHALL implement the choice consistently across the journal, checkpoint, and live paths.
*(`[24-DUR-04]`; 93 I-14 Rule S1)*

*(Optional feature)* `[KFX-13]` WHERE the decision of `[KFX-12]` is a fresh-epoch
succession, the recovery SHALL emit the supersession notice that makes it wave-observable,
so a glitch-free consumer recomputes its per-source completeness set. *(93 I-14 Rule S5,
I-22)*

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KFX-14]` Epoch transitions that are **not** durable recovery — cold start,
replica/candidate spawn, fallback promotion swap — SHALL continue to mint a fresh identity
exactly as they do today. *(93 I-14 Rule S1)*

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KFX-15]` Preserved-epoch continuations that already adopt wave state —
drain, migration, promotion state transfer — SHALL be unaffected. *(93 I-14 Rule S1)*

### Residual B — the null-timestamp frame

*(Unwanted behaviour)* `[KFX-16]` IF an invocation reaching an `Effectful` inlet carries no
message context and therefore no frontier position, THEN the ticket SHALL have decided and
implemented one of: stamping it at ingress, refusing to journal it, or recording it as an
explicit bounded limit — and the chosen behaviour SHALL be tested. *(`[24-DUR-05]`)*

*(Unwanted behaviour)* `[KFX-17]` IF the decision is to record a limit rather than close the
hole, THEN that limit SHALL be written into `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` against
`[24-DUR-05]` — it SHALL NOT be left as unremarked code behaviour, and no scenario SHALL be
written that asserts the weaker rule as though it were the decided one. *(`AGENTS.md`
honesty ledger)*

### Composition

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KFX-18]` Wave, source and tag continuity SHALL survive recovery: a
glitch-free consumer downstream of a recovered source SHALL NOT observe a torn or
double-counted wave. *(`[24-DUR-04]`; the wave-continuity invariant in `AGENTS.md`)*

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KFX-19]` PN-17 effect authority under replication SHALL be unchanged: a
disjoint-interest instance set stays effect-once by construction, and a total/overlapping
set's follower inlets stay suppressed. *(`doc/spec/30-execution-model/31-hosts.md`
§"Effects on instance sets")*

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KFX-20]` No exclusive payload SHALL be dropped on any suppression path this
ticket touches: a suppressed-as-already-acted invocation carrying an `Owned` or `Leased`
value SHALL discharge it explicitly. *(23 §Ownership; the no-silent-drop invariant in
`AGENTS.md`; the same class of defect KHYG already records against `MediateProxy`/`CompositeCell`)*

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KFX-21]` The change SHALL be additive on the wire and on disk: no existing
frame encoding or journal record type SHALL change meaning. *(`[24-DUR-02]`; `AGENTS.md`
compatibility rule)*

### Consuming CHA2

*(Event-driven)* `[KFX-22]` WHEN CHA2's C-9 reproduction tests are run against the merged
change, they SHALL pass without being weakened, re-seeded, or narrowed. *(`[24-DUR-05]`;
the preserve-deterministic-simulation invariant in `AGENTS.md`)*

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KFX-23]` The corpus `DISPUTES.md` entry recording the journaled-source
double-fire boundary SHALL be retired or narrowed to match what remains true after the fix.
*(`[24-DUR-05]`)*

### A requirement that cannot be checked honestly, stated rather than softened

`[KFX-24]` *(recorded, not asserted)* "The external effect fired exactly once **in the
outside world**" is not verifiable inside this repository. The processed-frontier makes the
*kernel's* delivery exactly-once across recovery; whether the actuator on the other side of
the sink observed one call depends on that system's own idempotency, which 93 I-7 already
names as the **external-idempotency ceiling** and states as a limit rather than a bug.
`[KFX-09]` is therefore written against an in-process observed effect log — the shape
`EffectfulRecoveryTest` and `DUR-REPLAY-01`'s `effect-count` already use. It must not be
restated as an end-to-end exactly-once claim; CON1's connector idempotency keys are where
that ceiling is actually addressed.

## Suggested task decomposition (list only — do not create these beads)

1. Audit pass; findings record incl. the stale C-9 gap row.
2. Decide `[KFX-12]` (preserved- vs fresh-epoch recovery) against `[24-DUR-04]`, 31-hosts
   and I-14 Rule S1; write the decision down.
3. Capture/restore outlet wave identity + high-water through the existing checkpoint and
   `waveState()`/`adoptWaveState()` seams.
4. Decide and implement `[KFX-16]` for the null-timestamp `Effectful` frame.
5. Exclusive-payload discharge on the suppression path (`[KFX-20]`).
6. Run CHA2's C-9 reproductions; fix until green without weakening them.
7. Regression sweep: replication/PN-17, promotion/drain/migration epoch adoption,
   glitch-free per-source completeness, PN-2 replayed-cone baselines.
8. Retire or narrow the `DISPUTES.md` boundary entry; fold `DUR-REPLAY-01`'s two subgraphs
   into one if and only if the fix genuinely permits it; regenerate `CONCORDANCE.md`.

## Verification

```bash
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.durability.EffectfulRecoveryTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.durability.CrashRecoveryTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.durability.MixedDurabilityTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.durability.DurableGlitchFreeReplayTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.evolve.*'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.replication.*'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.port.*'
./gradlew :concord:test -Pconcord.profiles=core,dur
./gradlew :concord:check
./gradlew :demo:shopping:test
./gradlew :demo:exchange:test
./gradlew test
```

`:demo:exchange:test` is named explicitly: `ExchangeCompositionExitTest` composes
partitioned + replicated + durable + glitch-free in one graph and is the repo's toughest
property gate — precisely the composition a source-identity change can break.
`:concord:test -Pconcord.profiles=core,dur` drives `DUR-REPLAY-01`, the scenario whose
two-subgraph construction this ticket may retire.

## Risks / open questions

1. **The plan's description is stale.** "Build a minimal processed-frontier" would rebuild
   a merged mechanism. `[KFX-01]`/`[KFX-02]` exist to force the audit first. This is the
   ticket's largest failure mode.
2. **`[KFX-12]` is a genuine spec fork.** 31-hosts ("durability subsumes RESTART … same
   mechanism") and I-14 Rule S1 ("RESTART mints fresh") point opposite ways for the
   recovery case. Both are decided text. This must be argued and written down, not
   resolved by convenience — and if they genuinely conflict, the divergence is made
   explicit per `AGENTS.md`, not smoothed over.
3. **Source-identity stability has wide blast radius.** `sourceId` is the key of glitch-free
   per-source completeness sets, of replication's delivered watermark, of PN-2 replayed-cone
   baselines, and of `mintFreshEpoch`/`reBaseline` supersession. "Small" describes the diff,
   not the regression surface. `[KFX-14]`, `[KFX-15]`, `[KFX-18]`, `[KFX-19]` are the
   guards; the exchange and replication suites are where they get tested.
4. **CHA2 is a hard input.** KFX without CHA2's failing tests is a fix without a
   reproduction, which is how a durability bug comes back. If CHA2 slips, the honest options
   are to wait or to write the reproduction as part of KFX and say so — not to declare the
   fix verified by the tests that already pass.
5. **Residual B may be larger than it looks.** Stamping ingress frames with a `Timestamp`
   touches every externally-driven path, including the wire ingress. If the analysis shows
   that, the right move is the recorded-limit option (`[KFX-17]`) plus a filed ticket — not
   quietly widening KFX.
6. **KHYG framing.** KFX changes recovery behaviour and is not behaviour-preserving; it is
   filed under KHYG for its lane-slot and latent-finding properties. If a reviewer reads
   KHYG's "behaviour-preserving in intent" as a hard boundary, KFX should move out rather
   than have its scope trimmed to fit the epic.
design:
# KFX — Behaviour specifications

Given/When/Then, specific enough to become named tests. Each names the requirement ids it
discharges and, where it belongs in the executable specification, a `covers:` line.

The corpus already carries `DUR-REPLAY-01` (`covers: [24-DUR-01, 24-DUR-02, 24-DUR-05]`)
and `DUR-SNAPTAIL-01` (`covers: [24-DUR-02, 24-DUR-03]`) in the `dur` profile, driven
against the real durability machinery. Everything below either strengthens those or is a
kernel test; nothing here may weaken them.

---

## Audit band

### BS-01 — The frontier is not rebuilt
**Given** the merged diff
**When** implementations of "per-`(cellRef, portName)` last-applied `(sourceId, counter)`
consulted before an `Effectful` invocation" are enumerated
**Then** exactly one exists, and it is the one that was already in `main`.
Discharges `[KFX-01]`, `[KFX-02]`.
*Not a concord scenario* — a structural property of the implementation; concord is
implementation-neutral. Findings record plus a review gate.

### BS-02 — The gap table is untouched
**Given** the merged diff
**When** `doc/spec/90-roadmap/91-gap-analysis.md`, `doc/spec/CONCORDANCE.md` and the plan
documents are diffed
**Then** the first two show no hand edit (`CONCORDANCE.md` regenerating byte-identically
except for entries the corpus change legitimately produces), and the plan documents are
unchanged — while the findings record states the C-9 row's staleness.
Discharges `[KFX-01]`, `[KFX-03]`.
*Not a concord scenario* — a process gate, checked by `./gradlew :concord:check` plus diff
review.

---

## The existing guarantee must not regress

### BS-10 — Volatile source, effectful sink, exactly once (the case that works today)
**Given** the `DUR-REPLAY-01` shape: a volatile source feeding a journaled `Effectful` sink
whose every add fires one externally-observed effect
**When** adds are applied, the durable host crashes and is rebuilt from its surviving
journal, then more adds are applied and the graph is driven to quiescence
**Then** each key fired exactly once — pre-crash keys were suppressed at or behind the
restored frontier on replay, and the post-recovery key fired once.
Discharges `[KFX-04]`, `[KFX-06]`.
`covers: [24-DUR-05]` — **this is the existing `DUR-REPLAY-01` and must keep passing
unchanged.** It is the regression floor for the whole ticket.

### BS-11 — Post-recovery live delivery obeys the same frontier
**Given** a recovered `Effectful` sink whose frontier was restored
**When** a *live* (not replayed) invocation arrives at or behind that frontier — the
duplicate an upstream retransmit or catch-up produces
**Then** it is suppressed as already-acted, by the same check replay used; **and when** one
arrives ahead of the frontier **then** it fires and advances the frontier.
Discharges `[KFX-05]`.
`covers: [24-DUR-05]` — corpus-worthy; `[24-DUR-05]` explicitly names both paths
("whether encountered during `recoverFrom` replay or post-recovery live delivery") and
only the replay half is exercised today.

### BS-12 — Cell state and frontier restore from the same point
**Given** an `Effectful` cell that is also `Stateful`, checkpointed and then advanced
further
**When** the host recovers
**Then** the restored state and the restored frontier correspond to the same point — there
is no recovery in which the state reflects an invocation the frontier does not, or vice
versa.
Discharges `[KFX-06]`.
`covers: [24-DUR-02], [24-DUR-05]` — corpus-worthy; atomicity of the checkpoint payload is
the property that makes suppression sound.

### BS-13 — Per-journal scoping holds
**Given** two cells on one host mapped to different journals, one carrying an `Effectful`
sink
**When** one journal is replayed
**Then** the co-hosted cell receives nothing and its effects do not fire.
Discharges `[KFX-07]`.
`covers: [24-DUR-03]` — corpus-worthy; `MixedDurabilityTest` is the kernel precedent.

---

## Residual A — replay-stable source identity

### BS-20 — The failing case, made to pass: journaled source → effectful sink
**Given** a **journaled** source feeding an `Effectful` sink — the construction
`DISPUTES.md` records as currently double-firing, and the one `DUR-REPLAY-01` deliberately
avoids by keeping two independent subgraphs
**When** adds are applied, the host crashes, recovery replays the source's frames so the
source re-emits, and the graph is driven to quiescence
**Then** each logical delta fired its effect exactly once — the replayed re-emission
carried the identity the sink's restored frontier already recorded and was suppressed.
Discharges `[KFX-08]`, `[KFX-09]`.
`covers: [24-DUR-04], [24-DUR-05]` — **the ticket's headline scenario.** It is corpus-worthy
and it is precisely the fold-into-one-subgraph outcome the existing `DISPUTES.md`
"Resolves" bullet predicts. If it passes, `[KFX-23]` retires that boundary entry; if it
cannot be made to pass, the entry stays and is narrowed to say exactly what remains broken —
it is **not** softened into a scenario that passes for a weaker reason.

### BS-21 — Counter high-water survives, so the next emission is fresh
**Given** a recovered outlet whose identity was preserved
**When** it emits after recovery
**Then** the emission's counter is strictly greater than any counter the network observed
from that identity before the crash — a downstream frontier does not suppress it as
already-acted.
Discharges `[KFX-10]`, `[KFX-11]`.
`covers: [24-DUR-04]` — corpus-worthy, and the exact failure a naive
"restore the identity, forget the counter" fix produces: **silent effect loss**, which is
worse than the double-fire it replaces. Test it directly.

### BS-22 — Non-recovery transitions still mint fresh
**Given** each of: a cold start, a replica/candidate spawn, and a fallback promotion swap
**When** each occurs
**Then** a fresh emission identity is minted, exactly as today; **and** where the decided
answer to `[KFX-12]` makes recovery a fresh-epoch succession, the supersession notice is
emitted and a glitch-free consumer downstream recomputes its per-source completeness set.
Discharges `[KFX-13]`, `[KFX-14]`.
`covers: [24-DUR-04]` for the recovery arm; the cold-start/spawn/fallback arms are existing
kernel behaviour and belong in kernel tests (they are wave-plane internals rather than
boundary-observable outcomes).

### BS-23 — Preserved-epoch continuations unaffected
**Given** a drain-and-resume, a migration, and a promotion state transfer
**When** each completes
**Then** the successor continues the same source lane with the same identity and high-water,
exactly as before this ticket — no adoption path changed.
Discharges `[KFX-15]`.
*Not a concord scenario* — these are existing behaviours with existing coverage
(`33-mobility` in the corpus, plus the evolve/promotion kernel suite). The requirement is a
regression gate, discharged by those suites passing unchanged.

---

## Residual B — the null-timestamp frame

### BS-30 — An externally-driven frame at an effectful inlet, across a crash
**Given** an `Effectful` cell driven directly by an external caller, so the accepted frames
carry no message context and therefore no frontier position
**When** the host crashes and replays those frames
**Then** the observed behaviour is exactly the behaviour the ticket **decided** under
`[KFX-16]` — stamped at ingress and deduped, or refused at journal time, or re-fired with a
recorded limit — and a named test asserts that decision.
Discharges `[KFX-16]`.
`covers: [24-DUR-05]` **only if** the decision closes the hole. If the decision is to record
a limit, this is a kernel test plus a `DISPUTES.md` entry and **no corpus scenario is
written**, because a scenario asserting "the effect re-fires" would state a weaker rule than
`[24-DUR-05]` as though it were the decided one.

### BS-31 — The limit, if kept, is written down
**Given** the decision to keep the current behaviour for null-timestamp frames
**When** `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` is read
**Then** it carries an entry against `[24-DUR-05]` naming the case, its cause, and what
would resolve it — in the same form as the existing G-59/C-9 boundary entry.
Discharges `[KFX-17]`.
*Not a concord scenario by construction* — it is the honesty ledger itself.

---

## Composition and non-regression

### BS-40 — Glitch-free continuity across recovery
**Given** a glitch-free consumer downstream of a recovering source, with a multi-input join
mid-wave at crash time
**When** the host recovers and the graph is driven to quiescence
**Then** the consumer's output equals the batch recompute over everything it accepted — no
torn wave, no double count, no stranded partial-wave buffer.
Discharges `[KFX-18]`.
`covers: [24-DUR-02], [24-DUR-04]` — corpus-worthy; `DurableGlitchFreeReplayTest` is the
kernel precedent and the corpus already has convergence checks of this shape.
Note this touches G-59's *partial-wave buffer* slice, which is **out of scope**: the
scenario asserts no regression, not that the buffer question is solved.

### BS-41 — PN-17 effect authority unchanged
**Given** (a) a disjoint-interest instance set and (b) a total-interest set with a declared
`SingleWriterReplication` leader, each fronting an `Effectful` sink
**When** a logical delta is applied, and again across a leader handoff
**Then** (a) fires once by construction; (b) fires exactly once per logical delta across the
handoff — never zero (a gap), never twice (a resurrected deposed leader) — and followers
stay suppressed.
Discharges `[KFX-19]`.
`covers: [24-DUR-05]` — corpus-worthy under `42-replication`; it is the composition most
likely to break under a source-identity change, since replication's delivered watermark and
the effect frontier both key on source identity.

### BS-42 — A suppressed exclusive is discharged, not dropped
**Given** an `Effectful` inlet whose contract carries an `Owned` (and, separately, a
`Leased`) payload
**When** an invocation at or behind the frontier is suppressed as already-acted
**Then** the payload is explicitly consumed or released — no exclusive is silently dropped,
and the accounting shows the discharge.
Discharges `[KFX-20]`.
`covers: [24-DUR-05]` and the ownership rules — **corpus-worthy under `23-ownership`, and
the scenario most likely to be forgotten.** The suppression path at `ManagedHost.kt:791-794`
is a `return`-shaped drop of exactly the kind `AGENTS.md` forbids and KHYG already records
against `MediateProxy`/`CompositeCell`. If the current code drops, that is a defect
discovered by this ticket and either fixed here or filed — never left unremarked.

### BS-43 — Additive on disk and on the wire
**Given** a journal written before this change
**When** it is replayed by the changed kernel
**Then** it replays to the same recovered state as before, and any new record or field is
absent-tolerated rather than required.
Discharges `[KFX-21]`.
`covers: [24-DUR-02]` — corpus-worthy as a compatibility gate, if the corpus can express a
pre-existing log; otherwise a kernel test with a checked-in fixture log.

---

## Consuming CHA2

### BS-50 — CHA2's C-9 reproductions go green on their own terms
**Given** CHA2's reproduction suite for C-9, failing against `main`
**When** it is run against the merged KFX change
**Then** every C-9 reproduction passes with its original seeds, its original assertions and
its original scope — none re-seeded, none narrowed, none marked expected-failure.
Discharges `[KFX-22]`.
*Not a concord scenario* — CHA2's rig is a DST harness over `SimulationController`, not a
corpus scenario. It is nevertheless the acceptance gate for this ticket.
**Do not replace a discovered failing seed with a friendlier seed** (`AGENTS.md`).

### BS-51 — The DISPUTES boundary matches reality afterwards
**Given** the merged change
**When** the G-59/C-9 boundary entry in `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` is read
**Then** it describes exactly what is still true — retired if BS-20 passes and the
journaled-source case is genuinely closed, narrowed if only part is, unchanged if neither.
Discharges `[KFX-23]`.
*The ledger itself* — and the one place where an over-claim would do the most damage,
because DISPUTES is what a future reader trusts when the code and the gap table disagree.

---

## Note on corpus admission

The scenarios above target `24-DUR-02`, `24-DUR-03`, `24-DUR-04` and `24-DUR-05` in the
existing `dur` profile, which already has the driver type bindings this needs
(`set-source`, `set-view`, `effect-sink`, `journal`) and the checks
(`effect-count`, `incremental-equals-batch`, `views-converge`, `no-dead-letters`).
`24-DUR-04` is currently exercised only *indirectly* (per `DISPUTES.md`, "not asserted head
on"); BS-20 and BS-21 are the natural place to assert it directly, which is a strict
improvement.

If a scenario needs a **new** check kind or type binding — a leader-handoff verb for BS-41,
an exclusive-discharge accounting check for BS-42 — that is a gated `concord/schema/*.md`
change. File it; do not invent a binding. Regenerate `doc/spec/CONCORDANCE.md` with
`./gradlew :concord:concordance`; never hand-edit it.

**The one thing that must not happen**: `DUR-REPLAY-01` being folded into a single subgraph
because it looks tidier, without BS-20 actually passing. The two-subgraph construction is
load-bearing today and its comment says why.

title: KE1 — E1: OR-map / tagged-map convergence class (E1.1–E1.6)
description:
# KE1 — E1: OR-map / tagged-map convergence class (E1.1–E1.6)

Plan row (`computenet-milestone-plan.md` §1, kernel lane): "E1: OR-map / tagged-map
convergence class (E1.1–E1.6) | Depends on: ORA1 leverage | Unblocks: AGO3, SOC1 keyed
state, ORA2, BB-TPCH deletions, BB-YCSB". §4 kernel-lane order position 2, "most-demanded
chunk". §3 names it the kernel gap on the critical path for incremental TPC-H and for
YCSB multi-writer keyed.

Normative source: `doc/spec/20-dataflow-semantics/24-data-cells.md` §Tagged maps
(`:289-395`), `doc/spec/40-distribution/42-replication.md` §Design as implemented
(`:70`), `doc/spec/90-roadmap/96-incremental-engines-plan.md` §E1 (`:44-158`),
`doc/spec/90-roadmap/91-gap-analysis.md` G-23 row, `doc/spec/90-roadmap/95-research-plan.md`
§R8 (promoted), §R10 and §R17 (excluded corners).

---

## 1. Ambition / why

G-23 — "delta merges are arrival-order biased; not replica-stable" — is the ceiling on
distributing any *map-shaped* feature. `MapDelta` carries no causal tags, so every keyed
edge (`MapCell`, `CombineLatestCell`, `LookupJoinCell`, `GroupByCell` outputs) is
single-writer-or-diverge. E1 lifts `SetCell`'s observed-remove idiom from a live/tombstoned
tag per *element* to a live/tombstoned **dot** per *key*, and then — crucially — makes that
convergent structure *consumable by the existing deterministic operator library* rather than
rewriting every join.

Four consumers wait on it, and they want different halves:

- **AGO3** (revision/retraction, stable claim identity across re-extraction) wants
  multi-writer per-key value convergence — the OR-map itself.
- **SOC1** (LDBC-SNB-backed social demo) wants keyed state that survives multi-peer writes.
- **ORA2** (oracle coverage for the tagged/keyed family) wants a batch-recomputable read
  model — i.e. the fold, `TaggedMapView`.
- **BB-TPCH** (RF2 deletions propagating through multi-join chains) and **BB-YCSB**
  (multi-writer keyed) want the *adoption seam*: converged tagged maps feeding the
  unmodified join family, which is exactly what E1.5 builds.

**What is already built, and why this bead is still real work.** E1.1 (spec), E1.2
(`TaggedMapDelta` + `OrMapCell` local core) and E1.3 (replication: echo-terminating gossip,
C-10 re-origination, pull baseline, `ReBaseline` dead-source fencing) have **shipped and
merged** — see `doc/spec/90-roadmap/99-defects-engines-plan/00-orchestration.md` waves C2/C3
(tickets E1-SPEC, E1-CORE, E1-REPL, all "Implemented — merged") and the code at
`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/OrMapCell.kt` and
`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/delta/TaggedMapDelta.kt`. The 24-data-cells
§Tagged maps section already says so verbatim: "§E1.4–E1.6 (embedded mergeable values,
`TaggedMapView`/`UntagCell`, demo adoption) remain with the 96-plan".

So KE1's live surface is **E1.4, E1.5, E1.6 plus the conformance debt E1.2/E1.3 left
behind**: `doc/spec/CONCORDANCE.md:140-143` and `:207-210` show `24-TMAP-01`,
`24-TMAP-02`, `24-TMAP-03`, `24-TMAP-04` all as **`gap` — no covering scenario**. Four
normative laws, shipped in code, unverified by the executable arbiter. Closing that is
non-optional here: the concordance is the repo's honesty instrument, and KE1 is the last
bead that can honestly claim to own those ids.

## 2. Why this is an epic, not a feature

Filed `--type=epic`. The test is "multiple novel mechanisms, weeks of work", not "six
sub-items":

- **Three genuinely distinct mechanisms**, none derivable from another: (a) a
  *value-folding* read semantics for embedded `MergeablePayload` values that changes what
  `value(k)` means when several dots are live concurrently (E1.4), including a runtime
  admission check with a documented counterexample; (b) an *adapter and view layer*
  (`TaggedMapView`, `View.taggedMap()`, `UntagCell`) that bridges a convergent tagged
  stream into the untagged `MapDelta` vocabulary the whole join family speaks, under
  effective-only emission discipline (E1.5); (c) a **two-JVM real-wire acceptance demo**
  with concurrent same-key writes converging to one deterministic board (E1.6).
- **Plus a conformance workstream** — four EARS ids to bind in `concord/corpus/24-data-cells/`
  through the implementation-neutral driver, and at least one replication scenario in
  `concord/corpus/42-replication/`, each needing a scenario-authoring pass against
  `concord/schema/*.md` and a concordance regeneration.
- **Cross-module diff**: `kernel/.../cell/data/`, `kernel/.../cell/data/view/`,
  `kernel/.../cell/data/op/`, `kernel/.../cell/observe/Observe.kt`, `demo/tiering/`,
  `concord/corpus/`, plus spec-row maintenance in 24-data-cells §Operator library.
- **A residual with a decision in it**: `OrMapCell`'s re-baseline fence is documented as
  *replica-local* (`OrMapCell.kt:334-348`) and the closing move — a fenced-source lattice
  on the gossip mesh — is explicitly named "96 §E1 follow-on work". KE1 must either take
  that on or file it, which is an epic-level judgement, not a feature-level one.

A single feature could not carry E1.4→E1.5→E1.6's internal ordering (E1.5 depends on E1.3's
gossip path being exercised concurrently; E1.6 depends on both E1.3 and E1.5) without
becoming a serialized mega-branch.

## 3. What we build

**In-place kernel change plus one demo variant. No new module.** The wire form is already
registered additively (`TaggedMapDeltaSerializer`, `@SerialName("TaggedMapDelta")`, in
`WireCodec`), and `MapOps` is reused verbatim — so there is still **no new `@Contract`
interface and no `gen/` descriptor work** anywhere in KE1.

Package layout and entry points:

| Path | Change |
|---|---|
| `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/OrMapCell.kt` | E1.4: `values(k): Set<V>` multi-value read; mergeable-value fold in `value(k)`; embedded-class admission check |
| `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/delta/TaggedMapDelta.kt` | E1.4: same fold on the delta-level `value(k)`, so the delta and the cell never disagree |
| `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/view/TaggedMapView.kt` | **new** — E1.5 consumer-side fold, dots → `Map<K, V>`, sibling of `MapView.kt` |
| `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/observe/Observe.kt` | E1.5: `View.taggedMap()` factory beside `View.set()`/`map()`/`count()` (`:85-110`), and a `taggedMap(name, source, outletName)` builder beside `:338-348` |
| `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/op/UntagCell.kt` | **new** — E1.5 adapter cell: inlet `Propagate<TaggedMapDelta<K,V>>`, outlet `Propagate<MapDelta<K,V>>`, effective-only per-key value changes |
| `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/op/{CombineLatestCell,LookupJoinCell,JoinCell,GroupByCell}.kt` | E1.5: KDoc only — the G-23 caveat is discharged when inputs arrive via `OrMapCell`+`UntagCell` |
| `doc/spec/20-dataflow-semantics/24-data-cells.md` | E1.5: §Operator library row for `UntagCell`; §Tagged maps embedded-value + adapter paragraphs become "built" |
| `concord/corpus/24-data-cells/24-TMAP-0{1,2,3,4}.yaml` | **new** — the four laws bound to executable scenarios |
| `concord/corpus/42-replication/` | **new** — an OR-map convergence scenario (partition/heal, duplicate delivery) |
| `demo/tiering/` | E1.6: two-host bridged variant, manual re-tier edge as a replicated `OrMapCell<String, Tier>` fused through `UntagCell` |

## 4. How, using ComputeNet

**The existing substrate to build on, not around.**

- `OrMapCell.kt:151-166` — `liveDots(key)` / `membership()` / `value(key)`. E1.4 changes
  `value` only in the `V : MergeablePayload` case; `membership` is untouched.
  `TaggedMapDelta.DOT_ORDER` (`:138-139`) stays the resolution for the non-mergeable case.
- `civictech.cell.MergeablePayload` (`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/MergeablePayload.kt`)
  — the one-method `mergeWith` interface. `PnCounterDelta`
  (`kernel/.../cell/data/delta/PnCounterDelta.kt`) is the idempotent-mergeable exemplar;
  `CounterDelta` (`.../CounterDelta.kt`, plain `amount: Long` addition) is the **documented
  counterexample** the admission check must refuse — that is Riak's embedded-counter anomaly
  in this repo's own types, and E1.4's runtime check should name it.
- `MergeableGroupByCell.kt:36-42` — the existing precedent for "idempotent merge terminates
  echoes, counted merge does not", including the CP-F2/CP-F3 `MergeClass.IDEMPOTENT` port
  marker and its link-time refusal. E1.4's admission check should reuse that classification
  rather than inventing a second one; if it cannot, the divergence is a reportable finding.
- `MapView.kt` (`kernel/.../cell/data/view/MapView.kt`) — the shape `TaggedMapView` mirrors:
  `apply(delta): Boolean` returning effective-change, `current()`, `snapshot()/restore()`.
  Its own KDoc carries the G-23 caveat that `TaggedMapView` exists to retire.
- `Observe.kt:70-110` — the `View<in D, out S>` interface and the three shipped folds.
  `taggedMap()` is a fourth adapter of the identical shape; `Observe.kt:338-348` is where
  the named-sink builders live.
- `CombineLatestCell.kt:27` — outlet is `Propagate<MapDelta<K, R>>` and its inlets are
  `MapDelta`-shaped, which is precisely why `UntagCell` (not a rewrite of the join) is the
  prescribed composition: feed convergent inputs to the deterministic recompute cells
  (research `05-gap-mapping.md` §Gap 3).
- `KeyedSetCell.kt` — the atomic retract+add invariant `OrMapCell.put` already lifts to
  dots; `UntagCell` must preserve it on the way out (one `MapDelta` per input delta,
  never a remove-then-put pair that windows a zero).
- `SetCell.kt` / `SetConvergenceTest.kt` / `UnionObservedRemoveTest.kt` — the element-shaped
  siblings of every seam and their test idioms. `OrMapCellTest.kt` is the existing
  dot-shaped test file.
- `testkit`'s `SimWorld`/`SimulationController`/`awaitUntil` and `JvmPeer` — seeded
  multi-replica meshes and the two-JVM harness. `demo/shopping/src/test/kotlin/civictech/demo/TwoJvmConvergenceTest.kt`
  is the template E1.6 mirrors.
- `demo/tiering/src/main/kotlin/civictech/demo/tiering/{Tiering,TieringApp}.kt` —
  `Tiering.tierOf`/`fuse` and `TieringApp.build(host)`'s `Refs`; the manual re-tier edge is
  the one to replace with a replicated `OrMapCell<String, Tier>`.
- `concord/src/main/kotlin/civictech/concord/driver/kernel/{KernelCatalog,KernelAdapters,KernelFunctions}.kt`
  — the only place `civictech.cell.*` may be imported from concord. Any new corpus scenario
  needs its cell registered there; `concord/corpus/24-data-cells/24-OP-KEYEDSET-01.yaml` and
  `42-replication/42-REPL-01.yaml` are the nearest authoring exemplars.

**Serialization constraint (stated explicitly, per plan §1).** KE1 is kernel-lane work: it
lands inside the single kernel SCC (G-63) and therefore **must not run concurrently with
another kernel-lane chunk**. Plan §4 fixes its position at 2, after KX (C-13
`LocationRegistry` extraction) and before KFX. KX touches the registry/`InstanceIndex`/
`DeliveryHold` seam that `OrMapCell`'s pull-baseline and replication paths transit, so KE1
consumes KX **from merged `main`**, never recreated locally (AGENTS.md multi-agent run
discipline). KAGG-R follows KE1 deliberately because it audits the operator-family surface
KE1 has just touched — so KE1 must leave `Aggregator`'s retraction-aware min/max/topK
(`kernel/.../cell/data/Aggregator.kt`) and `TaggedSetOperator`
(`kernel/.../cell/data/op/TaggedSetOperator.kt`) **unmodified**; any residual it finds there
is a finding handed to KAGG-R, not a fix taken in-lane.

## 5. Scope boundaries

**In scope**: E1.4, E1.5, E1.6, and concord coverage for `[24-TMAP-01..04]` plus an OR-map
replication scenario.

**Explicitly out of scope, with the dependency edge that puts it elsewhere:**

- **Weighted / multiset (bag) semantics.** Plan §3 phrases BB-TPCH's kernel gap as "KE1 —
  tagged multiset deltas". Read against the spec, that phrasing is loose and KE1 must not
  silently broaden to match it: G-23's row in `91-gap-analysis.md` states "Weighted/bag
  semantics still deferred, trigger unchanged … weighted family per-replica in 96 §E6,
  replicable bag stays research, 95 R17". **The RF2-deletion acceptance property is met by
  E1.5's composition** — a converged tagged map untagged into the unmodified retraction-aware
  join family, whose deletion propagation through multi-join chains already exists
  (`JoinSetCell`/`SemiJoinCell`/`JoinLedger`, M11) — **not by a Z-set.** If BB-TPCH later
  proves it needs true bag arithmetic (`EXCEPT ALL`, duplicate-preserving counts), that is a
  new E6/R17-parented bead and a finding, never a KE1 scope expansion.
- **Tombstone-free (context-only) wire form** — needs the causal-merging condition whose
  delivered-watermark prerequisite is KE3 (95 §R10). `TaggedMapDelta`'s KDoc excludes it
  explicitly.
- **Dot/tombstone reclamation and compaction** — G-25/G-42; `OrMapCell`'s two `ponytail:`
  markers (`:114-115`, `:146-147`) say dot sets and `deadSources` grow monotonically. KE3
  (tag/tombstone reclamation) owns this; KE1 must not shrink either set.
- **Delivered-watermark tracking on the OR-map seam** (`DeliveryTracking`, E3.3) — KE3.
- **Ordered key-range scan over keyed families, count-distinct, multi-column ordered top-K**
  — KAGG-R, the next kernel-lane chunk. Plan §1: KAGG-R is "audit+fill on the operator-family
  surface just touched by KE1".
- **The bounded read path** (`KRD`, riding V1C-KERNEL) — BB-YCSB needs both, but KE1 owns
  only the multi-writer-keyed half. `OrMapCell` is `Stateful`, not `BoundedStateful`;
  adding the paged read is KRD/KAGG-R territory, and KE1 should file it if BB-YCSB proves
  it blocking.
- **The oracle itself** — ORA1 (`computenet-4ru`) builds the batch-oracle differential
  tester; ORA2 extends it to the tagged/keyed family. KE1 *consumes* ORA1's leverage where it
  has landed and *hands ORA2 a target*; it does not build oracle infrastructure. If ORA1 has
  not merged when KE1 starts, KE1 falls back to in-repo batch recompute controls (the
  `SetConvergenceTest` idiom) and says so.
- **Consumers**: AGO3, SOC1, BB-TPCH, BB-YCSB are downstream beads. KE1 ships the kernel
  surface and the tiering proof; it does not implement any consumer.

## 6. Functional requirements (EARS)

Ids are epic-scoped `[KE1-nn]`, namespaced so they never collide with `doc/spec/`'s
`[NN-SLUG-nn]`. Each cites the normative spec id it makes true. Requirement type is named
in brackets.

### Embedded mergeable values (E1.4)

- `[KE1-01]` *(ubiquitous)* — The tagged map SHALL restrict embedded-value folding to values
  implementing `civictech.cell.MergeablePayload`. Makes true: 24-data-cells §Tagged maps
  decided point 3.
- `[KE1-02]` *(state-driven)* — While a key has more than one live dot and `V` implements
  `MergeablePayload`, `OrMapCell.value(k)` SHALL return the `mergeWith`-fold of every live
  dot's value, folded in `DOT_ORDER` so the result is reproducible. Makes true:
  24-data-cells §Tagged maps decided point 3; refines `[24-TMAP-03]`.
- `[KE1-03]` *(state-driven)* — While a key has exactly one live dot, or `V` does not
  implement `MergeablePayload`, `OrMapCell.value(k)` SHALL return the live dot with the
  greatest `TaggedMapDelta.DOT_ORDER`, unchanged from the shipped behaviour. Makes true:
  `[24-TMAP-03]`.
- `[KE1-04]` *(unwanted behaviour)* — If an embedded value implements `MergeablePayload` with
  a non-idempotent `mergeWith` (a plain counter — `CounterDelta`), then the cell SHALL refuse
  it with a diagnostic naming the Riak embedded-counter anomaly, rather than folding it.
  Makes true: 24-data-cells §Tagged maps decided point 3.
- `[KE1-05]` *(ubiquitous)* — The embedded fold SHALL NOT read a wall clock, and SHALL NOT
  depend on the order in which dots arrived. Makes true: `[24-TMAP-03]`, `[24-TMAP-01]`.
- `[KE1-06]` *(optional feature)* — Where the application opts into concurrency-aware reads,
  the cell SHALL expose `values(k): Set<V>` returning every live dot's value so the
  application resolves the conflict itself. Makes true: 96 §E1.4 (multi-value read).
- `[KE1-07]` *(state-driven)* — While a key has no live dot, `values(k)` SHALL return the
  empty set and `value(k)` SHALL return `null`. Makes true: `[24-TMAP-02]`.
- `[KE1-08]` *(ubiquitous)* — `TaggedMapDelta.value(k)` and `OrMapCell.value(k)` SHALL agree
  on every dot state, so a consumer folding the delta and a consumer reading the cell never
  disagree. Makes true: `[24-TMAP-03]`.
- `[KE1-09]` *(event-driven)* — When two replicas concurrently `put` mergeable values at the
  same key and the deltas merge, every replica SHALL expose the same folded value. Makes
  true: `[24-TMAP-01]`, `[24-TMAP-03]`.
- `[KE1-10]` *(unwanted behaviour)* — If the merge-class classification for an embedded value
  is unavailable at link time, the cell SHALL refuse the link rather than accepting a value
  it cannot classify. Makes true: 24-data-cells §Tagged maps decided point 3; consistent with
  `MergeableGroupByCell`'s CP-F3 refusal.

### `TaggedMapView` and `View.taggedMap()` (E1.5)

- `[KE1-11]` *(ubiquitous)* — `TaggedMapView` SHALL fold a `TaggedMapDelta` stream into the
  map `{k → value(k) : k ∈ membership()}` under the same four laws the cell obeys. Makes
  true: `[24-TMAP-01]`, `[24-TMAP-02]`, `[24-TMAP-03]`.
- `[KE1-12]` *(event-driven)* — When a delta is applied that changes no key's presence and no
  key's exposed value, `TaggedMapView.apply` SHALL return `false`. Makes true: 21-propagation
  effective-only emission; mirrors `MapView.apply`'s contract.
- `[KE1-13]` *(ubiquitous)* — `TaggedMapView` SHALL be order-insensitive: applying any
  permutation, duplication or interleaving of the same delta multiset SHALL yield the same
  `current()`. Makes true: `[24-TMAP-01]`.
- `[KE1-14]` *(ubiquitous)* — `TaggedMapView` SHALL expose `snapshot()`/`restore()` of the
  `Stateful` shape, and a restored view SHALL equal the snapshotted view. Makes true: G-25
  snapshot seam; mirrors `MapView`.
- `[KE1-15]` *(ubiquitous)* — `View.taggedMap()` SHALL be registered beside `View.set()`,
  `View.map()` and `View.count()` in `civictech.cell.observe.Observe`, and an observation sink
  built over it SHALL fire `onChange` exactly when `apply` returned `true`. Makes true: 96
  §E1.5; consistent with `ObservationSink`'s effective-change contract.
- `[KE1-16]` *(event-driven)* — When a `taggedMap` sink is linked to a live `OrMapCell`
  outlet, the producer's `onLinked` catch-up SHALL seed it such that the sink's `current()`
  equals a batch fold of the cell's `state()`. Makes true: `[24-CATCHUP-01]`.

### `UntagCell` adapter and the join family (E1.5)

- `[KE1-17]` *(ubiquitous)* — `UntagCell<K, V>` SHALL accept `Propagate<TaggedMapDelta<K, V>>`
  on its inlet and emit `Propagate<MapDelta<K, V>>` on its outlet. Makes true: 96 §E1.5.
- `[KE1-18]` *(event-driven)* — When an input delta changes a key's exposed value,
  `UntagCell` SHALL emit exactly one `MapDelta` put for that key carrying the new exposed
  value. Makes true: 21-propagation effective-only emission.
- `[KE1-19]` *(event-driven)* — When an input delta causes a key's last live dot to be
  tombstoned, `UntagCell` SHALL emit that key in `MapDelta.removals`. Makes true:
  `[24-TMAP-02]`, `[24-TMAP-04]`.
- `[KE1-20]` *(unwanted behaviour)* — If an input delta leaves every key's presence and
  exposed value unchanged (an echo, a duplicate, a tombstone for an already-covered dot),
  then `UntagCell` SHALL emit nothing. Makes true: 21-propagation effective-only emission.
- `[KE1-21]` *(ubiquitous)* — A re-put over an existing key SHALL cross `UntagCell` as a
  single `MapDelta` carrying the new value, never as a removal followed by a put — no
  downstream fold observes the key absent. Makes true: `[24-TMAP-04]` re-put atomicity;
  `KeyedSetCell`'s atomic retract+add invariant.
- `[KE1-22]` *(ubiquitous)* — `UntagCell` SHALL preserve the wave, source and tag continuity
  of the delta it adapts: the emitted `MapDelta` rides the arriving wave, and `UntagCell`
  SHALL NOT originate a new wave. Makes true: 21-propagation wave continuity; 22-consistency
  glitch-free completeness.
- `[KE1-23]` *(ubiquitous)* — `UntagCell` SHALL be `Stateful`, snapshotting the exposed-value
  map it diffs against, so a restored instance does not re-emit the whole map as novelty.
  Makes true: G-25 snapshot seam.
- `[KE1-24]` *(complex)* — When two peers each run `OrMapCell → UntagCell → CombineLatestCell`
  over the same replicated OR-map, and the replicas have reached idle, then both peers'
  `CombineLatestCell` outputs SHALL be equal to each other and to a batch recompute over the
  converged map state. Makes true: `[24-TMAP-01]`, `[24-OP-COMBINE-01]`, G-23 discharge.
- `[KE1-25]` *(ubiquitous)* — `CombineLatestCell`, `LookupJoinCell`, `JoinCell` and
  `GroupByCell` SHALL be functionally unmodified by KE1; only their KDoc changes, recording
  that the G-23 caveat is discharged for inputs arriving via `OrMapCell` + `UntagCell`. Makes
  true: 96 §E1.5's "do not rewrite each join"; protects `[24-OP-*]` coverage already bound in
  the corpus.
- `[KE1-26]` *(ubiquitous)* — `MapCell`, `MapDelta` and `KeyedSetCell` SHALL remain untouched
  by KE1 — the tagged map is additive. Makes true: 24-data-cells §Tagged maps ("additive new
  delta type … `MapDelta` and its single-writer cells are untouched").
- `[KE1-27]` *(unwanted behaviour)* — If the same schedule of concurrent same-key writes is
  driven through raw `MapCell`/`MapView` instead of `OrMapCell`+`UntagCell`, then the two
  peers' outputs SHALL differ on at least one seed — the divergence control that proves the

  asserts a *failure* of the un-fixed path, deliberately.)

### Replicated demo acceptance (E1.6)

- `[KE1-28]` *(complex)* — When two JVM hosts bridged over `:wire` each drive the tiering

  `OrMapCell<String, Tier>` fused with the computed board through `UntagCell`, then after

- `[KE1-29]` *(event-driven)* — When two hosts concurrently write different tiers for the

- `[KE1-30]` *(event-driven)* — When one host removes an item's manual tier concurrently with

- `[KE1-31]` *(event-driven)* — When a host restarts and replays its journal, it SHALL

- `[KE1-32]` *(event-driven)* — When a host joins the mesh late, the catch-up

### Honesty note on one requirement

`[KE1-04]` is verifiable only for values whose non-idempotence the kernel can *detect* —
in practice, a nominated deny-list plus the `MergeClass` port marker
(`MergeableGroupByCell`'s CP-F2/CP-F3 mechanism). There is no general decision procedure for
"is this `mergeWith` idempotent". The requirement is therefore stated as a refusal over the
*classified* set, not as a universal guarantee; the residual — an unclassified
`MergeablePayload` whose merge is silently non-idempotent — belongs in
`concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` if KE1 cannot close it, and must not be restated as "the cell
rejects all non-idempotent values", which would be unverifiable.

## 7. Behaviour specifications (Given/When/Then)

Each is specific enough to become a named test. `covers:` notes say where a scenario belongs
in the concord corpus and why, or why it does not.

**BS-1 — Embedded counters converge, LWW loses an increment.**
*Given* two replicas of an `OrMapCell<String, PnCounterDelta>` in a seeded `SimWorld` mesh,
*when* replica A puts `+3` and replica B concurrently puts `+5` at key `k` and the mesh
reaches idle, *then* `value("k")` on both replicas is the merged `+8`.
*Control*: with the fold disabled (LWW pick), one increment is dropped and the assertion
fails on every seed. Requirements: `[KE1-02]`, `[KE1-05]`, `[KE1-09]`.
`covers: 24-TMAP-03` — belongs in `concord/corpus/24-data-cells/` if the driver can express
two writers with controlled dot ordering; otherwise a kernel test plus a DISPUTES entry per
`[KE1-37]`.

**BS-2 — Non-idempotent embedded value is refused, not folded.**
*Given* an `OrMapCell<String, CounterDelta>` (plain additive counter),
*when* the cell is constructed or the value is first put,
*then* a diagnostic naming the Riak embedded-counter anomaly is raised, and no fold occurs.
Requirements: `[KE1-04]`, `[KE1-10]`. Not a corpus scenario: it asserts a *kernel diagnostic*
with an implementation-specific message, which the implementation-neutral corpus cannot
express without pinning the message.

**BS-3 — Multi-value read for the non-mergeable case.**
*Given* an `OrMapCell<String, String>` with two live concurrent dots at `k`,
*when* the application calls `values("k")`,
*then* both values are returned; and `value("k")` still returns the `DOT_ORDER` pick.
*Boundary*: with `k` absent, `values("k")` is empty and `value("k")` is `null`.
Requirements: `[KE1-03]`, `[KE1-06]`, `[KE1-07]`.
`covers: 24-TMAP-02, 24-TMAP-03`.

**BS-4 — View fold is order-insensitive.**
*Given* a fixed multiset of `TaggedMapDelta`s produced by a seeded write schedule,
*when* they are applied to `TaggedMapView` in any permutation, with arbitrary duplication,
*then* `current()` is identical for every permutation, and equals the batch fold of the merged
delta. Requirements: `[KE1-11]`, `[KE1-13]`.
`covers: 24-TMAP-01` — this is the cleanest executable statement of the merge law and is the
scenario the concordance gap most wants.

**BS-5 — View reports effective change honestly.**
*Given* a `TaggedMapView` holding `{a→1}`,
*when* a delta arrives whose only content is a dot already held, or a tombstone for a dot
already covered, *then* `apply` returns `false` and an observation sink built on
`View.taggedMap()` does not fire `onChange`.
*Boundary*: a delta that tombstones the last live dot at `a` returns `true` and removes `a`.
Requirements: `[KE1-12]`, `[KE1-15]`.
`covers: 24-TMAP-02`.

**BS-6 — View survives snapshot/restore.**
*Given* a `TaggedMapView` folded over an arbitrary seeded delta sequence,
*when* it is snapshotted, discarded, and restored into a fresh view,
*then* `current()` is equal, and a subsequent delta produces the same `apply` result and the
same `current()` as on the un-restored view. Requirements: `[KE1-14]`.
Not a corpus scenario: `snapshot()/restore()` is a kernel `Stateful` seam, not a
requirement-bearing observable in the corpus vocabulary.

**BS-7 — Late-linked sink is seeded by catch-up, tombstones included.**
*Given* an `OrMapCell` that has had keys put and one key removed,
*when* a `View.taggedMap()` sink is linked to its outlet afterwards,
*then* the sink's `current()` equals the batch fold of `state()`, and the removed key is
absent. Requirements: `[KE1-16]`, `[KE1-32]`.
`covers: 24-CATCHUP-01, 24-TMAP-04` — the corpus already has late-join scenarios
(`42-REPL-LATE-01`) to mirror.

**BS-8 — Untag emits one put per exposed-value change.**
*Given* `OrMapCell → UntagCell → MapView`,
*when* a key is put, then re-put with a different value, then re-put with the *same* value,
*then* the `MapView` sees exactly two effective puts (the third re-put mints a fresh dot but
does not change the exposed value, so `UntagCell` emits nothing), and never sees the key
absent between the first and second put. Requirements: `[KE1-18]`, `[KE1-20]`, `[KE1-21]`.
`covers: 24-TMAP-03, 24-TMAP-04`.
*Boundary worth pinning*: `OrMapCell.put` deliberately always mints, even on an equal value
(`OrMapCell.kt:66-70`) — so this scenario is exactly where the cell's "always mint" and the
adapter's "effective-only" disciplines meet, and the test must assert both halves.

**BS-9 — Untag emits a removal only when the last live dot dies.**
*Given* a key with two live dots (a concurrent-put state),
*when* one dot is tombstoned, *then* `UntagCell` emits a put with the surviving exposed value
and no removal; *when* the second is tombstoned, *then* it emits a removal.
Requirements: `[KE1-19]`, `[KE1-02]`.
`covers: 24-TMAP-02, 24-TMAP-04`.

**BS-10 — Untag does not originate a wave.**
*Given* a wave arriving at `UntagCell`'s inlet,
*when* the adapter emits, *then* the emitted `MapDelta` carries the arriving wave's context
and source, and a downstream `GlitchFreeCell`/`WaveFrontier` fold sees one wave, not two.
Requirements: `[KE1-22]`.
`covers: 21-*` wave-continuity ids — the exact id to be confirmed against
`doc/spec/20-dataflow-semantics/21-propagation.md` when authoring; if no existing id fits,
the scenario is a kernel test and the shortfall is a `DISPUTES.md` note, not a new spec id
invented by KE1 (AGENTS.md forbids KE1 editing spec beyond its named sections).

**BS-11 — Untag restore does not replay the map as novelty.**
*Given* an `UntagCell` that has emitted a full map downstream,
*when* the host checkpoints and restores it and an unchanged delta arrives,
*then* it emits nothing. Requirements: `[KE1-23]`, `[KE1-20]`.
Not a corpus scenario: checkpoint/restore of an operator is a host-lifecycle seam;
`15-durability` corpus scenarios cover the mechanism generically.

**BS-12 — Two peers, untagged joins, equal outputs (the E1.5 acceptance).**
*Given* two replicas of an `OrMapCell` gossiping over a seeded `SimulationController` mesh
with partition and heal, each peer running `UntagCell → CombineLatestCell` against a
locally-identical second input,
*when* a seeded schedule of concurrent same-key puts and removes is driven and the mesh
reaches idle, *then* both peers' outputs are equal to each other and to a batch recompute over
the converged map state, on every seed in the sweep.
*Control (`[KE1-27]`)*: the same schedule through raw `MapCell` + `MapView` diverges on at
least one seed. Requirements: `[KE1-24]`, `[KE1-25]`, `[KE1-27]`, `[KE1-33]`.
`covers: 24-TMAP-01, 24-OP-COMBINE-01` — the replication half belongs in
`concord/corpus/42-replication/` beside `42-REPL-01`.
*Honesty note*: the control must not be a friendlier seed. If raw `MapCell` happens to
converge on the chosen sweep, widen the sweep or construct the schedule — do not soften the
control into "may differ".

**BS-13 — Echo termination survives KE1.**
*Given* a three-replica diamond mesh,
*when* a delta reaches a replica by two paths, *then* the second arrival re-emits nothing, and
the total emission count is bounded independent of mesh diameter.
Requirements: `[KE1-38]`, `[KE1-39]`.
`covers: 42-REPL-01` — already-bound behaviour; this is the regression guard, so the existing
scenario must stay green unmodified rather than gaining a new one.

**BS-14 — Two-JVM tiering convergence (the E1.6 acceptance).**
*Given* two JVM hosts bridged over `:wire` running the tiering demo with the manual re-tier
edge as a replicated `OrMapCell<String, Tier>` fused through `UntagCell`,
*when* both hosts concurrently re-tier the same item to different tiers and then reach idle,
*then* both hosts' boards are equal and show exactly one tier, the `DOT_ORDER` winner.
Requirements: `[KE1-28]`, `[KE1-29]`.
Not a corpus scenario: it is an application-level two-JVM acceptance over a real socket,
which the corpus (single-driver, implementation-neutral) cannot host. Mirrors
`demo/shopping/src/test/kotlin/civictech/demo/TwoJvmConvergenceTest.kt`.

**BS-15 — Concurrent remove loses to concurrent re-tier.**
*Given* the same two-host tiering setup with item `x` tiered,
*when* host A removes `x`'s manual tier while host B concurrently re-tiers `x`,
*then* after idle `x` is tiered on both hosts with B's value — B's dot was never observed by
A's remove. Requirements: `[KE1-30]`.
`covers: 24-TMAP-04` — the in-kernel form of this (two `OrMapCell` replicas, no demo) is the
corpus-appropriate scenario; the demo form is the acceptance proof.

**BS-16 — Crash, journal replay, no resurrection.**
*Given* a two-host tiering mesh where host A has put and then removed key `x`,
*when* host A crashes and restarts, replaying its journal,
*then* A re-mints the exact dots (ref-derived `dotSource`, restored counter), `x` stays
removed on both hosts, and no post-restore put collides with a spent dot.
Requirements: `[KE1-31]`, `[KE1-42]`.
`covers: 24-TAG-01` — the failure/recovery case; mirrors
`demo/shopping/.../CrashRestartConvergenceTest.kt`.

**BS-17 — Late joiner does not resurrect a removed key.**
*Given* a two-replica mesh where `x` was put and removed,
*when* a third replica joins and receives the catch-up delta-from-empty,
*then* it shows `x` absent, and it re-emits nothing that resurrects `x` elsewhere.
Requirements: `[KE1-32]`, `[KE1-38]`.
`covers: 42-REPL-LATE-01, 24-TMAP-04`.

**BS-18 — Wire round-trip is exact under the compact encoding.**
*Given* an arbitrary seeded `TaggedMapDelta` with many dots across few sources,
*when* it is serialized through `TaggedMapDeltaSerializer` and deserialized,
*then* the result is `equals` to the original, and the encoded size is strictly smaller than a
naive per-dot source encoding for any delta with more than one dot per source.
Requirements: `[KE1-41]`.
Not a corpus scenario: it is a codec property. Belongs in `:wire`'s test-vector corpus, and is
a natural donation to **WIR1** (`computenet-ncz`) — flagged as such rather than duplicated.

**BS-19 — Scope boundary held: no bag arithmetic appeared.**
*Given* the KE1 diff,
*when* it is reviewed,
*then* no weighted/multiset delta type exists, `Aggregator.kt` and `TaggedSetOperator.kt` are
unmodified, and no reclamation of dots, tombstones or `deadSources` was added.
Requirements: `[KE1-40]`, `[KE1-42]`, plus §5's exclusions.
Not a corpus scenario: a diff-shaped acceptance check for the reviewer, verified by
`git diff --stat` and by `ArchitectureRatchetTest` staying green.

## 8. Suggested feature decomposition

*(List only — do not create these beads from this specification.)*

1. **KE1-F1 — Embedded mergeable values** (96 §E1.4): the `MergeablePayload` fold in
   `value(k)`, `values(k)` multi-value read, the non-idempotent refusal reusing
   `MergeableGroupByCell`'s merge-class marker. Requirements `[KE1-01..10]`.
2. **KE1-F2 — `TaggedMapView` + `View.taggedMap()`** (96 §E1.5, view half): the consumer-side
   fold and its observation-sink registration. Requirements `[KE1-11..16]`.
3. **KE1-F3 — `UntagCell` adapter + join-family discharge** (96 §E1.5, adapter half):
   the adapter cell, the KDoc discharge on the four join cells, the two-peer
   untag→combine equality property with its divergence control. Requirements
   `[KE1-17..27]`.
4. **KE1-F4 — Concord coverage for `[24-TMAP-01..04]`**: four corpus scenarios plus an
   OR-map replication scenario, driver-catalog registration, concordance regeneration,
   DISPUTES entries for anything that cannot be checked honestly. Requirements
   `[KE1-34..37]`.
5. **KE1-F5 — Replicated `:demo:tiering` proof** (96 §E1.6): the two-host bridged variant and
   its convergence / concurrent-remove / crash-restart tests. Requirements `[KE1-28..33]`.
6. **KE1-F6 — Residual triage and handoff**: the replica-local re-baseline fence residual
   (`OrMapCell.kt:334-348`), any `Aggregator`/`TaggedSetOperator` residual found in passing
   (handed to KAGG-R), the `BoundedStateful` question for BB-YCSB, and the bag-semantics
   question for BB-TPCH — each filed as its own bead with a finding, never fixed in-lane.
   Requirements `[KE1-40]`, §5's exclusions.

Ordering inside the epic: F1 ∥ F2 → F3 → F5; F4 can start as soon as F2 lands (the view is
what makes a law observable through the driver); F6 closes the epic.

## 9. Verification

Narrowest first, then expand:

```bash
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.data.OrMapCellTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.data.OrMapEmbeddedValueTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.data.TaggedMapViewTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.data.op.UntagCellTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.replication.OrMapConvergenceTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test
./gradlew :concord:test -Pconcord.profiles=core
./gradlew :concord:concordance      # regenerate CONCORDANCE.md — never hand-edit
./gradlew :concord:check            # dangling covers: / orphan scenario gate
./gradlew :concord:docLints
./gradlew :concord:test             # full acceptance corpus (core, dist, dur)
./gradlew :wire:test
./gradlew :demo:tiering:test
./gradlew :demo:exchange:test       # composition exit gate
./gradlew :demo:agora:test          # API/behaviour regression detector
./gradlew test                      # repository-wide gate
```

Gates that must hold, not merely run:

- `doc/spec/CONCORDANCE.md` shows `24-TMAP-01..04` as covered, and the regeneration diff
  contains no hand edits.
- Every divergence control trips (`[KE1-27]`, BS-1's control, BS-12's control). A control
  that passes is a broken test, not a green one.
- `demo/exchange`'s `ExchangeCompositionExitTest` and `GlitchFreeBridgedDiamondTest` stay
  green **unmodified**.
- `git diff --stat` shows no change to `Aggregator.kt`, `TaggedSetOperator.kt`, `MapCell.kt`,
  `KeyedSetCell.kt`, `SetCell.kt`, or any `build/generated/` output.
- No new `@Contract` interface, so `:gen:test` output is unchanged.

## 10. Risks and open questions

1. **The plan says "tagged multiset deltas"; the spec says bags are E6/R17.** Resolved above
   in favour of the spec (AGENTS.md authority order), but the BB-TPCH owner must agree that
   RF2 deletion propagation through multi-join chains is met by untag→retraction-aware-joins.
   If it is not, KE1 delivers a *finding*, not a Z-set. **Open — needs the BB-TPCH bead's
   agreement.**
2. **The replica-local re-baseline fence.** `OrMapCell.kt:334-348` documents that two
   replicas can fail to re-converge when only one processed a `ReBaseline` notice, and states
   the hole is unreachable through shipped wiring. E1.6's crash-restart test walks closer to
   that wiring than anything shipped. If it becomes reachable, KE1 must stop and file, not
   improvise a fenced-source lattice — that is named as E1 follow-on work and is arguably
   KE3-adjacent.
3. **`[KE1-04]`'s verifiability** — see §6's honesty note. Likely lands partly in
   `DISPUTES.md`.
4. **Corpus expressiveness for concurrent same-key writes.** The concord driver may not be
   able to control dot ordering across two writers, which is precisely what
   `[24-TMAP-03]`/`[24-TMAP-04]` need. If so, the corpus gets the deterministic
   single-replica laws and `DISPUTES.md` gets the concurrency shortfall with the reason —
   never a scenario weakened until it passes.
5. **ORA1 timing.** KE1 is listed as depending on "ORA1 leverage" (soft). If ORA1 has not
   merged, the batch-recompute controls are written in-repo and ORA2 later replaces them.
   Not a blocker; a reportable substitution.
6. **`UntagCell` wave continuity vs. `GlitchFreeCell` replay.** `[KE1-22]` assumes the
   adapter can emit on the arriving wave. The E2-SUITE finding recorded at CC3 (an ungated
   binary operator emitting twice per wave) is a warning that single-inlet assumptions about
   wave settling are easy to get wrong. `UntagCell` is single-inlet, so it should be clean —
   verify, do not assume.
7. **Kernel-lane serialization.** If KX (`computenet-iyi`) is still in flight, KE1 cannot
   start; if a KX follow-up lands mid-KE1, KE1 rebases on merged `main` rather than
   recreating the registry split locally.
