# KE1 design notes — what is already built, and the seams KE1 attaches to

## Landed already (do NOT rebuild)

E1.1, E1.2 and E1.3 shipped and merged via the 99-defects-engines-plan track C waves
(tickets E1-SPEC, E1-CORE, E1-REPL; see
`doc/spec/90-roadmap/99-defects-engines-plan/00-orchestration.md` waves C2/C3, all marked
"Implemented — merged").

- `doc/spec/20-dataflow-semantics/24-data-cells.md:289-395` — §Tagged maps, normative, with
  `[24-TMAP-01..04]` and the five decided points. Its own header states E1.4–E1.6 remain.
- `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/delta/TaggedMapDelta.kt` — the delta type,
  `merge` (pointwise dot union), `liveDots`/`membership`/`value`, `DOT_ORDER`
  (`compareBy { counter }.thenBy { sourceId }`), `Scoped.within` for interest-scoped links,
  and `TaggedMapDeltaSerializer` (source-dictionary compact encoding, `@SerialName
  ("TaggedMapDelta")`, registered additively in `WireCodec`).
- `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/OrMapCell.kt` — `@CellBase interface OrMapApi`
  reusing the existing `@Contract MapOps` verbatim (no gen/ work); `puts`/`dels` dot maps in
  one causal namespace; ref-derived replay-stable `dotSource`
  (`UUID.nameUUIDFromBytes("or-map-tags:${ref.id}:${ref.instanceId}")`) plus `dotCounter`;
  atomic re-put (tombstones + fresh dot in one delta); reset-remove; `Replicable` gossip via
  `deltaInlet`/`applyRemote` with a `novelty` echo terminator; C-10 `originate` re-emission
  with `PendingReBaseline.with(null)`; `catchUpOnLinked` state-as-delta with tombstones;
  `pullServe` since-filtered scoped baseline with `currentFrontier`; `ReBaseline`
  dead-source fencing; `snapshot`/`restore` incl. counter and `dead` set.
- Tests: `kernel/src/test/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/OrMapCellTest.kt`, plus an E1-REPL
  convergence test under `kernel/src/test/.../cell/replication/`.

## The conformance debt that is genuinely open

`doc/spec/CONCORDANCE.md:140-143` and `:207-210`:

    | 24-TMAP-01 | — | gap |
    | 24-TMAP-02 | — | gap |
    | 24-TMAP-03 | — | gap |
    | 24-TMAP-04 | — | gap |
    - Coverage gap: requirement '24-TMAP-0n' ... has no covering scenario

Four shipped normative laws with no executable arbiter. `concord/corpus/24-data-cells/`
already holds 29 scenarios (`24-OP-KEYEDSET-01.yaml` and `24-OP-SET-01.yaml` are the
nearest shape); `concord/corpus/42-replication/` holds `42-REPL-01`, `42-REPL-LATE-01`,
`42-REPL-DEPART-01`, `42-INTEREST-01`. Registration for any new cell goes through
`concord/src/main/kotlin/civictech/concord/driver/kernel/KernelCatalog.kt` +
`KernelAdapters.kt` + `KernelFunctions.kt` — the only files in `concord/` permitted to
import `civictech.cell.*`.

## Seams KE1 attaches to

| Seam | File | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| `MergeablePayload` | `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/MergeablePayload.kt` | one-method `mergeWith`; the class E1.4 restricts embedded values to |
| idempotent exemplar | `kernel/.../cell/data/delta/PnCounterDelta.kt` | composes; the value type BS-1 uses |
| non-idempotent counterexample | `kernel/.../cell/data/delta/CounterDelta.kt` | plain `amount: Long` addition — the Riak embedded-counter anomaly in this repo's own types; `[KE1-04]`'s refusal target |
| merge-class marker + link-time refusal | `kernel/.../cell/data/op/MergeableGroupByCell.kt:36-42` | CP-F2 scan stamps `MergeClass.IDEMPOTENT`, CP-F3 refuses a non-idempotent accumulator at link time — reuse, do not reinvent |
| view shape | `kernel/.../cell/data/view/MapView.kt` | `apply(): Boolean` / `current()` / `snapshot()` / `restore()`; carries the G-23 caveat `TaggedMapView` retires |
| view registry | `kernel/.../cell/observe/Observe.kt:70-110`, `:338-348` | `View<in D, out S>` interface + `set()`/`map()`/`count()` factories and the named-sink builders |
| join family (consume, do not rewrite) | `kernel/.../cell/data/op/{CombineLatestCell,LookupJoinCell,JoinCell,GroupByCell}.kt` | `CombineLatestCell.kt:27` outlet is `Propagate<MapDelta<K,R>>` — `UntagCell` is what lets these stay unmodified |
| atomic retract+add invariant | `kernel/.../cell/data/KeyedSetCell.kt` | the invariant `UntagCell` must preserve on the way out |
| element-shaped siblings | `kernel/.../cell/data/SetCell.kt`, tests `SetConvergenceTest.kt`, `UnionObservedRemoveTest.kt` | every OR-map seam has an element-shaped original; read them beside the dot-shaped form |
| demo host | `demo/tiering/src/main/kotlin/civictech/demo/tiering/{Tiering,TieringApp}.kt` | `Tiering.tierOf`/`fuse`, `TieringApp.build(host): Refs`; the manual re-tier edge becomes the replicated `OrMapCell<String, Tier>` |
| two-JVM template | `demo/shopping/src/test/kotlin/civictech/demo/TwoJvmConvergenceTest.kt`, `CrashRestartConvergenceTest.kt` | the harness E1.6 mirrors (real wire, seeded schedules, final-state equality) |
| simulation controls | `testkit` — `SimWorld`, `SimulationController`, `awaitUntil`, `JvmPeer` | seeded meshes, partition/heal, bounded waits |

## Documented residual KE1 inherits (decision needed, not a defect to improvise on)

`OrMapCell.kt:334-348` states the `ReBaseline` fence is **replica-local**: a dot from a
superseded source held by a peer that never processed a notice stays live there and can
never reach a fenced replica, so those two replicas do not re-converge on that key. The
element-shaped family (`TagState` via `UnionSetCell`) makes the opposite trade and carries
over-retraction instead. The code states neither hole is reachable through shipped wiring
(nothing emits a `TaggedMapDelta` re-baseline; a replica RESTART keeps its ref-derived
`dotSource`). E1.6's crash-restart test is the closest anything has come to that wiring.
Closing it properly needs a fenced-source lattice on the gossip mesh — named in the code as
"96 §E1 follow-on work". KE1's job is to *test whether it stays unreachable* and file if
not, not to build the lattice in-lane.

## Kernel-lane serialization (G-63, single SCC)

Plan §4 fixes KE1 at position 2: after KX (C-13 `LocationRegistry` → registry +
`InstanceIndex` + `DeliveryHold`), before KFX, with KAGG-R immediately after. Consequences:

- KE1 must not run concurrently with another kernel-lane chunk.
- KX is consumed from merged `main`, never recreated locally (AGENTS.md multi-agent run
  discipline) — `OrMapCell`'s pull-baseline and replication paths transit that seam.
- `Aggregator.kt` and `TaggedSetOperator.kt` stay untouched: KAGG-R owns that surface and
  runs next precisely because KE1 has just touched the operator family around it. Residuals
  found there are findings handed forward, not fixes taken in-lane.
- Every lane writes findings to its own `doc/<lane>/findings.md` citing G-ids; nothing edits
  `91-gap-analysis.md` or `CONCORDANCE.md` by hand (plan §6).

title: KHYG — Kernel structural hygiene (behaviour-preserving kernel-lane work)
description:
# KHYG — Kernel structural hygiene

Umbrella epic for behaviour-preserving structural work inside the kernel SCC (G-63).

## Ambition / Why

Three pieces of work surfaced during the milestone-plan epic breakdown are too small to be
epics on their own but share every scheduling property that matters:

- each edits `kernel/` and therefore **takes a kernel-lane slot**, serializing against the
  others and against KE1/KAGG-R/KE3 (G-63 single SCC);
- each is **behaviour-preserving in intent** — restructuring or completing existing
  mechanisms, or making code match an already-decided spec rule, rather than adding
  semantics;
- each carries a **latent correctness finding** that the work either pins as current
  behaviour or fixes outright.

Grouping them gives the kernel-lane queue one admission unit instead of three competing
ones, and gives the findings below a single owner.

## Children

Requirements live in the child features, not here. This epic adds no EARS ids of its own.

1. **KX — C-13 extraction** (`LocationRegistry` → registry + `InstanceIndex` +
   `DeliveryHold`). Pure extraction; 37 requirements exist to pin current behaviour, not
   to add any. Opens the kernel lane per §4 of the milestone plan.
2. **SEC1 — `BoundaryPolicy` denial accounting**. The I-28 seams already landed with
   W4.1/G-54; what is missing is effective enforcement at the bridge and explicit
   accounting on denial.

3. **KFX — C-9 fix + minimal G-59 processed-frontier for `Effectful`**. Making code match a
   decided-but-divergent spec rule is hygiene. Note the audit finding: the processed-frontier
   itself is already landed and `91-gap-analysis.md:18` is stale; the real residuals are
   `FanOutlet`'s `UUID.randomUUID()` sourceId outside any `Stateful.snapshot` (journaled source
   into an `Effectful` sink double-fires on recovery, violating `[24-DUR-04]`) and the
   `timestamp == null` frontier-check skip at `ManagedHost.kt:790` that makes externally-driven
   frames always re-fire. Hard-blocks CON1.

## Findings this epic owns

These were discovered while specifying the children and must not be lost if any child
is rescheduled:

- **Silent ownership drop (live, in `main`).** Every `BoundaryPolicy` denial is a bare
  `return null` at `MediateProxy.kt:42,52-57`, `CompositeCell.kt:205-215` and
  `CompositeCell.kt:229-249`, discharging no `Owned`/`Leased` while the KDoc claims
  "dead-lettered". This violates the system-wide invariant in `AGENTS.md` that no
  suppression path may silently drop an exclusive payload. Owned by SEC1.
- **`C-13` names two different conflicts.** The gap-analysis row is the `LocationRegistry`
  co-location marker; `22-consistency.md:420` and `41-location-transparency.md:15,20,189`
  use `⚠ CONFLICT (C-13)` for the bridged link bypassing `handshake()` (closed by CP-A2).
  Any ticket citing "C-13" is ambiguous until the ids are split. Observed independently by
  the KX and WIR1 analyses. Owned by KX (as a findings note; the id split itself is
  documentation maintenance and is not authorized here).
- **`interests` retention leak.** Never cleared by `unpublish`/`mirrorUnpublish`/
  `unpublishRemotes`, unlike `byLogicalId` and `descriptions`. KX preserves it verbatim —
  clearing would let a re-published ref fall back to `Interest.Total` and widen a shed
  range, contradicting PN-6's admission rule. Filed, not fixed.
- **`install()`-vs-hold asymmetry.** `deliver()` and `replay()` short-circuit on
  `ref in held`; `install()` does not, so a `publish()` during a hold drains the parked
  queue anyway. Pinned as current behaviour by KX `[KX-26]`/BS-10.
- **`FanOutlet` applies `disclosureFilter` twice per emission** (consumer path +
  `notifyObserver`) — a double-consume hazard for `Project` over an `Owned`. Owned by SEC1.

## Scope boundaries

- No new semantics. Anything that changes observable behaviour outside the denial-accounting
  path named in SEC1 belongs to a spec-cited work item, not here.
- Not KE1/KAGG-R/KE3 — those are their own kernel-lane admissions (KAGG-R/KBLK/KRD sit
  under the KENA epic).
- Not documentation maintenance: the C-13 id split and any normative `[43-*]` id minting
  require an explicit documentation-maintenance authorization (see SEC1 feature 6).
- No wire or binary format change.

## Sequencing

KX first (it is the lane opener per §4 and de-conflicts the distribution chunks), then KFX
(§4 position 3, and CON1 is hard-blocked on it), then SEC1. No two may run concurrently —
they share the single kernel-lane slot, and KX and SEC1 both touch
`CompositeCell`/`MediateProxy`-adjacent paths.

SEC1 additionally orders **before** ECO1, which builds its budget seam on the same
`asProtocolFilter` denial path (ECO1 `computenet-66m`, recorded there as a soft edge).

## Exit criteria

- All three children closed against their own acceptance criteria.
- `./gradlew test` green; `./gradlew :concord:check` green with `CONCORDANCE.md`
  regenerating byte-identically (neither child mints a normative id without explicit
  authorization).
- Every finding above is either fixed or recorded in a lane findings file with its
  reasoning — none silently dropped. This includes the two stale-spec observations (the
  `C-13` id collision and `91-gap-analysis.md:18`'s pending-fix row for G-59), which are
  reported, not edited away.
acceptance_criteria: All three children (KX, KFX, SEC1) closed against their own acceptance criteria; ./gradlew test green; :concord:check green with CONCORDANCE.md regenerating byte-identically; every finding in the description either fixed or recorded in a lane findings file with reasoning.

title: ZZ B
ORA1 — Batch-oracle differential tester over the operator algebra
description:
# ORA1 — Batch-oracle differential tester

Milestone-plan row (`computenet-milestone-plan.md` §1, Evidence lanes):

> **ORA1** — Batch-oracle differential tester: random graph + input sequence, naive recompute
> reference, over the existing operator algebra. **Depends on:** — . **Unblocks:** KE1 acceptance;
> BB-TPCH/QRY1 oracle; subsumes per-cell seed tests.

Rank **1** in §5 ("Correctness oracle; three consumer lanes; highest leverage per effort"), with the
explicit ordering decision **ORA1 before BEN1** — "correctness evidence outranks performance
evidence while the E-plan is unbuilt". Zero dependencies: it is buildable today against the
operator algebra as it stands.

---

## 1. Ambition / Why

ComputeNet's central claim is that an *incrementally maintained* dataflow graph produces exactly the
answer a *batch recompute* would produce, under arbitrary interleaving, late subscription, host
migration, replication and crash-restart. Today that claim is defended by roughly two dozen
hand-written per-cell seed tests, each with its own private, ad-hoc reference fold: `OperatorTest`'s
`batch` list, `RelationalGraphsTest`'s left-join recompute, `DataflowSuiteExitTest`'s `batchSums`,
`ExchangeCompositionExitTest`'s `batch(live)`, `AgoraExitTest`'s `BatchReference.solve`,
`GenerativeGraphTest`'s `held.flatten().filter { predicates }`, `InternalConsistencyTest`'s
wave-prefix `Oracle`. Each one re-derives a sliver of the algebra by hand, for one pipeline shape,
and dies with that test file.

That is expensive and, more importantly, **shallow**: the shapes that get tested are the shapes
someone thought to write down. The interesting failures — a retraction crossing a diamond into an
antijoin whose minted tags are then grouped, an unobserved remove arriving before its add across a
fan-in — live in the combinatorial space nobody enumerates by hand.

ORA1 replaces the sliver-per-test pattern with **one reusable differential-testing engine**: a single
declarative *reference model* of the whole operator algebra, a *generator* that synthesizes random
well-typed graphs and input scripts over that algebra, and a *runner* that drives the real kernel and
diffs it against the reference — with shrinking, pinned regression seeds, and a public API so other
lanes can bring their own graph and their own expected answer.

What it unblocks (from the plan's DAG, §2):

- **KE1 acceptance** (`ORA1 -.acceptance.-> KE1`). E1 is the OR-map / tagged-map convergence class
  (E1.1–E1.6, `doc/spec/90-roadmap/96-incremental-engines-plan.md`). §4 admits KE1 as the second
  kernel-lane chunk explicitly with "ORA1 leverage". A new convergence class without a differential
  oracle is a new class of silent wrongness.
- **QRY1** (`ORA1 -.oracle.-> QRY1`). §5 rank 10: "Starts once ORA1 is usable as oracle." A
  Datalog/relational frontend is a *compiler into the operator algebra*; the only tractable way to
  test a compiler is a differential oracle over generated programs.
- **BB-TPCH** (`ORA1 -.oracle.-> BBTPCH`). §1 BB table lists ORA1 as a direct dependency; §3's TPC-H
  row names "ORA1 as cross-check" beside QRY1. RF2 deletions propagating through multi-join chains is
  precisely a generated-retraction property.
- **ORA2** (§1: "Oracle coverage for tagged/keyed family (OR-map, weighted)") is this epic's direct
  successor and consumes its extension seam.
- **Subsumes per-cell seed tests**: existing bespoke folds become either (a) callers of the shared
  diff engine, or (b) pinned regression cases in the corpus. That consolidation is a deliverable, not
  a side effect.

Spec anchors this makes checkable rather than asserted: `[24-OP-*]` in
`doc/spec/20-dataflow-semantics/24-data-cells.md` (the per-operator SHALLs), `[21-PROP-01]` /
`[21-CATCHUP-02]` / `[24-CATCHUP-01]` in `21-propagation.md`, the glitch-freedom and wave-prefix

## 3. How, using ComputeNet

Every type named here exists today; paths are absolute-from-repo-root.

### 3.1 The algebra being modelled

`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/` and `.../data/op/`:

- **Sources**: `SetCell<E>` (OR-set, `Use<SetOps<E>>` inlet with `add`/`remove`),
  `KeyedSetCell<K,E>` (`KeyedSetOps`: `put`/`remove`, re-put ships retract+add in one `SetDelta`),
  `MapCell<K,V>` (`MapOps`, untagged LWW), `OrMapCell<K,V>` (`TaggedMapDelta`, add-wins presence,
  LWW-by-dot value), `CounterCell`, `PnCounterCell`, `ListCell<E>`.
- **Unary set ops**: `FilterCell<E>(predicate)`, `FlatMapSetCell<A,B>(f)` (+ helper `mapSet(f)`),
  `UnionSetCell<E>`, `CountCell<E>` (→ `CounterDelta`), `PresenceCountCell<E>` (→ `MapDelta<E,Int>`),
  `QuorumSetCell<E>(threshold)`.
- **Binary set ops**: `IntersectSetCell<E>`, `JoinSetCell<A,B,K,C>(leftKey, rightKey, combine)`
  (+ `joinSet`, `crossProduct`), `SemiJoinCell<A,B,K>(leftKey, rightKey, negated, emitOnFrontier)`
  (+ `differenceSet`).
- **Map ops**: `JoinCell<K,V,W>` (keyed inner join), `CombineLatestCell<K,V,W,R>(emitOnFrontier,
  combine)` (keyed outer), `LookupJoinCell<K,V,J,D,R>(fk, combine)` (FK/dimension left-outer),
  `CoalescingCombineCell` (wave-aligned scalar sum).
- **Grouping**: `GroupByCell<E,K,A,ACC>(keyFn, aggregator)` → `MapDelta<K,A>`, plus
  `GroupByCell.global(...)`; `MergeableGroupByCell<E,K,A>` (replicable, no retract).
- **Aggregators** (`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/Aggregator.kt`):
  `Aggregator<E,A,ACC>` with `empty`/`insert`/`retract`/`value`, and `Aggregators.count`, `sumOf`,
  `avgOf`, `minOf`, `maxOf`, `topK`, `collectToSet`. **Retraction is first-class** — the reference
  model mirrors each of these as a pure fold over the live multiset.
- **Windowing** (`Windows.kt`): `Windows.tumbling(size): (Long) -> Long`,
  `Windows.sliding(size, slide): (Long) -> List<Long>` — event time is an element attribute and the
  window is part of the group key, so windowing is modelled as key derivation + `FlatMapSetCell`,
  with **no** window-close/eviction semantics (that is KE4, out of scope — see §5).
- **Deltas** (`.../data/delta/`): `SetDelta<E>` (`adds`/`dels` as element → tag sets; observed-remove,
  add-wins), `MapDelta<K,V>` (`puts`/`removals`, untagged, documented arrival-order limit),
  `TaggedMapDelta<K,V>` (per-key dots; `membership()` add-wins, `value()` LWW by
  `DOT_ORDER`), `CounterDelta`, `PnCounterDelta`, `ListDelta<E>`.
- **Sink folds** (`.../data/view/`): `SetView<E>.apply/current`, `MapView<K,V>`, `CountView<K>`,
  `SetHubCell`/`MapHubCell`. These are how the runner reads a terminal's observable state.

### 3.2 Graph construction and driving

`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/graph/GraphDsl.kt`:

```kotlin
fun graph(host: Use<HostManagementApi>, block: GraphBuilder.() -> Unit): GraphSpec
fun <R> graphOf(host: Use<HostManagementApi>, block: GraphBuilder.() -> R): Pair<R, GraphSpec>
class GraphBuilder {
    fun <C : Cell> spawn(name: String, identity: IdentityBinding = FreshLogical,
                         parent: CellHandle? = null, factory: TypedCellFactory<C>): TypedCellHandle<C>
    fun connect(from: CellHandle, outlet: String, to: CellHandle, inlet: String)
    fun <Api> link(out: Subscribe<Api>, inn: Serve<Api>)
}
infix fun CellHandle.linkTo(target: CellHandle)   // "outlet" -> "inlet"
data class GraphSpec(steps: List<GraphStep>) { fun applyTo(host: Use<HostManagementApi>): Map<String, CellRef> }
```

The generator emits a **`GraphSpec`**, not a live object graph. That matters twice: a spec is
`Serializable` and replayable onto a second host verbatim (`GenerativeGraphTest` already does this to
compare two independently-built views), and it is the natural payload for a shrunk counterexample.
Factory lambdas must capture only serializable indices into static tables — `GenerativeGraphTest`'s
`companion object { val PREDICATES }` is the idiom to follow.

Typed lookup for driving inputs: `TypedRef<A>`, `TypedCellHandle.refAs<A>()`,
`ManagedHost.lookupOrThrow(tref)` (`kernel/.../graph/TypedRef.kt`), or `HostedCellProxy.create(...)`.

### 3.3 Determinism and execution

`testkit/src/main/kotlin/civictech/testkit/SimWorld.kt`:

```kotlin
class SimWorld(seed: Long? = null, attention: AttentionPolicy? = null) {
    val controller: SimulationController
    val registry: LocationRegistry
    val host: ManagedHost
    fun runToIdle(budget: Int = 200_000): Int   // throws IllegalStateException on non-quiescence
}
```

`SimulationController(seed)` (`kernel/.../host/SimulationController.kt`) randomizes **across hosts
only**; within a host `(priority, submission)` order is inviolable. `controller.step()` advances one
task, so the runner can interleave op injection with partial drains — the
`repeat(rnd.nextInt(4)) { controller.step() }` idiom from `GenerativeGraphTest`.

`testkit/.../ForEachSeed.kt`: `forEachSeed(seeds: LongRange, block: (Long) -> Unit)` runs **every**
seed and reports failure *density* ("failed on N of M seeds; first: seed=K"). The sweep uses this,
never a fail-fast loop.

`testkit/.../AwaitUntil.kt`: `awaitUntil(what, timeoutMs, condition)` — for any real-time path;
the simulated path uses `runToIdle`.

Dead-letter observation: `ManagedHost.deadLetterOutlet.subscribe(Use.fixed(Propagate<DeadLetter>{...},
PortRef.generate()))`, as in `GenerativeGraphTest`.

### 3.4 Prior art inside the repo that this epic generalizes (read before building)

- `kernel/src/test/kotlin/civictech/cell/verify/GenerativeGraphTest.kt` — the G-31 harness: one fixed
  shape (union → 0..2 filters → count), random op script, late joiner, host migration, `GraphSpec`
  replay onto a second host, five invariants including a `naiveFold` **divergence control**. ORA1 is
  this, generalized to the whole algebra and extracted into a reusable module.
- `kernel/src/test/kotlin/civictech/cell/consistency/InternalConsistencyTest.kt` — the wave-prefix
  `Oracle` class: recompute from scratch, folded forward one transfer wave at a time, producing a
  list of legal `prefixes`; a composite observation must equal *some* prefix and never regress. This
  is the model for `[ORA1-DIFF-06]` and is materially stronger than final-state equality.
- `concord/src/main/kotlin/civictech/concord/generator/ScenarioGenerator.kt` and
  `concord/corpus/24-data-cells/24-GEN-01.yaml` — concord's own generative layer, deliberately
  restricted ("the honesty rule") to the set-algebra core where all four standard properties hold,
  with `window`, `combine-latest`, keyed/counter/list/map sources and semi/lookup-join/partition/
  quorum **excluded**. ORA1's job includes making several of those exclusions unnecessary; §5 and §8
  say which, and how the two harnesses relate.
- `demo/exchange/.../ExchangeCompositionExitTest.kt` — `batch(live)` group-by oracle under
  repartition, migration, peer partition/recover and a late joiner; the epic's model for how far a
  differential test can be pushed.

## 4. Functional requirements (EARS)

EARS style mirrors `doc/spec/`'s `[NN-SLUG-nn]` convention (see
`doc/spec/20-dataflow-semantics/24-data-cells.md`), but ids are **epic-scoped** as `[ORA1-GROUP-nn]`
so they can never collide with normative spec ids. "The oracle" = the `:oracle` module as a whole;
"the model", "the generator", "the runner", "the shrinker" name its components. Where a requirement
makes an existing normative requirement checkable, the spec id is cited in parentheses.

### 4.1 Reference model (`civictech.oracle.model`)

- `[ORA1-MODEL-01]` The model shall compute, from a complete input script alone, the observable
  state of every terminal in a graph, without executing any kernel cell.
- `[ORA1-MODEL-02]` The model shall cover at least: `SetCell`, `KeyedSetCell`, `MapCell`,
  `CounterCell`, `PnCounterCell`, `FilterCell`, `FlatMapSetCell`/`mapSet`, `UnionSetCell`,
  `IntersectSetCell`, `CountCell`, `PresenceCountCell`, `QuorumSetCell`, `GroupByCell` (over all of
  `Aggregators.count`/`sumOf`/`avgOf`/`minOf`/`maxOf`/`topK`/`collectToSet`), `JoinSetCell`,
  `SemiJoinCell` in both polarities, `JoinCell`, `CombineLatestCell`, `LookupJoinCell`
  (cites `[24-OP-FILTER-01]`, `[24-OP-MAP-01]`, `[24-OP-UNION-01]`, `[24-OP-INTERSECT-01]`,
  `[24-OP-COUNT-01]`, `[24-OP-GROUPBY-01]`, `[24-OP-GROUPBY-02]`, `[24-OP-JOIN-01]`,
  `[24-OP-JOINSET-01]`, `[24-OP-JOINSET-02]`, `[24-OP-SEMIJOIN-01]`, `[24-OP-LOOKUP-01]`,
  `[24-OP-FLATMAP-01]`, `[24-OP-FLATMAP-02]`, `[24-AGG-01]`).
- `[ORA1-MODEL-03]` The model shall derive every result from element **membership** and value only,
  never from tag identity, tag counts, wave ids, or any `SetDelta`/`TaggedMapDelta` internals — so
  the oracle is independent of the tag algebra it is checking.
- `[ORA1-MODEL-04]` The model shall implement set membership as observed-remove semantics defined on
  the *script*: an element is live iff it has been added at least once and every such add has been
  covered by a later remove **observed by that writer** (cites `[24-SET-01]`, `[24-SET-03]`).
- `[ORA1-MODEL-05]` If a script removes an element that the removing writer has not observed, then
  the model shall treat the remove as a no-op (cites `[24-SET-03]`).
- `[ORA1-MODEL-06]` The model shall reproduce `Aggregators` retraction semantics exactly, including
  that a group disappears from the result map on the retraction of its last member
  (cites `[24-OP-GROUPBY-02]`).
- `[ORA1-MODEL-07]` Where an operator mints fresh output tags per live combination (`JoinSetCell`,
  `SemiJoinCell`), the model shall compute the output as the set of live combinations, and shall not
  attempt to model minted tag identity (cites `[24-OP-JOINSET-01]`, `[24-OP-SEMIJOIN-02]`).
- `[ORA1-MODEL-08]` Where an operator's kernel semantics are documented as arrival-order dependent
  or non-convergent under concurrency (`MapCell`/`MapDelta` LWW, `ListCell`/`ListDelta`), the model
  shall define the result only for a single-writer FIFO script (cites `[24-OP-MAP-01]`,
  `[24-OP-LIST-01]`).
- `[ORA1-MODEL-09]` If a generated case would place an operator from `[ORA1-MODEL-08]` under more
  than one writer, then the generator shall reject the case at generation time rather than emit an
  instance whose expected value is undefined.
- `[ORA1-MODEL-10]` The model source set shall not reference any type from `civictech.cell.data.op`
  or any concrete data-cell class; it may reference only value, key and delta types. (Verified by an
  import-scanning architecture test — this is the requirement that keeps the oracle an *independent*
  reference rather than a second copy of the implementation.)
- `[ORA1-MODEL-11]` The model shall be a pure function of the script: two evaluations of the same
  script shall produce equal results, and evaluation shall not mutate the script.

### 4.2 Case generator (`civictech.oracle.gen`)

- `[ORA1-GEN-01]` When the generator is invoked with a seed and a `GeneratorConfig`, it shall produce
  a `GeneratedCase` (graph spec + op script + terminal list) that is identical for identical
  (seed, config) across JVM runs and machines.
- `[ORA1-GEN-02]` The generator shall only connect ports whose element shapes are compatible by
  construction, so no generated graph can fail to link.
- `[ORA1-GEN-03]` The generator shall guarantee at least one operator cell between every source and
  every terminal — no generated case is a bare source→view pass-through.
- `[ORA1-GEN-04]` The generator shall accept configuration of at least: pipeline depth range, source
  count, operator vocabulary, element domain size, op-script length, add/remove ratio,
  unobserved-remove ratio, and terminal count.
- `[ORA1-GEN-05]` The generator shall be able to emit non-linear topologies — fan-in, fan-out, and
  diamonds (one source reaching one terminal by two distinct paths) — not only unary chains
  (cites `[24-OP-UNION-01]`, which exists precisely to make diamond re-delivery idempotent).
- `[ORA1-GEN-06]` The generator shall bias the op script so that a configurable fraction of removes
  target elements the removing writer has actually added, and the remainder are deliberately
  unobserved removes.
- `[ORA1-GEN-07]` The generator shall derive the `SimulationController` seed from the case seed, so
  one seed identifies one reproducible (graph, script, schedule) triple.
- `[ORA1-GEN-08]` If the configured vocabulary names a catalog id that has a kernel binding but no
  reference model (or vice versa), then the generator shall fail loudly at configuration time and
  shall not silently drop the operator from the vocabulary.
- `[ORA1-GEN-09]` Where `late-joiner` is enabled, the generator shall emit a second terminal that is
  linked only after a mid-script quiesce barrier (cites `[24-CATCHUP-01]`, `[21-CATCHUP-02]`).
- `[ORA1-GEN-10]` Where multi-host placement is enabled, the generator shall distribute cells across
  more than one `ManagedHost` sharing one `LocationRegistry`, so link and delivery cross a host
  boundary.

### 4.3 Differential runner (`civictech.oracle.run`)

- `[ORA1-DIFF-01]` When a `GeneratedCase` is executed, the runner shall apply the graph spec to the
  host(s), drive the op script, drive the system to quiescence, fold each terminal through the
  matching view (`SetView`/`MapView`/`CountView`), and compare each folded state to the model's
  result for the same script.
- `[ORA1-DIFF-02]` If any terminal's folded state differs from the model's result, then the runner
  shall report a failure naming the seed, the terminal, the rendered graph spec, the op script, the
  expected value, the actual value, and their symmetric difference.
- `[ORA1-DIFF-03]` When a sweep runs a seed range, it shall execute every seed and report failure
  density in the `forEachSeed` form, never abort at the first failure.
- `[ORA1-DIFF-04]` The runner shall assert that no host emitted a dead letter during the run, and
  shall report any dead letter as a distinct failure kind from a value mismatch.
- `[ORA1-DIFF-05]` Where a late joiner is present, the runner shall assert that the late terminal's
  final folded state equals the early terminal's (cites `[24-CATCHUP-01]`).
- `[ORA1-DIFF-06]` While a case is being driven, every intermediate observation of a terminal shall
  equal the model's result for **some prefix of the wave sequence**, and the sequence of observations
  shall be non-regressing for that terminal — i.e. no observation may correspond to a partially
  applied wave (the glitch-freedom property; modelled on
  `kernel/src/test/kotlin/civictech/cell/consistency/InternalConsistencyTest.kt`'s prefix oracle).
- `[ORA1-DIFF-07]` If the system does not reach quiescence within the configured step budget, then
  the runner shall report a non-quiescence failure naming the seed and the step budget, and shall not
  report it as a value mismatch.
- `[ORA1-DIFF-08]` If the model itself throws, then the runner shall report a model-evaluation
  failure distinct from a mismatch, so a broken oracle is never read as a broken kernel.
- `[ORA1-DIFF-09]` The suite shall include at least one **divergence control**: a deliberately wrong
  reference (naive arrival-order fold ignoring tag algebra) that the runner asserts *fails* on at
  least one seed of a fixed range. An oracle that cannot fail is not evidence.
- `[ORA1-DIFF-10]` The suite shall include at least one **mutation check**: a case run against a
  deliberately mutated operator model (e.g. a group-by that omits the last-retraction removal) that
  the runner asserts is detected.
- `[ORA1-DIFF-11]` The runner shall expose a bring-your-own entry point accepting a caller-supplied
  graph builder, script, and reference function, using the same comparison, reporting, and failure
  taxonomy as the generated path.

### 4.4 Shrinking (`civictech.oracle.shrink`)

- `[ORA1-SHRINK-01]` When a case fails, the shrinker shall attempt to reduce it — first by deleting
  op-script steps, then by narrowing the element domain, then by removing operator cells and
  terminals — while preserving the failure.
- `[ORA1-SHRINK-02]` The shrinker shall re-execute every candidate reduction and shall retain a
  reduction only if it still fails with the same failure kind on the same terminal.
- `[ORA1-SHRINK-03]` If the shrink budget (candidate count or wall-clock) is exhausted, then the
  shrinker shall report the smallest failing case found so far and state that shrinking was truncated.
- `[ORA1-SHRINK-04]` When shrinking completes, the shrinker shall emit the counterexample in a form
  that replays deterministically as a standalone test: the seed, the reduced `GraphSpec`, and the
  reduced script, printed as pasteable Kotlin.
- `[ORA1-SHRINK-05]` The shrinker shall never report a "minimal counterexample" that passes on
  re-execution.

### 4.5 Regression corpus (`civictech.oracle.corpus`)

- `[ORA1-REPRO-01]` When a seed is discovered to fail and the underlying defect is fixed, that seed
  shall be pinned in the checked-in regression list and shall run on every build thereafter.
- `[ORA1-REPRO-02]` A pinned seed shall never be removed, replaced, or reordered in order to make the
  suite green (repository invariant: "do not replace a discovered failing seed with a friendlier
  seed", `AGENTS.md`).
- `[ORA1-REPRO-03]` If a pinned case can no longer be constructed because the generator's shape rules
  changed, then the build shall fail with an explicit incompatibility message rather than skipping the
  case.

### 4.6 Extension and consumption (`civictech.oracle.bind`)

- `[ORA1-API-01]` The oracle shall be consumable from another module's test source set through a
  plain `testImplementation(project(":oracle"))` with no further configuration.
- `[ORA1-API-02]` The catalog shall register a kernel cell factory and a reference model together
  under one catalog id; registering one without the other shall fail at registration time
  (this is `[ORA1-GEN-08]`'s enforcement point, and the seam ORA2 widens for the tagged/keyed family).
- `[ORA1-API-03]` Where a consumer registers a new operator, the generator's shape rules shall pick
  it up without edits to the generator itself.
- `[ORA1-API-04]` The oracle shall not depend on `:concord`, `:wire`, `:inspect`, or any `:demo:*`
  module.

### 4.7 Execution budget

- `[ORA1-PERF-01]` The default sweep shall complete within the repository's normal per-module test
  budget on `./gradlew :oracle:test`.
- `[ORA1-PERF-02]` Where a larger sweep is requested via a Gradle property (`-Poracle.seeds=N`), the
  sweep shall honour it without source changes.
- `[ORA1-PERF-03]` While a sweep is running, the runner shall report the current seed and case index
  so a hang is attributable to a specific case.

### 4.8 Honesty ledger

- `[ORA1-HONEST-01]` The correctness of the reference model itself is **not** verifiable by this
  epic. It is defended, not proven, by `[ORA1-MODEL-10]` (independence), `[ORA1-DIFF-09]`
  (divergence control), `[ORA1-DIFF-10]` (mutation check), and agreement with the hand-authored
  concord scenarios in `concord/corpus/24-data-cells/`. This limitation shall be stated in the
  module KDoc rather than hidden.
- `[ORA1-HONEST-02]` If an operator's specified behaviour cannot be checked honestly by a batch
  reference, the operator shall be excluded from the vocabulary with a written reason, and the
  exclusion filed per repository policy (`concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` where it concerns a spec
  requirement) — never modelled approximately so that a scenario passes.

## 5. Behaviour specifications

Each scenario below should become one named test. `covers:` notes mark the ones that belong in the
concord corpus; those are authored under `concord/corpus/` per `concord/schema/*.md` (single-writer,
schema-change-gated) and are **not** part of the `:oracle` module.

**BS-1 — Baseline differential agreement.**
*Given* a generated case with pipeline depth 1–4 over the set-algebra vocabulary and 200 ops;
*when* the script is driven to quiescence; *then* every terminal's folded state equals the reference
model's result, and no dead letter is emitted.
→ `[ORA1-DIFF-01]`, `[ORA1-DIFF-04]`. Test: `OracleSweepTest.baseline sweep agrees with the batch reference on every seed`.

**BS-2 — Unobserved remove is a no-op.**
*Given* two writers into one `SetCell`-fed pipeline; *when* writer B removes an element only writer A
has added, and B has not observed A's add; *then* the element remains live in both the kernel result
and the model.
→ `[ORA1-MODEL-05]`. Concord-worthy: `covers: [24-SET-03]`.

**BS-3 — Re-add after remove resurrects with a fresh tag.**
*Given* an element added, removed, and added again; *when* the pipeline quiesces; *then* the element
is live, and the model — which tracks membership only — agrees without modelling the new tag.
→ `[ORA1-MODEL-03]`, `[ORA1-MODEL-04]`. Concord-worthy: `covers: [24-SET-01]`.

**BS-4 — Diamond delivery is idempotent.**
*Given* a generated diamond where one source reaches one `UnionSetCell` by two paths; *when* the
script runs; *then* the terminal equals the model, and the union forwards no duplicate tag
information.
→ `[ORA1-GEN-05]`. Concord-worthy: `covers: [24-OP-UNION-01]`.

**BS-5 — Antijoin retraction (non-monotone).**
*Given* a `SemiJoinCell(negated = true)` whose right side later gains a matching key; *when* that key
arrives; *then* the previously-emitted left element is retracted downstream, and the model's set
difference agrees.
→ `[ORA1-MODEL-07]`. Concord-worthy: `covers: [24-OP-SEMIJOIN-01, 24-OP-SEMIJOIN-02]`.

**BS-6 — Group disappears on last retraction.**
*Given* a `GroupByCell` with `Aggregators.maxOf`; *when* every member of one group is removed;
*then* the key is absent from the terminal map (not present with a stale or identity value), and the
surviving group keeps its max.
→ `[ORA1-MODEL-06]`. Already in the corpus as `concord/corpus/24-data-cells/24-OP-GROUPBY-02.yaml`;
the oracle must reproduce it generatively.

**BS-7 — Late joiner is indistinguishable.**
*Given* a case with `late-joiner: true`; *when* the second terminal links after a mid-script quiesce
barrier and the script completes; *then* the late terminal's fold equals the early terminal's fold and
equals the model.
→ `[ORA1-GEN-09]`, `[ORA1-DIFF-05]`. Concord-worthy: `covers: [24-CATCHUP-01, 21-CATCHUP-02]`.

**BS-8 — No intermediate observation is a torn wave.**
*Given* a multi-path graph observed after every scheduler step; *when* a source delta fans out and
reconverges; *then* every observation matches the model's result for some wave prefix, and the
observation sequence never regresses for a terminal.
→ `[ORA1-DIFF-06]`. Test: `WavePrefixTest.every intermediate observation matches a wave prefix`.
Cross-check against `InternalConsistencyTest`'s existing prefix oracle.

**BS-9 — Cross-host placement changes nothing observable.**
*Given* the same case generated once with all cells on one host and once distributed across two hosts
sharing a `LocationRegistry`; *when* both run under the same seed; *then* both terminals equal the
model and each other.
→ `[ORA1-GEN-10]`.

**BS-10 — Non-quiescence is reported as itself.**
*Given* a case configured with an artificially small step budget; *when* `runToIdle` exceeds it;
*then* the runner reports a non-quiescence failure naming seed and budget, and does not report a
value mismatch.
→ `[ORA1-DIFF-07]`. Boundary/failure case; assert on the failure *kind*, not the message text alone.

**BS-11 — A broken model is not read as a broken kernel.**
*Given* a registered reference model that throws on a particular element; *when* a case exercising it
runs; *then* the runner reports a model-evaluation failure kind.
→ `[ORA1-DIFF-08]`.

**BS-12 — The divergence control actually diverges.**
*Given* the naive arrival-order fold substituted for the reference; *when* a fixed 60-seed range runs;
*then* at least one seed fails. If none does, the sweep is not discriminating and the test itself
fails.
→ `[ORA1-DIFF-09]`. This mirrors `GenerativeGraphTest`'s existing `naiveFold` control and
`ExchangeCompositionExitTest`'s "epoch-blind repartition forks a region" control.

**BS-13 — A mutated operator is caught.**
*Given* a mutant group-by model that keeps a group after its last retraction; *when* the standard
sweep runs against it; *then* the sweep fails, and the reported terminal is the group-by terminal.
→ `[ORA1-DIFF-10]`. This is the epic's own acceptance evidence: it measures the sweep's power, not
the kernel's correctness.

**BS-14 — Shrinking reduces and preserves.**
*Given* an injected failure reproducible at seed S with a 200-step script; *when* the shrinker runs
to completion; *then* the emitted counterexample is strictly smaller, still fails on re-execution
with the same failure kind and terminal, and prints as replayable Kotlin.
→ `[ORA1-SHRINK-01]`…`[ORA1-SHRINK-05]`.

**BS-15 — Pinned seeds are load-bearing.**
*Given* the checked-in pinned-seed list; *when* the regression test runs; *then* every pinned case is
constructible and passes. *If* a pinned case is no longer constructible, *then* the build fails with
an explicit incompatibility message.
→ `[ORA1-REPRO-01]`, `[ORA1-REPRO-03]`.

**BS-16 — Reproducibility across runs.**
*Given* one seed and config; *when* the case is generated twice in separate JVMs; *then* the graph
specs and scripts are equal.
→ `[ORA1-GEN-01]`.

**BS-17 — Vocabulary/model mismatch fails loudly.**
*Given* a config naming a catalog id with a kernel binding but no model; *when* the sweep is
configured; *then* configuration fails with a message naming the id — the operator is not silently
dropped.
→ `[ORA1-GEN-08]`, `[ORA1-API-02]`.

**BS-18 — Model independence is enforced.**
*Given* the `civictech.oracle.model` source set; *when* the architecture test scans its imports;
*then* it references no `civictech.cell.data.op.*` type and no concrete data-cell class.
→ `[ORA1-MODEL-10]`.

---

## 6. Scope boundaries

Explicitly **not** in ORA1 — each exclusion follows a dependency edge or an ordering decision in the
plan:

- **The tagged/keyed convergence family (OR-map, weighted sets).** That is **ORA2** (§1: "Oracle
  coverage for tagged/keyed family (OR-map, weighted)", depends on `ORA1, KE1 core types`). ORA1
  builds the *extension seam* (`[ORA1-API-02]`, `[ORA1-API-03]`); it does not model `OrMapCell` /
  `TaggedMapDelta` semantics. If `OrMapCell` is cheap to model as it stands, model it — but its
  KE1-era semantics are ORA2's.
- **Any kernel change.** ORA1 is evidence-lane, test-only, and has no dependency on the kernel SCC
  (§2: `ORA1` is a free-standing node). If the sweep finds a defect, ORA1's deliverable is the pinned
  failing seed and a findings entry — the fix is admitted to the kernel lane per §4/§6. Do not fix
  kernel semantics inside this epic beyond what a shrunk counterexample plus a filed issue requires.
- **KE4 windowing/eviction.** `Windows` is modelled as key derivation only. Watermark-driven
  eviction is `KE4` and pulls `BB-NEX`; a batch reference for an evicting window is not definable
  without it.
- **KE5 cycles and fixpoints.** Generated graphs are acyclic. Recursion is `KE5` → `QRY2`/`BB-GRA`.
- **Replication, partition, crash-restart, membership churn.** `CHA1`'s adversarial DST rig owns
  partition/reorder/duplicate/crash-mid-drain/journal-truncation, and `CHA3` owns membership churn.
  ORA1 may run cells across hosts (`[ORA1-GEN-10]`) but does not inject faults. The composition of
  ORA1's generator with CHA1's fault injection is a later, separately-scheduled join.
- **Performance measurement.** `BEN1` owns the `:bench` module, JMH, and slow-test gating. ORA1's
  only performance requirement is `[ORA1-PERF-01]`.
- **Rewriting `:concord`.** Concord is the implementation-neutral executable specification with its
  own single-writer schema gate and its own generative layer (`24-GEN-01`). ORA1 is a
  kernel-coupled differential *tester*, not a second spec. Where ORA1 discovers that an operator
  concord currently excludes is now honestly checkable, the correct move is a separate,
  schema-gated concord change (a `24-GEN-02` widening) — proposed as a follow-up bead, not done here.
  `[ORA1-API-04]` keeps the modules independent in both directions.
- **`QRY1`'s query language.** ORA1 provides the oracle API `QRY1` will call
  (`[ORA1-DIFF-11]`); it does not model relational query syntax.

---

## 7. Suggested feature decomposition

Do not create these as beads from this epic's description — a later planning pass owns that.

1. **`:oracle` module skeleton + operator catalog seam.** `settings.gradle.kts` include,
   `build.gradle.kts`, package layout, `OperatorCatalog.register(id, shape, kernel, model)` with the
   paired-registration failure, the `civictech.oracle.model` import-boundary architecture test.
   Realizes `[ORA1-API-01..04]`, `[ORA1-MODEL-10]`, `[ORA1-GEN-08]`, BS-17, BS-18.
2. **The reference model over the operator algebra.** Membership semantics, all `Aggregators`, the
   binary/keyed/map operator family, the order-dependence exclusions. Realizes
   `[ORA1-MODEL-01..09]`, `[ORA1-MODEL-11]`, BS-2, BS-3, BS-5, BS-6.
3. **Shape-typed case generator.** `GeneratorConfig`, shape rules, `GraphSpec` emission, op-script
   synthesis, late joiner, multi-host placement, determinism. Realizes `[ORA1-GEN-01..10]`, BS-4,
   BS-7, BS-9, BS-16.
4. **Differential runner + failure taxonomy + wave-prefix check.** Driving, folding, comparison,
   the distinct failure kinds, the `forEachSeed` sweep, and the prefix oracle for glitch-freedom.
   Realizes `[ORA1-DIFF-01..08]`, `[ORA1-DIFF-11]`, `[ORA1-PERF-01..03]`, BS-1, BS-8, BS-10, BS-11.
5. **Controls and mutation evidence.** The divergence control, the mutant-operator check, and the
   module KDoc honesty statement. Realizes `[ORA1-DIFF-09]`, `[ORA1-DIFF-10]`, `[ORA1-HONEST-01..02]`,
   BS-12, BS-13.
6. **Shrinking + pinned regression corpus + migration of existing bespoke folds.** The shrinker,
   replayable counterexample emission, `PinnedSeeds`, and converting at least three existing
   hand-rolled batch folds (candidates: `OperatorTest`, `RelationalGraphsTest`,
   `GenerativeGraphTest`) to the shared engine — the "subsumes per-cell seed tests" clause of the
   plan row. Realizes `[ORA1-SHRINK-01..05]`, `[ORA1-REPRO-01..03]`, BS-14, BS-15.

---

## 8. Verification

```bash
./gradlew :oracle:test                                   # the module's own suite: sweep, controls, shrinker, pinned seeds
./gradlew :oracle:test -Poracle.seeds=2000               # extended sweep (nightly / on demand)
./gradlew :oracle:test --tests 'civictech.oracle.run.WavePrefixTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test                                   # migrated call sites must stay green
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.verify.GenerativeGraphTest'
./gradlew :concord:test                                  # unchanged; proves ORA1 did not perturb the spec suite
./gradlew test                                           # repository-wide gate
```

Kinds of test that constitute proof:

- **Differential sweeps** over a seed range with `forEachSeed`, asserting incremental == batch on
  every terminal (BS-1).
- **Discrimination evidence** — the divergence control and the mutant-operator check (BS-12, BS-13).
  These are the tests that make the sweep *evidence* rather than decoration; a green sweep with no
  discrimination test proves nothing.
- **Named behaviour tests** for each of BS-2…BS-11, BS-14…BS-18.
- **An architecture test** on the model's imports (BS-18).
- **Cross-check against the existing corpus**: at least the operators covered by hand-authored
  `concord/corpus/24-data-cells/*.yaml` scenarios must produce the same answers under the oracle's
  model, so a disagreement between the two harnesses is caught at build time rather than in review.

Report exactly which commands ran, the seed ranges used, and any operator excluded from the
vocabulary with its written reason (`[ORA1-HONEST-02]`).

---

## 9. Risks / open questions

1. **The oracle's own correctness is unfalsifiable from inside** (`[ORA1-HONEST-01]`). Mitigations
   are structural (independence, controls, mutation, corpus cross-check), not proofs. This must be
   stated in the KDoc; do not let a later reader mistake the sweep for a proof.
2. **Model drift.** The reference is a second implementation of the algebra; when a kernel operator's
   semantics change, the model must change with it, and nothing forces that. Partial mitigation:
   `[ORA1-GEN-08]`'s paired registration plus the corpus cross-check. **Open question:** should a
   change to `civictech.cell.data.op` fail the build until the model is touched (e.g. a checked-in
   operator inventory the catalog is diffed against)? Decide in feature 1.
3. **Combinatorial blow-up vs. CI budget** (`[ORA1-PERF-01]`). The default sweep must stay fast while
   the extended sweep stays useful. **Open question:** where do extended sweeps run — a Gradle
   property invoked ad hoc, or a scheduled job? BEN1 will face the same question for slow-test
   gating; do not invent a second mechanism if BEN1's is imminent.
4. **Shrinking cost.** Re-executing candidates is expensive at depth. Budget-bounded shrinking
   (`[ORA1-SHRINK-03]`) is the guard; the risk is a shrinker so slow it gets disabled.
5. **Non-determinism leaking in.** `SimulationController` randomizes across hosts only, but hash
   iteration order, `UUID.randomUUID()` in default `CellRef` parameters, and `HashSet` ordering can
   still make a "reproducible" seed irreproducible. Feature 3 must pin every such source; BS-16 is
   the check, and it should run in two JVMs (`setForkEvery` already forks) rather than twice in one.
6. **Overlap with concord's generative layer.** `24-GEN-01` already does a restricted version of this
   over the set-algebra core. The boundary asserted in §6 (concord = implementation-neutral spec;
   oracle = kernel-coupled differential tester) is a decision, not a discovered fact — if a reviewer
   rejects it, the alternative is folding ORA1 into `concord`'s generator, which costs the
   `civictech.cell.*` import boundary and the schema-change gate on every vocabulary widening.
   Settle this in feature 1 before writing the model.
7. **`MapCell`/`ListCell` exclusions** (`[ORA1-MODEL-08]`, `[ORA1-MODEL-09]`) shrink the vocabulary in
   a way that may hide real defects on those paths. The honest position is the exclusion plus a
   single-writer sub-sweep; the dishonest one is a model that guesses an arrival order.
design:
# ORA1 — design decisions and alternatives considered

## D1. A new leaf module `:oracle`, not an extension of `:testkit` or `:concord`

**Decision.** Create `oracle/` as a leaf Gradle module, sources in `src/main` (so consumers reach it
through a plain project dependency, exactly as `testkit/build.gradle.kts` documents), depending on
`:kernel` and `:testkit`, consumed as `testImplementation` by `:kernel` and by demo modules.

**Alternatives.**

- *Put it in `:testkit`.* Rejected: `:testkit` is `api(project(":kernel"))` and is consumed by
  `:kernel` and every demo. Adding a full second implementation of the operator algebra plus a
  generator and a shrinker into the module every test module already pulls in is a large, permanent
  compile-time tax on modules that will never call it. `:testkit` is deliberately five small files
  (`SimWorld`, `AwaitUntil`, `ForEachSeed`, `HttpProbe`, `JvmPeer`); ORA1 is an order of magnitude
  bigger and has its own release cadence (ORA2 widens it).
- *Put it in `:concord`.* Rejected on the repository's own boundary rule (`AGENTS.md`: "Only
  `civictech.concord.driver.kernel` may import `civictech.cell.*`"). ORA1 must build real
  `GraphSpec`s from real cell factories; it is kernel-coupled by construction. Concord is also
  single-writer and schema-change-gated — every vocabulary widening would become a schema change.
  Concord's own generative layer (`ScenarioGenerator`, `24-GEN-01`) stays as it is: the
  implementation-neutral, deliberately restricted sweep. ORA1 is the deep, kernel-coupled one.
  See risk 6 in the description — this boundary is the decision most worth challenging early.
- *Keep it in `kernel/src/test`.* Rejected: `QRY1`, `BB-TPCH` and the demo modules cannot depend on
  another module's test source set without a test-fixtures plugin the repo does not use, and the
  plan's whole point is that three consumer lanes call this.

## D2. The model is an independent second implementation, enforced by an import boundary

**Decision.** `civictech.oracle.model` may reference value, key and delta types but no
`civictech.cell.data.op.*` type and no concrete data-cell class (`[ORA1-MODEL-10]`), verified by an
architecture test that scans imports.

**Rationale.** A differential test whose reference shares code with the implementation under test
detects only crashes. The reference must re-derive results from *membership over the script*, not
from tag algebra (`[ORA1-MODEL-03]`) — that independence is exactly what makes an incremental/batch
mismatch informative about the tag machinery.

**Alternative considered.** Deriving the reference by replaying deltas through the existing
`SetView`/`MapView` folds. Rejected: those folds are the thing being tested; agreement would be
tautological. (They are still used to *read* the kernel side — that is fine, it is the actual
observation path applications use.)

**Cost accepted.** Two implementations drift. Risk 2 in the description; mitigation is paired
registration (`[ORA1-API-02]`) and cross-checking against the hand-authored concord scenarios.

## D3. Generate `GraphSpec`, not live object graphs

**Decision.** The generator emits `civictech.cell.graph.GraphSpec` (a `Serializable` list of
`SpawnStep`/`ConnectStep`), applied via `GraphSpec.applyTo(host.managementInlet)`.

**Rationale.** Three properties fall out for free: (a) the same generated graph can be replayed
verbatim onto a second host to compare two independently built views — the idiom
`GenerativeGraphTest` already uses; (b) a shrunk counterexample is a serializable value that prints
as pasteable Kotlin (`[ORA1-SHRINK-04]`); (c) multi-host placement (`[ORA1-GEN-10]`) is a matter of
which host the spec is applied to, not a different code path.

**Constraint this imposes.** Factory lambdas inside a spec must capture only serializable data.
Follow `GenerativeGraphTest`'s `companion object { val PREDICATES: List<(String) -> Boolean> }`
pattern: static tables, captured by index. Reject any generator design that closes over a random
generator or a live object.

## D4. Shape-typed generation over post-hoc validation

**Decision.** Each catalog entry declares an input/output `ElementShape` rule; the builder only
appends an operator whose input shape it can already satisfy (`[ORA1-GEN-02]`), so no generated graph
can fail to link.

**Rationale.** The alternative — generate freely, then discard invalid graphs — silently biases the
distribution toward whatever happens to type-check and wastes most of the budget at depth. Concord's
`ScenarioGenerator` already reached this conclusion with its `INT_SET` / `PAIR_SET` / `TRIPLE_SET`
regimes; ORA1 generalizes the mechanism rather than the fixed three-regime table.

## D5. Final-state equality is not enough — the prefix oracle is required

**Decision.** `[ORA1-DIFF-06]`: intermediate observations must match the model's result for *some
prefix of the wave sequence*, and must not regress.

**Rationale.** Final-state equality after quiescence cannot see a glitch. The repository already has
the stronger construction —
`kernel/src/test/kotlin/civictech/cell/consistency/InternalConsistencyTest.kt` builds a list of
legal prefixes by folding the reference forward one transfer wave at a time and asserts the composite
observation equals *some* prefix. Building ORA1 without it would be a regression against an existing
test's rigour.

**Cost.** Requires stepping the `SimulationController` and observing between steps, which is slower
and constrains how the runner drains. Applied to a configurable subset of cases, not all of them, if
`[ORA1-PERF-01]` demands it — but never dropped.

## D6. Discrimination tests are first-class deliverables

**Decision.** `[ORA1-DIFF-09]` (divergence control) and `[ORA1-DIFF-10]` (mutation check) are
required, not optional hardening.

**Rationale.** This is the repository's established pattern, not an invention:
`GenerativeGraphTest` asserts its `naiveFold` control *must* diverge on ≥1 of 30 seeds;
`ExchangeCompositionExitTest` asserts an epoch-blind repartition forks a region;
`InternalConsistencyTest` asserts a point-consistent wiring matches *no* prefix;
`CollaborativeAppTest` asserts naive arrival-order folding diverges. A sweep that is green because it
is blind is worse than no sweep — it converts absence of evidence into a false positive signal for
KE1, QRY1 and BB-TPCH.

## D7. Shrinking is in scope; a generator without one is a bug report generator

**Decision.** Budget-bounded shrinking with re-verification (`[ORA1-SHRINK-01..05]`).

**Rationale.** A 200-op random script over a depth-4 graph across two hosts is not a bug report; it
is a haystack. The three downstream consumers (KE1, QRY1, BB-TPCH) will each be handed failures by
this harness, and the value of the handoff is proportional to how small the counterexample is.

**Alternative considered.** Rely on seed-only reproduction and manual reduction. Rejected: it puts
the reduction cost on every consumer, every time, and produces no reusable regression case.

## D8. Pinned seeds, never rotated

**Decision.** `[ORA1-REPRO-01..03]` — discovered failing seeds are checked in and permanent; a pinned
case that can no longer be constructed fails the build loudly rather than being skipped.

**Rationale.** Direct application of the standing repository invariant ("Preserve deterministic
simulation/generative tests. Do not replace a discovered failing seed with a friendlier seed",
`AGENTS.md`). The `[ORA1-REPRO-03]` loud-failure clause is the interesting part: as the generator's
shape rules evolve, the tempting move is to silently skip stale pinned cases, which quietly erases the
regression suite.

## D9. Exclusions are written down, not modelled approximately

**Decision.** `[ORA1-MODEL-08]`/`[ORA1-MODEL-09]` (order-dependent `MapCell`/`ListCell`) and
`[ORA1-HONEST-02]` (anything not honestly checkable) are handled by *exclusion with a written
reason*, never by an approximate model that lets a scenario pass.

**Rationale.** This is the corpus's own honesty rule, applied to a non-corpus artifact — the same
discipline that made `24-GEN-01` exclude `window`, `combine-latest` and the keyed sources rather than
fake them. A requirement that cannot be checked honestly gets filed, not weakened.

## D10. Scope: evidence lane, no kernel edits

**Decision.** ORA1 files findings and pinned seeds; it does not fix kernel semantics.

**Rationale.** Plan §6 (standing hygiene): "Every lane writes findings to its own append-only
`doc/<lane>/findings.md`, citing G-ids, never editing `91-gap-analysis.md` or `CONCORDANCE.md`
directly." Plan §2 makes ORA1 a free-standing node with no kernel-lane dependency; a kernel fix
discovered here is admitted to the serial kernel lane by §4's ordering, not smuggled in through an
evidence-lane branch. Keeping ORA1 kernel-free is also what lets it merge while KX/KE1 are in flight.

MODULE + SEAM: [ORA1-API-01] [ORA1-API-02] [ORA1-API-03] [ORA1-API-04] [ORA1-MODEL-10] [ORA1-GEN-08] — :oracle exists as a leaf module in settings.gradle.kts, consumable by testImplementation(project(':oracle')); paired kernel/model registration is enforced; the model's import boundary is asserted by an architecture test (BS-17, BS-18).

REFERENCE MODEL: [ORA1-MODEL-01] through [ORA1-MODEL-09] and [ORA1-MODEL-11] — the modelled vocabulary of [ORA1-MODEL-02] is covered, membership-only derivation holds, and the order-dependent operators are excluded with a written reason rather than approximated (BS-2, BS-3, BS-5, BS-6).

GENERATOR: [ORA1-GEN-01] through [ORA1-GEN-07], [ORA1-GEN-09], [ORA1-GEN-10] — seed-reproducible across JVMs, shape-consistent, non-trivial depth, diamonds and fan-in emitted, late joiner and multi-host placement supported (BS-4, BS-7, BS-9, BS-16).

RUNNER: [ORA1-DIFF-01] through [ORA1-DIFF-08] and [ORA1-DIFF-11] — incremental equals batch on every terminal and every seed; failure kinds (mismatch / dead letter / non-quiescence / model-evaluation) are distinct and separately asserted; the wave-prefix glitch-freedom check is present and not weakened to final-state equality; the bring-your-own entry point is exercised by at least one caller-supplied case (BS-1, BS-8, BS-10, BS-11).

DISCRIMINATION (blocking — a green sweep without these is not evidence): [ORA1-DIFF-09] [ORA1-DIFF-10] — the naive arrival-order control provably fails on at least one seed of a fixed range, and a deliberately mutated operator model is detected and attributed to the right terminal (BS-12, BS-13).

SHRINKING + REGRESSION: [ORA1-SHRINK-01] through [ORA1-SHRINK-05], [ORA1-REPRO-01] through [ORA1-REPRO-03] — counterexamples shrink, re-verify, and print as replayable Kotlin; pinned seeds run on every build and a non-constructible pinned case fails the build loudly (BS-14, BS-15).

SUBSUMPTION (the plan row's 'subsumes per-cell seed tests' clause): at least three existing hand-rolled batch folds are migrated to the shared engine with :kernel:test still green — candidates OperatorTest, RelationalGraphsTest, GenerativeGraphTest.

BUDGET + HONESTY: [ORA1-PERF-01] through [ORA1-PERF-03], [ORA1-HONEST-01] [ORA1-HONEST-02] — the default sweep fits the normal module test budget, -Poracle.seeds widens it without source edits, and the module KDoc states plainly that the reference model's own correctness is defended (independence, controls, mutation, corpus cross-check) rather than proven.

OUT OF SCOPE, must remain untouched: no kernel semantic changes, no :concord edits, no OR-map/tagged-map modelling (ORA2), no windowing eviction (KE4), no cycles (KE5), no fault injection (CHA1/CHA3), no benchmark harness (BEN1).

title: KX — C-13 extraction: LocationRegistry → registry + InstanceIndex + DeliveryHold
description:
# KX — C-13 extraction: `LocationRegistry` → registry + `InstanceIndex` + `DeliveryHold`

**Lane:** kernel (serial — the single kernel SCC, G-63). **This is an in-place extraction inside
`kernel/`, NOT a new Gradle module.** No `settings.gradle.kts` change, no new build file, no new
`:` project. Everything lands under `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/` and
`kernel/src/test/kotlin/...`.

**Serialization constraint:** only one kernel-lane epic may be in flight at a time. KX is the
first item in the kernel-lane order (`computenet-milestone-plan.md` §4 item 1) and opens the SCC;
KE1, KFX, KAGG-R, KE3, MEM1 queue behind it. Do not start a second kernel-lane epic concurrently.

---

## 1. Ambition / Why

### What C-13 says

`doc/spec/90-roadmap/91-gap-analysis.md`, conflicts table, row **C-13** (verbatim intent):

> `LocationRegistry` (`cell/host/LocationRegistry.kt`) co-locates three off-mandate distribution
> lanes beyond its stated job (where a ref lives + parking): the interest-assignment table
> (`interests`/`setInterest`/`interestOf`, CP-D2/CP-D3), the `byLogicalId` membership index (PN-7
> perf cliff fix), and repartition hold/release (the flip-window buffer, 93 I-19) — an undocumented
> accretion four subsystems (replication, partitioning, attention scatter, promotion) edit blind,
> with no marker recording the scope creep.
>
> Resolution: No behavior change proposed here — each lane is independently correct and documented
> in its own KDoc. **Extraction target (deferred)**: split into `LocationRegistry` (location +
> parking only) + `InstanceIndex` (the `byLogicalId`/interest-assignment membership surface,
> CP-D2/CP-D3) + `DeliveryHold` (the repartition flip-window buffer, 93 I-19) once a second consumer
> needs one lane without the other two.
>
> Where: 30/33, 40/41, 40/42, 20/24.

**⚠ Naming collision to be aware of, and to not act on:** the string `C-13` also appears inside
`doc/spec/20-dataflow-semantics/22-consistency.md:420` and
`doc/spec/40-distribution/41-location-transparency.md:15,20,189`, where it marks a *different*
conflict — the bridged link installed by `WireEdgeLink.bridgeTo`/`bridgeFrom` bypassing
`handshake()`, closed by CP-A2. **That is not this epic.** KX is the gap-analysis-table C-13 (the
`LocationRegistry` co-location marker) only. Do not touch `WireEdgeLink` or the handshake path.
Report the id collision as a finding; do not renumber spec markers (only the periodic integration
pass writes `91-gap-analysis.md`).

### The trigger has fired

C-13's own deferral condition is "once a second consumer needs one lane without the other two".
That condition is now met three times over:

- **MEM1 (G-44 epoch-claim election + failure detection)** needs to add per-logical-id membership
  state and a lock discipline over it. Today that state would have to be bolted onto a class whose
  hot path is a lock-free `ConcurrentHashMap` read plus a per-ref `synchronized(parkQueue)` monitor
  — mixing election state into the delivery fast path's monitor is exactly the mistake the
  extraction prevents.
- **Distribution chunks de-conflict.** `Replication`, `SingleWriterReplication`, `ReplicaQuorum`,
  `PartitionedShardSet` and `ReplicaConvergence` all edit or read `LocationRegistry` today. Any two
  of those chunks running in different waves collide in one 526-line file. After the split they
  touch three files with disjoint mandates.
- **The inspector and the bounded read** consume only the hold lane (`ManagedHost` line ~1368,
  `inspect/.../Cold.kt` line ~138) — a consumer of one lane that has no interest in the other two.

### What the conflation costs today

`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/LocationRegistry.kt` is 526 lines holding, in one class:

| Lane | State | Mandate |
|---|---|---|
| Location + parking (**on-mandate**) | `locations`, `parked`, `descriptions` | spec 33/41: where a ref lives now; park/replay on absence or closed intake |
| Topology (on-mandate, announced registry state) | `topology: TopologyIndex`, `localLinkIds`, `onLink`/`onUnlink`/`onLocalLink`/`onLocalUnlink` | registry-held edge set, mirrored from peers |
| **Membership index (off-mandate)** | `byLogicalId` (L61) | PN-7 perf cliff: `instancesOf` must be O(instances-of-one-id) |
| **Interest assignment (off-mandate)** | `interests` (L79), `setInterest`, `interestOf` | 40/42 §Interest-scoped instance sets, CP-D2/CP-D3 |
| **Flip-window hold (off-mandate)** | `held` (L346), `hold`, `isHeld`, `release` | 20/24 §Partitioned state, 93 I-19 |

Concrete costs, each observable in the current tree:

1. **Blind cross-lane edits.** `install()` mutates the park queue, `locations`, *and* `byLogicalId`
   inside one `synchronized(queue)` block. `deliver()` consults `held` inside the same monitor. A
   change to the membership index therefore lands inside the delivery fast path's critical section
   with no type-level signal that it did.
2. **No independent testability.** There is no way to unit-test the membership index or the
   flip-window buffer without constructing a whole `LocationRegistry` (and, for anything that
   drains, a `ManagedHost`). Every hold test in the tree (`InspectorColdTest`,
   `BoundedReadProvenanceTest`, `PartitionedPullTest`, `BridgedRepartitionTest`,
   `PartitionedShardsAcrossHostsTest`) reaches through the registry to get at a five-line set.
3. **A latent asymmetry nobody can see.** `deliver()` and `replay()` both short-circuit on
   `ref in held`; `install()` does not — a `publish()` during a hold drains the parked queue into the
   new location despite the hold being active. That may well be correct (publish *is* the flip), but
   it is invisible today. Extraction makes it a named, documented boundary of `DeliveryHold`.
4. **A latent retention leak.** `unpublish`, `mirrorUnpublish` and `unpublishRemotes` all call
   `indexRemove(ref)` and `descriptions.remove(ref)` — and none of them removes the `interests`
   entry. The interest table grows monotonically with every ref ever published. **KX must preserve
   this behaviour verbatim** (see §5) because clearing it would let a re-published ref fall back to
   `Interest.Total`, i.e. silently *widen* a shed range, contradicting the PN-6 admission rule
   ("an older epoch cannot widen a shed range back", `InstanceSet` KDoc). Extraction makes the leak
   addressable as its own decision; fixing it here is out of scope.

### What it unblocks

- **MEM1** (G-44 election) — the named beneficiary; gets a membership surface it can lock and extend.
- **KE3, MEM2, PLC3** — everything downstream in the kernel lane inherits a smaller conflict surface.
- **Distribution chunks** (`Replication`, partitioning, `ReplicaQuorum`) — parallel work stops
  colliding in one file.

Cost/benefit per `computenet-milestone-plan.md` §4: *"cheap, spec-blessed, de-conflicts everything."*
§5 rank 2: *"Cheap, decided, buys concurrency."*

---

## 2. What we build

Three types in `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/`. All are kernel-internal collaborators;
none is serialized, none crosses the wire, none appears in a descriptor.

### 2.1 `LocationRegistry` (existing file, reduced)

`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/LocationRegistry.kt`

**Keeps** (its stated mandate — spec 33/41: where a ref lives, plus parking):

- `sealed interface Location`, `Local(host)`, `Remote(sink, peer)`
- `locations`, `parked`, `descriptions`
- `deliver`, `send`, `replay`, `install`, `publish` (both overloads), `unpublish`,
  `mirrorUnpublish`, `unpublishRemotes`
- `locate`, `location`, `localRefs`, `remoteRefs`, `describe`, `parkedFor`
- The publish/unpublish hook set (`onLocalPublish`, `onPublish`, `onLocalUnpublish`, `onUnpublish`)
- The topology surface (`topology: TopologyIndex`, `localLinkIds`, `link`, `unlink`, `mirrorLink`,
  `mirrorUnlink`, `localLinks`, `isLocalLink`, `swapSet`, `wouldCloseCycle`, `all`,
  `onLocalTopology`, `onTopology`) — **topology stays.** C-13 names exactly three off-mandate lanes
  and topology is not one of them; it is announced registry state (T21). Do not opportunistically
  extract it.

**Loses**: `byLogicalId`/`indexAdd`/`indexRemove`/`instancesOf`/`replicasOf`, `interests`/
`setInterest`/`interestOf`, `held`/`hold`/`isHeld`/`release` — as owned state. See §2.4 for the
delegation policy.

### 2.2 `InstanceIndex` (new file)

`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/InstanceIndex.kt`

Owns the **membership surface** of one logical id (CP-D2/CP-D3, PN-7, 40/42 §Interest-scoped
instance sets):

- `byLogicalId: ConcurrentHashMap<UUID, MutableSet<CellRef>>`
- `add(ref)` / `remove(ref)` — the lifecycle hooks the registry drives
- `instancesOf(logicalId): Set<CellRef>` — O(instances-of-one-id), never a scan of `locations`
- `replicasOf(logicalId): Set<CellRef>` — the spec-42 alias, unchanged
- `interests: ConcurrentHashMap<CellRef, Interest>`, `setInterest(ref, interest)`,
  `interestOf(ref): Interest` (unset ⇒ `Interest.Total`)

**Boundary:** knows nothing about `ManagedHost`, `InvocationSink`, park queues, or delivery. It must
be constructible and fully unit-testable standing alone (`InstanceIndex()` with no arguments).

**Deliberately NOT here:** `InstanceSet`
(`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/replication/InstanceSet.kt`) is the *lattice model* of the
interest-assignment table — a `Replicable` max-register keyed by `(interest, epoch)`, the oracle the
substrate tests check against, explicitly "not a struct read on the live path today" (its own KDoc).
`InstanceIndex` is the **live** registry-side table. **Do not merge them, do not make one delegate
to the other, and do not reconcile their two `interestOf` methods.** That reconciliation is PN-6 /
leaderless-R1 work and is out of scope (§4).

### 2.3 `DeliveryHold` (new file)

`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/DeliveryHold.kt`

Owns the **repartition flip-window buffer** (20/24 §Partitioned state "park the flip window",
93 I-19, CP-D4):

- `held: ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet<CellRef>()`
- `hold(ref)`, `isHeld(ref): Boolean`, `release(ref)`
- Per-ref granularity is the funnel rule (93 I-19): a held key range confines its parking to itself;
  every other range flows unblocked.

`release` must drain what the hold parked. Two shapes are acceptable; pick one and document it:

- **(a) callback-constructed:** `DeliveryHold(private val onRelease: (CellRef) -> Unit)`; the
  registry passes `{ ref -> locations[ref]?.let { replay(ref, it) } }`. `DeliveryHold` then stands
  alone in tests with a recording lambda.
- **(b) split verb:** `DeliveryHold.release(ref)` clears the flag and returns `Boolean`; the
  registry's own `release(ref)` calls it and then drives the drain.

Shape (a) is preferred: it keeps the "release drains, always" contract inside one type.
Whichever is chosen, the reuse property in the current KDoc is normative — **the hold reuses the
ordinary park/replay path, it is not a second buffer.**

### 2.4 Wiring and the delegation policy

`LocationRegistry` composes both: `val instances = InstanceIndex()` and
`private val holds = DeliveryHold { ref -> locations[ref]?.let { replay(ref, it) } }`, exposed as
needed.

**Ordering is load-bearing and must be preserved exactly.** Specifically:

- `install()` today does, inside `synchronized(queue)`: `drainWhile(send)` → `locations[ref] = …` →
  `indexAdd(ref)` → conditional `onIntakeAvailable`. The `instances.add(ref)` call must stay in that
  position, inside that monitor. Do not move it before the drain and do not move it outside the lock.
- `deliver()` reads the hold **twice**: once on the lock-free fast path
  (`invocation.cellRef !in held && send(...)`) and once re-checked inside `synchronized(queue)`.
  Both reads must survive as `holds.isHeld(...)` in the same two positions.
- `replay()` returns early when held, before taking the queue. Preserve.
- `unpublish`/`mirrorUnpublish` call `indexRemove` **before** firing listeners;
  `unpublishRemotes` calls it *inside* the `removeIf` scan and fires listeners only after the whole
  batch has left `locations` (the re-entrancy guard documented at L497-513). Preserve both.
- Interest entries are **not** removed on any unpublish path today. Preserve (see §5, RISK-3).

**Delegation:** keep `LocationRegistry.instancesOf/replicasOf/setInterest/interestOf/hold/isHeld/
release` as one-line delegates so the ~50 out-of-kernel call sites (inspector tests, `demo/exchange`
tests, `SimWorld`-based tests) do not churn. Migrate **kernel main-source** call sites to the new
surfaces. Whether the delegates are eventually deleted is an explicit open question (§5, OQ-1) —
resolve it inside the epic, do not leave both answers half-applied.

---

## 3. How, using ComputeNet — the real call graph today

Read these before changing anything. Line numbers are as of this epic's writing; re-locate by symbol.
