---

## 4. Scope boundaries

**In scope:** moving three lanes of state and their methods out of `LocationRegistry` into two new
kernel-internal types in the same package, rewiring kernel main-source call sites, preserving every
observable behaviour, and adding focused tests for the newly standalone types.

**Explicitly NOT in scope:**

- **MEM1 / G-44** — no epoch-claim election, no failure detector, no lease, no leader state. KX
  *prepares* the surface; it adds none of it.
- **KE3** — no watermark substrate, no causal stability, no tag/tombstone reclamation.
- **Placement (G-24 / G-61 / PLC1-3)** — no placement policy, no cost model, no spawn redirection.
- **The bridged-handshake C-13** in spec 20/22 and 40/41 (closed by CP-A2) — a different conflict
  that happens to share the id. Do not touch `WireEdgeLink`, `handshake()`, or link policies.
- **`InstanceSet` reconciliation (PN-6, leaderless R1)** — do not merge the lattice model with the
  live index.
- **The `interests` retention leak** — preserve it verbatim; file it, do not fix it (RISK-3/OQ-2).
- **The `install()`-ignores-`held` asymmetry** — preserve it verbatim; document it as a
  `DeliveryHold` boundary and file it (OQ-3).
- **Topology extraction** — `TopologyIndex`, `localLinkIds` and the topology hooks stay on
  `LocationRegistry`.
- **Any behaviour change at all.** If a test has to be edited for anything other than a mechanical
  symbol rename or import, stop and report it — that is a behaviour change, not an extraction.
- **Doc/spec edits.** Do not remove or amend C-13 in `doc/spec/90-roadmap/91-gap-analysis.md`; per
  `computenet-milestone-plan.md` §6, a periodic single-agent integration pass is the only writer of
  the gap table and the concordance matrix. Write lane findings instead. KDoc inside `kernel/` is
  code, not a plan document — update it freely, and it must be updated.
- **New Gradle modules.** None.

---

## 5. Functional requirements (EARS)

Ids are epic-scoped (`[KX-nn]`) and deliberately do not collide with normative spec ids
(`[NN-SLUG-nn]`, e.g. `[41-LOC-01]`, `[42-INT-01]`, `[24-PART-04]`, `[33-MOVE-01]`). Where a
requirement makes an existing normative id true, the spec id is cited alongside. Pattern in
parentheses: Ubiquitous / Event-driven / State-driven / Unwanted / Optional-feature / Complex.

### Structural — the extraction itself

`[KX-01]` The kernel SHALL provide a class `civictech.cell.host.InstanceIndex` in
`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/InstanceIndex.kt` that owns the instances-by-logical-id
membership table and the per-instance interest-assignment table (Ubiquitous). *(C-13, CP-D2/CP-D3,
PN-7, cites `[42-INT-01]`.)*

`[KX-02]` The kernel SHALL provide a class `civictech.cell.host.DeliveryHold` in
`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/DeliveryHold.kt` that owns the repartition flip-window
hold set (Ubiquitous). *(C-13, 93 I-19, cites `[24-PART-04]`.)*

`[KX-03]` `LocationRegistry` SHALL declare no field whose value is the interest-assignment table,
the by-logical-id membership index, or the flip-window hold set (Ubiquitous). *(Checkable: a test
asserting `LocationRegistry::class.java.declaredFields` contains no field of the removed names, and
that any surviving `InstanceIndex`/`DeliveryHold` field is of the extracted type.)*

`[KX-04]` `InstanceIndex` SHALL be constructible with no arguments and SHALL depend on no
`ManagedHost`, `InvocationSink`, `ParkQueue`, or `LocationRegistry` type (Ubiquitous). *(Checkable:
it is unit-tested with no registry present, and by an import check on the file.)*

`[KX-05]` `DeliveryHold` SHALL be constructible and exercisable in a test with a recording drain
callback and no `LocationRegistry` present (Ubiquitous).

`[KX-06]` The extraction SHALL add no new Gradle module, SHALL not modify `settings.gradle.kts`, and
SHALL not add a dependency edge between existing modules (Ubiquitous).

### Membership index behaviour

`[KX-07]` When a ref is published — local (`publish(ref, host, cell?)`) or remote
(`publish(ref, sink, peer?)`) — the registry SHALL record the ref in the `InstanceIndex` inside the
same per-ref park-queue monitor in which it assigns `locations[ref]`, and after the park drain
attempt (Event-driven). *(Preserves the `install()` order pinned by `InstallDrainSafetyTest` and
`RelocationTest`.)*

`[KX-08]` When any `onPublish` or `onLocalPublish` listener is invoked for a ref, `instancesOf` on
that ref's logical id SHALL already report that ref (Event-driven). *(This is the ordering
`Replication.maybeLink` depends on: it reads `replicasOf(cell.ref.id)` from inside the publish hook.)*

`[KX-09]` When a ref is removed by `unpublish`, `mirrorUnpublish`, or `unpublishRemotes`, the
`InstanceIndex` SHALL no longer report it in `instancesOf`/`replicasOf` before any `onUnpublish` or
`onLocalUnpublish` listener is invoked for that ref (Event-driven). *(Cites `[42-REPL-06]`-class
eviction behaviour; pinned by `LocationRegistryHooksTest`.)*

`[KX-10]` `instancesOf(logicalId)` SHALL be served from the by-logical-id table alone and SHALL NOT
read or scan the `locations` map (Ubiquitous). *(PN-7 perf cliff. Honest check: `InstanceIndex` is
unit-testable with **no** `LocationRegistry` and therefore no `locations` map in existence — a
scan-based implementation cannot pass. A wall-clock complexity assertion would be flaky and is
deliberately not required.)*

`[KX-11]` `replicasOf(logicalId)` SHALL return exactly what `instancesOf(logicalId)` returns
(Ubiquitous). *(Spec 42's alias; unchanged.)*

`[KX-12]` `instancesOf` SHALL return a snapshot copy such that a caller iterating the result while a
concurrent publish or unpublish runs SHALL NOT observe a `ConcurrentModificationException`
(Ubiquitous).

`[KX-13]` If a logical id's last instance is removed, then the `InstanceIndex` SHALL drop the

## 6. Behaviour specifications (Given/When/Then)

Each scenario is specific enough to become one named test. Suggested homes are
`kernel/src/test/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/`. Unless stated, these are **JVM unit/integration
tests, not concord scenarios** — see §6.11.

**BS-1 — membership visible to the publish hook** *(`[KX-07]`, `[KX-08]`)*
Given a registry with an `onPublish` listener that records `instancesOf(ref.id)` at the moment it
fires, when a local ref is published, then the recorded set contains that ref.
*(This is exactly what `Replication.maybeLink` does at `Replication.kt:205`; if it regresses, gossip
links stop forming and `demo/exchange` fails downstream — catch it here.)*

**BS-2 — membership gone before the unpublish hook** *(`[KX-09]`)*
Given two refs of one logical id published, and an `onUnpublish` listener recording
`replicasOf(logicalId)`, when one is unpublished, then the recorded set contains only the survivor.

**BS-3 — last instance drops the logical-id entry** *(`[KX-13]`)*
Given one ref published under logical id L, when it is unpublished, then `instancesOf(L)` is empty
**and** the index holds no entry for L. *(Assert via an `InstanceIndex`-level accessor or size probe
added for the test — a standalone `InstanceIndex` makes this checkable without reflection.)*

**BS-4 — re-publish is idempotent in the index** *(`[KX-14]`)*
Given a ref published to host A, when it is published again to host B without an intervening
unpublish (the `resumeHost` path), then `instancesOf` reports it exactly once and `locate` returns B.

**BS-5 — interest default and assignment** *(`[KX-15]`)*
Given a fresh `InstanceIndex`, when `interestOf(ref)` is called for a ref never assigned, then it
returns `Interest.Total`; and when `setInterest(ref, partial)` then `interestOf(ref)` returns
`partial`. *(Standalone `InstanceIndex` unit test — no registry, no host: this is the `[KX-04]`
proof.)*

**BS-6 — interest survives unpublish (pinned, not endorsed)** *(`[KX-17]`)*
Given a ref with a narrowed interest, when it is unpublished and republished, then `interestOf` still
returns the narrowed interest, **not** `Interest.Total`. *(The test's name and KDoc must say this
pins current behaviour deliberately, cite PN-6's no-widening rule, and point at OQ-2.)*

**BS-7 — hold parks, release drains in order** *(`[KX-19]`, `[KX-22]`)*
Given a published local ref with a collecting cell, when `hold(ref)` then three invocations are
delivered, then the host has received none and `parkedFor(ref)` lists all three in arrival order;
and when `release(ref)` then the cell receives exactly those three, in that order, exactly once.

**BS-8 — the funnel rule** *(`[KX-21]`)*
Given two refs published to the same host, when one is held and both receive invocations, then the
unheld ref's invocation is delivered immediately while the held ref's is parked.

**BS-9 — held ref does not drain on an intake wake-up** *(`[KX-20]`)*
Given a held ref whose host intake was saturated and then crosses low-water (firing
`onIntakeAvailable`), when the wake-up drives `replay`, then nothing drains until `release`.
*(Build on `SaturationTest`'s existing saturation harness.)*

**BS-10 — publish during a hold drains (the documented asymmetry)** *(`[KX-26]`)*
Given a held ref with parked invocations, when `publish(ref, newHost)` runs while the hold is still
active, then the parked batch drains into `newHost` — the hold does not survive an install.
*(Name the test for the asymmetry, e.g. `install drains despite an active hold (pinned, see OQ-3)`.)*

**BS-11 — refused drain retains the remainder** *(`[KX-29]`)*
Given a park batch of N invocations and a target host whose intake refuses at item k, when `install`
drains, then items k..N remain parked in order, nothing is dead-lettered, and no `Owned`/`Leased`
payload is dropped. *(This is `InstallDrainSafetyTest`'s existing property — it must pass unmodified;
add an `Owned`-carrying variant only if one does not already exist.)*

**BS-12 — concurrent relocation stays exactly-once** *(`[KX-28]`, cites `[33-MOVE-01]`)*
Given real threads delivering while a ref relocates, when the relocation completes, then every
invocation is delivered exactly once in per-host order. *(`RelocationTest`'s
`concurrent relocation is exactly-once under real threads`, unmodified. **This is the canary for a
botched extraction** — if the `instances.add` call is moved out of the `synchronized(queue)` block
or the `locations` assignment is moved before the drain, this test fails.)*

**BS-13 — peer disconnect is a batch, and re-entrant** *(`[KX-30]`)*
Given several remote refs announced through one sink and an `onUnpublish` listener that re-enters
`unpublishRemotes(sameSink)`, when the transport drops the sink, then the re-entrant call finds

`instancesOf` at the time the first listener runs, and each ref is notified exactly once.
*(`LocationRegistryHooksTest` covers the batching today; extend it to assert the index is drained in
the same batch.)*

**BS-14 — throwing listener does not break the publish** *(`[KX-31]`)*
Given an `onPublish` listener that throws, when a ref is published, then `locate` returns the host,
`instancesOf` reports the ref, and the second listener still fires.

**BS-15 — bounded read answers MIGRATING while held** *(`[KX-23]`)*
Given a host with a registry and a published `BoundedStateful` cell, when the ref is held and a
bounded state read is issued, then the answer is `unavailable(MIGRATING)`; and when released, a

**BS-16 — registry-less host** *(`[KX-32]`)*
Given `ManagedHost(registry = null)`, when a bounded read is issued and when a cell is spawned and
despawned, then no NPE occurs and behaviour matches the current tree.

**BS-17 — inspector HELD classification** *(`[KX-25]`, `[KX-34]`)*

## 9. Risks / open questions

**RISK-1 — Concurrency / happens-before is the whole game.** The extraction moves state that is read
and written inside a per-ref `synchronized(parkQueue)` monitor and on a lock-free fast path. Three
orderings are load-bearing and each has a test that catches its violation: `install`'s
drain→assign→index sequence (`InstallDrainSafetyTest`, `RelocationTest`), `deliver`'s double hold
check (BS-7/BS-9), and `unpublishRemotes`' drain-then-notify batching (`LocationRegistryHooksTest`).
*Mitigation:* move state, never move a call; keep every call in the exact lexical position it holds
today, then verify by diffing the method bodies line-for-line.

**RISK-2 — Binary / wire compatibility.** Assessed **low**. None of the three lanes is serialized:
`LocationRegistry`, `InstanceIndex` and `DeliveryHold` are process-local; the only serialized
neighbour is `Interest` (via `Assignment`/`AssignmentDelta` in
`cell/replication/InstanceSet.kt`, `@Polymorphic` on the wire) and KX does not touch its
encoding. No `WireFrame` field, no VERSION bump (`[KX-33]`). *Watch:* the peering path
(`cell/wire/Peering.kt`, `RegistryMirrorCell`) calls registry methods by name — a rename there is a
source change, not a wire change, but it must be swept completely.

**RISK-3 — The `interests` retention leak.** Real and preserved on purpose (`[KX-17]`, BS-6). A
reviewer will be tempted to "fix" it during the move. It must not be fixed here: clearing on
unpublish would let a re-published ref widen a shed range back to `Interest.Total`, contradicting
PN-6's admission rule.

**RISK-4 — Out-of-kernel call-site churn.** `inspect` tests, `demo/exchange`'s
`ExchangeCompositionExitTest` (lines ~394, ~490, ~498, ~517) and `SimWorld`-based tests all call the
registry's delegating methods. Keeping the delegates (OQ-1) holds the churn to zero; deleting them
makes the boundary real but touches several modules. Decide once, apply uniformly.

**RISK-5 — Kernel-lane serialization.** KX must be the only kernel-lane epic in flight. Landing it
while another kernel-lane epic edits `cell/host/` or `cell/replication/` produces exactly the merge
conflict KX exists to prevent.

**RISK-6 — `:kernel:compileKotlin` depends on `:gen:test`.** A generator regression surfaces as a
kernel compile failure. KX should not touch `gen/` at all; if `:gen:test` fails, the cause is almost
certainly unrelated — report it rather than working around it.

**OQ-1 — Keep or delete the `LocationRegistry` delegates?** Keeping them is the smallest coherent
change and costs one line each; deleting them makes the new boundary load-bearing but churns
`inspect`, `demo/exchange` and a dozen kernel tests. *Recommendation:* keep them for the extraction,
marked in KDoc as compatibility delegation, and migrate kernel main-source call sites off them.
Decide explicitly in F4; do not leave the tree half-migrated.

**OQ-2 — Should interest entries be cleared on unpublish, and under what epoch rule?** Not decided,
not in scope. The honest answer probably involves PN-6 epochs (an entry may be dropped only when no
future assignment could be older than what it replaces). File as a follow-up bead against the
distribution lane.

**OQ-3 — Should `install()` respect an active hold?** Today it does not; `deliver` and `replay` do.
Preserved verbatim by `[KX-26]`/BS-10. Whether the hold should survive an install is a real semantic
question for 93 I-19 / `[24-PART-04]`; file it, do not answer it here.

**OQ-4 — The C-13 id collision.** Two different conflicts carry the id `C-13`: the gap-analysis
`LocationRegistry` co-location row (this epic) and the in-body ⚠ CONFLICT in
`22-consistency.md`/`41-location-transparency.md` about the bridged link bypassing `handshake()`
(closed by CP-A2). KX must not touch the latter. Renumbering is a spec-editing decision for the
periodic integration pass; report it as a finding.

# KX — design notes

## Target shape (all in `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/`)

```
LocationRegistry.kt        (existing, reduced ~526 → ~400 lines)
  locations: ConcurrentHashMap<CellRef, Location>
  parked:    ConcurrentHashMap<CellRef, ParkQueue<HostedPortInvocation>>
  descriptions: ConcurrentHashMap<CellRef, WeakReference<Class<out Cell>>>
  topology: TopologyIndex + localLinkIds + topology hooks      <-- STAYS
  publish/unpublish/mirror*/deliver/send/replay/install         <-- STAYS
  val instances = InstanceIndex()                               <-- composed
  private val holds = DeliveryHold { ref -> locations[ref]?.let { replay(ref, it) } }

InstanceIndex.kt           (new)
  byLogicalId: ConcurrentHashMap<UUID, MutableSet<CellRef>>
  interests:   ConcurrentHashMap<CellRef, Interest>
  add(ref) / remove(ref)
  instancesOf(logicalId) / replicasOf(logicalId)
  setInterest(ref, interest) / interestOf(ref)   // unset => Interest.Total
  // imports: CellRef, Interest, ConcurrentHashMap, UUID.  Nothing else.

DeliveryHold.kt            (new)
  class DeliveryHold(private val onRelease: (CellRef) -> Unit)
  held: MutableSet<CellRef> (ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet)
  hold(ref) / isHeld(ref) / release(ref)   // release clears then calls onRelease
```

## Call positions that must not move (diff the method bodies line-for-line)

`install(ref, location)`:
```
synchronized(queue) {
    queue.drainWhile { send(location, it) }   // 1. drain FIRST (T05 / RelocationTest)
    locations[ref] = location                 // 2. then assign
    instances.add(ref)                        // 3. then index  <-- was indexAdd(ref)
    if (!queue.isEmpty()) (location as? Local)?.host?.onIntakeAvailable { replay(ref, location) }
}
```

`deliver(invocation)` — the hold is read TWICE, once lock-free and once under the monitor:
```
if (!holds.isHeld(ref) && send(locations[ref], invocation)) return
… synchronized(queue) { if (!holds.isHeld(ref) && send(...)) return; queue.park(...); … }
```

`replay(ref, expected)` — early return before touching the queue:
```
if (holds.isHeld(ref)) return
```

`unpublish` / `mirrorUnpublish` — index removal BEFORE listeners fire.
`unpublishRemotes(via)` — index removal inside the `removeIf` scan; listeners only after the whole
batch has left `locations` (re-entrancy guard, WsTransport calls this from inside a propagate).

## Why topology stays

C-13 names three off-mandate lanes. Topology (`TopologyIndex`, `localLinkIds`, `onLink`/`onUnlink`,
`mirrorLink`/`mirrorUnlink`, `swapSet`, `wouldCloseCycle`) is announced registry state (T21), on
mandate, and not named. Extracting it is scope creep and would collide with distribution chunks.

## Why `InstanceSet` is not touched

`cell/replication/InstanceSet.kt` is the PN-6 **lattice model** of the assignment table — a
`Replicable` max-register `(interest, epoch)` gossiped over the mesh, explicitly "not a struct read
on the live path today" per its own KDoc. `InstanceIndex` is the live registry table. Two
`interestOf` methods coexist by design until PN-6 / leaderless R1. Do not merge.

## Preserved anomalies (pin with named tests, do NOT fix)

1. `interests` is never cleared on any unpublish path — unbounded growth. Clearing it would let a
   re-published ref widen a shed range back to `Interest.Total`, breaking PN-6's admission rule.
2. `install()` drains despite an active hold; `deliver()`/`replay()` both honour it. The asymmetry is
   invisible today; extraction makes it a named `DeliveryHold` boundary.

## Not this C-13

`⚠ CONFLICT (C-13)` in `22-consistency.md:420` and `41-location-transparency.md:15,20,189` is a
DIFFERENT conflict — bridged links bypassing `handshake()`, closed by CP-A2. Do not touch
`WireEdgeLink`, `handshake()`, or link policies.

## Lane discipline

Kernel lane, serial (G-63 SCC). In-place extraction inside `kernel/` — no new Gradle module, no
`settings.gradle.kts` change. Only one kernel-lane epic in flight at a time; KX opens the lane
(milestone plan §4 item 1, §5 rank 2). Do not edit `doc/spec/90-roadmap/91-gap-analysis.md`'s C-13
row — the periodic integration pass owns the gap table (milestone plan §6); write lane findings
instead.

title: BEN1 — :bench module: JMH harness and first measurements
description:
# BEN1 — `:bench` module: JMH harness and first measurements

Lane: evidence (`lane:evidence`). Priority P1. Source: `computenet-milestone-plan.md`
§1 (evidence-lane row BEN1), §2 (DAG), §3 (kernel-enablement matrix — `:bench` is
named as the home for benchmark generator sources and reference-answer harnesses),
§5 rank 3.

Depends on: nothing. Unblocks: BEN2 (macro sweeps), PLC1 (cost model inputs),
G-21 phase 3 (pooling trigger), and every BB-* suite (`:bench` is their host module).

---

## 1. Ambition / Why

**The numbers are the product.** This epic does not make the runtime faster and
must not try to. It builds the instrument that turns three trigger-gated
deferrals from "unmeasured, therefore unbuildable" into decidable, and gives
every future measurement gate a permanent, cheap home.

Three deferrals in `doc/spec/90-roadmap/` are explicitly gated on profiling that
does not exist:

- **G-21 phase 3 — lease pooling.** `94-implementation-plan.md:312` records the
  deferral verbatim: *"lease pooling; trigger: profiling shows allocation
  pressure (20/23 §Implementation)."* `91-gap-analysis.md:55` repeats it: phases
  1+2 landed, *"phase 3 pooling awaits profiling."* Nobody can fire or retire
  that trigger today because the repo has no allocation measurement.
- **G-43 — re-baseline cost under wide fan-out.** `91-gap-analysis.md:83` asks
  to *"bound the push-authoritative re-baseline (diff-against-last-acked /
  delta-since-generation)"*. "Bound" is a cost claim. BEN1 supplies the fan-out
  scaling curve that BEN2 then re-baselines against.
- **PLC1 — mesh simulator + cost model.** §5's standing rule is *"no simulating
  against fictional costs"*: PLC1 is gated on BEN2, and BEN2 is gated on BEN1's
  harness.

**The V1C-BENCH precedent this epic deliberately reverses.**
`doc/spec/90-roadmap/98-inspector-v4-plan/tickets/V1C-BENCH.md` — the wave-7
measurement ticket whose GO recommendation authorised the whole bounded-read
chain — was forced to write its harness into a document appendix and delete it
from the tree. Its "What NOT to do" says so explicitly:

> **Do not check in a benchmark test.** This repository has no JMH, no benchmark
> source set, and no tag-gating convention for slow tests (verified: zero matches
> for `jmh`/`Benchmark` under `kernel`, `demo`, `testkit`, `inspect`). Adding
> that infrastructure for a one-shot measurement is not this ticket's job, and a
> slow test in `./gradlew test` is a permanent tax.

That reasoning was correct *for a one-shot*. It is wrong for a programme with a
benchmark-bridge lane (BB-NEX, BB-YCSB, BB-TPCH, BB-SNB, BB-GRA), a cost model
(PLC1/PLC2), and at least three profiling-gated triggers. BEN1 pays the
infrastructure cost once, under a gating convention that keeps `./gradlew test`
and `./gradlew build check` exactly as fast as they are today — so the tax is
not permanent and not paid by the default build. The measurement numbers that
`30-bounded-read-measurement.md` currently carries only as a prose appendix
become re-runnable artifacts. (See also
`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/BoundedRead.kt`, whose KDoc now cites
those numbers as load-bearing design justification — a number the tree cannot
re-derive.)

**What BEN1 measures, first pass:** per-operator delta-application throughput,
fan-out scaling, and per-cell memory footprint. Nothing else. Those three are
exactly the inputs the deferrals above are waiting on.

---

## 2. What we build

### 2.1 The `:bench` Gradle module

- **Path**: `bench/` at the repository root (sibling of `kernel/`, `testkit/`,
  `concord/`). Registered in `settings.gradle.kts` as `include(":bench")`,
  placed with the other infrastructure modules (`:gen`, `:nature`, `:testkit`)
  rather than under `demo/`.
- **Build script**: `bench/build.gradle.kts`, applying
  `id("buildsrc.convention.kotlin-jvm")` (toolchain 21, shared JUnit5 stack,
  the repo's `Test` task defaults) exactly like every other leaf module. If
  benchmark sources author `@Contract`/`@CellBase` cells of their own, apply
  `buildsrc.convention.ksp-cell` instead — prefer *not* to, and drive existing
  kernel cells.
- **Dependencies**: `implementation(project(":kernel"))`,
  `implementation(project(":testkit"))` (for `SimWorld`/`awaitUntil` — note
  `:testkit` exposes `:kernel` as `api`), plus the JMH artifacts. No dependency
  on `:wire`, `:inspect`, `:concord`, or any `demo/` module in this epic.
- **Nothing depends on `:bench`.** It is a leaf. `:kernel` must not gain a
  dependency on it, and no production module may.

### 2.2 JMH

- Plugin: `me.champeau.jmh` (the maintained Gradle JMH plugin), version pinned
  in `gradle/libs.versions.toml` under `[versions]`/`[plugins]` following the
  existing catalogue style (`ksp`, `kotlin-plugin-serialization`). Pin both the
  plugin and the `jmh-core`/`jmh-generator-annprocess` version explicitly; do
  not float.
- JMH's annotation processor runs over `bench/src/jmh/kotlin` via `kapt`/`ksp`
  or the plugin's own configuration — **verify which combination actually
  generates the JMH `_jmhType` classes for Kotlin sources in this repo before
  writing benchmarks**; a JMH plugin that silently generates zero benchmarks is
  the classic failure and must be caught by the smoke check (§Verification).
- The plugin's `jmh` source set (`bench/src/jmh/kotlin`) holds `@Benchmark`
  bodies. Shared fixtures (graph builders, delta generators, allocation
  probes) live in `bench/src/main/kotlin/civictech/bench/` so both the `jmh`
  source set and any JUnit smoke tests can use them.
- **Configuration cache**: `gradle.properties` sets
  `org.gradle.configuration-cache=true` repo-wide. If the JMH plugin is not
  configuration-cache compatible, resolve it in the build script's own scope —
  do **not** disable the configuration cache globally.

### 2.3 Source sets

| Source set | Path | Contents | Runs in `./gradlew test`? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | `bench/src/main/kotlin/civictech/bench/` | fixtures, generators, result model, findings writer | n/a (compiled by `build`) |
| `jmh` | `bench/src/jmh/kotlin/civictech/bench/` | `@Benchmark` bodies | no |
| `test` | `bench/src/test/kotlin/civictech/bench/` | fast unit tests of the fixtures/generators/reporters, plus a *sub-second* smoke test | yes |

### 2.4 Slow-test gating convention

The repo already has the pattern to copy: `@Tag("multi-jvm")` +
`-PexcludeMultiJvm` / `-PmultiJvmOnly`, implemented in
`buildSrc/src/main/kotlin/kotlin-jvm.gradle.kts` and consumed by both CI lanes
in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. BEN1 adds the analogous `@Tag("bench")` gate to
the same convention plugin, with the same shape:

- Default `./gradlew test` **excludes** `@Tag("bench")`.
- `-PbenchOnly` (or equivalent, named consistently with `multiJvmOnly`) runs
  only the tagged tests.
- The full JMH run is a separate Gradle task (`:bench:jmh`) that is **not**
  wired into `build`, `check`, or `test`.

This is the concrete mechanism by which BEN1 refutes V1C-BENCH's "permanent
tax" objection: the default build's wall-clock must be unchanged.

### 2.5 CI posture

- The five required checks (`build-test-fast`, `build-test-serial`,
  `concord-full`, `ui-test`, `agora-ui-test`) must **not** gain a JMH run.
  BEN1 adds no benchmark execution to any required check.
- `build-test-fast` will compile `:bench` (it runs `./gradlew build check`), so
  the module must compile fast and its `test` source set must stay sub-second.
  A *compile-and-smoke* guarantee in CI, with *execution* on demand, is the
  posture.
- Optional, if cheap and clearly non-blocking: a manually dispatched
  (`workflow_dispatch`) benchmark workflow. It must not be a required check and
  must not run on `push`/`pull_request`. Numbers from a shared GitHub runner are
  for regression smell only, never for the findings file (see §6 risks).

### 2.6 The findings file

- **`doc/bench/findings.md`** — new, append-only, per §6 of the milestone plan
  ("Every lane writes findings to its own append-only `doc/<lane>/findings.md`,
  citing G-ids, never editing `91-gap-analysis.md` or `CONCORDANCE.md`
  directly").
- Every entry records: date, the harness commit SHA, JVM vendor/version, heap
  settings, machine (CPU model, core count, OS), JMH mode/forks/warmup/
  measurement iterations, and the run's variance, alongside the numbers.
- Every entry that touches a gap cites its G-id (G-21, G-43) and states what the
  number does to the trigger: **fires it**, **retires it**, or **is
  inconclusive**. An entry that reports numbers without answering that question
  is incomplete.
- The file must carry the `**Status**:` header vocabulary that
  `:concord:docLints` enforces (see
  `doc/spec/90-roadmap/98-inspector-v4-plan/10-design-notes.md` binding
  constraint 9) if docLints covers `doc/bench/`; check, and comply if so.

---

## 3. How, using ComputeNet

Benchmarks drive **real kernel entry points on a real `ManagedHost`**, not
reimplemented arithmetic. Three families:

### 3.1 Per-operator delta-application throughput

Subjects (all under `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/`):

- Operator cells in `data/op/`: `FilterCell.kt`, `UnionSetCell.kt`,
  `IntersectSetCell.kt`, `JoinSetCell.kt`, `LookupJoinCell.kt`,
  `SemiJoinCell.kt`, `GroupByCell.kt`, `MergeableGroupByCell.kt`,
  `CountCell.kt`, `FlatMapSetCell.kt`, `CombineLatestCell.kt`,
  `CoalescingCombineCell.kt`, `PresenceCountCell.kt`, `QuorumSetCell.kt`,
  `TaggedSetOperator.kt`.
- Aggregators in `data/Aggregator.kt` (retraction-aware sum/avg/count/min/max/
  topK — the TreeMap-backed retraction path is the interesting one).
- Data cells in `data/`: `SetCell.kt`, `MapCell.kt`, `OrMapCell.kt`,
  `KeyedSetCell.kt`, `ListCell.kt`, `CounterCell.kt`, `PnCounterCell.kt`.
- Delta vocabulary in `data/delta/`: `SetDelta.kt`, `MapDelta.kt`,
  `TaggedMapDelta.kt`, and critically `TagState.kt` — tag-map growth is a
  prime suspect for dominating any set-shaped number.

The unit is *deltas applied per second at steady state*, driven through the
real link/port path (`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/port/`,
`.../link/`), not by calling an operator's method directly. Both the **insert**
and the **retraction** direction must be measured separately for every
retraction-aware operator — retraction is where incremental engines actually
differ, and reporting only inserts would be misleading.

`testkit/src/main/kotlin/civictech/testkit/SimWorld.kt` (`runToIdle`) and
`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/SimulationController.kt` give
deterministic drive; `ManagedHost` with
`VirtualThreadScheduler`/`CoroutineScheduler`
(`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/`) gives the real-threads number.
Report which of the two a benchmark used — they answer different questions and
must never be mixed in one table.

### 3.2 Fan-out scaling

Vary the number of downstream subscribers on one outlet
(`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/port/FanOutlet.kt`, plus
`FanInlet.kt`, `link/CatchUp.kt`) and measure per-delta cost as a function of
fan-out degree. This is the curve G-43 ("re-baseline cost under wide fan-out")
and PLC1's cost model both consume. Include a late-join/catch-up variant, since
`CatchUp` is the path a re-baseline actually takes.

### 3.3 Per-cell memory footprint

For each data-cell family at 10³/10⁴/10⁵ elements, report retained bytes per
element and total retained size, separating payload from tag/metadata overhead
(`TagState`, `MintedTags.kt`) — the split is the number G-21 phase 3's
allocation-pressure trigger needs. Prefer allocation counting via
`com.sun.management.ThreadMXBean.getThreadAllocatedBytes` (the technique
`V1C-BENCH.md` already sanctioned in this repo) and/or JMH's
`-prof gc`. If a footprint cannot be attributed honestly, report it as
unattributed rather than estimating.

### 3.4 Reproducing V1C-BENCH

As the harness's first real exercise, re-express `V1C-BENCH`'s E1–E3 (whole
`Stateful.snapshot()` copy cost; live-traffic occupancy dip; paged
counterfactual) against the now-landed
`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/BoundedRead.kt` and
`ManagedHost.snapshotOf`/`readState`. This validates the harness against a
number the repo already accepted at C7, and converts a document appendix into a
runnable artifact. **Do not change any constant** the measurement touches
(`MAX_CELLS`, `BUDGET_MS`, `MAX_ROWS`, `MAX_BYTES`); recommendations go in
`doc/bench/findings.md`.

---

## 4. Scope boundaries

**In scope**: the `:bench` module, the JMH plugin and pinned versions, the
`jmh`/`main`/`test` source sets, the `@Tag("bench")` gating convention in
`buildSrc`, `doc/bench/findings.md`, and the three first-measurement families
of §3 (per-operator delta throughput, fan-out scaling, per-cell footprint),
plus the §3.4 replication.

**Explicitly NOT in scope:**

- **NOT BEN2.** No macro workloads, no graph-shape × cardinality × host-count
  sweeps, no multi-host measurement, no re-baseline cost study. BEN1 stops at
  single-host micro.
- **NOT any BB-\* suite.** No Nexmark generator, no YCSB adapter, no TPC-H
  queries, no LDBC SNB or Graphalytics harness, no TPC-C bridge document. BEN1
  builds the module those will later live in; it does not start them.
- **NOT PLC1.** No mesh simulator, no cost model, no placement policy. BEN1
  produces inputs, not the model.
- **NOT KBLK.** BEN1 does not add WAL-off/async host config, a batched ingress
  path, or deterministic-time drive hooks. If WAL sync dominates a number, BEN1
  **reports** that as a finding naming KBLK — it does not implement KBLK.
- **NOT any kernel optimisation.** No changes under `kernel/src/main` to make a
  benchmark faster. A slow path found is a finding, not a patch.
- **NOT a performance regression gate.** No threshold that fails CI on a number.
  BEN1 establishes baselines; enforcement is a later, separately-argued
  decision.
- **NOT concord.** No `concord/corpus/` scenarios, no `CONCORDANCE.md` edits.
  See §7.
- **NOT gap-table edits.** `91-gap-analysis.md` and `CONCORDANCE.md` stay
  untouched; findings go to `doc/bench/findings.md` per milestone-plan §6.

---

## 5. Functional requirements (EARS)

Ids are epic-scoped `[BEN1-nn]` so they cannot collide with the normative
`[NN-SLUG-nn]` ids in `doc/spec/`. Where a requirement makes an existing
normative requirement or gap trigger true, the spec id / G-id is cited.

### Module and build

- **[BEN1-01]** (ubiquitous) The build shall provide a Gradle module `:bench`
  rooted at `bench/`, registered in `settings.gradle.kts`.
- **[BEN1-02]** (ubiquitous) The `:bench` module shall apply the
  `buildsrc.convention.kotlin-jvm` convention plugin, and shall therefore build
  on Java toolchain 21.
- **[BEN1-03]** (ubiquitous) The `:bench` module shall declare project
  dependencies only on `:kernel` and `:testkit` among repository modules.
- **[BEN1-04]** (unwanted) If any module other than `:bench` declares a
  dependency on `:bench`, then the build shall fail. *(Verifiable as a test
  asserting over the resolved project dependency graph.)*
- **[BEN1-05]** (ubiquitous) The build shall pin the JMH Gradle plugin version
  and the `jmh-core` / `jmh-generator-annprocess` versions in
  `gradle/libs.versions.toml`.
- **[BEN1-06]** (ubiquitous) The `:bench` module shall expose a `jmh` source
  set at `bench/src/jmh/kotlin` whose `@Benchmark`-annotated methods are
  discovered by the JMH generator.
- **[BEN1-07]** (unwanted) If the JMH generator discovers zero benchmarks in
  the `jmh` source set, then the build shall fail rather than report a
  successful benchmark run. *(This is the silent-zero-benchmarks failure mode.)*
- **[BEN1-08]** (ubiquitous) Benchmark fixtures, generators, the result model
  and the findings writer shall live in `bench/src/main/kotlin` so that both
  the `jmh` and `test` source sets can consume them.

### Gating and CI posture

- **[BEN1-09]** (ubiquitous) The shared test convention shall support a
  `@Tag("bench")` gate with the same shape as the existing `@Tag("multi-jvm")`
  gate in `buildSrc/src/main/kotlin/kotlin-jvm.gradle.kts`.
- **[BEN1-10]** (state-driven) While no bench-selecting project property is
  set, `./gradlew test` shall exclude all `@Tag("bench")` tests.
- **[BEN1-11]** (event-driven) When the bench-only project property is set,
  the test task shall run only `@Tag("bench")` tests.
- **[BEN1-12]** (ubiquitous) The `:bench:jmh` task shall not be a dependency of
  `build`, `check`, or `test` in any module.
- **[BEN1-13]** (ubiquitous) The `:bench` module's `test` source set shall
  complete in under one second on a developer machine, so that
  `build-test-fast` gains compile cost only.
- **[BEN1-14]** (unwanted) If a change would add a JMH execution to any of the
  five required status checks (`build-test-fast`, `build-test-serial`,
  `concord-full`, `ui-test`, `agora-ui-test`), then it shall be rejected.
- **[BEN1-15]** (optional-feature) Where a manually dispatched benchmark CI
  workflow is included, it shall be triggered only by `workflow_dispatch` and
  shall not be a required check.
- **[BEN1-16]** (ubiquitous) The repository-wide configuration cache setting in
  `gradle.properties` shall remain enabled.

### What the harness must measure

- **[BEN1-17]** (ubiquitous) The harness shall measure per-operator delta
  application throughput for each operator cell listed in §3.1, driving deltas
  through the real link/port dispatch path rather than by direct method call.
- **[BEN1-18]** (ubiquitous) For every retraction-aware operator or aggregator,
  the harness shall report the insert path and the retraction path as separate
  results.
- **[BEN1-19]** (ubiquitous) The harness shall measure per-delta cost as a
  function of outlet fan-out degree over `FanOutlet`, across at least four
  degrees spanning at least two orders of magnitude. *(Feeds G-43's
  "re-baseline cost under wide fan-out".)*
- **[BEN1-20]** (ubiquitous) The harness shall measure per-cell retained
  footprint for each data-cell family at 10³, 10⁴ and 10⁵ elements, reporting
  payload bytes and tag/metadata bytes separately. *(Feeds G-21 phase 3's
  allocation-pressure trigger.)*
- **[BEN1-21]** (unwanted) If the payload/metadata footprint split cannot be
  attributed by measurement, then the harness shall report the amount as
  unattributed rather than estimating it.
- **[BEN1-22]** (ubiquitous) The harness shall reproduce `V1C-BENCH`'s E1, E2
  and E3 against the landed `BoundedRead`/`snapshotOf`/`readState` surface.

### What every result must carry

- **[BEN1-23]** (ubiquitous) Every reported result shall carry the JVM vendor
  and version, heap settings, machine CPU model and core count, OS, JMH mode,
  fork count, warmup and measurement iteration counts, and the harness commit
  SHA.
- **[BEN1-24]** (ubiquitous) Every result shall carry a dispersion statistic
  (JMH's error at 99.9% confidence, or an explicitly stated equivalent).
- **[BEN1-25]** (unwanted) If a benchmark result's relative dispersion exceeds
  a declared threshold, then the harness shall mark that result **unreportable**
  and shall not admit it to `doc/bench/findings.md` as a finding. The threshold
  shall be a named constant in `bench/src/main/kotlin`, stated in the findings
  file, and chosen from an observed noise floor rather than asserted.
- **[BEN1-26]** (ubiquitous) Every result shall record whether it was driven
  under `SimWorld`/`SimulationController` (deterministic) or under a real
  scheduler (`VirtualThreadScheduler`/`CoroutineScheduler`).
- **[BEN1-27]** (unwanted) If a single reported table mixes deterministic-drive
  and real-scheduler results, then that table shall be rejected as invalid.
- **[BEN1-28]** (unwanted) If a measurement is dominated by a cost the
  benchmark did not intend to measure — WAL/journal sync
  (`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/durability/`), GC, tag-map growth in
  `TagState` — then the harness shall report the dominating cost as the finding
  and shall not tune it away.
- **[BEN1-29]** (event-driven) When WAL/journal sync is found to dominate a
  throughput number, the findings entry shall name **KBLK** as the blocking
  chunk and shall not implement a WAL-off path.

### Findings file

- **[BEN1-30]** (ubiquitous) The lane shall record results in an append-only
  `doc/bench/findings.md`. *(Milestone plan §6.)*
- **[BEN1-31]** (unwanted) If a finding bears on a gap, then its entry shall
  cite the G-id and shall state whether the measurement **fires**, **retires**,
  or is **inconclusive** for that gap's trigger.
- **[BEN1-32]** (unwanted) If a run produces numbers but answers no trigger
  question, then its entry shall be marked incomplete rather than presented as
  a finding.
- **[BEN1-33]** (ubiquitous) The lane shall not edit
  `doc/spec/90-roadmap/91-gap-analysis.md` or `doc/spec/CONCORDANCE.md`.
  *(Milestone plan §6: a periodic single-agent integration pass is their only
  writer.)*
- **[BEN1-34]** (optional-feature) Where `:concord:docLints` covers
  `doc/bench/`, `findings.md` shall carry a `**Status**:` header from the
  enforced vocabulary.

### Boundaries as requirements

- **[BEN1-35]** (unwanted) If a benchmark result suggests a kernel
  optimisation, then this epic shall record it as a finding and shall not
  modify `kernel/src/main`.
- **[BEN1-36]** (ubiquitous) The epic shall not modify `concord/corpus/`,
  `inspect/src`, `wire/src`, or any `demo/` module.
- **[BEN1-37]** (ubiquitous) The epic shall not change `MAX_CELLS`,
  `BUDGET_MS`, `MAX_ROWS` or `MAX_BYTES`; recommendations belong in
  `doc/bench/findings.md`.
- **[BEN1-38]** (unwanted) If a benchmark regression threshold would fail CI on
  a measured number, then it shall not be added under this epic.

### Honesty note on verifiability

`[BEN1-13]` (sub-second `test` source set) and `[BEN1-25]`'s threshold value
are the two requirements that cannot be checked by a pure pass/fail assertion
without becoming flaky on a shared runner. `[BEN1-13]` should be verified by
observation and recorded in the findings file, not asserted by a timing test in
CI. `[BEN1-25]`'s threshold must be derived from an observed noise floor and
stated; a threshold picked to make results pass is a violation of `[BEN1-32]`
in spirit and must be called out rather than accepted.

---

## 6. Behaviour specifications (Given/When/Then)

Each scenario should become a named test or a documented, reproducible
procedure. Scenarios marked *(observational)* are procedures recorded in
`doc/bench/findings.md`, not automated tests.

**BS-1 — Module exists and builds clean.**
Given a fresh clone at toolchain 21;
When `./gradlew :bench:build` runs;
Then it succeeds, and `bench/src/jmh/kotlin` compiles under the JMH plugin.
Covers `[BEN1-01]`, `[BEN1-02]`, `[BEN1-06]`.

**BS-2 — Benchmarks are actually discovered (the silent-zero failure).**
Given the `jmh` source set contains at least one `@Benchmark` method;
When the JMH generator task runs;
Then the generated benchmark list is non-empty;
And if it is empty, the build fails with a message naming the empty source set.
Covers `[BEN1-06]`, `[BEN1-07]`. This is the epic's single most important
negative test: a green JMH build with zero benchmarks is the default failure
mode of a Kotlin + JMH wiring.

**BS-3 — Default test task is unchanged.**
Given a test annotated `@Tag("bench")` that sleeps longer than a second;
When `./gradlew :bench:test` runs with no bench property;
Then that test is not executed.
Covers `[BEN1-09]`, `[BEN1-10]`, `[BEN1-13]`.

**BS-4 — Bench-only selection works.**
Given the same tagged test;
When the test task runs with the bench-only project property set;
Then only `@Tag("bench")` tests execute.
Covers `[BEN1-11]`.

**BS-5 — `check` does not run JMH.**
Given the full build;
When `./gradlew build check -PexcludeMultiJvm=true` runs (the `build-test-fast`
command);
Then no JMH forked benchmark process starts, and `:bench:jmh` is not in the
task graph.
Covers `[BEN1-12]`, `[BEN1-14]`. Verifiable with `--dry-run` task-graph
inspection.

**BS-6 — Leaf-module boundary.**
Given the resolved Gradle project graph;
When a test enumerates every project's project-dependencies;
Then no project other than `:bench` depends on `:bench`, and `:bench` depends
only on `:kernel` and `:testkit`.
Covers `[BEN1-03]`, `[BEN1-04]`.

**BS-7 — Operator throughput, insert and retract.**
Given a `UnionSetCell` (and each other operator of §3.1) fed by a set source
over a real link;
When a steady stream of `SetDelta` adds is applied to steady state, and
separately a steady stream of removes;
Then two distinct throughput results are produced and reported separately.
Covers `[BEN1-17]`, `[BEN1-18]`.

**BS-8 — Fan-out curve.**
Given one outlet with fan-out degree in {1, 4, 16, 64, 256};
When one delta is applied per iteration;
Then per-delta cost is reported per degree, and the findings entry states
whether the observed growth is linear in degree or worse.
Covers `[BEN1-19]`. Feeds G-43.

**BS-9 — Late-join catch-up cost.**
Given an operator at steady state with 10⁵ live elements;
When a new subscriber attaches and takes the `CatchUp` path;
Then the catch-up cost and its occupancy of the source's execution context are
reported.
Covers `[BEN1-19]`. This is the re-baseline-shaped case G-43 cares about.

**BS-10 — Footprint attribution.**
Given a `SetCell` at 10³/10⁴/10⁵ elements;
When retained size is measured;
Then payload and tag/metadata bytes are reported separately, or the unattributed
remainder is reported as unattributed.
Covers `[BEN1-20]`, `[BEN1-21]`. Feeds G-21 phase 3.

**BS-11 — Unwanted: noisy result is refused.**
Given a benchmark whose relative dispersion exceeds the declared threshold;
When results are collected;
Then the result is marked unreportable, is excluded from `doc/bench/findings.md`
as a finding, and the run's log names it.
Covers `[BEN1-24]`, `[BEN1-25]`.

**BS-12 — Unwanted: mixed-drive table is rejected.**
Given results collected under both `SimWorld` and a real scheduler;
When the reporter is asked to emit one table containing both;
Then it refuses.
Covers `[BEN1-26]`, `[BEN1-27]`. Directly testable against the result model in
`bench/src/main/kotlin` — a fast unit test, no benchmark run required.

**BS-13 — Unwanted: missing environment metadata is refused.**
Given a result lacking JVM version, heap, machine, iteration counts or harness
SHA;
When the findings writer is invoked;
Then it refuses to emit the entry.
Covers `[BEN1-23]`, `[BEN1-30]`. Also a fast unit test.

**BS-14 — Unwanted: WAL dominates.**
Given a throughput benchmark on a durable host;
When journal sync is found to account for the majority of wall time;
Then the finding reports WAL dominance, names KBLK, and no WAL-off path is
added in this epic.
Covers `[BEN1-28]`, `[BEN1-29]`. *(Observational; the durability-off decision
is KBLK's.)*

**BS-15 — Recovery: V1C-BENCH replication agrees or explains.**
Given `doc/spec/90-roadmap/98-inspector-v4-plan/30-bounded-read-measurement.md`
and its accepted GO recommendation;
When E1/E2/E3 are re-run through `:bench` against the landed `BoundedRead`;
Then the findings entry states whether the numbers reproduce within dispersion,
and if they do not, states which of {harness difference, code change since C7,
machine difference} explains the divergence — without editing the original
document.
Covers `[BEN1-22]`, `[BEN1-31]`.

**BS-16 — Boundary: a slow path found is not patched.**
Given a benchmark that exposes a hot allocation in `TagState`;
When the run completes;
Then the diff contains no change under `kernel/src/main`, and the finding names
the site.
Covers `[BEN1-28]`, `[BEN1-35]`.

### Concord

**No scenario in this epic belongs in `concord/corpus/`.** The corpus is the
implementation-neutral arbiter of *semantic* spec↔code agreement (see
`concord/schema/`, and the corpus samples under `concord/corpus/24-data-cells/`
whose checks are `final-view` / `incremental-equals-batch` /
`no-dead-letters`). A throughput or footprint number is machine-dependent and
not implementation-neutral; encoding one as a conformance scenario would make
the corpus fail on a slow machine, which is precisely the dishonesty
`concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` exists to prevent. Therefore this epic carries
**no `covers:` ids**, adds no corpus files, and does not regenerate
`doc/spec/CONCORDANCE.md`. If a later agent believes a scenario here is
concord-shaped, that belief should be filed as a question, not as a scenario.

---

## 7. Suggested feature decomposition

1. **F1 — `:bench` module skeleton and JMH wiring.** Module, settings
   registration, convention plugin, pinned JMH versions, `jmh`/`main`/`test`
   source sets, the non-empty-benchmark guard. `[BEN1-01..08]`, BS-1/BS-2/BS-6.
2. **F2 — Slow-test gating convention and CI posture.** `@Tag("bench")` in
   `buildSrc`, project-property selection, task-graph guarantees, optional
   `workflow_dispatch` workflow. `[BEN1-09..16]`, BS-3/BS-4/BS-5.
3. **F3 — Result model, dispersion gate, and findings writer.** Environment
   capture, dispersion threshold, mixed-drive refusal, `doc/bench/findings.md`
   format. `[BEN1-23..27]`, `[BEN1-30..34]`, BS-11/BS-12/BS-13.
4. **F4 — Per-operator delta throughput suite.** `[BEN1-17..18]`, BS-7.
5. **F5 — Fan-out scaling and catch-up suite.** `[BEN1-19]`, BS-8/BS-9.
6. **F6 — Per-cell footprint suite and the V1C-BENCH replication.**
   `[BEN1-20..22]`, BS-10/BS-15, plus the first real findings entries against
   G-21 and G-43.

F1→F2→F3 are sequential; F4/F5/F6 are parallel once F3 lands.

---

## 8. Verification

- `./gradlew :bench:test` — the fast unit tests (result model, dispersion gate,
  findings writer, project-graph assertions). Sub-second.
- `./gradlew :bench:jmh` — the benchmark run. Not part of any gate.
- `./gradlew build check -PexcludeMultiJvm=true` — the `build-test-fast`
  command; must pass and must not start a JMH fork.
- `./gradlew build check -PmultiJvmOnly=true` — the `build-test-serial`
  command; unchanged.
- `./gradlew :concord:check` and `./gradlew :concord:test` — must be unaffected
  (no corpus or concordance change).
- `./gradlew test` — the repository-wide gate; wall-clock must not materially
  increase. Record before/after in `doc/bench/findings.md`.
- `--dry-run` task-graph inspection proving `:bench:jmh` is absent from
  `build`/`check`/`test`.
- `git status --porcelain -uall -- doc '*/src'` clean (CI's untracked-files
  guard).
- `doc/bench/findings.md` exists and contains at least one complete entry per
  §3.1, §3.2, §3.3, and §3.4, each satisfying `[BEN1-23]`, `[BEN1-24]` and
  `[BEN1-31]`.

---

## 9. Risks / open questions

- **JMH-in-CI cost.** JMH runs are minutes-to-hours and noisy on shared
  runners. Mitigation: `[BEN1-12]`/`[BEN1-14]` keep execution out of every
  required check; `[BEN1-15]` confines any CI run to manual dispatch, for
  regression smell only. **Open**: whether a nightly cheap-mode run is worth
  having at all — deliberately deferred, not decided here.
- **Measurement noise.** A laptop under thermal throttling produces numbers
  that will be quoted for years (`V1C-BENCH`'s already are, in
  `BoundedRead.kt`'s KDoc). Mitigation: `[BEN1-23]`–`[BEN1-25]`. **Open**: the
  dispersion threshold value; it must come from an observed noise floor, and
  choosing it is F3's job, not this epic's.
- **WAL dominating throughput.** The journal/durability path
  (`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/durability/`) can swamp any
  operator-level number. **KBLK exists precisely for this** (milestone plan §1
  kernel lane: "WAL off/async host config, batched ingress path,
  deterministic-time drive hooks", and §3's Nexmark row: "KBLK for honest
  throughput (WAL sync would otherwise dominate)"). BEN1 reports the
  domination and names KBLK; it does not implement it. Consequence: some BEN1
  numbers may be honestly labelled *WAL-bound* rather than
  *operator-bound* — that is a legitimate deliverable, not a failure.
- **Kotlin + JMH annotation processing.** The wiring that generates JMH
  benchmark classes from Kotlin sources is the most likely place to lose a day.
  `[BEN1-07]`/BS-2 exist to make failure loud rather than silent.
- **Configuration cache compatibility.** The JMH plugin may not be
  configuration-cache compatible. `[BEN1-16]` forbids solving this by disabling
  the cache repo-wide. **Open**: if no compatible configuration exists, the
  fallback (task-scoped opt-out vs. a different plugin vs. a hand-rolled JMH
  invocation) needs deciding in F1.
- **Microbenchmarks measuring the harness.** Driving deltas through the real
  link/port path means the measurement includes dispatch. That is intentional
  (it is what the runtime actually costs), but every result must say so, or
  readers will compare a ComputeNet operator number against a bare-loop
  DBSP number and draw a false conclusion. **Open**: whether to also report a
  direct-call floor per operator as a denominator; recommended, but not
  required by any requirement above.
- **`:bench` becoming a dumping ground.** The BB-* suites will land here. F1
  should establish a package layout (`civictech.bench.micro`,
  `civictech.bench.suite.*`) that keeps BEN1's micro work separable from the
  suites that follow.

# BEN1 — design notes

## Concrete shape of the module

```
bench/
  build.gradle.kts
  src/main/kotlin/civictech/bench/
    Env.kt            # JVM/heap/machine/JMH-config capture -> RunEnvironment
    Result.kt         # BenchResult(value, unit, dispersion, drive, env), Drive = SIM | REAL
    Dispersion.kt     # NOISE_FLOOR threshold constant + reportable()/unreportable()
    Findings.kt       # renders entries for doc/bench/findings.md; refuses incomplete entries
    micro/Graphs.kt   # real ManagedHost + link/port graph builders per operator
    micro/Deltas.kt   # SetDelta/MapDelta stream generators (insert & retract directions)
    micro/Footprint.kt# ThreadMXBean.getThreadAllocatedBytes + retained-size probes
  src/jmh/kotlin/civictech/bench/micro/
    OperatorThroughputBenchmark.kt
    FanOutScalingBenchmark.kt
    CellFootprintBenchmark.kt
    BoundedReadBenchmark.kt   # V1C-BENCH E1/E2/E3 replication
  src/test/kotlin/civictech/bench/
    ResultModelTest.kt        # BS-12, BS-13
    ProjectGraphTest.kt       # BS-6
    BenchmarkDiscoverySmokeTest.kt  # BS-2 companion (sub-second)
```

`settings.gradle.kts`: add `include(":bench")` in the infrastructure block next
to `:testkit`, not under `demo/`.

## Build script sketch

```kotlin
plugins {
    id("buildsrc.convention.kotlin-jvm")
    alias(libs.plugins.jmh)          // pinned in gradle/libs.versions.toml
}

dependencies {
    implementation(project(":kernel"))
    implementation(project(":testkit"))   // SimWorld, awaitUntil; brings :kernel as api
}

jmh {
    // conservative, explicit; every value shows up in the findings entry
    fork = 2; warmupIterations = 5; iterations = 10
    // resultFormat / resultsFile so runs are machine-readable, not scraped from stdout
}
```

Note `buildsrc.convention.kotlin-jvm` already sets `jvmToolchain(21)`, the JUnit5
stack, `maxHeapSize = "2g"`, `forkEvery(80)` and a 5-minute per-method JUnit
timeout — inherit all of it rather than re-declaring.

## The gating convention

`buildSrc/src/main/kotlin/kotlin-jvm.gradle.kts` currently has:

```kotlin
when {
    project.hasProperty("multiJvmOnly") -> includeTags("multi-jvm")
    project.hasProperty("excludeMultiJvm") -> excludeTags("multi-jvm")
}
```

Extend to a tag list rather than nesting a second `when`, so `bench` and
`multi-jvm` compose:

- default: `excludeTags("bench")` **always** (unlike `multi-jvm`, which runs by
  default in a plain `./gradlew test`). Benchmarks are never part of a default
  run — that is the whole "not a permanent tax" argument.
- `-PbenchOnly`: `includeTags("bench")`.

Keep the existing `multi-jvm` semantics byte-identical; both CI lanes depend on
them.

## Why `@Tag("bench")` at all, when JMH already lives outside `test`

Two different things need gating. `:bench:jmh` is outside `test` by
construction. But measurement work also produces *JUnit-shaped* long-running
probes (occupancy dips, catch-up cost, footprint at 10⁵) that are far easier to
write as tests than as JMH benchmarks, and those must not enter the default
run. `@Tag("bench")` is for those. Both mechanisms are needed; neither replaces
the other.

## Driving real entry points

Reuse, do not reinvent:
- `kernel/src/test/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/SnapshotOfHardeningTest.kt` — the
  existing real-host `snapshotOf` harness `V1C-BENCH` was told to copy.
- `kernel/src/test/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/` — existing source→cell graph
  construction per operator.
- `testkit` `SimWorld.runToIdle(budget)` for deterministic drive;
  `civictech.cell.host.SimulationController` for controlled stepping.

A benchmark's `@Setup` builds the graph and warms it; the `@Benchmark` body
applies deltas and drives to quiescence. Report the quiescence-drive cost as
part of the number and say so — a benchmark that excludes it is measuring an
operator that never propagates.

## Result model invariants (the testable half)

`BenchResult` should make BS-12/BS-13 structurally impossible to violate:
- `RunEnvironment` has no nullable fields; construction fails without JVM/heap/
  machine/iterations/SHA.
- `Drive` is a required enum on every result; `FindingsTable` takes a
  `Set<Drive>` of size 1 or refuses.
- `Dispersion` carries the threshold comparison; `Findings.entry()` accepts
  only `Reportable` results.

These are ordinary unit tests, run in `build-test-fast`, and they are what makes
the epic's honesty requirements enforceable rather than aspirational.

## Findings entry template

```
## <date> — <what was measured>
Status: <docLints vocabulary if applicable>
Harness: <sha> · JVM <vendor/version> · heap <...> · <cpu>, <cores> cores, <os>
JMH: mode=<...> forks=<n> warmup=<n> iters=<n> · drive=<SIM|REAL>
| subject | insert (ops/s ± err) | retract (ops/s ± err) | notes |
Trigger: G-21 phase 3 — FIRES / RETIRES / INCONCLUSIVE, because <...>
```

## Ordering rationale

F3 (result model + findings writer) before F4–F6 deliberately: writing the
refusal rules after the numbers exist means the numbers get grandfathered in.
The dispersion gate has to be able to reject the first real run.

## Things a later agent will be tempted to do, and must not

- Add `:bench` to `check` "so it doesn't rot" — `[BEN1-12]`, `[BEN1-14]`.
  Compile coverage from `build` is the rot protection.
- Turn WAL off to get a nicer number — that is KBLK, `[BEN1-29]`.
- Fix the hot path it finds — `[BEN1-35]`.
- Add a concord scenario for a throughput floor — see description §6 Concord.
- Widen into Nexmark "since the module is there now" — BB-NEX is a separate
  chunk with its own kernel dependencies (KE4, KBLK).

description:
# CHA3 — Generative membership-churn harness (the G-45 ask, verbatim)

Milestone-plan row (`computenet-milestone-plan.md` §1, Evidence lanes), verbatim:

> | CHA3 | Generative membership-churn harness (the G-45 ask, verbatim) | CHA1 | MEM2 |

Filed as a **feature under CHA1** (`computenet-umx`): it builds no fault injector. Partition
(park/drop, directional), crash, journal mutation, arbitrary-frontier restart, seeded
replay, shrinking, dead-letter and exclusive-payload accounting are CHA1 deliverables
(`[CHA1-10]`…`[CHA1-24]`, `[CHA1-30]`…`[CHA1-40]`, `[CHA1-52]`, `[CHA1-53]`). CHA1 §6 says
so directly: *"Generative membership churn — that is CHA3 (the G-45 ask, verbatim). CHA1
must make churn **expressible** (crash + partition + interest/epoch reassignment as
faults) but ships no churn generator, no reconvergence property, and no last-replica-handoff
work."* CHA3 ships the churn generator and the reconvergence property. It does **not** ship
last-replica handoff — that is MEM2.

---

## 0. The ask, verbatim

The plan says "verbatim", so here is the G-45 ask exactly as `doc/spec/` states it. It
appears in two places, word-identical.

`doc/spec/40-distribution/42-replication.md:285-296`:

> ⚠ GAP (G-45, narrowed W3.3): the gossip-mesh skeleton still lacks its liveness/churn
> **argument** — membership-churn reconvergence is unproven — and graceful last-replica
> handoff to durable storage is undesigned. The gate half is built (above:
> suspend-when-partitioned, drain-gated despawn, peer reconciliation) and the
> convergence-invariant harness now carries a departed-stream rule
> (`cell.verify.ReplicaConvergence`, 50/52), so a replica's orderly departure no longer
> false-positives a live divergence.
> `[42-REPL-06]` IF a replica departs orderly (evict/despawn) while its peers keep
> accepting writes, THEN the surviving replicas SHALL still converge and the departed
> replica's frozen final stream SHALL NOT be counted as a divergence.
> **Proposal**: state the bounded-gossip-hop reconciliation argument (duplicate/stale mesh
> links safe by tag idempotence) with a generative membership-churn harness (R1, 95);
> define graceful last-replica handoff to durable storage (G-25) vs accidental deletion.

`doc/spec/50-development-process/52-verification.md:51-62` repeats the same ⚠ GAP block
and adds the **departed-stream rule** it is paired with:

> **Departed-stream rule** (G-45): a replica evicted mid-run (42's gated despawn) drops out
> of `replicasOf(id)` — `ReplicaConvergence.converged()` only requires agreement among
> replicas still counted as live membership, so an orderly departure no longer
> false-positives a divergence against the departed replica's frozen last fold.

And the gap row, `doc/spec/90-roadmap/91-gap-analysis.md:96`, which splits built from
residual:

> **Built**: the eviction gate itself (membership-gated suspend-when-partitioned +
> drain-gated despawn, `Replication.evict`), peer-side reconciliation on despawn
> (`RegistryAnnounce.unpublished`), and the replica-convergence invariant harness with its
> departed-stream rule (`cell.verify.ReplicaConvergence`) — a departed replica no longer
> false-positives a live divergence.
> **Proposal**: State the bounded-gossip-hop reconciliation argument (duplicate/stale mesh
> links safe by tag idempotence) with a generative membership-churn harness (R1, 95);
> define graceful last-replica handoff to durable storage (G-25) vs accidental deletion.

**Reading the ask precisely.** It has two clauses joined by a semicolon, and they are
different kinds of work:

1. *"State the bounded-gossip-hop reconciliation argument (duplicate/stale mesh links safe
   by tag idempotence) **with** a generative membership-churn harness (R1, 95)"* — an
   argument **evidenced by** a harness. CHA3 owns the harness and the evidence, and states
   the argument in its lane findings file. It does **not** edit `doc/spec/`: promoting the
   argument into normative text is documentation maintenance (milestone plan §6: a
   periodic single-agent integration pass is the only writer of the gap table).
2. *"define graceful last-replica handoff to durable storage (G-25) vs accidental
   deletion"* — a **design** obligation. That is **MEM2** ("G-45 churn-reconvergence +
   last-replica handoff", plan §1 kernel lane, depending on `MEM1, CHA3`). CHA3's
   contribution to it is to make the *last-replica condition itself* observable and
   generatable, so MEM2 designs against measured behaviour rather than intuition.

Everything in §4 sits on one side of that split, and §6 states the line.

Note the standing sub-clause "(R1, 95)". `doc/spec/90-roadmap/95-research-plan.md:17`
(R1 — Leader election & failover) is **research-gated**: its actions are "simulate
partition/heal/leader-crash on the `SimulationController` with the `LeaderMark` fold and
measure split-brain windows". CHA3 supplies that simulator and those measurements as
evidence; it does **not** pick between R1's directions (1) and (2), and does not implement
election. Election is MEM1 (G-44).

---

## 1. Ambition / Why

Every other property in ComputeNet's replication story is checked on a **fixed** membership.
`ReplicatedSessionTest`, `SetConvergenceTest`, `OrMapConvergenceTest`,
`PnCounterReplicationTest` all stand up N replicas, gossip, partition/heal, and assert
convergence — with the same N throughout. `GossipLinkIdempotenceTest` covers exactly one
disconnect/reconnect cycle, by hand, and its KDoc names the reason it exists: *"Membership
convergence cannot see this: the mergeable merge is idempotent, so duplicated delivery
still converges. Only the subscription count exposes it"* — one cycle adds one orphaned
consumer, "every cycle would add one, unbounded". `MemberDepartureFrontierTest` covers one
orderly departure. `UnknownJoinerFenceTest` covers one unknown joiner.

That is a set of point samples through a space whose whole difficulty is *sequences*: join
during a partition, depart during a heal, rejoin under a stale link, crash before the
final push-catch-up, evict down to one replica, evict the last one. Membership is
explicitly **not** a consensus (`42-replication.md`, decided 93 I-3): `replicasOf(id)` is
an eventually-consistent local fold, "Peers MAY transiently disagree on the set; gossip
idempotence makes that safe (a late-learned peer catches up; a stale peer's extra link
delivers a duplicate that merges to a no-op)". That sentence *is* the bounded-gossip-hop
argument — asserted, never generated against. CHA3 generates against it.

What CHA3 unblocks:

- **MEM2** (plan §2: `CHA3 --> MEM2`; §1: "MEM2 | G-45 churn-reconvergence + last-replica
  handoff | MEM1, CHA3"). MEM2 cannot design last-replica handoff without a harness that
  can *reach* the last-replica condition on demand, under arbitrary churn, reproducibly.
- **R1 / MEM1 evidence** (95 §R1's stated actions: measure split-brain windows under the
  `LeaderMark` fold). CHA3 is the instrument; MEM1 is the mechanism.
- **R13** (95 §R13 — membership completeness & departed-replica liveness for the stability
  read; "Actions: run the E3.5 harness under join/churn seeds"). CHA3 is the join/churn
  seed source those actions need.
- **E3.6** (`96 §E3.6` — membership and departure gates, the G-45 seam; its test clause is
  "3-peer seeded mesh — evict mid-run → stability advances past the closed row; kill
  without evict → stability frozen and the notice observed"). CHA3 generalises that
  scripted 3-peer test into a generated one.

## 2. What we build

A churn layer in CHA1's rig package (`testkit/src/main/kotlin/civictech/testkit/dst/churn/`),
plus its own test suite. Four pieces.

### 2.1 The churn plan generator

A seeded generator producing `ChurnPlan` — an ordered, step-indexed sequence of membership
**events** over a logical id: `Join(peer)`, `Depart(peer, mode)`, `Rejoin(peer)`,
`Reassign(peer, interest, epoch)`, composed with CHA1 `Fault`s so that a departure can be
orderly (`Replication.evict`) or unclean (`CrashFault`), and a join can land during a
partition. Activation points are `SimulationController` steps, never wall clock
(`[CHA1-02]`).

Departure modes, matching what the kernel actually distinguishes:
`EVICT_CLEAN` (drain-gated despawn + watermark row close), `EVICT_NO_CLOSE`
(`Replication.evict(closeDepartedRow = false)` — the existing PN-0c control seam),
`CRASH_UNCLEAN` (CHA1 `CrashFault`, no close), and `PARTITION_SUSPEND` (the
membership-gated suspend when no peer in `replicasOf(id) − {local}` is reachable).

### 2.2 The reconvergence property

The standing assertion over any generated plan: after the plan's last event and
quiescence, every replica **still counted as live membership** exposes the same fold, and
that fold equals a batch reference over the ops each surviving replica actually accepted.
This is `[42-REPL-06]` generalised from one orderly departure to arbitrary churn, and it
composes with `cell.verify.ReplicaConvergence` (whose `liveRefs()` already implements the
departed-stream rule) rather than reimplementing membership.

### 2.3 The bounded-gossip-hop instrumentation

The measurable form of the argument: per churn event, the number of gossip **hops** until
every live replica has absorbed every effective delta; the count of outbound gossip
subscriptions per replica (the `GossipLinkIdempotenceTest` quantity, generalised); the
count of *stale* links — links to refs no longer in `replicasOf(id)` — and the number of
duplicate deliveries they cause. The argument's claim is that all three are **bounded**
(hops by mesh diameter, subscriptions by live membership size, duplicates absorbed to
no-ops). The harness reports them so "bounded" is a measured statement, not a hope.

### 2.4 The last-replica probe

A generated plan that drives membership down to one replica, and then to zero, recording
what the kernel does at each step: which departures are refused (`evict` returns `false`
and suspends when `reachablePeers.isEmpty()`), whether unique un-gossiped state exists at
the moment of refusal, and what a crash of the last replica leaves behind. CHA3 **reports**;
MEM2 designs the handoff.

## 3. How, using ComputeNet

### 3.1 Which CHA1 machinery is reused (not rebuilt)

| CHA1 deliverable | CHA3's use |

| `PartitionFault(edge, from, until, direction, mode ∈ {PARK, DROP})` (`[CHA1-11]`…`[CHA1-13]`) | join-during-partition, depart-during-partition, asymmetric visibility |
| `CrashFault(host, atStep, mode)` (`[CHA1-17]`, `[CHA1-18]`) | `CRASH_UNCLEAN` departure |
| `JournalFault` / `RestartAtFrontierFault` (`[CHA1-19]`…`[CHA1-22]`) | rejoin-from-a-stale-prefix |
| `DuplicateFault` (`[CHA1-16]`) | the tag-idempotence half of the argument, adversarially |
| step-indexed activation, budget, outcomes (`[CHA1-02]`, `[CHA1-03]`) | churn events are scheduled the same way |
| trace digest + same-seed-same-trace (`[CHA1-05]`, `[CHA1-33]`) | churn plans are deterministic |
| artifact / replay / seed-invariant shrink (`[CHA1-30]`…`[CHA1-40]`) | a failing churn plan is replayable and shrinkable |

### 3.3 The bounded-gossip-hop argument, made measurable

The claim (42-replication.md, 93 I-3): *duplicate and stale mesh links are safe by tag
idempotence*. Its three measurable consequences, and how the harness observes each:

| Claim | Observable | Source |
|---|---|---|
| a stale peer's extra link delivers a duplicate that **merges to a no-op** | count of effective-vs-received deltas at each replica; effective count unchanged by the duplicate | `Replicable.applyRemote` re-emitting only new information (echo termination) |
| a late-learned peer **catches up** | after a join, the joiner's fold reaches the mesh fold within a bounded number of gossip hops | `maybeLink`'s catch-up re-fire; `[42-REPL-05]` |
| link count does not grow with churn | `Replication.linkCountAmong(liveRefs)` bounded by live membership size across N cycles | the `GossipLinkIdempotenceTest` quantity |

A fourth, from the eviction gate: a replica with no reachable peer **suspends rather than
evicting**, so unique un-gossiped state is never dropped — observable as `evict` returning
`false` plus `partitionSuspended` membership.
