## 4. Functional requirements (EARS)

Ids are feature-scoped `[CHA3-nn]` and never collide with normative `[NN-SLUG-nn]` ids,
with `[CHA1-nn]`, or with ORA2/CHA2's. "The harness" = the CHA3 deliverable. The
*Makes true* citation names the normative requirement or gap id each item makes checkable.

### 4.1 Ubiquitous — the churn generator

- `[CHA3-01]` The harness shall generate, from one seed, an ordered membership-churn plan
  over a logical id composed of join, depart, rejoin and interest/epoch-reassignment
  events, and the plan shall be identical for identical (seed, config) across JVM runs.
  *(G-45: "generative membership-churn harness")*
- `[CHA3-02]` The harness shall express every churn event's activation point as a
  `SimulationController` step index and shall never use wall-clock time. *(reuses
  `[CHA1-02]`)*
- `[CHA3-03]` The harness shall support the departure modes clean evict, evict without
  closing the departed watermark row, unclean crash, and partition-induced suspend, and
  shall label which mode each departure used in its report. *(`Replication.evict`'s two
  arms + `closeDepartedRow`; `96 §E3.6` (b)/(c))*
- `[CHA3-04]` The harness shall compose churn events with CHA1 faults so that a join, a
  departure or a rejoin can occur while a partition is active. *(reuses `[CHA1-11]`…`[CHA1-13]`)*
- `[CHA3-05]` The harness shall accept configuration of at least: peer-count range, churn
  event count, per-mode departure weights, concurrency of churn with writes, partition
  overlap probability, and op-script length.
- `[CHA3-06]` The harness shall derive every source of randomness in a run — the
  controller's host pick, the churn plan, the fault plan and the op script — from one run
  seed. *(reuses `[CHA1-30]`)*
- `[CHA3-07]` The harness shall introduce no fault injector, artifact format, replay
  mechanism or shrinker of its own, and shall consume CHA1's. *(CHA1 §6 scope split)*

### 4.2 Ubiquitous — the reconvergence property

- `[CHA3-10]` The harness shall assert, at quiescence after every churn plan, that every
  replica still counted as live membership exposes an equal fold. *(`[42-REPL-04]`,
  `[42-REPL-06]`)*
- `[CHA3-11]` The harness shall assert that the converged fold equals a batch reference
  over the operations the surviving replicas actually accepted, and shall not settle for
  replica-vs-replica agreement alone. *(`[42-REPL-04]`)*
- `[CHA3-12]` The harness shall determine live membership through
  `LocationRegistry.replicasOf(logicalId)` composed with
  `cell.verify.ReplicaConvergence.liveRefs()`, and shall not reimplement membership
  filtering. *(the departed-stream rule, `52-verification.md:51`)*
- `[CHA3-13]` The harness shall assert that a departed replica's frozen final fold is
  excluded from the convergence judgement rather than counted as a divergence.
  *(`[42-REPL-06]`)*
- `[CHA3-14]` The harness shall assert that a replica joining after deltas have already
  gossiped through the mesh reaches a fold indistinguishable from a replica present from
  the start. *(`[42-REPL-05]`)*

### 4.3 Event-driven — the bounded-gossip-hop argument

- `[CHA3-20]` When a churn plan completes, the harness shall report, per replica, the
  number of outbound gossip subscriptions, and shall assert it is bounded by the live
  membership size. *(93 I-3 "a stale peer's extra link delivers a duplicate that merges to
  a no-op"; generalises `GossipLinkIdempotenceTest`)*
- `[CHA3-21]` When a peer rejoins, the harness shall assert that no orphaned gossip
  subscription from the prior attachment survives on the local delta outlet or in the
  port's link record. *(the T21 regression `GossipLinkIdempotenceTest` pins for one cycle)*
- `[CHA3-22]` When a stale link delivers a delta whose information the receiver already
  holds, the harness shall assert the receiver's effective-delta count is unchanged.
  *(echo termination / tag idempotence)*
- `[CHA3-23]` When a replica joins mid-run, the harness shall record the number of gossip
  hops until its fold equals the mesh fold, and shall assert it is bounded by the mesh
  diameter for that membership. *(the "bounded-gossip-hop" claim, made measurable)*
- `[CHA3-24]` When a duplicate fault re-delivers gossip frames during churn, the harness
  shall assert the converged fold is unchanged. *(reuses `[CHA1-16]`; `[24-SET-02]`)*
- `[CHA3-25]` The harness shall report the measured hop count, subscription count, stale-link
  count and duplicate-absorption count per run, so "bounded" is a measured statement rather
  than an assertion of faith. *(G-45: the missing **argument**)*

### 4.4 State-driven

- `[CHA3-30]` While a replica has no reachable peer in `replicasOf(id) − {local}`, the
  harness shall assert the replica is suspended rather than evicted, and that its state is
  retained. *(the membership-gated suspend arm of `Replication.evict`; 93 I-3)*
- `[CHA3-31]` While a partition-suspended replica awaits heal, the harness shall assert its
  delivered-watermark row is suspended and not closed. *(`96 §E3.6` (b): "a
  partition-suspended replica does **not** close — its frozen row is correct")*
- `[CHA3-32]` While membership contains exactly one live replica, the harness shall record
  whether that replica holds effective state not present at any durable store, and shall
  report it as the last-replica condition. *(G-45's second clause, as an observation)*

### 4.5 Unwanted behaviour

- `[CHA3-40]` If a churn plan causes two live replicas to expose different folds at
  quiescence, then the harness shall fail the run, name both replicas, the differing keys
  or elements, and emit a replayable CHA1 artifact. *(`[42-REPL-04]`)*
- `[CHA3-41]` If a replica departs cleanly and the surviving replicas' stability fails to
  advance past its closed row, then the harness shall fail the run. *(`96 §E3.6` (b))*
- `[CHA3-42]` If a replica departs uncleanly, then the harness shall assert the frontier
  freezes and the `Stall`-family notice is observed, and shall **not** treat a silent
  unfreeze as success. *(`96 §E3.6` (c): "surfaced as a `Stall`-family notice on the reads,
  **not** worked around")*
- `[CHA3-43]` If a rejoin cycle increases a replica's outbound gossip subscription count,
  then the harness shall fail the run. *(the unbounded-accumulation defect T21 fixed)*
- `[CHA3-44]` If an exclusive payload is dropped, suppressed, parked or shadowed during a
  churn plan without an explicit consume, release or discharge, then the harness shall fail
  the run through CHA1's accounting rather than a bespoke assertion. *(reuses `[CHA1-53]`;
  `[23]` ownership)*
- `[CHA3-45]` If a dead letter is produced during a churn plan and is not explained by a
  labelled churn event or fault, then the harness shall fail the run. *(reuses `[CHA1-52]`)*
- `[CHA3-46]` If a churn event names a peer, host or logical id absent from the graph under
  test, then the harness shall fail immediately with a naming error and shall not run to
  quiescence reporting a green pass. *(reuses `[CHA1-23]`)*
- `[CHA3-47]` If a churn event never fires within the run's step budget, then the harness
  shall mark it inert with `fired=0`, so a sweep cannot accumulate plans that silently test
  nothing. *(reuses `[CHA1-24]`)*
- `[CHA3-48]` If a discovered failing seed would make a churn sweep red, then that seed
  shall not be removed, replaced, narrowed or reordered; the shrinker shall reduce only the
  churn plan and the fault plan, and shall hold the seed constant. *(`AGENTS.md`;
  `[CHA1-35]`, `[CHA1-38]`)*
- `[CHA3-49]` If a churn-reachable property cannot be checked honestly, then it shall be
  filed in `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` with its reasoning and shall not be weakened into a
  passing scenario. *(`AGENTS.md`)*

### 4.6 Optional feature — single-writer churn and the R1 measurement

- `[CHA3-50]` Where the replica set is single-writer, the harness shall support churn of the
  leader and shall measure the window during which more than one instance believes itself
  leader. *(95 §R1 action: "measure split-brain windows")*
- `[CHA3-51]` Where a leader departs, the harness shall record whether any accepted write is
  lost or duplicated across the transition, and shall report the interleaving that produced
  it. *(95 §R1 action: "prove or refute that epoch fencing plus parked-writes yields no
  lost/duplicated write in every interleaving")*
- `[CHA3-52]` The harness shall not implement leader election and shall not choose between
  R1's directions; it shall report measurements only. *(95 §R1 is research-gated; election
  is MEM1/G-44)*
- `[CHA3-53]` Where the delivered-watermark stability read is present, the harness shall
  provide its churn seeds to that read's own harness rather than duplicating it.
  *(95 §R13 action: "run the E3.5 harness under join/churn seeds")*

### 4.7 Complex

- `[CHA3-60]` Where churn is configured to overlap writes, the harness shall issue a
  configurable fraction of operations while a churn event is in flight, and shall report the
  **achieved** overlap, so a configured-but-unrealised overlap is visible rather than
  silently zero.
- `[CHA3-61]` Where a plan drives membership to a single replica, the harness shall continue
  the plan through an attempted departure of that replica and shall record the kernel's
  refusal (`evict` returning false plus suspension) as the observed last-replica behaviour.
  *(G-45's second clause; the observation MEM2 designs against)*
- `[CHA3-62]` Where a plan drives membership to zero live replicas, the harness shall record
  what state survives and where, and shall state plainly that CHA3 defines no handoff.
  *(G-45's second clause belongs to MEM2)*

### 4.8 Discrimination — blocking

A green churn sweep without these is not evidence.

- `[CHA3-70]` The harness shall include a control in which a departing replica's final
  push-catch-up is suppressed, and shall assert the run **fails** on at least one seed —
  proving the reconvergence check can detect lost state.
- `[CHA3-71]` The harness shall include a control in which the departed-stream rule is
  disabled (a departed replica's frozen fold counted as live), and shall assert the run
  fails — proving `[CHA3-13]` is load-bearing and not vacuous.
- `[CHA3-72]` The harness shall include the existing PN-0c control
  (`Replication.evict(closeDepartedRow = false)`) and shall assert the resulting wedge is
  detected, not silently tolerated. *(`MemberDepartureFrontierTest`'s control seam)*
- `[CHA3-73]` The harness shall include a control in which rejoin re-links without dropping
  the prior subscription, and shall assert `[CHA3-43]` fires.
- `[CHA3-74]` If any control does not diverge, then the corresponding property shall be
  treated as unproven and the harness shall fail its own self-test. *(mirrors `[CHA1-63]`)*

### 4.9 Reporting and boundaries

- `[CHA3-80]` The harness shall run every seed in a requested sweep regardless of earlier
  failures and shall report failure density as `N of M`. *(reuses `[CHA1-39]`)*
- `[CHA3-81]` The harness shall write the bounded-gossip-hop argument, in prose, with the
  measured numbers that support it, to an append-only lane findings file citing G-45 — and
  shall not edit `doc/spec/`, `91-gap-analysis.md`, `CONCORDANCE.md` or any plan document.
  *(milestone plan §6)*
- `[CHA3-82]` The harness shall make no kernel `main` change; a discovered divergence yields
  a shrunk counterexample, a pinned seed and a findings entry.
- `[CHA3-83]` The harness shall add no concord scenario and no corpus schema change; churn
  verbs in the scenario language are schema-change-gated. *(CHA1 §6)*
- `[CHA3-84]` The harness shall define no last-replica handoff mechanism and shall
  implement no leader election. *(MEM2 and MEM1 respectively)*

## 5. Behaviour specifications

Each becomes one named test. `covers:` notes mark concord-corpus candidates; where a
scenario does not belong there, the reason is stated. The concord scenario language has no
fault or churn verbs (CHA1 §6), so most CHA3 scenarios cannot be corpus scenarios today
regardless of merit — flag and stop.

**BS-1 — Reconvergence under a generated churn plan** (`[CHA3-01]`, `[CHA3-10]`,
`[CHA3-11]`, `[CHA3-12]`)
*Given* a seeded churn plan over a replicated `SetCell` mesh with concurrent writes.
*When* the plan runs to completion and the mesh quiesces.
*Then* every live replica exposes an equal fold, and that fold equals the batch reference
over accepted operations. Run over a seed sweep with density reported.
*Corpus candidate*: `covers: [42-REPL-04]` **only if** churn verbs ever exist; today no.

**BS-2 — An orderly departure is not a divergence** (`[CHA3-13]`)
*Given* a 3-peer mesh with writes in flight.
*When* one replica is cleanly evicted mid-run and peers keep accepting writes.
*Then* survivors converge, and the departed replica's frozen final fold is excluded from
the judgement. *Corpus*: already covered by
`concord/corpus/42-replication/42-REPL-DEPART-01.yaml` (`covers: [42-REPL-06]`) — CHA3
cites it and adds the generated generalisation locally.

**BS-3 — Lost final catch-up is detected** (`[CHA3-70]`)
*Given* the BS-2 setup with the departing replica's final push-catch-up suppressed.
*When* the sweep runs. *Then* at least one seed fails with a fold mismatch naming the lost
elements. The control that proves BS-2 can fail.

**BS-4 — Disabling the departed-stream rule breaks the check** (`[CHA3-71]`)
*Given* a churn plan with a clean departure.
*When* the departed replica's frozen fold is counted as live membership.
*Then* the run fails — proving `[CHA3-13]` is load-bearing.

**BS-5 — Rejoin does not accumulate subscriptions** (`[CHA3-20]`, `[CHA3-21]`,
`[CHA3-43]`)
*Given* a generated plan with N depart/rejoin cycles for one peer.
*When* the plan completes.
*Then* the peer's outbound gossip subscription count is bounded by live membership size —
checked on the outlet's consumer map **and** the port's link record, exactly as
`GossipLinkIdempotenceTest` does for one cycle — and no orphaned subscription survives.
*And* the control (`[CHA3-73]`) that re-links without dropping the prior subscription fails.

**BS-6 — A stale link's duplicate is a no-op** (`[CHA3-22]`, `[CHA3-24]`)
*Given* a plan in which peer A retains a link to departed peer B, and a duplicate fault
re-delivers gossip frames.
*When* the plan completes. *Then* the converged fold is unchanged and each receiver's
effective-delta count is unchanged by the duplicates.
*Corpus candidate*: `covers: [24-SET-02]` for the idempotence half only, without churn verbs.

**BS-7 — A late joiner catches up in bounded hops** (`[CHA3-14]`, `[CHA3-23]`)
*Given* a mesh that has gossiped a substantial script.
*When* a new replica joins mid-run.
*Then* its fold reaches the mesh fold, the hop count until it does is recorded, and the
count is bounded by the mesh diameter for that membership.
*Corpus candidate*: `covers: [42-REPL-05]` for the catch-up half.

**BS-8 — Join during a partition** (`[CHA3-04]`)
*Given* a joiner whose announcement is issued while an A→B partition is active.
*When* the partition heals and the plan completes.
*Then* the joiner converges with the mesh, and every peer's membership fold reaches the same
set — the transient disagreement 93 I-3 permits resolves, and is *recorded* while it lasts.

**BS-9 — No reachable peer means suspend, not evict** (`[CHA3-30]`, `[CHA3-31]`)
*Given* a replica whose peers are all partitioned away.
*When* an eviction is attempted.
*Then* `evict` returns false, the replica is suspended with its state retained, its
delivered-watermark row is **suspended and not closed**, and on heal it resumes and
converges. This is the arm that protects unique un-gossiped state.

**BS-10 — Clean departure advances stability; unclean freezes it, loudly** (`[CHA3-41]`,
`[CHA3-42]`)
*Given* a 3-peer mesh with the delivered-watermark stability read attached.
*When* a replica is cleanly evicted. *Then* stability advances past its closed row.
*When instead* a replica is crashed without evict.
*Then* stability freezes and the `Stall`-family notice is observed; a control asserts there
is no silent unfreeze. This is `96 §E3.6`'s scripted test, generated.

**BS-11 — The PN-0c wedge is detected** (`[CHA3-72]`)
*Given* a clean departure run with `closeDepartedRow = false`.
*When* the plan completes. *Then* the harness detects the wedge rather than tolerating it,
reusing the existing control seam rather than inventing one.

**BS-12 — Down to one replica** (`[CHA3-32]`, `[CHA3-61]`)
*Given* a plan that evicts replicas until one remains.
*When* departure of the last replica is attempted.
*Then* the kernel refuses (`evict` returns false, the replica suspends), the harness records
whether that replica held effective state present at no durable store, and reports it as the
last-replica condition. **No handoff is defined here** — the report is MEM2's input.

**BS-13 — Down to zero replicas** (`[CHA3-62]`)
*Given* a plan that crashes the last replica without evict.
*When* the plan completes. *Then* the harness records exactly what survives and where, and
states plainly that CHA3 defines no handoff and that "graceful last-replica handoff to
durable storage (G-25) vs accidental deletion" remains undesigned and owned by MEM2.

**BS-14 — Leader churn measures the split-brain window** (`[CHA3-50]`, `[CHA3-51]`,
`[CHA3-52]`)
*(single-writer sets only)* *Given* a single-writer replica set with a designated leader.
*When* the leader departs under a generated churn plan.
*Then* the harness reports the window during which more than one instance believes itself
leader, and whether any accepted write was lost or duplicated across the transition — as a
**measurement**, with no election implemented and no R1 direction chosen.

**BS-15 — Achieved churn/write overlap is reported** (`[CHA3-60]`)
*Given* a configuration requesting 50% of writes to land during in-flight churn.
*When* a sweep runs. *Then* the achieved overlap is reported per run; a
configured-50%/achieved-2% sweep is a red result, not a green one.

**BS-16 — Inert churn events and unknown targets** (`[CHA3-46]`, `[CHA3-47]`)
*Given* a plan naming a peer the graph does not contain, and separately a churn event
scheduled past quiescence.
*When* each runs. *Then* the first fails immediately naming the unknown peer and the known
set; the second is marked `fired=0` inert in the report.

**BS-17 — Exclusive payloads survive churn or fail the run** (`[CHA3-44]`)
*Given* a replicated graph carrying `Owned` payloads through a bridge.
*When* a churn plan with unclean departures runs over a seed sweep.
*Then* every exclusive payload is accounted — consumed, released, discharged or explicitly
dead-lettered — through CHA1's accounting, and any silent loss fails the run.

**BS-18 — Seeds are pinned, plans shrink** (`[CHA3-48]`)
*Given* a churn plan failing on seed `s`.
*When* shrinking runs to fixpoint. *Then* the artifact holds both the original and the
shrunk churn+fault plan, the shrunk plan still fails with the same check, and the seed field
is byte-identical in both. No seed is ever swapped for a friendlier one.

**BS-19 — The argument is written with its numbers** (`[CHA3-25]`, `[CHA3-81]`)
*Given* a completed sweep.
*When* the findings file is written. *Then* it states the bounded-gossip-hop reconciliation
argument in prose — duplicate and stale mesh links are safe by tag idempotence — with the
measured hop counts, subscription counts, stale-link counts and duplicate-absorption counts
that support it, citing G-45, and edits no spec, gap-table, concordance or plan document.

**BS-20 — A control that does not diverge fails the harness's self-test** (`[CHA3-74]`)
*Given* the four controls of §4.8.
*When* any fails to diverge. *Then* the harness fails its own self-test and the
corresponding property is reported unproven.

---

## 6. Scope boundaries

- **The rig is CHA1.** Faults, artifacts, replay, shrink, trace digest, dead-letter and
  exclusive accounting, reporting format. The plan's edge is `CHA3 depends on CHA1`, and
  CHA1 §6 names CHA3's half explicitly.
- **Last-replica handoff is MEM2.** G-45's second clause — "define graceful last-replica
  handoff to durable storage (G-25) vs accidental deletion" — is a **design** obligation
  and the plan assigns it to MEM2 ("G-45 churn-reconvergence + last-replica handoff |
  MEM1, CHA3"). CHA3 makes the condition observable and reachable (`[CHA3-32]`,
  `[CHA3-61]`, `[CHA3-62]`, BS-12, BS-13) and stops. `[CHA3-84]`.
- **Leader election is MEM1 (G-44).** 95 §R1 is research-gated and explicitly ranks its
  directions without choosing. CHA3 supplies R1's stated *actions* — simulate
  partition/heal/leader-crash, measure split-brain windows — as measurements only
  (`[CHA3-50]`…`[CHA3-52]`). It picks no direction and implements no election.
- **The stability read and its compaction are E3.5/E3.7.** `[CHA3-53]` supplies churn seeds
  to that harness; it does not build it. R13's completeness question is research-gated and
  is not answered here.
- **Any kernel change.** Evidence lane, test-only (`[CHA3-82]`). A divergence yields a
  shrunk counterexample, a pinned seed and a findings entry; the fix is admitted to the
  kernel lane per plan §4/§6.
- **Spec text.** The ask says "state the argument"; CHA3 states it in the lane findings
  file with its numbers (`[CHA3-81]`). Promoting it into `doc/spec/` and closing or
  narrowing the G-45 row is documentation maintenance for the integration pass, not this
  feature. `CONCORDANCE.md` is generated and must never be hand-edited.
- **Concord churn/fault verbs.** Schema-change-gated under `concord/schema/*.md`
  (`[CHA3-83]`). Flag candidates; stop.
- **C-9/C-11 reproductions are CHA2**; operator differential testing is ORA1/ORA2.
- **Interest-scoped and sharded replication beyond what churn touches.**
  `InterestScopedGossipTest`/`ShardedReplicationTest` cover their own ground; CHA3 varies
  interest/epoch only as a churn event (`[CHA3-01]`'s `Reassign`).
- **Performance.** BEN1/BEN2. Churn sweeps may be slow.
- **Multi-JVM.** Excluded from the replay guarantee by `[CHA1-40]`; CHA3 runs single-JVM
  and deterministic.

---

## 7. Suggested task decomposition

List only — **do not create these as beads from this description**.

1. **Churn plan model and generator.** `ChurnPlan`, the four departure modes, join/rejoin/
   reassign events, step-indexed activation, composition with CHA1 fault plans, config
   surface, one-seed derivation. Realizes `[CHA3-01]`…`[CHA3-07]`, `[CHA3-60]`, BS-15, BS-16.
2. **The reconvergence property.** Batch reference over accepted ops, composition with
   `ReplicaConvergence.liveRefs()`, the departed-stream exclusion, late-joiner equality.
   Realizes `[CHA3-10]`…`[CHA3-14]`, `[CHA3-40]`, BS-1, BS-2, BS-7, BS-8.
3. **Bounded-gossip-hop instrumentation.** Hop counting, subscription counting on both
   observables, stale-link counting, duplicate-absorption counting, and the per-run report.
   Realizes `[CHA3-20]`…`[CHA3-25]`, `[CHA3-43]`, BS-5, BS-6.
4. **Departure-gate and watermark behaviour.** Suspend-not-evict under no reachable peer,
   watermark suspend vs close, clean vs unclean stability behaviour, the PN-0c control.
   Realizes `[CHA3-30]`, `[CHA3-31]`, `[CHA3-41]`, `[CHA3-42]`, `[CHA3-72]`, BS-9, BS-10, BS-11.
5. **Controls and self-test.** Suppressed final catch-up, disabled departed-stream rule,
   accumulating rejoin, and the fail-if-a-control-does-not-diverge self-test. Realizes
   `[CHA3-70]`…`[CHA3-74]`, BS-3, BS-4, BS-20.
6. **Last-replica probe.** Down-to-one and down-to-zero plans with their recorded
   observations and the explicit "no handoff defined here" statement. Realizes
   `[CHA3-32]`, `[CHA3-61]`, `[CHA3-62]`, BS-12, BS-13.
7. **Single-writer churn measurement (optional, R1).** Leader departure, split-brain window
   measurement, lost/duplicated-write accounting, with no election implemented. Realizes
   `[CHA3-50]`…`[CHA3-53]`, BS-14.
8. **Findings, pinned seeds, hand-off.** The written argument with its numbers, pinned
   seeds, the shrinker's churn-plan moves, and the MEM2 hand-off note. Realizes
   `[CHA3-25]`, `[CHA3-48]`, `[CHA3-49]`, `[CHA3-80]`, `[CHA3-81]`, BS-18, BS-19.

---

## 8. Verification

```bash
./gradlew :testkit:test --tests 'civictech.testkit.dst.churn.*'              # the harness's own self-tests
./gradlew :testkit:test --tests 'civictech.testkit.dst.churn.ChurnControlsTest'  # BS-3, BS-4, BS-11, BS-20 — blocking
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.replication.ChurnReconvergenceTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.replication.GossipLinkIdempotenceTest'   # unchanged
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.replication.MemberDepartureFrontierTest' # unchanged
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.replication.ReplicatedSessionTest'       # unchanged
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.replication.SingleWriterReplicationTest' # unchanged
./gradlew :kernel:test
./gradlew :concord:test                                                     # unchanged; no scenario added
./gradlew :demo:shopping:test                                               # convergence demo unchanged
./gradlew test                                                              # repository-wide gate
```

What constitutes proof:

- **Churn sweeps** over a seed range asserting reconvergence on every seed, with density
  reported `N of M` (`[CHA3-80]`) — never first-failure abort.
- **The four controls** (`[CHA3-70]`…`[CHA3-73]`) each provably diverging, and the self-test
  that fails when one does not (`[CHA3-74]`). A green churn sweep without these is not
  evidence and the feature is not delivered.
- **The measured argument**: hop counts, subscription counts, stale-link counts and
  duplicate-absorption counts written to the findings file alongside the prose statement of
  the bounded-gossip-hop reconciliation argument, citing G-45 (`[CHA3-25]`, `[CHA3-81]`).
- **Named behaviour tests** for BS-1 … BS-20.
- **Per-seed outcome parity** for the existing replication tests: `GossipLinkIdempotenceTest`,
  `MemberDepartureFrontierTest`, `ReplicatedSessionTest` and
  `SingleWriterReplicationTest` unchanged in outcome.
- The report must name which seed ranges ran, the achieved churn/write overlap, every inert
  churn event, and every property left unproven with its reason.

No kernel `main` edits. No corpus scenarios. No `doc/spec/`, `91-gap-analysis.md`,
`CONCORDANCE.md` or plan edits. No generated/build output in the diff.

---

## 9. Risks / open questions

1. **"Bounded" needs a definition before it can be asserted.** Mesh diameter for a full
   mesh is 1, but during churn the effective topology is transiently not a full mesh (a
   late-learned peer has fewer links). `[CHA3-23]`'s bound must be stated against the
   *membership the joiner's peers actually knew at that step*, not the eventual set.
   **Open question:** is the honest bound "one hop per membership-fold generation" or
   "bounded by the number of peers that had learned the joiner"? Decide in task 3, and if
   neither is defensible, report the measured distribution and say the bound is unproven —
   do not assert a bound the data does not support.
2. **Churn determinism.** Crash faults require deterministic host rebuild (CHA1 risk 5:
   "crash faults require the consumer to supply a deterministic rebuild function"). Churn
   multiplies that: a *rejoining* replica must derive the same `CellRef` and the same
   ref-derived tag source, or the mesh sees a new member rather than a returning one. If
   the harness cannot guarantee this for an arbitrary consumer graph, say so — the honest
   form is a required rebuild function, not a harness that silently produces a different
   member.
3. **The convergence property needs a batch reference, and ORA2 is building one for the
   tagged family.** `[CHA3-11]` demands "equals a batch reference over accepted
   operations", which for `OrMapCell` means dot-order semantics — exactly ORA2's model.
   **Open question:** should CHA3 depend on ORA2's reference for tagged meshes, or carry a
   local set-only reference and defer tagged churn? Recommendation: set-only and
   `PnCounterCell` first (both have trivial references), tagged meshes as a later join with
   ORA2. Both features touch `ReplicaConvergence`; coordinate the seam before task 2.
4. **`[CHA3-42]`'s `Stall`-family notice may not exist yet.** `96 §E3.6` (c) describes it
   as part of E3.6, which is unbuilt. If the notice is absent, BS-10's second half cannot be
   asserted and the honest outcome is a `DISPUTES.md`-style filed record plus a findings
   note that the property becomes checkable when E3.6 lands — not a weakened assertion that
   "stability froze" without observing the notice.
5. **Single-writer churn may be premature.** `[CHA3-50]`…`[CHA3-52]` are optional-feature
   requirements because `SingleWriterReplication` ships with *explicit* failover (95 §R1:
   "the core ships with explicit failover"). Measuring a split-brain window presumes
   something that can produce one. If explicit-only failover makes the measurement vacuous,
   report that as the finding and leave the requirement dormant until MEM1.
6. **Overlap with MEM2's scope.** `[CHA3-32]`/`[CHA3-61]`/`[CHA3-62]` sit right at the
   boundary. The rule this feature holds to: CHA3 **observes and reports**; MEM2 **defines
   and implements**. A CHA3 task that starts proposing a handoff mechanism has crossed the
   line.
7. **Achieved overlap, not configured overlap.** As with any generative harness, the
   dominant silent failure is a configuration that never realises the interesting
   interleaving. `[CHA3-60]` exists because of it; treat a low achieved overlap as red.
8. **Corpus pressure.** `[42-REPL-04]`, `[42-REPL-05]`, `[42-REPL-06]` and `[24-SET-02]` are
   honest `covers:` targets, but the scenario language has no churn verbs. Do not smuggle a
   schema change in (`[CHA3-83]`); `42-REPL-DEPART-01.yaml` already covers `[42-REPL-06]`
   for the single orderly departure and CHA3 cites rather than duplicates it.
design:
# CHA3 — design decisions and alternatives considered

## D0. The ask is two clauses, and only one of them is this feature

G-45's proposal text (identical at `doc/spec/40-distribution/42-replication.md:293-296`,
`doc/spec/50-development-process/52-verification.md:57-62`, and
`doc/spec/90-roadmap/91-gap-analysis.md:96`):

> State the bounded-gossip-hop reconciliation argument (duplicate/stale mesh links safe by
> tag idempotence) with a generative membership-churn harness (R1, 95); define graceful
> last-replica handoff to durable storage (G-25) vs accidental deletion.

- **Clause 1** — argument, evidenced by a harness. CHA3's whole content. The harness is
  the evidence; the "statement" lands in the lane findings file with its measured numbers
  (`[CHA3-25]`, `[CHA3-81]`), not in `doc/spec/` — promoting it and narrowing the G-45 row
  is documentation maintenance for the integration pass (milestone plan §6).
- **Clause 2** — a *design* obligation, assigned by the plan to **MEM2** ("G-45
  churn-reconvergence + last-replica handoff | MEM1, CHA3"). CHA3 makes the last-replica
  condition reachable and observable (`[CHA3-32]`, `[CHA3-61]`, `[CHA3-62]`) and defines
  nothing (`[CHA3-84]`).

The "(R1, 95)" sub-clause is likewise bounded: 95 §R1 is research-gated and its *actions*
are simulation and measurement. CHA3 performs those actions (`[CHA3-50]`…`[CHA3-52]`) and
picks no direction. Election is MEM1/G-44.

## D1. A feature under CHA1, not an epic

CHA1 §6 states the split verbatim: CHA1 "must make churn **expressible** … but ships no
churn generator, no reconvergence property, and no last-replica-handoff work." CHA3 adds
a generator, a property and instrumentation on top of CHA1's fault plane — a widening of
an existing rig, not a new one. `[CHA3-07]` makes the no-reinvention rule a requirement.

## D2. Compose with `ReplicaConvergence`; never reimplement membership

`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/verify/ReplicaConvergence.kt` already carries the
departed-stream rule — `liveRefs() = registry.replicasOf(logicalId) ∩ folds.keys`, so
`converged()` only requires agreement among live membership. That *is* `[42-REPL-06]`'s
harness half, already built (W3.3). A churn harness that filtered membership itself would
diverge from the kernel's own definition of "live" at exactly the moments churn makes
interesting. `[CHA3-12]` forbids it.

Note the coupling with ORA2: ORA2's convergence oracle also composes with
`ReplicaConvergence` (it supplies the batch half the invariant structurally lacks).
Both features must agree on that seam — see §9 risk 3.

## D3. What `ReplicaConvergence` cannot see, and why the argument needs its own instruments

`GossipLinkIdempotenceTest`'s KDoc states the trap precisely: *"Membership convergence
cannot see this: the mergeable merge is idempotent, so duplicated delivery still
converges. Only the subscription count exposes it"* — one disconnect/reconnect cycle adds
one orphaned consumer, and "every cycle would add one, unbounded". A churn harness that
only asserts convergence would be *green on an unbounded leak*.

Hence §2.3's four instruments — hop count, subscription count, stale-link count,
duplicate-absorption count — and `[CHA3-25]`'s requirement that they be **reported**, not
merely asserted. "Bounded" is exactly the word the gap uses; the harness has to produce
the number behind it. `[CHA3-21]` checks both observables the existing test checks (the
outlet's consumer map *and* the port's `LinkSupport` record), because either alone can
miss a half-orphaned attachment.

## D4. Four departure modes, because the kernel distinguishes four

`Replication.evict(cell, host, closeDepartedRow = true)` has two arms — refuse-and-suspend
when `replicasOf(id) − {local}` is empty, versus suspend → final push-catch-up → despawn →
conditionally close the watermark row — and a control seam (`closeDepartedRow = false`,
the PN-0c control `MemberDepartureFrontierTest` already uses). A crash bypasses all of it.
`96 §E3.6` (b)/(c) then splits the *consequences*: clean departure closes the row so
stability advances; partition-suspend must **not** close (the frozen row is correct);
unclean departure leaves it frozen and must surface a `Stall`-family notice, "**not**
worked around". A three-mode generator would collapse distinctions the spec makes.
Hence `[CHA3-03]`'s four.

## D5. Controls are blocking, and one of them targets the check itself

Four controls (`[CHA3-70]`…`[CHA3-73]`): suppressed final catch-up (proves reconvergence
can detect lost state), disabled departed-stream rule (proves `[CHA3-13]` is not vacuous —
a check that always passes because it excludes everything is worse than no check),
accumulating rejoin (proves `[CHA3-43]` fires), and the existing PN-0c wedge. `[CHA3-74]`
mirrors CHA1's `[CHA1-63]`: a control that does not diverge means the property is
**unproven** and the harness fails its own self-test.

The second one deserves emphasis. `[CHA3-13]` says a departed replica's frozen fold is
excluded from the judgement. An implementation that excluded *too much* would pass every
churn sweep trivially. BS-4 is the guard.

## D6. Set-only reference first; tagged meshes as a later join with ORA2

`[CHA3-11]` demands equality with a batch reference, and for `OrMapCell` that reference is
dot-order semantics — precisely ORA2's `DotModel`. Rather than build a second one,
recommend: `SetCell` and `PnCounterCell` meshes first (trivial references), tagged meshes
as a scheduled join once ORA2's model exists. Recorded as an open question rather than a
decision, because it changes what BS-1 can cover.

## D7. Honest reporting beats a flattering bound

Two places where the specification deliberately declines to assert:

- `[CHA3-23]`'s hop bound. During churn the effective topology is transiently not a full
  mesh, so "diameter 1" is wrong mid-plan. If neither candidate bound is defensible against
  the data, report the measured distribution and say the bound is unproven (§9 risk 1).
- `[CHA3-42]`'s `Stall`-family notice is part of the unbuilt `96 §E3.6`. If it is absent,
  BS-10's second half is not assertable, and the honest outcome is a filed record plus a
  findings note — not "stability froze" dressed up as the full property (§9 risk 4).

`[CHA3-49]` generalises this: an uncheckable property is filed in
`concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md`, never weakened into a passing scenario.

## D8. Seeds are pinned; only plans shrink

`AGENTS.md`: "Do not replace a discovered failing seed with a friendlier seed."
`[CHA3-48]` restates it for churn and constrains the shrinker to reduce the **churn plan
and fault plan only**, holding the seed constant — inheriting CHA1's `[CHA1-35]`
discipline rather than inventing a churn-specific one.

## D9. Dependency wiring

Wired: **CHA3 → CHA1** (`computenet-umx`).
Consumers, unwired here: **MEM2** (G-45 churn-reconvergence + last-replica handoff) and
**MEM1** (G-44 epoch-claim election) — neither has a bead id yet. When MEM2 is filed, wire
`CHA3 → MEM2` and hand it BS-12/BS-13's recorded observations as its design input.
Soft consumers, no edge: **R13** (95, churn seeds for the E3.5 stability harness) and
**E3.6** (the generated form of its scripted 3-peer test).
acceptance_criteria:
Accepted when every requirement id below is realized by a named test and the feature is verifiable via ./gradlew :testkit:test --tests 'civictech.testkit.dst.churn.*' plus ./gradlew :kernel:test and ./gradlew test.

REUSE (blocking): [CHA3-07] — no fault injector, artifact format, replay mechanism or shrinker of its own; partition, crash, journal, restart, duplicate, trace digest, dead-letter accounting and exclusive-payload accounting all come from CHA1.

GENERATOR: [CHA3-01] through [CHA3-06] and [CHA3-60] — seed-reproducible churn plans of join/depart/rejoin/reassign over a logical id; all four departure modes (clean evict, evict without closing the row, unclean crash, partition-suspend) labelled per event; churn composable with in-flight partitions; ACHIEVED churn/write overlap reported, not merely configured (BS-15, BS-16).

RECONVERGENCE: [CHA3-10] through [CHA3-14] and [CHA3-40] — every live replica converges to an equal fold AND that fold equals a batch reference over accepted ops; live membership determined through replicasOf composed with ReplicaConvergence.liveRefs(), never reimplemented; the departed replica's frozen fold excluded, not counted as divergence; late joiner indistinguishable from an original member (BS-1, BS-2, BS-7, BS-8).

THE BOUNDED-GOSSIP-HOP ARGUMENT: [CHA3-20] through [CHA3-25], [CHA3-43], [CHA3-81] — subscription count per replica bounded by live membership and checked on BOTH the outlet consumer map and the port link record; no orphaned subscription survives a rejoin cycle; stale-link duplicates leave effective-delta counts unchanged; join hop count recorded; all four instruments reported per run; and the argument written in prose WITH its measured numbers to an append-only lane findings file citing G-45 (BS-5, BS-6, BS-19).

DEPARTURE GATES: [CHA3-30], [CHA3-31], [CHA3-41], [CHA3-42] — no reachable peer means suspend with state retained and the watermark row suspended NOT closed; clean departure advances stability past the closed row; unclean departure freezes it AND surfaces the Stall-family notice, with no silent unfreeze tolerated (BS-9, BS-10).

LAST-REPLICA PROBE, OBSERVED NOT DESIGNED: [CHA3-32], [CHA3-61], [CHA3-62], [CHA3-84] — down-to-one and down-to-zero plans record the kernel's refusal and what state survives, and state plainly that CHA3 defines no handoff and implements no election. Defining graceful last-replica handoff is MEM2; election is MEM1/G-44. A CHA3 deliverable proposing a handoff mechanism is a rejection (BS-12, BS-13).

R1 MEASUREMENT (optional): [CHA3-50] through [CHA3-53] — leader churn measures the split-brain window and lost/duplicated writes as MEASUREMENTS only; no R1 direction chosen; churn seeds handed to the E3.5 stability harness rather than duplicating it (BS-14).

DISCRIMINATION (blocking — a green churn sweep without these is not evidence): [CHA3-70] [CHA3-71] [CHA3-72] [CHA3-73] [CHA3-74] — suppressed final catch-up fails on at least one seed; disabling the departed-stream rule fails, proving the exclusion is not vacuous; the existing PN-0c closeDepartedRow=false wedge is detected; accumulating rejoin fires; and a control that does not diverge fails the harness self-test (BS-3, BS-4, BS-11, BS-20).

HONESTY AND REGRESSION: [CHA3-44] through [CHA3-49], [CHA3-80], [CHA3-82], [CHA3-83] — exclusive payloads accounted through CHA1's check; unexplained dead letters fail the run; unknown churn targets fail fast; inert events marked fired=0; discovered seeds pinned and never replaced, narrowed or reordered with the shrinker reducing plans only; uncheckable properties filed in concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md, never weakened into a passing scenario; sweeps report N of M density; zero kernel main edits; zero concord scenarios and no schema change (BS-17, BS-18).

Green, with per-seed outcome parity for GossipLinkIdempotenceTest, MemberDepartureFrontierTest, ReplicatedSessionTest and SingleWriterReplicationTest: ./gradlew :testkit:test, ./gradlew :kernel:test, ./gradlew :concord:test (unchanged), ./gradlew :demo:shopping:test, ./gradlew test. No doc/spec, 91-gap-analysis.md, CONCORDANCE.md or plan edits.

# CHA2 — Reproduction suite for the decided-but-divergent rules (C-9, C-11; C-12 adjudicated closed)

Milestone-plan row (`computenet-milestone-plan.md` §1, Evidence lanes), verbatim:

> | CHA2 | Reproduction suite for the decided-but-divergent rules: C-9 (effect replay), C-11 (shadow drops exclusives), C-12 (RESTART aliasing) | CHA1 | KFX |

Filed as a **feature under CHA1** (`computenet-umx`): it builds no rig. Every injector it
needs — crash mid-drain/mid-wave, journal mutation, arbitrary-prefix restart,
processed-frontier rollback, seeded replay, shrinking, dead-letter and exclusive-payload
accounting — is a CHA1 deliverable (`[CHA1-17]`…`[CHA1-22]`, `[CHA1-30]`…`[CHA1-40]`,
`[CHA1-52]`, `[CHA1-53]`). CHA2 supplies *verdicts and standing tests*, not machinery.

---

## 0. The stale-row finding, verified first

The plan row names three divergences. **Verified against `doc/spec/` and the kernel in
`main` on 2026-08-08, the row is stale on all three — but in three different ways, and
only one of them means "nothing to do".** This section is the feature's first
deliverable, because a reproduction suite that manufactures failures to match a stale
planning row is worse than no suite.

### C-12 — genuinely closed. No reproduction will be written.

`doc/spec/90-roadmap/91-gap-analysis.md:20` now reads, in full, that the divergence claim
was *"**stale**, transcribed from the M3.5 prose rather than the code (adjudicated D-C12)"*
and the row's status is **"Resolved (W2.1 core, adjudicated + conformance-covered D-C12)"**:
the supervision RESTART branch bumps the host-held generation, mints a fresh per-epoch
`sourceId` on every outlet, restores the checkpoint, and emits `ReBaseline(supersedes,

## 1. Ambition / Why

A "decided-but-divergent" rule is the most dangerous entry in the spec ledger: the design
is settled, so nobody re-argues it; the code disagrees, so nobody's tests catch it; and
the gap row ages until someone re-derives the whole argument. C-12 already demonstrated
the full failure mode — a divergence recorded in four spec sites, a test whose KDoc
overstated its own coverage, and an adjudication (D-C12) that concluded the *prose* was
wrong, not the code. C-9 and C-11 are now in precisely the same state, one adjudication
behind.

CHA2 makes the ledger *executable*:

- Every remaining residual becomes a **named, standing test** that fails for a stated
  reason, not a paragraph.
- Every rule found to be **already true** becomes a passing test plus a written finding
  that the gap row is stale — evidence a later integration pass can act on
  (milestone plan §6: "A periodic single-agent integration pass is the only writer of the
  gap table"; CHA2 writes findings, never the table).
- KFX receives failing tests it can flip green, which is the plan's edge
  (`CHA2 -.failing tests.-> KFX`, §2) and the reason §5 ranks CHA1→CHA2 fifth: *"Failing
  tests ready before KFX enters the lane."*

Note the plan's KFX row — "C-9 fix + minimal G-59 processed-frontier for `Effectful`" —
is stale in the same direction: the minimal frontier landed. CHA2's findings are what
lets KFX be re-scoped onto the residual that actually exists (source identity under
replay) instead of rebuilding a mechanism already in `main`. That re-scoping is a finding
CHA2 reports; **CHA2 does not edit the plan.**

### 3.3 The expected-failure discipline

This is the unusual part of the feature and it must be specified, not improvised. A test
that is *expected to fail until a kernel fix lands* has to satisfy four constraints at
once: it must actually run, it must not redden the build gate, it must not be ignorable
into oblivion, and it must **fail loudly the moment it starts passing**.

The mechanism:

- Each reproduction is a JUnit 5 test annotated with a project-local
  `@ExpectedFailure(reason, owner, filedAs)` meta-annotation carrying (a) a one-line reason,
  (b) the owning work item (`KFX` or `SEC1`), and (c) the `DISPUTES.md` / findings anchor.
- The annotation is realized as a JUnit 5 **extension**, not `@Disabled` and not
  `@Ignore`: the test body executes on every build. The extension inverts the verdict —
  an assertion failure whose message matches the recorded signature is reported as
  *passed-as-expected*; **any other** failure (a different assertion, an exception, a
  timeout, a budget exhaustion) is reported as a **failure**, because an
  expected-failure that fails for a new reason is a new defect.
- **The flip is the point.** If the body *passes*, the extension fails the build with
  "expected failure now passes — the fix landed; remove the annotation, keep the test,
  and update the findings entry". This is what turns a reproduction into KFX's acceptance
  test rather than a permanently-yellow marker.
- Every reproduction records the CHA1 replay artifact path and the copy-pasteable replay
  command (`[CHA1-50]`, `[CHA1-51]`), so a reader can reproduce the failure outside the
  suite.
- A reproduction is **never** softened to pass. `AGENTS.md` is explicit; the correct
  escape hatch when a residual turns out not to be checkable is a `DISPUTES.md` entry.
- A reproduction is **never** re-seeded to a friendlier seed
  (`AGENTS.md`; `[CHA1-35]`, `[CHA1-38]`). The shrinker reduces the fault plan only.

`@Disabled` was rejected: a disabled test does not execute, so it cannot detect that the
defect was fixed, and it decays into permanent dead code. A "soft assertion that logs" was
rejected for the same reason plus the worse one — it makes the suite green whether or not
the kernel is correct.

  is the failing test plus the filed record; the fix is KFX's (or SEC1's).
- `[CHA2-51]` The suite shall add no concord scenario and no corpus schema change; it may
  only **extend** the existing `DISPUTES.md` C-9/G-59 boundary entry with its reproduction
  ids. *(`concord/schema/*.md` single-writer, schema-change-gated; CHA1 §6)*
- `[CHA2-52]` The suite shall not regress `./gradlew :concord:test`, `:kernel:test`,
  `:demo:exchange:test` or the repository gate.

## 5. Behaviour specifications

Each becomes one named test. `covers:` notes mark concord-corpus candidates; where a
scenario does not belong there, the reason is stated. Note that the concord scenario
language has **no fault verbs** (CHA1 §6 — `Step.kt`/`Driver` carry no partition/crash/drop
verb, and adding them is schema-change-gated), so most CHA2 scenarios cannot be corpus
scenarios today regardless of merit.

**BS-1 — The C-9 core holds: frontier suppression on replay** (`[CHA2-10]`, `[CHA2-02]`)
*Given* a durable host with a journaled `Effectful` sink that has applied `(s, 1..7)`, and
a **volatile** source (discarded by the crash).
*When* the host crashes mid-drain and recovers from its journal.
*Then* the external effect log is unchanged in size across replay, and advances only for
post-recovery invocations. This test **passes**, and its purpose is to pin the landed
mechanism. *Corpus*: already covered by `concord/corpus/15-durability/DUR-REPLAY-01.yaml`
(`covers: [24-DUR-05]`) — CHA2 cites it and adds the adversarial generalisation locally.

**BS-2 — Arbitrary-prefix restart never double-fires** (`[CHA2-11]`)
*Given* a durable host whose journal holds `R` records after a scripted effect workload.
*When* the host is restarted from prefix `k` for every `k` in `0..R`.
*Then* for every `k` each `(sourceId, counter)` appears at most once in the external effect
log. Any failing `k` is reported with its own CHA1 artifact and pinned.
*Not a corpus scenario*: needs `[CHA1-21]`'s prefix sweep, which has no scenario verb.

**BS-3 — Frontier rollback: the verdict CHA1 deferred** (`[CHA2-12]`)
*Given* a journaled `Effectful` sink that has applied up to `(s, 7)`.
*When* the frontier is rolled back to `(s, 3)` and the host restarts from the full journal.
*Then* invocations 4..7 are re-delivered, and the test records the observed outcome:
exactly-once (the decided rule holds under rollback) **or** a reproduced C-9-class
re-fire. Whichever it is, the finding is written and, if it re-fires, the test is an
expected failure owned by KFX. **The test must not assume the answer**; CHA1's BS-11 hands
this verdict here precisely because it is unknown until run.

**BS-4 — A journaled source feeding an effectful sink double-fires** (`[CHA2-13]`)
*Given* a **journaled** source cell whose emissions carry the outlet's random per-instance
`sourceId`, feeding an `Effectful` sink on the same host, both journaled.
*When* the host crashes and recovers, replaying the source's frames.
*Then* the sink's restored frontier cannot match the re-minted `sourceId`, and the effect
fires a second time. **Expected failure, owner KFX**, signature recorded, anchored to
`DISPUTES.md:511`. Flipping this green requires ref-derived (or output-mode) wave identity
for spontaneously-emitting sources — which is what the DISPUTES entry's "Resolves" clause
already names.
*Not a corpus scenario*: `DUR-REPLAY-01` deliberately keeps the data-recovery and
effect-once paths as two independent subgraphs *because* of this boundary; folding them is
the fix's job, not the suite's.

**BS-5 — Baseline-stamped replay at/behind the frontier** (`[CHA2-14]`)
*Given* a PN-2 replay in which frames are stamped `MessageContext.baseline`.
*When* such a frame arrives at an `Effectful` inlet at or behind the restored frontier.
*Then* the test records whether the frontier check exempts baselines. If it does not and
that is reachable, the reproduction is an expected failure; if it is unreachable in-order,
the finding says so and no test is manufactured (`[CHA2-46]`).

**BS-6 — Torn tail vs. corrupted record, with effects** (`[CHA2-15]`)
*Given* a `FileJournal` with `R` records behind an effect sink.
*When* the tail is truncated mid-record. *Then* replay drops exactly the torn record,
recovery completes, and no effect fires for it.
*When instead* record `i` is corrupted. *Then* `RecoveryIncomplete(recordIndex = i,
total = R)` is raised, no effect fires for any record beyond `i`, and the caller does not
treat the partial replay as complete.

**BS-7 — The C-11 core holds: discharge at a shadow-suppressed inlet** (`[CHA2-20]`,
`[CHA2-02]`)
*Given* a shadowed `Effectful` cell with `Owned<T>` and `Leased<T>` inlets.
*When* payloads are pushed at both.
*Then* each `Owned` is taken exactly once and each `Leased` released exactly once, and the
sink's own handler never runs. Passes; pins `ShadowOwnershipTest`'s guarantee under the
rig. *Corpus candidate*: `covers: [23-*]` if a discharging-sink id exists; if none does,
file the missing id in `DISPUTES.md` rather than minting one.

**BS-8 — A nested exclusive escapes the discharging proxy** (`[CHA2-21]`)
*Given* a `@Contract` method whose parameter is a data class with an `Owned<T>` field
(not a `Map`/`Iterable`/`Array`).
*When* it crosses a shadow-suppressed discharging proxy.
*Then* the `Owned` is never taken — CHA1's exclusive accounting (`[CHA1-53]`) fails the run.
**Expected failure, owner KFX** (or whoever carries the 93 I-6/I-8 exclusive-bit widening),
anchored to `12-ports.md`'s "decided … unimplemented" sentence.

**BS-9 — A shadowed non-`Effectful` cell is not suppressed at all** (`[CHA2-22]`)
*Given* a cell that does **not** implement `Effectful` but serves an inlet whose contract
is declared effect-carrying.
*When* it is spawned through `Shadow.spawn`.
*Then* `spawn`'s `if (cell is Effectful)` guard skips suppression entirely and the effect
fires. **Expected failure**, anchored to 93 I-17 and the G-32 row's "landed cell-granularity
NoOp diverges".

**BS-10 — A denied boundary invocation drops its exclusive silently** (`[CHA2-23]`,
`[CHA2-26]`)
*Given* a mediated/composite boundary with a `BoundaryPolicy` that denies, and an inbound
invocation carrying `Owned`.
*When* the denial fires.
*Then* the payload is neither taken, released, discharged nor dead-lettered — CHA1's
exclusive accounting fails the run. **Expected failure, owner SEC1**, cross-referenced to
the KHYG finding. CHA2 does not fix it and does not restate SEC1's specification.

**BS-11 — Sanitizing paths are the baseline** (`[CHA2-25]`)
*Given* an invocation carrying `Owned`/`Leased` that the ADMIT tier drops, and one that is
dead-lettered.
*When* each fires. *Then* the payload is discharged in both cases, with the drop counted
against the tier's own accounting — establishing that "denied ⇒ discharged" is the kernel's
own standard, so BS-10 is a divergence and not a design choice.

**BS-12 — Missing descriptor is loud** (`[CHA2-24]`)
*Given* a contract with no generated `ContractRegistry` descriptor.
*When* a discharging proxy is requested. *Then* it fails naming the class — it does not
degrade to a plain NoOp that would silently drop exclusives.

**BS-13 — C-12 is closed, and the suite says so with evidence** (`[CHA2-30]`,
`[CHA2-31]`, `[CHA2-32]`, `[CHA2-33]`)
*Given* the plan row naming C-12 as decided-but-divergent.
*When* the suite is built. *Then* it contains **no** C-12 reproduction; its recorded
finding cites `91-gap-analysis.md:20` and `:115`, the four corrected spec sites,
`D-C12.md`, `21-REBASE-01.yaml` and `DISPUTES.md:360`; and it states explicitly that the
G-43/G-42 residuals are out of scope. *Not a test of the kernel* — a documentation-of-record
assertion, which is why it asserts over checked-in artifacts rather than behaviour.

**BS-14 — An expected failure that starts passing breaks the build** (`[CHA2-44]`)
*Given* a reproduction tagged expected-failure.
*When* the underlying defect is fixed (simulated in the suite's own self-test by a stubbed
passing body).
*Then* the build fails with the "remove the annotation, keep the test" message. This is the
test that makes the whole discipline load-bearing.

**BS-15 — An expected failure that changes signature breaks the build** (`[CHA2-43]`)
*Given* a reproduction whose recorded signature is a specific assertion message.
*When* the body instead throws a different exception or exhausts the step budget.
*Then* the build fails rather than reporting expected-as-passed.

**BS-16 — Expected failures are visible without reading source** (`[CHA2-45]`)
*Given* a run with N standing expected failures.
*When* the suite finishes. *Then* the report lists each with its reason and owner, and the
count, so the residual ledger is an artifact rather than folklore.

**BS-17 — Seeds are pinned, never rotated** (`[CHA2-47]`)
*Given* a reproduction discovered on seed `s`.
*When* a later change alters failure density.
*Then* `s` remains pinned; the shrinker reduced only the fault plan; the seed field is
byte-identical in the original and shrunk artifacts.

---

## 6. Scope boundaries

- **The rig itself is CHA1.** Every injector, the artifact format, replay, shrink,
  dead-letter and exclusive accounting, and the reporting format. The plan's edge is
  `CHA2 depends on CHA1`; CHA1 §6 names CHA2's half explicitly.
- **Any kernel fix is KFX** (`CHA2 -.failing tests.-> KFX`, plan §2). CHA2 produces failing
  tests and filed records. It does not patch `ManagedHost`, `HostDurability`, `Proxy`,
  `Evolution`, or the KSP exclusive-bit scan.
- **The `BoundaryPolicy` denial fix is SEC1**, under the KHYG epic — not KFX and not here.
  `[CHA2-23]`/BS-10 reproduce and route; they do not specify the fix.
- **C-12 is closed.** No reproduction, no expected failure, no manufactured divergence
  (`[CHA2-30]`). Its residuals (G-43 freshest-checkpoint tiers and pull-merge direction;
  G-42 epoch/generation reclamation) belong to those G-items.
- **Membership churn is CHA3**; ORA-style operator differential testing is ORA1/ORA2. CHA2
  touches neither.
- **Concord scenario-language fault verbs** are schema-change-gated under
  `concord/schema/*.md` and are not this feature. CHA2 may only extend the existing
  `DISPUTES.md` C-9/G-59 boundary entry (`[CHA2-51]`).
- **The gap table and the concordance matrix.** Milestone plan §6: a periodic single-agent
  integration pass is their only writer. CHA2 writes lane findings
  (`[CHA2-03]`) — including the finding that the C-9, C-11 and KFX rows are stale — and
  stops there.
- **Widening `internal` visibility.** `ManagedHost.replayAsBaseline` stays `internal`;
  CHA2 lives in `:kernel`'s test source set instead (`[CHA2-05]`, CHA1 risk 3).
- **Performance.** BEN1/BEN2. The suite may be slow.
- **Multi-JVM.** `JvmPeer`-driven runs are excluded from the replay guarantee
  (`[CHA1-40]`); CHA2 reproductions are single-JVM and deterministic.

## 8. Verification

```bash
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.repro.*'                     # the suite
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.repro.ExpectedFailureSelfTest' # BS-14, BS-15 — blocking
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.repro.EffectReplayReproTest'   # BS-1..BS-6
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.repro.ExclusiveDischargeReproTest' # BS-7..BS-12
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.durability.EffectfulRecoveryTest'  # unchanged
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.evolve.ShadowOwnershipTest'        # unchanged
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.host.RestartReBaselineTest'        # unchanged (C-12 cited)
./gradlew :testkit:test                                                     # CHA1's rig, unchanged
./gradlew :kernel:test
./gradlew :concord:test                                                     # unchanged; no scenario added
./gradlew :demo:exchange:test                                               # composition gate unchanged
./gradlew test                                                              # repository-wide gate
```

What constitutes proof:

- **The build is green** with every standing expected failure still failing for its
  recorded reason (`[CHA2-42]`).
- **The self-tests** (BS-14, BS-15) prove the discipline is load-bearing: an
  expected-failure that starts passing, or fails differently, breaks the build. Without
  these the whole suite is decoration.
- **The pinned-mechanism tests** (BS-1, BS-7, BS-11) pass, proving the landed halves of
  C-9 and C-11 are actually pinned and not merely assumed.
- **The reproductions** fail with recorded, replayable CHA1 artifacts and copy-pasteable
  replay commands.
- **The findings file** states, with file:line evidence, that the C-9 and C-11 gap rows and
  the KFX plan row are stale, and that C-12 is closed — without editing any of them.
- The report names exactly which tests ran, which expected failures stand, and their
  owners (`[CHA2-45]`).

No kernel `main` edits. No corpus scenarios. No `doc/spec/`, `CONCORDANCE.md` or plan edits.
No generated/build output in the diff.

---

## 9. Risks / open questions

1. **The plan row is stale and this feature says so.** The largest risk is that a reviewer
   expects three failing tests and receives two reproductions plus an adjudication. §0
   exists to make that legible. The alternative — manufacturing a C-12 failure — is
   forbidden by `AGENTS.md`'s authority order and by the D-C12 adjudication itself.
2. **KFX's scope moves as a consequence.** The plan's KFX row ("C-9 fix + minimal G-59
   processed-frontier") describes work already in `main`; the residual KFX should actually
   fix is source identity under replay. CHA2 **reports** this; re-scoping KFX is a
   planning decision, and editing the plan is out of scope (`[CHA2-03]`).
3. **`[CHA2-12]`/BS-3's answer is unknown until run.** The honest specification is "record
   the observed outcome", not "assert the divergence". If the rollback turns out not to
   re-fire, BS-3 becomes a passing pin and the finding says so. Do not write the assertion
   to match the expectation.
4. **Expected-failure infrastructure can rot.** A signature match that is too loose turns
   `[CHA2-43]` into a no-op; too tight and unrelated refactors redden the gate. Recommend
   matching on a stable assertion *identifier* the test emits, not on a formatted message.
   Decide in task 2.
5. **`@ExpectedFailure` is a new project-local mechanism.** Nothing in the repo currently
   expresses "expected to fail until fixed"; the closest idiom is a diverging *control*
   (`[CHA1-62]`), which asserts failure inline. **Open question:** should a reproduction be
   written as a control-style inline `shouldThrow`/negated assertion instead of an
   extension? Rejected in §3.3 because a negated assertion silently keeps passing after the
   fix lands — `[CHA2-44]` is the whole point. Confirm before task 2.
6. **BS-8's nested-exclusive case may need a `@Contract` that KSP refuses.** If the
   generator rejects the shape, the reproduction cannot be written and the honest outcome is
   a `DISPUTES.md` entry (`[CHA2-46]`), not a weaker test.
7. **BS-10 overlaps SEC1.** Two work items must not both specify the denial-accounting fix.
   CHA2 owns the *reproduction*; SEC1 owns the *fix and its requirements*. Coordinate before
   task 6 so the eventual fix flips CHA2's expected failure rather than duplicating it.
8. **Corpus pressure.** Several scenarios are morally corpus material but the scenario
   language has no fault verbs. Do not smuggle a schema change in; flag and stop
   (`[CHA2-51]`).
9. **The stale spec prose.** Three ⚠ CONFLICT (C-11) blocks and one C-9 gap row are now
   contradicted by the code. Correcting them is documentation maintenance and requires
   explicit authorization (the same shape D-C12 needed). CHA2 files the finding; it does not
   edit `doc/spec/`.

# CHA2 — design decisions and alternatives considered

## D0. The plan row is stale on all three items — verified, not assumed

CHA1's own scope section already flagged one of these ("C-12 was adjudicated **resolved**
in `91-gap-analysis.md` (D-C12) … do not manufacture a failure for it"). Re-verifying that
claim turned up two more:

| Ledger id | Plan row says | Verified state in `main` (2026-08-08) |
|---|---|---|
| C-9 | decided-but-divergent | processed-frontier **landed** (`HostDurability.kt`, `ManagedHost.kt:785-815`, "G-59, fixes C-9"); `[24-DUR-05]` covered by `DUR-REPLAY-01`. Real residual = random per-instance `sourceId` on a journaled source (`DISPUTES.md:511`), plus the `ctx.baseline` non-exemption (`CatchUp.kt:52-58`) |
| C-11 | decided-but-divergent | discharging proxy **landed** (`Evolution.kt:78-88` → `Proxy.discharging`, `Proxy.kt:101-133`); `ShadowOwnershipTest` is its exit test. Real residuals = exclusive-bit reach (nested payloads; 93 I-6/I-8 "unimplemented"), suppression granularity (93 I-17; G-32 row), and the `BoundaryPolicy` denial drop (SEC1/KHYG) |
| C-12 | decided-but-divergent | **resolved**, adjudicated D-C12; `91-gap-analysis.md:20`,`:115`; `21-REBASE-01.yaml` green; `DISPUTES.md:360` |

The feature is therefore an **adjudication + residual reproduction** suite. Writing three
failing tests to match the row would aim KFX at mechanisms already in `main`.

## D1. A feature under CHA1, not an epic

CHA2 builds no rig. Its injectors (`CrashFault`, `JournalFault`, `RestartAtFrontierFault`,
`PartitionFault`), its artifact/replay/shrink surface, and — critically — its
exclusive-payload accounting (`[CHA1-53]`) are all CHA1 deliverables. CHA1 §6 states the
split in so many words. What CHA2 adds is verdicts, standing tests, and one small test
infrastructure piece (D3).

## D2. Reproductions live in `kernel/src/test`, not `testkit`

`ManagedHost.replayAsBaseline` is `internal` — reachable from `:kernel`'s test source set,
not from `:testkit` (CHA1 risk 3, "Do not widen it casually"). The PN-2 baseline path is
central to `[CHA2-14]`/BS-5. Putting the suite in `:kernel`'s tests costs nothing and
avoids a visibility change made for a test's convenience.

## D3. `@ExpectedFailure` as a JUnit 5 extension — and why not the three alternatives

The suite's defining constraint: a test expected to fail until a kernel fix lands must
run, must not redden the gate, must not be ignorable, and **must break the build the
moment it starts passing** (`[CHA2-44]`).

- **`@Disabled`** — rejected. A disabled body never executes, so it cannot detect the fix
  and it decays into dead code. This is exactly how a "reproduction suite" becomes folklore.
- **A negated/inline assertion (`shouldThrow`, control-style)** — rejected, and this is the
  subtle one. It is the repo's existing idiom for diverging *controls* (`[CHA1-62]`), and
  it keeps the gate green. But after the fix lands it keeps *passing* — the negation is now
  wrong and nothing says so. The whole value of a reproduction is the flip.
- **An opt-in Gradle property / excluded test tag** — rejected: same non-execution problem,
  plus it hides the residual ledger from anyone not reading build files.
- **A JUnit 5 extension that inverts the verdict** — chosen. The body runs every build; a
  match on the recorded signature reports expected-as-passed (`[CHA2-42]`); any *other*
  failure fails the build, because a reproduction failing for a new reason is a new defect
  (`[CHA2-43]`); a pass fails the build with "remove the annotation, keep the test"
  (`[CHA2-44]`). BS-14 and BS-15 are the self-tests that make this load-bearing, and they
  are blocking acceptance.

Signature matching should key on a stable assertion identifier the test emits, not a
formatted message (§9 risk 4) — too loose and `[CHA2-43]` is a no-op, too tight and
unrelated refactors go red.

## D4. Reproductions carry an owner, and not every owner is KFX

The plan's edge is `CHA2 -.failing tests.-> KFX`. But one C-11-class residual — the
`BoundaryPolicy` denial dropping exclusives at `MediateProxy.kt:42,52-57` and
`CompositeCell.kt:205-215,229-249` — is already owned by **SEC1** under the KHYG epic.
Routing it to KFX would create two specifications of one fix. So `[CHA2-41]` makes the
owner a required field of every expected failure, and `[CHA2-23]`/BS-10 is explicitly
SEC1's. CHA2 reproduces and hands over; it never specifies someone else's fix.

## D5. BS-3's assertion is "record the answer", not "assert the divergence"

CHA1's BS-11 hands the frontier-rollback verdict to CHA2 precisely because the outcome is
unknown until run: "the run reports either exactly-once effect firing (the decided rule
holds) **or** a reproduced C-9-class divergence — whichever the code actually does". A
specification that pre-decides it would be a test written to a belief. `[CHA2-12]` is
therefore phrased as an observation requirement, and the finding is written either way.

## D6. C-12 gets a documentation-of-record assertion, not a reproduction

`[CHA2-30]`…`[CHA2-33]` / BS-13 assert over checked-in artifacts (the corrected spec
sites, `D-C12.md`, `21-REBASE-01.yaml`, `DISPUTES.md:360`) rather than over kernel
behaviour, because there is no divergence to observe. The value is that the next reader who
finds "C-12" in a planning document meets counter-evidence instead of re-deriving the
adjudication. `[CHA2-33]` guards the opposite error: D-C12's own residuals (G-43
freshest-checkpoint tiers and pull-merge direction; G-42 epoch/generation reclamation) are
**not** closed and are not covered here.

## D7. Findings, never the gap table

Milestone plan §6: every lane writes its own append-only findings file citing G-ids, and
"a periodic single-agent integration pass is the only writer of the gap table and the
concordance matrix". CHA2 has three stale rows to report (C-9, C-11, and the KFX plan row)
and reports all three as findings. `doc/spec/CONCORDANCE.md` is generated and must never be
hand-edited. Correcting the three ⚠ CONFLICT (C-11) prose blocks is documentation
maintenance requiring explicit authorization — the same shape D-C12 needed — and is
out of scope.

## D8. DISPUTES.md is extended, not duplicated

The G-59/C-9 boundary is *already* filed honestly at `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md:511`,
including the "Resolves" clause naming ref-derived/output-mode wave identity as the fix.
`[CHA2-51]` therefore permits extending that entry with the reproduction's id and forbids a
second entry for the same boundary. Any genuinely new unverifiable residual gets its own
entry — and **no** manufactured test (`[CHA2-46]`).

## D9. Dependency wiring

Wired: **CHA2 → CHA1** (`computenet-umx`).
Consumers, unwired here: **KFX** and **SEC1** (`computenet-usd`, under KHYG). KFX has no
bead id yet; when it is filed, the edge `CHA2 → KFX` should be added, and the KFX scope
should be re-read against CHA2's findings before it is written, since the plan's KFX row
describes work already in `main`.

EXPECTED-FAILURE DISCIPLINE (blocking — without this the suite is decoration): [CHA2-40] through [CHA2-47] — every reproduction executes on every build (no @Disabled, no @Ignore, no Gradle filter, no opt-in property); carries reason, owner and findings anchor; a recorded-signature failure passes the gate; ANY other signature fails the build; a reproduction that starts PASSING fails the build with a remove-the-annotation message (BS-14); a signature change fails the build (BS-15); standing expected failures and owners are reported per run (BS-16); an unreproducible residual is filed in concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md with NO test manufactured for it; discovered seeds are pinned and never replaced, narrowed or reordered (BS-17).
