title: KRD — Request/response bounded read: public query primitive over the landed V1C-KERNEL seam
description:
# KRD — Request/response bounded read: the public-primitive generalization

Kernel-lane chunk **KRD**, milestone plan §1 (*"riding, not scheduled here — V1C-KERNEL
(v4 wave 8, already ticketed) delivers the core: wave-neutral, bounded, any-scheduler
`snapshotOf` successor. Bench lane generalizes it into a public query primitive after it
merges"*), §3 (YCSB and SNB-interactive rows), §4 (*"KRD rides inspector-v4 wave 8
(V1C-KERNEL) and gets a small generalization pass afterward"*).

## What already exists — V1C-KERNEL has landed

This is the ticket's most important fact, and it is verified, not assumed. **The core is
in `main`.** Anyone treating KRD as "build a bounded read" would rebuild a substantial,
carefully-specified subsystem.

| Landed surface | Where |
|---|---|
| `interface BoundedStateful : Stateful` with `readBounded(StateRead): StatePage`, `supportsSince`, `supportsScope` | `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/BoundedRead.kt:81,92,112,124` |
| `StateRead(cursor, limit, byteBudget, scope, since, allowWholeCopy)` with validation | `BoundedRead.kt:154-166` |
| `StatePage(entries, next, frontier, provenance, exclusivesElided, attributes, caveats)` | `BoundedRead.kt:251-259` |
| `Cursor` (opaque, cell-minted, kernel never interprets) | `BoundedRead.kt:271-272` |
| `Provenance` (`LIVE`, `LIVE_SUSPENDED`, `CHECKPOINT`) | `BoundedRead.kt:279-296` |
| `ReadCaveat` (`STALE_FRONTIER`, `POSITIONAL_CURSOR`) | `BoundedRead.kt:303-322` |
| `ExclusiveEntry` — a page never carries an `Owned`/`Leased` value | `BoundedRead.kt:353-398` |
| `StateReadResult` = `Page` \| `Unbounded` \| `Unavailable(Reason)` with 9 named reasons | `BoundedRead.kt:409-475` |
| `ManagedHost.readState(ref, request): CompletableFuture<StateReadResult>` — wave-neutral, one page = one scheduler task at priority 0, per-page cancellation, never completes exceptionally, refusals decided on the caller's thread, drained-host and suspended-cell arms decided | `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/ManagedHost.kt:1360-1454` |
| 20 `BoundedStateful` implementors, incl. `MapCell`, `KeyedSetCell`, `SetCell`, `ListCell`, `ShardCell`, `WatermarkCell`, `InstanceSet`, and all 13 `data/op` cells via `OperatorPaging.pageOver` | `data/`, `partition/`, `replication/`, `data/op/OperatorPaging.kt:308` |
| Deterministic total key order + O(page)-resume cursor | `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/BoundedWalk.kt:51,88,115` |
| Kernel tests | `kernel/src/test/.../host/BoundedReadWaveNeutralityTest.kt`, `BoundedReadCursorCostTest.kt`, `BoundedReadProvenanceTest.kt`, `data/op/OperatorBoundedReadTest.kt`, `OperatorBoundedReadEdgesTest.kt`, `OperatorCursorOrderTest.kt` |
| Normative spec | `[21-PULL-02]`, `[21-PULL-03]` (`doc/spec/20-dataflow-semantics/21-propagation.md:160,184`), `[24-BOUND-01]`, `[24-BOUND-02]` (`24-data-cells.md:119,122`) |
| A live consumer proving the seam works | `inspect/src/main/kotlin/civictech/inspect/PagedState.kt`, `DataSearch.kt:333`, `InspectorServer.kt:275-277` |

**Nothing in the list above is in scope to build, redesign, or re-specify.**

## The generalization delta — what is actually missing

`readState` is a method **on a `ManagedHost`**. A benchmark adapter, a YCSB client, or an
SNB interactive query does not hold a `ManagedHost`; it holds a `CellRef` and wants an
answer. Four specific things stand between the landed seam and a public query primitive,
and each is visible in how the one existing consumer had to compensate:

1. **Routing is open-coded.** The inspector does
   `registry.locate(ref)?.readState(ref, request)` (`InspectorServer.kt:275-277`), with
   `locate` returning null for anything not `Local` (`LocationRegistry.kt:262`). Every
   future consumer will re-derive that expression, and each will pick its own answer for
   the null case — which the landed design already has a named reason for
   (`NOT_HOSTED` / `MIGRATING`, `BoundedRead.kt:433,458`). Routing should produce those
   reasons, not a null.
2. **The walk is hand-rolled, and so is the stability check.** `StatePage`'s contract is
   *"a sequence of per-page-consistent reads, not a snapshot"* (`BoundedRead.kt:172-223`),
   and `[21-PULL-03]` states the exact condition under which a walk's union *is* a
   snapshot: an unchanged frontier across the walk, **for a family in which every state
   change mints or absorbs a tag**. Getting that check right — including the OR-set caveat
   where it is necessary but not sufficient — is subtle enough that every consumer
   reimplementing it will get it subtly differently. The inspector's `PagedState` is one
   implementation of the loop; a second, third and fourth are exactly what a shared
   primitive prevents.
3. **There is no walk-level completion.** Today a caller gets one
   `CompletableFuture<StateReadResult>` per page and owns the loop, the deadline, the
   cancellation and the accumulation. §3 names this explicitly — *"generalize
   V1C-KERNEL's read into a public request/response primitive **with completion
   semantics**"*.
4. **There is no app-facing home for a pull-side read.** `civictech.cell.observe` is the
   app-facing read package per `AGENTS.md`, but it contains only push-side machinery —
   `ObservationSink`, `View`, `ObserveCell`, `observe`/`observeAll`/`observeAligned`
   (`observe/Observe.kt:43,72,143,285-558`, `observe/AlignedObserve.kt:137-567`). Pull-side
   reads have no declared home, which is why the inspector reaches into `host` directly.

That is the whole delta: **routing, a walk with a correct stability check, walk-level
completion, and a home.** It is a facade plus one carefully-specified loop over a seam
that already carries every hard guarantee.

## Sizing

Filed as a **feature, not an epic**, and the pre-ticket inspection above is why: the
subsystem — wave-neutrality, paging, cursor semantics, exclusive elision, provenance,
refusal taxonomy, per-family cursors — is merged and tested. Had `BoundedRead.kt` not
existed, KRD would have been an epic. It does exist, in full, with its normative
requirements already in `doc/spec/` and already covered by kernel tests and a shipping
consumer.

## Ambition / Why

BB-YCSB's point read and scan phases and BB-SNB's interactive complex reads both need a
read that (a) can be issued against a `CellRef` from adapter code, (b) terminates with a
stated completeness outcome rather than "the pages stopped", and (c) does not perturb what
it measures. A benchmark whose read path silently advances a wave position or fires a tap
measures a different system than the one it claims to. `[21-PULL-02]` is precisely the
guarantee that makes the numbers mean something, and it is already true of `readState`;
KRD's job is to make it *reachable* without every consumer re-deriving the plumbing and
risking a variant that is not wave-neutral.

## What we build

1. **A routed read entry point** — resolve a `CellRef` to its hosting `ManagedHost` and
   delegate, answering the landed `StateReadResult.Reason` arms for the unroutable cases
   instead of null.
2. **A walk primitive** — drive `readState` page by page to termination under a caller
   deadline and a caller cancellation, accumulating pages, one page per round trip (never
   batching pages inside one invocation), and terminating on `next == null`.
3. **A walk outcome with completion semantics** — a result that states which of
   *complete-and-stable*, *complete-but-smeared*, *refused (with the named reason)*,
   *cancelled*, or *deadline-exceeded* occurred, plus the caveats and elision counts the
   pages carried.
4. **The `[21-PULL-03]` stability determination**, computed once, correctly, in one place —
   including the honest degradation for families whose mutations do not all mint tags and
   for families with no frontier at all.
5. **The documented `since` escalation** (`BoundedRead.kt:217-223`, `21-propagation.md:199-201`)
   offered as a supported step for a caller who needs a real snapshot, available only where
   `supportsSince` is true.
6. **A public home** in the app-facing read package, so the inspector's open-coded routing
   can become a consumer of the primitive rather than a second implementation of it.

## How, using ComputeNet

The primitive lives in `civictech.cell.observe` (app-facing reads per `AGENTS.md`),
beside — not inside — the push-side `View`/`ObservationSink` machinery, because a read is
explicitly *not* a subscription (`BoundedRead.kt:78-79`).

Routing goes through `LocationRegistry` (`LocationRegistry.kt:262,264`): `locate(ref)`
gives the local `ManagedHost` and `location(ref)` distinguishes "placed elsewhere" from
"unknown" — exactly the distinction `readState` itself already makes internally when the
cell is absent from `cells` (`ManagedHost.kt:1370-1382`). The primitive must produce the
same two reasons for the same two situations, so a caller sees one taxonomy rather than
two.

The walk loop is the shape `PagedState` (`inspect/.../PagedState.kt:116,176`) and
`DataSearch` (`inspect/.../DataSearch.kt:333`) already run, lifted into the kernel: issue
`readState`, await with the caller's deadline, honour `cancel(false)` (which `readState`
already respects per page — `ManagedHost.kt:1448`), append the page's entries, carry
`next` into the following request, stop at `next == null`. **One page per scheduler
task** is a hard rule of the landed design (`BoundedRead.kt:26-28`,
`ManagedHost.kt:1289-1298`) and the walk must not defeat it by requesting an unbounded
limit; a walk's page limit stays the caller's `StateRead.limit`.

The stability determination implements `[21-PULL-03]` literally: compare the opening
page's `frontier` with the closing page's. Both are exact by contract
(`BoundedRead.kt:232-236`), a `TagFrontier` is monotone, so equal endpoints imply no
intermediate difference — and `ReadCaveat.STALE_FRONTIER` on intermediate pages is
therefore *not* a reason to weaken the verdict. Three degradations must be represented
honestly rather than collapsed into "stable":

- `frontier == null` (families with no tag frontier — `MapCell`, `ListCell`,
  `WatermarkCell`, `InstanceSet`, per `BoundedRead.kt:96-105`): stability is
  **undeterminable**, not "stable".
- A family whose mutations do not all mint tags — the OR-set observed-remove case spelled
  out at `BoundedRead.kt:195-204` and in `21-propagation.md:203-205`: an equal-frontier
  verdict is **necessary but not sufficient**, and the outcome must say so.
- `exclusivesElided > 0` (`BoundedRead.kt:242-243`): the union is complete as a *presence*
  answer but the exclusive values were never in it. Carried, never dropped.

The `since` escalation reuses `StateRead.since` (`BoundedRead.kt:159`) and is refused up
front on a cell with `supportsSince == false` by `readState` itself
(`ManagedHost.kt:1408-1410`) — the primitive surfaces that refusal, it does not
pre-empt or work around it.

## Scope boundaries

- **Not V1C-KERNEL.** `BoundedStateful`, `StateRead`, `StatePage`, `Cursor`, `Provenance`,
  `ReadCaveat`, `ExclusiveEntry`, `StateReadResult`, `ManagedHost.readState` and every
  per-family `readBounded` are landed and out of scope to redesign.
- **No remote or scattered bounded read.** `BoundedRead.kt:266-270` states that remote
  bounded reads are explicitly out of scope and that a cursor's meaning across a
  scatter-gather boundary (where the answering instance may change between pages) is an
  **open research question**. KRD does not open it. A `CellRef` that resolves to a remote
  location is answered with the existing `MIGRATING`/`NOT_HOSTED` taxonomy.
- **No new bound on `StateRead`.** An ordered key-range bound is **KAGG-R**'s
  (`[KAGG-R-19]`). KRD consumes whatever bounds `StateRead` carries.
- **No snapshot isolation.** Explicitly rejected in the landed design
  (`BoundedRead.kt:211-216`): it would need per-message copy-on-write (forbidden by P2) or
  holding the cell's context for the whole walk. Detection is the design; KRD implements
  detection, not locking.
- **No emission, link, tap, or attention.** `[21-PULL-02]` is absolute; the primitive must
  not become a subscription with a walk attached.
- **No `StateRequest` pull path change.** A pull reply installs a `MessageContext.baseline`
  in a consumer's fold and needs a link or tap to be received at all
  (`BoundedRead.kt:133-138`); that is why an instrument cannot use one, and none of it
  changes here.
- **No new normative spec id.** `[21-PULL-02]`, `[21-PULL-03]`, `[24-BOUND-01]`,
  `[24-BOUND-02]` already state the rules. If the generalization needs a new normative id,
  that is documentation maintenance requiring explicit authorization — file it as a finding.
- **No YCSB or SNB adapter.** Those are BB-YCSB and BB-SNB.

## Functional requirements (EARS)

### Routing

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KRD-01]` The kernel SHALL provide a bounded read that a caller may issue
against a `CellRef` without holding the hosting `ManagedHost`. *(`[21-PULL-02]`)*

*(Event-driven)* `[KRD-02]` WHEN a routed read's `CellRef` resolves to a locally hosted
cell, the read SHALL be served by that host's existing bounded-read path with identical
semantics — same page contract, same refusal reasons, same provenance. *(`[21-PULL-02]`,
`[24-BOUND-01]`)*

*(Unwanted behaviour)* `[KRD-03]` IF a routed read's `CellRef` is placed on another host or
is held for a migration flip, THEN the read SHALL answer with the existing named reason for
that case and SHALL NOT be served from any local object. *(`[21-PULL-02]`)*

*(Unwanted behaviour)* `[KRD-04]` IF a routed read's `CellRef` is unknown to the registry,
THEN the read SHALL answer with the existing not-hosted reason, and SHALL NOT answer with
`null`, an empty page, or an exception. *(`[21-PULL-02]`)*

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KRD-05]` A routed read SHALL surface exactly the existing refusal taxonomy;
no new reason SHALL be minted and no existing reason SHALL be collapsed into another.
*(`[21-PULL-02]`)*

### Wave neutrality — the guarantee the benchmarks depend on

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KRD-06]` A read issued through the primitive SHALL emit nothing, link
nothing, fire no tap, raise no attention, advance no wave counter, advance no delivered
watermark, and join no completeness set. *(`[21-PULL-02]`)*

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KRD-07]` A read issued through the primitive SHALL never advance an
`Effectful` inlet's processed frontier. *(`[21-PULL-02]`, `[24-DUR-05]`)*

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KRD-08]` A read SHALL never complete exceptionally: every failure SHALL be
a named outcome the caller can act on. *(`[21-PULL-02]`)*

### The walk and its completion semantics

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KRD-09]` The primitive SHALL drive a walk from a fresh cursor to
termination, issuing one page request per round trip and carrying each page's resume token
into the next request. *(`[24-BOUND-02]`)*

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KRD-10]` A walk SHALL terminate exactly when a page reports no resume
token; a short or empty page carrying a resume token SHALL NOT terminate it.
*(`[24-BOUND-02]`; `BoundedRead.kt:228-231`)*

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KRD-11]` A walk SHALL NOT batch multiple pages inside one invocation of
the underlying host read, and SHALL NOT widen the caller's page limit. *(`[24-BOUND-01]`;
the one-page-one-task rule, `BoundedRead.kt:26-28`)*

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KRD-12]` A walk SHALL complete with a stated outcome distinguishing at
least: completed, refused (carrying the named reason), cancelled, and deadline-exceeded.
*(`[21-PULL-02]`; §3's "completion semantics")*

*(Event-driven)* `[KRD-13]` WHEN a caller cancels a walk in progress, the walk SHALL stop
issuing further page requests and SHALL report cancellation; at most one already-submitted
page request SHALL remain outstanding. *(`[21-PULL-02]`; `ManagedHost.kt:1448`)*

*(Event-driven)* `[KRD-14]` WHEN a walk exceeds its caller-supplied deadline, it SHALL
report deadline-exceeded together with the pages already accumulated, and SHALL NOT present
a partial walk as complete. *(`[24-BOUND-02]`)*

*(Event-driven)* `[KRD-15]` WHEN any page of a walk is refused, the walk SHALL stop and
report that refusal reason rather than continuing or reporting completion. *(`[21-PULL-02]`)*

### Stability — `[21-PULL-03]`, computed once and honestly

*(Event-driven)* `[KRD-16]` WHEN a walk over a tag-carrying family completes and its opening
and closing frontier stamps are equal, the outcome SHALL report the union as a snapshot at
that frontier. *(`[21-PULL-03]`)*

*(Event-driven)* `[KRD-17]` WHEN a walk's opening and closing frontier stamps differ, the
outcome SHALL report the union as smeared, and SHALL NOT report it as a snapshot.
*(`[21-PULL-03]`)*

*(Unwanted behaviour)* `[KRD-18]` IF a walk's pages carry no frontier at all, THEN the
outcome SHALL report stability as undeterminable, and SHALL NOT report the union as either
stable or smeared. *(`[21-PULL-03]`)*

*(Unwanted behaviour)* `[KRD-19]` IF the read family's state changes do not all mint or
absorb a tag, THEN an equal-frontier verdict SHALL be reported as necessary-but-not-
sufficient rather than as an unqualified snapshot. *(`[21-PULL-03]`; the family
qualification at `21-propagation.md:203-205` and the OR-set caveat at `BoundedRead.kt:195-204`)*

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KRD-20]` An intermediate page's stale-frontier caveat SHALL NOT weaken the
stability verdict, since the opening and closing stamps are exact and a tag frontier is
monotone. *(`[21-PULL-03]`; `BoundedRead.kt:305-313`)*

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KRD-21]` Every caveat and every elided-exclusive count carried by any page
of a walk SHALL appear in the walk's outcome. *(`[24-BOUND-01]`)*

*(Optional feature)* `[KRD-22]` WHERE the target family supports `since`, the primitive
SHALL offer the documented escalation — record the opening frontier, walk to completion,
then issue one further read with `since` set to it — as a supported operation.
*(`[21-PULL-03]`; `BoundedRead.kt:217-223`)*

*(Unwanted behaviour)* `[KRD-23]` IF the target family does not support `since`, THEN the
escalation SHALL be refused with the existing named reason and SHALL NOT be emulated by any
other means. *(`[21-PULL-03]`; `ManagedHost.kt:1408-1410`)*

### Ownership and disclosure

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KRD-24]` No page delivered through the primitive SHALL carry an `Owned` or
`Leased` value or a copy of one; elided entries SHALL remain represented by their presence
descriptor and counted. *(`[24-BOUND-01]`; `BoundedRead.kt:328-340`; the exclusive-payload
invariant in `AGENTS.md`)*

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KRD-25]` A bound the caller set SHALL never be silently widened: a scope or
`since` the target family cannot honour SHALL be refused, on the caller's thread, before any
task reaches the cell. *(`[24-BOUND-01]`; `ManagedHost.kt:1405-1413`)*

*(Unwanted behaviour)* `[KRD-26]` IF the caller has not opted into a whole-state answer,
THEN a cell that is stateful but not bounded-readable SHALL be refused rather than copied
whole. *(`[24-BOUND-01]`; `BoundedRead.kt:441-443`)*

### Non-duplication

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KRD-27]` The primitive SHALL become the single implementation of the walk
loop and the stability determination; the existing open-coded consumer implementations SHALL
be migrated onto it or explicitly recorded as deliberate exceptions with reasons.
*(`[21-PULL-03]`)*

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KRD-28]` The generalization SHALL be additive: no existing
`ManagedHost.readState` signature, `StateRead` default, `StatePage` field, or
`StateReadResult` arm SHALL change. *(`[21-PULL-02]`, `[24-BOUND-01]`)*

### A requirement that cannot be checked honestly, stated rather than softened

`[KRD-29]` *(recorded, not asserted)* "A completed walk's union equals the cell's state"
cannot be asserted unconditionally, and the ticket must not write a test that pretends
otherwise. `[24-BOUND-02]` holds only for a cell that accepts no operation for the walk's
duration; `[21-PULL-03]` holds only for a family in which every state change mints or
absorbs a tag; and for the OR-set the equal-frontier check is provably *necessary but not
sufficient* — an observed-remove copies existing add-tags into the del-map and mints
nothing, so a mid-walk removal of an already-paged element leaves both endpoint stamps
equal while the union still names it present (`BoundedRead.kt:195-204`). `[KRD-19]` encodes
that limit rather than hiding it. Closing it is a state-family question already filed as
research; **it is not KRD's to solve and not KRD's to paper over.** Any scenario that would
need it closed belongs in `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md`.

## Suggested task decomposition (list only — do not create these beads)

1. Routed read entry point over `LocationRegistry`, producing the existing reason taxonomy.
2. Walk driver: cursor threading, termination on absent resume token, deadline,
   cancellation, accumulation.
3. Walk outcome type with completion semantics and carried caveats/elision counts.
4. `[21-PULL-03]` stability determination with all three honest degradations.
5. The `since` escalation as a supported operation, with refusal passthrough.
6. Migrate the inspector's open-coded routing and walk onto the primitive, or record the
   exception.
7. Tests: routing arms, wave-neutrality, cancellation, deadline, refusal propagation,
   stable/smeared/undeterminable verdicts, OR-set qualification, exclusive elision.
8. Concord scenarios for the walk-completeness and stability rules (see design notes);
   regenerate `CONCORDANCE.md`.

## Verification

```bash
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.host.BoundedReadWaveNeutralityTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.host.BoundedReadProvenanceTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.host.BoundedReadCursorCostTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.data.op.OperatorBoundedReadTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.data.op.OperatorBoundedReadEdgesTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.data.op.OperatorCursorOrderTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.observe.*'
./gradlew :inspect:test
./gradlew :concord:test -Pconcord.profiles=core
./gradlew :concord:check
./gradlew test
```

`:inspect:test` is named explicitly: the inspector is the existing consumer of
`ManagedHost.readState` (`PagedState.kt`, `DataSearch.kt`, `InspectorServer.kt:275-277`)
and is the regression gate for `[KRD-27]` and `[KRD-28]`.

## Risks / open questions

1. **Scope creep into the remote read.** The instant someone asks "why can't I read a cell
   on another host?", this feature becomes an epic. `BoundedRead.kt:266-270` records that
   the cross-boundary cursor is open research. Answer with the existing reason arm and file
   the demand as a finding.
2. **Where the primitive lives.** `civictech.cell.observe` is proposed because `AGENTS.md`
   names it the app-facing read package, but it currently holds only push-side machinery,
   and a read is emphatically not a subscription. If a reviewer prefers a separate
   package, the argument should be settled before the code lands, not after consumers
   import it.
3. **The stability verdict's vocabulary is where correctness lives.** Three degradations
   (null frontier, non-tag-minting family, elided exclusives) all want to collapse into a
   comfortable boolean. `[KRD-18]`, `[KRD-19]` and `[KRD-21]` exist to stop that; they are
   the requirements most likely to be quietly softened during implementation.
4. **Migrating the inspector.** `[KRD-27]` is the anti-duplication requirement and also the
   riskiest part of the diff — `PagedState`/`DataSearch` carry inspector-specific budget
   and search behaviour that may not fit the general walk. Recording a deliberate exception
   with reasons is an acceptable outcome; silently leaving two loops is not.
5. **YCSB read latency will want a per-page fast path.** A YCSB point read is one entry;
   driving it as a walk costs a round trip it does not need. Whether a single-page
   convenience is worth a second entry point is a question BB-YCSB should answer with a
   number, not one KRD should pre-emptively optimize.
6. **The milestone plan lists KRD as depending on the inspector-v4 lane.** That dependency
   is **satisfied** — V1C-KERNEL is merged, as the table above evidences. The lane note
   should not be read as a live blocker.
design:
# KRD — Behaviour specifications

Given/When/Then, specific enough to become named tests. Each names the requirement ids it
discharges and, where it belongs in the executable specification, a `covers:` line.

---

## Routing

### BS-01 — Local cell, identical semantics
**Given** a `CellRef` for a `BoundedStateful` cell hosted on a host known to the registry
**When** the same `StateRead` is issued once through the routed primitive and once directly
through that host's bounded read
**Then** the two answers are equivalent: same entries, same resume token, same frontier,
same provenance, same caveats, same elision count.
Discharges `[KRD-01]`, `[KRD-02]`, `[KRD-28]`.
*Not a concord scenario* — it asserts an API equivalence between two kernel entry points,
which is implementation-facing. Kernel test.

### BS-02 — Elsewhere, held, and unknown are three distinguishable answers
**Given** three refs: one placed on a different host, one held for a migration flip, one
unknown to the registry
**When** each is read through the routed primitive
**Then** each answers with its own existing named reason; none answers `null`, an empty
page, or an exception; and no local object is consulted for the held ref.
Discharges `[KRD-03]`, `[KRD-04]`, `[KRD-05]`, `[KRD-08]`.
`covers: [21-PULL-02]` — corpus-worthy in part: "a read of a cell that is not here answers
a stated refusal rather than a fabricated value" is boundary-observable. The
three-way *distinguishability* is finer than the corpus SPI expresses today; if it needs a
new driver verb that is a gated `concord/schema` change — file it rather than inventing a
binding.

---

## Wave neutrality

### BS-10 — A walk perturbs nothing
**Given** a quiescent graph containing a large `BoundedStateful` cell, with the wave state,
delivered watermarks, completeness sets, tap-fire counts and attention state all recorded
**When** a full multi-page walk is driven to completion through the primitive
**Then** every recorded quantity is unchanged, no link exists that did not exist before,
and no `PullOnOpen` fired.
Discharges `[KRD-06]`.
`covers: [21-PULL-02]` — corpus-worthy, and the single most important scenario in this
ticket: it is the guarantee that makes every BB read number mean what it claims.
`BoundedReadWaveNeutralityTest` is the existing kernel precedent for the same property at
the host seam; this is its routed-primitive analogue.

### BS-11 — A walk does not advance an Effectful frontier
**Given** an `Effectful` cell that is also `BoundedStateful`, with a recorded
processed-frontier
**When** it is walked to completion through the primitive, and the host is then crashed and
recovered
**Then** the processed-frontier is unchanged by the walk, and recovery behaves exactly as it
would have without it — the read neither suppressed a later real delivery nor caused one to
re-fire.
Discharges `[KRD-07]`.
`covers: [21-PULL-02], [24-DUR-05]` — corpus-worthy: it composes the read primitive with
the durability rule, and the `dur` profile already drives crash-and-recover with an
effect-count check.

### BS-12 — A broken cell does not break the caller
**Given** a cell whose `readBounded` throws
**When** it is walked
**Then** the walk reports the existing read-failed reason and the caller's future completes
normally — no exception escapes.
Discharges `[KRD-08]`, `[KRD-15]`.
*Not a concord scenario* — it requires injecting a faulty cell implementation, which is a
driver-internal capability. Kernel test.

---

## Walk mechanics and completion

### BS-20 — Termination is by absent resume token, not by an empty page
**Given** a cell whose walk yields a short page and then an **empty** page, both carrying a
resume token, before a final page with none — the case `since`/`scope`/byte-budget skipping
produces
**When** it is walked
**Then** the walk continues past both the short and the empty page and terminates only at
the token-less one; the union is the full in-scope state.
Discharges `[KRD-09]`, `[KRD-10]`.
`covers: [24-BOUND-02]` — corpus-worthy; "only `next == null` terminates a walk" is a
stated contract and a classic off-by-one.

### BS-21 — Page limit is the caller's, and one page is one task
**Given** a cell with `n` entries and a caller page limit of `L`
**When** it is walked to completion
**Then** the number of underlying host reads is at least `ceil(n/L)`, no single answered
page exceeds `L` entries, and the walk never issues a request with a limit larger than `L`.
Discharges `[KRD-11]`.
*Not a concord scenario* — it counts scheduler tasks, which is implementation detail.
Kernel test beside `BoundedReadCursorCostTest`, which is the existing precedent for "a
correctness test with a cost assertion, not a benchmark".

### BS-22 — Cancellation mid-walk
**Given** a multi-page walk in progress with one page request outstanding
**When** the caller cancels
**Then** the walk reports cancelled, issues no further page requests, and leaves at most one
outstanding request — which, when it runs, costs a dequeue rather than a page.
Discharges `[KRD-12]`, `[KRD-13]`.
*Not a concord scenario* — cancellation is a caller-side API property. Kernel test on the
deterministic scheduler, where "still outstanding" is exactly observable by stepping.

### BS-23 — Deadline exceeded is not completion
**Given** a walk over a cell large enough that the deadline expires mid-walk, driven on the
deterministic scheduler so the expiry point is exact
**When** the deadline passes
**Then** the outcome is deadline-exceeded, carries the pages already accumulated, and is
**not** reportable as complete, stable, or a snapshot.
Discharges `[KRD-14]`, `[KRD-12]`.
`covers: [24-BOUND-02]` — corpus-worthy as the negative half: a truncated walk must not
present itself as satisfying the union-equals-state promise.

### BS-24 — A refusal mid-walk stops the walk
**Given** a walk whose second page is refused — the cell is migrated away between pages
**When** the refusal arrives
**Then** the walk stops and reports that reason; it does not retry, does not skip, and does
not report completion with a hole.
Discharges `[KRD-15]`.
`covers: [21-PULL-02]` — corpus-worthy: mid-walk migration is a real failure/recovery case
and the corpus already drives migration (`33-mobility`).

---

## Stability — `[21-PULL-03]`

### BS-30 — Quiescent walk over a tag-carrying family is a snapshot
**Given** a tag-carrying `BoundedStateful` cell accepting no operations
**When** it is walked to completion with a page limit far below its size
**Then** the opening and closing frontier stamps are equal, the outcome reports a snapshot
at that frontier, and the union equals the cell's whole state — for several page limits.
Discharges `[KRD-16]`.
`covers: [21-PULL-03], [24-BOUND-02]` — corpus-worthy; it is the requirement stated almost
verbatim.

### BS-31 — Concurrent mutation yields smeared, never a false snapshot
**Given** a tag-carrying cell being walked, with adds applied mid-walk after the walk has
passed their position
**When** the walk completes
**Then** the stamps differ and the outcome reports smeared; **and** the union is never torn
at entry granularity and never contains a duplicate.
Discharges `[KRD-17]`.
`covers: [21-PULL-03]` — corpus-worthy; the smeared case is what stops a caller from
mistaking detection for isolation.

### BS-32 — No frontier means undeterminable, not stable
**Given** a family whose pages carry no frontier (`MapCell`, `ListCell`, `WatermarkCell`,
`InstanceSet`)
**When** it is walked to completion, quiescently
**Then** the outcome reports stability as undeterminable — explicitly not "stable" — while
still reporting the walk as complete.
Discharges `[KRD-18]`.
`covers: [21-PULL-03]` — corpus-worthy; the requirement's family qualification is
load-bearing and this is the case that proves the implementation respects it rather than
defaulting to a comfortable answer.

### BS-33 — The OR-set qualification, demonstrated
**Given** a `SetCell` (observed-remove) being walked, and an element removed mid-walk
*after* the walk has already paged it — the removal copies existing add-tags into the
del-map and mints no tag
**When** the walk completes
**Then** both endpoint stamps are equal **and** the union names the removed element
present; the outcome reports the verdict as necessary-but-not-sufficient rather than as an
unqualified snapshot.
Discharges `[KRD-19]`.
`covers: [21-PULL-03]` — corpus-worthy, and it is the scenario a reviewer should look for
first, because it is the one that documents a real limit instead of a capability. Note the
existing `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` already records related state-family limits; if this
scenario cannot be driven implementation-neutrally, it belongs there rather than being
softened into a passing assertion.

### BS-34 — Stale intermediate frontiers do not weaken the verdict
**Given** a family that stamps intermediate pages with the stale-frontier caveat
**When** a quiescent walk completes with equal endpoint stamps
**Then** the outcome is a snapshot; the intermediate caveat is reported but does not
downgrade the verdict.
Discharges `[KRD-20]`, `[KRD-21]`.
`covers: [21-PULL-03]` — corpus-worthy; it pins the monotonicity argument that the landed
design rests on.

### BS-35 — The `since` escalation, and its refusal
**Given** a tag-carrying, `since`-supporting cell walked while being mutated
**When** the caller records the opening frontier, walks to completion, then issues one
further read with `since` set to it and folds the delta over the smeared union
**Then** the result equals the cell's state at the closing frontier.
**And given** a cell that does not support `since`, **when** the escalation is attempted
**then** it is refused with the existing named reason, on the caller's thread, and no
alternative path is taken.
Discharges `[KRD-22]`, `[KRD-23]`, `[KRD-25]`.
`covers: [21-PULL-03]` — corpus-worthy; the escalation is the spec's own stated remedy
(`21-propagation.md:199-201`) and is currently unexercised end to end.

---

## Ownership, disclosure, and non-duplication

### BS-40 — Exclusives are elided and counted, never paged
**Given** a cell whose state holds `Owned` and `Leased` values
**When** it is walked to completion
**Then** no page carries an exclusive value or a copy of one, each is replaced by its
presence descriptor, the elision count is non-zero, and that count appears in the walk
outcome — **and** no exclusive was borrowed, taken, released, or reflected into.
Discharges `[KRD-24]`, `[KRD-21]`.
`covers: [24-BOUND-01]` — corpus-worthy under `23-ownership`: the no-silent-drop,
no-copy rule for exclusive payloads is a system-wide invariant and boundary-observable
through the descriptor and the count.

### BS-41 — A bound is refused, never widened
**Given** a cell that declares no scope support (and, separately, no `since` support)
**When** a read carrying that bound is issued through the primitive
**Then** it is refused with the matching named reason, decided before any task reaches the
cell, and no wider state is returned.
Discharges `[KRD-25]`.
`covers: [24-BOUND-01]` — corpus-worthy; never-silently-widen is a decided rule.

### BS-42 — Stateful-but-not-bounded is refused, not copied
**Given** a `Stateful` cell that is not `BoundedStateful`, and a caller who did not opt into
a whole-state answer
**When** it is read through the primitive
**Then** it is refused with the not-bounded reason; **and when** the caller does opt in
**then** the whole value is returned, labelled as such.
Discharges `[KRD-26]`.
`covers: [24-BOUND-01]` — corpus-worthy; "never a silent whole copy" is the primitive's
stated purpose.

### BS-43 — One walk loop in the codebase
**Given** the merged diff
**When** implementations of "loop `readState` until the resume token is absent" and
"compare opening and closing frontier stamps" are enumerated
**Then** exactly one of each exists, or every additional one is recorded as a deliberate
exception with its reason.
Discharges `[KRD-27]`.
*Not a concord scenario* — a structural property. Kernel/architecture assertion plus the
`:inspect:test` regression gate.

---

## Note on corpus admission

The corpus-worthy scenarios above target `21-PULL-02`, `21-PULL-03`, `24-BOUND-01`,
`24-BOUND-02` and `24-DUR-05`. `21-PULL-02` and `21-PULL-03` reached the corpus through
V1C-CONCORD, which added a bounded-read verb to the conformance SPI
(`21-propagation.md:115-118`), so the machinery exists. If a scenario here needs a **new**
SPI verb — a three-way routing distinction (BS-02), fault injection (BS-12), or a
cancellation handle (BS-22) — that is a gated `concord/schema/*.md` change: file it, do not
invent a binding. Regenerate `doc/spec/CONCORDANCE.md` with
`./gradlew :concord:concordance`; never hand-edit it.

BS-33 is the scenario most likely to be undrivable implementation-neutrally. If it is, its
home is `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md`, recorded as the honest limit it describes — not a
weakened scenario that passes.

Ownership and disclosure: [KRD-24] [KRD-25] [KRD-26]. Non-duplication and additivity: [KRD-27] [KRD-28]. title: KBLK — Benchmark/bulk mode: durability-class journals, batched ingress dispatch, deterministic drive hooks
description:
# KBLK — Benchmark/bulk mode

Kernel-lane chunk **KBLK**, milestone plan §1 (kernel lane: *"WAL off/async host config,
batched ingress path, deterministic-time drive hooks"*, "config-level, small"), §3
(Nexmark row: *"KBLK for honest throughput (WAL sync would otherwise dominate)"*;
Graphalytics row: *"KBLK bulk load"*), §4 (*"KBLK is config-surface and slots into any
gap"*).

## Ambition / Why

Every BB throughput number depends on this, and BB-GRA's bulk load is blocked on it. The
reason is measured in the code, not assumed: `FileJournal.append` opens a
`FileOutputStream` **per record** and calls `out.fd.sync()` on every one
(`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/durability/Journal.kt:63-72`), and
`ManagedHost.enqueueHostedInvocation` submits **one scheduler task per accepted
invocation** (`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/ManagedHost.kt:644`, invariant
stated at `:630-632`). A throughput number taken through that path measures fsync latency
and task-dispatch overhead, not the dataflow engine — which makes it useless as a
comparability claim against Feldera/Flink and, worse, actively misleading in a findings
file.

Both deferrals are already marked in the code as awaiting exactly this workload:
- `Journal.kt:53-55` — *"one file, fsync per append, whole-log replay in memory — segments, group commit, and streaming replay when a real workload's journal hurts."*
- `ManagedHost.kt:626-628` — *"append holds `dataLock` so journal order == acceptance order; decouple via accept-sequence + async append if fsync contention matters."*
- The spec's own trigger, `doc/spec/20-dataflow-semantics/24-data-cells.md`: *"Remaining with a trigger: journal segmentation/rotation and the disk-overflow mailbox (33) — the first workload where one fsync'd file hurts."*

KBLK is the workload that pulls that trigger. It is small because the mechanisms it needs
are additive to a design that already anticipated them.

## The footgun, named up front

**A durability-off or relaxed-durability mode is a correctness footgun, and the shape of
the API decides whether it is a safe one.** The design rule this ticket is built around:

> **A relaxed durability guarantee is a property of the `Journal` instance a deployer
> constructs, never a host-level flag, an environment variable, or a system property.**

The reason is structural, not stylistic. `[24-DUR-01]` already makes durability a
**per-cell** decision expressed through `journalFor(cellRef)`. A host-level "WAL off"
boolean would sit *beside* that selector and silently override it: `journalFor` would keep
returning a real `Journal` for a `DURABLE`-manifest cell while the data went nowhere. Every
existing safety net in the codebase keys off the selector and would go on reporting green:

- `GraphDsl` refuses a `DURABLE` cell declared with no `journalId`
  (`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/graph/GraphDsl.kt:107,181-186`).
- `ManagedHost.volatileDurableSpawnCount` counts every `Manifest.DURABLE` cell spawned
  while `journalSelector(cell.ref) == null` (`ManagedHost.kt:375,963-965`, readable via
  `volatileDurableSpawns()` at `:378`) — it counts rather than refuses, deliberately
  (`:367-374`).

Routing the unsafe mode through the *journal instance* keeps every one of those nets
live, and makes "is this deployment durable?" answerable by inspecting the journals the
host was given — which is a thing a startup assertion can do.

Second consequence of the same rule: **"WAL off" is not a new feature.** The kernel
already has a correct, spec-blessed way to say it — `journalFor` returning `null`, which
`[24-DUR-01]` defines as *volatile: never journaled, never replayed*. A benchmark that
wants no durability configures that selector. Building a second way to mean the same thing
is how the two diverge. What is genuinely missing is the **middle** setting: a cell that
*is* journaled but whose journal batches its fsyncs — and that setting must announce
itself.

## What we build

1. **A durability class declared on `Journal`** — every journal states the guarantee it
   offers (synchronous-durable / batched / volatile-in-memory), so a host, a startup
   assertion and a findings file can all read it instead of guessing from the concrete
   type.
2. **A batched/group-commit `Journal`** implementing the relaxed class: records are
   appended and made visible in order, but fsync is amortized over a batch or a bound, with
   an explicit, documented loss window on crash.
3. **Deployment-gate accounting**: a host exposes how many of its cells are served by a
   journal that is not synchronously durable, alongside the existing
   `volatileDurableSpawns()` counter, so a durable deployment can assert zero at startup
   and a benchmark run can record what it actually ran with.
4. **A batched ingress path**: an admission seam that lets many accepted invocations share
   one scheduler dispatch task, changing *only* the number of tasks — never per-message
   ordering, wave/context semantics, journal order, or attention fairness.
5. **Deterministic drive hooks**: a supported, non-test-source-set way for a benchmark
   harness to drive a graph through the existing `SimulationController`
   (`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/SimulationController.kt:34`) —
   `step()`/`runToIdle(budget)`/seeded ordering — so a bulk load is driven to a defined
   quiescent point rather than slept on.

## How, using ComputeNet

**Durability class.** `Journal` (`Journal.kt:19`) gains a declared guarantee alongside
its three existing methods (`append`, `replay`, `reset`). `FileJournal` (`Journal.kt:56`)
declares synchronous-durable — it already fsyncs unconditionally at `Journal.kt:70` and
`:108`. `InMemoryJournal` (`Journal.kt:28`) declares itself non-durable across process
death, which is the honest statement of what it is and which nothing currently says out
loud. The new batched journal declares the relaxed class. The declaration is a constant
per instance and readable without touching the log.

**Batched journal.** A new implementation in `civictech.cell.durability` beside the
existing two. It keeps one file handle rather than reopening per record
(`Journal.kt:63-72` reopens every time), appends length-prefixed records in the same
format so `replay()` and `reset()` are unchanged and a batched log is byte-compatible with
`FileJournal`'s reader, and syncs on a bound. **Ordering is not relaxed**: records still
become replayable in append order, because `ManagedHost` appends under `dataLock` so that
journal order equals acceptance order (`ManagedHost.kt:626-628,639`) and `recoverFrom`
replays `journal.replay()` in index order (`HostDurability.kt:142-143`). What is relaxed
is *only* how much of the tail can be lost to a crash — and that window is the thing that
must be stated, bounded, and impossible to mistake for zero.

**Deployment gate.** The counter follows the precedent of `volatileDurableSpawnCount`
(`ManagedHost.kt:375,963-965`): the host observes, at spawn time, the class of the journal
its `journalSelector` returns for the cell, and accumulates a count per class. A durable
deployment asserts zero relaxed and zero volatile-durable at startup; a benchmark run
records the counts in its findings. Following the existing rationale at
`ManagedHost.kt:367-374`, the kernel **counts and exposes** rather than refusing — the
refusal belongs to the deployment's own assertion, because the kernel cannot know whether
a given host is a benchmark or production.

**Batched ingress.** The seam is the pair `ManagedHost.enqueueHostedInvocation`
(`ManagedHost.kt:567`, specifically the `enqueue(20) { attentionScheduler.dispatchOne() }`
at `:644`) and `AttentionScheduler.dispatchOne()`
(`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/control/AttentionScheduler.kt:93`, which dequeues
exactly one message at `:131`). Staging (`stage(...)`, `AttentionScheduler.kt:73`) is
untouched: every invocation is still staged individually, in order, and still journalled
individually under `dataLock` (`ManagedHost.kt:639`). Only the *dispatch task count*
changes — a dispatch task may drain up to a bound of staged messages instead of exactly
one.

This is deliberately **not** the coalescing path. `IntakeControl.coalesce`
(`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/IntakeControl.kt:73`, gated by
`IntakeBound`/`SaturationPolicy.Coalesce`,
`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/IntakeSaturation.kt:11,22`) *merges* messages
under saturation and is a backpressure device. Batched dispatch merges nothing and drops
nothing; it changes only how many scheduler tasks carry the same message sequence.

The invariant comment at `ManagedHost.kt:630-632` ("one dispatcher task per message keeps
message count <= task count") becomes false under this mode and must be restated rather
than left to rot — that is part of the diff, not a follow-up.

**Deterministic drive hooks.** `SimulationController` already provides everything needed:
seeded ordering (`:34-36`), `step()` (`:63`), `runToIdle(budget)` (`:79`) and a hard step
budget `DEFAULT_BUDGET = 60_000` (`:39-56`). It lives in `kernel/src/main`, so a future
`:bench` module can depend on it without depending on `:testkit`. The work here is to make
that a *supported* seam for a non-test consumer — a stable way to build a host on a
simulated scheduler and drive it to quiescence — rather than a new mechanism.
`testkit`'s `SimWorld` (`testkit/src/main/kotlin/civictech/testkit/SimWorld.kt:19-32`)
stays the test-side convenience; note its host is constructed with no journal, so it is
volatile by construction.

**No clock is introduced.** `kernel/src/main` contains no `Clock`, `TimeSource`,
`nanoTime` or `currentTimeMillis` — by design, per P1: *"there is no wall clock"*
(`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/Windows.kt:6`), *"No clock is read anywhere in
this file"* (`data/delta/TaggedMapDelta.kt:34`), *"never wall-clock"*
(`evolve/PromotionPolicy.kt:10,44`). "Deterministic-time drive hooks" in the chunk title
means *deterministic drive* — `step`/`runToIdle` — plus event time as an explicit element
attribute, which `Windows` already models. Reading the title as "add an injectable clock"
would violate P1 and is out of scope.

## Scope boundaries

- **No new host-level durability flag, environment variable, or system property.** See
  the footgun section — the whole design turns on this.
- **No change to the journal record format** (`RECORD_FRAME`/`RECORD_CHECKPOINT`/
  `RECORD_FRONTIER`, `HostDurability.kt:19-21`) and no change to `recoverFrom`'s replay
  order or its `RecoveryIncomplete` failure shape (`HostDurability.kt:120-174,30`).
- **No journal segmentation or rotation.** That is the *other* half of the same trigger
  sentence in spec 24 and a larger change; if the benchmark shows one file is the wall,
  that is a finding and a candidate ticket.
- **No relaxation of ordering.** Journal order equals acceptance order; replay order equals
  journal order. Only the fsync boundary moves.
- **No change to coalescing, saturation, parking or backpressure.**
- **No `:bench` module.** It does not exist (`settings.gradle.kts`) and it is BEN1's
  deliverable. KBLK provides the kernel seams BEN1 and the BB lane consume.
- **No wall clock, injectable or otherwise** (P1).
- **No `Effectful` interaction.** Whether a relaxed journal changes the processed-frontier
  story is KFX's and G-59's territory; KBLK must not touch
  `advanceAndJournalFrontier` (`HostDurability.kt:273`) semantics — but see
  `[KBLK-14]`, which forbids KBLK from *silently* weakening it.

## Functional requirements (EARS)

### Durability declaration and the unsafe mode

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KBLK-01]` Every `Journal` implementation SHALL declare the durability
guarantee it provides, and that declaration SHALL be readable without appending to or
replaying the log. *(`[24-DUR-01]`)*

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KBLK-02]` The existing `FileJournal` SHALL declare a synchronous-durable
guarantee and SHALL continue to fsync every append; `InMemoryJournal` SHALL declare that it
does not survive process death. No existing behaviour SHALL change. *(`[24-DUR-01]`,
`[24-DUR-02]`)*

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KBLK-03]` A relaxed-durability journal SHALL be selectable **only** by
constructing that journal instance and naming it from `journalFor(cellRef)`. There SHALL
be no host constructor flag, environment variable, system property, or global switch that
weakens the durability of a journal the selector named. *(`[24-DUR-01]`)*

*(Unwanted behaviour)* `[KBLK-04]` IF a caller wants no durability for a cell, THEN the
supported expression SHALL remain `journalFor(cellRef) == null` — the volatile case
`[24-DUR-01]` already defines — and no second mechanism meaning the same thing SHALL be
introduced. *(`[24-DUR-01]`)*

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KBLK-05]` A relaxed-durability journal SHALL state a bounded loss window
— the maximum quantity of appended-but-unsynced records — and that bound SHALL be a
constructor parameter of the instance, not a default a caller can inherit unknowingly.
*(`[24-DUR-01]`, `[24-DUR-02]`)*

*(State-driven)* `[KBLK-06]` WHILE a host is serving cells, it SHALL expose a per-durability-class
count of the cells its `journalFor` selector maps to, alongside the existing
volatile-durable-spawn count. *(`[24-DUR-01]`)*

*(Unwanted behaviour)* `[KBLK-07]` IF a deployment requires synchronous durability, THEN it
SHALL be able to assert that condition from `[KBLK-06]`'s counts at startup and fail
before accepting traffic; the kernel SHALL NOT make that refusal on the deployment's
behalf. *(`[24-DUR-01]`; matches the count-don't-refuse rationale at `ManagedHost.kt:367-374`)*

*(Unwanted behaviour)* `[KBLK-08]` IF a relaxed-durability journal is in use, THEN that fact
SHALL appear in the host's exposed accounting from the moment the first cell is mapped to
it — it SHALL NOT be inferable only from a crash. *(`[24-DUR-01]`)*

### Recovery is unchanged

*(Event-driven)* `[KBLK-09]` WHEN a host recovers from a relaxed-durability journal, it
SHALL replay the surviving records through the same `recoverFrom` path, in the same order,
with the same record-type dispatch, as it does for a synchronous journal. *(`[24-DUR-02]`)*

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KBLK-10]` A relaxed-durability journal's on-disk record format SHALL be
readable by the existing reader, so a log written by one implementation and replayed by
the other yields the identical record sequence. *(`[24-DUR-02]`)*

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KBLK-11]` A relaxed-durability journal SHALL preserve append order:
records SHALL become replayable in the order they were appended, so journal order continues
to equal acceptance order. *(`[24-DUR-02]`, `[24-DUR-03]`)*

*(Unwanted behaviour)* `[KBLK-12]` IF a crash truncates a relaxed-durability journal, THEN
recovery SHALL either replay a **prefix** of the appended records or fail with the existing
`RecoveryIncomplete` shape — it SHALL NOT replay a gapped or reordered subsequence.
*(`[24-DUR-02]`)*

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KBLK-13]` A journal SHALL continue to hold only its own cells' records, so
a relaxed journal's replay re-delivers nothing to a co-hosted cell mapped elsewhere.
*(`[24-DUR-03]`)*

*(Unwanted behaviour)* `[KBLK-14]` IF a relaxed-durability journal makes it possible for an
`Effectful` inlet's processed-frontier advance to be lost while the effect it recorded
already fired, THEN that SHALL be stated as a named limitation of the relaxed class and
recorded, and SHALL NOT be left implicit. *(`[24-DUR-05]`)*

### Batched ingress

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KBLK-15]` A batched ingress dispatch SHALL change only the number of
scheduler tasks used to dispatch a given sequence of accepted invocations. *(`[24-DUR-01]`;
30/31 normative rule 3, per-link FIFO)*

*(Event-driven)* `[KBLK-16]` WHEN batched dispatch is enabled, the per-link FIFO order of
delivered invocations SHALL be identical to the order produced without it, for the same
input sequence. *(30/31 normative rule 3)*

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KBLK-17]` Batched dispatch SHALL NOT merge, drop, reorder, or re-context
any invocation: each accepted invocation SHALL still be staged individually, journalled
individually, and delivered with the `MessageContext` it would otherwise carry.
*(`[24-DUR-01]`, `[21-PULL-02]`)*

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KBLK-18]` Wave, source and tag continuity SHALL be identical with and
without batched dispatch — a graph driven to quiescence SHALL reach the same state and the
same wave observations either way. *(`[24-BOUND-01]`; the wave-continuity invariant in
`AGENTS.md`)*

*(Unwanted behaviour)* `[KBLK-19]` IF batched dispatch is enabled, THEN a low-priority or
attention-yielding cell SHALL NOT be starved for longer than the batch bound — the batch
SHALL be bounded, and the bound SHALL be explicit. *(30/34 attention/stride rules)*

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KBLK-20]` The in-code invariant statement that message count is at most
task count SHALL be corrected in the same change that makes it false. *(documentation
consistency; no normative id — an accuracy obligation on the diff)*

*(Optional feature)* `[KBLK-21]` WHERE batched dispatch is not enabled, dispatch behaviour
SHALL be byte-for-byte the behaviour that exists today — one task per accepted invocation.
*(`[24-DUR-01]`)*

### Deterministic drive

*(Ubiquitous)* `[KBLK-22]` A non-test consumer SHALL be able to construct a host on the
existing simulated scheduler and drive it deterministically with the existing
`step()`/`runToIdle(budget)` seams, without depending on `:testkit`. *(50/52 verification:
deterministic simulation)*

*(Event-driven)* `[KBLK-23]` WHEN a bulk load is driven with the deterministic hooks and
the same seed, the resulting quiescent state SHALL be identical across runs.
*(50/52; the preserve-deterministic-simulation invariant in `AGENTS.md`)*

*(Unwanted behaviour)* `[KBLK-24]` IF the deterministic drive exceeds its step budget, THEN
it SHALL surface that as a bounded failure rather than looping — the existing budget
behaviour SHALL be preserved. *(50/52)*

*(Unwanted behaviour)* `[KBLK-25]` No wall-clock or injectable time source SHALL be added to
`kernel/src/main` under this ticket. *(P1, `doc/spec/00-foundations/02-design-principles.md`)*

### A requirement that cannot be checked honestly, stated rather than softened

`[KBLK-26]` *(recorded, not asserted)* "A relaxed-durability journal loses at most N
records on crash" cannot be verified end-to-end here. A real fsync-loss test needs power
loss or a filesystem fault injector; a JVM-level kill proves only that the *process* buffer
was flushed to the page cache, which is a strictly weaker claim. `[KBLK-05]` and
`[KBLK-12]` are therefore written as (a) the bound must be **declared** and (b) recovery
must be prefix-or-fail — both of which *are* checkable — and the physical-durability claim
is deliberately not made. A JVM-kill test may be written, and it must be documented as
proving prefix-consistency, **not** the loss bound. If someone wants the physical bound
asserted, it belongs in `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` as an open item, not as a
comfortably-passing test.

## Suggested task decomposition (list only — do not create these beads)

1. Durability-class declaration on `Journal`; declare it on `FileJournal` and
   `InMemoryJournal` with no behaviour change.
2. Batched/group-commit `Journal` implementation with an explicit loss bound and a single
   retained file handle; format-compatible with the existing reader.
3. Host-side per-class accounting beside `volatileDurableSpawnCount`, plus the read seam a
   startup assertion uses.
4. Batched dispatch at the `enqueue`/`dispatchOne` seam, bounded, off by default; correct
   the stale invariant comment.
5. Supported deterministic-drive entry point for a non-test consumer over
   `SimulationController`.
6. Tests: recovery equivalence across journal classes; prefix-or-fail truncation;
   FIFO/wave/state equivalence with and without batching; starvation bound; seeded
   determinism; the deployment-gate assertion.
7. Concord scenarios for the recovery-equivalence and prefix rules (see design notes);
   regenerate `CONCORDANCE.md`.

## Verification

```bash
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.durability.*'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.durability.CrashRecoveryTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.durability.EffectfulRecoveryTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.durability.MixedDurabilityTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.durability.DurableGlitchFreeReplayTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.host.*'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.control.AttentionSchedulerTest'
./gradlew :concord:test -Pconcord.profiles=core,dur
./gradlew :concord:check
./gradlew :demo:shopping:test
./gradlew :demo:exchange:test
./gradlew test
```

`:demo:exchange:test` is named explicitly: `ExchangeCompositionExitTest` is the repo's
toughest property gate and is the composition (partitioned + replicated + durable +
glitch-free) most likely to expose a dispatch-batching semantic regression.
`:concord:test -Pconcord.profiles=core,dur` is the durability profile that already drives
`DUR-REPLAY-01`/`DUR-SNAPTAIL-01` against the real machinery.

## Risks / open questions

1. **The footgun is the whole ticket.** The single most likely way this ticket does harm is
   by shipping a convenient host-level "fast mode" boolean because it is three lines
   shorter than a journal class. `[KBLK-03]`/`[KBLK-04]` exist to make that a review
   failure, not a taste argument.
2. **Batched dispatch and attention fairness.** `AttentionScheduler` exists to arbitrate
   priority and stride (30/34). Draining N messages in one task is exactly the shape that
   quietly starves a LOW-priority monitor. `[KBLK-19]` bounds it; whether the bound
   interacts correctly with the stride floor needs a directed test, and if it does not,
   batching may have to be per-priority-band rather than global. Flagged as the most
   likely place this "small" ticket grows.
3. **`dataLock` contention.** `ManagedHost.kt:626-628` notes that the append holds
   `dataLock`, so journal order equals acceptance order. A batched journal shortens the
   fsync but not the lock hold; if lock contention rather than fsync turns out to dominate,
   the accept-sequence decoupling named in that same comment is a *separate*, larger change
   — file it, don't absorb it.
4. **Interaction with `Effectful`.** `advanceAndJournalFrontier` (`HostDurability.kt:273`)
   advances the in-memory frontier and journals it together, in that order. Under a relaxed
   journal the durable half can be lost while the effect already fired. `[KBLK-14]` requires
   this be stated; whether it should also be *refused* (a relaxed journal declining to serve
   an `Effectful` cell) is an open question this ticket should answer explicitly rather than
   default.
5. **Where does "bulk load" actually hurt?** BB-GRA's bulk load may turn out to be bound by
   graph construction or per-cell spawn cost rather than by journal or dispatch. That is a
   BEN1/BB finding; KBLK should not pre-emptively optimize a path no number has indicted.
6. **Stale invariant comments.** `[KBLK-20]` covers the one known case
   (`ManagedHost.kt:630-632`). The diff should sweep for others in the touched paths rather
   than leaving contradicting prose in the kernel.
design:
# KBLK — Behaviour specifications

Given/When/Then, specific enough to become named tests. Each names the requirement ids it
discharges and, where it belongs in the executable specification, a `covers:` line.

---

## Durability declaration and the deployment gate

### BS-01 — A durable deployment refuses to start on a relaxed journal
**Given** a host whose `journalFor` maps at least one cell to a relaxed-durability journal
**When** a deployment that requires synchronous durability runs its startup assertion over
the host's per-class counts
**Then** the assertion fails and names the offending class and count, before any traffic is
accepted; **and** the kernel itself has neither refused nor logged a warning of its own.
Discharges `[KBLK-06]`, `[KBLK-07]`, `[KBLK-08]`.
*Not a concord scenario* — it asserts a host configuration API, not observable graph
behaviour. Kernel test beside the existing `volatileDurableSpawns()` coverage.

### BS-02 — There is no back door
**Given** a host constructed with a `journalFor` returning a synchronous-durable
`FileJournal` for every cell
**When** every host construction parameter, every system property and every environment
variable available to the process is exercised
**Then** no combination causes that cell's appends to skip their fsync — the guarantee is
determined by the instance and by nothing else.
Discharges `[KBLK-03]`.
*Not a concord scenario* — it is an API-shape assertion. Enforce it as a test plus an
explicit review checklist item; a grep-style architecture assertion (no durability-related
`System.getenv`/`getProperty` in `civictech.cell.durability` or `ManagedHost`) is the
cheapest durable form.

### BS-03 — "No durability" has exactly one spelling
**Given** the requirement to run a cell with no journal
**When** the codebase is searched for mechanisms that make a cell non-journaled
**Then** the only one is `journalFor(cellRef) == null`, and any `DURABLE`-manifest cell
reaching that path is still counted by `volatileDurableSpawns()`.
Discharges `[KBLK-04]`.
`covers: [24-DUR-01]` — the *volatile* half is corpus-worthy: a volatile cell is never
journaled and never replayed, which is boundary-observable through a crash-and-recover
scenario. The "exactly one spelling" half is a kernel/architecture assertion.

---

## Recovery equivalence

### BS-10 — Same log, same recovery, either implementation
**Given** an identical sequence of accepted invocations applied to two hosts, one using
`FileJournal` and one using the batched journal, each cleanly closed
**When** each log is replayed by `recoverFrom` — and then cross-replayed, each log read by
the *other* implementation's reader
**Then** all four replays yield the identical record sequence and the identical recovered
state.
Discharges `[KBLK-09]`, `[KBLK-10]`, `[KBLK-11]`.
`covers: [24-DUR-02]` — corpus-worthy: "restore from a snapshot plus the journal tail
equals an uninterrupted twin" is already the shape of `DUR-SNAPTAIL-01`, and this is that
property held invariant across durability classes.

### BS-11 — Truncation yields a prefix, or a named failure
**Given** a batched journal whose file is truncated at an arbitrary byte offset, swept
across many offsets including mid-record
**When** the host recovers from it
**Then** for every offset the outcome is either (a) replay of a proper **prefix** of the
appended records, in order, or (b) the existing `RecoveryIncomplete(recordIndex, total,
cause)` failure with a dead-letter — never a gapped subsequence, never a reordered one,
never a silently-shortened success that claims completeness.
Discharges `[KBLK-12]`.
`covers: [24-DUR-02]` — corpus-worthy as the failure/recovery boundary case; the corpus
already drives crash-and-replay through a journal controller.
**Note the honesty limit**: this proves prefix-consistency of the *reader*, not the
physical loss bound — see `[KBLK-26]`.

### BS-12 — Per-cell scoping survives the new class
**Given** two cells on one host mapped to two different journals, one relaxed and one
synchronous
**When** the relaxed journal alone is replayed
**Then** only its own cell's records are re-delivered; the co-hosted cell receives nothing.
Discharges `[KBLK-13]`.
`covers: [24-DUR-03]` — corpus-worthy; `MixedDurabilityTest` is the existing kernel
precedent for the same property.

### BS-13 — The Effectful window is stated, not discovered
**Given** an `Effectful` cell served by a relaxed journal, whose effect fires and whose
processed-frontier advance is appended but not yet synced
**When** the process dies and the host recovers
**Then** whatever happens — the effect re-fires, or it does not — is the documented,
declared behaviour of the relaxed class, recorded in the ticket's findings; **and** if the
answer is "the effect can re-fire", the relaxed class says so in its own contract rather
than leaving `[24-DUR-05]` looking unconditional.
Discharges `[KBLK-14]`.
*Not a new concord scenario, and deliberately so* — `24-DUR-05` is already covered by
`DUR-REPLAY-01`, and `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` already records the G-59/C-9 boundary
around that requirement. A relaxed-journal weakening of `24-DUR-05` belongs in
**`DISPUTES.md` as an extension of that existing boundary entry**, not as a corpus
scenario asserting a weaker rule. Writing a passing scenario for the weaker behaviour would
be exactly the "weakened into a passing scenario" failure `AGENTS.md` forbids.

---

## Batched ingress

### BS-20 — Identical order, identical state, fewer tasks
**Given** a graph with several links and a fixed input sequence, driven on the
deterministic scheduler with a fixed seed
**When** it is run once with batched dispatch off and once with it on
**Then** the delivered per-link invocation sequences are identical, the quiescent state is
identical, and the observed wave positions are identical — while the count of dispatch
tasks is strictly lower in the batched run.
Discharges `[KBLK-15]`, `[KBLK-16]`, `[KBLK-17]`, `[KBLK-18]`.
`covers: [24-BOUND-01]` for the state half — but the *equivalence* framing is
implementation-facing (task counts are not boundary-observable), so the primary home is a
kernel test. The corpus contribution is the ordinary FIFO/convergence property, which the
existing corpus already asserts and which must simply keep passing under the batched mode.

### BS-21 — A batch does not starve a yielding cell
**Given** a saturated high-priority ingress and a LOW-priority monitor cell in the same
host, with batched dispatch enabled at bound `B`
**When** the graph is driven
**Then** the monitor is dispatched at least once every `B` dispatched messages — the batch
bound is the starvation bound, and it holds.
Discharges `[KBLK-19]`.
*Not a concord scenario* — scheduling fairness is internal timing, and `AGENTS.md`
directs tests to assert semantic outcomes rather than scheduling timing. This is a
counted, deterministic kernel test on `SimulationController`, expressed as "dispatch
counts", not wall time.

### BS-22 — Off means unchanged
**Given** batched dispatch disabled (the default)
**When** any existing host test in `kernel/src/test` is run
**Then** every one passes unchanged, and the dispatch path is the same one-task-per-message
path as before.
Discharges `[KBLK-21]`.
*Not a concord scenario* — it is the regression gate, discharged by the existing suite.

### BS-23 — Journal order still equals acceptance order under batching
**Given** batched dispatch enabled on a journaled host
**When** a sequence of invocations is accepted and the log is replayed
**Then** the replayed record order equals the acceptance order — batching dispatch did not
reorder the append that happens under `dataLock`.
Discharges `[KBLK-11]`, `[KBLK-15]`.
`covers: [24-DUR-02]` — corpus-worthy; it is the composition of the two mechanisms this
ticket touches, and it is exactly where an incorrect implementation would break.

---

## Deterministic drive

### BS-30 — Same seed, same quiescent state
**Given** a bulk load of a fixed input set driven through the deterministic hooks with seed
`S`
**When** the run is repeated with the same seed, several times
**Then** the quiescent state is identical every time, and so is the step count to reach it.
Discharges `[KBLK-22]`, `[KBLK-23]`.
*Not a concord scenario* — the corpus is already run as a seeded sweep by its own harness;
this asserts the drive seam a `:bench` consumer uses. Kernel test.
**Do not replace a failing seed with a friendlier seed** (`AGENTS.md`).

### BS-31 — Budget exhaustion is bounded, not a hang
**Given** a graph that cannot reach quiescence (a live-locked or continuously-emitting
shape) driven with `runToIdle(budget)`
**When** the budget is exhausted
**Then** the drive returns or fails within the budget, reporting the step count — it does
not loop indefinitely.
Discharges `[KBLK-24]`.
*Not a concord scenario* — a harness liveness property. Kernel test; the budget behaviour
already exists (`SimulationController.DEFAULT_BUDGET`) and must be preserved, not
reinvented.

### BS-32 — No clock enters the kernel
**Given** the diff produced by this ticket
**When** `kernel/src/main` is searched for `Clock`, `TimeSource`, `Instant`,
`System.nanoTime`, `System.currentTimeMillis`
**Then** the count of code (non-KDoc) hits is still zero.
Discharges `[KBLK-25]`.
*Not a concord scenario* — an architecture assertion. It is worth writing as an actual
guard test, because "just inject a clock for the benchmark" is the natural and wrong
instinct here, and P1 is a system-wide invariant.

---

## Note on corpus admission

Scenarios marked corpus-worthy above target `24-DUR-01/02/03` and reuse the existing
`dur`-profile machinery (journal controller cell, crash/restart via despawn,
`views-converge`, `incremental-equals-batch`). If any needs a **new** check kind or driver
type binding, that is a `concord/schema/*.md` change and is gated — file it rather than
inventing a binding. Regenerate `doc/spec/CONCORDANCE.md` with
`./gradlew :concord:concordance`; never hand-edit it.

The one thing that must **not** happen: a relaxed-durability weakening of `24-DUR-05`
turning into a corpus scenario that passes. That belongs in
`concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md`, appended to the existing G-59/C-9 boundary entry.
acceptance_criteria: Durability declaration and the unsafe mode: [KBLK-01] [KBLK-02] [KBLK-03] [KBLK-04] [KBLK-05] [KBLK-06] [KBLK-07] [KBLK-08]. Recovery unchanged: [KBLK-09] [KBLK-10] [KBLK-11] [KBLK-12] [KBLK-13] [KBLK-14]. Batched ingress: [KBLK-15] [KBLK-16] [KBLK-17] [KBLK-18] [KBLK-19] [KBLK-20] [KBLK-21]. Deterministic drive: [KBLK-22] [KBLK-23] [KBLK-24] [KBLK-25]. Recorded-not-asserted: [KBLK-26] must be honoured as written (no physical fsync loss-bound claim). [KBLK-03] and [KBLK-04] are hard review gates: a host-level durability flag, env var or system property is a review failure, not a taste argument. Behaviour specs BS-01..BS-32 in the design notes; corpus-marked scenarios admitted per their covers: ids, and any relaxed-journal weakening of 24-DUR-05 goes to concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md, never to a passing scenario.
