## 3. Risks and open questions

- **The handoff store is a placement decision in disguise.** "Durable storage" for a *decentralized*
  system begs the question *whose disk*. This chunk takes the narrow, buildable reading: the
  departing peer's own `Journal`, selected exactly like per-cell durability. That means the data
  survives only if that peer comes back. Handing off to *another* peer's store is migration, and is
  scoped out (§4) — but SOC3's real requirement may be the wider one, and if so this chunk delivers
  a stepping stone rather than the answer. Worth deciding before claiming.
- **`[MEM2-03]`'s bound holds only for a bounded membership.** Stated honestly in body §5.8(2). If
  SOC3 needs the open-mesh bound, that is a research entry, not a test.
- **CHA3's shape is not yet fixed.** MEM2's suite consumes whatever CHA3 exposes. If CHA3 lands as
  a scripted rather than a seeded/shrinking rig, `[MEM2-22]` (retain the failing seed) and
  `[MEM2-33]` (no inconclusive run) become harder to honor. Flag at CHA3 review time.
- **`Peering.Loopback.partition()` is a park, not a loss.** Until CHA1's frame interposer lands,
  every "churn" test here uses a strictly weaker adversary than the network. Named blocker in the
  disputes entry.
- **`shipTo` link-identity asymmetry.** `Replication.maybeLink` derives `gossipRef`;
  `SingleWriterReplication.shipTo` does not and relies on `onUnpublish` unlinking. MEM1 adds a
  second teardown route (step-down); MEM2's churn plan is where an accumulated orphan would first
  become visible. Either derive the ref or prove teardown is total —
  `ShippingLinkIdempotenceTest` is the guard, and it currently tests one cycle, not N.
- **No normative spec id for handoff.** `[42-REPL-*]` covers convergence, catch-up and orderly
  departure; nothing states handoff. Corpus coverage waits on a spec ticket (body §5.8(5)); this
  chunk does not edit `doc/spec/` (§4).
- **Stale spec status header.** `doc/spec/40-distribution/42-replication.md:300` still reads
  "not built" for single-writer replication, which *is* built. Recorded in
  `doc/replication/findings.md` for the periodic integration pass (plan §6), not fixed here.
acceptance_criteria: Ubiquitous [MEM2-01]..[MEM2-05]; event-driven [MEM2-06]..[MEM2-11]; state-driven [MEM2-12]..[MEM2-15]; unwanted-behaviour [MEM2-16]..[MEM2-23]; optional-feature [MEM2-24]..[MEM2-28]; complex [MEM2-29]..[MEM2-33]. Behaviours 5.1 last replica leaves with handoff, 5.2 last replica leaves without handoff (accidental-deletion refusal), 5.3 handoff interrupted mid-flight (a/b/c), 5.4 data loss on reconvergence with divergence control, 5.5 duplicate/stale link accumulation, 5.6 unclean departure stays frozen, 5.7 rehydration into a live set. Properties named in 5.8 are filed in concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md, not asserted by a weak test. Verification per section 6.

title: MEM1 — G-44 epoch-claim election + failure detection
description:
# MEM1 — G-44 epoch-claim election + failure detection

Milestone-plan chunk **MEM1** (kernel lane, §4 position 6: *"MEM1 → MEM2 — election, then
churn with CHA3"*). Row verbatim: *"MEM1 | G-44 epoch-claim election + failure detection |
Depends on: KX, KE3 | Unblocks / feeds: SOC3."* The DAG additionally carries
`KE3 -.E3.6 gates.-> MEM1`.

**Kernel-lane serialization (G-63, one SCC).** This chunk edits `civictech.cell.replication`,
`civictech.cell.host` and `civictech.cell.wire` — the exact files every other kernel chunk
touches. It MUST be admitted to the lane alone, after KE3 has merged to `main`, and its branch
MUST start from the merged KE3 commit rather than from a locally recreated equivalent
(AGENTS.md §Multi-agent run discipline). MEM2 follows it in the same lane; nothing else runs
concurrently inside the SCC.

---

## 1. Ambition / Why

Single-writer replication **is built** (contrary to the stale status header on
`doc/spec/40-distribution/42-replication.md:300`, which still says "not built"):
`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/replication/SingleWriterReplication.kt` ships the
`LeaderMark` epoch fold, `Stamped<D>` epoch-stamped log units, one-direction leader→follower
shipping (`shipTo`), typed follower redirect/reject (`forwardWrites`), and RESTART-by-peer-
catch-up (`restartCatchUp`). What it ships is the **safety half**. Its own KDoc names the
hole (lines 30-33):

> *"Automatic election that mints these marks is the deferred liveness half (G-44 residual,
> 95 §R1); this ticket ships EXPLICIT/orchestrated designation only."*

G-44 (`91-gap-analysis.md:95`) is exactly that residual: *"no automatic leader election, no
failure detector, and split-brain reconciliation beyond last-epoch-wins is undesigned."*

Three facts from the survey make the size of the gap concrete:

1. **`LeaderMark` never crosses the wire.** It is not registered in
   `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/wire/WireCodec.kt` (`Stamped`, `WatermarkDelta`,
   `Assignment`, `RoutedCommand`'s `routingEpoch` all are). `leaderMarks` is a peer-local
   `MutableMap<UUID, LeaderMark>`. So today two peers can hold different leaders with no
   mechanism that converges them. An election that mints marks locally without an
   announcement kind would manufacture split brain rather than resolve it.
2. **There is no failure detector, heartbeat, lease, clock, or timer anywhere in `:kernel`,
   `:wire` or `:testkit`.** Failure is observed *structurally*: transport close →
   `LocationRegistry.unpublishRemotes(sink)` → `onUnpublish` → linker reconciliation, and
   `replicasOf(id)` shrinking **is** the "partitioned" observation `Replication.evict`
   already gates on. `SimulationController` is step/priority ordered with no `advanceTime`
   and no scheduled-delay API. G-44's own wording — *"a failure-detection window that does
   not become a second heartbeat protocol"* — is therefore a hard constraint, not a
   preference: there is nothing to build a heartbeat *on*.
3. **`designateLeader` is the only claim path and it is manual.** It folds strictly-greater
   epochs and returns `false` otherwise. Nothing ever calls it in response to a failure.

SOC3 ("decentralized: open mesh, **election-backed groups**, budget-bounded interest") is
hard-blocked on this. MEM2's churn story needs a leadership answer to churn against.

Research entry **95 §R1** already ranked the directions: (1) leadership as a fold over
registry announcements with a deterministic rendezvous, (2) leadership-as-promotion via the
53 machinery, (3) classical consensus — explicitly *not* preferred. 93 I-25 §4.5 already
**decided** the shape: *"an opt-in posture lets a follower claim leadership by minting a
higher epoch and re-announcing a `LeaderMark` … a deterministic epoch bump folded from
ordinary announcements, not a vote."* MEM1 is the implementation of that decided design plus
the failure-detection window and the reconciliation hook G-44 names, and the honest statement
of what a no-consensus election cannot promise.

---

## 2. What we build

**In-place kernel change**, not a new module. Replication is a kernel concern and the kernel
must stay transport-neutral (AGENTS.md); the only new transport-adjacent work is one
additional `RegistryAnnounce` method and one `WireCodec` registration.

### 2.1 Package layout

| Path | Change |
|---|---|
| `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/replication/SingleWriterReplication.kt` | Extend: `ElectionPosture`, claim minting, step-down on strictly-greater fold, unlink-on-stepdown, per-shard leader routing |
| `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/replication/LeaderElection.kt` (**new**) | The claim rule and the detection window — a pure, injected policy object so it is testable without a host |
| `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/replication/Reconciliation.kt` (**new**) | The application-level hook for fenced divergent writes (G-44's *"application-level reconciliation hook"*) |
| `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/wire/Peering.kt` | Add `RegistryAnnounce.leaderMarked(mark)` — a fifth ids-only announcement, served by `RegistryMirrorCell` |
| `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/wire/WireCodec.kt` | Register `LeaderMark` (ids-only: `UUID`, `Long`, `CellRef`); additive, no version bump |
| `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/LocationRegistry.kt` | The leader-mark fold lands on the membership lane KX extracts as `InstanceIndex` — **this is why MEM1 depends on KX** |
| `kernel/src/test/kotlin/civictech/cell/replication/LeaderElectionTest.kt` (**new**) | Election safety + seeded leader-churn suite |
| `kernel/src/test/kotlin/civictech/cell/replication/SplitBrainReconciliationTest.kt` (**new**) | Partition/heal, dual-leader window, reconciliation delivery |
| `concord/corpus/42-replication/` | Scenarios per §5 `covers:` notes (spec-id availability caveat in §5) |
| `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` | The unverifiable-in-one-process properties (§5.7) |
| `doc/replication/findings.md` | Lane findings per plan §6 (append-only; never edits `91-gap-analysis.md`) |

### 2.2 Entry points

- `SingleWriterReplication(registry, keyOf, election: LeaderElection = LeaderElection.Manual)`
  — the constructor gains one defaulted parameter. `LeaderElection.Manual` reproduces today's
  behaviour byte-for-byte.
- `LeaderElection.EpochClaim(window: DetectionWindow)` — the opt-in posture.
- `SingleWriterReplication.designateLeader(mark)` — unchanged signature, unchanged semantics
  (strictly-greater wins); the claim path calls the same fold, so there is one fold, not two.
- `SingleWriterReplication.onDivergentWrite(handler)` — the reconciliation hook.
- `RegistryAnnounce.leaderMarked(mark: LeaderMark)` — the announcement kind.

---

## 3. Functional requirements (EARS)

Ids are epoch-scoped `[MEM1-nn]`, namespaced so they never collide with `doc/spec/`'s
`[NN-SLUG-nn]`. Each cites the normative text it makes true.

### Ubiquitous

- **[MEM1-01]** A leadership claim SHALL be an ordinary `LeaderMark` announcement folded into
  the eventually-consistent membership index — never a vote, quorum, view number, lease, or
  second synchronization protocol. *(42 §Single-writer replication "a deterministic epoch bump
  folded from ordinary announcements, not a vote"; 93 I-25 §4.5, §5 P4; G-44)*
- **[MEM1-02]** Epoch order SHALL be total over `(counter, tiebreak = instanceId)`: compare
  counter, then instanceId. *(93 I-25 §4.1 `Epoch = (counter: Long, tiebreak: InstanceId)`)*
- **[MEM1-03]** `leaderOf(logicalId)` SHALL be a pure maximum over locally folded marks — no
  blocking, no round trip, and no presence on the write fast path. *(93 I-25 §5 P2; 42
  §Leadership is a `LeaderMark` epoch fold)*
- **[MEM1-04]** Every delta a leader produces SHALL carry the epoch it applied under
  (`Stamped.epoch`), and any delta or forwarded command stamped below the locally folded epoch
  SHALL be inert. *(42 §Leadership is a `LeaderMark` epoch fold; `[42-REPL-04]`)*
- **[MEM1-05]** Automatic election SHALL be opt-in per single-writer logical cell; with the
  posture unset, behaviour SHALL be identical to the shipped explicit-designation path.
  *(42 §Failover is explicit by default; 93 I-25 §4 "Candidate C as its default failover
  posture"; P6)*
- **[MEM1-06]** Leadership state SHALL be derivable from announcements alone: a peer joining
  an already-elected set SHALL converge to the same `leaderOf` as its peers without any
  peer-to-peer election exchange. *(42 §Replica discovery & membership; `[41-LOC-01]`)*

### Event-driven (WHEN)

- **[MEM1-07]** WHEN a follower with `EpochClaim` enabled observes that `leaderOf(id)`'s
  `leaderRef` is absent from `LocationRegistry.replicasOf(id)` for a full detection window, it
  SHALL mint `epoch = (maxSeenCounter + 1, selfInstanceId)` and announce a `LeaderMark` naming
  its own ref. *(42 §Failover is explicit by default, opt-in clause; 93 I-25 §4.5; G-44)*
- **[MEM1-08]** WHEN a peer folds a `LeaderMark` whose epoch is strictly greater than the
  folded epoch, a local leader SHALL step down: stop serving the real write inlet, revert its
  write inlet to a `forwardWrites` delegate at the new `leaderRef`, and catch up from it.
  *(42 §Leadership is a `LeaderMark` epoch fold; 93 I-25 §4.5 epoch fence)*
- **[MEM1-09]** WHEN a peer folds a `LeaderMark` whose epoch is not strictly greater than the
  folded epoch, it SHALL reject the mark and leave every local role unchanged.
  *(93 I-25 §4.1; today's `designateLeader` return-`false` path)*
- **[MEM1-10]** WHEN a claim is adopted, every local follower SHALL re-point its command-
  forward delegate at the new `leaderRef` before the next write is accepted at that inlet.
  *(42 §Leader = the single applying instance; 93 I-25 §4.2)*
- **[MEM1-11]** WHEN a `LeaderMark` is adopted locally, it SHALL be announced to peers as an
  ids-only `RegistryAnnounce` variant. *(93 I-25 §4.1 "one more `RegistryAnnounce` variant
  carrying ids only, wire ids-only, version byte reserved"; §5 P9)*
- **[MEM1-12]** WHEN a partition heals and two `LeaderMark`s are folded, the strictly higher
  epoch SHALL become canonical and the loser SHALL step down and re-catch-up from the winner.
  *(42 §Always-fenced writes; `[42-REPL-05]`)*
- **[MEM1-13]** WHEN a stepped-down leader holds writes it served under a now-superseded epoch
  which the winner did not receive, those writes SHALL be surfaced on the cell's
  error/dead-letter path and delivered to any registered reconciliation handler, carrying
  epoch, source and payload. *(42 §Always-fenced writes "surfaced on the error/dead-letter
  path, never silently dropped"; G-44 "an application-level reconciliation hook for fenced
  divergent writes")*
- **[MEM1-14]** WHEN supervision RESTART recovers a leader in place (same `instanceId`), no
  claim SHALL be minted and no epoch SHALL be bumped. *(42 §RESTART = peer catch-up; 93 I-25
  §4.4 step 1, §4.5 first bullet)*
- **[MEM1-15]** WHEN a leader steps down, its outbound shipping links SHALL be `Link.unlink`ed,
  not merely dropped from bookkeeping, because follower apply is non-idempotent.
  *(`SingleWriterReplication` `onUnpublish` KDoc, T07 finding 1 Divergence B)*

### State-driven (WHILE)

- **[MEM1-16]** WHILE `leaderOf(id)` is unresolved or contested, a write parked on the
  single-writer cell SHALL remain parked, and SHALL be released only once exactly one
  epoch-confirmed leader exists. *(93 I-25 §4.6 the parked-sender safety rule)*
- **[MEM1-17]** WHILE `EpochClaim` is enabled and the current leader's ref is present in
  `replicasOf(id)`, no claim SHALL be minted. *(P6 "no leader elected just in case"; 93 I-25
  §5 P6)*
- **[MEM1-18]** WHILE a follower has an established shipping link from its leader, it SHALL NOT
  gossip deltas back. *(42 §One-direction shipping, follower FIFO apply)*
- **[MEM1-19]** WHILE an election is in progress, `ReplicaQuorum.frontier` reads, delivered-
  watermark rows and the FU-2 membership barrier SHALL be unaffected — election SHALL introduce
  no new hold on wave settlement. *(96 §E3.6; 20/22 §Interest-scoped settlement)*

### Unwanted behaviour (IF/THEN)

- **[MEM1-20]** IF two followers claim concurrently at the same counter, THEN exactly one epoch
  SHALL be canonical at every peer once the marks converge (decided by the `instanceId`
  tiebreak), and the loser's deltas SHALL be fenced inert at every follower.
  *(93 I-25 §4.1 total order; §4.5 epoch fence)*
- **[MEM1-21]** IF the detection window fires against a leader that is alive but merely
  unreachable, THEN the resulting dual-leader window SHALL NOT produce a silently merged
  history: the loser's post-claim writes SHALL be surfaced per `[MEM1-13]`, and both sides'
  states SHALL remain individually well-formed. *(93 I-25 §4.7 `AVAILABLE_FENCED`; 42
  §Always-fenced writes)*
- **[MEM1-22]** IF a folded epoch would regress — a lower or equal mark, a replayed
  announcement, a duplicate delivery, or a mark re-announced by a peer that has not yet learned
  of a higher one — THEN it SHALL be discarded and every local role SHALL be unchanged.
  *(93 I-25 §4.1; 42 §Anti-entropy idempotence)*
- **[MEM1-23]** IF a would-be claimant's reachable membership is only itself, THEN it SHALL NOT
  claim. A sole survivor minting an epoch it can never gossip is the split-brain generator, and
  the last-replica case is MEM2's handoff, not an election. *(42 §Eviction is a gated
  drain+despawn suspend rule; G-45 last-replica handoff)*
- **[MEM1-24]** IF a `Leased` payload write lands off-leader, THEN it SHALL be `Rejected` and
  SHALL NOT be forwarded — unchanged by election. *(42 §Leader = the single applying instance;
  20/23; 93 I-25 §4.2)*
- **[MEM1-25]** IF a detection window is expressed as a wall clock, a background thread, a
  periodic heartbeat frame, or any new timer subsystem, THEN it SHALL be refused. Detection
  MUST ride the existing announcement/unpublish substrate and the host scheduler.
  *(G-44 "a failure-detection window that does not become a second heartbeat protocol"; P1;
  the survey finding that no clock/timer/heartbeat exists in `:kernel`, `:wire` or `:testkit`)*
- **[MEM1-26]** IF a synchronous ack-from-k durability tier is requested, THEN it SHALL be
  refused with the stated async primary-backup window rather than implemented. G-44's proposal
  line names an *optional* ack tier; 93 I-25 §4.4 decided against it ("would be a second
  protocol and is explicitly **not** adopted"), and the authority order puts the integrated
  decision above the older gap prose. The durability lever is G-25 checkpointing (MEM2).
  *(93 I-25 §4.4 Durability bound; AGENTS.md authority order)*

### Optional feature (WHERE)

- **[MEM1-27]** WHERE a single-writer logical structure is partitioned into disjoint-`Interest`
  shards, leadership SHALL be per shard: each partition ref folds its own `LeaderMark`, and no
  cross-shard leader SHALL exist. *(G-44 "per-shard leader routing when partitions replicate";
  93 I-8, I-25 §6 "a partitioned SW structure's partitions are ordinary cells, each replicating
  SW per its own `replicasOf(partitionRef)`")*
- **[MEM1-28]** WHERE an application registers a reconciliation handler, fenced divergent writes
  SHALL be delivered to it in addition to the dead-letter path; WHERE none is registered, the
  dead-letter path alone SHALL carry them. *(G-44; 42 §Always-fenced writes)*
- **[MEM1-29]** WHERE the single-writer cell is also `Effectful` on a Total/overlapping instance
  set, the elected leader SHALL remain the sole effect authority across the handoff: exactly one
  effect firing per logical delta across an election. *(31 §Effects on instance sets, PN-17;
  `SingleWriterReplication.requireEffectAuthority`)*
- **[MEM1-30]** WHERE `WritePosture.SAFETY_PARK` is reintroduced (G-67, not in scope here), the
  election path SHALL compose with it without redesign — the claim rule reads the posture, it
  does not encode one. *(G-67; 93 I-25 §4.7)*

### Complex (combinations)

- **[MEM1-31]** WHEN a claim is adopted WHILE the previous leader is mid-shipment, a follower
  SHALL apply an in-flight delta only if its `Stamped.epoch` is at or above the locally folded
  epoch, and SHALL fence the remainder, such that no follower's state contains a mix of two
  epochs' non-idempotent applies. *(42 §One-direction shipping; 93 I-25 §4.5 epoch fence;
  `[42-REPL-04]`)*
- **[MEM1-32]** WHERE election is enabled AND the cell declares durable journaling, IF the
  claimant's catch-up donor is unreachable, THEN the claimant SHALL fall back to its own
  checkpoint and SHALL announce the resulting state as a re-baseline rather than as a
  continuation. *(42 §RESTART = peer catch-up "checkpoint restore is the solo fallback";
  `[24-DUR-02]`, `[24-TAG-02]`)*
- **[MEM1-33]** WHEN a claim is adopted WHILE a downstream `ReplicaQuorum` consumer holds a
  keyed wave, the new leader's first shipment SHALL NOT release that wave earlier than the
  covering quorum permits — election SHALL NOT bypass the R13 creation fence or the FU-2
  membership barrier. *(96 §E3.4 PN-7 amendment; `ReplicaQuorum.frontier`)*

---

## 4. Scope boundaries

Traced to the plan's dependency edges.

**In scope:** the four G-44 residuals that 93 I-25 already decided or that follow from it —
opt-in epoch-claim election, a failure-detection window built on the existing announcement
substrate, split-brain reconciliation beyond last-epoch-wins (the application hook), and
per-shard leader routing.

**Out of scope, by dependency edge:**

- **KX (`computenet-iyi`) — hard prerequisite.** The claim fold lands on the `byLogicalId` /
  interest membership lane C-13 flags for extraction into `InstanceIndex`
  (`91-gap-analysis.md:21`). MEM1 MUST consume KX's extracted surface, not re-fold membership
  locally and not perform the extraction itself.
- **KE3 — hard prerequisite, E3.6 gates.** 96 §E3.6 fixes what membership means for the two
  watermark reads: `replicasOf` snapshotted per read with the eventual-consistency caveat;
  clean departure closes a row; unclean departure freezes stability and surfaces a `Stall`,
  *not worked around*. MEM1's failure detector observes the same membership seam, so it must
  be built against E3.6's landed semantics. **KE3 is being created by another agent — it is an
  unwired dep here.**
- **MEM2 (G-45 churn + last-replica handoff)** — everything about a replica set shrinking to
  zero, and every durable-handoff question, belongs there. `[MEM1-23]` is the boundary marker.
- **R13 lease-fenced row eviction** — explicitly research-gated (95 §R13, 96 §E3.6(c)). MEM1
  MUST NOT introduce a lease to evict a frozen row.
- **G-67 `WritePosture.SAFETY_PARK`** — deleted in remediation T03 for having zero installs;
  reintroduction waits on a real user. `[MEM1-30]` only requires composability.
- **G-62 economic layer** — *when* to elect (attention, placement, budget) stays with PLC2/ECO1.
- **Consensus of any kind** — rejected in 93 I-25 §3 Candidate A and 95 §R1 direction 3.
- **CHA3 / generative membership-churn harness** — MEM2 consumes it. MEM1 writes its own seeded
  leader-churn suite (95 §R1 names one) but does not build the general churn rig.
- **Plan/spec editing** — no edits to `91-gap-analysis.md`, `42-replication.md`,
  `CONCORDANCE.md` or the milestone plan from this chunk; lane findings go to
  `doc/replication/findings.md` (plan §6). The stale "not built" status header on
  `42-replication.md:300` is a finding, not a fix.

---

## 5. Behaviour specifications

Given/When/Then, specific enough to become named tests.

### 5.1 Split brain — partition with a leader on each side

> **Given** a three-peer single-writer replica set with `EpochClaim` enabled, leader `L@epoch(1,L)`
> on peer A and followers on B and C
> **When** the mesh partitions into {A} and {B,C}, B's detection window fires, B claims
> `epoch(2,B)`, both A and B accept writes, and the partition then heals
> **Then** `epoch(2,B)` is canonical at all three peers, A steps down to a command-forward
> follower and re-catches-up from B, every delta A shipped under `epoch(1,L)` after the split is
> fenced inert at C, and A's divergent post-partition writes appear exactly once on the
> dead-letter path and once at the registered reconciliation handler.
>
> Covers `[MEM1-08]`, `[MEM1-12]`, `[MEM1-13]`, `[MEM1-21]`, `[MEM1-31]`.
> Concord: `covers: [42-REPL-04]` — survivors converge to equal folds at quiescence — is
> corpus-eligible. The *reconciliation delivery* half is **not**: the handler is a kernel API
> with no implementation-neutral vocabulary in `concord/schema/scenario.md`, and only
> `civictech.concord.driver.kernel` may import `civictech.cell.*`. It stays a kernel test.

### 5.2 Simultaneous claims at the same counter

> **Given** a replica set whose leader has just unpublished, with two followers B and C both
> election-enabled and both observing the absence in the same scheduling step
> **When** B and C each mint `epoch(2, B)` and `epoch(2, C)` and announce
> **Then** every peer converges on the mark with the greater `instanceId` tiebreak, the loser
> steps down without a second round, no peer ever holds two marks at the same total order, and
> the losing claimant's shipping links are unlinked rather than left attached.
>
> Covers `[MEM1-02]`, `[MEM1-20]`, `[MEM1-15]`.
> Runs as a `forEachSeed` suite over interleavings of the two announcements.

### 5.3 False-positive failure detection

> **Given** a leader that is alive and applying writes, made transiently unreachable from one
> follower only (asymmetric partition via `Peering.Loopback.partition()` on one side)
> **When** that follower's detection window fires and it claims `epoch+1`, then reachability is
> restored before any write lands on the claimant
> **Then** the old leader steps down on folding the higher epoch (the claim is *not* rolled
> back — an adopted epoch is never un-adopted), leadership is single-valued at every peer, no
> write is lost, and no write is applied twice.
>
> Covers `[MEM1-08]`, `[MEM1-17]`, `[MEM1-21]`, `[MEM1-22]`.
> The honest finding this test must record: a false positive costs an unnecessary failover, not
> correctness. If it ever costs correctness, that is a `DISPUTES.md` entry, not a retuned window.

### 5.4 Epoch regression

> **Given** a set at `epoch(5, X)` with all peers converged
> **When** a peer that was partitioned since `epoch(2, W)` heals and re-announces its stale
> `LeaderMark`, and separately a duplicated `leaderMarked` announcement redelivers `epoch(5, X)`
> **Then** both are discarded, `leaderOf` stays `epoch(5, X)` at every peer, no local role
> changes, and no shipping link is torn down and rebuilt.
>
> Covers `[MEM1-09]`, `[MEM1-22]`, `[MEM1-06]`.
> Concord-eligible as an idempotence property once a normative id exists (see §5.8).

### 5.5 RESTART is not an election

> **Given** an elected leader under supervision
> **When** RESTART deactivates and reactivates it, preserving `instanceId`
> **Then** no claim is minted, the epoch is unchanged, its `LeaderMark` and shipping links
> survive, and it re-catches-up from the most-advanced reachable follower rather than from its
> spawn-time checkpoint; with no follower reachable it falls back to checkpoint and announces a
> re-baseline.
>
> Covers `[MEM1-14]`, `[MEM1-32]`.
> Extends the shipped `SingleWriterReplicationTest."RESTART recovers by peer catch-up rather
> than trusting a stale checkpoint"`.

### 5.6 Parked write during a contested window

> **Given** a writer whose write has parked on a closed intake while the leader is unpublishing
> **When** two claims are in flight and `leaderOf` is transiently contested
> **Then** the write stays parked, is released only once a single epoch-confirmed leader exists,
> lands on that leader, and is stamped under the winning epoch — and a deliberately mistimed
> release (control) lands inert at the fence rather than corrupting state.
>
> Covers `[MEM1-16]`, `[MEM1-04]`, `[MEM1-31]`.

### 5.7 Last-reachable-peer refusal (the MEM2 boundary)

> **Given** a follower whose reachable membership has shrunk to itself
> **When** its detection window fires
> **Then** it does not claim; the cell parks writes and the situation surfaces as the shipped
> suspend-when-partitioned condition, awaiting MEM2's handoff decision.
>
> Covers `[MEM1-23]`.

### 5.8 What a single-process test genuinely cannot establish → `DISPUTES.md`

These are filed in `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md`, **not** written as requirements a weak test
appears to satisfy (AGENTS.md: *"A requirement that cannot be checked honestly is filed in
`concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md`, never weakened into a passing scenario"*).

1. **No real concurrency.** `SimulationController` is single-threaded and step-ordered.
   "Simultaneous claims" (§5.2) are *interleavings*, not races. The claim rule's behaviour under
   genuine parallel mutation of `leaderMarks` — a `MutableMap`, unlike `LocationRegistry`'s
   `ConcurrentHashMap` — is unestablished by any test in this chunk.
2. **No time, therefore no liveness bound.** There is no clock in kernel/wire/testkit and
   `SimulationController` has no `advanceTime`. Any statement of the form "leadership converges
   within T" is unverifiable here. `[MEM1-07]`'s "detection window" is therefore specified in
   *announcement events*, not milliseconds — and the corresponding real-time bound is a dispute
   entry, not a requirement.
3. **The split-brain window cannot be bounded without a synchrony assumption.** A no-consensus
   election under an asynchronous network has no upper bound on dual-leader duration; 93 I-25 §2
   states this ("safe automatic failover under partition is *mathematically* unavailable without
   consensus"). The requirement set above states only *safety* properties (fencing,
   monotonicity, surfacing). The absent liveness bound is the dispute.
4. **Loopback is a park, not a loss.** `Peering.Loopback.partition()` unpublishes remotes so
   senders park and replay — it cannot express a dropped announcement. Election behaviour under
   genuine announcement *loss* needs CHA1's frame interposer and is unestablished until it lands.
5. **A wire-level `LeaderMark` needs a normative spec id.** Concord scenarios need a `covers:`
   id and `doc/spec/CONCORDANCE.md` fails on a dangling one. Spec 42 currently offers only
   `[42-REPL-04]`, `[42-REPL-05]`, `[42-REPL-06]` and `[42-INT-01]` — none states the election
   rule. Scenarios for `[MEM1-07]`/`[MEM1-11]`/`[MEM1-22]` therefore wait on a spec ticket
   minting (say) `[42-LEAD-nn]`; **this chunk does not edit the spec** (§4), so the corpus work
   is filed as a dispute-with-named-blocker rather than authored against an invented id.

---

## 6. Verification

Narrowest first, then outward.

```bash
# the two new suites
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.replication.LeaderElectionTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.replication.SplitBrainReconciliationTest'

# the suites this chunk must not regress
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.replication.SingleWriterReplicationTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.replication.ShippingLinkIdempotenceTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.replication.ReplicatedEffectTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.replication.ReplicationTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.consistency.ReplicaQuorumTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.replication.MemberDepartureFrontierTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.host.LocationRegistryHooksTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.wire.*'

# the wire/codec addition (LeaderMark registration + RegistryAnnounce method)
./gradlew :gen:test
./gradlew :wire:test

# module + repo gates
./gradlew :kernel:test
./gradlew :concord:test -Pconcord.profiles=core     # fast loop
./gradlew :concord:test                             # core, dist, dur
./gradlew :concord:concordance                      # regenerate; never hand-edit CONCORDANCE.md
./gradlew :concord:check
./gradlew :demo:exchange:test                       # composition exit gate
./gradlew test                                      # repository-wide
```

diff, confirm `doc/spec/CONCORDANCE.md` is regenerated rather than edited, and review the diff

design:
# MEM1 — design: how, decomposition, risks

## 1. How, using ComputeNet (real types, real paths)

Every mechanism below rides shipped machinery. Nothing here is a new kernel primitive — 93 I-25
§4.8 is explicit that election must be "no leader registry, no lease, no quorum, no consensus,
and no second synchronization protocol".

### 1.1 The fold already exists — give it a wire

`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/replication/SingleWriterReplication.kt`:

```kotlin
data class LeaderMark(val logicalId: UUID, val epoch: Long, val leaderRef: CellRef)   // line 35
private val leaderMarks = mutableMapOf<UUID, LeaderMark>()                            // line 161
fun designateLeader(mark: LeaderMark): Boolean {                                      // line 214
    val current = leaderMarks[mark.logicalId]
    if (current != null && mark.epoch <= current.epoch) return false
    ...
}
```

`designateLeader` is already the strictly-greater-wins fold `[MEM1-09]`/`[MEM1-22]` want. Three
changes:

1. **`epoch: Long` becomes the total order of 93 I-25 §4.1.** Today ties on `Long` are simply
   rejected, which is safe but not *decisive*: two claimants at the same counter both fail to
   adopt each other's mark and each keeps its own. Introduce the tiebreak
   (`compareBy(LeaderMark::epoch, { it.leaderRef.instanceId })`) so §5.2 converges. Wire-additive:
   the tiebreak is already on the mark (`leaderRef.instanceId`), so no new field is needed —
   only the comparator changes, and the serialized shape is unchanged.
2. **`LeaderMark` becomes an announcement.** Add `fun leaderMarked(mark: LeaderMark)` to
   `RegistryAnnounce` (`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/wire/Peering.kt:22-37`), served in
   `RegistryMirrorCell`'s `inlet.serve(object : RegistryAnnounce { ... })` (line 97) by calling
   the local engine's `designateLeader`. `Peering.announceTo` (line 199) gains one more
   subscription so a locally adopted mark propagates, and its catch-up loop replays currently
   held marks to a newly connected peer — this is what makes `[MEM1-06]` true. `RegistryAnnounce`
   is `@Contract(management = true)`, so KSP regenerates the proxy
   (`RegistryAnnounce_Proxy_*.kt`) — hence `:gen:test` in the verification list.
3. **`LeaderMark` gets a `WireCodec` registration.** `kernel/.../wire/WireCodec.kt` already
   registers `Stamped`, `WatermarkDelta`, `Assignment`. `LeaderMark` is ids-only
   (`UUID`, `Long`, `CellRef`) so this is additive at `VERSION = 2` — no version bump, satisfying
   AGENTS.md's wire-compatibility rule and 93 I-25 §5 P9.

### 1.2 The failure detector is the membership index, not a heartbeat

The substrate already reports death. `LocationRegistry`
(`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/LocationRegistry.kt`) exposes
`onPublish`/`onUnpublish` hooks and `replicasOf(logicalId)` (an alias of `instancesOf`, backed by
`byLogicalId`). `WsTransport.Session.onClose()` → `registry.unpublishRemotes(sink)` →
`onUnpublish` is the real death signal; `Replication.evict` already treats
`replicasOf(id) - self == ∅` as "partitioned" (`Replication.kt:285`).

So the detector is:

```kotlin
class LeaderElection private constructor(...) {
    object Manual : LeaderElection                  // today's behaviour, the default
    class EpochClaim(val window: DetectionWindow) : LeaderElection
}
```

with `DetectionWindow` counted in **announcement events observed on the membership seam**, not
milliseconds — `[MEM1-25]`. Concretely: on each `onUnpublish` naming the current `leaderRef`, and
on each subsequent `onPublish` for the same logical id that does *not* restore it, the engine
increments a per-logical-id miss counter; the claim fires when it crosses the window. This is
countable, deterministic under `SimulationController`, and adds zero traffic — exactly G-44's
"a failure-detection window that does not become a second heartbeat protocol".

**Why KX is a hard prerequisite.** This counter is membership state keyed by logical id. It
belongs on the lane C-13 (`91-gap-analysis.md:21`) marks for extraction as `InstanceIndex` — the
`byLogicalId` membership index plus the interest-assignment table. Adding a fourth off-mandate
lane to `LocationRegistry` before the extraction would deepen the accretion the C-13 marker
exists to stop. MEM1 consumes KX's boundary; it does not perform the split.

**Why KE3/E3.6 gates.** 96 §E3.6 fixes what "membership" means for reads that depend on it:
`replicasOf` snapshotted per read with the eventual-consistency caveat; clean departure closes a
`WatermarkCell` row; **unclean departure freezes and surfaces a `Stall`, deliberately not worked
around** (lease-based row eviction is 95 §R13, out of scope). The failure detector reads the same
seam and must not contradict that disposition: an election must never be the back-door lease that
E3.6 refused. `[MEM1-19]` is the guard.

### 1.3 The claim, the step-down, and the fence

The claim path reuses the existing fold rather than adding a second one:

```
detector fires
  -> mint LeaderMark(id, maxSeenEpoch + 1, selfRef)          [MEM1-07]
  -> designateLeader(mark)                                   the ONE fold
  -> announce leaderMarked(mark) to peers                    [MEM1-11]
```

`designateLeader`'s existing body already does the role application: for each local replica,
`ref == mark.leaderRef` ⇒ `becomeLeader(epoch)` + `shipTo(...)` at every
`registry.replicasOf(logicalId)`; otherwise `becomeFollower(leaderRef, epoch, registry)`, which
installs the `forwardWrites` delegate. Step-down (`[MEM1-08]`) is therefore *already implemented*
as the else-branch — what is missing is (a) unlinking the ex-leader's outbound `shipped` links
(`[MEM1-15]`; the class already `unlink()`s on `onUnpublish` precisely because follower apply is
non-idempotent — the step-down path must do the same) and (b) the catch-up from the new leader,
which is `restartCatchUp(local, donor = newLeader)` with the donor resolved through
`HostedCellProxy`.

Fencing (`[MEM1-04]`, `[MEM1-31]`) rides `Stamped<D>` (`SingleWriterReplication.kt:44`), already
registered in `WireCodec` and already re-stamped through the interest slicer in `shipTo`
(`Stamped(stamped.epoch, it)`). The follower's `deltaInlet` serve gains the comparison against the
locally folded epoch. That is a two-line predicate, not a mechanism.

### 1.4 Reconciliation of fenced divergent writes

42 §Always-fenced writes: divergent post-partition writes are *"surfaced on the error/dead-letter
path, never silently dropped"*. The dead-letter path exists (host `deadLetter`, `HostDurability`
wiring, spec 31 rule 5). G-44 asks for one thing more — an **application-level hook**. Model it
after the existing observer idiom (`LocationRegistry.onPublish`, `Replication.onWatermarkAdvance`):

```kotlin
fun onDivergentWrite(handler: (logicalId: UUID, fencedEpoch: Long, canonicalEpoch: Long,
                               payload: Any?) -> Unit): AutoCloseable
```

A stepping-down leader replays the deltas it produced above the winner's high-water through the
handler *and* the dead-letter path. `[MEM1-28]` keeps the dead-letter behaviour when no handler is
registered, so no existing graph changes.

### 1.5 Per-shard leader routing

`[MEM1-27]` needs no new routing. 93 I-25 §6 already resolved it: *"a partitioned SW structure's
partitions are ordinary cells, each replicating SW per its own `replicasOf(partitionRef)`"*.
`SingleWriterReplication` is keyed on `cell.ref.id`, and a shard *is* a distinct ref, so per-shard
leadership falls out. The work is the *test* (`[MEM1-27]`) plus confirming the interest gate in
`shipTo` (`registry.interestOf(leader.ref).overlaps(targetInterest)`, line 246) does not let a
shard leader ship outside its slice. `ShardedReplicationTest` and `ShardedReplicaFrontierTest` are
the neighbours to extend rather than duplicate.

### 1.6 Test seams that already exist

- `SimulationController` (`kernel/.../host/SimulationController.kt`) — seeded step order,
  `runToIdle(budget)`.
- `Peering.Loopback.partition()/heal()` — partition and heal (a *park*, not a loss; see body §5.8).
- `SingleWriterReplication.shipCountAmong(refs)` — the existing internal seam for asserting
  shipping topology; the step-down unlink assertion uses it.
- `civictech.cell.verify.ReplicaConvergence` — `converged()` already excludes departed refs via
  `liveRefs()`, so it is the right invariant cell for the seeded churn suite.
- `forEachSeed` (`testkit/.../ForEachSeed.kt`) — 95 §R1's "generative leader-churn harness".

## 2. Suggested feature decomposition

**List only — do NOT create these beads.** They are the shape a breakdown should take when this
epic is actually claimed.

1. **Epoch total order + tiebreak.** `LeaderMark` comparator becomes `(epoch, leaderRef.instanceId)`;
   `designateLeader` decisive on equal counters. `[MEM1-02]`, `[MEM1-20]`.
2. **`LeaderMark` as an announcement.** `RegistryAnnounce.leaderMarked`, `RegistryMirrorCell` serve,
   `Peering.announceTo` subscription + catch-up replay, `WireCodec` registration.
   `[MEM1-06]`, `[MEM1-11]`, `[MEM1-22]`.
3. **`LeaderElection` posture + membership-event detection window.** New
   `replication/LeaderElection.kt`; `SingleWriterReplication` constructor parameter defaulting to
   `Manual`. `[MEM1-05]`, `[MEM1-07]`, `[MEM1-17]`, `[MEM1-23]`, `[MEM1-25]`.
4. **Step-down completeness.** Unlink outbound shipping on demotion; catch-up from the new leader;
   follower delegate re-point ordering. `[MEM1-08]`, `[MEM1-10]`, `[MEM1-15]`, `[MEM1-32]`.
5. **Follower-side epoch fence at apply.** `deltaInlet` compares `Stamped.epoch` against the folded
   epoch. `[MEM1-04]`, `[MEM1-31]`.
6. **Parked-write release gate.** Release only on a single epoch-confirmed leader; the mistimed-
   release control. `[MEM1-16]`.
7. **Reconciliation hook.** `onDivergentWrite`; dead-letter parity when unregistered.
   `[MEM1-13]`, `[MEM1-28]`.
8. **Per-shard leadership verification.** Extend `ShardedReplicationTest`; interest-gate assertion.
   `[MEM1-27]`.
9. **Seeded leader-churn suite** (95 §R1's named action) + `SplitBrainReconciliationTest`.
   Body §5.1–§5.7.
10. **Findings + disputes.** `doc/replication/findings.md`; `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` entries
    from body §5.8, each naming its blocker (spec id, CHA1 frame interposer, real concurrency).

## 3. Risks and open questions

### 3.1 The §4/§5 ordering tension — MEM1 ↔ KE4 swap

Plan §4 places MEM1 at position 6 (straight after KE3) and KE4 at position 9. Plan §5 states the
condition under which that flips:

> *"**MEM1 before KE4** stands *unless* Feldera/Flink comparability becomes a stated goal — then
> swap (§4)."*

and §4 spells out the mechanism: *"BB-NEX wants KE4 early (it's the flagship comparative suite),
but KE4 sits behind KE3, and MEM1 also sits behind KE3. If benchmark comparability against
Feldera/Flink becomes the priority, the swap is MEM1 ↔ KE4 (run KE4 straight after KE3, delay
election) — legal, since nothing in BB depends on MEM1."*

**Risk to this chunk:** MEM1 can be pre-empted in the kernel lane at any point before it is
claimed, by a *product* decision made outside the lane (making BB-NEX comparability a stated
goal). The cost of the swap is not symmetric: MEM1 delayed also delays MEM2 and SOC3, whereas KE4
delayed only delays BB-NEX's windowed queries. Whoever schedules the lane should record which of
the two goals is currently stated, because the plan makes the swap legal but does not decide it.

### 3.2 Open questions

- **Detection-window units.** `[MEM1-25]` forces the window into announcement events. That is
  deterministic and buildable, but it means a leader that dies *without* its transport closing
  (a wedged host that still holds its socket) is never detected. Is that acceptable, or does it
  pull a liveness signal that would be the heartbeat G-44 forbids? Current answer: acceptable,
  and filed as a `DISPUTES.md` limitation rather than solved. Revisit only with a real user.
- **`leaderMarks` concurrency.** `SingleWriterReplication`'s maps are plain `mutableMap` (the
  documented single-threaded/simulated assumption, same as `Replication`), while
  `LocationRegistry` uses `ConcurrentHashMap`. Once marks arrive over the wire the fold is driven
  from the announce path. Does that stay on one host queue in every configuration? If not, this is
  a real defect that election *surfaces* rather than introduces.
- **G-44's ack-from-k vs 93 I-25 §4.4.** The gap row proposes "an optional ack-from-k durability
  tier"; the integrated decision refuses it as a second protocol. `[MEM1-26]` resolves this by the
  authority order (integrated decision wins) and points at G-25 checkpointing. If a reviewer
  disagrees, that is a spec-editor question, not an implementation choice — flag it rather than
  build an ack path.
- **`shipTo` has no derived `PortRef`.** `Replication.maybeLink` keys its subscription on a
  derived `gossipRef` (T21) so re-linking replaces rather than accumulates;
  `SingleWriterReplication.shipTo` calls `streamTo(sink)` with no `at =`. It is currently safe
  because `onUnpublish` genuinely `unlink()`s — but the step-down path added here is a *second*
  teardown route, and the asymmetry becomes load-bearing. Either derive the ref (cheap,
  self-healing) or prove the teardown is total. `ShippingLinkIdempotenceTest` is the guard.
- **Stale spec status header.** `doc/spec/40-distribution/42-replication.md:300` still reads
  "decided in 93 I-25, **not built**" while `SingleWriterReplication.kt` exists and is tested.
  This chunk does not edit the spec (scope §4); it records the discrepancy in
  `doc/replication/findings.md` for the periodic integration pass (plan §6).

# KE2 — E2: vector-frontier observation edge, absorb-acks, aligned multi-view sink

Kernel-lane chunk, position **8** of `computenet-milestone-plan.md` §4. Realizes the
remainder of `doc/spec/90-roadmap/96-incremental-engines-plan.md` §"Milestone E2 —
Vector-frontier observation edge" (E2.1–E2.6) against the normative text already landed
in `doc/spec/20-dataflow-semantics/22-consistency.md` §"The observation frontier".

Normative anchors: **`[22-OBS-01]`** (22-consistency.md — internal consistency as
per-source-vector-frontier alignment, Ubiquitous) and **`[22-OBS-02]`** (the
aligned-composite rule: per-name inlets, assembly only after every contributing view has
settled every wave ≤ the shared frontier, State-driven). Both are **`gap` rows in
`doc/spec/CONCORDANCE.md` lines 81–82** with no covering scenario. Supporting: G-13
(static-link-set / phantom expected edge), G-40 (completeness over silent or stuck
edges) in `doc/spec/90-roadmap/91-gap-analysis.md`; 20/24 §Operator library
(non-monotone emission gating); 93 I-18; research-gated corners 95 **R11** (frontier
alignment across origination points) and 95 **R12** (observation-edge triggering policy).

Plan row, verbatim: *"Depends on: FRM1 informs. Unblocks: WKB2 snapshots; BB latency
measurement. **Note:** the BB lane supplies its first concrete consumers —
write-visibility acks for BB-YCSB/BB-NEX latency. A minimal sink-side ack slice may be
split out early if latency fidelity demands it."* §4 position 8 adds: *"if BB-YCSB
latency fidelity is wanted earlier, split the sink-side ack slice out and run it after
KAGG-R."*

---

## 0. Scope correction — read this before designing anything

**Most of milestone E2 is already merged.** The `99-defects-engines-plan` run landed
`E2-SPEC`, `E2-ALIGN`, `E2-GATE` and `E2-SUITE` (all four ticket files under
`doc/spec/90-roadmap/99-defects-engines-plan/tickets/` header `**Status**: Implemented —
merged`). The milestone-plan row was written against the 96-plan's *proposed* state and
is stale. KE2 is therefore **not** "build the aligned sink"; it is "close the residuals
the shipped sink honestly documents, and build the one consumer-facing primitive that
was never in E2 at all".

Landed, do **not** rebuild:

| E2 item | Real artifact | Note |
|---|---|---|
| E2.1 spec | `doc/spec/20-dataflow-semantics/22-consistency.md` §The observation frontier, `[22-OBS-01]`/`[22-OBS-02]` | merged |
| E2.2 absorb-acks | `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/control/AbsorbAck.kt` — `internal fun FanOutlet<*>.absorbAck()`; helper `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/op/Emit.kt` `emitOrAbsorb(isEmpty, emit, absorbAck)` | Path is `control/`, **not** the 96-plan's `data/AbsorbAck.kt`. Adopted by `FilterCell`, `SemiJoinCell`, `IntersectSetCell`, `GroupByCell`, `CombineLatestCell`, `LookupJoinCell`, plus beyond-plan `CountCell`, `JoinSetCell`, `JoinCell`, `UnionSetCell`, `QuorumSetCell`, `FlatMapSetCell`, `CoalescingCombineCell`. Test: `kernel/src/test/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/op/OperatorAbsorbAckTest.kt` |
| E2.3 first half | `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/consistency/WaveFrontier.kt` — `class WaveFrontier(mode, onDropped, onViolation) : InletFrontier`, `tier = PolicyTier.ALIGN` | `GlitchFreeCell` (`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/consistency/GlitchFree.kt`, 128 lines) is now a bare pass-through delegating via `inlet.install(frontier)`; no inline fold remains |
| E2.3 second half | `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/observe/AlignedObserve.kt` — `class AlignedCompositeCell(views, registeredAs, ref) : Cell, Stateful, ObservationSink<Map<String, Any?>>`; entry points `ManagedHost.observeAligned { … }` and `Use<HostManagementApi>.observeAligned { … }`; builder `AlignedObserveBuilder.set/map/count(name, source, outletName)` | Path is `observe/`, **not** `host/`. One `FanInlet` per view name (the `[22-OBS-02]` per-name clause, structural). The cross-inlet fold is **mirrored, not delegated** — `WaveFrontier` is a per-inlet `InletFrontier` and cannot span N named inlets |
| E2.4 | `emitOnFrontier` opt-in flag on `SemiJoinCell` and `CombineLatestCell` over `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/op/WaveGate.kt`; test `kernel/src/test/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/op/FrontierGatedEmissionTest.kt` | Default stays ungated |
| E2.5 | `kernel/src/test/kotlin/civictech/cell/consistency/InternalConsistencyTest.kt` — balanced transfers, 50 waves × 200 seeds, three pipelines through one `observeAligned`, three asserted failure controls | The suite has teeth |

Point-consistent sibling, deliberately kept: `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/observe/Observe.kt`
— `interface ObservationSink<out S>`, `interface View<in D, out S>`, `class CompositeSink`,
`ManagedHost.observeAll { … }`. Its KDoc deferral already points at `observeAligned`.

Adjacent, **not** KE2's to change: `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/BoundedRead.kt`
(`interface BoundedStateful { fun readBounded(request: StateRead): StatePage }`,
`data class StateRead`, `StatePage`, `sealed interface StateReadResult`) reached through
`ManagedHost.readState(ref, request): CompletableFuture<StateReadResult>`
(`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/ManagedHost.kt:1360`, beside the older
`snapshotOf(ref): CompletableFuture<Serializable?>` at `:1257`). That is KRD/V1C-KERNEL
territory — wave-neutral by design. KE2 *composes with* it (§F9) and must not fold wave
semantics into it.

---

## 1. Ambition / Why

`[22-OBS-01]` and `[22-OBS-02]` are the only two requirements in `22-consistency.md`
that the concordance still calls `gap`. The mechanism exists and is exercised by a
strong kernel test; what is missing is (a) the corpus closure that makes the claim
implementation-neutral, and (b) every seam the shipped sink's own KDoc admits it does
not cover. The sink is a WAIT-shape, in-process, statically-attached, single-origination
instrument. Four honest limitations are written into
`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/observe/AlignedObserve.kt` itself:

1. **Bridged alignment is untested** (`AlignedObserve.kt:115-120`). `EdgeOpen`/`EdgeClose`
   and `Progress` already cross as frames, so it *should* work — but `:kernel` cannot
   depend on `:wire`, so nothing proves it. Every distribution consumer of an aligned
   read is standing on an unverified claim.
2. **WAIT only** — no `DEGRADE` frontier shrinking, no RE-SCOPE on terminal stall, no
   replica-fed settlement, no pull-on-open. A single stalled arm holds every wave
   indefinitely. `WaveFrontier` *has* WAIT | DEGRADE | RE-SCOPE; the aligned sink mirrored
   only the first.
3. **Attach-time skew.** Catch-up traffic (`onLinked` state-as-delta, pull baselines)
   installs as arm state and joins no completeness set; an edge opened mid-stream floors
   below the already-flushed waves. A sink attached to a live graph can transiently
   publish arms seeded at different points — aligned only *from its first waved delta
   onward*.
4. **The gating rule is narrower than the sink's promise.** `emitOnFrontier` exists on
   `SemiJoinCell` and `CombineLatestCell` only. `E2-SUITE`'s finding 1 measured the rest
   of the binary-join family (`JoinSetCell`, `JoinCell`, `IntersectSetCell`,
   `LookupJoinCell`) tearing at **50/50 seeds, 50 torn composites per 50 waves**. The
   shipped rule is therefore an unenforced convention: *only a gated `SemiJoinCell` or
   `CombineLatestCell` may feed a view of an `observeAligned` composite, or the inlet of
   another gated operator.* Nothing in the type system, the builder, or the link
   admission path checks it. A user who wires `IntersectSetCell` into `observeAligned`
   gets torn composites and a passing build — which is exactly the failure mode
   `[22-OBS-01]` exists to forbid.

And one thing that was never in E2 at all, which the milestone plan is really asking for:

5. **There is no write-visibility ack anywhere in the tree.** Repository-wide search
   finds no `WriteAck`, `visibilityAck`, `awaitVisible`, or write-completion future in
   `kernel`, `wire`, `runtime`, or `demo`. `Progress` (`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/control/Progress.kt:17`,
   lane `Protocols.Progress`) is a *downstream metadata-plane* watermark advance between
   cells — not writer-facing. Ingress writers return immediately with no visibility
   guarantee (`demo/shopping/src/main/kotlin/civictech/demo/Main.kt:340-348`: `itemOps.add(item)`
   then `exchange.respond(200, "ok")`). Tests substitute `scheduler.step()`/`runToIdle()`.

Consequence for the BB lane: **BB-YCSB and BB-NEX cannot measure end-to-end latency
honestly today.** A latency number needs a per-write signal that says "this write is now
visible at this named sink, in wave (s, t)". Quiescence-based measurement measures the
scheduler, not the system, and collapses entirely under concurrent load — the only regime
a benchmark cares about. This is the "sink-side ack slice" the plan names, and it is the
single highest-leverage piece of KE2: it is the only part with a consumer already
waiting, and it is genuinely separable from everything else.

Consequence for WKB2: a graph-edit UI applying a `GraphSpec` through `Promotion` needs to
read back a state that corresponds to *some* frontier of its own writes. Today it can
only read point-consistent views or a wave-neutral `readState` page.

## 3. How, using ComputeNet

The mechanisms are all already present; KE2 is composition, not invention.

**Gating the rest of the join family.** `WaveGate<T>`
(`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/op/WaveGate.kt:94`) already buffers a wave's
deltas across inlets and reconciles at completeness, emitting the wave's net effect. It is
constructed identically inside `SemiJoinCell` and `CombineLatestCell`. The remaining four
cells buffer nothing; each needs the same `emitOnFrontier` constructor flag, the same
`WaveGate`, and the same effective-only net emission — with `emitOrAbsorb`
(`data/op/Emit.kt`) still firing the absorb-ack when the net effect is empty, so a gated
cell that swallows a wave still advances downstream watermarks (`[22-OBS-02]`'s assembly
clause depends on that: a gated arm that goes silent must not stall the sink).

**Structural rejection of an ungated contributor.** `AlignedObserveBuilder`
(`AlignedObserve.kt:475`) resolves each view's `source: CellRef` + `outletName`. At build
time the host can walk the upstream link set — `TopologyIndex` already answers reachability
for cycle admission — and refuse a contributor whose ancestor set contains an ungated
non-monotone cell. Loud rejection is the smallest honest step; it is the same shape as
R11's direction (1), and the two checks share one traversal.

**Stall policy.** `WaveFrontier` already carries `GlitchFreeCell.WaveMode` WAIT | DEGRADE |
RE-SCOPE keyed on `Stall(reason, recoverable)` recoverability. The aligned sink's fold
(`edges`, `expectedEdges(timestamp)`, `ready()`, `flushReady()`, `AlignedObserve.kt:169-376`)
mirrors only WAIT. DEGRADE means: drop a terminally-stalled edge out of
`expectedEdges` and publish. The correctness question the gap row G-40 already flags —
*how does a consumer distinguish a degraded emission from a genuine one* — becomes
load-bearing here, because the aligned sink's whole product is a consumer-visible
composite. The answer must be **in the published value**, not a log line: a composite
published under a shrunken frontier is a different kind of object than one published
under the full one, and `[22-OBS-01]` is only true of the latter unless the shrink is
itself part of the frontier the composite claims.

**Write-visibility ack.** Composition of three landed things: `MessageContext`'s
`Timestamp(sourceId, counter)` identifies the originating wave; the `Progress` lane
already carries per-source watermark advance downstream through absorbing cells; the
aligned sink already knows, at `flushReady()`, exactly which `(sourceId, counter)` it just
published. A writer-side token minted at ingress records `(sourceId, counter)`; the sink
completes every outstanding token whose counter ≤ the wave it publishes. Nothing new
crosses the wire. Two honest boundaries fall out immediately and must be stated in the
API, not hidden: (a) a write absorbed to no effective output is visible-by-vacuity and
must complete on the absorb-ack, not hang; (b) a write whose wave is never published
because its sink degraded must complete *as degraded*, not silently as success.

**Serialization constraint (G-63).** All of the above is `civictech.cell.*` — `observe`,
`consistency`, `data.op`, `control`, `host`. Those packages are inside the **single
strongly-connected component** recorded as G-63 (`doc/spec/90-roadmap/91-gap-analysis.md`
row G-63: all 20 non-leaf `civictech.cell.*` packages form one SCC). There is no physical
layering to hide behind: **KE2 must run serially in the kernel lane**, at §4 position 8,
after KE5 and not concurrently with any other kernel-lane chunk. The one legitimate
exception is §F1 (the ack slice), which the plan explicitly permits pulling forward — and
pulling it forward means running it *in the lane* after KAGG-R, not *beside* the lane.
Two kernel-lane chunks in flight at once is the thing G-63 makes unsafe.

## 5. Functional requirements (EARS)

Ids are epic-scoped and never collide with `doc/spec/`'s `[NN-SLUG-nn]` namespace. Each
line names the normative id it makes true.

### 5.1 The aligned composite — core guarantee

- **[KE2-01]** *(Ubiquitous)* Every composite published by an aligned observation edge SHALL be the correct composite for exactly one per-source vector frontier of this replica's inputs. — makes `[22-OBS-01]` true.
- **[KE2-02]** *(Ubiquitous)* An aligned observation edge SHALL expose one named inlet per registered contributing view, and the view's identity SHALL be recoverable from every buffered delta. — `[22-OBS-02]` inlet clause.
- **[KE2-03]** *(State-driven)* While any contributing view has not settled a wave `(s, t)`, the aligned observation edge SHALL NOT publish a composite for `(s, t)`. — `[22-OBS-02]` assembly clause.
- **[KE2-04]** *(Event-driven)* When every contributing view has settled wave `(s, t)`, the aligned observation edge SHALL publish at most one composite for `(s, t)`, with the wave's buffered deltas applied in per-source-counter order. — `[22-OBS-02]`.
- **[KE2-05]** *(Unwanted)* If a wave's net effect across all contributing views is empty, then the aligned observation edge SHALL publish no composite for that wave and SHALL still advance its own downstream watermark for that wave. — `[22-OBS-02]`, G-40.

### 5.2 Gated non-monotone emission (closes the E2-SUITE finding-1 residual)

- **[KE2-06]** *(Ubiquitous)* Every operator cell in the binary-join family — `SemiJoinCell`, `CombineLatestCell`, `JoinSetCell`, `JoinCell`, `IntersectSetCell`, `LookupJoinCell` — SHALL offer a frontier-gated emission mode with identical observable semantics. — 20/24 §Operator library; `[22-OBS-01]`.
- **[KE2-07]** *(State-driven)* While a cell is in frontier-gated mode, its outlet SHALL show the wave's net effect only, and SHALL NOT show an enter-then-exit pair originating within one wave. — 20/24 §Operator library.
- **[KE2-08]** *(State-driven)* While a cell is in frontier-gated mode and a wave's net effect is empty, the cell SHALL emit an absorb-ack for that wave. — G-40; `[22-OBS-02]`.
- **[KE2-09]** *(Unwanted)* If an aligned observation edge is built over a contributing view whose upstream ancestor set contains an ungated non-monotone operator cell, then construction SHALL fail loudly at build time, naming the offending cell and outlet. — `[22-OBS-01]`; G-13.
- **[KE2-10]** *(Ubiquitous)* Frontier-gated mode SHALL remain opt-in; the default emission behaviour of every named cell SHALL be byte-identical to its behaviour before this epic. — repository invariant (wire/behaviour compatibility).

### 5.3 Stall handling and degraded composites

- **[KE2-11]** *(Optional-feature)* Where an aligned observation edge is configured with a degrade policy, it SHALL, on a stall marked non-recoverable, remove the stalled edge from the wave's expected-edge set and publish the resulting composite. — G-40; `WaveFrontier` WaveMode parity.
- **[KE2-12]** *(Ubiquitous)* A composite published under a shrunken expected-edge set SHALL be distinguishable, in the published value itself, from one published under the full set, and SHALL name every edge that was dropped. — `[22-OBS-01]` (the shrink is part of the frontier the composite claims); G-40 open item "pin the DEGRADE correctness contract".
- **[KE2-13]** *(State-driven)* While an aligned observation edge is configured to wait, a stalled contributing edge SHALL hold every wave at or above the stall, and the edge SHALL report the stalled edge and the held wave on demand. — G-40.
- **[KE2-14]** *(Event-driven)* When a stalled contributing edge resumes, the aligned observation edge SHALL publish the held waves in per-source-counter order without loss and without reordering. — `[22-OBS-02]`.
- **[KE2-15]** *(Unwanted)* If a contributing edge closes (`EdgeClose`) while waves are held on it, then the aligned observation edge SHALL shrink the expected-edge set and publish the released waves rather than hold them indefinitely. — G-13, G-40.

### 5.4 Attach-time contract

- **[KE2-16]** *(Ubiquitous)* An aligned observation edge SHALL declare, as part of its published state, the wave from which its alignment guarantee holds.
- **[KE2-17]** *(Event-driven)* When an aligned observation edge is attached to a graph that is already writing, every composite it publishes from its first waved delta onward SHALL satisfy [KE2-01]. — `[22-OBS-01]`.
- **[KE2-18]** *(Unwanted)* If catch-up traffic (`onLinked` state-as-delta or a pull baseline) installs arm state, then that traffic SHALL NOT be admitted to any wave's completeness set and SHALL NOT cause a composite to be published as aligned. — `[22-OBS-02]`.

### 5.5 Write-visibility acks — the separately-schedulable slice

- **[KE2-19]** *(Ubiquitous)* An ingress writer SHALL be able to obtain, at write time, a handle identifying the wave `(sourceId, counter)` its write originated.
- **[KE2-20]** *(Event-driven)* When an aligned observation edge publishes a composite for wave `(s, t)`, every outstanding handle for source `s` with counter ≤ `t` registered against that edge SHALL complete as visible, naming `(s, t)`.
- **[KE2-21]** *(Event-driven)* When a write's wave is absorbed to no effective output at every contributing view, the handle SHALL complete as visible-vacuously rather than remain outstanding. — G-40; depends on [KE2-05]/[KE2-08].
- **[KE2-22]** *(Unwanted)* If the wave a handle names is published only under a shrunken expected-edge set, then the handle SHALL complete as visible-degraded and SHALL NOT complete as visible. — [KE2-12].
- **[KE2-23]** *(Unwanted)* If the observation edge a handle is registered against is closed or its host is shut down before the handle's wave is published, then the handle SHALL complete exceptionally with a named reason and SHALL NOT be abandoned.
- **[KE2-24]** *(Ubiquitous)* Obtaining and completing a visibility handle SHALL introduce no additional wire frame and no additional protocol lane; it SHALL be a local fold over information the edge already holds.
- **[KE2-25]** *(Ubiquitous)* The number of outstanding handles SHALL be bounded and observable, and the bound SHALL be reachable by a caller without blocking a cell's execution context.
- **[KE2-26]** *(Complex)* While an aligned observation edge is publishing under a degrade policy, when a handle completes, the completion SHALL name the edges dropped from that wave's expected set. — [KE2-12], [KE2-22].
- **[KE2-27]** *(Optional-feature)* Where a visibility handle is registered against a point-consistent `CompositeSink` rather than an aligned edge, the handle SHALL be refused at registration, and the refusal SHALL name `[22-OBS-01]` as the reason. — honesty: a point-consistent sink cannot witness a frontier.

### 5.6 Bridged (cross-host) alignment

- **[KE2-28]** *(Ubiquitous)* An aligned observation edge whose contributing views arrive across a wire bridge SHALL satisfy [KE2-01] and [KE2-03] identically to the in-process case. — repository invariant (in-process and remote paths preserve the same observable semantics).
- **[KE2-29]** *(Event-driven)* When an absorbing operator cell on a remote host swallows a wave, the resulting `Progress` absorb-ack SHALL cross the bridge and settle the local aligned edge's corresponding arm. — G-40 (bridged CP-A2).
- **[KE2-30]** *(Unwanted)* If a bridged contributing arm cannot be shown to satisfy [KE2-28] under test, then the limitation SHALL be recorded in `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` with the missing capability named, and SHALL NOT be asserted in KDoc or spec prose as holding.

### 5.7 Origination points (R11's smallest honest step)

- **[KE2-31]** *(Unwanted)* If an aligned observation edge's contributing views do not share a common ancestor for every re-origination point on their upstream paths, then construction SHALL fail loudly, naming the origination point. — 95 R11 direction (1).
- **[KE2-32]** *(Ubiquitous)* The rejection in [KE2-31] SHALL be a structural, build-time check and SHALL NOT be inferred from runtime symptoms.

### 5.8 Consumers

- **[KE2-33]** *(Event-driven)* When `demo/shopping` applies one ingress operation, its SSE stream SHALL emit exactly one frame, and no frame SHALL show a `produce` or `wanted` item absent from `items`. — 96 §E2.6 acceptance.
- **[KE2-34]** *(Optional-feature)* Where a consumer needs a bounded, paged read of a cell's state, it SHALL use `ManagedHost.readState`, which SHALL remain wave-neutral; an aligned read SHALL be composed beside it and SHALL NOT change its semantics. — KRD boundary.
- **[KE2-35]** *(Ubiquitous)* `[22-OBS-01]` and `[22-OBS-02]` SHALL each have at least one covering scenario in `concord/corpus/22-consistency/`, and `doc/spec/CONCORDANCE.md` SHALL no longer report them as `gap`.

### 5.9 Requirements that cannot be checked honestly today

Filed as such rather than softened — per AGENTS.md, `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` is the
home for these:

- **[KE2-30]** is written as a *disclosure* obligation precisely because the bridged proof may not be constructible inside `:kernel` (no `:wire` dependency). If `demo/shopping`'s two-JVM harness cannot exercise a bridged aligned arm, the honest outcome is a DISPUTES entry naming "cross-host aligned observation, no in-corpus driver binding", not a weakened scenario.
- **[KE2-12]**'s "distinguishable in the published value" is checkable; "the consumer does the right thing with the distinction" is not, and is deliberately not stated as a requirement. G-40's open item ("pin the DEGRADE correctness contract") stays open after KE2 unless a real consumer is available to pin it against.
- **[KE2-25]**'s bound is checkable; a *useful* bound is a tuning question that needs BEN1 numbers. KE2 ships a bound and an observation counter, not a calibrated one.

## 6. Behaviour specifications (Given / When / Then)

Named so each becomes a test.

**BS-1 — aligned diamond, no mixed waves** *(→ concord: `22-OBS-01`)*
Given one source fanning to two derived views into one aligned observation edge; When 200 seeded interleavings drive 50 waves each; Then every published composite corresponds to exactly one input prefix, and the point-consistent `CompositeSink` control trips under the same seeds. Covers [KE2-01], [KE2-03], [KE2-04].
*Belongs in the corpus*: it is implementation-neutral (source, two derived views, one composite read) and is the direct witness for the `gap` row.

**BS-2 — per-name inlet identity** *(→ concord: `22-OBS-02`)*
Given two registered views whose deltas have the same runtime type; When both emit in one wave; Then each delta is folded under its own named accumulator and the composite reports both names with distinct values. Covers [KE2-02].

**BS-3 — absorbing arm settles the wave** *(→ concord: `22-OBS-02`)*
Given a source → filter → aligned-edge arm where the filter drops the wave's only delta; When the wave completes; Then the composite for that wave is published without waiting for a subsequent write; Control: with the absorb-ack suppressed, the wave stalls. Covers [KE2-05], [KE2-08].

**BS-4 — gated join family, no intra-wave flicker** *(kernel test, not corpus)*
Given each of `JoinSetCell`, `JoinCell`, `IntersectSetCell`, `LookupJoinCell` in gated mode behind a shared-source diamond; When 200 seeded opposing-update schedules run; Then no outlet shows enter-then-exit within one wave and no null-extended row is retracted by its own wave; Control: ungated mode tears at the rate `E2-SUITE` measured (50/50 seeds).
*Not corpus*: it names concrete kernel operator classes and an opt-in constructor flag — implementation detail, not an implementation-neutral requirement. The corpus expresses the *consequence* via BS-1.

**BS-5 — ungated contributor rejected at build**
Given an `observeAligned` builder registering a view whose ancestor set contains an ungated `IntersectSetCell`; When the edge is built; Then construction fails naming that cell and outlet, and no cell is spawned. Covers [KE2-09].

**BS-6 — stalled arm holds, then releases in order**
Given a three-view aligned edge in WAIT mode; When one arm stalls at wave 5 and waves 6–10 arrive on the others, then the arm resumes; Then no composite for waves ≥5 is published while stalled, and on resume waves 5–10 publish in per-source-counter order with none lost or reordered. Covers [KE2-03], [KE2-13], [KE2-14].

**BS-7 — degrade publishes, and says so**
Given the same edge in DEGRADE mode; When one arm reports a non-recoverable stall at wave 5; Then wave 5 publishes with the stalled edge removed from the expected set, and the published composite names the dropped edge; and a composite published before the stall is not retroactively marked degraded. Covers [KE2-11], [KE2-12].

**BS-8 — edge close releases held waves**
Given a WAIT-mode edge holding waves on a stalled arm; When that arm's link closes (`EdgeClose`); Then the held waves publish against the shrunken expected set rather than hanging. Covers [KE2-15].

**BS-9 — attach mid-stream**
Given a graph already writing at wave 40; When an aligned edge attaches and catch-up baselines install as arm state; Then the edge reports its guarantee-from wave, no catch-up traffic is admitted to a completeness set, and every composite from the first waved delta onward satisfies BS-1's invariant. Covers [KE2-16], [KE2-17], [KE2-18].

**BS-10 — write becomes visible**
Given a writer holding a visibility handle for wave `(s, 7)` registered against an aligned edge; When that edge publishes the composite for `(s, 7)`; Then the handle completes naming `(s, 7)`, and it completes exactly once. Covers [KE2-19], [KE2-20].

**BS-11 — vacuous visibility**
Given a write whose wave is absorbed to no effective output at every contributing view; When the wave's absorb-acks settle the edge; Then the handle completes as visible-vacuously and does not remain outstanding. Covers [KE2-21].

**BS-12 — degraded visibility is not success**
Given a handle for a wave that publishes only under a shrunken expected set; When the composite publishes; Then the handle completes as visible-degraded, names the dropped edges, and a caller distinguishing the two outcomes can do so without parsing a string. Covers [KE2-22], [KE2-26].

**BS-13 — shutdown does not abandon handles**
Given outstanding handles; When the observation edge is closed or the host shut down; Then every outstanding handle completes exceptionally with a named reason, and none is left incomplete. Covers [KE2-23].

**BS-14 — handles add no frames**
Given a two-host bridged graph with visibility handles in use; When N writes are driven; Then the frame count and the set of protocol lanes on the wire are identical to the same run without handles. Covers [KE2-24].

**BS-15 — point-consistent sink refuses a handle**
Given a `CompositeSink` from `observeAll`; When a visibility handle is registered against it; Then registration is refused with a reason naming `[22-OBS-01]`. Covers [KE2-27].

**BS-16 — bridged alignment** *(→ concord if a driver binding exists; else DISPUTES)*
Given a two-JVM graph over `:wire` with one contributing view sourced from the remote host; When seeded schedules drive both hosts; Then every published composite satisfies BS-1's invariant, and a remote absorbing cell's `Progress` ack settles the local arm. Covers [KE2-28], [KE2-29], [KE2-30].
*Corpus placement is conditional*: the concord driver's kernel binding is in-process (`civictech.concord.driver.kernel`). If it cannot host a two-JVM bridge, this scenario stays a `demo/shopping` test and `[22-OBS-28/29]`'s corpus coverage is filed in DISPUTES per [KE2-30] — that is the honest outcome, not a same-JVM stand-in dressed as a bridge.

**BS-17 — divergent origination rejected**
Given two contributing views whose upstream paths pass through a re-origination point that is not a common ancestor; When the aligned edge is built; Then construction fails naming the origination point. Covers [KE2-31], [KE2-32].

**BS-18 — shopping emits one frame per op**
Given `demo/shopping` wired through one `observeAligned` sink, single-JVM and two-JVM peer mode; When one ingress operation is applied; Then exactly one SSE frame is emitted and no frame shows a `produce`/`wanted` item absent from `items`. Covers [KE2-33].
*Not corpus*: demo-level acceptance over an HTTP/SSE shell, not an implementation-neutral kernel requirement.

**BS-19 — `readState` stays wave-neutral**
Given a graph mid-wave; When `ManagedHost.readState` is called; Then it answers between invocations, moves no wave counter, and its result is unchanged by the presence or absence of an aligned edge. Covers [KE2-34].

**BS-20 — concordance closes**
Given the corpus after this epic; When `./gradlew :concord:concordance` regenerates `doc/spec/CONCORDANCE.md`; Then `22-OBS-01` and `22-OBS-02` are no longer `gap` rows and no orphan scenario or dangling `covers:` id is reported. Covers [KE2-35].

7. **KE2-F7 — Concord corpus closure over `[22-OBS-01]`/`[22-OBS-02]`.** Scenarios +
   regenerated concordance; DISPUTES entry if bridged coverage is not constructible.
   **[KE2-35]**, **[KE2-30]**, BS-1…BS-3, BS-20.
8. **KE2-F8 — Bridged aligned observation (two-JVM).** In `demo/shopping` or `:wire`.
   **[KE2-28]–[KE2-30]**, BS-16.
9. **KE2-F9 — Consumer adoption.** `demo/shopping` E2.6 (and the `skillmatch`/`tiering`
   follow-ons noted in `doc/demo-findings.md`), plus the WKB2-facing aligned read composed

Ordering within the epic: F2 → F3 → {F4, F5, F6} → F7 → F8 → F9, with **F1 free-floating
and pullable to the front of the lane**.

---

## 8. Verification

```bash
# Narrowest first
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.observe.AlignedObserveTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.observe.AlignedObserveStallTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.observe.WriteVisibilityTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.data.op.FrontierGatedEmissionTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.data.op.OperatorAbsorbAckTest'

# The regression harness for the extracted fold — must stay green byte-for-byte
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.consistency.*'

# The acceptance suite with teeth (E2.5), including its three failure controls
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.consistency.InternalConsistencyTest'

# Corpus + concordance (the two gap rows)
./gradlew :concord:test -Pconcord.profiles=core
./gradlew :concord:test
./gradlew :concord:concordance
./gradlew :concord:check

# Bridged and consumer surfaces
./gradlew :wire:test
./gradlew :demo:shopping:test
./gradlew :demo:exchange:test

# Full gate before completion
./gradlew test
```

`:kernel:compileKotlin` depends on `:gen:test`, so a generator regression surfaces as a
kernel compile failure — no separate `:gen:test` invocation is needed to notice one, but
run it if descriptors are touched (they should not be).

---

## 9. Risks and open questions

1. **The milestone-plan row is stale.** The single largest risk is a worker rebuilding
   `AlignedCompositeCell` or `AbsorbAck` from the 96-plan text (which still says
   `host/AlignedObserve.kt` and `data/AbsorbAck.kt` — both wrong). §0 is mandatory reading.
2. **DEGRADE's correctness contract is genuinely open** (G-40, verbatim: "pin the DEGRADE
   correctness contract — how downstream distinguishes a degraded emission from a genuine
   one"). [KE2-12] states the disclosure obligation, which is what KE2 can honestly
   deliver. Whether that disclosure is *sufficient* needs a consumer; if none exists at
   implementation time, F4 should ship WAIT + disclosure and leave DEGRADE opt-in and
   documented as unpinned rather than invent a consumer contract.
3. **Bridged coverage may not be constructible in the corpus.** `:kernel` cannot depend on
   `:wire`, and the concord kernel driver is in-process. [KE2-30] pre-commits the honest
   outcome (DISPUTES entry) so the epic cannot quietly degrade into a same-JVM stand-in.
4. **The gating rule may be the wrong shape.** [KE2-09]'s build-time rejection assumes an
   ungated non-monotone ancestor is always an error. It might instead be legitimate when
   the ancestor's output is monotone in practice. If the check proves too strict against a
   real demo graph, the escape must be an explicit opt-out at the call site, never a
   silent downgrade of the check.
5. **R11 interacts with KE5.** A `CycleHead` is a re-origination point. [KE2-31]'s check
   will reject aligned reads over cycle regions. If KE5 lands first (it does, §4 position
   7), that rejection is immediately visible to AGO4/QRY2 consumers. Filing the follow-up
   is in scope; solving it is 95 R11.
6. **KE3 overlap on `WaveFrontier`.** E3.4 shares the component and runs earlier in the
   lane. KE2 must consume the merged KE3 state, not a locally reconstructed one
   (AGENTS.md multi-agent run discipline).
7. **Ack-slice ordering cost.** Pulling F1 forward to after KAGG-R means it ships before
   F4 exists, so [KE2-22]/[KE2-26] are vacuously satisfied at that point. That is
   acceptable and expected; the follow-up edit when F4 lands must be filed at the time F1
   merges, not discovered later.
8. **G-63 serialization.** KE2 touches `observe`, `consistency`, `data.op`, `control`,
   `host` — all inside the single kernel SCC. No part of this epic may run concurrently
   with another kernel-lane chunk, including its own pulled-forward F1.
