# KE5 — E5: cycles, `LoopContext`, iteration-cut fixpoints, stratification

Kernel-lane chunk, position 7 of `computenet-milestone-plan.md` §4. Realizes
`doc/spec/90-roadmap/96-incremental-engines-plan.md` §"Milestone E5 — Cycles and incremental
fixpoints" (E5.1–E5.7) against the decided-but-partial cycle model in
`doc/spec/20-dataflow-semantics/21-propagation.md` §Cycles.

Normative anchors: `[21-CYCLE-01]`, `[21-CYCLE-02]`, `[21-CYCLE-03]` (21-propagation.md
lines 326–342); G-19 residual and G-41 (`90-roadmap/91-gap-analysis.md` rows G-19, G-41);
93 I-5 (wave semantics in cycles), I-6 (divergence guard), I-23 (upstream frontier
traversal / settled composition); research-gated corners 95 R2 (weak-tier convergence) and
95 R16 (cross-host + nested cycle structure).

---

## 1. Ambition / Why

Today ComputeNet can *survive* a cycle; it cannot *mean* one.

`[21-CYCLE-02]` — bounded-lap termination — is implemented and covered
(`concord/corpus/34-cycles/34-CYCLE-01.yaml`). `[21-CYCLE-03]` — strong-tier convergence to
a fixpoint — is a **gap row in `doc/spec/CONCORDANCE.md` line 71** with no covering
scenario. That single uncovered id is the whole of KE5's reason to exist: the kernel
terminates loops but never claims, observes, or exports a fixpoint.

Three consequences, each a downstream blocker recorded in the plan:

- **BB-GRA** (LDBC Graphalytics: PageRank, BFS, SSSP, WCC, CDLP, LCC) and **BB-SNB BI**
  are listed in the plan's §3 kernel-enablement matrix with *nothing* in the "already in
  the kernel" column and **KE5** as the sole kernel gap. PageRank-on-cells is named as
  "the E5 stress test with a published reference answer" — i.e. the first workload where
  ComputeNet's answer can be *wrong* rather than merely slow.
- **QRY2** (recursive queries → cycle regions) has no substrate: a recursive Datalog rule
  needs an iteration identity, a fixpoint cut, and a stratification check, none of which
  exist.
- **AGO4** must replace `:demo:agora`'s *application-level* head approximation
  (`demo/agora/src/main/kotlin/civictech/agora/cell/EdgeCell.kt:32-55`: `quiescence > 0`
  designates an edge a head; `AgoraService.kt:135` decides which edges get it) with kernel
  machinery, closing agora's G-19 residual for the set-valued (strong-tier) view.

The research package is already written down and decided (96 §E5 preamble): Naiad's
ingress/feedback/egress structural triple (`doc/research/incremental-engines/02-*`, §1)
gives an iteration a place to live; DBSP's cycle rule
(`doc/research/incremental-engines/01-dbsp-feldera.md` §4) says the incremental loop *is*
the loop of the incremental body — so the delta circulation ComputeNet already performs is
semi-naive evaluation by construction, and termination is exactly "a full iteration
produces only empty effective deltas", which effective-only emission already detects. KE5
is the work of *cashing in* that alignment, not of inventing it.

Honesty constraint carried verbatim from the plan: **weak-tier convergence stays
research-gated under 95 R2.** Every KE5 item ships the bounded-lap contract for the weak
tier and an exact claim only for the strong (idempotent-merge) tier. No item may promote
"the damper stopped firing" into "the loop converged".

---

## 2. What already exists (searched; do NOT rebuild)

Per AGENTS.md's warning about partial substrate — the following is *landed code*, and the
96 §E5 preamble's claim that the model is "decided and partially built" understates it in
one place and overstates it in another.

| Concern | Real type / file | State |

| Non-monotone operator | `data/op/SemiJoinCell.kt` (antijoin / `negated`, difference) — classified non-monotone in `doc/spec/20-dataflow-semantics/24-data-cells.md` §`[24-OP-SEMIJOIN-01..04]` | **Exists, unmarked.** No `NonMonotone` marker anywhere in the tree |
| Conformance surface | `concord/corpus/34-cycles/34-CYCLE-01.yaml`, `34-CYCLE-REJECT-01.yaml`; driver cells `feedback`/`loopOutlet`/`feedbackInput` in `concord/src/main/kotlin/civictech/concord/driver/kernel/KernelAdapters.kt:204-250` and `KernelCatalog.kt:202` | **Exists.** Covers `[21-CYCLE-01]`, `[21-CYCLE-02]` |
| App-level approximation | `demo/agora/.../cell/EdgeCell.kt:32-55`, `AgoraService.kt:135`; tests `CycleQuiescenceTest.kt`, `AgoraExitTest.kt` (100 seeds, step-budgeted) | **Exists.** The thing AGO4 replaces for the set-valued view |
| Drain-to-idle harness | `testkit/src/main/kotlin/civictech/testkit/SimWorld.kt:31-36` (hard step budget, "quiescence is asserted, not hoped for") | **Exists.** Reuse; do not write a second drain loop |

**Does not exist anywhere in the tree** (verified by repository-wide grep for
`LoopContext|loopContext|stratif|fixpoint|IterationCut|iteration-cut` over `*.kt`):
no `LoopContext`, no iteration counter, no cycle-region/SCC capture, no ingress/egress
classification, no `settled` probe, no `NonMonotone` marker, no stratification check. The
`fixpoint` hits are all prose in `doc/` plus a closed-form decay assertion in
`demo/exchange/.../ExchangeCompositionExitTest.kt`.

Net: **the termination half is built; the semantics half is empty.** KE5 is the semantics
half.

---

## 3. What we build

**In-place kernel change — no new Gradle module.** The work touches four existing kernel
packages plus one generator marker and one demo:

| Package (existing) | Change |
|---|---|
| `civictech.cell` (`MessageContext.kt`) | New `LoopContext` type; additive `loop: LoopContext? = null` field on `MessageContext` |
| `civictech.cell.port` (`Cycle.kt`, `FanOutlet.kt`) | `FeedbackInlet` stamps `loop` alongside its fresh `Timestamp`; per-`(outerWave, iteration)` accounting; `settled: LoopContext?` probe generalizing `lastQuiescent`; transparent-flow copies `loop` |
| `civictech.cell.host` (`TopologyIndex.kt`, `LinkAdmission.kt`, `LocationRegistry.kt`, `ManagedHost.kt`) | `wouldCloseCycle` boolean → SCC/cycle-region capture; region registry; ingress-stamp / egress-strip edge classification; settled-egress hold buffer; `CycleRequiresStratification` rejection |
| `civictech.cell.data` / `.data.op` | `NonMonotone` marker on `SemiJoinCell` in negated/difference mode; verification that in-loop cells circulate deltas **against integrated state** (re-entry), fixing any that reset per lap |
| `civictech.cell.evolve` (`PromotionPolicy.kt`) | `PromotionJudge` cycle gate reads `settled` instead of `lastQuiescent` (deferral semantics preserved) |
| `civictech.cell.wire` (`WireCodec.kt`) | `loop` rides `MessageContext` additively; absent field decodes `null`; **no frame-version bump** |
| `:gen` | If `94 W1.3`'s descriptor-bit scan family has landed, `NonMonotone` becomes a `CellDescriptor` bit (preferred); otherwise a runtime `is`-check exactly like `Magnitude` |
| `:demo:agora` | Grounded-extension labelling as a kernel-headed set-valued least fixpoint (AGO4's substrate; the payoff demo, E5.7) |

### Entry points (the public surface a consumer sees)

1. `MessageContext.loop: LoopContext?` — read-only for cell authors, like `hop`.
2. `FeedbackInlet.settled: LoopContext?` — the fixpoint probe. Non-null names the outer
   wave and the final iteration of the settled region.
3. `LinkResult.Rejected("CycleRequiresStratification: …")` — the new admission verdict,
   joining `CycleWithoutHead` and `CycleWithoutDamping`.
4. A per-region **egress mode** (eager pass-through default; opt-in settled egress) —
   declared at head/region scope, not per-cell.

### How, using ComputeNet's real mechanisms

**Iteration identity is a nested context, not a `Timestamp` extension.** The decision is
already made in the 96 §E5 preamble and must not be relitigated: `Timestamp` stays
one-dimensional and per-source (`MessageContext.kt:16-19`), 20/22's wave rules stay
untouched, and the wire stays additive. The head's fresh-`Timestamp`-per-lap
(`Cycle.kt:118`) remains the wave mechanism; `LoopContext(outerWave, iteration)` is a
second, orthogonal coordinate that is **never part of the wave join key** — the same
contract `hop` already carries (`MessageContext.kt:40-46`).

**Ingress / feedback / egress falls out of admission.** `admitCycle`
(`LinkAdmission.kt:81`) already runs exactly once, on the connect that closes the cycle,
and already has the topology in hand. That is the natural place to promote
`wouldCloseCycle`'s boolean answer into the *set* of cells on the cycle (the SCC reachable
both ways across the closing edge) and record it. Region-crossing edges are then
classifiable: inbound ⇒ stamp `LoopContext(currentWave, 0)`; the `FeedbackInlet` ⇒
`iteration + 1`, `outerWave` preserved; outbound ⇒ strip. Region membership must be
maintained on later `link`/`unlink` touching region cells — `TopologyIndex.linked` /
`unlinked` (`TopologyIndex.kt:32-42`) are the hooks.

**The fixpoint cut is free.** DBSP's "the differentiated change stream is empty" is
observable without a new mechanism, because ComputeNet's emitters already enforce
effective-only emission: an idempotent-merge lap carrying no new information derives an
empty delta and *is not emitted* (21-propagation.md:305-310). So "a full iteration
delivered no effective delta to any of the region's feedback inlets" is the cut. For the
strong tier that is exact and threshold-free. For the weak tier the existing `quiescence`
damper (`Cycle.kt:114-116`) feeds the same probe, and the resulting cut is *damped* — it
reports settling, and under 95 R2 it must not be read as convergence.

**Incremental re-entry is a verification task before it is an implementation task.** A new
outer input reaching a settled region opens `LoopContext(newOuterWave, 0)`. If loop cells
circulate deltas against their integrated state (which `SetCell`/`OrMapCell`/the
`data/op/` family are believed to do already), the lap sequence *is* the stream of fixpoint
adjustments and semi-naive equivalence holds for free — DBSP Thm-5.4 shape. The engineering
is to *verify the association and fix anything that resets state per lap*, not to build an
adjustment engine.

**Stratification is a marker plus one admission predicate.** `SemiJoinCell`'s antijoin is
already documented non-monotone in 24-data-cells (`[24-OP-SEMIJOIN-03/04]`: "absence
assertions … non-monotone in the CALM sense"). Marking it and rejecting a region that
contains one on the cycle path is the entire mechanism.

---

## 4. Scope boundaries

**In scope** (from the plan's edges): everything AGO4, QRY2, BB-GRA and BB-SNB-BI need from
the kernel to express a recursive computation and observe its fixpoint.

**Out of scope — belongs to 95-research-plan.md, do not silently solve:**

- **Weak-tier fixpoint convergence (95 R2, G-19 residual).** Ship the bounded-lap contract.
  A numeric/`Magnitude` loop gets a *damped cut* and no convergence claim. Do not add a
  convergence proof, a contraction classifier, or a backoff schedule.
- **Cross-host cycles and nested loops (95 R16, G-41 residual).** Link-time admission
  cannot see a cycle closed across hosts; the hop guard stays the backstop. `LoopContext`
  is **single-level**: nested cycle regions are *rejected at admission*, not supported.

**Out of scope — other chunks:**

- KE5's plan row is `Depends on: —`. It has **no hard prerequisite**. It sits at kernel-lane
  position 7 (after `MEM1`, before `KE2`) purely as a serialization ordering; that ordering
  is recorded here, not as a dependency edge.
- **KE2** (E2 observation edge, aligned multi-view sink) composes *with* settled egress but
  neither blocks the other (96 §E5 dependency note). Do not build ack/absorb machinery here.
- **KBLK** (bulk/benchmark mode) is what makes BB-GRA's bulk load fast. KE5 makes it
  *correct*. Do not fold WAL/ingress-batching config into this chunk.
- **BB-GRA / BB-SNB-BI** are the acceptance suites and live in the benchmark-bridge lane
  (`:bench`), not in the kernel diff. KE5 ships kernel tests plus the agora payoff demo; the
  Graphalytics reference-answer harness is BB-GRA's deliverable.
- **AGO4 / QRY2** consume KE5 from merged `main`. E5.7 (the agora grounded-extension
  fixpoint) is KE5's own strong-tier adopter and proof-of-payoff; the wider AGO4 story
  (replacing all app-side heads, including the weak-tier credence loop) stays in AGO4 and
  stays R2-gated.
- **E6 `negate` / Z-sets.** KE5's `NonMonotone` marker must be *extensible to* E6's `negate`
  (96 §E6 notes the interop) but does not build the weighted family.

**Kernel-lane serialization constraint (G-63).** The kernel is a single SCC. KE5 is a
kernel-lane chunk and **must not run concurrently with another kernel-lane chunk** (`KX`,
`KE1`, `KFX`, `KAGG-R`, `KE3`, `MEM1`, `MEM2`, `KE2`, `KE4`, `PLC3`, `SEC1`). It enters the
lane at position 7, after `MEM1`/`MEM2` and before `KE2`, and holds the lane until merged.
Its features may parallelize *within* the chunk along 96 §E5's internal dependency note
(E5.2 → E5.3 → {E5.4, E5.6}; E5.4 → E5.5 → E5.7), but the chunk itself is exclusive. Its
diff touches `MessageContext`, `FanOutlet`, `TopologyIndex`, `LinkAdmission` and
`PromotionPolicy` — the highest-traffic seams in the kernel — so concurrent kernel work
would conflict structurally, not just textually.

---

---

## 7. Risks and open questions

1. **`CycleWithoutDamping` is undocumented in the spec.** `LinkAdmission.kt:106-113`
   rejects a headed cycle with no damping witness (FU-8 / ADR 1 feature 8), but
   `[21-CYCLE-01]` lists only `CycleWithoutHead`, `CycleRequiresMagnitude` and
   `CycleRejectsLeased`. A strong-tier `SetDelta` loop is admitted today only because
   `hasDampingWitness` (`Handshake.kt:124`) accepts a MONOTONE/IDEMPOTENT producer nature —
   so **E5.7's set-valued agora fixpoint depends on a check the spec does not describe.**
   KE5-F1 must reconcile the two (most likely: document the damping witness as the
   `CycleRequiresMagnitude` realization). If it cannot be reconciled honestly, it is a
   `DISPUTES.md` entry, not a quietly relaxed check.
2. **96 §E5.3's cited seam is stale.** It says "extend `ManagedHost.wouldCloseCycle`"; the
   function lives on `TopologyIndex` (`TopologyIndex.kt:68`) since RS-8.4
   (`ManagedHost.kt:1456-1458`). Cosmetic, but a worker following the ticket literally will
   look in the wrong file.
3. **Wrapper seam is implementer's choice** (96 E5.3 flags Medium certainty): ingress/egress
   stamping can be a link-install proxy or a port decoration. Both must preserve
   `Owned`/`Leased` accounting — a stamping wrapper that copies a payload would break the
   exclusive-payload invariant, and `Leased` is already forbidden on cycle edges
   (`Cycle.kt:108-112`).
4. **SCC capture cost on the link path.** `wouldCloseCycle` is a rare-path DFS today (10/13
   permits expensive linking, P2). Full SCC capture plus membership maintenance under churn
   is strictly more work on every region-touching connect/unlink. If a graph with many
   regions makes linking pathological, that is a finding for BEN1/BEN2, not a reason to
   cache incorrectly.
5. **Region membership under RESTART / promotion / evolution is unpinned** (G-41 names
   "head behavior under RESTART/promotion" explicitly). KE5 must at minimum not *regress*
   `PromotionJudge`'s deferral semantics; full RESTART-at-a-head semantics may need to stay
   an explicit residual.
6. **Concurrent outer waves** through one region (E5.5) are claimed safe because iteration
   identity is per-`outerWave`. Under `SimulationController` this is single-threaded and
   easy; under a real `ManagedHost` with the head as a fusion barrier, the per-region
   accounting is shared mutable state and needs the same discipline as `TopologyIndex`'s
   concurrent maps.
7. **The honest gap that will remain.** `[21-CYCLE-03]` will be coverable for the strong
   tier only. If the concord corpus cannot express "strong-tier loop converges to the batch
   least fixpoint" without smuggling in a threshold, the requirement goes to
   `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` rather than being weakened into a bounded-lap restatement
   that `[21-CYCLE-02]` already covers.
8. **Hop-bound calibration stays uncalibrated.** `hopBound = 64` (`ManagedHost.kt:97`) is
   the magic number G-41 names. KE5 relies on it as the divergent-control backstop
   (behaviour spec BS-04) but does not calibrate it against loop diameter — that is G-41
   residual work.

# KE5 — Functional requirements (EARS) and behaviour specifications

Ids are epic-scoped (`[KE5-nn]`), mirroring `doc/spec/`'s `[NN-SLUG-nn]` shape but
namespaced so they never collide with a spec id. Each cites the normative spec id or
decision it makes true. "Cites" column: `21-CYCLE-0n` are requirement ids in
`doc/spec/20-dataflow-semantics/21-propagation.md`; `24-OP-SEMIJOIN-0n` in
`doc/spec/20-dataflow-semantics/24-data-cells.md`; `I-n` are integrated decisions in
`doc/spec/90-roadmap/93-feature-interactions.md`; `G-n` are gap rows in
`91-gap-analysis.md`; `R2`/`R16` are research items in `95-research-plan.md`.

---

## A. `LoopContext` — the iteration coordinate (96 E5.2)

- **[KE5-01]** (Ubiquitous) The kernel SHALL define `LoopContext(outerWave: Timestamp?, iteration: Long)` as a `@Serializable @SerialName("LoopContext")` data class in `civictech.cell`. — *cites 93 I-5; 96 E5.2*
- **[KE5-02]** (Ubiquitous) `MessageContext` SHALL carry an additive field `loop: LoopContext? = null` whose default is `null` and whose absence in an encoded frame SHALL decode to `null`. — *cites 21-CYCLE-01 (context extension), 93 I-5*
- **[KE5-03]** (Ubiquitous) `MessageContext.loop` SHALL NOT participate in any wave join key, glitch-free completeness set, or wave-identity comparison, on the same terms as `MessageContext.hop`. — *cites 20/22 rule 2 as cited by 21-CYCLE-01; 93 I-5*
- **[KE5-04]** (Event-driven) WHEN a transparent-flow emission copies an incoming `MessageContext`, the outlet SHALL propagate `loop` unchanged, in the same copy that already rewrites `sourcePort` and increments `hop`. — *cites 21-CYCLE-01; 93 I-5*
- **[KE5-05]** (Event-driven) WHEN a `FeedbackInlet` re-originates a lap, it SHALL be the only writer of `loop`, stamping `LoopContext(outerWave = incoming.loop?.outerWave, iteration = (incoming.loop?.iteration ?: 0) + 1)` alongside its existing freshly minted `Timestamp`. — *cites 21-CYCLE-01 (re-origination), 93 I-5*
- **[KE5-06]** (Event-driven) WHEN a `FeedbackInlet` re-originates a lap, `MessageContext.hop` SHALL continue to reset to 0, unchanged by the introduction of `loop`. — *cites 21-CYCLE-02 (hop guard as backstop); 93 I-5*
- **[KE5-07]** (Ubiquitous) Encoding and decoding a loop-stamped `MessageContext` across the wire SHALL NOT require a frame-version bump, and a decoder built before KE5 SHALL decode a loop-stamped frame without error, observing `loop == null`. — *cites 96 E5.2 (wire-additive); AGENTS.md wire-compatibility invariant*
- **[KE5-08]** (Ubiquitous) `LoopContext` SHALL be single-level: no `LoopContext` value shall reference or nest another. — *cites 96 E5.1 point 1; deferred structure → 95 R16*
- **[KE5-09]** (State-driven) WHILE a delivery is inside a cycle region, its `loop.iteration` SHALL be strictly monotone non-decreasing per `outerWave` along the feedback path. — *cites 21-CYCLE-02; 93 I-5*
- **[KE5-10]** (Unwanted behaviour) IF a cell author attempts to write `MessageContext.loop` from outside a `FeedbackInlet` re-origination or an ingress stamp, THEN the API SHALL NOT expose a supported means to do so (`loop` is read-only to cell code, as `hop` is). — *cites 93 I-5; AGENTS.md invariant "cell authors never touch MessageContext"*

## B. Cycle-region capture and edge classification (96 E5.3, G-41 partial)

- **[KE5-11]** (Event-driven) WHEN a `connect` closes a locally-visible cycle and is admitted, the host SHALL capture the cycle region — the set of cells mutually reachable across the closing edge (its strongly connected component) — and record it in the topology index. — *cites 21-CYCLE-01; G-41; 96 E5.3*
- **[KE5-12]** (Ubiquitous) Every edge whose target is inside a captured cycle region and whose source is outside it SHALL be classified **ingress**; every edge whose source is inside and target outside SHALL be classified **egress**; the region's `FeedbackInlet` edges SHALL be classified **feedback**. — *cites 96 E5.1 point 1 (Naiad structural triple); research 02 §1*
- **[KE5-13]** (Event-driven) WHEN a delivery crosses an ingress edge, it SHALL be stamped `LoopContext(outerWave = the incoming wave's Timestamp, iteration = 0)`. — *cites 96 E5.1 point 1*
- **[KE5-14]** (Event-driven) WHEN a delivery crosses an egress edge under the default eager mode, its `loop` SHALL be stripped to `null` before the delivery leaves the region. — *cites 96 E5.1 point 5; 21-CYCLE-01*
- **[KE5-15]** (Event-driven) WHEN a `link` or `unlink` touches a cell in a captured region, region membership SHALL be recomputed so that classification stays correct for subsequent deliveries. — *cites 96 E5.3; 20/22 §Topology versioning*
- **[KE5-16]** (Unwanted behaviour) IF a `connect` would create a cycle region nested inside or overlapping an existing captured region, THEN the connect SHALL be `Rejected` with a distinct reason naming nested cycles as unsupported. — *cites 96 E5.1 point 1; deferred to 95 R16*
- **[KE5-17]** (Unwanted behaviour) IF a cycle is closed across hosts, THEN admission SHALL NOT claim to have detected it, and the runtime hop guard SHALL remain the backstop that dead-letters the runaway invocation as `CycleError`. — *cites 21-CYCLE-02; G-41; 95 R16*
- **[KE5-18]** (Ubiquitous) Region capture SHALL NOT weaken any existing admission verdict: a headless closure SHALL still be `Rejected` as `CycleWithoutHead`, an undamped headed closure SHALL still be `Rejected` as `CycleWithoutDamping`, and a `Leased` payload on a cycle edge SHALL still raise `CycleError` at runtime. — *cites 21-CYCLE-01; FU-8 / ADR 1 feature 8*
- **[KE5-19]** (Ubiquitous) Ingress stamping and egress stripping SHALL NOT copy, clone, or duplicate an `Owned` payload; absorption at the head SHALL remain the single consumption. — *cites 21-CYCLE-01 ("`Owned` is permitted — absorption *is* the single consumption"); 20/23*

## C. Iteration-cut fixpoint detection (96 E5.4, G-19 mechanics)

- **[KE5-20]** (Ubiquitous) A `FeedbackInlet` SHALL account absorbed laps per `(outerWave, iteration)`. — *cites 96 E5.4; 93 I-6*
- **[KE5-21]** (Ubiquitous) The **fixpoint cut** SHALL be defined as: an iteration in which no feedback inlet of the region receives an effective delta. — *cites 21-CYCLE-03; research 01 §4 (DBSP: "the differentiated change stream is empty")*
- **[KE5-22]** (Ubiquitous) `FeedbackInlet` SHALL expose `settled: LoopContext?`, generalizing `lastQuiescent: Boolean?`; non-null SHALL name the outer wave and the final iteration at which the cut was observed. — *cites 96 E5.4; 50/53 promotion-gate wording*
- **[KE5-23]** (Event-driven) WHEN the fixpoint cut is observed for an outer wave in a region whose feedback deltas are idempotent-merge (strong tier), `settled` SHALL become non-null exactly at that iteration and SHALL be exact and threshold-independent. — *cites 21-CYCLE-03*
- **[KE5-24]** (State-driven) WHILE a region is strong-tier and settled for an outer wave, the region's integrated state SHALL equal the least fixpoint of the loop body over the inputs of that outer wave. — *cites 21-CYCLE-03; research 01 §4 (guarantee scope: stratified queries, finite domains, idempotent-merge tier)*
- **[KE5-25]** (Ubiquitous) For a weak (`Magnitude`-only) tier region, `settled` SHALL be derived from the existing per-inlet `quiescence` damper and SHALL be documented as a *damped* cut carrying the bounded-lap contract only. — *cites 21-CYCLE-02; G-19 residual; 95 R2*
- **[KE5-26]** (Unwanted behaviour) IF a region is weak-tier, THEN no API, KDoc, spec sentence, or test assertion introduced by KE5 SHALL state or imply that a non-null `settled` constitutes convergence to a fixpoint. — *cites 21-CYCLE-03 ("the weak tier converges only if its loop map is contractive w.r.t. `size()`, which the framework does not verify"); 95 R2*
- **[KE5-27]** (Ubiquitous) `null` `settled` SHALL be treated by every consumer as "not settled", never as vacuously settled, preserving the rule `lastQuiescent` already carries. — *cites 50/53 ("without G-19 throttling, cycle promotion is deferred, not attempted"); G-50*
- **[KE5-28]** (Event-driven) WHEN `PromotionJudge` gates a promotion on a cycle head, it SHALL consult `settled` and SHALL preserve its existing deferral verdict when `settled` is `null`. — *cites 50/53; 93 I-6*
- **[KE5-29]** (Unwanted behaviour) IF a region never reaches the cut, THEN laps SHALL continue until the host hop bound is exceeded, at which point the invocation SHALL be dead-lettered as `CycleError` and `settled` SHALL remain `null`. — *cites 21-CYCLE-02 (hop-guard dead-letter as the hard backstop)*
- **[KE5-30]** (Unwanted behaviour) IF a region never reaches the cut, THEN the dead-letter SHALL be attributable — the recorded failure SHALL identify the cycle region and, where available, the outer wave — and SHALL NOT silently drop an `Owned` payload. — *cites 21-CYCLE-02; AGENTS.md exclusive-payload invariant*

## D. Incremental re-entry (96 E5.5)

- **[KE5-31]** (Event-driven) WHEN a new outer input reaches a settled region, the region SHALL begin a fresh `LoopContext(newOuterWave, iteration = 0)` rather than resuming the previous outer wave's iteration counter. — *cites 96 E5.5; research 01 §4*
- **[KE5-32]** (Ubiquitous) Cells inside a cycle region SHALL circulate deltas **against their integrated state**; no in-loop cell shall reset its state at the start of a lap. — *cites 96 E5.5; research 01 §4 Thm 5.4 shape*
- **[KE5-33]** (State-driven) WHILE a region is settled for outer wave *W*, its output SHALL equal the batch fixpoint over the region's inputs as of *W* (semi-naive equivalence). — *cites 21-CYCLE-03*
- **[KE5-34]** (Complex) WHEN two outer waves are in flight through one region AND both eventually settle, THEN each SHALL be accounted independently by its own `outerWave`, and neither settle SHALL be reported against the other's outer wave. — *cites 96 E5.5 ("iteration identity is per-outerWave — the two-dimensional time"); 93 I-5*
- **[KE5-35]** (Unwanted behaviour) IF a retraction reaches a settled region, THEN the region SHALL re-open, adjust, and re-settle to the fixpoint over the reduced input — it SHALL NOT retain state derived only from the retracted input. — *cites 21-CYCLE-03; 24 retraction semantics*

## E. Stratification (96 E5.6, G-41 partial)

- **[KE5-36]** (Ubiquitous) The kernel SHALL provide a `NonMonotone` classification for operator cells, realized as a `CellDescriptor` bit where the descriptor scan family permits it and otherwise as a runtime marker check on the same terms as `Magnitude`. — *cites 24-OP-SEMIJOIN-03 (non-monotone in the CALM sense); 10/12 descriptor-bit note*
- **[KE5-37]** (Ubiquitous) `SemiJoinCell` in negated (antijoin) or difference mode SHALL be classified `NonMonotone`. — *cites 24-OP-SEMIJOIN-01, 24-OP-SEMIJOIN-03*
- **[KE5-38]** (Unwanted behaviour) IF admission would capture a cycle region containing a `NonMonotone` cell on the cycle path, THEN the closing `connect` SHALL be `Rejected` with reason `CycleRequiresStratification`. — *cites 96 E5.1 point 4; G-41*
- **[KE5-39]** (Ubiquitous) A `NonMonotone` cell *outside* the cycle path SHALL NOT cause rejection, even when it is topologically adjacent to the region. — *cites 96 E5.1 point 4 ("on a cycle path")*
- **[KE5-40]** (Ubiquitous) The `NonMonotone` classification SHALL be extensible to a future weighted-family `negate` operator without a second mechanism. — *cites 96 §E6 (E5.6 interop note)*
- **[KE5-41]** (Ubiquitous) Descriptor-carried classification SHALL be threaded from the generated descriptor through the registry to the admission consumer, never recomputed reflectively at runtime. — *cites AGENTS.md invariant "generated descriptors/proxies are authoritative runtime metadata"*

## F. Egress modes (96 E5.1 point 5, I-23)

- **[KE5-42]** (Ubiquitous) Eager pass-through SHALL remain the default egress mode: a head's outlet fan-out is never gated by cycle throttling and no external subscriber is silenced. — *cites 21-CYCLE-01 ("the throttle gates re-origination, never fan-out")*
- **[KE5-43]** (Optional feature) WHERE **settled egress** is enabled for a region, egress deliveries SHALL be held in a buffer keyed by `outerWave` and released only when that outer wave's fixpoint cut is observed. — *cites 96 E5.1 point 5; 93 I-23*
- **[KE5-44]** (Optional feature) WHERE settled egress is enabled, released deliveries SHALL be re-associated to `outerWave` — the wave a downstream glitch-free consumer joins on SHALL be the outer wave, not any head-minted lap wave. — *cites 93 I-23; 20/22 rule 2*
- **[KE5-45]** (Complex) WHEN settled egress is enabled AND a downstream cell is glitch-free AND two arms of that cell are fed from the same cycle region, THEN the downstream cell SHALL observe one complete, mutually consistent set of arm values per outer wave — no partial-fixpoint intermediate SHALL be observable. — *cites 93 I-23; 20/22 §glitch-freedom; 21-CYCLE-01*
- **[KE5-46]** (Unwanted behaviour) IF settled egress is enabled AND a region never settles for an outer wave, THEN the held buffer SHALL be released or accounted at dead-letter time rather than leaked, and any `Owned` payload it holds SHALL be explicitly discharged. — *cites AGENTS.md exclusive-payload invariant; 21-CYCLE-02*
- **[KE5-47]** (Ubiquitous) Settled egress SHALL be opt-in per region and SHALL NOT change the observable behaviour of any graph that does not enable it. — *cites 96 E5.1 point 5*

## G. Honesty and coverage

- **[KE5-48]** (Ubiquitous) The concord corpus SHALL gain at least one scenario covering `[21-CYCLE-03]`, closing the gap row at `doc/spec/CONCORDANCE.md:71`. — *cites 21-CYCLE-03; AGENTS.md concord rules*
- **[KE5-49]** (Unwanted behaviour) IF a KE5 requirement cannot be checked honestly by a scenario or test, THEN it SHALL be recorded in `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` and SHALL NOT be weakened into a passing restatement of a requirement already covered. — *cites AGENTS.md ("a requirement that cannot be checked honestly is filed in DISPUTES.md, never weakened into a passing scenario")*
- **[KE5-50]** (Ubiquitous) `doc/spec/CONCORDANCE.md` SHALL be regenerated, never hand-edited, and `./gradlew :concord:check` SHALL pass with no dangling `covers:` id and no orphan scenario. — *cites AGENTS.md*

### Requirements that are deliberately NOT stated

Named so a reader can see the omission is a decision, not an oversight:

- No requirement asserts weak-tier convergence, a convergence *rate*, or a contraction
  classification. That is 95 R2, and `[21-CYCLE-03]` explicitly disclaims it.
- No requirement asserts cross-host cycle detection or nested-loop support. That is 95 R16;
  `[KE5-16]`/`[KE5-17]` state the *rejection* and the *backstop* instead, which are
  checkable.
- No requirement calibrates the hop bound. G-41 residual.
- **Candidate DISPUTES entry:** `[KE5-24]` ("integrated state equals the least fixpoint")
  is only honestly checkable against an independent batch solver over a *finite* domain.
  For an infinite or unbounded-domain recursion it is unfalsifiable by test. If KE5's
  corpus cannot bound the domain in a scenario, `[KE5-24]` is scoped to finite domains in
  the spec text and the unbounded case goes to `DISPUTES.md` — it must not be restated as
  "the loop terminates", which `[21-CYCLE-02]` already covers.

---

# Behaviour specifications

Given/When/Then, specific enough to become named tests. `covers:` names the requirement
ids a concord scenario would carry; where a scenario does not belong in the corpus, the
reason is stated.

## BS-01 — Loop stamping and hop reset across a lap
**Given** a single-host graph with a `CycleHead` whose `loopOutlet` closes onto its own
`feedbackInput`, seeded from an external source,
**When** the seed is applied and the loop runs to quiescence under `SimWorld`'s step
budget,
**Then** every delivery observed inside the region carries a non-null `loop`; `loop.outerWave`
equals the seeding wave's `Timestamp` for every lap of that outer wave; `loop.iteration`
increases by exactly 1 per lap and never repeats within an outer wave; and
`MessageContext.hop` is 0 on the first delivery after each re-origination.
*Test:* `civictech.cell.port.LoopContextTest`. *Concord:* `covers: [KE5-04, KE5-05, KE5-06, KE5-09]`.

## BS-02 — Wire round-trip against an old decoder (boundary)
**Given** an invocation whose `MessageContext` carries a non-null `loop`,
**When** it is encoded by the post-KE5 codec and decoded by a fixture representing the
pre-KE5 decoder, and vice versa,
**Then** the old decoder succeeds and observes `loop == null`; the new decoder observes
`loop == null` for a pre-KE5 frame; no frame-version bump is required; and no other context
field is perturbed.
*Test:* `civictech.cell.wire.WireCodecTest` + `:wire:test`. *Concord:* not a corpus
scenario — the corpus is implementation-neutral and codec-fixture compatibility is a
JVM-implementation property, not a specified observable behaviour.

## BS-03 — Strong-tier exact fixpoint (the load-bearing positive case)
**Given** a transitive-closure-shaped region over `SetDelta`-carrying cells (idempotent
merge ⇒ strong tier) around a kernel `CycleHead`, and a batch reference solver computing
the least fixpoint over the same input,
**When** an input relation is applied and the graph is drained to idle,
**Then** `settled` is non-null; the region's output equals the batch solver's answer
**exactly** (no threshold, no tolerance); and `settled.iteration` is less than or equal to
the batch solver's iteration count.
*Test:* `civictech.cell.port.IterationCutTest`. *Concord:* `covers: [KE5-21, KE5-23, KE5-24, KE5-33, KE5-48]` — this is the scenario that closes the `21-CYCLE-03` gap row.

## BS-04 — Non-termination: divergent weak-tier control exhausts the iteration budget (failure case)
**Given** a weak-tier region whose loop map is deliberately non-contractive (each lap's
`Magnitude.size()` grows), wired with a `quiescence` threshold it can never fall under, on
a host with `hopBound` configured,
**When** the region is seeded and the host is driven,
**Then** `settled` remains `null` for the entire run; laps continue until `hop` exceeds
`hopBound`; the offending invocation is dead-lettered as `CycleError` naming the hop bound;
the dead-letter is attributable to the region; the graph as a whole still reaches idle (the
budget is exhausted, not the process); no `Owned` payload is silently dropped; and no
assertion anywhere in the test claims convergence.
*Test:* `civictech.cell.port.IterationCutTest` (divergent control) +
`civictech.cell.host.CycleDeadLetterTest`. *Concord:* `covers: [KE5-25, KE5-26, KE5-29, KE5-30]`.

## BS-05 — Iteration-budget exhaustion under a *strong*-tier region with an adversarial input (failure case)
**Given** a strong-tier region whose least fixpoint requires more laps than the configured
hop bound permits (e.g. a long path in a transitive closure with a deliberately low
`hopBound`),
**When** the input is applied and the graph is driven,
**Then** the region is dead-lettered as `CycleError` **rather than** reporting a non-null
`settled` over an incomplete state — i.e. budget exhaustion must never be mistaken for a
fixpoint; and re-running with a hop bound above the loop diameter produces the exact batch
answer of BS-03.
*Test:* `civictech.cell.port.IterationCutTest`. *Concord:* `covers: [KE5-21, KE5-23, KE5-29]`.
This is the scenario that keeps `[KE5-23]` from being vacuous.

## BS-06 — Glitch-freedom across a cycle boundary under settled egress (the load-bearing composition case)
**Given** a cycle region with **two** egress edges feeding two arms of one downstream
glitch-free (`CombineLatest`-shaped) consumer, with settled egress enabled,
**When** an outer wave enters the region, laps several times producing intermediate values
on both arms, and finally settles,
**Then** the downstream consumer observes **exactly one** combined value per outer wave;
that value is composed of both arms' *fixpoint* values (never a mixed
fixpoint/intermediate pair); the delivery it joins on is associated with `outerWave`, not
with any head-minted lap `Timestamp`; and with settled egress **disabled** the same graph
observes the intermediate values eagerly (proving the mode is what makes the difference,
not an accident of scheduling).
*Test:* `civictech.cell.consistency.CycleEgressGlitchFreedomTest`. *Concord:*
`covers: [KE5-43, KE5-44, KE5-45, KE5-47]`.

## BS-07 — Eager egress does not gate fan-out (regression boundary)
**Given** a weak-tier cycle head with an external subscriber on its broadcast outlet, in
the default eager mode,
**When** the loop laps and the damper absorbs a lap without re-originating,
**Then** the external subscriber still receives every effective emission — throttling gates
re-origination only; and every delivery it receives has `loop == null` (stripped at egress).
*Test:* `civictech.cell.port.CycleEgressTest`. *Concord:* `covers: [KE5-14, KE5-42]`.

## BS-08 — Region capture and reclassification under topology churn (recovery/boundary)
**Given** a seeded topology-churn run that repeatedly connects and unlinks edges around a
captured cycle region,
**When** the run executes,
**Then** every in-region delivery is loop-stamped and every egress delivery is stripped, at
every point in the churn sequence; a headless closure is still rejected as
`CycleWithoutHead`; an undamped headed closure is still rejected as `CycleWithoutDamping`;
unlinking the closing edge dissolves the region so subsequent deliveries carry `loop == null`;
and the existing `34-cycles` corpus stays green.
*Test:* `civictech.cell.host.CycleRegionAdmissionTest` (seeded; keep the discovered failing
seed if one appears). *Concord:* `covers: [KE5-11, KE5-12, KE5-13, KE5-15, KE5-18]`.

## BS-09 — Nested and cross-host cycles (unwanted-behaviour boundary)
**Given** (a) a graph with a captured region and a second closing edge that would nest a
region inside it, and (b) two hosts wired so that the cycle closes only across the host
boundary,
**When** each closure is attempted,
**Then** (a) is `Rejected` at connect with a reason naming nested cycles as unsupported;
(b) is **admitted** (link-time admission cannot see it — the test asserts the honest
limitation, not a detection), and at runtime the hop guard dead-letters it as `CycleError`.
*Test:* `civictech.cell.host.CycleRegionAdmissionTest` +
`civictech.cell.host.CrossHostCycleTest`. *Concord:* `covers: [KE5-16, KE5-17]` — the
cross-host arm belongs in the `dist` profile.

## BS-10 — Incremental re-entry: adjustment, not recomputation
**Given** a settled transitive-closure region,
**When** the input relation grows by one edge, then shrinks by a different edge, each
followed by a drain,
**Then** after each settle the region's output equals the batch fixpoint over the *current*
input; each adjustment's total delta count is bounded well below a from-scratch
recomputation (the control: a from-scratch-per-wave variant blows an explicit delta-count
budget); and a state-resetting variant (a control cell that clears state per lap) fails to
settle or settles to the wrong answer.
*Test:* `civictech.cell.data.CycleReEntryTest`. *Concord:* `covers: [KE5-31, KE5-32, KE5-33, KE5-35]` for the correctness arms; the delta-count budget arm is **not** a corpus
scenario — it is an efficiency property, and the corpus asserts semantics, not cost.

## BS-11 — Concurrent outer waves interleave safely
**Given** a region reachable from two independent sources,
**When** two outer waves enter the region overlapping in time and both drain,
**Then** each settles against its own `outerWave`; `settled` for one never reports the
other's outer wave; and the final region state equals the batch fixpoint over the union of
both inputs.
*Test:* `civictech.cell.data.CycleReEntryTest`. *Concord:* `covers: [KE5-34]`.

## BS-12 — Stratification rejection and its control (unwanted-behaviour)
**Given** a graph whose prospective cycle region contains a `SemiJoinCell` in negated mode
on the cycle path, and a sibling graph where the same cell sits adjacent to but outside the
cycle path,
**When** the closing `connect` is attempted in each,
**Then** the first is `Rejected` with reason `CycleRequiresStratification`; the second is
admitted; and the **control** — the same unstratified graph with the check disabled, on an
adversarial seed — oscillates membership until the hop guard fires, demonstrating the check
prevents a real failure rather than a hypothetical one.
*Test:* `civictech.cell.host.StratificationAdmissionTest`. *Concord:*
`covers: [KE5-37, KE5-38, KE5-39]`. The control arm is **not** a corpus scenario: it
requires disabling a normative admission check, which the corpus has no vocabulary for and
should not acquire.

## BS-13 — Promotion gate migration preserves deferral (regression)
**Given** a `PromotionJudge` constructed with a cycle head,
**When** no delta has been observed, and separately when the region has settled,
**Then** the first yields the existing "cycle promotion deferred, not attempted" rejection
(`settled == null` is never read as vacuously settled), and the second permits the
window/threshold evaluation to proceed — matching the pre-KE5 `lastQuiescent` behaviour
exactly for every case that behaviour already defined.
*Test:* `civictech.cell.evolve.PromotionPolicyTest`. *Concord:* not a corpus scenario —
promotion-gate wiring is a 50/53 evolution concern already covered by its own suite; this
is a regression guard on a KE5 refactor.

## BS-14 — Owned payload accounting on the cycle path (failure/recovery)
**Given** a cycle region carrying an `Owned` payload, with settled egress enabled,
**When** (a) the region settles normally, and (b) the region diverges and dead-letters,
**Then** in (a) the payload is consumed exactly once by absorption at the head and the
egress buffer releases without duplicating it; in (b) the held buffer's payloads are
explicitly discharged at dead-letter time and the failure accounting shows zero silently
dropped exclusives.
*Test:* `civictech.cell.port.CycleOwnershipTest`. *Concord:*
`covers: [KE5-19, KE5-30, KE5-46]`.

## BS-15 — Agora grounded extension: exact strong-tier payoff (the demo-level acceptance)
**Given** the agora argumentation graph with grounded IN/OUT/UNDEC labelling expressed as a
set-valued least fixpoint over `SetDelta`-carrying cells around a **kernel** `CycleHead`
(replacing `EdgeCell`'s app-side head for this view), and a batch grounded-extension
reference implementation,
**When** the existing agora exit-test idiom runs — 100 seeds, including cyclic argument
graphs, each drained under the `SimWorld` step budget,
**Then** the incremental labelling equals the batch grounded extension **exactly** on every
seed (no threshold bound — the strong-tier point, and the observable improvement over
today's bounded cyclic assertion); the weak-tier credence loop's behaviour is unchanged;
and a retraction-blind control diverges.
*Test:* `civictech.agora.GroundedFixpointTest` alongside the existing `AgoraExitTest`
idiom. *Concord:* not a corpus scenario — it is application-level, and the corpus is
implementation-neutral kernel conformance. Its kernel content is already covered by BS-03.
acceptance_criteria: Requirements [KE5-01]..[KE5-50] (design section A-G) are implemented and verified. Load-bearing gates: [KE5-23]+[KE5-24]+[KE5-33] (strong-tier exact fixpoint, BS-03) close the 21-CYCLE-03 gap row in doc/spec/CONCORDANCE.md; [KE5-29]+[KE5-30] and [KE5-26] (non-termination / iteration-budget exhaustion, BS-04+BS-05) hold with no convergence claim for the weak tier; [KE5-43]..[KE5-45] (glitch-freedom across a cycle boundary under settled egress, BS-06) hold; [KE5-38] rejects an unstratified region (BS-12); [KE5-19]+[KE5-46] preserve exclusive-payload accounting (BS-14); [KE5-49]+[KE5-50] satisfied (DISPUTES.md entry for any requirement not honestly checkable; CONCORDANCE.md regenerated, :concord:check green).
notes: Kernel-lane (G-63 single SCC): strictly serial, must not run concurrently with KX/KE1/KFX/KAGG-R/KE3/MEM1/MEM2/KE2/KE4/PLC3/SEC1. Enters the lane at position 7 (milestone plan section 4), after MEM1/MEM2 and before KE2. Plan row: 'Depends on: —' — no hard prerequisite; the position-7 ordering is recorded here rather than as a dependency edge.

title: KE4 — E4: event-time waterline eviction
description:
# KE4 — E4: event-time waterline eviction

Kernel-lane epic realizing **Milestone E4** of `doc/spec/90-roadmap/96-incremental-engines-plan.md`
(§E4, lines 429–537), the chunk named `KE4` in `computenet-milestone-plan.md` §1 (kernel lane),
§3 (Nexmark row) and §4 (kernel-lane order, item 9).

## Ambition / Why

`Windows` shipped as **key derivation** and shipped honest about its cost. The KDoc of
`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/Windows.kt` says it in as many words:

> "Windows never close: late elements are ordinary adds and retractions flow (view
> semantics). **Watermark-driven eviction is deferred with trigger (24).**"

That deferral is the whole of this epic. `doc/spec/20-dataflow-semantics/24-data-cells.md`
§Grouped aggregation states the same deferral normatively — `[24-OP-WINDOW-02]` ("Windows SHALL
NOT close") with the trailing "Deferred with triggers: watermark-driven eviction … trigger: real
window-state memory pressure".

**The trigger has fired.** `computenet-milestone-plan.md` §3 (kernel-enablement matrix, Nexmark
row): *"**KE4** — watermark-driven eviction is the only kernel blocker for the windowed queries,
and it is literally the deferred trigger named in `Windows`' KDoc."* Everything else Nexmark's
windowed queries (Q5, Q7, Q8) need already exists: window assignment
(`Windows.tumbling`/`Windows.sliding`), equi-join (`JoinSetCell`), grouped aggregation
(`GroupByCell` + retraction-aware `Aggregator` min/max/topK). §1's BB-NEX row is explicit that
windowing itself is *not* the gap — **state boundedness is**.

Without KE4, a window-keyed `GroupByCell` is an unbounded memory leak by design: every window key
ever seen keeps a live `Group` and every element keeps its tags in `TagState`. A continuous query
over an unbounded auction stream therefore cannot run to a benchmark's end, let alone in
production.

The design is decided, not open. Feldera's lateness → waterline shape (research
`doc/research/incremental-engines/01-dbsp-feldera.md` §5) fits ComputeNet without coordination:
lateness is a per-inlet declaration; the waterline is a monotone `max(event time) − lateness`
computed **inside the dataflow** by an ordinary cell, riding the existing per-source
`Timestamp(sourceId, counter)` waves. No wall clock (P1 holds), no consensus, no new protocol.

What the research **refutes 0-3** is the comfortable framing that "lateness GC is a pure
optimization that never changes outputs". It is not. E4's decision, taken in
`96-incremental-engines-plan.md` §E4 preamble, is therefore:

- **Eviction is destructive and semantic**: dropped state leaves through the *ordinary retraction
  path*, so a cell's state stays equal to its integrated output. Catch-up, `Stateful` snapshots
  and per-peer recompute keep working with zero new machinery.
- **Late arrivals below the waterline are dropped** at a guarded inlet and re-emitted verbatim on
  a `late` side-channel outlet — a stated, declared exception to `[24-OP-WINDOW-02]`.
- **Equivalence is conditional, and stated as such**: *incremental == batch over the
  late-filtered input*, conditional on the waterline being derivable from a monotone event-time
  attribute. Checked per pipeline, never assumed.

### Naming hazard, stated up front

The kernel **already has a `WatermarkCell`** at
`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/Watermark.kt`. It is a *delivered*-watermark lattice
over `(replica slot, sourceId) → delivered counter` — E3's substrate, spec 40/42, the KE3 chunk.
It is **not** an event-time construct and has nothing to do with this epic beyond both words
sounding alike. E4's construct is deliberately named **waterline** (Feldera's coinage, adopted in
`96` §E4.2 as `WaterlineCell`/`WaterlineDelta`) precisely to keep the two apart. Any
implementation that folds event time into `WatermarkCell`'s lattice is wrong: its key space is
`(replica, source)` in *wave counters*, not event time, and its `Replicable` gossip semantics are
not what a waterline needs.

## What we build

**In-place kernel change**, no new module. `:kernel` only; `:demo:slotfinder` is the adoption site.

New and changed files, following `96` §E4.2–E4.6:

- `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/delta/WaterlineDelta.kt` — **new**.
  `WaterlineDelta(floor: Long)`, `@Serializable @SerialName("WaterlineDelta")`, implementing
  `civictech.cell.MergeablePayload` (`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/MergeablePayload.kt`)
  merging **by max**. The one weight-adjacent delta that is genuinely gossip-safe, because max is
  idempotent, commutative and associative — unlike `CounterDelta`.
- `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/Waterline.kt` — **new**. `WaterlineCell<E>(timeFn,
  lateness)`: inlet `Propagate<SetDelta<E>>`, outlet `Propagate<WaterlineDelta>`; folds per-source
  max event time keyed on the arriving wave's `sourceId` (read off `CurrentContext`, exactly as
  `WatermarkCell.trackDeliveriesOf` reads it), emits **effective-only** monotone floor advances;
  `Stateful` (per-source maxima + last floor); `catchUpOnLinked` emits the current floor.
  Delta-only cell — **no `@Contract`**, mirroring `WatermarkCell`'s precedent.
- `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/Windows.kt` — **changed**. Add the named
  `Serializable` lateness declaration beside the assigners (`Lateness(timeFn, lateness)` shape per
  §E4.1(1)), and **retract the deferral sentence from the KDoc** — this epic is the only work
  permitted to remove that sentence.
- `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/delta/TagState.kt` — **changed**. New
  `fun evictBelow(predicate: (E) -> Boolean): SetDelta<E>` destructively dropping live tags of
  matching elements and returning the dels-delta. It must interact correctly with the existing
  `tombstones`/`deadSources` fields and `retainTombstones` mode.
- `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/op/GroupByCell.kt` — **changed**. Optional
  `waterline` inlet (`Propagate<WaterlineDelta>`) plus `keyTime: (K) -> Long` (window end); on
  floor advance, evict every element whose window key lies **entirely** below the floor through
  the ordinary retraction fold, so `Group.count` decrements, groups die and `MapDelta` removals
  emit under the waterline delta's wave. Main-inlet guard drops sub-floor adds and forwards them
  verbatim on a new `late` outlet.
- An internal `Evictable` seam (§E4.5) shared with
  `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/op/JoinSetCell.kt`,
  `.../op/SemiJoinCell.kt`, `.../op/IntersectSetCell.kt`, covering both per-side row indexes and
  minted pairs (`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/delta/MintedTags.kt`).
- `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/wire/WireCodec.kt` — **changed**, additively: register
  `WaterlineDelta` as a polymorphic subclass, exactly as `WatermarkDelta` is registered.
- Adoption: `demo/slotfinder/src/main/kotlin/civictech/demo/slotfinder/SlotFinderApp.kt`'s `byDay`
  `GroupByApi<Slot, String, Long>` fold — its natural event-time window — as the first real
  consumer (§E4.6).

Entry points for a graph author: `Windows.tumbling`/`Windows.sliding` unchanged for assignment;
a `WaterlineCell` spawned beside the source and linked into the group-by's `waterline` inlet; the
`late` outlet linked wherever the application wants dropped elements (or left unlinked).

## How, using ComputeNet

The design is a *composition of substrate that already exists*, which is why it is a milestone and
not a research item:

- **Per-source event-time maxima** ride the existing wave identity. `Timestamp(sourceId, counter)`
  is minted per outlet (`[22-SRC-01]`, `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/port/FanOutlet.kt`),
  and `CurrentContext.get()?.timestamp` already exposes it inside a fold — the pattern
  `WatermarkCell.trackDeliveriesOf` uses.
- **Monotone floor by min-over-sources** is an ordinary data cell, not a coordinator. It is "one
  more use of the monotone-clock shape — never a wave, never part of any completeness set" (§E4.1
  spec clause on 20/22).
- **Destructive eviction as retraction** reuses `TagState`'s existing dels path and `GroupByCell`'s
  existing membership-flip fold, so `[24-OP-GROUPBY-02]` (group death on last retraction) and
  `[24-OP-GROUPBY-03]` (one `MapDelta` per input delta under that delta's wave id) hold unchanged —
  the evicting delta is just another input delta, carrying the waterline delta's wave.
- **Source churn** hooks the two events that already exist: `EdgeClose`
  (`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/protocol/Protocols.kt`, `EdgeEvent`) and
  `ReBaselineNotice` (`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/MessageContext.kt:85`, folded by
  `TagState.applyReBaseline`). A RESTART'd producer mints a fresh per-epoch `sourceId`
  (`[21-REBASE-01]`); its stale pre-restart maximum must be retired or it gates the floor forever.
- **Late-join catch-up** uses `catchUpOnLinked`, the same `[21-CATCHUP-02]` seam every data cell
  uses.
- **Bounded reads** — if `WaterlineCell` implements `BoundedStateful`, follow `WatermarkCell`'s
  `readBounded` precedent (frozen `KeyWalk` order, `frontier = null` where the key space is not a
  tag frontier).

## Functional requirements (EARS)

Ids are epic-scoped `[KE4-nn]`, namespaced so they never collide with `doc/spec/`'s
`[NN-SLUG-nn]`. Each cites the normative spec id it makes true, or the E4 clause that creates it.

### Ubiquitous

- `[KE4-01]` A lateness declaration SHALL be a per-inlet value binding an event-time extractor
  `timeFn: (E) -> Long` to a non-negative `lateness: Long`. (Makes true: `96` §E4.1(1).)
- `[KE4-02]` A lateness declaration SHALL be a named `Serializable` class, not a lambda or
  anonymous object, so it survives graph-spec capture. (Makes true: `96` §E4.1(1); mirrors
  `Windows.Tumbling`/`Windows.Sliding` under `[24-OP-WINDOW-01]`.)
- `[KE4-03]` The waterline floor SHALL be defined as the minimum over contributing sources of
  (maximum observed event time for that source − that inlet's declared lateness). (Makes true:
  `96` §E4.1(2).)
- `[KE4-04]` The waterline SHALL be computed by an ordinary data cell inside the dataflow, using
  no wall clock and no cross-host coordination. (Makes true: `96` §E4.1(2); preserves P1 as cited
  by `[24-OP-WINDOW-01]`.)
- `[KE4-05]` The waterline floor SHALL be monotone non-decreasing on every prefix of every
  execution. (Makes true: `96` §E4.1(2), §E4.2 invariant.)
- `[KE4-06]` `WaterlineDelta` SHALL merge by maximum and SHALL therefore be idempotent,
  commutative and associative under `MergeablePayload.mergeWith`. (Makes true: `96` §E4.2.)
- `[KE4-07]` A source's contribution to the waterline SHALL be keyed by the arriving wave's
  `sourceId`, never by cell ref, host or link. (Makes true: `[22-SRC-01]`.)
- `[KE4-08]` The waterline floor SHALL NOT be a wave and SHALL NOT participate in any
  completeness set or glitch-free frontier. (Makes true: `96` §E4.1 spec clause on 20/22;
  preserves `[22-GF-01]`/`[22-GF-02]`.)
- `[KE4-09]` Evicted state SHALL leave through the ordinary retraction path, such that after
  eviction a cell's state remains equal to its integrated output. (Makes true: `96` §E4.1(3).)
- `[KE4-10]` For a pipeline whose waterline is derivable from a monotone event-time attribute,
  the post-quiescence state of every evicting cell SHALL equal a batch recompute over the
  late-filtered input. (Makes true: `96` §E4 preamble, the conditional-equivalence statement;
  research `01` §5's refuted-variant correction.)
- `[KE4-11]` Steady-state memory held by an evicting cell for window-keyed state SHALL be bounded
  by the lateness horizon rather than by stream length. (Makes true: `96` §E4 preamble, gap 6 in
  `91-gap-analysis.md` G-42.)
- `[KE4-12]` The deferral sentence "Watermark-driven eviction is deferred with trigger (24)" SHALL
  be removed from `Windows`' KDoc and the corresponding deferral bullet replaced in
  `doc/spec/20-dataflow-semantics/24-data-cells.md` §Grouped aggregation. (Makes true: `96` §E4.1
  spec clause; discharges the trigger named in `[24-OP-WINDOW-02]`'s trailing paragraph.)
- `[KE4-13]` The `late` outlet SHALL carry dropped elements **verbatim**, preserving their original
  tags, so a downstream consumer can reconstruct exactly what was excluded. (Makes true: `96`
  §E4.3.)

### Event-driven

- `[KE4-14]` WHEN a `SetDelta<E>` arrives at a `WaterlineCell` inlet, the cell SHALL update the
  arriving wave's source's maximum observed `timeFn(e)` over the delta's adds. (Makes true: `96`
  §E4.2.)
- `[KE4-15]` WHEN a source's maximum advances such that the computed floor strictly increases, the
  `WaterlineCell` SHALL emit exactly one `WaterlineDelta` carrying the new floor. (Makes true: `96`
  §E4.2; effective-only emission per `[21-PROP-01]`.)
- `[KE4-16]` WHEN a source's maximum advances without strictly increasing the computed floor, the

- `[KE4-19]` WHEN an add whose `timeFn(e)` is strictly below the current floor arrives at a guarded

- `[KE4-20]` WHEN a del whose element lies below the current floor arrives at a guarded inlet, the

- `[KE4-21]` WHEN a `WaterlineDelta` arrives that does not raise the local floor, the receiving

- `[KE4-23]` WHEN a `ReBaselineNotice` supersedes a source, the `WaterlineCell` SHALL retire the

### State-driven

- `[KE4-26]` WHILE no source has yet contributed an event time, the floor SHALL be the identity
  that admits all elements (no eviction, no late-drop). (Makes true: `96` §E4.2 monotonicity.)
- `[KE4-27]` WHILE at least one contributing source is open but idle, the floor SHALL NOT advance
  past that source's promise. (Makes true: `96` §E4.4; this is the accepted frozen-but-correct
  residual, cross-referenced to research plan R15.)
- `[KE4-28]` WHILE a cell holds `Replicable` state, destructive eviction of that state SHALL be
  refused until E3.7 (stability-scoped tag/tombstone reclamation) exists. (Makes true: `96` §E4
  preamble restriction and §E4.1(5).)
- `[KE4-29]` WHILE a pipeline declares no lateness on any inlet, behaviour SHALL be exactly
  today's: windows never close, late elements are ordinary adds, retractions flow. (Makes true:
  `[24-OP-WINDOW-02]` for every non-opted-in graph.)

### Unwanted behaviour

- `[KE4-30]` **The safety condition.** IF evicting a piece of state would make a subsequently
  admissible retraction unrepresentable — i.e. the state is still reachable by a del that the
  guard would not itself drop — THEN the cell SHALL NOT evict it. Eviction that drops state still
  needed for a correct retraction is silent corruption, not an optimization. (Makes true: `96` §E4
  preamble "eviction is **not** a pure optimization"; research `01` §5's 0-3 refutation.)
- `[KE4-31]` IF a cell evicts state without emitting the corresponding retractions, THEN a
  late-linking subscriber's catch-up fold diverges from an already-linked subscriber's fold — this
  SHALL NOT occur. (Makes true: `96` §E4.3 control; `[21-PROP-01]`'s equal-folds-at-quiescence
  clause.)
- `[KE4-32]` IF a windowed join evicts minted pairs without emitting their exit tags, THEN
  tombstone-folding consumers are left permanently holding dead pairs — this SHALL NOT occur.
  (Makes true: `96` §E4.5 control, the M11.2 tag-hygiene control inverted.)
- `[KE4-33]` IF the floor is computed as a max over sources rather than a min, THEN a fast source
  evicts a slow source's admissible data — this SHALL NOT occur. (Makes true: `96` §E4.2's named
  control variant.)
- `[KE4-34]` IF a `WaterlineDelta` is redelivered or delivered out of order, THEN the receiving
  cell's state SHALL be identical to the in-order single-delivery state. (Makes true: `96` §E4.2
  duplicate-delivery invariant.)
- `[KE4-35]` IF an evicted element carries an `Owned` or `Leased` payload, THEN eviction SHALL NOT
  silently drop it — the exclusive must be consumed, released or discharged on an explicit path.
  (Makes true: `doc/spec/20-dataflow-semantics/23-ownership.md`'s no-silent-drop rule; this epic
  adds a *new* state-destroying path and must not become the first one that leaks.)
- `[KE4-36]` IF a stale pre-restart `sourceId`'s maximum is retained after re-baseline, THEN the
  floor is gated forever by a source that will never advance again — this SHALL NOT occur. (Makes
  true: `96` §E4.4; `[21-REBASE-01]`.)
- `[KE4-37]` IF event time is derived from anything other than an explicit element attribute — a
  wall clock, a wave counter, an arrival tick — THEN window contents become placement-dependent
  and batch equivalence breaks; this SHALL NOT occur. (Makes true: `[24-OP-WINDOW-01]`; 24's
  explicit rejection of wave/tick-based windows.)

### Optional feature

- `[KE4-38]` WHERE a `GroupByCell` is constructed with a `waterline` inlet and a `keyTime: (K) ->
  Long`, it SHALL participate in eviction; WHERE it is not, it SHALL behave exactly as today.
  (Makes true: `96` §E4.3; additive-by-construction.)
- `[KE4-39]` WHERE the `late` outlet is left unlinked, dropped elements SHALL still be excluded
  from the fold and their exclusion SHALL be observable through the cell's own accounting. (Makes
  true: `96` §E4.3 — the drop must not be invisible merely because nobody subscribed.)
- `[KE4-40]` WHERE a member of the join family (`JoinSetCell`, `SemiJoinCell`, `IntersectSetCell`)
  declares lateness, it SHALL evict through the shared `Evictable` seam under the same
  destructive-with-retraction rule as `GroupByCell`. (Makes true: `96` §E4.5.)
- `[KE4-41]` WHERE a management operator calls `retire(sourceId)` on a `WaterlineCell`, that
  source SHALL stop gating the floor. (Makes true: `96` §E4.4's explicit manual escape hatch for
  the idle-source residual.)

### Complex

- `[KE4-42]` WHEN a floor advance and a main-inlet delta touch the same group, WHILE the cell is
  wrapped glitch-free, the cell SHALL NOT expose a state mixing pre-eviction and post-eviction
  membership within one wave. (Makes true: `[22-GF-01]`, `[22-GF-02]`.)
- `[KE4-43]` WHEN an element arrives whose event time is below the floor, WHILE that element is
  already live in the cell's state (a re-add of retained state), the cell SHALL drop the add per
  `[KE4-19]` and SHALL NOT retract the existing live element as a side effect. (Makes true: `96`
  §E4.3's guard semantics; membership flips drive emission, `[24-OP-GROUPBY-02]`.)
- `[KE4-44]` WHEN a source is retired, WHILE that source was the unique minimum, the floor SHALL
  resume advancing and SHALL still never exceed any remaining live source's promise. (Makes true:
  `96` §E4.4.)
- `[KE4-45]` WHEN a cell is checkpointed after eviction, WHILE recovery later restores it, the
  restored state SHALL equal the pre-crash post-eviction state and SHALL NOT re-admit evicted
  elements. (Makes true: `96` §E4.1(3)'s "state = integrated output keeps `Stateful` snapshots
  correct"; `[22-REC-01]`.)

### Honesty note on verifiability

`[KE4-11]` ("bounded by the lateness horizon") is the requirement most easily softened into
something vacuous. It is stated as a *steady-state* bound over a seeded generative run with a
declared disorder envelope, measured as element/tag/group counts held by the cell — not as JVM
heap, which is not honestly attributable. If the implementer finds the count-based formulation
cannot be checked against a real pipeline shape, the correct response is a
`concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` entry naming what cannot be checked — **not** a weaker assertion such
as "memory does not grow monotonically".

`[KE4-27]` is a requirement about a *known residual*, not a defect: it asserts the frozen-but-
correct behaviour is exactly what ships, so a future fix has a baseline to change. It is
cross-linked to research plan R15 (`doc/spec/90-roadmap/95-research-plan.md`).

## Behaviour specifications

Given/When/Then, specific enough to become named tests. The two load-bearing families —
**late arrival after eviction** and **eviction interacting with retraction** — are first.

### B1 — Late arrival after eviction is dropped, not resurrected (`[KE4-19]`, `[KE4-13]`, `[KE4-30]`)
**Given** a tumbling-window `GroupByCell` with lateness L, whose window `[t, t+w)` has been evicted
because the floor advanced past `t+w`;
**When** an element with event time inside `[t, t+w)` arrives on the main inlet;
**Then** the element is excluded from the fold, no group for that window is re-created, no
`MapDelta` put is emitted for that key, and the element is forwarded verbatim — original tags
intact — on the `late` outlet.
*Concord*: yes — `covers: [24-OP-WINDOW-02]` (as the declared exception) in
`concord/corpus/24-data-cells/`, once E4.1's spec text lands and mints the eviction requirement
ids. Implementation-neutral: it is a pure input/output statement about a windowed pipeline.

### B2 — Late arrival *before* eviction is an ordinary add (`[KE4-29]`, `[KE4-19]`)
**Given** the same pipeline, and a window whose end is **above** the current floor;
**When** an out-of-order element for that window arrives;
**Then** it is an ordinary add: the group updates, retractions flow normally, and nothing appears
on the `late` outlet. The boundary is exactly the floor, not "out of order".
*Concord*: yes, same file — this is the half of `[24-OP-WINDOW-02]` that survives E4 and must be
pinned so the exception cannot be over-applied.

### B3 — Eviction emits retractions; the two-subscriber divergence control (`[KE4-09]`, `[KE4-31]`)
**Given** a windowed group-by with subscriber A linked from the start;
**When** the floor advances and evicts several windows, **and then** subscriber B links and takes
`catchUpOnLinked`;
**Then** A's fold and B's catch-up fold are equal.
**Control (must be red-capable)**: an eviction path that drops state *without* emitting the dels
makes A and B diverge; the test must fail if the control is used.
*Concord*: yes — `covers: [21-PROP-01]` (equal folds at quiescence) in
`concord/corpus/21-propagation/`, plus the E4 eviction id.

### B4 — Eviction under an in-flight retraction (`[KE4-20]`, `[KE4-43]`, `[KE4-30]`)
**Given** an element E live in an about-to-be-evicted window, and a del for E already in flight;
**When** the floor advances and evicts the window before the del is folded, and the del then
arrives;
**Then** the del is a no-op — no double retraction, no negative group count, no
`retract for untracked group` failure (the `checkNotNull` in `GroupByCell.onInlet` is the exact
crash this scenario exists to prevent), and the group count never goes below zero.
*Concord*: yes — `covers: [24-OP-GROUPBY-02]`. This is the scenario most likely to catch a naive
implementation.

### B5 — Eviction must not destroy state a live retraction still needs (`[KE4-30]`)
**Given** a windowed join whose left side holds a row for window W and whose right side has not yet
seen its match, with the floor rising to the boundary of W;
**When** eviction is considered for the left row;
**Then** eviction proceeds only if a subsequent del for that row would itself be dropped by the
guard; otherwise the row is retained. The invariant asserted is: **no admissible del can ever
reference evicted state.**
*Concord*: yes, as a safety property over a join pipeline. If the property proves unstatable
implementation-neutrally, file it in `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` rather than weakening it.

### B6 — Batch equivalence over the late-filtered input (`[KE4-10]`)
**Given** a seeded generative run: multiple writers → union → tumbling group-by, event times
shuffled within a bounded disorder envelope, lateness L declared;
**When** the run reaches quiescence;
**Then** the cell's state equals a naive batch recompute over the input **with sub-floor elements
filtered out**, on every seed. The `late` outlet's contents equal exactly the set the batch filter
removed.
*Concord*: yes, as a property scenario. This is also the natural bridge to ORA1's batch-oracle
differential tester — ORA2's row in the plan explicitly names "KE4-era work".

### B7 — Memory bounded by the lateness horizon (`[KE4-11]`)
**Given** a long seeded run with a bounded disorder envelope;
**When** the stream length grows by an order of magnitude;
**Then** the element/tag/group counts held by the evicting cell stay within the lateness horizon's
bound and do not grow with stream length.
*Concord*: **no.** A resource-bound assertion measured in counts is arguably statable, but the
threshold is pipeline-shape dependent and the scenario is a soak, not a semantics check. It belongs
in `:kernel` tests (and feeds `doc/spec/50-*/52` invariants per §E4.6), not in the
implementation-neutral corpus.

### B8 — Floor monotonicity and the max-vs-min control (`[KE4-05]`, `[KE4-33]`)
**Given** interleaved multi-source streams with different progress rates;
**When** the run is replayed under seeded interleavings;
**Then** the floor is monotone non-decreasing on every prefix and never exceeds the minimum source
promise.
**Control**: a `max`-over-sources variant admits a violating seed — the control must be red-capable.
*Concord*: yes — the monotone-floor invariant is implementation-neutral.

### B9 — Duplicate and reordered `WaterlineDelta` (`[KE4-34]`, `[KE4-21]`)
**Given** a converged pipeline;
**When** `WaterlineDelta`s are duplicated, reordered and replayed (the `CHA1` adversarial-DST rig
shape: reorder + duplicate);
**Then** final state is identical to single in-order delivery, and no eviction fires twice.
*Concord*: yes — idempotent merge is a wire-relevant semantic property.

### B10 — Source retirement on `EdgeClose` (`[KE4-22]`, `[KE4-44]`)
**Given** three contributing sources, the slowest of which is then unlinked;
**When** its edge fires `EdgeClose`;
**Then** the floor resumes advancing, bounded by the slowest *remaining* source; and it never
overtakes a live source's promise.
*Concord*: yes — links to `concord/corpus/13-links/`'s edge-event vocabulary.

### B11 — Source retirement on re-baseline after RESTART (`[KE4-23]`, `[KE4-36]`)
**Given** a producer that has contributed a high event-time maximum and then RESTARTs, minting a
fresh per-epoch `sourceId` and emitting `ReBaselineNotice(supersedes, supersede = true)`;
**When** the notice is folded;
**Then** the superseded `sourceId`'s maximum stops gating the floor, the fresh epoch contributes
from scratch, and the floor does not regress.
*Concord*: yes — `covers: [21-REBASE-01]`, extending
`concord/corpus/21-propagation/21-REBASE-01.yaml`'s shape to the waterline consumer.

### B12 — Idle-but-open source freezes the floor, correctly (`[KE4-27]`, `[KE4-41]`)
**Given** a source that is linked but has stopped emitting;
**When** other sources advance far past it;
**Then** the floor stops at the idle source's promise, no eviction occurs, and no data is lost;
**And when** `retire(sourceId)` is invoked, the floor resumes.
*Concord*: the frozen-floor half, yes; the `retire` op is a management verb whose corpus home
depends on E4.1's spec text — file it in `:kernel` tests if 24 does not make `retire` normative.

### B13 — Crash and recovery after eviction (`[KE4-45]`)
**Given** a windowed pipeline that has evicted several windows and checkpointed;
**When** the host crashes and the cell is restored from the journal;
**Then** the restored state equals the pre-crash post-eviction state, evicted elements are not
re-admitted, and the floor is at or above its pre-crash value.
*Concord*: yes — `covers: [22-REC-01]`, in `concord/corpus/15-durability/` or `22-consistency/`
per the corpus's existing recovery placement.

### B14 — Windowed join evicts both indexes and minted pairs (`[KE4-25]`, `[KE4-32]`, `[KE4-40]`)
**Given** a windowed equi-join over two late-declaring inputs;
**When** the floor advances past a window;
**Then** both per-side row indexes and the corresponding minted pairs are evicted, exit tags are
emitted, the minted-tag count stays bounded, and the result equals a batch join over the
late-filtered inputs.
**Control**: evicting minted pairs without exit-tag emission leaves tombstone-folding consumers
dead — red-capable.
*Concord*: yes, in `concord/corpus/24-data-cells/`.

### B15 — Exclusive payloads are not silently dropped by eviction (`[KE4-35]`)
**Given** a windowed fold over elements carrying `Owned` payloads;
**When** eviction destroys that state;
**Then** every exclusive is consumed, released or discharged on an explicit path, and the
ownership accounting balances — no failure, suppression, shadow, park or dead-letter path swallows
one.
*Concord*: yes — `covers:` the relevant `[23-*]` no-silent-drop id in
`concord/corpus/23-ownership/`. If the honest answer is that eviction of exclusives should be
*refused* rather than discharged, that is a spec decision for E4.1 and must be recorded there, not
decided in a test.

### B16 — Glitch-free wrap around an evicting cell (`[KE4-42]`)
**Given** a glitch-free-wrapped evicting group-by;
**When** a main-inlet delta and a floor advance touch the same group in one wave;
**Then** no observer sees membership mixing pre-eviction and post-eviction state within that wave.
*Concord*: yes — `covers: [22-GF-01]`/`[22-GF-02]`.

### B17 — Replicable eviction is refused before E3.7 (`[KE4-28]`)
**Given** a cell holding `Replicable` state;
**When** an eviction is attempted on it;
**Then** the attempt is refused with a clear diagnostic naming the E3.7 dependency — a replica
evicting locally while a peer still gossips below the floor would re-admit ghosts.
*Concord*: no — this is a scaffolding restriction with a scheduled expiry, not a durable semantic.
It belongs in `:kernel` tests and must be **deleted** when E3.7 lands, not carried into the corpus
where it would later have to be retracted.

## Scope boundaries

Citing the plan's dependency edges:

- **Depends on KE3** (`computenet-milestone-plan.md` §1 kernel-lane row, §2 DAG edge
  `KE3 → KE4`). The single coupling named in `96` §E4's dependency note is the `Replicable`-eviction
  restriction, lifted by **E3.7**. E4.1–E4.6 need nothing from E1 or E2.
- **Unblocks BB-NEX windowed queries** (§2 edge `KE4 → BB-NEX`; §3 Nexmark row: KE4 is *the only*
  kernel blocker for them) **and streaming state bounds** generally (§1).
- **Kernel-lane serialization (G-63).** This is kernel-lane work: it must serialize through the
  single kernel SCC and enter the lane at its §4 position (item 9 — immediately after KE3 if BB-NEX
  is prioritized, otherwise after KE2). It does not run concurrently with another kernel-lane
  chunk. It touches `GroupByCell`, `TagState` and the join family — files KE1 and KAGG-R also own —
  which is precisely why the SCC is serial.
- **Not in scope**: reader-frontier compaction of consumer views (`96` §E4 dependency note is
  explicit — `View`/`ObserveCell` folds hold no history to compact); replicated-tag GC (that is
  E3.7 / KE3); session windows (a separate deferral in 24 with its own trigger: first
  proximity-session consumer); wave/tick-based windows (**rejected** in 24, not deferred);
  epoch-column hygiene (research, `95` R14); the idle-source liveness fix (research, `95` R15 — E4
  ships frozen-but-correct).
- **No benchmark work.** The Nexmark harness, generator and query graphs live in BB-NEX and `:bench`
  (BEN1). KE4 delivers kernel capability; it does not produce numbers.
- **Marker hygiene.** Only the gap/consistency markers this epic actually closes may be removed —
  G-42's event-time-eviction share, not its epoch-hygiene or frontier-GC shares.
