title: AGO4 — Strong-tier fixpoint semantics replacing app-side heads
description:
# AGO4 — Strong-tier fixpoint semantics replacing app-side heads

Milestone-plan chunk **AGO4** (`computenet-milestone-plan.md` §1 product lanes: *"Strong-tier
fixpoint semantics replacing app-side heads … closes agora's G-19 residual"*; §2 DAG:
`KE5 --> AGO4`; §5 rank 20, second wave). Depends on: **KE5** (E5 — cycles, `LoopContext`,
iteration-cut fixpoints, stratification), being filed separately and listed here as an **unwired
dependency**. AGO4 has no AGO1 dependency: it does not touch the extraction pipeline.

**Sizing note (filed as `feature`, not `epic`).** AGO4 is one coherent mechanism — *replace an
application's approximation of a kernel model with the kernel model, and add the one view where an
exact fixpoint is claimable*. It is already scoped as a single ticket in the E-plan:
`doc/spec/90-roadmap/96-incremental-engines-plan.md` **§E5.7 — "Agora grounded-extension fixpoint
(gap-5 payoff; strong-tier adopter) — P2 · Medium · `demo` (`:demo:agora`)"**, whose `Depends` are
E5.1–E5.5 and whose implement clause is a demo adoption, not a subsystem. Inflating it to an epic
would double-count E5's own decomposition. Its natural parent is the KE5 epic, which does not exist
yet — hence unparented rather than mis-parented under AGO1 (`computenet-2aw`), which it does not
extend.

---

## 1. Ambition / Why

### 1.1 What agora does today, in code

`:demo:agora` is the kernel cycle model's first and only consumer, and it consumes it by
**re-implementing it in application code**. `doc/spec/20-dataflow-semantics/21-propagation.md`
§Cycles says so explicitly:

> The first weak-tier consumer is the `:agora` argumentation app (M17): it **approximates the head
> model in application code** — its topology-owning service designates each cycle-closing edge a
> head and puts the `quiescence` threshold on that edge's inbound feedback inlet … and its
> step-budgeted 100-seed exit test is the empirical probe for weak-tier quiescence (G-19 residual).

The approximation is five concrete pieces of code, and AGO4's job is to delete or subsume each:

| # | Real code today | What replaces it |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `AgoraService.reaches(from, to)` — an app-side DFS over the service's own `nodes` index (`demo/agora/src/main/kotlin/civictech/agora/AgoraService.kt:209-220`) | kernel cycle-region capture at admission (E5.3 extends `ManagedHost.wouldCloseCycle` from a boolean DFS to SCC capture) |
| 2 | `AgoraService.createEdge`'s `val head = reaches(from = target, to = source)` and `EdgeCell(..., quiescence = if (head) quiescence else 0.0)` (`AgoraService.kt:134-135`) — the app *designating* heads | kernel `CycleHead` / `FeedbackInlet` admission; `[21-CYCLE-01]`'s `CycleWithoutHead` / `CycleRequiresMagnitude` rejections |
| 3 | `EdgeCell`'s absorb gate — `if (quiescence > 0 && abs(value.credence - sourceCredence) < quiescence) return@onEach` (`demo/agora/src/main/kotlin/civictech/agora/cell/EdgeCell.kt:52-58`) plus the `quiescence` constructor parameter and its KDoc "the app-side form of the decided I-5/I-6 model" | the kernel feedback inlet's own damper, gating **re-origination** rather than an app-level inlet early-return |
| 4 | `AgoraService`'s `quiescence: Double = 1e-3` constructor default (`AgoraService.kt:32`), `NodeInfo.head` (`AgoraService.kt:51`), `AgoraApp.NodeDto.head`, and the `⟳` head marker in `AgoraApp`'s inline page and `demo/agora/ui`'s `NodeRec.head` | kernel-derived head/region membership, surfaced rather than app-computed |
| 5 | `CycleQuiescenceTest`'s `headless probe` (`demo/agora/src/test/kotlin/civictech/agora/CycleQuiescenceTest.kt:99-125`), whose own comment says *"the ONLY reason it terminates at all is that the base clamp makes every single loop contractive; the decided kernel hop guard (spec 21 §Cycles, unbuilt) is the backstop this app-level model still lacks"* | the kernel hop guard: a headless or cross-host loop dead-letters as a `CycleError` instead of running to floating-point resolution |

And one number that is the *price* of the approximation:
`AgoraExitTest`'s cyclic tolerance, `val tolerance = if (cyclic) 25 * q else 1e-9`
(`demo/agora/src/test/kotlin/civictech/agora/AgoraExitTest.kt:91`). On cyclic seeds the app cannot
claim equality with the batch fixpoint — only "within 25 threshold-widths of it". That is the
honesty tax G-19's residual charges, written into the lane's own exit gate.

### 1.2 What KE5 makes possible, and what it honestly does not

E5's decided package (96 §E5, adopting Naiad's ingress/feedback/egress triple and DBSP's cycle
rule) gives: `LoopContext(outerWave, iteration)` on `MessageContext` (E5.2), cycle-region capture
and ingress/egress classification at admission (E5.3), **iteration-cut fixpoint detection at the
head** (E5.4 — "a lap delivering no effective delta to any of the region's feedback inlets is the
fixpoint cut"), incremental re-entry (E5.5), and stratification admission (E5.6).

Crucially, E5.4 distinguishes the tiers exactly as `[21-CYCLE-03]` does:

- **Strong tier** — idempotent-merge deltas (tag-set union, pointwise max). Termination is
  structural and threshold-free; the fixpoint cut is *exact*.
- **Weak tier** — `Magnitude`-only numeric deltas. The `quiescence` damper feeds the same probe, but
  the guarantee is bounded-lap termination, **not convergence**. Weak-tier convergence remains
  research (`doc/spec/90-roadmap/95-research-plan.md` §R2).

Agora's DF-QuAD credence loop is **weak tier**: `CredenceUpdate`/`InfluenceDelta` carry
`Magnitude`-style sizes, and `DfQuad`'s only convergence argument is the `BASE_FLOOR` clamp keeping
single-cycle loop gain below 1 (`demo/agora/src/main/kotlin/civictech/agora/semantics/Semantics.kt:12-17`).

So the plan's line *"closes agora's G-19 residual"* is true in a precise and limited sense, and
AGO4 must say which:

- **Closed by AGO4**: the *app-side approximation* residual. The five pieces above stop being an
  application's hand-rolled cycle engine and become kernel machinery with kernel guarantees, and
  agora gains a view — the grounded extension — where a fixpoint is *exactly* detected rather than
  empirically probed.
- **Not closed by AGO4, and no requirement here may claim it**: weak-tier fixpoint *convergence*
  for the numeric credence loop. That is G-19's stated residual and 95 §R2's research question.
  E5.7 says it plainly: *"the weak-tier credence loop stays as-is, R2-gated"*.

### 1.3 The payoff: a view where a fixpoint is real

E5.7's implement clause names the adopter: **grounded labelling (IN/OUT/UNDEC) as a set-valued
least fixpoint** over the agora argument graph — `SetDelta`-carrying cells (idempotent-merge →
strong tier) around a kernel `CycleHead`, exact and threshold-free termination via E5.4's
iteration cut.

This is worth having on its own product merits, not just as a kernel demo. Gradual semantics
(DF-QuAD credence) answers *how strongly is this believed*; grounded extension answers *what
survives the argument* — which arguments are accepted, defeated, or undecided under Dung-style
semantics. A live argument map that shows both is strictly more informative than one showing a
number, and the second view is the one with an exact answer.

---

## 2. What we build

### 2.1 Module shape (decided): inside `demo/agora`, no new module

AGO4 lands in `:demo:agora`: a new package `civictech.agora.grounded` for the labelling cells and
view, plus edits to `AgoraService`, `EdgeCell`, `AgoraApp` and the cycle tests.

**Justification.** Unlike AGO2/AGO3 — which extend the *extraction* side and were deliberately
placed in `:demo:dialogue` to keep `demo/agora`'s exit gate free of transcript and LLM concerns —
AGO4 changes the argumentation engine itself: how its cycles are admitted, headed, damped and
detected. That is `demo/agora`'s own subject matter, and E5.7 assigns it to `:demo:agora` by name.
A separate module could not replace `AgoraService.reaches` or `EdgeCell.quiescence` without
exporting them, which would be strictly worse.

**AGO4 therefore *does* change `demo/agora`, deliberately and visibly** — the inverse of AGO2's and
AGO3's scope guards. What it must not change is the *meaning* of the existing gate: `AgoraExitTest`
must keep its teeth (`[AGO4-MIG-04]`).

### 2.2 The replacement, piece by piece

```
BEFORE (app-side)                          AFTER (kernel-backed)
─────────────────────────────────          ────────────────────────────────────────
AgoraService.reaches() DFS            →    kernel region capture at connect (E5.3)
createEdge: head = reaches(...)       →    FeedbackInlet-closed admission; [21-CYCLE-01]
EdgeCell(quiescence = if head ...)    →    kernel CycleHead + feedback inlet damper
EdgeCell.sourceInlet absorb gate      →    re-origination gate at the head, not an inlet return
NodeInfo.head / NodeDto.head (app)    →    head/region membership read from the host topology
"terminates because the clamp"        →    hop guard dead-letters CycleError as the backstop
AgoraExitTest cyclic tol = 25*q       →    unchanged for credence (weak tier, R2);
                                            EXACT equality for the new grounded view
(no such view)                        →    grounded extension: SetDelta least fixpoint, strong tier
```

Two views, two tiers, honestly separated:

| view | delta | tier | guarantee |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-QuAD credence (existing) | numeric, `Magnitude` | weak | bounded-lap termination; convergence R2-open |
| grounded labelling (new) | `SetDelta` (idempotent merge) | strong | exact, threshold-free fixpoint via E5.4's iteration cut |

### 2.3 The grounded view

Grounded labelling as a set-valued least fixpoint over the existing claim/edge topology:

- Sets of accepted (`IN`) and defeated (`OUT`) node refs circulate as `SetDelta`s around a kernel
  `CycleHead`; `UNDEC` is the complement at fixpoint. Merge is tag-set union — idempotent, hence
  strong tier by construction (`[21-CYCLE-03]`).
- The characteristic-function iteration is exactly the semi-naive delta circulation E5 makes free:
  DBSP's cycle rule means the incremental loop *is* the loop of the incremental body, and E5.4's
  cut ("a full iteration produces only empty effective deltas") is detected by the effective-only
  emission rule the operators already enforce.
- Edge-on-edge attacks are already first-class in agora (`EdgeCell` is a `ClaimCell`), so the
  labelling must treat edges as attackable arguments too — this is the one place where agora's
  model is richer than textbook Dung and where the implementer must state the chosen convention.
- The batch reference is a plain iterative grounded-extension solver, sibling to
  `BatchReference.solve` in `demo/agora/src/test/kotlin/civictech/agora/` — and the incremental
  result must match it **exactly**, not within a tolerance.

### 2.4 How, using ComputeNet (concrete seams)

| Concern | Type / file |
|---|---|
| cycle admission, region capture | KE5/E5.3 — `ManagedHost.wouldCloseCycle` → SCC capture; `civictech.cell.link` admission errors (`CycleWithoutHead`, `CycleRequiresMagnitude`, `CycleRejectsLeased`) |
| head + feedback inlet | KE5 `CycleHead` / `FeedbackInlet` (the built half named in 21 §Cycles) |
| iteration identity | KE5/E5.2 `LoopContext(outerWave, iteration)` on `MessageContext` — additive, never a wave join key |
| fixpoint detection | KE5/E5.4 `settled: LoopContext?` at the feedback inlet |
| settled egress (optional) | KE5/E5.3 hold-until-settled buffer keyed by `outerWave` |
| stratification | KE5/E5.6 `CycleRequiresStratification` at admission |
| set-valued labelling | `SetCell` / `UnionSetCell` / `SetDelta` tag-set union — `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/SetCell.kt`, `.../data/op/` |
| magnitude / bands (unchanged) | `civictech.cell.control.Magnitude`, `AgoraService.MAGNITUDE_BANDS` |
| existing argumentation core | `ClaimCell`, `EdgeCell`, `DfQuad` — `demo/agora/src/main/kotlin/civictech/agora/` |
| observation | `ObserveCell` / `ManagedHost.observe` — `.../cell/observe/Observe.kt` |
| tests | `SimWorld`, `forEachSeed`, `awaitUntil` — `testkit/src/main/kotlin/civictech/testkit/` |

### 2.5 Output surface

Additive to `AgoraApp`:

- `GET /graph` — `NodeDto` gains `label` (`IN`/`OUT`/`UNDEC`) and keeps `head`, now kernel-derived.
  Additive and omitted-when-default, so `demo/agora/ui`'s normalizer parses it unchanged.
- `GET /fixpoint` — the grounded view's settled state: the iteration count at which it settled and
  whether the region is currently settled.
- The existing SSE `/events` stream carries both views.

## 3. Functional requirements (EARS)

Style mirrors `doc/spec/` (`[NN-SLUG-nn] <EARS sentence>`). Ids are scoped (`AGO4-*`) and cannot
collide with normative spec ids. "The app" = `:demo:agora`. Cited spec ids name the normative
requirement each AGO4 requirement makes true in this module.

### 3.1 Migration off the app-side approximation

- `[AGO4-MIG-01]` The app SHALL NOT compute cycle membership or designate cycle heads in application
  code; `AgoraService.reaches` and the `head = reaches(...)` designation in `createEdge` SHALL be
  removed (Ubiquitous; replaces `AgoraService.kt:134` and `:209-220`).
- `[AGO4-MIG-02]` `EdgeCell` SHALL NOT carry an application-level absorb gate on its source inlet;
  the `quiescence` constructor parameter and the early-return in `sourceInlet.onEach` SHALL be
  removed, and damping SHALL be the kernel feedback inlet's (Ubiquitous; replaces
  `EdgeCell.kt:42` and `:52-58`).
- `[AGO4-MIG-03]` WHERE a node is reported as a cycle head or a cycle-region member, that report
  SHALL be derived from the host's topology, not recomputed by the app (Ubiquitous).
- `[AGO4-MIG-04]` The existing exit gate SHALL keep its teeth: `AgoraExitTest`'s retraction-blind
  control SHALL still be required to diverge, and its DAG-seed exactness SHALL remain `1e-9`
  (Ubiquitous; a migration that softens the gate has failed regardless of what else it achieves).
- `[AGO4-MIG-05]` The app SHALL NOT retain a second, parallel cycle mechanism after migration: at
  most one head-designation and one damping mechanism SHALL exist in the codebase (Ubiquitous).

### 3.2 Kernel-backed admission

- `[AGO4-ADMIT-01]` WHEN a `connect` closes a locally-visible cycle in the argumentation graph, the
  host SHALL admit it only if the cycle contains a head and every data edge is throttle-capable, and
  the app SHALL surface the rejection reason unchanged (Event-driven; realizes `[21-CYCLE-01]`).
- `[AGO4-ADMIT-02]` IF an edge creation would close a headless cycle, THEN the app SHALL report the
  `CycleWithoutHead` rejection to its caller as a named error and SHALL leave the graph unchanged
  (Unwanted; `AgoraApp.handleOp`'s existing `IllegalArgumentException` → 400 path is the model).
- `[AGO4-ADMIT-03]` IF a cycle-region path would contain a non-monotone operator, THEN admission
  SHALL be rejected with `CycleRequiresStratification` and the app SHALL NOT construct that region
  (Unwanted; realizes E5.6's stratification rule).
- `[AGO4-ADMIT-04]` WHEN a cycle-closing edge is removed and the cycle ceases to exist, the region
  and its head designation SHALL be released without disturbing surviving nodes' credences or labels
  (Event-driven; the existing cascade in `AgoraService.remove` must compose with region release).

### 3.3 Strong-tier grounded fixpoint

- `[AGO4-GROUND-01]` The app SHALL maintain a grounded labelling assigning every claim and every edge
  a label of `IN`, `OUT` or `UNDEC` (Ubiquitous).
- `[AGO4-GROUND-02]` The grounded labelling SHALL be carried by idempotent-merge deltas (tag-set
  union), placing it in the strong tier (Ubiquitous; the precondition for `[21-CYCLE-03]`'s fixpoint
  guarantee to apply).
- `[AGO4-GROUND-03]` WHEN the argument graph reaches quiescence, the grounded labelling SHALL equal
  the batch grounded extension over the same graph **exactly** — no tolerance (Event-driven; this is
  what the strong tier buys and what the credence view cannot claim).
- `[AGO4-GROUND-04]` WHEN a cycle region containing the labelling settles, the head SHALL report a
  fixpoint cut naming the outer wave and the final iteration, and that report SHALL be exact and
  threshold-free (Event-driven; realizes `[21-CYCLE-03]` for this region via E5.4's iteration cut).
- `[AGO4-GROUND-05]` WHEN new input reaches a settled region — a claim added, an edge added or
  removed, a stance changed — the region SHALL re-settle to the grounded extension of the updated
  graph, and the result SHALL equal a from-scratch batch solve (Event-driven; E5.5's incremental
  re-entry, applied).
- `[AGO4-GROUND-06]` The grounded labelling SHALL treat an edge as an attackable argument in its own
  right, consistent with agora's existing edge-on-edge model, and the chosen convention SHALL be
  stated in the module's documentation and pinned by a test (Ubiquitous).
- `[AGO4-GROUND-07]` The grounded labelling SHALL be a function of the graph and stances alone, and
  SHALL NOT depend on arrival order, scheduler seed, or wall clock (Ubiquitous).

### 3.4 Weak tier — what AGO4 explicitly does not claim

- `[AGO4-WEAK-01]` The DF-QuAD credence loop SHALL remain weak-tier, and the app SHALL NOT claim,
  document, or test for a convergence guarantee on it (Ubiquitous; G-19's stated residual, 95 §R2;
  E5.7's *"the weak-tier credence loop stays as-is, R2-gated"*).
- `[AGO4-WEAK-02]` `AgoraExitTest`'s cyclic-seed tolerance for **credence** SHALL remain a stated
  bound rather than exactness, and SHALL NOT be tightened on the basis of KE5 alone (Ubiquitous;
  tightening it would assert a convergence result nobody has).
- `[AGO4-WEAK-03]` WHILE a weak-tier cycle fails to reach its damping threshold within the host's hop
  bound, the invocation SHALL be dead-lettered as a `CycleError` rather than looping to
  floating-point resolution (State-driven; the hop guard is the backstop the app-side model lacked —
  `CycleQuiescenceTest`'s own comment names its absence).
- `[AGO4-WEAK-04]` The app SHALL NOT present the weak-tier credence and the strong-tier labelling as
  carrying the same kind of guarantee on any surface (Ubiquitous; two tiers, two claims).
- `[AGO4-WEAK-05]` IF a seed is discovered on which the weak-tier loop fails to quiesce within
  budget, THEN that seed SHALL be retained, recorded in `doc/demo-findings.md`, and — where it
  conflicts with a cited requirement — filed in `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md`; it SHALL NOT be
  replaced with a friendlier seed (Unwanted; AGENTS.md's determinism rule, restated because this is
  exactly where it will be tempting).

### 3.5 Iteration context and egress

- `[AGO4-ITER-01]` The app SHALL NOT mint wave ids, iteration numbers, or `LoopContext` values; only
  the kernel's head re-origination writes them (Ubiquitous).
- `[AGO4-ITER-02]` The head's outlet broadcast SHALL NOT be gated by cycle throttling; only
  re-origination is gated (Ubiquitous; 21 §Cycles — "the throttle gates re-origination, never
  fan-out", so no external subscriber is silenced).
- `[AGO4-ITER-03]` WHERE settled egress is enabled for the grounded region, downstream observers
  SHALL receive the labelling only at fixpoint, re-associated to the triggering outer wave
  (Optional-feature; E5.3's settled-egress mode).
- `[AGO4-ITER-04]` WHERE settled egress is not enabled, intermediate labellings MAY be observed, and
  no requirement or test SHALL assert a property of an intermediate labelling (Optional-feature +
  Unwanted).

### 3.6 Durability, recovery and evolution

- `[AGO4-DUR-01]` WHERE a journal directory is configured, WHEN the process is killed and restarted,
  the recovered graph SHALL reproduce the same head/region designations and the same grounded
  labelling as before the kill (Optional-feature + Event-driven; agora's `DurabilityTest` pattern).
- `[AGO4-DUR-02]` WHILE the structure log replays, cycle admission SHALL produce the same regions as
  the original construction order, and replay SHALL NOT reject an edge the original construction
  admitted (State-driven; the replay path in `AgoraService`'s `init` reconstructs edges in log
  order).
- `[AGO4-DUR-03]` WHEN a cell in a cycle region is restarted or promoted, the region SHALL either be
  re-established or the failure SHALL be reported; the app SHALL NOT silently continue with a
  half-established region (Event-driven; G-41 names head behaviour under RESTART/promotion as
  unpinned — see §3.8).

### 3.7 Observation

- `[AGO4-OBS-01]` The app SHALL expose each node's grounded label alongside its credence
  (Ubiquitous).
- `[AGO4-OBS-02]` The app SHALL expose, per cycle region, whether it is currently settled and the
  iteration at which it settled (Ubiquitous).
- `[AGO4-OBS-03]` The `/graph` response SHALL remain parseable by the existing `demo/agora/ui`
  normalizer without modification (Ubiquitous; new fields additive and omitted-when-default).
- `[AGO4-OBS-04]` The head marker exposed to clients SHALL reflect the kernel's head designation
  (Ubiquitous; the `head` field and the `⟳` marker keep their meaning but change their source).

### 3.8 Requirements that cannot be checked honestly today

- **`[AGO4-DUR-03]` is bounded by G-41, not by AGO4.** `doc/spec/90-roadmap/91-gap-analysis.md` G-41
  lists *"head behavior under RESTART/promotion is unpinned"* among the adopted structure's open
  holes, and E5 defers cross-host and nested-cycle structure to research (95 R16). AGO4 therefore
  requires *report-or-re-establish*, not a specific recovery semantics. If a test cannot distinguish
  the two, that is a `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` entry against G-41, not a weakened assertion.
- **Cross-host cycles remain invisible.** E5.3 states cross-host cycles stay invisible to admission
  with the hop guard as the only backstop. AGO4 is single-host and MUST NOT claim otherwise; a
  distributed agora cycle is out of scope and out of guarantee.
- **`[AGO4-WEAK-01]`'s negative claim is verified by absence, which is weak.** The check is a review
  obligation plus a documentation test: no file in `:demo:agora` asserts credence convergence, and
  `AgoraExitTest`'s cyclic tolerance is unchanged. If a stronger mechanical check exists, use it;
  do not pretend the absence check is stronger than it is.
- **"Closes agora's G-19 residual" is true only in the §1.2 sense.** The completion report MUST state
  which half closed (the app-side approximation, plus an exactly-detected strong-tier fixpoint view)
  and which did not (weak-tier numeric convergence, 95 §R2). Reporting the plan's phrase unqualified
  would misrepresent the result.

## 4. Behaviour specifications

Each scenario becomes one named test. `**[concord]**` marks kernel-semantic, implementation-neutral
scenarios belonging in `concord/corpus/`; the rest are `:demo:agora` tests. Note the existing corpus
already has `concord/corpus/34-cycles/34-CYCLE-01.yaml` (`covers: [21-CYCLE-01, 21-CYCLE-02]`) and
`34-CYCLE-REJECT-01.yaml` — kernel cycle scenarios belong to **KE5**, not AGO4; AGO4 adds a corpus
scenario only where it finds a genuine uncovered kernel property, and coins no new ids.

**BS4-01 — mutual attack, kernel-headed.**
GIVEN claims A and B and an ATTACK edge A→B.
WHEN the cycle-closing edge B→A is created.
THEN the connect is admitted, the head is designated by the kernel (not by `AgoraService`), the
graph quiesces, and the credences match the batch fixpoint within the existing stated bound.
*(`[AGO4-MIG-01]`, `[AGO4-ADMIT-01]`, `[AGO4-WEAK-02]`)*
This is `CycleQuiescenceTest`'s existing first test, re-pointed at kernel machinery; its assertions
must not weaken.

**BS4-02 — headless closure is rejected, not silently damped.**
GIVEN a graph configuration in which the closing edge is not admitted as a head.
WHEN the closing connect is attempted.
THEN it is `Rejected` with `CycleWithoutHead`, the app returns a named error, and the graph is
byte-identical to before the attempt.
*(`[AGO4-ADMIT-02]`)*
**[concord]** this is a kernel property already covered by `34-CYCLE-REJECT-01`; add nothing unless a
genuine gap exists, and if it does, it is KE5's scenario.

**BS4-03 — the grounded labelling equals the batch grounded extension, exactly.**
GIVEN 100 seeded randomly grown-and-churned argument graphs — the `AgoraExitTest` generator, cyclic
seeds included.
WHEN each is driven to quiescence.
THEN the incremental grounded labelling equals a batch grounded-extension solve over the final state
**exactly on every seed, cyclic ones included** — no tolerance.
*(`[AGO4-GROUND-01]`, `[AGO4-GROUND-02]`, `[AGO4-GROUND-03]`, `[AGO4-GROUND-07]`)*
This is the epic's headline result and the visible difference from the credence view.

**BS4-04 — the fixpoint cut is exact and reported.**
GIVEN a cyclic argument graph carrying the grounded labelling.
WHEN it settles.
THEN the head reports settled with an outer wave and a final iteration, the iteration count is at
most the batch solver's round count, and no threshold was consulted.
*(`[AGO4-GROUND-04]`)*

**BS4-05 — incremental re-entry after settling.**
GIVEN a settled grounded labelling over a cyclic graph.
WHEN an edge is added, then removed, then a stance is changed, each run to settle.
THEN after each settle the labelling equals a from-scratch batch solve over the current graph, and
the delta count is bounded well below a from-scratch recomputation (a from-scratch-per-wave control
must blow the budget).
*(`[AGO4-GROUND-05]`)*

**BS4-06 — edges are arguments too.**
GIVEN A attacks B, and C attacks the A→B edge.
WHEN the graph settles.
THEN the labelling assigns the edge its own label under the stated convention, and B's label reflects
the edge being defeated — the edge-on-edge property, in the labelling view.
*(`[AGO4-GROUND-06]`)*

**BS4-07 — the app has no cycle code left.**
GIVEN the AGO4 branch.
WHEN `:demo:agora` is searched for `reaches(`, for an `EdgeCell` `quiescence` parameter, and for an
app-side absorb early-return.
THEN none exists, exactly one head-designation mechanism exists in the codebase, and the head
reported on `/graph` comes from the host topology.
*(`[AGO4-MIG-01]`, `[AGO4-MIG-02]`, `[AGO4-MIG-03]`, `[AGO4-MIG-05]`, `[AGO4-OBS-04]`)*

**BS4-08 — the exit gate keeps its teeth.**
GIVEN the migrated `AgoraExitTest`.
WHEN it runs over 100 seeds.
THEN the retraction-blind control still diverges (the harness asserts it does), DAG seeds still match
to `1e-9`, and the cyclic-seed credence tolerance is unchanged from before the migration.
*(`[AGO4-MIG-04]`, `[AGO4-WEAK-02]`)*

**BS4-09 — the hop guard is the backstop the app never had.**
GIVEN a weak-tier loop configured not to reach its damping threshold within the host's hop bound.
WHEN it runs.
THEN the invocation is dead-lettered as a `CycleError`, the host stays live, and the loop does not
run to floating-point resolution.
*(`[AGO4-WEAK-03]`)*
This is `CycleQuiescenceTest`'s `headless probe` re-purposed: the old test measured how many laps the
absence of a backstop costs; the new one asserts the backstop exists.

**BS4-10 — no convergence claim leaked in.**
GIVEN the AGO4 branch.
WHEN the credence view's documentation, API responses and tests are reviewed.
THEN no statement asserts that the DF-QuAD loop converges, the cyclic tolerance is intact, and the
two views are presented with distinguishable guarantees on every surface.
*(`[AGO4-WEAK-01]`, `[AGO4-WEAK-04]`)*
Verified by review plus the tolerance assertion; §3.8 records that this check is weak by nature.

**BS4-11 — a divergent seed is kept.**
GIVEN a seed on which the weak-tier loop fails to quiesce within budget, if one is found.
WHEN it is discovered.
THEN it is retained in the suite as a documented expected-limitation case, recorded in
`doc/demo-findings.md`, and not replaced.
*(`[AGO4-WEAK-05]`)*
If no such seed is found, that fact is reported — not asserted as evidence of convergence.

**BS4-12 — region release on removal.**
GIVEN a cyclic graph whose closing edge is removed, cascading over dependent edges.
WHEN the removal completes and the graph quiesces.
THEN the region and its head designation are released, every surviving node's credence and label
equal a fresh batch solve over the remaining graph, and no dangling influence remains.
*(`[AGO4-ADMIT-04]`)*

**BS4-13 — stratification is enforced at admission.**
GIVEN a proposed region whose path would contain a non-monotone operator.
WHEN the closing connect is attempted.
THEN it is rejected with `CycleRequiresStratification` and the region is not constructed.
*(`[AGO4-ADMIT-03]`)*
**[concord]** this is KE5/E5.6's kernel property; the corpus scenario belongs to KE5.

**BS4-14 — kill -9 reproduces regions and labels.**
GIVEN a journalled agora with a cyclic graph, settled, with a known labelling.
WHEN the process is killed with `-9` and restarted against the same journal directory.
THEN the structure log replays, the same regions and head designations are established, every
credence and every grounded label matches the pre-kill state, and no edge the original construction
admitted is rejected on replay.
*(`[AGO4-DUR-01]`, `[AGO4-DUR-02]`)*

**BS4-15 — restart of a cell inside a region is reported, not hidden.**
GIVEN a cell inside a settled cycle region.
WHEN it is restarted.
THEN either the region is re-established and the labelling re-settles to the correct extension, or
the failure is reported; the app does not continue with a half-established region.
*(`[AGO4-DUR-03]`)*
Bounded by G-41 (§3.8): the test asserts report-or-re-establish, not a specific recovery semantics.

**BS4-16 — the existing frontend still renders it.**
GIVEN a `/graph` response carrying `label` and the kernel-derived `head`.
WHEN `demo/agora/ui`'s `diff.normalize` is fed it.
THEN it normalizes without error, produces a non-empty node set, and the existing head marker still
renders.
*(`[AGO4-OBS-03]`, `[AGO4-OBS-04]`)*

## 5. Scope boundaries

Citing the plan's dependency edge (`computenet-milestone-plan.md` §2: `KE5 --> AGO4`, a *solid* edge
= hard prerequisite; AGO4 has no edge from AGO1):

**In scope**: removing the five app-side approximation pieces (§1.1); adopting kernel cycle
admission, heads, damping, `LoopContext` and the E5.4 fixpoint cut; the grounded-extension
strong-tier view and its exact batch equivalence; migrating the existing cycle tests; the additive
`/graph` and `/fixpoint` surface; the honesty requirements in §3.4.

**NOT in scope — belongs to a named edge or successor:**

- **KE5 itself** (unwired dependency). E5.1–E5.6 — the spec text, `LoopContext`, region capture,
  the iteration cut, incremental re-entry, stratification — are kernel work. AGO4 is E5.7, the
  adopter. AGO4 SHALL NOT modify `kernel/`, `gen/`, `nature/` or `wire/`; a gap in KE5 is a KE5
  dependency or a `doc/demo-findings.md` entry, never a local patch.
- **Weak-tier convergence — 95 §R2.** Classifying delta algebras by contraction behaviour, a
  convergence guarantee for numeric loops, or a damping-policy vocabulary are research, explicitly
  gated. `[AGO4-WEAK-01..05]` are the guard rails.
- **Cross-host and nested cycles — G-41 / 95 R16.** Single-host only; the hop guard is the stated
  backstop.
- **The extraction pipeline — AGO1/AGO2/AGO3.** AGO4 does not touch `:demo:dialogue`. Extraction
  generates cycles; AGO4 makes them better-founded, and that is the whole interaction.
- **QRY2 and BB-GRA**, the other KE5 consumers (`KE5 --> QRY2`, `KE5 --> BB-GRA`). Recursive queries
  and PageRank-class analytics are separate adopters of the same kernel work.
- **Editing plan or spec documents.** 21 §Cycles cross-references the demo (E5.7 says so), but the
  spec edit belongs to E5.1, not here. Findings → `doc/demo-findings.md`; honest spec↔code conflicts
  → `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md`; `CONCORDANCE.md` is generated, never hand-edited.

```bash
./gradlew :demo:agora:test --tests '*CycleQuiescence*'
./gradlew :demo:dialogue:test                       # AGO1/AGO2/AGO3 must still pass; AGO4 changes their sink's cycle handling
./gradlew :concord:test                             # KE5's cycle scenarios must be green; AGO4 adds none by default
./gradlew :concord:concordance && ./gradlew :concord:check   # only if a scenario was genuinely added
./gradlew :demo:exchange:test                       # the repo's toughest property gate — composition must not regress
./gradlew test                                      # repository-wide gate
cd demo/agora/ui && npm test                        # BS4-16 fixture compatibility
```

Manual: `./gradlew :demo:agora:run --args="<port> --journal /tmp/agora"`, build a mutual attack, and
watch both the credence bars and the grounded labels settle.

Discipline:
- Seeded `SimWorld` + `forEachSeed`; a discovered failing seed is **kept**, never swapped
  (`[AGO4-WEAK-05]` exists because this is where the temptation lives).
- Assert semantic outcomes at quiescence and failure-path accounting — never scheduling timing.
- Do not tighten `AgoraExitTest`'s cyclic credence tolerance (`[AGO4-WEAK-02]`).
- Check the diff for `kernel/`, `gen/`, `nature/`, `wire/` and for generated output.
- The completion report MUST state which half of G-19's residual closed and which did not (§3.8).

---

## 8. Risks and open questions

**R1 — over-claiming G-19. (The central risk.)** The plan's phrase is *"closes agora's G-19
residual"*, and the tempting report is "G-19 closed". It is not: weak-tier fixpoint convergence for
the numeric credence loop stays open under 95 §R2, and E5.7 says the credence loop *stays as-is*.
`[AGO4-WEAK-01..05]` and §3.8 exist to keep the report honest. What genuinely closes is the app-side
approximation plus the arrival of a view where an exact fixpoint is detectable.

**R2 — deleting `AgoraService.reaches` deletes a working thing.** The app-side approximation is not
broken; it passes a 100-seed gate today. A migration that swaps working code for kernel code and
comes out *slightly worse* on some seeds is a real possibility. `[AGO4-MIG-04]` and BS4-08 make the
existing gate the floor: same teeth, same DAG exactness, same cyclic tolerance. If kernel-backed
damping cannot match it, that is a KE5 finding, not a reason to loosen the test.

**R3 — grounded labelling over an edge-attacking graph is a modelling decision, not a lookup.**
Textbook Dung semantics has no edges-as-arguments. Agora does (`EdgeCell : ClaimCell`). The chosen
convention (`[AGO4-GROUND-06]`) must be stated and pinned, and the batch reference must implement
the *same* convention or BS4-03 becomes a test of two different definitions agreeing by luck.

**R4 — two views, one UI.** Showing a credence bar and a label in the same node risks implying they
carry the same authority. `[AGO4-WEAK-04]` requires distinguishable presentation; the frontend work
to do that well is a separate item, but the API must not blur them.

**R5 — RESTART/promotion inside a region is genuinely unpinned.** G-41 names it. `[AGO4-DUR-03]`
requires report-or-re-establish, which is the strongest honest requirement available. If the
implementer finds the behaviour underdetermined in practice, that is a `DISPUTES.md` entry against
G-41 and a finding for KE5 — not an invented semantics.

**R6 — dependency latency.** KE5 sits late in the kernel lane (§4 order: KX → KE1 → KFX → KAGG-R →
KE3 → MEM1/MEM2 → **KE5**), so AGO4 is genuinely second-wave (§5 rank 20). Nothing here should be
prototyped against a placeholder cycle API; a placeholder would reproduce exactly the app-side
approximation this item exists to delete.

**Open questions for the implementing agent to decide and record:**
(a) Is the grounded labelling a separate cell layer over the same `ClaimCell`/`EdgeCell` topology, or
a second port family on the existing cells? Prefer the separate layer — it keeps the strong-tier
delta type cleanly separated from the weak-tier numeric one, which is the whole point.
(b) Is settled egress (`[AGO4-ITER-03]`) enabled by default for the labelling view? Eager is the
kernel default; settled is nicer for a projected map. Record the choice and make it configurable.
(c) Does `NodeDto.head` keep its name once it is kernel-derived, or become a richer region
descriptor? Prefer keeping the field additive-compatible for `demo/agora/ui`.
(d) Should `UNDEC` be materialized or derived as the complement at fixpoint? Deriving is cheaper;
materializing makes the SSE frame self-describing. Record the reasoning.
design:
# AGO4 — design notes (the exact code being replaced, and the exact claim being made)

## Sizing: filed as `feature`, not `epic`

AGO4 corresponds one-to-one with an already-decomposed E-plan ticket:
`doc/spec/90-roadmap/96-incremental-engines-plan.md` **§E5.7 — "Agora grounded-extension fixpoint
(gap-5 payoff; strong-tier adopter) — P2 · Medium · `demo` (`:demo:agora`)"**, depending on
E5.1–E5.5. Its implement clause is a *demo adoption*: put the grounded labelling on `SetDelta`
cells around a kernel `CycleHead`, and let E5.4's cut terminate it exactly.

One mechanism (adopt kernel cycles; add the one view where the strong tier applies), one module, a
Medium rating from the plan that owns the decomposition. Filing it as an epic would double-count E5's
own breakdown and inflate the lane.

**Parenting**: its natural parent is the KE5 epic, which is being filed by another agent and whose id
is unknown. It is therefore left unparented rather than mis-parented under AGO1
(`computenet-2aw`) — AGO4 has no AGO1 dependency and does not touch `:demo:dialogue`.

## The five pieces of app-side cycle code, with line references

This is the "name the real code being replaced" list. Each was written as an explicit stand-in for
kernel machinery, and each says so in its own KDoc.

**1. `AgoraService.reaches(from, to)` — `demo/agora/src/main/kotlin/civictech/agora/AgoraService.kt:209-220`.**
A DFS along the influence-flow direction over the service's own `nodes` index. The service's class
KDoc frames it: *"cells stay topology-blind; the service owns the index — which is also what lets it
designate cycle heads at edge-creation time (the app-side form of the decided cycle model, spec 21
§Cycles / 93 I-5+I-6)."* Replaced by E5.3's SCC capture on `FeedbackInlet` admission.

**2. Head designation in `createEdge` — `AgoraService.kt:134-135`.**
```kotlin
val head = reaches(from = target, to = source)
val edge = EdgeCell(polarity, ref, semantics, quiescence = if (head) quiescence else 0.0)
```
The app decides which edge is a head and hands it a threshold. Replaced by kernel admission: a cycle
is admitted only if it contains a head and every data edge is throttle-capable (`[21-CYCLE-01]`).

**3. The absorb gate in `EdgeCell` — `demo/agora/src/main/kotlin/civictech/agora/cell/EdgeCell.kt:42, 52-58`.**
```kotlin
sourceInlet.onEach { value ->
    if (quiescence > 0 && abs(value.credence - sourceCredence) < quiescence) return@onEach
    ...
}
```
Its KDoc: *"[quiescence] > 0 designates this edge a cycle head (the app-side form of the decided
I-5/I-6 model, spec 21 §Cycles)."* Note it is an *inlet early-return*, not a re-origination gate —
close to the decided model but not it. Replaced by the kernel feedback inlet's damper, which gates
re-origination and never fan-out.

**4. The head surface — `AgoraService.kt:32` (`quiescence: Double = 1e-3`), `:51`
(`NodeInfo.head`), `AgoraApp.NodeDto.head`, the `⟳` marker in `AgoraApp`'s inline page, and
`demo/agora/ui/src/api/types.ts` (`NodeRec.head`).** The field keeps its meaning and changes its
source: kernel topology instead of app DFS.

**5. The termination story — `demo/agora/src/test/kotlin/civictech/agora/CycleQuiescenceTest.kt:99-125`.**
The `headless probe`'s own comment is the confession: *"the ONLY reason it terminates at all is that
the base clamp makes every single loop contractive; the decided kernel hop guard (spec 21 §Cycles,
unbuilt) is the backstop this app-level model still lacks."* Under KE5 the hop guard exists and
dead-letters a `CycleError`.

**And the price**: `AgoraExitTest.kt:91` — `val tolerance = if (cyclic) 25 * q else 1e-9`. On cyclic
seeds the lane's exit gate asserts nearness, not equality. That number is G-19's residual made
executable.

## Decision D1 — two views, two tiers, never blurred

| | DF-QuAD credence (existing) | grounded labelling (new) |
|---|---|---|
| delta | numeric, `Magnitude`-carrying | `SetDelta`, tag-set union |
| merge | non-idempotent | idempotent |
| tier (`[21-CYCLE-03]`) | weak | strong |
| termination | bounded-lap, damper-assisted | structural, threshold-free |
| fixpoint | **not guaranteed** — 95 §R2 | guaranteed and exactly detected (E5.4 cut) |
| test bound | `25 * q` on cyclic seeds, unchanged | exact equality with the batch solve |

The design's core honesty move is refusing to let the second column's guarantee rub off on the
first. `DfQuad`'s only convergence argument is the `BASE_FLOOR` clamp
(`demo/agora/src/main/kotlin/civictech/agora/semantics/Semantics.kt:12-17`: *"the clamp is what keeps
a single cycle's loop gain below 1 … so feedback decays geometrically"*) — a per-single-cycle
argument that says nothing about multi-cycle interleavings, which is exactly what AGO1 §3.8 bullet 2
already flagged as agora's open G-19 residual.

`[AGO4-WEAK-01..05]` encode this: no convergence claim, no tolerance tightening, hop guard as the
real backstop, distinguishable presentation, and a discovered divergent seed is kept.

## Decision D2 — grounded extension is the right strong-tier adopter

Chosen by E5.7 and correct for three reasons:

1. **It is genuinely set-valued.** IN/OUT/UNDEC labellings are sets of refs; the least fixpoint of
   the characteristic function is computed by union. Idempotent merge → strong tier → the guarantee
   applies by construction rather than by hope.
2. **It has a reference answer.** A batch iterative grounded-extension solver is small and
   uncontroversial, sibling to the existing `BatchReference.solve`. Exact equality is assertable,
   which is what makes BS4-03 a real gate rather than a tolerance negotiation.
3. **It is a product feature, not a demo prop.** Credence answers "how strongly is this believed";
   grounded extension answers "what survives the argument". A live map showing both is more useful,
   and the second one has an exact answer.

The one genuine modelling decision is that agora's edges are themselves attackable arguments
(`EdgeCell : ClaimCell`), which textbook Dung semantics does not model. `[AGO4-GROUND-06]` requires
the convention to be stated and pinned — and the batch reference must implement the *same*
convention, or BS4-03 tests two definitions agreeing by coincidence.

## Decision D3 — the migration must not soften the existing gate

`AgoraExitTest` is the argumentation lane's correctness gate: 100 seeds, incremental == batch, with a
retraction-blind reference required to diverge (`assertTrue(removalDivergenceSeen, "retraction-blind
control never diverged — the harness has no teeth")`, `AgoraExitTest.kt:123`).

A migration from working app code to kernel code that comes out marginally worse on some seeds is a
realistic outcome. `[AGO4-MIG-04]` makes the current gate the floor — same teeth, same `1e-9` DAG
exactness, same cyclic tolerance — and BS4-08 checks it. If kernel-backed damping cannot meet it,
that is a KE5 finding, not a licence to loosen a test.

Symmetrically, `[AGO4-WEAK-02]` forbids *tightening* the cyclic tolerance on the strength of KE5
alone: doing so would assert a weak-tier convergence result that 95 §R2 explicitly does not have.
The tolerance moves in neither direction.

## Decision D4 — the app writes no iteration state

`[AGO4-ITER-01]`: the app mints no wave ids, no iteration numbers, no `LoopContext`. E5.2 makes the
`FeedbackInlet` the only writer of `loop`, and transparent flow copies it like `hop`. The app's job
is to *be* a well-formed cycle region, not to simulate one — which is precisely the difference
between AGO4 and the code it replaces.

`[AGO4-ITER-02]` restates 21 §Cycles' rule that the throttle gates re-origination and never fan-out,
because the code being deleted (an inlet early-return) is subtly the other thing.

## Decision D5 — what the completion report must say

Per §3.8 and R1: report which half of G-19's residual closed.

- **Closed**: agora no longer approximates the kernel cycle model in application code; head
  designation, damping, admission and termination are the kernel's; and the grounded view has an
  exactly-detected fixpoint (`[21-CYCLE-03]`'s strong-tier guarantee, actually claimable).
- **Not closed**: weak-tier fixpoint convergence for the numeric credence loop — G-19's stated
  residual, 95 §R2's research question, and E5.7's explicit carve-out.

Reporting the milestone plan's phrase *"closes agora's G-19 residual"* without that split would
misrepresent the result.

## Kernel seams (implementation crib)

| Concern | Type | Source |
|---|---|---|
| region capture at admission | E5.3 — `ManagedHost.wouldCloseCycle` → SCC capture; ingress/egress classification | KE5 |
| head + feedback inlet | `CycleHead` / `FeedbackInlet` | KE5 (partially built per 21 §Cycles) |
| iteration identity | E5.2 `LoopContext(outerWave, iteration)` on `MessageContext` | KE5 |
| fixpoint cut | E5.4 `settled: LoopContext?` at the feedback inlet | KE5 |
| settled egress | E5.3 hold-until-settled buffer keyed by `outerWave` | KE5 |
| stratification | E5.6 `CycleRequiresStratification` | KE5 |
| hop guard | `MessageContext.hop`, `CycleError` dead-letter | 21 §Cycles |
| set-valued labelling | `SetCell`, `UnionSetCell`, `SetDelta` | `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/` |
| magnitude bands (unchanged) | `AgoraService.MAGNITUDE_BANDS`, `civictech.cell.control.Magnitude` | `AgoraService.kt:234-248` |
| existing core | `ClaimCell`, `EdgeCell`, `DfQuad`, `BatchReference` | `demo/agora/src/{main,test}/kotlin/civictech/agora/` |
| corpus precedent | `34-CYCLE-01.yaml` (`covers: [21-CYCLE-01, 21-CYCLE-02]`), `34-CYCLE-REJECT-01.yaml` | `concord/corpus/34-cycles/` |

## Invariants to protect while implementing

- Never claim weak-tier convergence; never tighten and never loosen the cyclic credence tolerance
  (`[AGO4-WEAK-01]`, `[AGO4-WEAK-02]`).
- Never leave two cycle mechanisms in the codebase (`[AGO4-MIG-05]`) — a half-migration is worse
  than either state.
- Never mint iteration or wave state in the app (`[AGO4-ITER-01]`).
- Never gate the head's fan-out (`[AGO4-ITER-02]`).
- Keep the exit gate's teeth: retraction-blind divergence and `1e-9` DAG exactness
  (`[AGO4-MIG-04]`).
- Keep a discovered divergent seed (`[AGO4-WEAK-05]`); it is a finding, not a nuisance.
- `kernel/`, `gen/`, `nature/`, `wire/` untouched — AGO4 is E5.7, the adopter, not E5 itself.
  Findings → `doc/demo-findings.md`; honest spec↔code conflicts → `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md`.

title: JAR3 — Jar-attached GraphSpec deploy; upgrade variant
description:
# JAR3 — Jar-attached `GraphSpec` deploy; upgrade variant

Source: `computenet-milestone-plan.md` §1 (Product lanes, row JAR3: "Jar-attached
`GraphSpec` deploy; upgrade variant … the deployment story"), §2 DAG
(`JAR1 --> JAR2 --> JAR3`), §5 rank 20 (second wave).

Depends on: **JAR1** (`computenet-051`) — `:loader`, `ModuleClassLoader`,
`ModuleHandle.cellFactory(fqn)`, validate-then-commit registration, unload lifecycle —
and **JAR2** (`computenet-9yf`) — `shapeVersion`/`schemaVersion`, `ModuleVersion`,
`PriorState` migration chains, `RollbackCheckpoint`.
Unblocks: the deployment story; feeds **WKB2**/**WKB3** (the workbench renders what this
epic makes expressible).

**JAR3 must not assume JAR1's or JAR2's fixes exist until they land.** In particular the
three pre-existing defects JAR1 owns — `ContractRegistry.register` mutating mid-loop
with no `unregister`; `WireCodec.json` built once at object init so a late-loaded jar's
`WireSerializers` can never reach the codec; loader-agnostic
`Class.forName(descriptor.fqn)` — are **JAR1's**, consumed from `main`, never re-solved
here. If `[JAR1-REG-08]` resolves to "refuse non-wire-capable modules", JAR3 inherits
that constraint and must surface it as a deploy-time refusal rather than quietly
widening it.

---

## Why this is filed as an epic, not a feature

The sizing rule says file `--type=epic` only for a genuine subsystem, and notes JAR3 may
be smaller than JAR2. Judged honestly, it is still a subsystem, for one specific reason
that only becomes visible after reading the code:

**`GraphSpec` cannot be shipped inside a jar as it stands.** It is
`data class GraphSpec(val steps: List<GraphStep>) : Serializable`
(`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/graph/GraphDsl.kt:232`), and a `SpawnStep`
carries `val factory: CellFactory` — a `fun interface … : Serializable` whose instances
in every existing call site are **Kotlin lambdas** (`GraphBuilder.spawn`, `:378`).
Java-serializing a lambda pins a synthetic class name and an implementation-specific
`SerializedLambda` shape that is not stable across recompiles of the same source. A jar
whose deployment descriptor is a serialized `GraphSpec` would therefore break on a
rebuild of the very module it describes — the exact thing an upgrade story cannot
tolerate.

So JAR3 is not "read a file and call `applyTo`". It has to introduce a **declarative
deployment descriptor** — handles, cell FQNs, identity bindings, connections, and
per-instance data — that is resolved against a loaded `ModuleHandle` and *lowered* into
a `GraphSpec` whose factories are constructed at deploy time from live `Class` objects.
That is a new serialized artifact with its own compatibility surface, its own resolver,
its own failure taxonomy, and a second mode (upgrade) that plans a diff and drives JAR2's
promotion machinery per changed cell. Six features, two modules, one new format.

The alternative filing — `--type=feature --parent=computenet-9yf` — was rejected on
that basis, and also because bd refuses `blocks` edges from an epic to a `type=feature`
item, which would have made the JAR2→JAR3 edge unwireable.

---

## Ambition / Why

Spec 53's thesis is that *"Deployments are incremental graph operations, not binary
releases"* (`doc/spec/50-development-process/53-evolution.md:11-12`). The kernel already
makes topology serializable data — `GraphSpec`, `IdentityBinding`, `HostManagementApi.spawnBound`,
`GraphSpec.applyRemote`/`ApplyReport`, all shipped (`51-construction.md:9`). JAR1 makes
code a live, addressable, reversible unit. JAR2 makes a version mean something and makes
a state transition safe.

What is still missing is the **artifact**. Today a deployment is: hand the operator a
jar, and separately hand them a Kotlin program that builds the graph. The two are
uncoupled — nothing says *which* topology this jar wants, nothing checks that the jar
actually provides the cells the topology names, and nothing describes how to get from
the topology version 1.0 built to the one 2.0 wants. That gap is why the live-programming
story stops short of being a deployment story: you can load code and you can apply a
graph, but you cannot ship "a thing that deploys".

JAR3 closes it with one idea: **a module carries the topology it wants.** A jar becomes
self-describing — code plus a declarative graph — and deployment becomes two operations
over that artifact:

- **deploy** — load the module (JAR1), resolve its declared graph against the module's own
  `CellFactory`s, apply it, report per step.
- **upgrade** — load version N+1 alongside N (JAR2's coexistence rules), diff the two
  declared graphs, and execute the difference: added cells spawn, removed cells despawn,
  changed cells promote through `Promotion.promote` with JAR2's migration chain, unchanged
  cells are untouched.

That second operation is the payoff, and it is the first time every piece of the arc —
loader, versioning, migration, rollback, promotion, `GraphSpec` — is exercised as one
motion. It is also what WKB2/WKB3 need to exist before a workbench can offer "upload a
module and swap the running version" as a button.

---

## What we build

**Extends JAR1's `:loader`** with a `civictech.loader.deploy` package. **No new Gradle
module**, and specifically **no new `:kernel` surface**: 53's own guardrail says *"any
deployment feature that would require a new kernel mechanism should trigger a design
review (P1 violation likely)"* (`53-evolution.md:80-83`). JAR3 must be pure orchestration
over `spawn` / `connect` / `despawn` / `Promotion.promote`, and if it finds itself
wanting a kernel primitive, that is a finding to report, not a thing to build.

| Where | What |
|---|---|
| `loader/src/main/kotlin/civictech/loader/deploy/` | `DeploymentSpec` (the declarative descriptor), its serial form, `DeploymentReader`, `DeploymentResolver` (spec → `GraphSpec`), `Deployer.deploy` / `Deployer.upgrade`, `UpgradePlan`, `DeployReport` |
| jar `META-INF/` | a `META-INF/computenet/deployment.json` (or equivalent) resource plus a manifest attribute naming it — discovered exactly like JAR1 discovers `META-INF/services/*` |
| `gen/` (optional, decide in feature 1) | build-time emission of the descriptor from an annotated declaration, so the FQNs it names are compiler-checked rather than string-typed |

### The descriptor

`DeploymentSpec` is a small, versioned, **string-and-data** document — deliberately not a
serialized object graph:

```
deploymentVersion   the descriptor format version (not the module version)
moduleId, requires  the module this belongs to, and other module ids+version ranges it needs
cells[]             handle, cellFqn, identity (FreshLogical | NewInstanceOf | Exact),
                    parentHandle?, instanceSpec? (interest, instanceId, placement,
                    journalId, frontierPolicy)
links[]             fromHandle.outlet -> toHandle.inlet
```

Every field mirrors a `GraphStep` field that already exists (`SpawnStep`, `ConnectStep`,
`InstanceSetStep`, `InstanceSpec`, `IdentityBinding`, `GraphDsl.kt:41-190`). The resolver's
whole job is `cellFqn` → `ModuleHandle.cellFactory(fqn)` → `SpawnStep(handle, factory,
identity, parent)`, then `GraphSpec(steps)`. Nothing is invented; the descriptor is the
wire-safe projection of a `GraphSpec` whose factories are named rather than serialized.

`InstanceSetStep` is carried through as data because it already lowers to N × `SpawnStep`
(`GraphDsl.kt:153-162`) and already validates its own mis-compositions
(`InstanceSetStep.validate()`, `:169-189`) — JAR3 must call `lower()` and let those
refusals fire, not reimplement them.

### Deploy

1. `ModuleLoader.load(jar)` (JAR1) → `ModuleHandle`.
2. Read the descriptor from the module's own classloader resource.
3. **Validate before applying**: every `cellFqn` resolves through
   `ModuleHandle.cellFactory`; every `links` endpoint names a declared handle; every
   `requires` module is loaded at a satisfying `ModuleVersion` (JAR2); the descriptor's
   `deploymentVersion` is supported.
4. Resolve to a `GraphSpec` and apply.
5. Return a `DeployReport` folding the `ApplyReport`.

### Upgrade

1. Load module `M@N+1` alongside `M@N`. JAR2's `[JAR2-MOD-01]` gates this: permitted iff
   every shared contract FQN agrees on `shapeVersion`. A refused load is a refused
   upgrade, before anything moves.
2. Diff `DeploymentSpec@N` against `DeploymentSpec@N+1`, matched **by handle** (the
   descriptor's stable name), producing an `UpgradePlan` of typed actions:
   `Added`, `Removed`, `Promoted(fromFqn, toFqn)`, `Relinked`, `Unchanged`.
3. **Validate the whole plan before executing any of it** — every `Promoted` action's
   candidate must pass JAR2's PRECHECK conditions *as a dry run*, so a missing migration
   chain is a refused upgrade rather than a half-migrated graph.
4. Execute: spawn additions, run each promotion through `Promotion.promote` with JAR2's
   chain, apply relinks, despawn removals last.
5. Report per action; retain JAR2's `RollbackCheckpoint` per promoted cell.

### What the upgrade explicitly does not attempt

**Atomicity of a multi-step upgrade is not on the table.** `GraphSpec.applyRemote`'s
decided semantics are *"partial + report"*, and compensating rollback of the successful
prefix is **research-gated** (95 §R4, named at `15-lifecycle.md:76-78` and in
`GraphDsl.kt:288-291`). JAR3 inherits that boundary exactly: it validates the whole plan
up front so that *admission* is all-or-nothing, and reports honestly per action when
execution partially succeeds. It does **not** invent compensating rollback. Per-cell
rollback (JAR2's) is available and is a different, smaller claim — `[JAR3-UPG-08]` says
so precisely.

---

## Functional requirements (EARS)

Style follows `doc/spec/`'s convention: uppercase WHEN / WHILE / IF-THEN / WHERE, SHALL
for the obligation. Ids are epic-scoped (`[JAR3-…]`) and do not occupy the normative
`[NN-SLUG-nn]` namespace. Each cites the normative statement it makes true; spec 53 and
51 carry decided prose with no EARS ids (verified — zero `[NN-SLUG-nn]` in either), so
those citations are section-anchored.

### Descriptor form and discovery — ubiquitous

`[JAR3-DESC-01]` A module jar SHALL be able to carry exactly one deployment descriptor,
discovered as a resource through the module's own `ModuleClassLoader`. *(51 §Graph
construction DSL — `GraphSpec` is graphs-as-data; `[JAR1-DISC-02]`'s scoped-discovery
rule.)*

`[JAR3-DESC-02]` The deployment descriptor SHALL be a declarative document naming cell
FQNs, handles, identity bindings, instance data, and links, and SHALL NOT contain a
serialized `CellFactory`, lambda, or any other implementation-bound object.
*(`GraphDsl.kt:27` — `CellFactory` instances are lambdas whose serialized identity is not
stable across recompiles; 93 I-21's "no lambdas/handles on the wire" principle, P9.)*

`[JAR3-DESC-03]` The descriptor SHALL declare its own format version, distinct from the
module's `ModuleVersion`. *(Two independently-evolving things need two version fields;
JAR2 `[JAR2-VER-04]` owns the module one.)*

`[JAR3-DESC-04]` IF a descriptor declares a format version the reader does not support,
THEN the deploy SHALL be refused with a diagnostic naming both versions, and nothing SHALL
be spawned.

`[JAR3-DESC-05]` A module without a deployment descriptor SHALL remain loadable and
usable. *(`[JAR1-DISC-05]`'s library-only-module rule: a descriptor is optional, not a
new precondition for being a module.)*

`[JAR3-DESC-06]` Every field of the descriptor SHALL correspond to an existing
`GraphStep`, `IdentityBinding`, or `InstanceSpec` field, and the descriptor SHALL NOT
introduce a topology concept absent from `GraphSpec`. *(51: "the DSL gains parameters, not
verbs"; 53's guardrail that a deployment feature needing a new kernel mechanism is a
design-review trigger, `:80-83`.)*

### Resolution and deploy — event-driven

`[JAR3-DEP-01]` WHEN a descriptor is resolved, each declared `cellFqn` SHALL be resolved
to a `CellFactory` via `ModuleHandle.cellFactory(fqn)` on the module that carried the
descriptor. *(`[JAR1-SPAWN-01]`; the `ModuleHandle` surface JAR1 built for this purpose.)*

`[JAR3-DEP-02]` WHEN a descriptor is resolved, the resolver SHALL produce an ordinary
`GraphSpec` and SHALL apply it through the existing `applyTo`/`applyRemote` paths.
*(51 §Graph construction DSL; `GraphDsl.kt:251,292`. A second apply path would fork the
semantics the kernel already fixed.)*

`[JAR3-DEP-03]` WHEN a descriptor declares an `InstanceSetStep`-shaped entry, the resolver
SHALL lower it through the existing `InstanceSetStep.lower()` and SHALL let
`InstanceSetStep.validate()`'s refusals fire unchanged. *(`GraphDsl.kt:153-189`: a
SINGLETON cell partitioned, or a DURABLE cell declared journal-less, is already refused on
a named axis; re-implementing that check would let the two disagree.)*

`[JAR3-DEP-04]` The whole descriptor SHALL be validated before any spawn is attempted:
every `cellFqn` resolvable, every link endpoint a declared handle, every `requires`
satisfied, the format version supported. *(`[JAR1-REG-01]`'s validate-then-commit
discipline, applied one level up; 53 PRECHECK's "freely abortable" principle,
`53-evolution.md:115-122`.)*

`[JAR3-DEP-05]` WHEN a deploy completes, it SHALL return a report giving, per declared
handle and per declared link, either the applied `CellRef`/link or a named rejection.
*(`[15-APPLY-01]`; `ApplyReport`, `GraphDsl.kt:221`.)*

`[JAR3-DEP-06]` WHEN a descriptor declares a `requires` on another module, the deploy
SHALL check that module is loaded at a `ModuleVersion` satisfying the declared range, and
SHALL resolve that module's cell FQNs through *its* `ModuleHandle`. *(JAR2
`[JAR2-VER-04]`, `[JAR2-MOD-02]`; `[JAR1-ISO-04]` — a cross-module FQN must not resolve
through the wrong loader.)*

### Unwanted behaviour — deploy

`[JAR3-BAD-01]` IF a descriptor names a cell FQN the module does not provide, THEN the
deploy SHALL be refused before any cell is spawned, with a diagnostic naming the FQN and
the module. *(`[JAR1-SPAWN-05]`; a deploy that spawns half a graph and then discovers a
missing class leaves an unowned partial topology nobody planned to clean up.)*

`[JAR3-BAD-02]` IF a descriptor names a contract the jar does not provide — a link whose
endpoints' ports carry a `contractId` absent from the registry, or present under a
different `shapeVersion` — THEN the deploy SHALL be refused before any cell is spawned,
naming the contract FQN. *(JAR2 `[JAR2-COEX-04/05]`; `[12-CARD-01]`/link-time policy, 13.
This is the "deploy of a `GraphSpec` referencing a contract the jar does not provide"
case, and the refusal must be pre-spawn, not a link rejection three steps in.)*

`[JAR3-BAD-03]` IF a declared link's endpoints are structurally incompatible, THEN the
link SHALL be rejected by the ordinary link-time handshake and SHALL be reported as a
rejection, and the deploy SHALL NOT suppress or retry it. *(`[13-LINK-01]`; JAR3 does not
get its own linking semantics.)*

`[JAR3-BAD-04]` IF a deploy is refused at validation, THEN no cell SHALL have been
spawned, no link SHALL have been made, and the module SHALL remain loaded and unloadable.
*(`[JAR1-UNL-02]` — a partially deployed graph would pin the module as un-unloadable with
no record of why.)*

`[JAR3-BAD-05]` IF a deploy partially succeeds under `applyRemote`'s partial+report
semantics, THEN the report SHALL name every rejected step, and the deploy SHALL NOT claim
success. *(`[15-APPLY-01]`; `GraphDsl.kt:280-291` — partial apply is the decided
behaviour, silent partial success is not.)*

`[JAR3-BAD-06]` The deployer SHALL NOT expose a network-reachable deploy endpoint.
*(`[JAR1-SEC-03]` verbatim: an upload-a-jar-and-run-it surface is remote code execution
and belongs behind 53 §Trust boundary's still-open G-50 authority half,
`53-evolution.md:282-290`. WKB2 owns that decision; it must not arrive incidentally
here.)*

### Upgrade — event-driven

`[JAR3-UPG-01]` WHEN an upgrade is requested between two loaded module versions, the
system SHALL compute a plan by matching descriptor entries **by handle**, classifying each
as added, removed, promoted, relinked, or unchanged. *(53 §Model — "Deployments are
incremental graph operations"; the handle is the descriptor's stable identity, matching
`GraphSpec`'s own spec-local handles, `GraphDsl.kt:73`.)*

`[JAR3-UPG-02]` WHEN a handle's cell FQN or module version changes between descriptors,
the plan SHALL classify it as a promotion and SHALL execute it through
`Promotion.promote` with JAR2's migration chain. *(53 §The promotion swap; JAR2
`[JAR2-MIG-02/04]`. Despawn-and-respawn as a substitute for promotion would discard the
cell's state and break source continuity, `[22-SRC-01]`.)*

`[JAR3-UPG-03]` WHEN a promoted handle's candidate is spawned, it SHALL be spawned under
`IdentityBinding.NewInstanceOf(incumbentLogicalId)`. *(53 §"The graphs-as-data cut": the
candidate spawns as a fresh instance of the incumbent's logical cell, `:85-89`;
`GraphDsl.kt:47`.)*

`[JAR3-UPG-04]` The entire upgrade plan SHALL be validated before any action executes,
including a dry run of each promotion's PRECHECK conditions. *(53 PRECHECK "no side
effects, freely abortable", `:115-122`; JAR2 `[JAR2-MIG-04]`. Discovering a missing
migration chain after three cells have already swapped is the failure this requirement
exists to prevent.)*

`[JAR3-UPG-05]` WHEN an upgrade plan executes, additions SHALL be applied before
promotions, promotions before relinks, and removals last. *(A removal before its
replacement is linked is an observable topology hole; `[13-NOLOSS-01]` — messages accepted
before an unlink must be delivered or parked.)*

`[JAR3-UPG-06]` WHEN an upgrade completes, it SHALL report per handle the action taken,
and for each promoted handle the resolved migration chain and the retained
`RollbackCheckpoint`. *(JAR2 `[JAR2-OBS-02]`, `[JAR2-RB-01]`.)*

`[JAR3-UPG-07]` WHERE a handle is classified `Unchanged`, the upgrade SHALL NOT despawn,
respawn, relink, or promote its cell. *(53 §Model: deployments are *incremental* graph
operations; a full-graph reapply is the binary-release model wearing a costume.)*

`[JAR3-UPG-08]` The system SHALL support rolling back an individual promoted handle
through JAR2's `RollbackCheckpoint`, and SHALL NOT claim to roll back a multi-handle
upgrade as one transaction. *(Compensating rollback of a successful prefix is
research-gated, 95 §R4, `15-lifecycle.md:76-78`; JAR2 `[JAR2-RB-03]` is the per-cell claim
that can be made honestly.)*

### Unwanted behaviour — upgrade

`[JAR3-BAD-07]` IF any promotion in an upgrade plan would fail PRECHECK — missing
migration chain, schema-version gap, downgrade, hidden-state cell, `shapeVersion`
mismatch — THEN the whole upgrade SHALL be refused at validation and no action SHALL
execute. *(JAR2 `[JAR2-MIG-04]`, `[JAR2-BAD-03/04]`, `[JAR2-MIG-06]`.)*

`[JAR3-BAD-08]` IF a promotion fails during execution, THEN that promotion SHALL roll
back per JAR2 `[JAR2-BAD-01]`, the upgrade SHALL halt without executing further actions,
and the report SHALL name the executed prefix, the failed action, and the unexecuted
remainder. *(53 §Rollback, `:144-150`; `[15-APPLY-01]`'s leave-and-report contract. A
silent halt leaves an operator with no way to know what state the graph is in.)*

`[JAR3-BAD-09]` IF the new descriptor removes a handle whose cell holds `Owned` or
`Leased` state, THEN the removal SHALL discharge those payloads explicitly.
*(`[12-EXCL-01]`; AGENTS.md core invariant — no failure, suppression, shadow, park, or
dead-letter path may silently drop an exclusive payload. A despawn driven by a config
diff is exactly the path nobody thinks to check.)*

`[JAR3-BAD-10]` IF two loaded module versions' descriptors declare the same handle with
incompatible link endpoints, THEN the upgrade SHALL be refused at validation naming the
handle and both endpoint sets. *(`[13-REBIND-02]`: a rebind requires a matching
`(portName, contractId)`, else `Rejected` — refusing at plan time makes it a diagnosable
config error instead of a mid-swap rejection.)*

`[JAR3-BAD-11]` The upgrade SHALL NOT unload the old module while any of its cells remain
live, and SHALL NOT make unloading a precondition of the upgrade. *(`[JAR1-UNL-01/02]`;
JAR2 `[JAR2-MOD-04]` additionally pins the module while a `RollbackCheckpoint` lives — an
upgrade that unloads eagerly destroys its own rollback.)*

### Optional-feature and state-driven

`[JAR3-OPT-01]` WHERE a descriptor is generated at build time from an annotated
declaration, the generated document SHALL be byte-identical to a hand-written one
declaring the same graph. *(51's "parameters, not verbs" equality check, mirroring
`InstanceCellFactory`'s data-class rationale, `GraphDsl.kt:120-129`.)*

`[JAR3-OPT-02]` WHILE an upgrade is executing, the host SHALL remain able to report which
plan is in flight and which actions have completed. *(WKB2/WKB3 render this; an
unobservable in-flight upgrade cannot be supervised.)*

### Honest non-requirements

- *"An upgrade shall be atomic."* False, and stating it would be vacuous: partial-apply
  atomicity is research-gated (95 §R4). `[JAR3-UPG-04]` makes *admission* all-or-nothing
  and `[JAR3-BAD-08]` makes execution halt-and-report; that is the honest claim.
- *"A deploy shall roll back on failure."* Same reason. Per-handle rollback via JAR2 is
  the claim (`[JAR3-UPG-08]`); a whole-graph compensating rollback is not.
- *"A descriptor shall be forward-compatible."* Not verifiable against formats that do
  not exist. `[JAR3-DESC-03/04]` require an explicit version and a loud refusal instead.
- *"Deploying a module is safe."* A loaded jar runs with the host's full privileges
  (`[JAR1-SEC-01]`). JAR3 changes nothing about that and `[JAR3-BAD-06]` keeps it from
  acquiring a network surface.
- *"Two module versions of the same contract can be deployed side by side."* Refused by
  JAR2 `[JAR2-COEX-04/06]` as a permanent constraint of the ids-only wire, not a deferral.

## Behaviour specifications (Given / When / Then)

### B1 — Deploy a self-describing jar

```
Given a module jar carrying a deployment descriptor declaring two cells and one link
When the module is loaded and deployed
Then both cells are spawned from the module's own CellFactorys
  And the link is established
  And a delta applied at the upstream cell reaches the downstream cell with the same
      wave/tag continuity as an equivalent hand-built graph
  And the report names both handles as applied
```
Covers `[JAR3-DESC-01]`, `[JAR3-DEP-01]`, `[JAR3-DEP-02]`, `[JAR3-DEP-05]`.

### B2 — The descriptor survives a rebuild

```
Given a module jar with a descriptor, deployed successfully
When the module's source is recompiled unchanged and the jar rebuilt
Then the descriptor is byte-identical
  And the rebuilt jar deploys to an identical topology
```
This is the scenario that justifies the declarative format: the same test written against
a serialized `GraphSpec` fails, because `SpawnStep.factory` is a lambda. Worth asserting
explicitly — including, once, that a serialized-`GraphSpec` descriptor *would* fail, so
the decision is documented by a test rather than by prose. Covers `[JAR3-DESC-02]`.

### B3 — Deploy of a `GraphSpec` referencing a contract the jar does not provide

```
Given a module jar whose descriptor declares a link between a cell it provides and a
      port whose contract FQN is not in the module's ContractModule and not registered
      by any loaded module
When the deploy is attempted
Then the deploy is refused at validation, naming the contract FQN
  And no cell was spawned and no link was made
  And the module remains loaded and can be unloaded cleanly
And the variant where the contract IS registered but under a different shapeVersion is
    refused with a version diagnostic naming both shapeVersions
And the variant where a declared cellFqn is absent from the module is refused naming
    the FQN and the module
```
The pre-spawn clause is the load-bearing one: a naive resolver discovers this at
`connect` time, three steps into an apply, leaving orphan cells. Covers `[JAR3-BAD-01]`,
`[JAR3-BAD-02]`, `[JAR3-BAD-04]`, `[JAR3-DEP-04]`.

### B4 — Cross-module deploy

```
Given module A providing contract C and a cell, and module B whose descriptor declares
      a cell linking to A's, with requires: A >= 1.0
When A@1.0 and B are loaded and B is deployed
Then B's cells resolve through B's ModuleHandle and A's through A's
  And the cross-module link is established
When instead only A@0.9 is loaded
Then B's deploy is refused naming the unsatisfied requirement
```
Covers `[JAR3-DEP-06]`, `[JAR3-BAD-02]`.

### B5 — An instance-set declaration keeps the kernel's own refusals

```
Given a descriptor declaring an instance set over a SINGLETON cell with non-Total
      interests
When the deploy is attempted
Then it is refused on the INSTANCE_SCOPING axis with the message
     InstanceSetStep.validate() already produces
And the DURABLE-cell-with-null-journalId variant is refused on the DURABLE nature
```
Asserting the *existing* message proves JAR3 delegated rather than re-implemented.
Covers `[JAR3-DEP-03]`, `[JAR3-DESC-06]`.

### B6 — Upgrade: the happy path, one changed cell

```
Given module M@1.0 deployed, with handles a, b, c and links a->b->c
  And module M@2.0 whose descriptor is identical except that handle b names a cell
      class at schemaVersion 2 with a declared v1->v2 transform
When the upgrade is executed
Then the plan classifies a and c Unchanged and b Promoted
  And a and c are neither despawned, respawned, relinked, nor promoted
  And b's candidate is spawned under NewInstanceOf(b's logicalId)
  And b is promoted through Promotion.promote with the v1->v2 chain
  And downstream (c) observes no glitch and a continuous (sourceId, highWater)
  And the report names the resolved chain and the retained RollbackCheckpoint
```
Covers `[JAR3-UPG-01]`, `[JAR3-UPG-02]`, `[JAR3-UPG-03]`, `[JAR3-UPG-06]`,
`[JAR3-UPG-07]`.

### B7 — Upgrade refused wholesale for one bad promotion

```
Given a deployed M@1.0 with five handles
  And M@2.0 changing three of them, one of which has a schemaVersion gap with no chain
When the upgrade is requested
Then the upgrade is refused at validation, naming the offending handle and the missing
     version step
  And NONE of the other two promotions executed
  And no cell was added, removed, relinked or promoted
  And the deployed graph is byte-identical in topology to before the request
And the same holds for a downgrade, a hidden-state candidate, and a shapeVersion mismatch
```
This is JAR3's central claim and the reason `[JAR3-UPG-04]` demands a dry-run PRECHECK
per promotion. Covers `[JAR3-BAD-07]`, `[JAR3-UPG-04]`.

### B8 — A promotion fails mid-upgrade

```
Given an upgrade plan with three promotions that passed validation
  And the second promotion's migration transform throws during COMMIT
When the upgrade executes
Then the first promotion is complete and its cell is live on the candidate
  And the second promotion rolled back per JAR2: incumbent retained, gate re-greened,
      incumbent not despawned, candidate state unchanged
  And the third promotion did NOT execute
  And the report names the executed prefix, the failed action, and the unexecuted remainder
  And no whole-upgrade rollback is claimed or attempted
When the operator then rolls back the first promoted handle individually
Then it succeeds through its RollbackCheckpoint
```
The "no whole-upgrade rollback is claimed" assertion is what keeps the epic inside 95 §R4.
Covers `[JAR3-BAD-08]`, `[JAR3-UPG-08]`.

### B9 — Ordering: additions, promotions, relinks, removals

```
Given an upgrade adding handle d, promoting b, relinking a->d->c, and removing e
When the upgrade executes
Then d is spawned before any relink names it
  And e is despawned only after every link naming it has been re-pointed
  And no delta accepted by a link before its unlink is dropped or dead-lettered
```
Covers `[JAR3-UPG-05]`, and asserts `[13-NOLOSS-01]` across the reconfiguration.

### B10 — Removing a handle holding exclusive state

```
Given a deployed graph where handle e's cell holds an Owned payload
  And an upgrade whose descriptor removes handle e
When the upgrade executes
Then e's Owned payload is explicitly discharged and the discharge is observable
  And it is not dropped, finalized, or left to GC
```
Covers `[JAR3-BAD-09]`.

### B11 — Incompatible handle across versions

```
Given M@1.0's handle b exposing outlet "out" on contract C
  And M@2.0's handle b exposing outlet "out" on a different contract D
When the upgrade is requested
Then it is refused at validation, naming handle b and both (portName, contractId) sets
  And nothing executed
```
A contract change is not a promotion (53 §G-33 invariance line) — this is where that rule
meets a config diff. Covers `[JAR3-BAD-10]`, `[JAR3-UPG-04]`.

### B12 — The old module stays pinned

```
Given a completed upgrade from M@1.0 to M@2.0 with RollbackCheckpoints retained
When unload of M@1.0 is requested
Then it is refused while the checkpoints are within their horizon
  And the upgrade never attempted the unload itself
```
Covers `[JAR3-BAD-11]`, and connects to JAR2 `[JAR2-MOD-04]`.

### B13 — Descriptor format version refusal

```
Given a jar whose descriptor declares a format version the reader does not support
When the deploy is attempted
Then it is refused naming both versions, and nothing was spawned
And a jar with no descriptor at all loads successfully and is usable
```
Covers `[JAR3-DESC-03]`, `[JAR3-DESC-04]`, `[JAR3-DESC-05]`.

### Concord corpus note

**None of B1–B13 belongs in `concord/corpus/`, and this is a considered conclusion, not
an omission.** The corpus is graph/script/checks documents driven through the fixed cell
catalog in `concord/schema/cell-catalog.md`, and only `civictech.concord.driver.kernel`
may import `civictech.cell.*`. JAR3's entire subject — jars, manifests, descriptors,
module versions, deploy and upgrade commands — is *hosting and packaging*, with no
dataflow-semantic vocabulary in the schema. Adding deploy verbs would be a schema change,
which `concord/schema/*.md` gates deliberately as single-writer.

The *semantic* claims JAR3 makes are not its own: B6's glitch-freedom and source
continuity across a swap belong to JAR2/`Promotion` and are covered there (JAR2 B9,
`[22-GF-01]`/`[22-SRC-01]`); B9's no-loss-across-reconfiguration is `[13-NOLOSS-01]`,
whose home is the link/topology corpus area, not a deploy scenario. JAR3 asserts them as
`:loader` integration tests because what JAR3 adds is the *orchestration*, and the
orchestration is what the corpus cannot see.

If, during the epic, B9's no-loss claim turns out to be expressible through existing
corpus verbs by modelling the reconfiguration as ordinary link surgery, it should carry
`covers: [13-NOLOSS-01]` rather than a JAR3-local id. If it cannot be checked honestly
in either place, it goes in `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` — never substituted with an
easier scenario.
