## 5. Functional requirements (EARS)

Ids are epic-scoped (`[TTD2-nn]`) and deliberately do not collide with normative `doc/spec/` ids
(`[NN-SLUG-nn]`) or with `[TTD1-nn]`. Where a requirement is the UI-side realization of a TTD1
requirement, the `[TTD1-nn]` id is cited. Vocabulary: "the replay service" = `:inspect`'s replay
session layer; "the scrubber" = `inspect/ui`'s timeline control; "the UI" = `inspect/ui` as a whole;
"a state pane" = any pane rendering a cell's value (detail panel, value view, state pages, canvas
value badges, tooltips); "a session" = one open replay session.

### A. Journal sources and sessions

- `[TTD2-01]` The replay service shall expose the set of journal sources the host process was
  configured with, each carrying its graph-source verdict (`graphSpec`, `structureLog`, or `none`).
  (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD2-02]` The replay service shall open a session over a named source and return its id, its
  timeline length, the journal record count observed at open, and the run-level fidelity verdict
  (`[TTD1-37]`). (Event-driven)
- `[TTD2-03]` The replay service shall determine a source's graph-source verdict without performing
  a reconstruction, so that listing sources spawns no host. (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD2-04]` If a requested source path is not a readable journal, then the replay service shall
  answer `400` naming the path and the reason and shall not open a session. (Unwanted behaviour;
  UI side of `[TTD1-50]`)
- `[TTD2-05]` The replay service shall bound the number of concurrently open sessions and shall
  expire an idle session after a fixed TTL, releasing its sandbox host. (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD2-06]` If a request names an unknown, closed or expired session, then the replay service
  shall answer `410` and the UI shall drop the session and return to the source list rather than
  retrying. (Unwanted behaviour)
- `[TTD2-07]` When a session is closed or expires, the replay service shall shut down its sandbox
  host such that no scheduler thread, cell or link outlives it. (Event-driven; UI side of
  `[TTD1-15]`'s "no host outlives the call")
- `[TTD2-08]` The UI shall present the mode of the current view as exactly one of `live`, `replay`
  or `records-only` at all times, in persistent chrome that is visible without scrolling.
  (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD2-09]` While the UI is in `replay` or `records-only` mode, it shall not apply any live SSE
  event to any pane it is rendering. (State-driven)
- `[TTD2-10]` The UI shall encode the active session and position in the URL hash such that a
  reloaded or shared link restores the same position, and shall parse a hash written before TTD2
  unchanged. (Ubiquitous)

### B. The timeline and scrubbing

- `[TTD2-11]` The scrubber shall address positions using TTD1's `RunTimeline` positions and shall
  display, for the current position, its record index and its wave coordinate `(sourceId, counter)`
  when the record carries one. (Ubiquitous; `[TTD1-15]`)
- `[TTD2-12]` Where a position's record carries no `MessageContext`, the scrubber shall display it by
  record index alone and shall not display a synthesized wave coordinate. (Optional feature;
  `[TTD1-17]`)
- `[TTD2-13]` The scrubber shall mark every checkpoint anchor on the timeline. (Ubiquitous;
  `[TTD1-19]`)
- `[TTD2-14]` When the user moves the scrubber forward, the replay service shall advance the
  session's existing reconstruction rather than rebuilding the graph. (Event-driven; `[TTD1-30]`)
- `[TTD2-15]` When the user moves the scrubber backward, the replay service shall restart from the
  nearest preceding anchor, and the UI shall indicate that the position is being recomputed rather
  than appearing frozen. (Event-driven; `[TTD1-31]`)
- `[TTD2-16]` While a position request is in flight, the UI shall not display the previous position's
  values as if they were the requested position's. (State-driven — one of the three
  `[TTD1-34]`-defeating renderings)
- `[TTD2-17]` If the user moves the scrubber again while a position request is in flight, then the UI
  shall render the newest requested position and shall discard superseded responses rather than
  applying them out of order. (Unwanted behaviour)
- `[TTD2-18]` The scrubber shall support stepping one position at a time by keyboard as well as by
  drag. (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD2-19]` The UI shall let the user jump to a position by record index and by per-source frontier
  cut. (Optional feature; `[TTD1-18]`)
- `[TTD2-20]` The UI shall offer a return-to-live action from any replay position, and taking it
  shall restore the live SSE-driven view without a page reload. (Ubiquitous)

### C. Fidelity — the honesty requirements

- `[TTD2-21]` The UI shall display the fidelity verdict attached to every reconstructed cell state it
  renders. (Ubiquitous; `[TTD1-33]`)
- `[TTD2-22]` **If a cell's fidelity verdict is `UNRECONSTRUCTIBLE`, then every state pane shall
  render the verdict and its machine-readable reasons in place of a value, and shall render no value,
  no empty value, no zero, no placeholder and no previously fetched value for that cell.**
  (Unwanted behaviour — the epic's central requirement; UI realization of `[TTD1-34]`)
- `[TTD2-23]` If a response carries `kind = "unavailable"` with `unreadable = "unreconstructible"`,
  then the UI shall treat the absence of `value` as the answer and shall not substitute a default.
  (Unwanted behaviour; `[TTD1-34]`)
- `[TTD2-24]` The UI shall visually distinguish `DEGRADED` from `FAITHFUL` state wherever a value is
  shown, so that a degraded value is never presented with the same confidence as a faithful one.
  (Ubiquitous; `[TTD1-33]`, `[TTD1-38]`)
- `[TTD2-25]` The UI shall render each fidelity reason as its own named, human-readable explanation
  and shall render an unrecognized reason code verbatim rather than dropping it. (Ubiquitous;
  forward-compatibility, mirroring `CellState.UNKNOWN`)
- `[TTD2-26]` The canvas shall mark every node whose cell is `UNRECONSTRUCTIBLE` at the current
  position, so the unreconstructible region of the graph is visible without opening each cell.
  (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD2-27]` The UI shall display the run-level fidelity verdict for the session, and that verdict
  shall be no better than the worst per-cell verdict shown. (Ubiquitous; `[TTD1-37]`)
- `[TTD2-28]` If the journal was torn, held an unknown record, or held an undeserializable checkpoint
  at or before the current position, then the UI shall show that the whole position is at most
  `DEGRADED` and shall name which of the three occurred. (Unwanted behaviour; `[TTD1-36]`,
  `[TTD1-11]`)
- `[TTD2-29]` If a reconstruction reports `GRAPH_MISMATCH` for a cell ref, then the UI shall name the
  ref and shall not omit it from the graph view. (Unwanted behaviour; `[TTD1-24]`)
- `[TTD2-30]` The UI shall label a value read from a reconstruction with the `reconstructed`
  provenance and shall never label it `live`, `liveSuspended` or `checkpoint`. (Ubiquitous)

### D. No graph source — records-only mode

- `[TTD2-31]` If a session's source has no graph source, then the replay service shall open the
  session in records-only mode, answer timeline, record and record-level-diff requests, and refuse
  every state or topology request with an explicit no-topology reason. (Unwanted behaviour;
  `[TTD1-23]`)
- `[TTD2-32]` While in records-only mode, the UI shall render a dedicated notice stating that the
  journal carries no topology, that the graph is rebuilt out-of-band, and which two graph sources
  would enable state reconstruction. (State-driven)
- `[TTD2-33]` While in records-only mode, the UI shall render no graph canvas and no state pane at
  all, rather than rendering them empty. (State-driven)
- `[TTD2-34]` While in records-only mode, the UI shall keep the timeline, the record inspector and
  the record-level run diff fully functional. (State-driven)
- `[TTD2-35]` The record inspector shall show, for a frame record, its `cellRef`, `portName`, type,
  contract and method ids, and wave coordinate, and shall show decoded arguments only when the
  reader decoded them. (Ubiquitous; `[TTD1-03]`, `[TTD1-04]`)
- `[TTD2-36]` If a frame was read at structural fidelity only (`NO_DESCRIPTOR`) or its wire version
  mismatched (`WIRE_VERSION_MISMATCH`), then the record inspector shall say so on that record rather
  than showing an empty argument list. (Unwanted behaviour; `[TTD1-05]`, `[TTD1-06]`)

### E. Scrubbing a run that is still being written

- `[TTD2-37]` The replay service shall pin a session to the journal length observed when the session
  opened, so that every position in that session is answered from one fixed prefix. (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD2-38]` If the underlying journal has grown since a session opened, then the UI shall indicate
  that the live run has advanced beyond the session's history and shall offer an explicit refresh
  that opens a new session. (Unwanted behaviour)
- `[TTD2-39]` The UI shall never extend an open session's timeline in place while the user is
  scrubbing it. (Unwanted behaviour)
- `[TTD2-40]` While a session is open over the live process's own journal, the replay service shall
  neither block, delay, nor alter the live host's journal writes. (State-driven; `[TTD1-12]`)
- `[TTD2-41]` If the underlying journal was compacted (reset to a checkpoint) beneath an open
  session, then the replay service shall report the session as stale and shall not present a
  half-read history. (Unwanted behaviour; `COMPACTED_AWAY`)

### F. Large journals

- `[TTD2-42]` The replay service shall serve the timeline in bounded pages with an opaque, single-use
  cursor, answering `410` for an unknown, expired or wrong-session cursor. (Ubiquitous; the
  `StatePageView`/`CursorTable` discipline)
- `[TTD2-43]` The scrubber shall render a timeline of any length without holding every position in
  the client, loading only the window it displays plus a bounded margin. (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD2-44]` The replay service shall serve a reconstructed cell's state through the same bounded
  paged-read contract the live pane uses, including the applied limit, the entries count and the
  owned/leased presence count. (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD2-45]` If a position cannot be reconstructed within the server's bounded wait, then the
  response shall be `unavailable` with the reason and the UI shall show that the read did not land,
  not an empty state. (Unwanted behaviour; the existing `unanswered` vocabulary)
- `[TTD2-46]` The UI shall coalesce positions requested during a continuous drag so that a drag
  across N positions issues fewer than N reconstruction requests. (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD2-47]` The replay service shall bound the memory a session holds and shall answer with an
  explicit refusal, not an unbounded allocation, when a journal exceeds that bound. (Unwanted
  behaviour)

### G. Run diff

- `[TTD2-48]` The UI shall let the user select two open sessions and render TTD1's `RunDiffReport`
  for them. (Ubiquitous; `[TTD1-39]`)
- `[TTD2-49]` The diff view shall show the aligned prefix length, the first divergent position in
  each run, and the divergence classification. (Ubiquitous; `[TTD1-41]`)
- `[TTD2-50]` When both runs reconstruct, the diff view shall show the per-cell state difference at
  the first divergent position. (Event-driven; `[TTD1-42]`)
- `[TTD2-51]` If the two runs are not wave-alignable, then the diff view shall say so explicitly and
  shall label the fallback as record-index alignment, never presenting it as a wave alignment.
  (Unwanted behaviour; `[TTD1-43]`)
- `[TTD2-52]` If either run is `UNRECONSTRUCTIBLE`, then the diff view shall render the record-level
  diff and shall render the state-level diff as unavailable with the reason. (Unwanted behaviour;
  `[TTD1-44]`)
- `[TTD2-53]` The diff view shall offer a jump from the first divergent position to that position in
  each run's scrubber. (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD2-54]` The UI shall render the diff from the server's `RunDiffReport` DTO and shall not
  compute an alignment of its own. (Ubiquitous; `[TTD1-45]`)

### H. Read-only, and checkably so

- `[TTD2-55]` The replay surface shall neither write, truncate, rename nor lock any journal file.
  (Ubiquitous; `[TTD1-12]`)
- `[TTD2-56]` No replay request shall spawn, link, unlink, suspend, resume, despawn or deliver to any
  cell in the inspected process. (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD2-57]` No replay request shall cause an externally visible side effect, because every
  reconstruction runs with `Effectful` inlets suppressed. (Ubiquitous; `[TTD1-26]`)
- `[TTD2-58]` No replay request shall advance a wave counter, a delivered watermark, or an attention
  band in the inspected process. (Ubiquitous; the P6 property `PagedState` already states)
- `[TTD2-59]` The replay surface shall add no route that mutates the inspected graph — graph editing
  and `GraphSpec` apply belong to WKB2. (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD2-60]` `:timetravel` shall not gain a dependency on `:inspect`, and `:kernel` shall gain a
  dependency on neither. (Ubiquitous; `[TTD1-53]`)

**Verifiability note.** `[TTD2-24]` ("visually distinguish") and `[TTD2-08]`/`[TTD2-26]` are the
requirements whose honest check is hardest, because "a user can tell them apart" is not assertable in
`jsdom`. They are checkable in the concrete form the implementation will take — a distinct,
named, asserted DOM class/attribute per verdict and per mode, plus a `Legend` entry — and the tests
assert those markers, not an aesthetic judgement. That is an honest weakening of *the check*, not of
the requirement, and it is stated here rather than hidden. If a later agent finds even that
uncheckable, the fact is filed as a bead (or, for any corpus-facing part, in
`concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md`) — it is not rewritten into "the UI shall attempt to distinguish".
`[TTD2-40]` ("neither block, delay, nor alter") is checkable for *alter* (byte-identical journal
file, as BS-15 does for TTD1) and for *block* (the live host makes progress with a session open); a
strict no-added-latency claim is not honestly assertable in CI and is deliberately not made.

---

## 6. Behaviour specifications

Frontend scenarios become named `vitest` tests under `inspect/ui/test/` (pure stores) and
`inspect/ui/test/dom/` (rendered components, via `test/dom/harness.tsx`); backend scenarios become
named JUnit tests under `inspect/src/test/kotlin/civictech/inspect/`.

**Corpus placement, decided once for the whole epic:** none of these belong in `concord/corpus/`.
The corpus covers normative EARS ids in `doc/spec/` and is driven by `civictech.concord.driver.kernel`
— the only package permitted to import `civictech.cell.*`. There is no HTTP driver and no browser
driver, `[TTD2-nn]` ids are epic-scoped, and a `covers: [TTD2-nn]` would be a dangling id that fails
`./gradlew :concord:check`. So **no `covers:` id is claimed by any scenario below and no corpus
scenario is added**, exactly as TTD1 concluded for its own BS-7. The kernel-side properties these
scenarios rely on are already covered upstream (`concord/corpus/15-durability/DUR-REPLAY-01.yaml`,
`DUR-SNAPTAIL-01.yaml`) and are TTD1's to keep true, not TTD2's to re-cover.

### BS-1 — Scrubbing to a position that contains unreconstructible cells (**the anchor scenario**)
**Given** an open replay session over a journal whose graph contains a volatile cell
(`journalFor` returned `null`), a non-`Stateful` cell, and two ordinary reconstructible data cells,
and the UI is showing position p with all four cells rendered
**When** the user scrubs to position q, where the reconstruction reports
`UNRECONSTRUCTIBLE(VOLATILE_CELL)` and `UNRECONSTRUCTIBLE(NOT_STATEFUL)` for the first two
**Then** neither of those two cells renders a value, an empty value, a zero, a placeholder, or the
value it showed at position p; each renders its verdict and its reasons by name; the canvas marks
both nodes; the run-level verdict reads `UNRECONSTRUCTIBLE`; and the two reconstructible cells render
their own faithful values.
*Tests:* `test/dom/replay-unreconstructible.test.tsx`, `test/replayStore.test.ts`.
Covers `[TTD2-16]`, `[TTD2-21]`, `[TTD2-22]`, `[TTD2-23]`, `[TTD2-26]`, `[TTD2-27]`. UI realization
of `[TTD1-34]`.

### BS-2 — Stale value must not survive a position change
**Given** a cell rendering a value at position p
**When** the user scrubs to position q and the position-q response for that cell is `unavailable`
(for any reason: unreconstructible, unanswered, or a torn journal)
**Then** the pane never, at any render, shows position p's value labelled as position q — asserted by
driving the store through the transition and inspecting every intermediate render, not only the final
one.
*Test:* `test/dom/replay-stale-value.test.tsx`. Covers `[TTD2-16]`, `[TTD2-45]`.

### BS-3 — A journal with no structure log
**Given** a journal directory with `host.journal` and no `graph.jsonl` and no registered `GraphSpec`
**When** a session is opened over it
**Then** `GET /replay/sources` reported `graphSource: "none"` without spawning a host; the session
opens in records-only mode; the UI renders the no-topology notice naming both ways to supply a graph;
no canvas and no state pane is mounted at all; and the timeline, the record inspector and the
record-level diff all work.
*Tests:* `inspect/src/test/kotlin/civictech/inspect/ReplayNoGraphSourceTest.kt`,
`test/dom/records-only.test.tsx`. Covers `[TTD2-03]`, `[TTD2-31]`, `[TTD2-32]`, `[TTD2-33]`,
`[TTD2-34]`. UI realization of `[TTD1-23]`.

### BS-4 — Scrubbing during a live run
**Given** a live host still appending to the journal a session was opened over
**When** the user scrubs across the session's whole timeline while the host writes N further records
**Then** every position answers from the prefix pinned at open; the timeline does not grow under the
scrubber; the UI shows that the live run has advanced and offers an explicit refresh; taking the
refresh opens a *new* session whose timeline includes the N records; and the journal file's content
hash after the session closes equals what the live host wrote (the session added nothing and removed
nothing).
*Test:* `inspect/src/test/kotlin/civictech/inspect/ReplayDuringLiveRunTest.kt` (plus
`test/replayStore.test.ts` for the client-side pin). Covers `[TTD2-37]`, `[TTD2-38]`, `[TTD2-39]`,
`[TTD2-40]`, `[TTD2-55]`.

### BS-5 — Compaction beneath an open session
**Given** an open session and a live host that then checkpoints, resetting the journal to a single
checkpoint record
**When** the user requests a position the old prefix contained
**Then** the session reports itself stale with `COMPACTED_AWAY`, the UI surfaces that and offers a
new session, and no half-read history is presented as the run's past.
*Test:* `ReplayCompactedSessionTest.kt`. Covers `[TTD2-41]`.

### BS-6 — A very large journal pages instead of loading
**Given** a journal with substantially more positions than the scrubber's display window (fixture-
driven on the FE; generated on the BE)
**When** the session is opened and the user drags from one end of the timeline to the other
**Then** the timeline is fetched in bounded pages with single-use cursors; a replayed cursor answers
`410` and the client restarts the walk rather than believing it continued one; the client holds only
the displayed window plus its margin; and the drag issues strictly fewer reconstruction requests than
positions crossed.
*Tests:* `ReplayTimelinePagingTest.kt`, `test/replayPaging.test.ts`, `test/replayClient.test.ts`.
Covers `[TTD2-42]`, `[TTD2-43]`, `[TTD2-46]`.

### BS-7 — Diff view between two runs
**Given** two sessions over two journals of the same graph that diverge at one wave (TTD1's BS-11
shape)
**When** the diff view is opened for them
**Then** it renders the server's aligned prefix, the first divergent position in each run, the
divergence class, and the per-cell state delta; the jump action moves each run's scrubber to its own
divergent position; and the view computes no alignment client-side (asserted by rendering from a
fixture and mutating only the fixture).
*Tests:* `test/dom/run-diff.test.tsx`, `test/replayDiff.test.ts`. Covers `[TTD2-48]`, `[TTD2-49]`,
`[TTD2-50]`, `[TTD2-53]`, `[TTD2-54]`.

### BS-8 — Two runs that are not wave-alignable
**Given** two sessions whose runs minted disjoint `sourceId` UUIDs (the ordinary two-process case)
**When** the diff view is opened
**Then** it states that the runs are not wave-alignable, labels the alignment as record-index
alignment, and does not display wave coordinates as if they matched.
*Test:* `test/dom/run-diff-unalignable.test.tsx`. Covers `[TTD2-51]`. UI realization of `[TTD1-43]`.

### BS-9 — Torn journal at or before the current position
**Given** a session over a journal truncated mid-record
**When** the user scrubs to any position at or after the tear point's predecessor
**Then** the whole position is shown as at most `DEGRADED`, the tear is named as the reason, the last
intact record index is shown, and no cell at that position is shown as `FAITHFUL`.
*Test:* `test/dom/replay-torn-journal.test.tsx`. Covers `[TTD2-28]`. UI realization of `[TTD1-11]`,
`[TTD1-36]`.

### BS-10 — Mode is unmistakable, and returning to live works
**Given** the UI in live mode with an SSE stream applying events
**When** a session is opened, the user scrubs, and then takes return-to-live
**Then** the mode chrome reads `replay` for the whole scrubbing period; no SSE event is applied to
any pane while in replay; the hash round-trips the session and position across a reload; a
pre-TTD2 hash still parses; and return-to-live restores the live view with events applying again,
without a reload.
*Tests:* `test/dom/replay-mode.test.tsx`, `test/route.test.ts` (extended, keeping its existing
backward-compatibility case). Covers `[TTD2-08]`, `[TTD2-09]`, `[TTD2-10]`, `[TTD2-20]`.

### BS-11 — Read-only under every replay request
**Given** a live inspected process with a recorded topology, wave counters, attention state, and a
journal file hash
**When** every replay route is exercised — sources, open, timeline, topology, state, record, diff,
close — and a session is left to expire by TTL
**Then** the inspected process's topology, wave counters, delivered watermarks and attention bands
are unchanged; the journal hash is unchanged; any `Effectful` sink's external counter is unchanged;
and no sandbox scheduler thread survives session close or expiry.
*Test:* `ReplayReadOnlyTest.kt`. Covers `[TTD2-05]`, `[TTD2-07]`, `[TTD2-55]`, `[TTD2-56]`,
`[TTD2-57]`, `[TTD2-58]`.

---

## 7. Suggested feature decomposition

A list only — **no beads for these are created by this epic's filing.**

1. **Replay session model + source listing in `:inspect`** — `Replay.kt`, the TTL/bounded session
   table over TTD1's `RunTimeline`/`Reconstructor`, `GET /replay/sources`, `POST`/`DELETE`
   `/replay`. (`[TTD2-01]`–`[TTD2-07]`, `[TTD2-47]`, `[TTD2-55]`–`[TTD2-60]`; BS-3, BS-11)
2. **Position endpoints + additive DTOs** — timeline paging, topology-at-position, cell-state-at-
   position through `PagedState`/`ValueEncoder`, `CellState.fidelity`, the `reconstructed`
   provenance and the `unreconstructible` unreadable reason, and the `20-api-contract.md` additions.
   (`[TTD2-11]`–`[TTD2-15]`, `[TTD2-42]`, `[TTD2-44]`, `[TTD2-45]`)
3. **The scrubber and replay mode in `inspect/ui`** — `replayClient.ts`, `solid/replay.ts`,
   `ScrubBar`, mode chrome, hash routing, drag coalescing, return-to-live.
   (`[TTD2-08]`–`[TTD2-10]`, `[TTD2-16]`–`[TTD2-20]`, `[TTD2-43]`, `[TTD2-46]`; BS-2, BS-6, BS-10)
4. **Fidelity rendering across the panes** — the `[TTD1-34]` realization in `DetailPanel`,
   `ValueView`, `Canvas`, `Legend`, `Tooltip`, plus fixtures. (`[TTD2-21]`–`[TTD2-30]`; BS-1, BS-2,
   BS-9)
5. **Records-only mode + the record inspector** — the no-graph-source screen and per-record view.
   (`[TTD2-31]`–`[TTD2-36]`; BS-3)
6. **Live-run and compaction interaction** — session pinning, growth notice, staleness.
   (`[TTD2-37]`–`[TTD2-41]`; BS-4, BS-5)
7. **Run diff view** — session pair selection, `RunDiff` component, jump-to-divergence.
   (`[TTD2-48]`–`[TTD2-54]`; BS-7, BS-8)
8. **A demo walkthrough** — `demo/agora`'s `--journal <dir>` (which already writes `host.journal`
   beside a `graph.jsonl` structure log) scrubbed end to end in the inspector, and the same journal
   with its structure log removed to exercise records-only mode. Findings to `doc/demo-findings.md`.

---

## 8. Verification

```bash
./gradlew :inspect:test                       # replay endpoints, sessions, read-only properties
./gradlew :timetravel:test                    # TTD1 unchanged — no regression from the new consumer
./gradlew :kernel:test                        # nothing kernel-side changes; proves it
./gradlew :concord:test                       # green with NO new corpus scenario, NO CONCORDANCE.md edit
./gradlew :demo:agora:test                    # the one demo with a real FileJournal + structure log
./gradlew test                                # repository-wide gate
```

```bash
cd inspect/ui
npm ci                                        # lockfile-exact, as the ui-test job runs it
npm run typecheck                             # tsc --noEmit — a type error fails the required check
npm test                                      # vitest run — every BS-n frontend test above
npm run mock                                  # manual: the fixture-backed dev server, no JVM needed
```

`ui-test` (`npm ci` + `npm run typecheck` + `npm test` in `inspect/ui`) is one of the five required
status checks on `main`, alongside `build-test-fast`, `build-test-serial`, `concord-full` and
`agora-ui-test` (`AGENTS.md` §Branches, PRs, and auto-merge). Auto-merge is armed on every non-draft
PR, so this work stays in draft until all of them are green.

Before declaring completion: every BS-n scenario exists as a named test; no generated or build output
(`inspect/build/`, `inspect/ui/dist/`, `node_modules/`) enters the diff; `package-lock.json` changes
only if a dependency genuinely changed; and no existing FE test is re-fixtured to pass.

---

## 9. Risks / open questions

1. **The graph-source problem is the epic's biggest product risk, not a technical one.** TTD1 can
   refuse cleanly; a UI cannot make refusing feel good. Records-only mode is the mitigation, and it
   is genuinely useful (a record timeline and a record-level diff already answer "did run B get the
   input run A got?"). **Open question:** should `:inspect` standardize reading the agora-style
   `graph.jsonl` as *the* convention, or stay agnostic and take a registered `GraphSpec`?
   Recommendation: mirror TTD1's own answer — stay agnostic, read agora's format as one adapter, and
   file the standardization ask as a finding. Journaling topology is 93 I-7's decided-but-unlanded
   classification and belongs to the kernel lane.
2. **A replay session is a real `ManagedHost` inside the inspector process.** Memory and thread cost
   scale with open sessions, and the diff view wants two at once. `[TTD2-05]`/`[TTD2-47]` bound it,
   but the bounds are guesses until measured. **Open question:** is one session at a time (plus a
   second only for the diff view) the right ceiling for the first cut? Recommendation: yes — ship
   the ceiling low and raise it on evidence.
3. **Backward scrubbing is the slow direction, possibly badly so.** `[TTD1-31]` restarts from the
   nearest preceding anchor; a journal with no checkpoints means from record 0. TTD1 explicitly
   *deferred* the periodic in-memory anchor ("defer, measure, file a finding") to the point where the
   scrubber's real interaction cost is measurable — that point is this epic. **Open question:** does
   TTD2 measure and then ask TTD1 for in-memory anchors, or implement anchoring itself?
   Recommendation: measure here, file the ask against `computenet-ocv`; anchoring is reconstruction
   logic and belongs on TTD1's side of the seam.
4. **Pessimistic fidelity may make the demo look broken.** `[TTD1-35]`'s allow-list marks anything
   outside the known replay-stable kernel families `DEGRADED`, so an application's own perfectly
   deterministic cell renders as second-class. Erring this way is correct, but the UI copy has to
   explain *why* a verdict is pessimistic, or users will read a design decision as a bug.
5. **Scrubbing the live process's own journal is the most compelling demo and the most delicate
   case.** `[TTD2-37]`–`[TTD2-41]` pin, notice, and go stale rather than interleaving — but a user
   dragging a timeline that is "one refresh behind" reality is a UX problem this epic solves
   conservatively and may need to revisit.
6. **Should this run headless?** A `timetravel serve` mode — the inspector UI over a crash artifact
   with no live host in the process at all — is the highest-value follow-on and is explicitly out of
   scope (§4). The backend design above is deliberately compatible with it (replay sessions touch no
   live collaborator), so the follow-on is a main() and a wiring change, not a redesign.
7. **Contract-document ownership.** `inspect/ui/src/api/types.ts` states that
   `97-inspector-plan/20-api-contract.md` is the wire contract and that neither side edits it
   unilaterally. TTD2 adds a whole route subtree, so the contract addition must land *with* the first
   endpoint feature, not after it, or FE and BE will diverge inside one epic.
8. **Cross-host time travel.** A distributed run's history is spread across hosts with no shared
   clock. Out of scope for TTD1 and TTD2 both, and the scrubber is exactly where users will ask for
   it — expect the TTD3-shaped ask TTD1 already predicted.
design:
# TTD2 design notes

## Why `--type=epic` and not `--type=feature --parent=computenet-ocv`

The sizing rule says file as an epic only for a genuine subsystem. TTD2 is one, on four independent
grounds:

1. **It crosses a module boundary and a build toolchain boundary.** Backend work lands in `:inspect`
   (Kotlin/Gradle, new collaborator, new route subtree, additive DTOs, JUnit tests); frontend work
   lands in `inspect/ui` (npm/Vite/SolidJS, deliberately not wired into Gradle, vitest + jsdom,
   gated by the separate `ui-test` required check). No single feature spans both honestly.
2. **It introduces a new server-side resource with a lifecycle.** Replay sessions are bounded,
   TTL-expiring, hold a sandbox `ManagedHost` each, and must be reasoned about for staleness,
   compaction, memory and read-only containment. That is subsystem-shaped, not
   one-coherent-feature-shaped.
3. **The decomposition in §7 is genuinely 8 items, of which at least six are independently
   shippable and reviewable** (session model; position endpoints; scrubber; fidelity rendering;
   records-only mode; live/compaction; diff view; demo walkthrough) — several of them touching
   disjoint files.
4. **It is a different lane's deliverable from TTD1.** TTD1 is a headless library plus CLI that must
   not know about HTTP (`[TTD1-51]`); TTD2 is a product surface. Parenting TTD2 under
   `computenet-ocv` would make the epic's own scope boundary ("no `:inspect` routes, no `inspect/ui`
   changes, no SSE — that is TTD2") a boundary inside itself.

The milestone plan agrees: TTD1 and TTD2 are two chunks with a hard dependency edge, not one chunk
with a tail.

## Key design decisions carried into the requirements

**D1 — Reuse the inspector's existing "which nothing is this" vocabulary rather than forking it.**
`CellState.kind = "unavailable"` + `unreadable = <reason>` already exists precisely to prevent a
client from reading an absence as a value. `[TTD1-34]`'s no-value guarantee maps onto it exactly:
`kind = "unavailable"`, `unreadable = "unreconstructible"`, `value` absent, reasons in the new
`fidelity` field. The frontend's existing `unavailable` rendering path is therefore the *default*
path for the honesty case, which is the strongest possible structural defence against
`[TTD2-22]`/`[TTD2-23]` regressing later.

**D2 — `fidelity` is additive and null on live responses.** Per `98-inspector-v4-plan/10-design-notes.md`
binding constraint 8, an older client decoding a newer server and vice versa must both work. Nothing
about the live panes changes; a `fidelity` field a pre-TTD2 client ignores costs it nothing.

**D3 — A new `reconstructed` provenance, not a reuse of `checkpoint`.** `CellState.provenance`'s KDoc
is explicit that the field exists to make one distinction sharply. A replayed value is not a live
read, not a suspended-cell read, and not a DRAINED host's retained blob. Reusing `checkpoint` because
"it is also stale" would blur exactly what the field is for.

**D4 — Replay is pull-only; no new SSE event kind.** The live path is snapshot-then-seq over
`EVENTS_PATH`; a replayed view must never have a live event applied to it (`[TTD2-09]`). Keeping
replay entirely off the SSE stream makes that a structural property rather than a filtering rule.

**D5 — One `REPLAY_PATH` context, dispatched on method + tail.** `CELL_PATH` already does this for
the `/cell/{ref}`, `/cell/{ref}/state`, `/cell/{ref}/observe` subtree because the JDK http server
matches by longest path prefix; `InspectorServer.GRAPH_PATH`'s KDoc states the discipline once for
the whole module. A single non-colliding `replay` context avoids repeating the
`GRAPHS_PATH`/`GRAPH_PATH` length-and-order trap.

**D6 — Sessions are pinned at open, never extended in place.** The alternative (a live-tailing
session) makes the timeline move under the user's cursor and makes every position ambiguous about
which prefix produced it. Pin + explicit refresh is the conservative, honest choice, and it makes
`[TTD2-37]`–`[TTD2-39]` testable.

**D7 — The cursor discipline is copied from `PagedState`/`CursorTable`, not reinvented.**
Server-minted opaque ids, single-use, `410` on stale/unknown/wrong-owner, TTL expiry rather than
pinning. Its KDoc's own words — a silent restart would "let a client believe it was continuing a walk
it was not, which is the class of lie this whole contract exists to prevent" — are the same lie class
`[TTD1-34]` is about, at a different layer.

**D8 — Records-only is a mode, not a degraded main screen.** `ColdScreen` is the precedent: a whole
screen that says what is not being shown and why, rather than a live screen with holes in it.
`[TTD2-33]` forbids mounting an empty canvas or an empty state pane, because an empty pane is
indistinguishable from a pane showing an empty graph.

## What must NOT be built here

- Any reimplementation of TTD1's reader, `RunTimeline`, `Reconstructor`, `Fidelity` or `RunDiff`. A
  need for a position, prefix, verdict or alignment TTD1 does not expose is a TTD1 API gap filed
  against `computenet-ocv`.
- Any write path against the inspected graph. Graph create/edit and `GraphSpec` apply via
  `Promotion` are WKB2 (`WKB1 --> WKB2` in the plan DAG). `[TTD2-59]` states it normatively.
- Any journal format, record type or `WireCodec.VERSION` change (`[TTD1-52]`).
- Any restructuring of the merged inspector-v4 wave 1–6 surface, or work that collides with waves
  7–11 still in flight (V1C bounded read behind the V1C-BENCH gate, V4-PEERID, V4-PILOT). TTD2
  consumes `ManagedHost.readState`/`PagedState` as merged and does not fork them.

## Dependency wiring recorded normatively

- **TTD2 depends on TTD1 (`computenet-ocv`)** — wired as a `blocks` edge.
- **WKB1 is delivered external work** (inspector-v4 waves 1–6, merged). No bead exists for it and
  none is filed; the plan's `WKB1 --> TTD2` edge is satisfied by code already on `main`. The
  components this epic extends by name are `InspectorServer`, `PagedState`, `ValueEncoder`, `Dto`
  (`CellState`, `StatePageView`, `TopologySnapshot`), `Canvas`, `DetailPanel`, `ValueView`,
  `ColdScreen`, `Legend`, `Tooltip`, `nav/route.ts`, `sync/client.ts` and `solid/state.ts`.
- **TTD2 does not block WKB2**, and WKB2 does not block TTD2; they share the inspector surface and
  should avoid landing conflicting changes to `InspectorServer`'s route registration in the same
  window.

title: SOC3 — Decentralized social network: open mesh, election-backed groups, budget-bounded interest (north star)
description:
# SOC3 — Decentralized social network: open mesh, election-backed groups, budget-bounded interest

Source: `computenet-milestone-plan.md` §1 product row
`SOC3 | Decentralized: open mesh, election-backed groups, budget-bounded interest | SOC2, MEM1, DSC2, ECO1 | north star`;
§2 DAG (`SOC2 --> SOC3`, `MEM1 --> SOC3`, `DSC2 --> SOC3`, `ECO1 --> SOC3`); §5 rank 20 (second wave).

**This is the plan's declared north star.** §5 lists it in the second wave with no further
qualification, and §1's "Unblocks" column for SOC3 reads simply `north star`. A north star
with no exit criterion never closes, so §2 of this specification states, before anything
else, what *done* means — concretely, falsifiably, and with the non-claims named.

---

## 1. Ambition / Why

SOC1 was one node. SOC2 was several nodes that **know about each other because someone
configured them**, cooperating under locally-declared moderation policy, over identities that
cannot be spoofed.

SOC3 removes the configuration, and with it the last piece of centralization the demo still
carries. Three things arrive, and — as in SOC2 — none of them is meaningful alone:

1. **Open mesh.** A node is started with no peer list. DSC2's discovery (mDNS on a LAN, a
   rendezvous point beyond it) tells it who exists; DSC1's key-derived identity tells it who
   they are; SOC2's moderation membranes decide what it will accept from them. Membership is
   never a consensus — `replicasOf(id)` is "an eventually-consistent local fold of
   announcements — no view number, quorum, or barrier (P4)" (93 I-3, quoted in
   `doc/spec/40-distribution/42-replication.md` §Replica discovery & membership). Peers may
   transiently disagree on the set, and gossip idempotence makes that safe.
2. **Election-backed groups.** Content converges by OR-set merge, but **governance does not**.
   "Banned" and "unbanned" do not commute; a moderator roster is not a set you can union with
   a stranger's. So a *group* — a forum with a roster, a moderation ruleset and a membership
   policy — is single-writer replicated state: `SingleWriterReplication` with `LeaderMark(logicalId,
   epoch, leaderRef)` (`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/replication/SingleWriterReplication.kt:35,144,187,214`),
   leader = the single applying instance and single wave source, followers command-forwarding
   by `delegate`. What is missing today is exactly the liveness half — G-44: "no automatic
   leader election, no failure detector" — which is **MEM1**. SOC3 is MEM1's first real
   consumer, and the split it exercises is the interesting claim: **mergeable content,
   single-writer governance, one mesh**.
3. **Budget-bounded interest.** ECO1 gives per-`Principal` budgets and a cost to mint an
   identity (G-62, the Sybil half). Interest stops being free: following someone, subscribing
   to a forum, or holding a replica is a resource claim charged to a `Principal`'s budget
   (`40/43`: "authenticated principals are bounded by per-`Principal` quotas that reuse the
   G-28 host-hierarchy quota walk"). The consequence is the honest and uncomfortable one:
   **a user's view can be incomplete by design.** When the budget will not fund every
   interest leg, some legs are not funded, and the feed is a *bounded sample*, not the truth.

**Why the third one is the hard one.** An incomplete feed that says nothing is
indistinguishable from a broken feed, from censorship, and from data loss. The entire
credibility of a budget-bounded decentralized system rests on the system never presenting a
truncated view as complete. That is [SOC3-30] and BS-8, and it is the requirement this epic
would most like to quietly soften.

---

## 2. What "done" means — the north star's exit criterion

SOC3 closes when **one repeatable run** demonstrates all of the following, and the
non-claims in §4.8 are stated rather than tested:

**E1 — No configuration.** ≥5 nodes are started with **no `--peer` flag and no peer list**,
each with its own DSC1 keypair generated on first start. Every node discovers the others
through DSC2 and forms a mesh. Killing the discovery mechanism after formation does not
disconnect the mesh.

**E2 — Federated content converges under open membership.** A user on node A follows people
hosted on nodes B..E. Content posted on any node reaches A's feed, and all nodes' replicated
folds are equal at quiescence — with nodes joining and leaving throughout the run
([42-REPL-04], [42-REPL-06]).

**E3 — A group survives leadership loss.** A group with an elected moderator: the leader node
is killed mid-write; a successor is elected by MEM1's epoch-claim; the group's roster and
ruleset remain a single consistent history; writes that landed before the kill are not lost
except within the stated async primary-backup window (`42` §Single-writer replication:
"Writes served but not yet shipped to any follower at failure are lost — the stated async
primary-backup window"); divergent post-partition writes surface on the error path, never
silently ([SOC3-18], [SOC3-19]).

**E4 — Election churn is bounded.** Under repeated leader loss and heal, the group converges
to exactly one leader per logical group within a bounded number of steps, and the run does not
oscillate indefinitely ([SOC3-20], BS-5).

**E5 — Interest is budget-bounded and the truncation is visible.** Each node runs under an
ECO1 budget too small to fund every declared interest. Every feed read that is budget-limited
reports itself as incomplete, names which interest legs were unfunded, and offers the
remaining budget — and **no** read path presents a budget-truncated view as complete
([SOC3-30], [SOC3-31], [SOC3-32]).

**E6 — An adversarial peer changes no honest node's converged state.** A peer that forges
attribution, replays gossip, sends invalid signatures, floods interest, claims leadership with
a stale epoch, and relays policy-violating content is refused at every attempt with accounted
denials, and every honest node's fold is identical to a run without it ([SOC3-33..38], BS-9).

**E7 — The run is reproducible.** E1–E6 hold both as a seeded, deterministic in-process run
(`SimWorld`/`SimulationController` over `Peering.loopback` with a discovery stub) and as a
multi-JVM run over real sockets (`JvmPeer`), and every discovered failing seed is retained.

**E8 — The honesty ledger is written.** §4.8's non-claims — Sybil resistance, moderation
efficacy, byzantine tolerance, partition-tolerant governance liveness — are recorded in
`concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` and in the final report as explicitly unverified, with no test
written that appears to satisfy them.

SOC3 is **not** closed by "the demo runs". It is closed by E1–E8 with named tests, and by the
findings the run produces being filed to `doc/demo-findings.md`.

## 3. What we build

### 3.1 Module — extend `demo/social/` again

**Decision: SOC3 extends `:demo:social`,** the same artifact SOC1 created and SOC2 federated.
The plan's DAG is one artifact through three rows; a third module would fork the schema and
the moderation model, and would make the north-star run a comparison between two codebases
rather than a demonstration of one.

`demo/social/build.gradle.kts` gains `implementation(project(":discovery"))` **or** whatever
module DSC2 lands (its module name is DSC2's decision, not SOC3's — see §7 unwired deps),
alongside SOC2's `:wire` and `:identity`. ECO1's budget surface may land in `:kernel`
(quota walk) or its own module; SOC3 consumes it and does not choose.

New package `civictech.demo.social.mesh`. New flags: `--discover` (replacing `--peer` as the
default), `--budget <spec>`, `--group-policy <file>`.

**Inherited blocking constraint.** SOC2 §2.2's `DemoSurfaceAllowlistTest` problem applies
again and gets worse: `civictech.cell.membrane` is still not a demo-visible prefix, and SOC3
additionally wants `civictech.cell.replication.SingleWriterReplication`/`LeaderMark`
(`replication` **is** allowed — good) and whatever surface ECO1 exposes. Whatever SOC2 decided
in its F1, SOC3 inherits; if SOC2 escalated the widening, SOC3 must not widen it further
without the same escalation ([SOC3-03]).

### 3.2 Open mesh

- **Discovery is a source of announcements, not a new membership protocol.** DSC2 supplies
  peer endpoints; SOC3 turns each into an ordinary `Peering.Side` + `WsTransport.connect`,
  after which everything is the shipped path: `RegistryAnnounce` over the bridge,
  `LocationRegistry` folding `Local`/`Remote`, `Replication.maybeLink` forming the gossip mesh
  from ordinary announcements with no coordinator.
- **Admission is still SOC2's.** An open mesh is not an open door: a discovered peer is
  admitted or refused by the node's own moderation policy at seam 1, and a node in a fully
  open configuration must still bound what a stranger can cost it ([SOC3-08], [SOC3-34]).
- **Churn is the normal case, not an exception.** Nodes appear and vanish continuously.
  `Replication.evict`'s gate applies (`42` §Eviction is a gated drain+despawn): if no peer in
  `replicasOf(id) − {local}` is reachable, the replica MUST suspend rather than evict — it may
  hold unique un-gossiped state.

### 3.3 Election-backed groups

- **A group's governance state is single-writer.** `GroupGovernance` = roster + moderation
  ruleset + membership policy, replicated leader→follower by log shipping:
  `leader.deltaOutlet` → each follower's `deltaInlet`, followers apply in per-link-FIFO order,
  followers serve their write inlet by a command-forward `delegate` to the leader — a write
  landing on a follower is **redirected, not rejected** (`42` §Single-writer replication).
- **Leadership is a `LeaderMark` epoch fold**, not a vote: `leaderOf(id)` = the mark with max
  reachable epoch; deltas or commands stamped below the current epoch are fenced; a leader
  folding a strictly greater epoch steps down to a command-forwarding follower and catches up
  from the winner. **MEM1 supplies what is missing**: the epoch-claim election and the failure
  detector (G-44) that decide *when* a follower may claim.
- **Always-fenced writes.** On heal the higher epoch wins, the loser steps down and
  re-catches-up, and its divergent post-partition writes are surfaced on the error/dead-letter
  path, never silently dropped. `WritePosture.SAFETY_PARK` was specified and deleted (G-67) —
  SOC3 does **not** reintroduce it; if a group genuinely needs park-on-uncertainty, that is
  G-67's first real user and a separate bead ([SOC3-22]).
- **Group *content* stays mergeable.** Posts, comments and likes remain OR-set replicated
  exactly as in SOC1/SOC2. The single-writer path carries governance only. Mixing them would
  put every post through one leader and destroy the property the whole system exists to show.

### 3.4 Budget-bounded interest

- **Interest becomes a charged claim.** Declaring interest in a person, a forum, or a replica
  is charged to the declaring `Principal`'s ECO1 budget, through the G-28 host-hierarchy quota
  walk (`40/43`: "a remote-driven resource claim is charged to the claiming `Principal`'s
  budget"). SOC3 does not invent the budget or its pricing — that is ECO1 — it declares claims
  and consumes refusals.
- **Funding is a decision with a visible result.** When the budget will not fund every declared
  interest, the node funds a subset by a stated, deterministic rule (SOC3 fixes the rule and
  states it; it is not a hidden heuristic), and the unfunded remainder is a first-class,
  reportable object: `UnfundedInterest(legs, reason, budgetRemaining)`.
- **Incompleteness is carried, not inferred.** Every read result carries a completeness
  descriptor: `Complete` | `Truncated(unfundedLegs, deferredLegs, frontierPerLeg)`. PN-5
  already establishes the shape — "a shard that is unreachable simply defers its leg to a later
  pull", "per-shard-consistent, cross-shard-arbitrary", "a baseline is never a wave"
  (`42` §Scatter-gather pull over an instance set). SOC3 adds the *budget* reason alongside the
  *reachability* reason and requires both to be reported.
- **The UI must show it.** A truncated feed is labelled in the HTTP surface, not only in a log
  line. [SOC3-32].

## 4. Functional requirements (EARS)

Style mirrors `doc/spec/`'s `[NN-SLUG-nn]` convention; ids are epic-scoped (`[SOC3-nn]`) so
they cannot collide with normative spec ids. Pattern named in parentheses; each cites the
normative id or spec section it makes true.

**Honesty note on citable ids.** The distribution chapters mint few EARS ids: the complete set
in `doc/spec/40-distribution/` is `[41-LOC-01]`, `[42-INT-01]`, `[42-REPL-04]`, `[42-REPL-05]`,
`[42-REPL-06]`. There are **no** ids for security/moderation (40/43 is prose), none for
elections, none for PN-5's scatter-gather, and none for budgets. Requirements below cite prose
sections where no id exists, and any concord scenario that cannot bind honestly goes to
`concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md`.

### 4.1 Module and mesh formation

- **[SOC3-01]** (Ubiquitous) The decentralized demo SHALL be delivered as additional sources in `:demo:social` and SHALL NOT fork the SNB schema, generator, feed assembly or moderation model established by SOC1/SOC2. *(plan §1 SOC1→SOC2→SOC3 progression)*
- **[SOC3-02]** (Ubiquitous) The demo SHALL be startable with no peer list and no peer flag, and SHALL form a mesh from discovered peers alone. *(plan §1 "open mesh"; E1)*
- **[SOC3-03]** (Unwanted behaviour) IF the mesh, governance or budget code requires an import outside `DemoSurfaceAllowlistTest.demoCellPrefixes`, THEN the epic SHALL escalate with a written rationale and a note in `doc/architecture-decisions.md`, and SHALL NOT edit the allowlist to make the build pass. *(guardrail amendment policy; inherited from SOC2 §2.2)*
- **[SOC3-04]** (Event-driven) WHEN a peer is discovered, the node SHALL join it through an ordinary `Peering.Side` + transport connect, and SHALL NOT introduce a membership protocol, a view number, a quorum or a barrier. *(93 I-3; P4; 42 §Replica discovery & membership)*
- **[SOC3-05]** (Ubiquitous) The node's membership view SHALL be an eventually-consistent local fold of announcements, and two nodes SHALL be permitted to hold different membership views without either being in error. *(93 I-3, quoted in 42)*
- **[SOC3-06]** (State-driven) WHILE discovery is unavailable, an already-formed mesh SHALL continue operating on its learned peers. *(discovery is a source of announcements, not the membership authority; E1)*
- **[SOC3-07]** (Event-driven) WHEN a node leaves the mesh, surviving nodes SHALL reconcile by dropping the stale gossip link and SHALL converge without operator action. *(42 §Eviction; makes [42-REPL-06] true)*
- **[SOC3-08]** (Ubiquitous) A discovered peer SHALL be subject to the node's moderation policy at admission exactly as a configured peer is, and discovery SHALL NOT bypass any seam. *(SOC2 §2.4; 93 I-28 §4.3 seam 1)*
- **[SOC3-09]** (State-driven) WHILE no reachable peer other than the local replica exists for a logical cell, the node SHALL suspend that replica rather than evict it. *(42 §Eviction — it may hold unique un-gossiped state)*

### 4.2 Election-backed groups

- **[SOC3-10]** (Ubiquitous) A group's governance state (roster, moderation ruleset, membership policy) SHALL be single-writer replicated, and SHALL NOT be represented as mergeable state. *(42 §Single-writer replication; "banned" and "unbanned" do not commute)*
- **[SOC3-11]** (Ubiquitous) A group's content (posts, comments, likes) SHALL remain mergeable OR-set state and SHALL NOT pass through the group's leader. *(§3.3; preserves [42-REPL-04] for content)*
- **[SOC3-12]** (Ubiquitous) Exactly one instance SHALL serve a group's governance write inlet with the real implementation; every other instance SHALL serve it by a command-forward `delegate` to the leader. *(42 §Single-writer replication — leader = the single applying instance and single wave source)*
- **[SOC3-13]** (Event-driven) WHEN a governance write lands on a follower, the follower SHALL forward it to the leader and SHALL NOT apply it locally, and SHALL NOT reject it. *(42 — "a write landing on a follower is redirected, not rejected")*
- **[SOC3-14]** (Unwanted behaviour) IF a governance write carries a `Leased` payload and lands off-leader, THEN it SHALL be `Rejected`, because a `Leased` payload cannot cross a machine boundary. *(42 §Single-writer replication, type-determined exceptions; 20/23)*
- **[SOC3-15]** (Ubiquitous) Leadership SHALL be determined by the `LeaderMark` epoch fold — the mark with the greatest reachable epoch — and SHALL NOT be determined by a vote, a lease, a leader registry or a second protocol. *(42 §Single-writer replication)*
- **[SOC3-16]** (Event-driven) WHEN a leader folds a strictly greater epoch, it SHALL step down to a command-forwarding follower and SHALL catch up from the winner. *(42)*
- **[SOC3-17]** (Ubiquitous) Deltas or commands stamped below the current epoch SHALL be fenced and SHALL have no effect on governance state. *(42)*
- **[SOC3-18]** (Event-driven) WHEN a group's leader becomes unreachable, a successor SHALL be established through MEM1's epoch-claim election, and governance writes SHALL be parked rather than lost while no leader is established. *(G-44; 42 §Failover is explicit by default)*
- **[SOC3-19]** (Unwanted behaviour) IF a partition produced divergent governance writes under two epochs, THEN on heal the lower-epoch writes SHALL be surfaced on the error/dead-letter path with the group and epoch named, and SHALL NOT be silently discarded. *(42 §Always-fenced writes)*
- **[SOC3-20]** (State-driven) WHILE leadership churn is occurring, the group SHALL converge to exactly one leader per logical group within a bounded number of steps, and SHALL NOT oscillate indefinitely. *(G-44's asked-for "stated convergence/liveness bound"; E4)*
- **[SOC3-21]** (Event-driven) WHEN a RESTART preserves a leader's `instanceId`, the recovered leader SHALL re-catch-up from the most-advanced reachable follower and SHALL NOT treat its stale spawn-time checkpoint as authoritative. *(42 §RESTART = peer catch-up, not checkpoint trust)*
- **[SOC3-22]** (Ubiquitous) The epic SHALL NOT reintroduce `WritePosture` or a `SAFETY_PARK` posture; the always-fenced default stands. *(G-67 — deleted by remediation T03; its reintroduction needs its own first real user and its own bead)*
- **[SOC3-23]** (Ubiquitous) The epic SHALL state, in its findings, the async primary-backup loss window it inherits: governance writes served but not shipped to any follower at failure are lost. *(42 — "shrinking it (ack-from-k) is explicitly not adopted")*

### 4.3 Budget-bounded interest

- **[SOC3-24]** (Ubiquitous) Every declaration of interest — following a person, subscribing to a forum, holding a replica — SHALL be a resource claim charged to the declaring `Principal`'s budget. *(40/43 §Attention is a request, not an entitlement; G-62; G-28 quota walk)*
- **[SOC3-25]** (Event-driven) WHEN a `Principal`'s budget cannot fund every declared interest, the node SHALL fund a subset chosen by a stated deterministic rule, and the rule SHALL be documented and asserted by test. *(a hidden heuristic is indistinguishable from a bug)*
- **[SOC3-26]** (Ubiquitous) An unfunded interest SHALL be represented as a first-class value naming the legs, the reason, and the remaining budget, and SHALL NOT be represented by its absence. *(§3.4)*
- **[SOC3-27]** (State-driven) WHILE an interest is unfunded, no delta admitted only by that interest SHALL cross the wire to this node. *(this is the point of the budget; consistent with [42-INT-01]'s "no more … and no less" read over the funded interest)*
- **[SOC3-28]** (Event-driven) WHEN budget becomes available, a previously unfunded interest SHALL be funded and its state SHALL be brought current by ordinary state-as-delta catch-up, with no loss relative to a node that funded it from the start. *(makes [42-REPL-05] true under budget dynamics)*
- **[SOC3-29]** (Event-driven) WHEN a budget is exhausted mid-read, the read SHALL return the legs it funded, SHALL mark itself truncated, and SHALL NOT fail, block, or silently retry the unfunded legs. *(PN-5 — an unanswerable leg "simply defers its leg to a later pull"; BS-8)*
- **[SOC3-30]** (Unwanted behaviour) **IF a view is limited by budget, reachability, or moderation, THEN the system SHALL NOT present it as complete.** Every read result SHALL carry an explicit completeness descriptor distinguishing complete from truncated, and every truncated result SHALL name the cause class of each missing leg. *(the epic's central honesty requirement; PN-5's freshness contract; SOC2 [SOC2-30])*
- **[SOC3-31]** (Ubiquitous) A truncated result SHALL distinguish **unfunded** (budget), **deferred** (unreachable), and **withheld** (moderation) legs from one another, and SHALL NOT collapse them into one "missing" category. *(three different failures that demand three different user responses)*
- **[SOC3-32]** (Ubiquitous) The HTTP surface SHALL render the completeness descriptor on every affected view, and SHALL NOT confine it to a log line or a debug endpoint. *(E5)*

### 4.4 Unwanted behaviour — the adversarial mesh

- **[SOC3-33]** (Unwanted behaviour) IF a peer claims leadership of a group with an epoch not strictly greater than the current one, THEN the claim SHALL be fenced, accounted, and SHALL NOT change `leaderOf`. *([SOC3-15], [SOC3-17])*
- **[SOC3-34]** (Unwanted behaviour) IF a discovered peer floods interest assertions or link requests, THEN the node SHALL clamp and rate-limit per `Principal`, SHALL continue serving every other peer, and SHALL NOT allow an unauthenticated peer to raise its attention band above the configured floor. *(cross-references SOC2 [SOC2-37] and [SEC1-14..15]; 40/43)*
- **[SOC3-35]** (Unwanted behaviour) IF a peer replays gossip or emits deltas failing integrity verification, THEN they SHALL be refused at ingress with an accounted denial and recovery SHALL be drop-and-reconverge, adding no ack, retry, version vector or second synchronization protocol. *(cross-references SOC2 [SOC2-38..39], [SEC1-21..22]; 93 I-28)*
- **[SOC3-36]** (Unwanted behaviour) IF content is refused at any seam — moderation, budget, integrity, or election fencing — THEN it SHALL produce a typed denial record, increment a counter, and emit a sanitized dead letter; no path SHALL drop a message without accounting. *(cross-references [SEC1-25]; SOC2 [SOC2-33])*
- **[SOC3-37]** (Unwanted behaviour) IF a refused crossing carries an `Owned` or `Leased` payload, THEN that payload SHALL be discharged exactly once and a live exclusive handle SHALL NEVER reach the dead-letter fan-out. *(cross-references [SEC1-20], [SEC1-23], [SEC1-26]; SOC2 [SOC2-34]; standing repo invariant)*
- **[SOC3-38]** (Unwanted behaviour) IF an adversarial peer participates throughout a run, THEN every honest node's converged fold SHALL equal the fold of the same run without that peer. *(E6 — the operational definition of "cannot corrupt the mesh"; note the sharp limit in [SOC3-NV-03])*
- **[SOC3-39]** (Unwanted behaviour) IF a node's own budget is exhausted, THEN it SHALL continue to serve its local users and its peers, and SHALL NOT stop gossiping already-funded interests. *(a budget bounds new claims; it must not become a self-inflicted outage)*
- **[SOC3-40]** (Unwanted behaviour) IF an election, a budget refusal, or a governance fence occurs, THEN it SHALL NOT be classified as a cell fault, SHALL NOT trigger supervision RESTART, and SHALL NOT mint or advance a wave. *(cross-references [SEC1-29])*
- **[SOC3-41]** (Unwanted behaviour) IF a mesh-formation, election, or budget property fails for a discovered seed, THEN the seed SHALL be retained and SHALL NOT be replaced with a passing seed. *(AGENTS.md core invariant)*

### 4.5 Convergence under the whole thing

- **[SOC3-42]** (Ubiquitous) Replicas of one logical content cell SHALL converge to equal folds at quiescence regardless of which node accepted each write, under mesh churn, election churn and budget dynamics. *(makes [42-REPL-04] true under SOC3's conditions)*
- **[SOC3-43]** (Ubiquitous) Convergence SHALL be asserted over replicated *state*, never over *presented views*; nodes with different moderation policies or different budgets SHALL be permitted to present different views while their underlying folds are equal. *(inherited from SOC2 [SOC2-24]; the distinction that keeps [SOC3-42] meaningful)*
- **[SOC3-44]** (Ubiquitous) An orderly replica departure SHALL NOT be counted as a divergence. *(makes [42-REPL-06] true)*
- **[SOC3-45]** (Ubiquitous) Linking two ports SHALL behave identically whether the peers share a process or nothing but a network, and every SOC3 property SHALL be checkable in-process. *(makes [41-LOC-01] true; E7)*

### 4.6 Findings and hygiene

- **[SOC3-46]** (Ubiquitous) The epic SHALL append its findings to `doc/demo-findings.md` citing G-ids, and SHALL NOT edit `91-gap-analysis.md` or `CONCORDANCE.md` directly. *(plan §6)*
- **[SOC3-47]** (Unwanted behaviour) IF a required capability is missing (leaderless reassignment R1, ack-from-k durability, partition-tolerant governance liveness, capability revocation, multi-hop disclosure composition), THEN the epic SHALL file it citing the owning G-item and SHALL NOT implement it in-lane.
- **[SOC3-48]** (Ubiquitous) Every requirement above SHALL be covered by at least one named test or SHALL be explicitly listed as uncheckable with the reason.

### 4.7 The exit criterion, as requirements

- **[SOC3-49]** (Ubiquitous) The epic SHALL deliver a single named north-star run exercising E1–E7 of §2, as both a seeded in-process run and a multi-JVM run.
- **[SOC3-50]** (Ubiquitous) The epic SHALL NOT be declared complete on the basis that the demo runs; completion SHALL be the E1–E8 checklist with each item bound to a named test or an explicit DISPUTES.md entry.

### 4.8 Explicitly non-verifiable — stated, marked, not softened

These are open-mesh properties that **cannot be tested**. They are named here so that no weak
test is written that appears to satisfy them, and they belong in `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md`.

- **[SOC3-NV-01] Sybil resistance is not testable and MUST NOT be claimed.** ECO1 gives identity minting a *cost*; it does not give it a *bound*. Whether that cost deters a determined adversary is an economic question about a real deployment, not a property of a test. Any requirement of the form "the system SHALL resist Sybil attack" would be satisfied by a test that mints ten identities and observes a budget refusal, which proves nothing. **File in DISPUTES.md.**
- **[SOC3-NV-02] Moderation efficacy against a determined adversary is not testable.** Inherited verbatim from SOC2 [SOC2-NV-01]. SOC3 tests that declared rules are enforced and accounted on the paths tested; it cannot test that no bypass exists.
- **[SOC3-NV-03] SOC3 is not byzantine-fault-tolerant and MUST NOT be described as such.** [SOC3-38] is bounded by the adversary behaviours actually implemented in the harness. A peer that is admitted, authenticated, within budget and within policy can still emit *semantically* dishonest content — that is a moderation problem, not a convergence one, and no test distinguishes it. Election is last-epoch-wins, not consensus: a peer that mints ever-increasing epochs can take leadership of any group it is admitted to. **This is a real, unfixed hole and it must be stated, not buried.**
- **[SOC3-NV-04] Governance liveness under partition is not testable as stated.** With last-epoch-wins and explicit failover, a partition can leave a group leaderless on one side (writes park) or dual-led (both sides serve, higher epoch wins on heal, loser's writes surface on the error path). Which of those a deployment wants is `WritePosture`'s question (G-67), deliberately not reintroduced ([SOC3-22]). SOC3 tests the fencing and the surfacing; it does not claim liveness.
- **[SOC3-NV-05] "Decentralized" is not a testable predicate.** The nearest checkable proxies are E1 (no configured peer list) and the absence of any consensus, quorum, view number or coordinator in the code paths exercised. Do not write a requirement asserting decentralization itself.
