## 5. Functional requirements (EARS)

Ids are stable and scoped: `[WKB2-nn]`. They mirror `doc/spec/`'s `[NN-SLUG-nn]` style but
are namespaced so they never collide with a spec id.

**Citation honesty, stated once.** `doc/spec/50-development-process/51-construction.md` and
`53-evolution.md` — the two chapters this epic realizes — carry **zero EARS ids** and are
listed by name in `doc/spec/CONCORDANCE.md` §"Denominator honesty" among the 13 chapters
"structurally excluded from the table below; filed as a dispute, not silently passing
(`concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md`)". So requirements below cite the normative ids that *do*
exist (`15-APPLY-01`, `15-DESPAWN-01`, `15-PROMOTE-01`, `13-LINK-05`, `13-REBIND-02`,
`13-NOLOSS-01/02`, `33-MOVE-01`) and, where none exists, the decided-spec anchor by section
and gap/research id (`51 §G-51`, `95 §R4`, `53 §The promotion swap` / `93 I-11`,
`53 §Trust boundary` / G-50 residual, `93 I-21`, `93 I-26`). Requirements citing a
section rather than an id are verifiable by named test but **not** by the concordance
matrix; that asymmetry is stated, not hidden (see `[WKB2-63]`).

### Ubiquitous — the write plane exists and is bounded

- **[WKB2-01]** The inspector shall expose a graph-editing write plane whose entire
  implementation lives under `inspect/src/main/kotlin/civictech/inspect/edit/`, such that
  no route outside that package mutates host state. *(51 §The programming environment;
  `InspectorServer` §T19's per-route posture.)*
- **[WKB2-02]** The write plane shall express every proposed change as a `GraphSpec`
  (`civictech.cell.graph.GraphSpec`) composed only of the step types the kernel already
  accepts, and shall introduce no step verb the host does not already accept as a
  management invocation. *(51 §Graph construction DSL: "the DSL gains parameters, not
  verbs — every step MUST lower to a management invocation the host already accepts".)*
- **[WKB2-03]** The write plane shall apply every `GraphSpec` through
  `GraphSpec.lowered()`, so an `InstanceSetStep` is expanded to its N × `SpawnStep` form
  before any step executes. *(51 §`InstanceSetStep`, PN-13.)*
- **[WKB2-04]** Every applied change shall be recorded in an append-only audit entry
  carrying: apply id, submitting identity, submitted spec, base topology version, outcome
  per step, and wall-clock timestamps for submission and completion. *(53 §Trust boundary;
  G-50 residual.)*
- **[WKB2-05]** The inspector's existing read routes and SSE event families shall retain
  their contracted behaviour unchanged. *(`97-inspector-plan/20-api-contract.md`.)*

### State-driven — edit mode is off unless deliberately on

- **[WKB2-06]** While the host process was started without the explicit write-plane opt-in
  flag, the inspector shall serve no mutating route other than the pre-existing
  `POST /graph/{id}/wake`, and shall advertise the write plane as unavailable in its
  capability response. *(53 §Trust boundary.)*
- **[WKB2-07]** While the write plane is disabled, the frontend shall render no edit
  affordance, so a read-only deployment is visually indistinguishable from today's
  inspector. *(53 §Trust boundary.)*
- **[WKB2-08]** While the write plane is enabled, the inspector server shall continue to
  bind `InetAddress.getLoopbackAddress()` only. *(`InspectorServer` §T19.)*
- **[WKB2-09]** While an apply is staged and not yet cut over, the affected cells shall be
  reported with an explicit staged marker distinguishing them from live graph members.
  *(53 §graphs-as-data: candidate subgraph is data until the swap.)*

### Event-driven — precheck

- **[WKB2-10]** When a draft `GraphSpec` is submitted to the precheck route, the write
  plane shall validate it without spawning, linking, or despawning anything. *(95 §R4,
  third open item: eager cold structural pre-validation.)*
- **[WKB2-11]** When precheck runs, it shall resolve every `ConnectStep`'s endpoints and
  check port compatibility on `(portName, contractId)`. *(`[13-REBIND-02]`; 93 I-2
  structural port sameness.)*
- **[WKB2-12]** When precheck runs, it shall dry-run each proposed inbound link against the
  admission checks a live `connect` would apply — cardinality budget, ownership exclusive
  bit, contract compatibility, policy predicates — and report each rejection with the
  reason vocabulary the kernel already defines. *(`[13-LINK-05]`; 93 I-26's structural
  admission layer, which is "phase-independent… binding from construction".)*
- **[WKB2-13]** When precheck runs against a spec containing an `InstanceSetStep`, it shall
  run `InstanceSetStep.validate`'s existing axes and surface an `INSTANCE_SCOPING` or
  `DURABLE` refusal verbatim. *(51 §`InstanceSetStep`.)*
- **[WKB2-14]** When precheck completes, it shall return a plan enumerating, per step,
  whether the step would spawn, link, unlink, despawn, or promote, and which live refs it
  would touch. *(95 §R4's "defined error surface for an invalid spec".)*
- **[WKB2-15]** When precheck rejects any step, the write plane shall report the spec as
  not-appliable as a whole and shall not offer a partial apply of the remainder.
  *(This is the epic's central departure from `[15-APPLY-01]`'s leave-and-report default;
  see `[WKB2-20]`.)*

### Event-driven — the atomicity contract (the epic's core)

- **[WKB2-16]** When an apply is accepted, the write plane shall execute it in the ordered
  stages PRECHECK → STAGE → CUT-OVER → (UNWIND | RETIRE), and shall not interleave them.
  *(53 §The promotion swap, whose four-phase state machine is the model; 93 I-11.)*
- **[WKB2-17]** When the STAGE phase runs, the write plane shall execute every `SpawnStep`
  and every `ConnectStep` internal to the staged subgraph, and shall execute no
  `ConnectStep` whose endpoint is a pre-existing live cell. *(95 §R4 direction (1)'s
  rationale: "evolution (53) already provides the transactional idiom (build candidate →
  judge → swap)".)*
- **[WKB2-18]** When any step of the STAGE phase fails, the write plane shall compensate by
  despawning every cell it spawned in this apply, in reverse creation order, and unlinking
  every link it created. *(95 §R4 direction (2): compensating unlink of the applied prefix;
  `[15-DESPAWN-01]`.)*
- **[WKB2-19]** When a STAGE-phase compensation completes, the write plane shall report the
  live graph as unchanged, and the live graph shall be observationally identical to its
  pre-apply state for every inspector read route. *(This is the epic's atomicity claim,
  and it is checkable precisely because STAGE never touched live traffic.)*
- **[WKB2-20]** When the write plane applies a `GraphSpec`, it shall not expose
  `GraphSpec.applyRemote`'s leave-and-report semantics as the operator-visible outcome of a
  failed apply. *(`[15-APPLY-01]` describes the kernel default; 95 §R4 asks whether a
  transactional mode should exist; WKB2's answer is that an operator-facing applier must
  have one.)*
- **[WKB2-21]** The write plane shall leave `GraphSpec.applyTo` and `GraphSpec.applyRemote`
  semantics unchanged for every existing caller. *(AGENTS.md: smallest coherent change;
  `[15-APPLY-01]` is landed contract.)*
- **[WKB2-22]** When the CUT-OVER phase replaces a live instance, the write plane shall
  perform the replacement through `Promotion.promote` (or `Promotion.promoteReplica` for a
  replicated cell) rather than through an ad-hoc unlink/connect sequence. *(53 §The
  promotion swap; 53 §Replicated promotion.)*
- **[WKB2-23]** When `Promotion.promote` aborts, the write plane shall report the incumbent
  as retained and re-linked, and shall not attempt its own compensation on top of the
  kernel's rollback. *(53 §G-49-resolved: "a mid-COMMIT failure reverses every completed
  relink, restores the incumbent's gate subscription, and re-greens onto it unchanged".)*
- **[WKB2-24]** When the CUT-OVER phase completes successfully, the write plane shall
  report the apply as committed, and shall retire staged-but-superseded cells only after
  that report. *(53 §The promotion swap step 4: "RETIRE — despawn the incumbent. Only now
  is it gone.")*

### Unwanted behaviour — the residue that cannot be compensated

- **[WKB2-25]** If a compensating unwind cannot restore the pre-apply graph — because a
  staged cell already emitted downstream, consumed an `Owned` payload, or discharged a
  `Leased` one — then the write plane shall report the apply's outcome as
  **unwound-with-residue**, naming each un-compensated effect, and shall not report it as
  rolled back. *(AGENTS.md §Core invariants: "no failure, suppression, shadow, park, or
  dead-letter path may silently drop an exclusive payload"; 23 ownership.)*
- **[WKB2-26]** If a staged cell would consume an `Owned` payload during STAGE, then the
  write plane shall refuse the spec at precheck rather than stage it, since STAGE's
  compensability is the atomicity claim's whole basis. *(23 ownership; `[WKB2-19]`.)*
- **[WKB2-27]** If a spec's cut-over would cross a Symport/Antiport coupling, then the
  write plane shall refuse the apply with a reason naming G-53, and shall not attempt the
  swap. *(53 §The promotion swap ⚠ GAP (G-53): "the fate of a half-completed coupled
  transaction caught in a promotion-swap buffering window is undefined"; 95 §R3.)*
- **[WKB2-28]** If a spec would place cells on more than one host, then the write plane
  shall refuse it with a reason naming G-61, since no placement engine decides where cells
  land. *(51 §Replay is placement; 53 ⚠ GAP (G-61); 95 §R5.)*
- **[WKB2-29]** If a candidate declares `Promotion.NonIdempotentCatchUp` and no T0/T1 state
  transfer is available, then the write plane shall surface the kernel's PRECHECK refusal
  rather than retrying under any other tier. *(`[15-PROMOTE-01]`; 53 §G-33 three handoff
  tiers.)*
- **[WKB2-30]** If a message would be lost at any link operation the write plane performs,
  that is a defect and the epic shall treat the reproducing case as blocking.
  *(`[13-NOLOSS-01]`, `[13-NOLOSS-02]` — normative invariant, not a target.)*

### Event-driven — concurrency and a graph that changed underneath

- **[WKB2-31]** When a draft is opened for editing, the write plane shall record the base
  topology version the draft was authored against, derived from the monotonic `seq` the
  inspector's snapshot and SSE stream already share. *(`20-api-contract.md`: `?graph=`
  scoping "shar[es] `seq` with the unfiltered snapshot".)*
- **[WKB2-32]** When an apply is submitted, it shall carry that base topology version as a
  precondition. *(Optimistic concurrency; no global lock — P4.)*
- **[WKB2-33]** If the live graph's relevant swap set changed since the submitted base
  version, then the write plane shall reject the apply as conflicted, shall execute no
  step, and shall report which refs changed. *(53 §The promotion swap: the coordinator
  reads the incumbent's complete incident set from `TopologyIndex.swapSet(ref)`, which is
  the precise definition of "relevant".)*
- **[WKB2-34]** The conflict check shall be scoped to the swap set of the refs the spec
  touches, not to the whole topology, so an unrelated concurrent change does not reject an
  apply. *(53 §G-48-resolved: enumeration "proportional to that swap set rather than to
  all cells or links".)*
- **[WKB2-35]** When two operators submit applies whose swap sets intersect, at most one
  shall be admitted; the other shall be rejected as conflicted with no partial effect.
  *(Serialization is local and membrane-scoped — 53: "atomic per membrane at the membrane's
  host (management-preempts-data single-consumer serialization; no global lock, no
  coordinator)".)*
- **[WKB2-36]** When two operators submit applies whose swap sets are disjoint, both shall
  be admitted. *(Same anchor: no global lock.)*
- **[WKB2-37]** While an apply is in its STAGE or CUT-OVER phase, a second apply touching
  an intersecting swap set shall be rejected rather than queued. *(Rejection is honest;
  queueing invites an operator to reason about a graph that no longer exists.)*

### Event-driven — what an observer sees

- **[WKB2-38]** When an apply enters any phase, the inspector shall emit an `apply.*` SSE
  event on the existing `GET /api/inspect/events` stream carrying the apply id and the new
  phase, riding the shared monotonic `seq`. *(`20-api-contract.md` §SSE envelope; 95 §R4's
  "dataflow-linkable `ApplyReport` outlet" is the kernel-side counterpart.)*
- **[WKB2-39]** When an apply reaches a terminal outcome, the emitted event shall name the
  outcome as exactly one of: committed, refused-at-precheck, unwound-clean,
  unwound-with-residue, rolled-back-at-commit, or conflicted. *(A closed vocabulary is what
  makes `[WKB2-25]` non-evadable.)*
- **[WKB2-40]** While an apply is staged, `GET /api/inspect/topology` shall include the
  staged cells marked as staged, and shall not present them as ordinary live members.
  *(An observer must never mistake a half-built graph for a converged one — the plan's
  "what does a partially-applied graph look like to an observer?".)*
- **[WKB2-41]** When an apply ends as unwound-with-residue, every residual effect it named
  shall be retrievable from `GET /api/inspect/apply/{id}` after the apply completes.
  *(Corollary of `[WKB2-25]`; an SSE consumer that was not connected must still learn it.)*
- **[WKB2-42]** The apply audit ring shall be bounded for the whole process and shall
  answer with an empty list rather than 404 when empty. *(Consistency with
  `GET /api/inspect/activity`, "bounded at 200 for the whole process (not per cell); an
  empty ring answers `{"entries": []}`, never 404".)*

### Event-driven — authorization and confirmation

- **[WKB2-43]** When any mutating route is called without the write-plane capability the
  process was started with, the write plane shall reject the call before evaluating the
  request body and before touching host state. *(53 §Trust boundary; G-50 residual's
  "who may register or trigger a swap is ungated".)*
- **[WKB2-44]** Every mutating route shall require a non-simple request header, so a
  cross-origin browser request must preflight and — since the server registers no `OPTIONS`
  handler — fails closed. *(`InspectorServer` §T19's `WAKE_HEADER` mechanism, generalized.)*
- **[WKB2-45]** The write plane shall classify each step as destructive or non-destructive,
  where destructive means it unlinks a live link, despawns a live cell, or retires an
  incumbent. *(`[15-DESPAWN-01]`; 53 §The promotion swap step 4.)*
- **[WKB2-46]** When a submitted spec contains a destructive step, the write plane shall
  require an explicit per-apply confirmation token naming the destructive steps, and shall
  reject the apply if the token does not match the plan the operator was shown.
  *(Confirmation must bind to the *plan*, not merely to a click — otherwise the graph can
  change between the dialog and the submit.)*
- **[WKB2-47]** When the frontend is about to submit a destructive apply, it shall display
  each destructive step, the live refs it affects, and the blast radius the precheck
  reported, before enabling submission. *(The `POST /graph/{id}/wake` precedent already
  reports true blast radius: "`hosts`/`cells` report the true blast radius".)*
- **[WKB2-48]** If the confirmation token is absent, stale, or names a different plan, then
  the write plane shall reject the apply with no side effect. *(Corollary of
  `[WKB2-46]`.)*
- **[WKB2-49]** The write plane shall record the submitting identity on every mutation,
  even where that identity is only the capability presented. *(53 §Trust boundary; a
  weak identity recorded honestly beats an absent one.)*
- **[WKB2-50]** The write plane shall not weaken the existing gate on
  `POST /graph/{id}/wake`, nor add a gate to the existing read routes. *(No opportunistic
  churn on adjacent paths — AGENTS.md.)*

### Optional-feature

- **[WKB2-51]** Where the process was started with the write plane enabled, the capability
  response shall advertise which step verbs the running host admits, so the frontend
  renders only affordances the backend can honour. *(51: every step lowers to a management
  invocation the host already accepts.)*
- **[WKB2-52]** Where a `PromotionPolicy` is supplied with a candidate subgraph, the
  cut-over shall consult it through `PromotionJudge` and abort with the incumbent untouched
  unless the verdict is `Accept`. *(53 §Trust boundary G-50 policy half, resolved W4.4;
  `civictech.cell.evolve.PromotionPolicy`.)*
- **[WKB2-53]** Where a `PromotionJudge` returns `Pending`, the write plane shall report
  the apply as awaiting its observation window rather than as failed. *(`ObservationWindow`
  is "measured in observed production waves… never wall-clock, never a barrier" —
  53 §Judgment is declarative policy.)*
- **[WKB2-54]** Where the target of a replacement is a replicated cell, the write plane
  shall offer only the rolling form, one instance at a time. *(53 §Replicated promotion:
  set-atomic promotion "is a distributed consensus barrier — the P4-forbidden global lock —
  and is **out of scope**".)*
- **[WKB2-55]** Where a rolling promotion is offered, each instance's swap shall reuse the
  incumbent's `CellRef`, and a candidate presenting a different ref shall be refused.
  *(53 §Replicated promotion: a fresh ref "breaks crash-recovery equivalence, orphaning the
  incumbent's watermark row and restarting the tag lane".)*

### Complex

- **[WKB2-56]** When an apply is submitted while the write plane is enabled and its base
  topology version is current and its precheck passes and, where required, its confirmation
  token matches, the write plane shall stage the spec; otherwise it shall reject the apply
  with exactly one named reason and execute no step. *(Composite of `[WKB2-06]`,
  `[WKB2-15]`, `[WKB2-33]`, `[WKB2-46]`.)*
- **[WKB2-57]** While an apply is staged, if the operator aborts it, then the write plane

  two different notions of "undone".)*
- **[WKB2-58]** When the host is drained or a targeted cell is suspended, and an apply
  touching it is submitted, the write plane shall refuse rather than wake anything

- **[WKB2-59]** Every requirement id in this section shall be either covered by a named

## 6. Behaviour specifications (Given / When / Then)

Each is specific enough to become a named test. `covers:` notes say where a scenario
belongs in the concord corpus — and, more often, why it does not.

**B1 — Precheck refuses an incompatible link before anything runs.**
Given a live graph with a `SetCell` outlet and a draft spec connecting it to an inlet whose
contract differs; When precheck runs; Then the plan reports the `ConnectStep` as rejected
citing contract incompatibility, and no cell was spawned on the host.
*`covers:` a scenario binding `13-LINK-05` could live in `concord/corpus/13-links/` — but
only for the kernel-level admission refusal, not for the HTTP surface. The workbench half
is a `:inspect` test.*

**B2 — A spec that fails mid-STAGE leaves the live graph untouched.**
Given a live graph G and a spec whose third `SpawnStep` fails (deterministically injected);
When the apply runs; Then the two already-spawned cells are despawned in reverse order, the
apply outcome is `unwound-clean`, and a full topology snapshot equals the pre-apply snapshot
modulo `seq`. *This is `[WKB2-19]`'s test and the epic's headline property.*
*`covers:` not a concord scenario — the corpus is implementation-neutral dataflow semantics
(`concord/schema/cell-catalog.md`'s closed cell ids), and "the applier compensated its own
prefix" is an orchestration property with no neutral cell vocabulary. State so in DISPUTES
rather than inventing catalogue entries.*

**B3 — A spec that fails mid-STAGE after a staged cell emitted reports residue.**
Given a staged subgraph whose second cell has already emitted a delta into a *staged*
downstream sink, and a later step fails; When the unwind runs; Then the outcome is
`unwound-with-residue` only if an effect escaped the staged set, and `unwound-clean`
otherwise — and the test asserts *which*, not merely that a report exists.
*`covers:` no. Same reason as B2.*

**B4 — An `Owned` payload is never silently dropped by a compensating unwind.**
Given a spec staging a cell that would consume an `Owned` value; When precheck runs; Then
the spec is refused per `[WKB2-26]`; And in the control where such a cell is force-staged,
the unwind reports the exclusive payload as residue rather than dropping it.
*`covers: 12-EXCL-01` is the nearest existing id and it is about port exclusivity, not
about unwind. Do not bind it. File the gap.*

**B5 — Apply against a graph that changed underneath is rejected whole.**
Given an operator opened a draft at base version `seq=N`; And a second actor despawned one
of the refs the draft connects to; When the operator submits at `seq=N`; Then the apply is
rejected as conflicted, names the changed ref, and executes zero steps.
*`covers:` no — a base-version precondition is a workbench protocol, not a kernel semantic.*

**B6 — Two operators, intersecting swap sets: exactly one wins.**
Given two applies submitted concurrently whose swap sets share a ref; When both are
processed; Then exactly one commits and the other is rejected as conflicted with no partial
effect; And the audit ring contains both, with the rejection naming the winner's apply id.

**B7 — Two operators, disjoint swap sets: both commit.**
Given two applies whose swap sets are disjoint; When both are processed; Then both commit,
and neither observed a delay attributable to the other. *(No global lock — the assertion is
on outcome, not on timing; see `[WKB2-36]`.)*

**B8 — A cut-over that fails mid-COMMIT rolls back to the incumbent.**
Given a promotion cut-over whose relink of the second downstream subscriber throws; When
COMMIT fails; Then `Promotion.PromotionAborted` is raised, the incumbent is still linked and
green, the gate carries the incumbent's subscription, and downstream sees an unbroken stream
across the attempt. *The kernel half is already covered by `ShadowPromotionTest`
(mid-commit failure → retained-incumbent rollback); the WKB2 half asserts the write plane
reports `rolled-back-at-commit` and adds no compensation of its own (`[WKB2-23]`).*

**B9 — Rollback after a bad swap that already committed.**
Given a promotion that committed and retired the incumbent; And the candidate is judged bad
afterwards; When a reverse apply is submitted; Then it is an ordinary fresh apply in the
reverse direction under the same protocol, and the write plane does **not** claim to undo
the original. *53 is explicit: "Rollback *after* a successful promotion is a fresh swap in
the reverse direction, identical protocol", and the retention window for the retired
incumbent's export snapshot is listed as "still by-convention, not built" — so a
post-RETIRE rollback that needs the incumbent's snapshot is **out of scope here and
belongs to JAR2/WKB3**. The test asserts the honest refusal, not a fabricated undo.*

**B10 — A partially-applied graph is legible to an observer.**
Given an apply staged and paused before cut-over; When a second client fetches
`GET /api/inspect/topology` and subscribes to `GET /api/inspect/events`; Then the staged
cells appear marked as staged, the `apply.*` events name the phase, and no staged cell is
reported as an ordinary live member of a component.

**B11 — Destructive confirmation binds to the plan, not the click.**
Given a plan shown to the operator listing one despawn; And the live graph changes so the
plan would now despawn two cells; When the operator submits with the original confirmation
token; Then the apply is rejected per `[WKB2-48]` and nothing is despawned.

**B12 — The write plane is absent when not opted in.**
Given a host started without the write-plane flag; When every mutating route is called with
a valid capability; Then each answers as unavailable, and the frontend renders no edit
affordance. *(A negative test that must be written first — it is the safety default.)*

**B13 — Cross-origin mutation fails closed.**
Given a browser on a different origin; When it attempts a mutating `POST` without preflight
success; Then the request never reaches the write plane, and the belt-and-suspenders
header check rejects a non-browser caller that omits the header.

**B14 — A coupled flow in the cut-over path is refused, not attempted.**
Given a spec whose cut-over crosses a Symport/Antiport coupling; When precheck runs; Then
the apply is refused naming G-53; And no buffering window is ever opened.
*`covers:` no — G-53 is an open gap; a concord scenario asserting behaviour here would be
asserting undecided semantics. DISPUTES is the home if a reviewer wants it recorded.*

**B15 — Rolling replica promotion refuses a fresh ref and refuses T2.**
Given a replicated cell and a candidate with a different `CellRef`; When the apply is
submitted; Then it is refused; And the control with a `NonIdempotentCatchUp` candidate and
no T0/T1 transfer is refused too. *The kernel half has `ReplicatedPromotionTest`'s two
diverging controls; the WKB2 half asserts the refusal surfaces to the operator with the
kernel's reason text intact. `covers: 15-PROMOTE-01` is tempting but 15-lifecycle.md
records an ⚠ EARS-GAP on that id ("the decided restriction and the landed behavior
currently disagree… unclear which behavior a scenario should assert") — so do **not** bind
it; cite it and file the observation.*

**B16 — A drained host is not woken implicitly.**
Given a drained host holding a targeted cell; When an apply touching it is submitted; Then
it is refused; And no host or cell was resumed.

**B17 — Every read route is unchanged with the write plane enabled.**
Given the write plane enabled; When the existing `:inspect` test suite runs unmodified;
Then it passes. *(A ratchet, not a new assertion.)*

**B18 — Determinism.**
Given the failure-injection harness with a recorded seed that produced an unwind defect;
When the suite runs; Then that seed is still in the suite. *(AGENTS.md: "Do not replace a
discovered failing seed with a friendlier seed.")*

---

## 7. Suggested feature decomposition

**List only — do not create these beads as part of filing this epic.**

1. **Named-factory catalogue** — a registrable cell-constructor catalogue over
   `ContractRegistry`/`CellDescriptor`, plus the parameter schema a UI can render.
2. **Cold structural pre-validation** (R4's third open item) — cardinality / ownership /
   contract / `InstanceSetStep` axes, with a defined error surface, in
   `civictech.cell.graph`.
3. **Staged applier + compensating unwinder** (R4's atomicity decision) — the STAGE /
   CUT-OVER / UNWIND state machine and the residue vocabulary.
4. **Subscribable apply progress** (R4's second open item) — a dataflow-linkable
   `ApplyReport` surface in `civictech.cell.graph`, consumed by the inspector's `apply.*`
   SSE lane.
5. **Write-plane HTTP surface** — the five routes, the capability response, the audit ring.
6. **Authorization and confirmation** — opt-in flag, capability, non-simple-header gate,
   plan-bound destructive confirmation, audit identity.
7. **Concurrency preconditions** — base topology version, swap-set-scoped conflict
   detection, two-operator admission.
8. **Promotion integration** — candidate-subgraph authoring under
   `IdentityBinding.NewInstanceOf`, `PromotionPolicy`/`PromotionJudge` wiring, the rolling
   replica form.
9. **Frontend: edit mode** — canvas editing, palette from the catalogue, draft model.
10. **Frontend: plan review and conflict UX** — diff view, destructive confirmation,
    conflict resolution, staged-cell rendering.
11. **Failure-injection harness** — deterministic mid-stage and mid-commit failures over
    `SimWorld`, plus a generative apply/unwind property test.
12. **Findings and DISPUTES pass** — the R4 failure-case catalogue, and the
    `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` entries `[WKB2-63]` requires.

---

## 8. Verification

Narrowest first, then expand:

```bash
# backend
./gradlew :inspect:test
./gradlew :inspect:test --tests 'civictech.inspect.edit.*'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.graph.GraphSpecRemoteApplyTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.evolve.ShadowPromotionTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.evolve.ReplicatedPromotionTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.evolve.PromotionWaveStateTest'

# conformance + docs lints (a dangling covers: id or orphan scenario fails this)
./gradlew :concord:test -Pconcord.profiles=core   # fast local loop
./gradlew :concord:test                            # core, dist, dur
./gradlew :concord:check
./gradlew :concord:concordance                     # regenerate; never hand-edit CONCORDANCE.md

# repository-wide gate
./gradlew test
```

Frontend — **npm, not Gradle** (`inspect/ui` and `demo/agora/ui` are both outside the
Gradle build on purpose):

```bash
cd inspect/ui
npm ci
npm run typecheck      # tsc --noEmit
npm run test           # vitest run
npm run build          # vite build
```

CI: the five required checks are `build-test-fast`, `build-test-serial`, `concord-full`,
`ui-test`, `agora-ui-test` (AGENTS.md §Branches, PRs, and auto-merge). `ui-test` is the job
that runs `inspect/ui`. **Auto-merge is armed on every non-draft PR** — keep work in draft
until the whole epic branch is pushed.

Manual: run `demo/shopping` or `demo/skillmatch` with `--inspect-port` plus the new
write-plane opt-in, and exercise a real apply against a live graph. That the write plane is
opt-in on those two demos and nowhere else is itself a verification of `[WKB2-06]`.

---

## 9. Risks and open questions

1. **R4 is decided by this epic, and the decision is contestable.** 95 §R4's preferred
   direction is (1) — "keep partial+report as the *only* semantics… transactional
   construction may be redundant (preferred; YAGNI)". WKB2 does not overturn `[15-APPLY-01]`
   for existing callers (`[WKB2-21]`), but it does argue that an *operator-facing* applier
   needs a transactional shape, built as staging rather than as a new kernel transaction.
   If a reviewer reads that as scope creep past direction (1), the argument must be settled
   in the epic's first feature, not discovered at review. **Highest-leverage thing to
   resolve first.**
2. **Compensation honesty.** `[WKB2-25]`'s `unwound-with-residue` is the requirement most
   likely to be quietly weakened into "rolled back" by an implementation that does not look
   hard at what escaped. The ownership invariant makes this a correctness question, not a
   reporting nicety.
3. **The factory obstruction is real.** A `Serializable` `CellFactory` cannot originate in
   a browser. If the named-factory catalogue turns out to need a step verb the host does
   not already accept, that is the P1 design review 53 §Mechanical decomposition warns
   about — stop and file it.
4. **Trust posture may be judged too weak or too strong.** A capability plus loopback is
   the smallest honest gate; SEC1 (`computenet-usd`) and 43 own the real authority story,
   and G-50's authority residual is explicitly open. A reviewer who wants `Principal`-backed
   authorization here is asking for SEC1, and should be told so.
5. **G-52 (membranes) is undesigned at its edges**, so R4's direction (3) is unavailable.
   WKB2 borrows its shape via staging. If staging proves insufficient for some class of
   change, that class is a finding, not a reason to build membranes here.
6. **G-53 and G-61 are refusal surfaces, not solved problems** (`[WKB2-27]`, `[WKB2-28]`).
   Refusing loudly is the correct behaviour and will look like a missing feature to a user.
7. **No EARS ids in 51/53.** Every requirement here that cites a section rather than an id
   is invisible to `doc/spec/CONCORDANCE.md`. `[WKB2-63]` routes that to
   `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md`. The tempting shortcut — minting `[51-*]`/`[53-*]` ids in
   `doc/spec/` — is a spec edit this epic is not authorized to make.
8. **WKB1 waves 7–11 status is stated inconsistently** between the milestone plan ("in
   flight") and the v4 orchestration log (all merged, C-replan-2 closed 2026-07-31).
   Verify against `main` before starting. This dependency is external and unwired — there
   is no WKB1 bead.
9. **`ApplyReport` is a return value, not a port.** Until R4's second open item lands, the
   `apply.*` SSE lane is inspector-side bookkeeping rather than a dataflow observation.
   Building it inspector-only is the cheap path and the wrong long-term home; feature 4
   exists to keep that from calcifying.
10. **Measurement.** How long a cut-over holds the membrane red, and how much traffic parks,
    are the numbers an operator will ask for first. Under BEN1 (`computenet-x9e`) they
    belong in `:bench` behind the tag gate; without BEN1 they are a findings-file number
    with its method stated — never a benchmark checked into a required check, which is the
    V1C-BENCH mistake BEN1 exists to stop repeating.
design:
# WKB2 — design notes

## The one decision this epic exists to make

R4 (`doc/spec/90-roadmap/95-research-plan.md` §"R4 — Partial-apply atomicity for remote
GraphSpec (G-51 residual)") has three directions:

1. keep partial + report as the only semantics (R4's own preference, on YAGNI grounds,
   because "evolution (53) already provides the transactional idiom (build candidate →
   judge → swap)");
2. compensating unlink of the applied prefix, reusing journal reversal (G-49 machinery);
3. wrap remote application in a membrane swap: build hidden, expose atomically — needs G-52.

**WKB2's answer: (1) stays true for the kernel; the workbench gets (3)'s *shape* without
(3)'s cost.** The apply pipeline stages the whole new subgraph unexposed, so the only step
that touches live traffic is a single cut-over. A failure before cut-over compensates
completely, because nothing live was touched. A failure at cut-over is the kernel's already
built retained-incumbent rollback in `Promotion.promote`. Direction (2) survives as the
STAGE-phase unwind — reverse-order despawn of the prefix — which is cheap precisely because
the prefix is inert.

`[15-APPLY-01]`'s leave-and-report contract is **not** changed for existing callers
(`[WKB2-21]`). What changes is that an operator-facing applier never exposes it.

## Why the compensation claim is checkable

Compensation is usually a lie in distributed systems because effects escape. Here it is
checkable for a specific reason: STAGE runs no `ConnectStep` whose endpoint is a live cell,
so no staged cell can emit into the live graph and no live wave can enter the staged set.
The unwind therefore restores an observationally identical graph, and `[WKB2-19]` asserts
exactly that against a full topology snapshot.

The residue case (`[WKB2-25]`) is the honest remainder: an effect that escaped the staged
set, an `Owned` payload consumed, a `Leased` one discharged. It gets its own terminal
outcome name — `unwound-with-residue` — so an implementation cannot round it up to
"rolled back". `[WKB2-26]` closes the most common way residue appears by refusing such a
spec at precheck.

## Where each piece lives

- `civictech.cell.graph` (kernel): cold structural pre-validation; the subscribable
  `ApplyReport` surface. Both are R4 open items and both are kernel semantics — putting
  them in `:inspect` would make the tooling define a model the kernel owes.
- `civictech.inspect.edit` (`:inspect`): the whole write plane, in one directory, so
  "what can mutate?" has a single answer.
- `inspect/ui` (npm/Vite): edit mode, plan review, confirmation, conflict UX.

## Sequencing

Order that keeps the risk at the front:

1. Settle R4 in writing (feature 1 of the decomposition's ordering, before code) — an
   agreed statement of what atomicity WKB2 claims and what it does not.
2. Cold structural pre-validation. It is R4's cheapest half and it removes most partial
   applies before they can happen.
3. STAGE/UNWIND with the deterministic failure harness. Write `[WKB2-19]`'s test first;
   it is the epic's headline property and it is invisible in the happy path.
4. Authorization + audit, before any route that mutates is merged in a non-draft PR.
5. Cut-over via `Promotion`, then the HTTP surface, then the frontend.

The frontend must not lead. An edit UI built against a write plane that has not settled its
atomicity vocabulary will encode the wrong outcome names in its components and tests.

## Naming discipline

The terminal outcome vocabulary (`[WKB2-39]`) is closed: committed, refused-at-precheck,
unwound-clean, unwound-with-residue, rolled-back-at-commit, conflicted. Adding a seventh is
a design decision, not a convenience. The whole atomicity story is legible from that list,
which is the point.
acceptance_criteria: Closed when every requirement id in the description's §5 is either covered by a named test or explicitly listed as uncheckable with a stated reason, per [WKB2-59]. Specifically: (1) write plane exists and is bounded [WKB2-01..05]; (2) edit mode off by default [WKB2-06..09]; (3) precheck [WKB2-10..15]; (4) the atomicity contract [WKB2-16..24], with [WKB2-19] (unwound STAGE leaves the live graph observationally identical) and [WKB2-20] (leave-and-report is never the operator-visible outcome) treated as non-negotiable; (5) residue honesty [WKB2-25..30], with [WKB2-25] not weakened into 'rolled back'; (6) concurrency and stale-base rejection [WKB2-31..37]; (7) observer legibility of a partially-applied graph [WKB2-38..42]; (8) authorization and plan-bound destructive confirmation [WKB2-43..50]; (9) optional features [WKB2-51..55]; (10) complex [WKB2-56..58]; (11) verification discipline [WKB2-59..63]. Behaviour specs B1-B18 exist as named tests, with B2, B3, B5, B6, B8 and B11 written before their implementation. [WKB2-60]'s failure paths are covered by deterministic injection, not observation. ./gradlew :inspect:test, :kernel:test, :concord:check and ./gradlew test are green; npm run typecheck / test / build pass in inspect/ui. [15-APPLY-01]'s kernel contract is unchanged for existing callers per [WKB2-21]. The R4 failure-case catalogue is appended to a lane findings file per [WKB2-61]; the citation asymmetry is filed in concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md per [WKB2-63]. No plan or spec document edits [WKB2-62].

title: QRY2 — Recursive queries → cycle regions (stratification, iteration budget, :demo:reachability)
description:
# QRY2 — Recursive queries → cycle regions

Milestone-plan row (`computenet-milestone-plan.md` §1, Product lanes):

| **QRY2** — Recursive queries → cycle regions. **Depends on:** QRY1, KE5.
| **Unblocks:** *"E5's external consumer."*

§2's DAG carries `QRY1 --> QRY2` and `KE5 --> QRY2`; §5 places QRY2 in rank 20, the
"second wave". §1's kernel-lane row for KE5 lists its consumers as "AGO4, QRY2, BB-GRA,
BB-SNB BI".

--------

## 1. Ambition / Why

KE5 (`computenet-dud`, 96 §E5) builds cycles, `LoopContext`, iteration-cut fixpoint
detection and stratification admission. Its named in-repo adopter is `:demo:agora`'s
grounded-extension fixpoint (96 §E5.7) — an application that hand-builds one specific loop.
QRY2 is the *general* consumer the plan calls "E5's external consumer": the thing that turns
"the kernel can run a loop" into "any recursive query the user writes becomes a loop".

The gap this closes is the same one QRY1 closes for non-recursive queries, one level up.
Transitive closure, reachability, ancestor queries, PageRank-shaped iteration, LDBC SNB BI's
path queries and Graphalytics' BFS/WCC are all *recursion*, and every one of them is today
either impossible or hand-built. §1's BB rows make the demand concrete: **BB-GRA** ("PageRank,
BFS, SSSP, WCC, CDLP, LCC") depends on KE5, and **BB-SNB BI** "adds KE5". Neither can be
expressed without a recursive frontend unless someone hand-wires each algorithm as a cycle
region — the same "22 queries by hand" argument that justified QRY1, with a harder operator.

What makes QRY2 a *subsystem* rather than a QRY1 feature, and therefore an epic:

- It introduces a second compilation *shape*. QRY1's target is a DAG of `spawn`/`connect`
  steps. QRY2's target is a DAG **containing declared cycle regions**, each with a
  `CycleHead`, a `feedbackInput`, an ingress boundary, an egress boundary, and a settled/eager
  egress mode — structure `civictech.cell.graph.GraphSpec` must be able to express and that
  link-time admission must accept.
- It introduces **stratification** — a whole-program static analysis over the rule
  dependency graph with negation and aggregation edges, whose failure mode is not "slower"
  but "wrong or non-terminating".
- It introduces **non-termination** as a first-class outcome. A non-recursive compiler either
  answers or refuses. A recursive one can also run forever, and the requirements below must
  say precisely what happens then.

Spec anchors: `[21-CYCLE-01]` (admission: headless closure rejected, throttle-capability,
`Leased` forbidden), `[21-CYCLE-02]` (bounded-lap termination — the honest guarantee),
`[21-CYCLE-03]` (strong-tier fixpoint convergence — **a live gap row**), and 96 §E5.1's
decided stratification rule: *"non-monotone operators (antijoin/difference; E6's `negate`)
are inadmissible on a cycle path (`CycleRequiresStratification`)"*.

--------

## 2. What we build

### 2.1 Module decision, stated rather than assumed

**The compiler stays in `:query`.** QRY2 adds packages to the module QRY1 creates; it does
not fork a second compiler. A recursive query shares the catalog, the AST, the `Expr` algebra,
the lowering machinery, the rejection taxonomy and the `BatchEvaluator` seam with a
non-recursive one, and splitting them would duplicate every one of those.

**The new Gradle leaf module is the acceptance artifact: `:demo:reachability`
(directory `demo/reachability/`)** — a recursive-query demo application in the shape the
other incremental demos take (`demo/slotfinder`, `demo/skillmatch`), registered in
`settings.gradle.kts` and depending on `:demo:shell`, `:kernel` and `:query`:

```kotlin
include(":demo:reachability")     // <- new leaf module
```

```kotlin
// demo/reachability/build.gradle.kts
plugins { id("buildsrc.convention.kotlin-jvm") }
dependencies {
    implementation(project(":kernel"))
    implementation(project(":query"))
    implementation(project(":demo:shell"))
    testImplementation(project(":testkit"))
    testImplementation(project(":oracle"))
}
```

It hosts a live graph whose edges the user toggles and whose transitive closure, connected
components and shortest-hop distances are maintained incrementally — a directly observable
"the fixpoint adjusts, it does not recompute" artifact, and the substrate BB-GRA later plugs
its reference answers into.

### 2.2 New packages in `:query` (`query/src/main/kotlin/civictech/query/`)

| Package | Contents |
|---|---|
| `civictech.query.rec` | Recursive AST admission: `RecursiveRule`, the rule dependency graph `RuleGraph`, SCC computation over it |
| `civictech.query.strata` | `Stratifier` — negation/aggregation edge classification, stratum assignment, the `StratificationViolation` report |
| `civictech.query.plan` (extended) | `Fixpoint(recursivePredicates, body, stratum)` plan node; `LogicalPlan` becomes a stratified sequence of plan layers |
| `civictech.query.lower` (extended) | `CycleRegionLowering` — `Fixpoint` → a `GraphSpec` fragment carrying a `CycleHead`, its `feedbackInput`, ingress/egress boundary edges, and the egress mode |
| `civictech.query.diag` (extended) | New `RejectionCode` variants: `STRATIFICATION_VIOLATION`, `NONMONOTONE_IN_CYCLE`, `NESTED_RECURSION`, `WEAK_TIER_RECURSION`, `ITERATION_BUDGET_REQUIRED`, `EXCLUSIVE_ON_CYCLE_EDGE` |
| `civictech.query.ref` (extended) | `BatchEvaluator` gains naive stratified semi-naive-free evaluation: iterate each stratum to a fixpoint over plain collections |

### 2.3 Public entry points

No new top-level API. `QueryCompiler.compile` gains the ability to *accept* what
[QRY1-LANG-09] rejects, and `CompiledQuery` gains recursion metadata:

```kotlin
class CompiledQuery(
    val plan: LogicalPlan,
    val spec: GraphSpec,
    val sources: Map<String, TypedRef<SetApi<Row>>>,
    val outputs: Map<String, TypedRef<*>>,
    val strata: List<Stratum>,                 // QRY2: empty for a non-recursive query
    val budget: IterationBudget,               // QRY2: the declared bound, never a default
)
```

### 2.4 Tests shipped

`query/src/test/kotlin/civictech/query/rec/`, `.../strata/` — the stratification suite, the
cycle-region lowering structural tests, the new rejection tests, and the ORA1-driven recursive
differential suite. `demo/reachability/src/test/` — the demo's own seeded
incremental-vs-batch exit test in the `SlotPipeline`/`SkillPipeline` idiom.

--------

## 3. How, using ComputeNet

### 3.1 KE5 is consumed, never re-specified

This epic **cross-references** KE5's work rather than restating it. The following belong to
KE5 (`computenet-dud`, 96 §E5) and QRY2 must not re-implement, re-specify, or work around
them:

| Mechanism | Owner | What QRY2 does with it |
|---|---|---|
| `LoopContext(outerWave, iteration)` on `MessageContext` | KE5 / 96 §E5.2 | Never writes it. The head is its only writer. |
| Cycle-region identification (SCC capture at admission), ingress stamping, egress stripping | KE5 / 96 §E5.3 | Emits a `GraphSpec` whose admitted shape *produces* a region; reads the region back for diagnostics |
| Iteration-cut fixpoint detection at the head (`settled: LoopContext?`) | KE5 / 96 §E5.4 | Reads `settled` to decide when a recursive output is answerable |
| Incremental re-entry — fixpoint adjustment under new input | KE5 / 96 §E5.5 | Relies on it for BS-4; adds no per-lap state reset of its own |
| Stratification **admission check** (`NonMonotone` marker, `CycleRequiresStratification`) | KE5 / 96 §E5.6 | Rejects *earlier*, at compile time, with a better message; the kernel check remains the backstop |
| Hop guard, `CycleError` dead-letter | already landed / `[21-CYCLE-01]` | The hard backstop behind the compiler's budget |

The division is: **KE5 owns the iteration mechanism and its guarantees; QRY2 owns deciding
which queries may legally use it, and constructing the region.** Where they overlap — the
stratification check exists in both — QRY2's is a compile-time *refusal with a query-level
message*, and KE5's is the link-time admission that no compiler can be trusted to have run.

### 3.2 What a recursive query lowers to

For `path(x,z) :- edge(x,z). path(x,z) :- path(x,y), edge(y,z).`:

- `edge` → `SetCell<Row>` (`kernel/.../cell/data/SetCell.kt`), outside the region — an
  **ingress** source.
- The recursive predicate `path` → a `UnionSetCell<Row>`
  (`kernel/.../cell/data/op/UnionSetCell.kt`) designated the region's `CycleHead`, whose
  `feedbackInput` receives the recursive rule's output. `[24-OP-UNION-01]`'s tag-forwarding
  is exactly the "forward only new tag information" that makes a lap carrying no new
  information produce an empty effective delta — which is 96 §E5.4's fixpoint cut and
  `[21-CYCLE-02]`'s structural quiescence.
- The recursive rule body `path(x,y), edge(y,z)` → `JoinSetCell` + `FlatMapSetCell` inside
  the region, lowered by QRY1's existing rules.
- The join's output → the head's `feedbackInput`, closing the cycle.
- Downstream consumers of `path` → **egress** edges.

**Tier**: `SetDelta` is idempotent-merge, so a set-valued recursive query is
`[21-CYCLE-03]`'s **strong tier** — "WHERE a cycle's feedback deltas are idempotent-merge
(strong tier), the loop SHALL converge to a fixpoint". This is the only tier QRY2 admits;
[QRY2-REJECT-04] refuses the weak tier explicitly, because for `Magnitude`-only deltas the
spec states plainly that "the weak tier converges only if its loop map is contractive w.r.t.
`size()`, which the framework does not verify", and G-19 keeps weak-tier fixpoint convergence
an open research item.

**`[21-CYCLE-03]` is a live gap row** — the machinery it describes is not built. QRY2 is
therefore a consumer of genuinely unbuilt work, and [QRY2-HONEST-01] says so rather than
letting the epic read as if the kernel were ready.

### 3.3 Stratification, precisely

Build `RuleGraph`: a node per predicate, an edge `p → q` for each occurrence of `q` in a rule
defining `p`, labelled **positive**, **negative** (negated atom), or **aggregating** (the
occurrence is under a grouped aggregate).

- Compute SCCs. A predicate is *recursive* iff its SCC is non-trivial or it self-loops.
- A program is **stratified** iff no SCC contains a negative or aggregating edge.
- Stratum assignment: the condensation is a DAG; strata are its topological layers.

This is the standard rule, and it is also exactly what 96 §E5.1 point (4) decided at the
kernel level — "non-monotone operators (antijoin/difference; E6's `negate`) are inadmissible
on a cycle path" — read from the query side. The correspondence is the point: a query that
passes QRY2's stratifier compiles to a region containing no `SemiJoinCell(negated = true)`
and no `GroupByCell`, so KE5's admission check cannot fire on a query QRY2 accepted. If it
ever does, that is a compiler bug and [QRY2-STRAT-06] makes it a test.

### 3.4 The iteration budget

`[21-CYCLE-02]`'s guarantee is **bounded-lap termination**, backed structurally for the strong
tier and by the hop-guard dead-letter otherwise. It is a *termination* guarantee, not a
*bound the user chose*. A recursive query over a cyclic graph relation can legitimately need
many laps (transitive closure over a chain of length `n` needs `n` laps), so a compiler that
silently accepts any recursion accepts unbounded work.

QRY2 therefore requires an explicit `IterationBudget` per recursive query and reports budget
exhaustion as its own outcome — distinct from "no answer yet" and distinct from a value
mismatch. The budget is a **query-level policy**, layered above KE5's hop guard, not a
replacement for it: the hop guard remains the kernel's backstop for a region the compiler
mis-analysed. See [QRY2-TERM-01..07].

### 3.5 Determinism, driving, and the oracle seam

Unchanged from QRY1: `SimWorld`/`runToIdle`/`forEachSeed` from `testkit/`, and ORA1's
`DifferentialRunner.check(buildGraph, script, reference, seed)` bring-your-own entry point
(`[ORA1-DIFF-11]`). The reference is `BatchEvaluator`'s **stratified naive fixpoint** — iterate
each stratum to saturation over plain Kotlin collections, in stratum order — and the property
under test is that the incrementally maintained region equals it after every settle.

## 4. Functional requirements (EARS)

Ids are `[QRY2-<AREA>-nn]`. Each cites the normative spec id it makes true.

### 4.1 Recursive surface admission (`civictech.query.rec`)

- [QRY2-LANG-01] The frontend SHALL accept rules whose body reaches the rule's own head
  predicate through the rule dependency graph, superseding QRY1's blanket
  `RecursionUnsupported` refusal for programs that satisfy §4.2.
- [QRY2-LANG-02] The frontend SHALL accept **mutual** recursion — two or more predicates in
  one SCC — and compile the whole SCC as one cycle region, not as nested regions.
- [QRY2-LANG-03] The frontend SHALL require an explicit `IterationBudget` for every query
  containing at least one recursive predicate; the budget SHALL be part of the query or the
  compile call and SHALL NOT have a silent default.
- [QRY2-LANG-04] The `RuleGraph`, its SCC decomposition, and the stratum assignment SHALL be
  `Serializable` data reachable from `CompiledQuery`, so a compiled recursive query explains
  its own structure.
- [QRY2-LANG-05] Compilation of a recursive program SHALL be deterministic: the same
  `(Query, Catalog, IterationBudget)` SHALL yield an equal stratification and a structurally
  equal `GraphSpec` across JVM runs.

### 4.2 Stratification (`civictech.query.strata`)

- [QRY2-STRAT-01] The stratifier SHALL classify each rule-graph edge as positive, negative, or
  aggregating, where a negated atom yields a negative edge and an occurrence under a grouped
  aggregate yields an aggregating edge.
- [QRY2-STRAT-02] A program SHALL be admitted only if no strongly connected component of its
  rule graph contains a negative or aggregating edge (cites 96 §E5.1 point 4's decision that
  non-monotone operators are inadmissible on a cycle path).
- [QRY2-STRAT-03] IF a strongly connected component contains a negative or aggregating edge,
  THEN the compiler SHALL reject with `RejectionCode.STRATIFICATION_VIOLATION`, naming the
  cycle of predicates and the offending literal, and SHALL NOT compile the query
  (cites `[21-CYCLE-01]`).
- [QRY2-STRAT-04] WHEN a program is admitted, the compiler SHALL assign each predicate a
  stratum from a topological order of the rule graph's condensation, such that every negative
  or aggregating dependency crosses from a strictly lower stratum to a higher one.
- [QRY2-STRAT-05] The compiler SHALL lower strata in stratum order, such that no cycle region
  contains a cell derived from a higher or equal stratum's negation or aggregation.
- [QRY2-STRAT-06] A compiled recursive region SHALL contain no `SemiJoinCell` in negated mode
  and no `GroupByCell`, verified structurally over the emitted `GraphSpec`, such that KE5's
  link-time `CycleRequiresStratification` admission can never fire on a query QRY2 accepted
  (cites 96 §E5.6).
- [QRY2-STRAT-07] IF the compiler's structural check ([QRY2-STRAT-06]) fails on its own
  output, THEN compilation SHALL fail loudly as an internal compiler error rather than
  emitting the region and relying on the kernel to refuse it.

### 4.3 Lowering to cycle regions (`civictech.query.lower`)

- [QRY2-LOWER-01] Each `Fixpoint` plan node SHALL lower to a `GraphSpec` fragment containing
  exactly one `CycleHead` with a declared `feedbackInput` per strongly connected component,
  such that every admitted cycle contains a head (cites `[21-CYCLE-01]`).
- [QRY2-LOWER-02] The head SHALL be the union of the recursive predicate's rules — a
  `UnionSetCell` — so that a lap contributing no new tag information yields an empty effective
  delta and the loop quiesces structurally (cites `[24-OP-UNION-01]`, `[21-CYCLE-02]`).
- [QRY2-LOWER-03] Every data edge inside a compiled cycle region SHALL carry an
  idempotent-merge delta type (`SetDelta`), placing every compiled region in the strong tier
  (cites `[21-CYCLE-03]`).
- [QRY2-LOWER-04] Edges entering a region SHALL be lowered as ingress and edges leaving it as
  egress in the shape KE5's region classification expects; the compiler SHALL NOT stamp or
  strip `LoopContext` itself (cites 96 §E5.3).
- [QRY2-LOWER-05] WHERE a recursive query's consumer requires a settled answer rather than
  intermediate laps, the lowering SHALL select KE5's **settled egress** mode, re-associated to
  the outer wave; WHERE it does not, eager pass-through SHALL remain (cites 96 §E5.1 point 5).
- [QRY2-LOWER-06] The compiler SHALL NOT place an `Owned` or `Leased` payload on a cycle edge
  (cites `[21-CYCLE-01]`, which forbids `Leased` on cycle edges with `CycleRejectsLeased`).
- [QRY2-LOWER-07] A compiled recursive `GraphSpec` SHALL apply cleanly: `spec.applyTo(host)`
  SHALL produce no `StepResult.Rejected`, including no `CycleWithoutHead` and no
  `CycleRequiresMagnitude` (cites `[21-CYCLE-01]`).
- [QRY2-LOWER-08] All of QRY1's lowering requirements SHALL continue to hold inside a region —
  in particular the serializable-`Expr` factory discipline and the no-cell-class rule
  ([QRY1-LOWER-03], [QRY1-LOWER-06]).

### 4.4 Termination, budget, and non-terminating queries — the unwanted-behaviour core

`[21-CYCLE-02]` guarantees termination in bounded laps; it does **not** guarantee the bound is
one a user is willing to wait for, and `[21-CYCLE-03]`'s fixpoint convergence is scoped to the
strong tier. Everything in this section is written so that a recursive query that does not
settle produces a *named outcome*, never a hang and never a plausible-looking partial answer.

- [QRY2-TERM-01] An `IterationBudget` SHALL express a maximum lap count per outer wave, and
  SHALL be recorded in the compiled query rather than applied ambiently.
- [QRY2-TERM-02] IF a region reaches its `IterationBudget` for an outer wave without KE5's
  iteration cut reporting `settled`, THEN the outcome SHALL be reported as
  `BudgetExhausted(query, outerWave, laps)` — a distinct, named outcome, never a silent
  truncation and never a value mismatch.
- [QRY2-TERM-03] IF a region's budget is exhausted, THEN the region's output SHALL NOT be
  presented as an answer: a consumer reading through settled egress SHALL receive no settled
  answer for that outer wave, and a consumer reading eagerly SHALL be able to distinguish an
  unsettled intermediate state from a fixpoint (cites `[21-CYCLE-03]` — only a settled loop
  has converged to a fixpoint).
- [QRY2-TERM-04] WHILE a region is iterating and has not reported `settled`, no requirement of
  this epic SHALL claim its intermediate state equals the batch fixpoint — the equality claim
  is asserted **only** at a settle (cites `[21-CYCLE-03]`).
- [QRY2-TERM-05] The `IterationBudget` SHALL be a query-level policy layered above KE5's hop
  guard and SHALL NOT replace, raise, or disable it; the hop-guard `CycleError` dead-letter
  remains the kernel's backstop for a region the compiler mis-analysed (cites `[21-CYCLE-01]`).
- [QRY2-TERM-06] IF a compiled region dead-letters at the hop bound, THEN the failure SHALL be
  reported as a hop-guard failure distinct from `BudgetExhausted`, because the two indicate
  different defects — an under-budgeted query versus a mis-constructed region.
- [QRY2-TERM-07] WHEN new input reaches a settled region, the region SHALL adjust its fixpoint
  incrementally rather than recompute from empty, and the budget SHALL apply per outer wave
  rather than cumulatively (cites 96 §E5.5).
- [QRY2-TERM-08] IF a recursive query is written over a relation whose contents make its
  fixpoint infinite — recursion producing new constants without bound — THEN the compiler
  SHALL reject with `RejectionCode.UNSAFE_RULE` where the range-restriction analysis can prove
  it, and the budget SHALL catch what the analysis cannot; the compiler SHALL NOT claim to
  decide termination in general.

### 4.5 Rejection over best-effort lowering — unwanted behaviour

Everything QRY1's [QRY1-REJECT-01..10] states applies unchanged. The recursive additions:

- [QRY2-REJECT-01] IF any recursive construct cannot be lowered to a cycle region whose
  specified semantics realizes it exactly, THEN the compiler SHALL reject the whole query and
  SHALL NOT emit a partial region or a bounded unrolling as an approximation.
- [QRY2-REJECT-02] IF a query would require **nested** cycle regions — a recursive predicate
  whose body reaches a second, distinct recursion that is not in its own SCC and cannot be
  stratified below it — THEN the compiler SHALL reject with `RejectionCode.NESTED_RECURSION`,
  citing 96 §E5.1's decision that nested cycles are rejected at admission and single-level
  `LoopContext` only (→ 95 R16).
- [QRY2-REJECT-03] IF a recursive query's fixpoint would be reached only through a
  non-monotone operator, THEN the compiler SHALL reject with
  `RejectionCode.NONMONOTONE_IN_CYCLE` — this is [QRY2-STRAT-03] seen from the operator side,
  and the two SHALL agree on every input.
- [QRY2-REJECT-04] IF a recursive query's feedback deltas would not be idempotent-merge — a
  `Magnitude`-only weak-tier loop — THEN the compiler SHALL reject with
  `RejectionCode.WEAK_TIER_RECURSION`, citing `[21-CYCLE-03]` (the weak tier converges only
  under an unverified contractivity condition) and G-19 (weak-tier fixpoint convergence is an
  open research item). A weighted or numeric recursion is out of scope by refusal, not by
  approximation.
- [QRY2-REJECT-05] IF a recursive query carries no `IterationBudget`, THEN the compiler SHALL
  reject with `RejectionCode.ITERATION_BUDGET_REQUIRED` rather than supplying a default.
- [QRY2-REJECT-06] IF a compiled region would carry an exclusive payload, THEN the compiler
  SHALL reject with `RejectionCode.EXCLUSIVE_ON_CYCLE_EDGE` (cites `[21-CYCLE-01]`).
- [QRY2-REJECT-07] Every new `RejectionCode` variant SHALL be covered by at least one named
  test, extending [QRY1-REJECT-05]'s closed-enum discipline.

### 4.6 Validation against ORA1

- [QRY2-ORA-01] The recursive differential suite SHALL drive the kernel through ORA1's
  bring-your-own entry point (`[ORA1-DIFF-11]`) and SHALL NOT re-implement diffing, failure
  taxonomy or shrinking — the same constraint as [QRY1-ORA-01].
- [QRY2-ORA-02] The reference SHALL be `BatchEvaluator`'s **stratified naive fixpoint**:
  iterate each stratum to saturation over plain collections, in stratum order, with no
  incremental machinery.
- [QRY2-ORA-03] WHEN a compiled region reports `settled` for an outer wave, each recursive
  output relation's folded state SHALL equal the reference fixpoint over the script's contents
  at that point (cites `[21-CYCLE-03]`).
- [QRY2-ORA-04] The generated corpus SHALL include recursive programs over cyclic input
  relations — self-loops, mutual cycles, and dense graphs — because a recursion over an acyclic
  relation terminates for reasons that do not generalize.
- [QRY2-ORA-05] The generated update scripts SHALL include **deletions of edges participating
  in the fixpoint**, and the settled answer after deletion SHALL equal the reference recomputed
  from scratch (cites 96 §E5.5 — the fixpoint must *adjust*, not merely grow).
- [QRY2-ORA-06] The suite SHALL include a **divergence control**: a from-scratch-per-wave
  variant that blows a delta-count budget, and a state-resetting variant that diverges — both
  asserted to fail (mirrors 96 §E5.5's own control design and `[ORA1-DIFF-09]`).
- [QRY2-ORA-07] The suite SHALL include a **non-termination control**: a query whose budget is
  set below the fixpoint's required lap count, asserted to report `BudgetExhausted` naming the
  query and the lap count — and asserted **not** to report a value mismatch.
- [QRY2-ORA-08] The settled lap count SHALL be reported and asserted to be no greater than the
  batch solver's iteration count for the same input, so a lowering that iterates more than
  semi-naive evaluation requires is visible (mirrors 96 §E5.4's test design).
- [QRY2-ORA-09] IF the reference evaluator does not itself reach a fixpoint within its own
  bound, THEN the failure SHALL be reported as a reference-evaluation failure distinct from a
  compilation defect (mirrors `[ORA1-DIFF-08]`).

### 4.7 The demo artifact (`:demo:reachability`)

- [QRY2-DEMO-01] The demo SHALL express transitive closure, connected components, and
  shortest-hop distance as compiled recursive queries, not as hand-wired cycle regions.
- [QRY2-DEMO-02] WHEN a user adds or removes one edge, the demo SHALL show the affected
  derived answers changing without a full recompute, and the observable state SHALL equal the
  batch fixpoint at every settle.
- [QRY2-DEMO-03] The demo SHALL ship a seeded incremental-vs-batch exit test in the idiom of
  `demo/slotfinder` and `demo/skillmatch`, over a seed range including cyclic and disconnected
  input graphs.
- [QRY2-DEMO-04] The demo SHALL surface budget exhaustion visibly rather than appearing to
  hang, so `[21-CYCLE-02]`'s bounded-lap honesty is user-visible.

### 4.8 Honesty ledger

- [QRY2-HONEST-01] `[21-CYCLE-03]` is a **live gap row**: the fixpoint-convergence machinery
  is decided but unbuilt, and `LoopContext`/stratification do not exist in the kernel today.
  QRY2 is therefore a consumer of genuinely unbuilt work, and no requirement here may be
  reported as met while the KE5 mechanism it names is absent. The module KDoc SHALL state this
  dependency rather than hiding it behind a passing test over a stubbed loop.
- [QRY2-HONEST-02] Termination is **not decided** by this epic. [QRY2-TERM-08] is deliberately
  weak — range restriction where provable, budget otherwise — because deciding termination of
  a recursive query in general is not possible. Any requirement that would claim otherwise
  belongs in `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md`, not in a scenario.
- [QRY2-HONEST-03] Weak-tier (numeric/`Magnitude`) recursion is refused ([QRY2-REJECT-04]),
  which means **PageRank-shaped iteration is out of QRY2's scope**. BB-GRA's PageRank therefore
  still depends on G-19's research resolution or a hand-built weak-tier loop, not on QRY2. This
  narrows the plan's "BB-GRA depends on KE5" reading and SHALL be filed as a plan finding
  rather than silently assumed either way.
- [QRY2-HONEST-04] Cross-host cycles remain invisible to link-time admission (G-41; 96 §E5.3
  "cross-host cycles remain invisible to admission — the hop guard stays the backstop").
  QRY2 SHALL therefore compile regions on one host, and SHALL state that a placement splitting
  a region across hosts is unverified rather than assumed safe.

## 5. Behaviour specifications

Each becomes one named test. `covers:` notes mark corpus candidates.

**BS-1 — Transitive closure equals the batch fixpoint.**
*Given* `path(x,z) :- edge(x,z). path(x,z) :- path(x,y), edge(y,z).` with a budget above the
graph's diameter; *when* edges are added and the region settles; *then* `path` equals the
reference stratified fixpoint, and the settled lap count is no greater than the batch solver's.
→ [QRY2-ORA-03], [QRY2-ORA-08]. Concord-worthy: `covers: [21-CYCLE-03]` — but only once KE5
lands; until then it is a `:query` test and the corpus row stays a coverage gap
([QRY2-HONEST-01]).

**BS-2 — A non-terminating recursion is named, not hung.**
*Given* a transitive closure over a cyclic input graph with an `IterationBudget` deliberately
set below the required lap count; *when* the query runs; *then* `BudgetExhausted(query,
outerWave, laps)` is reported, no settled answer is emitted for that outer wave, and the
result is **not** reported as a value mismatch. *And* the test asserts on the outcome *kind*,
not on message text.
→ [QRY2-TERM-02], [QRY2-TERM-03], [QRY2-ORA-07]. This is the epic's defining failure case.

**BS-3 — A stratification violation is refused with the offending cycle named.**
*Given* `p(x) :- q(x), not p(x).`; *when* it is compiled; *then* it is rejected with
`RejectionCode.STRATIFICATION_VIOLATION` naming the predicate cycle and the negated literal,
and no `GraphSpec` is produced. *And* the equivalent operator-side check
([QRY2-REJECT-03]) agrees on the same input.
→ [QRY2-STRAT-03], [QRY2-REJECT-03], [QRY1-REJECT-04].

**BS-4 — The fixpoint adjusts under deletion.**
*Given* a settled transitive closure; *when* an edge participating in many derived paths is
deleted; *then* after the next settle `path` equals the reference recomputed from scratch —
every path that depended on the edge retracted, nothing else. *And* the from-scratch-per-wave
control blows the delta-count budget while this one does not.
→ [QRY2-ORA-05], [QRY2-ORA-06], [QRY2-TERM-07]. This is the "incremental must diverge from
naive recompute" case for recursion: naive recompute is *correct but ruinous*, and the control
proves the compiled form is doing semi-naive adjustment rather than restarting.

**BS-5 — An unsupported construct: weak-tier recursion.**
*Given* a recursion whose feedback carries a `Magnitude`-only numeric delta (a PageRank-shaped
loop); *when* it is compiled; *then* it is rejected with `RejectionCode.WEAK_TIER_RECURSION`
citing `[21-CYCLE-03]` and G-19, and no approximate bounded-unrolling graph is emitted.
→ [QRY2-REJECT-04], [QRY2-LOWER-03], [QRY2-HONEST-03].

**BS-6 — An empty relation.**
*Given* `path` defined over an `edge` relation that is declared and never written; *when* the
query is applied and driven to quiescence; *then* `path` is empty, the region settles at
iteration 0 (or 1) rather than iterating to the budget, and the host is quiescent — not
stalled and not dead-lettering.
→ [QRY2-ORA-03], [QRY2-TERM-02]. Boundary case.

**BS-7 — A self-join inside the region.**
*Given* `path(x,z) :- path(x,y), path(y,z).` — the recursive predicate joined with itself,
seeded by a base rule; *when* the region settles; *then* the answer equals the batch fixpoint,
and the region contains exactly one head despite two feedback paths.
→ [QRY2-LOWER-01], [QRY2-ORA-03]. The doubly-recursive form is where a per-rule head would be
wrongly emitted.

**BS-8 — Mutual recursion is one region.**
*Given* `even(0). even(x) :- odd(y), succ(y,x). odd(x) :- even(y), succ(y,x).`; *when* it is
compiled; *then* `even` and `odd` are in one SCC and lower to **one** cycle region with one
head, not two nested regions, and the settled answer equals the batch fixpoint.
→ [QRY2-LANG-02], [QRY2-LOWER-01], [QRY2-REJECT-02].

**BS-9 — Stratified negation above a recursion compiles.**
*Given* `path(...)` recursive, and `unreachable(x,y) :- node(x), node(y), not path(x,y).`;
*when* it is compiled; *then* it is admitted, `unreachable` sits in a strictly higher stratum,
and the emitted `GraphSpec` places its `SemiJoinCell(negated = true)` **outside** every cycle
region.
→ [QRY2-STRAT-04], [QRY2-STRAT-05], [QRY2-STRAT-06].

**BS-10 — The compiler never hands the kernel a region it must refuse.**
*Given* every query in the generated corpus that the compiler accepts; *when* each emitted
`GraphSpec` is applied to a host; *then* no step is `Rejected` — no `CycleWithoutHead`, no
`CycleRequiresMagnitude`, no `CycleRequiresStratification`, no `CycleRejectsLeased`.
→ [QRY2-LOWER-07], [QRY2-STRAT-06]. Concord-worthy: `covers: [21-CYCLE-01]` — the admission
rule itself is a kernel requirement and its corpus scenario belongs to KE5; this test is the
compiler-side claim that it never triggers, which is a `:query` test, not a corpus scenario.

**BS-11 — Budget exhaustion is distinguishable from a hop-guard dead-letter.**
*Given* a deliberately mis-constructed region (a headless closure forced past compile-time
checks in a test fixture); *when* it runs; *then* the hop guard dead-letters with `CycleError`
and the outcome is reported as a hop-guard failure, distinct from `BudgetExhausted`.
→ [QRY2-TERM-05], [QRY2-TERM-06].

**BS-12 — Compilation is deterministic and self-describing.**
*Given* one recursive program and catalog; *when* compiled twice in separate JVMs; *then* the
stratification and the `GraphSpec` are equal, and `CompiledQuery.strata` explains the
assignment.
→ [QRY2-LANG-04], [QRY2-LANG-05].

**BS-13 — The demo's exit test.**
*Given* `:demo:reachability` over a seed range of random graphs including cycles and
disconnected components; *when* each seeded script of edge adds and removes runs; *then* every
settled observable state equals the batch fixpoint on every seed, and no seed is replaced with
a friendlier one.
→ [QRY2-DEMO-02], [QRY2-DEMO-03].

## 6. Scope boundaries

- **KE5's mechanism.** `LoopContext`, region identification, ingress/egress stamping,
  iteration-cut detection, incremental re-entry, and the link-time stratification admission are
  **KE5** (`computenet-dud`, 96 §E5.1–E5.6). QRY2 consumes them (§3.1's table) and
  re-specifies none. If KE5's shape differs from §3.1's expectations, QRY2 adapts; it does not
  fork.
- **Weak-tier / numeric recursion.** Refused ([QRY2-REJECT-04]). G-19 keeps weak-tier fixpoint
  convergence an open research item and `[21-CYCLE-03]` scopes the fixpoint guarantee to the
  strong tier. Consequence for BB-GRA is stated in [QRY2-HONEST-03], not hidden.
- **Bag / weighted semantics.** Still deferred to 96 §E6 / 95 R17, exactly as in QRY1. `negate`
  is marked `NonMonotone` by E5.6 precisely so recursion through negation stays inadmissible;
  QRY2 inherits QRY1's set-semantic language unchanged.
- **Nested cycles.** Rejected at admission by 96 §E5.1's decision (single-level `LoopContext`
  only); the general structure is 95 R16. [QRY2-REJECT-02] refuses; it does not work around.
- **Cross-host cycle regions.** G-41 / 96 §E5.3 leave them invisible to admission.
  [QRY2-HONEST-04] states the limit; QRY2 does not build distributed cycle detection.
- **AGO4.** `demo/agora`'s grounded-extension fixpoint is 96 §E5.7 / AGO4's payload — a
  hand-built strong-tier adopter and KE5's own acceptance target. QRY2 must not pre-empt it,
  and must not build a third approximation of the head model on top of agora's application-level
  one.
- **BB-GRA and BB-SNB BI.** The suites, their generators, their reference answers and their
  numbers belong to the BB lane (`computenet-3xi`). QRY2 owes the recursive compiler and
  `:demo:reachability`, not a benchmark.
- **Cost-based recursive planning** (magic sets, demand transformation, join ordering inside a
  region). Not on the critical path; no requirement here depends on it.
- **Any kernel change.** QRY2 adds no cell and no kernel behaviour ([QRY1-LOWER-03] carried
  forward by [QRY2-LOWER-08]). A defect found in KE5's machinery is a pinned failing case plus
  a findings entry admitted to the kernel lane per plan §4/§6.
