title: JAR2 — Module versioning: schemaVersion discipline (G-49 residual), state migration, rollback
description:
# JAR2 — Module versioning: `schemaVersion` discipline (G-49 residual), state migration, rollback

Source: `computenet-milestone-plan.md` §1 (Product lanes, row JAR2), §2 DAG
(`JAR1 --> JAR2 --> JAR3`, `JAR2 --> WKB3`), §5 rank 20 ("Second wave").

Depends on: **JAR1** (`computenet-051`) — the `:loader` module, `ModuleClassLoader`,
validate-then-commit registration with provenance, and the unload lifecycle.
Unblocks: **WKB3** (live version-swap UI) and **JAR3** (jar-attached `GraphSpec`
deploy, upgrade variant).

**JAR2 must not assume JAR1's defect fixes exist until JAR1 lands.** JAR1 owns three
pre-existing defects (`ContractRegistry.register` mutating mid-loop with no
`unregister`; `WireCodec.json` built once at object init so a late jar's
`WireSerializers` can never reach the codec; loader-agnostic
`Class.forName(descriptor.fqn)` sites). JAR2 consumes those fixes *from `main`*, does
not re-solve them, and does not begin on the assumption that they are done.

---

## Ambition / Why

JAR1 makes a jar an addressable unit of live code. It deliberately records the
module's version string and **interprets nothing** (`[JAR1-DISC-04]`), and refuses a
same-`contractId` collision outright (`[JAR1-REG-05]`). That is the honest stopping
point for a chunk that cannot yet reason about *what a version means*.

JAR2 is where a version acquires meaning, and it lands on the last unresolved half of
**G-49**. `doc/spec/50-development-process/53-evolution.md:254-260` names exactly what
is "still by-convention, not built":

> a contract-version discipline guarding `importFrom` `schemaVersion` against
> same-FQN hash collisions; an explicit non-promotable declaration for hidden-state
> cells; a retention window for the retired incumbent's export snapshot with
> rollback-*after*-retire journal-reversal semantics (today's rollback only covers the
> in-window, pre-RETIRE case); and a transform-correctness generative harness.

Three of those four are JAR2's. (The fourth — coupled-flow windows — is G-53 and stays
out.) The same list appears verbatim as the G-49 gap block in
`doc/spec/10-programming-model/13-links.md:130-145`,
`doc/spec/20-dataflow-semantics/24-data-cells.md:755-772`, and the G-49 row of
`doc/spec/90-roadmap/91-gap-analysis.md:111`.

Why it matters now, concretely. `StateMigrating` today is:

```kotlin
interface StateMigrating {
    /** [prior] is the previous instance's [Stateful.snapshot] output. */
    fun importFrom(prior: Serializable)
}
```

(`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/evolve/Evolution.kt:31-34`.) The parameter is a
bare `java.io.Serializable`. **There is no `schemaVersion` anywhere in the codebase** —
`grep -rn schemaVersion --include=*.kt` returns nothing outside `doc/`. The decided
shape (93 I-27 §"Data shapes",
`doc/spec/90-roadmap/93-feature-interactions.md:10469-10477`) is:

```kotlin
interface StateMigrating { fun importFrom(prior: PriorState) }
data class PriorState(
    val snapshot: Delta,
    val schemaVersion: Int,                          // predecessor snapshot schema tag (P9)
    val outletWaves: Map<PortName, OutletWaveState>, // I-11 source continuity
)
```

So today a T1 transform receives an untagged blob and must *guess* which schema it is
looking at. That guess is the data-destruction path: a v3 candidate handed a v1
snapshot it silently mis-reads writes a wrong-but-plausible state into a live cell, the
gate goes green, downstream absorbs it as truth, and the incumbent is despawned at
RETIRE with no checkpoint retained. There is no undo. Every failure mode this epic
exists to prevent runs through that one missing integer.

And a second, sharper reason to do it *after JAR1*: 93 I-27 §8's first follow-on gap is
that `contractId = hash(FQN)` (`nature/src/main/kotlin/civictech/nature/ContractDescriptor.kt:24-33`,
`StableHash` at `:330`) means **two builds of the same-FQN contract interface with
different method sets collide on one id**. Before dynamic loading that could not happen
in a single process — one classpath, one build. JAR1 makes it reachable for the first
time. JAR2 is where it must be answered rather than discovered.

### Two-version coexistence — the question JAR1 declined, answered here

JAR1's honest non-requirements say: *"Two versions of the same contract shall coexist.
That is JAR2. JAR1 refuses the collision."* Answering it head-on, from the code:

**The answer is a split, and both halves are requirements.**

**(a) Two versions of the same *contract* FQN with divergent method sets MUST NOT
coexist. Ever. This is a permanent design constraint, not a scheduling deferral.**
`contractId = StableHash.of(fqn)` and the wire decodes ids only
(`ContractRegistry.register`'s own error message:
*"the wire decodes ids only, so a silent repoint mis-decodes frames"*,
`nature/src/main/kotlin/civictech/nature/ContractRegistry.kt:28-33`). Two divergent
descriptors under one id is a frame mis-decode by construction, and spec 53's
invariance line already forbids the operation that would want it: *"A contract or
merge-semantics change is not a promotion — it is ordinary topology surgery"*
(`53-evolution.md:196-199`). JAR2 therefore does **not** build side-by-side contract
versioning; it builds the discipline that makes the refusal *loud and early* instead of
a hash coincidence. Concretely: a contract **shape version** derived from the method-id
set, carried on `ContractDescriptor`, checked at registration and at PRECHECK.

**(b) Two versions of the same *cell implementation* FQN MUST coexist — and today they
silently clobber.** This is the case promotion depends on: an incumbent and a candidate
are two builds of the same logical cell, and during a shadow window both are live.
`ContractRegistry.register`'s last line is

```kotlin
module.cells.forEach { cellsByFqn[it.fqn] = it }
```

(`ContractRegistry.kt:37`) — a bare `put`. **No collision check, last write wins,
silently.** A second module contributing a `CellDescriptor` for the same cell FQN with a
different `manifest`, `color`, or `ports` overwrites the first, and every consumer
(spawn checks, `Proxy` resolution, drift assertions, the Inspector) reads the wrong
descriptor for one of the two live versions. JAR1 makes contract registration
provenance-tagged and reversible; JAR2 must extend that to **cell** descriptors, keyed
by `(owningModule, fqn)`, with resolution by the *live cell's own module* rather than by
FQN alone.

So: *coexistence of implementations, yes and it must be fixed; coexistence of contract
surfaces, no and it must be refused loudly.* `[JAR2-COEX-01..06]` state both.

---

## What we build

**Extends JAR1's `:loader`** (`loader/`, package `civictech.loader`) with a
`civictech.loader.version` sub-package, plus **additive changes in three existing
modules**. No new Gradle module: every piece of JAR2 has an existing owner, and a
second loader-adjacent module would fragment the registration story JAR1 just
consolidated.

| Where | What | Why there |
|---|---|---|
| `nature/src/main/kotlin/civictech/nature/ContractDescriptor.kt` | `ContractDescriptor.shapeVersion: Long` (additive, defaulted); `CellDescriptor.schemaVersion: Int` (additive, defaulted `0`) | Generated descriptors are authoritative runtime metadata (AGENTS.md); a version recomputed reflectively at runtime is exactly the forbidden shape |
| `nature/.../ContractRegistry.kt` | cell-descriptor provenance keying + shape-version conflict refusal | The `cellsByFqn` last-write-wins defect above; JAR1 fixed the contract half, JAR2 fixes the cell half |
| `gen/src/main/kotlin/civictech/gen/wire/ContractProcessor.kt` | emit `shapeVersion` (derived from the sorted `methodId` set) and `schemaVersion` (from a `@CellBase(schemaVersion = n)` / `@SchemaVersion` declaration) into the generated `ContractModule` tables | Generation time is the only place these are honest; computing them at load time re-derives from bytecode, which JAR1 `[JAR1-DISC-03]` forbids |
| `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/evolve/Evolution.kt` | `PriorState`; `StateMigrating.importFrom(PriorState)`; `Promotion.MigrationRefused`; `Promotion.NonPromotable`; a retained-checkpoint handle returned by `promote` | 93 I-27's decided shape; `Promotion` is the only caller of `importFrom` |
| `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/evolve/` (new file) | `MigrationPath` — the declared v→v transform chain and its gap/downgrade rules | The chain is the thing that must refuse rather than guess |
| `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/durability/` | rollback-checkpoint retention window + journal-reversal reader for post-RETIRE rollback | R9's "retention horizon" is a durability concern; the journal already exists here |
| `loader/src/main/kotlin/civictech/loader/version/` | `ModuleVersion` parsing/ordering; upgrade/downgrade classification; the module-level version policy that gates a load | JAR1 recorded the string; this is the "interpretation is JAR2" half |

### The four mechanisms

**1. Version discipline (two distinct versions, deliberately).**
- *Contract shape version* — `ContractDescriptor.shapeVersion`, a stable hash over the
  sorted `(methodId, exclusive, magnitude, idempotentMerge, keyIndex)` tuples. Not a
  human number: its only job is to make "same FQN, different surface" a detectable
  inequality instead of an id coincidence. Additive contract evolution keeps every
  existing `methodId` resolvable and therefore keeps the *superset* check passing (93
  I-27 R3/R5) while changing `shapeVersion` — so the two are checked separately: the
  superset governs promotion admission, the shape version governs registration.
- *Snapshot schema version* — `CellDescriptor.schemaVersion: Int`, declared by the cell
  author. This is the integer `PriorState.schemaVersion` carries and the thing a T1
  transform switches on.
- *Module version* — JAR1's recorded manifest string, now parsed and ordered.

**2. State migration with a declared path.** A candidate declares which predecessor
schema versions it can import, as a chain of single-step transforms (v1→v2, v2→v3), not
an open `importFrom(Serializable)`. `Promotion` PRECHECK resolves the chain from
`prior.schemaVersion` to the candidate's; **an unresolvable chain aborts PRECHECK, before
the gate ever turns red** — the phase 53 guarantees is "freely abortable" with "the
incumbent untouched and zero traffic buffered" (`53-evolution.md:115-122`).

**3. Rollback, in both windows.**
- *In-window* (pre-RETIRE) already works: `Promotion.promote`'s catch block reverses
  relinks and re-greens onto the retained incumbent (`Evolution.kt:228-242`). JAR2 must
  not weaken it, and must extend it to reverse a *partially applied migration chain*.
- *Post-RETIRE* does not exist. 93 I-27 R9 decides the shape: the single `exportState`
  snapshot doubles as the rollback checkpoint, retained for a **retention horizon**;
  rollback re-spawns the incumbent from it as the reverse candidate, with journal
  reversal for anything emitted since. JAR2 builds the retention window, the reversal,
  and — critically — the **refusal** when the horizon has passed.

**4. Non-promotable declaration for hidden-state cells.** 93 I-27 §8: a cell whose
recoverable state is not fully expressible in its invariant delta contract can be
bridged neither by the delta interchange (R4) nor by catch-up (R6). Today it promotes
anyway and loses state silently. JAR2 gives it a declaration and PRECHECK refuses it.

### What a migration is allowed to touch

The invariance line (`53-evolution.md:189-199`, 93 I-27 R3) is inherited unchanged and
is a **scope wall for this epic**: a promotion MAY evolve private representation, cell
logic, and the snapshot schema. It MAY NOT evolve a port contract or a delta's merge
semantics. JAR2 makes the snapshot-schema half safe. It does **not** invent contract
migration, adapter synthesis, or delta-format negotiation.

---

## How, using ComputeNet

Real types, real paths, in the order the swap touches them.

**PRECHECK** (`Promotion.promote`, `Evolution.kt:145-176`) gains four checks, all
side-effect-free and all before `gate.controlInlet.call.setRed()`:

1. *Shape check.* `ContractRegistry.descriptor(outlet.clazz)?.shapeVersion` for
   incumbent and candidate must be equal, in addition to the existing
   `from.clazz != to.clazz` structural check at `:161`. Under JAR1 both classes may come
   from different `ModuleClassLoader`s, so `clazz` identity alone no longer proves the
   surfaces agree — this is the concrete same-FQN-hash-collision guard G-49 asks for.
2. *Chain resolution.* Read `incumbent`'s `CellDescriptor.schemaVersion` and
   `candidate`'s; ask the candidate's `MigrationPath` for a transform chain. Absent
   chain ⇒ `PromotionAborted("PRECHECK", …)`. Equal versions ⇒ T0 (`restore`) and no
   chain needed.
3. *Direction check.* A candidate schema version strictly lower than the incumbent's is
   a **downgrade** and is refused unless the candidate declares a reverse transform
   explicitly (see `[JAR2-DOWN-01..03]`).
4. *Non-promotable check.* A candidate or incumbent declaring the hidden-state marker
   is refused.

The existing `NonIdempotentCatchUp` refusal (`Evolution.kt:169-176`) stays exactly as
written; JAR2 adds to it, never relaxes it.

**COMMIT** (`Evolution.kt:186-227`) changes in one place. Today:

```kotlin
(candidate as StateMigrating).importFrom((incumbent as Stateful).snapshot())
to.adoptWaveState(from.waveState())
```

becomes: build `PriorState(snapshot, incumbentSchemaVersion, outletWaves)`, run the
resolved chain, then adopt wave state. `adoptWaveState`/`waveState()` (T0/T1 source
continuity, 93 I-11) and the T2 `mintFreshEpoch()` + `ReBaselineEmitting.reBaseline`
fallback at `:200-210` are untouched — JAR2 does not renegotiate the tier model, it
supplies the version tag T1 was always supposed to read.

COMMIT is **non-vetoing** (`53-evolution.md:128-133`): an exception there is an
infrastructure fault, not admission. That is why chain resolution is PRECHECK's job.
A transform that *throws* mid-chain is an infrastructure fault and takes the existing
rollback path — which is precisely the "migration failing halfway" scenario, and the
reason `[JAR2-MIG-05]` demands the candidate be left in no partially-migrated state
that a retry could observe.

**RETIRE** (`Evolution.kt:244-247`) is where the retention window is installed:
`host.managementInlet.call.despawn(incumbent.ref)` runs only after a successful COMMIT
(`[15-DESPAWN-01]`, and `[15-SNAPSHOT-01]` captures `Stateful` snapshots at the drain
point). JAR2 hands the caller a `RollbackCheckpoint` holding the already-taken
`exportState` snapshot plus the incumbent's `CellDescriptor.schemaVersion` and its
`OutletWaveState` — *one capture, two consumers*, per R9. No second snapshot in the
drain window.

**Post-RETIRE rollback** re-spawns the incumbent as the reverse candidate through the
same `Promotion.promote` — "a fresh swap in the reverse direction, identical protocol"
(`53-evolution.md:148-150`). The reverse direction is a *downgrade* by construction,
which is exactly why `[JAR2-DOWN-02]` exempts a checkpoint-backed reverse swap from the
downgrade refusal: it is restoring a state that provably existed, not inventing one.
Journal reversal for deltas emitted after RETIRE uses the existing per-cell journal
(`[24-DUR-02]`, `[24-DUR-03]`, `civictech.cell.durability`).

**`Owned`/`Leased` in a snapshot.** `Stateful.snapshot(): Serializable` is
state-as-delta-from-empty. If that delta carries an exclusive payload
(`MethodDescriptor.exclusive`, `[12-EXCL-01]`), a discarded snapshot — the T2 path, a
refused migration, an expired checkpoint — is a **silent exclusive drop**, which
AGENTS.md's core invariants forbid outright: *"no failure, suppression, shadow, park, or
dead-letter path may silently drop an exclusive payload."* `[JAR2-OWN-01..04]` make
every discard path an explicit discharge.

**Loader integration.** JAR1's `ModuleHandle.version` is a recorded string. JAR2 parses
it into `ModuleVersion`, and the loader gains a **version-aware refusal**: loading
module `M@2.0` while `M@1.0` is registered is legal iff every contract FQN they share
has an equal `shapeVersion` (case (a) above). This is the load-time counterpart of the
PRECHECK shape check, and it is what makes JAR3's upgrade variant expressible.

---

## Functional requirements (EARS)

Style follows `doc/spec/`'s convention (`[21-PULL-01]`, `[24-CATCHUP-01]`): uppercase
WHEN / WHILE / IF-THEN / WHERE, SHALL for the obligation. Ids are epic-scoped
(`[JAR2-…]`) and deliberately do not occupy the normative `[NN-SLUG-nn]` namespace.
Each cites the normative statement it makes true. Where the cited target is decided
prose without an EARS id (spec 53 has **zero** `[NN-SLUG-nn]` ids — verified), the
citation is section-anchored.

### Version discipline — ubiquitous

`[JAR2-VER-01]` Every `ContractDescriptor` SHALL carry a `shapeVersion` derived at
generation time from its complete method set, such that two builds of the same contract
FQN with different method sets carry different `shapeVersion` values. *(G-49 residual:
"a contract-version discipline guarding `importFrom` `schemaVersion` against same-FQN
hash collisions", `53-evolution.md:254-256`; 93 I-27 §8.)*

`[JAR2-VER-02]` Every `CellDescriptor` SHALL carry a `schemaVersion: Int` declaring the
schema of the state its `Stateful.snapshot()` produces, defaulting to `0` for a cell
that declares none. *(93 I-27 §"Data shapes"; 53 §G-33 "T1 … reads the predecessor
`schemaVersion`".)*

`[JAR2-VER-03]` `shapeVersion` and `schemaVersion` SHALL be emitted by the KSP
`ContractProcessor` into the generated `ContractModule` tables, and SHALL NOT be
computed, re-derived, or inferred reflectively at load or promotion time. *(AGENTS.md
"Generated descriptors/proxies are authoritative runtime metadata"; `[JAR1-DISC-03]`.)*

`[JAR2-VER-04]` A module's recorded version string SHALL be parsed into an orderable
`ModuleVersion`, and two module versions SHALL be comparable as strictly-greater,
strictly-less, or equal-or-incomparable. *(Completes `[JAR1-DISC-04]`, which records
without interpreting.)*

`[JAR2-VER-05]` IF a module's recorded version string cannot be parsed as a
`ModuleVersion`, THEN the loader SHALL refuse the load with a diagnostic naming the
string, and SHALL NOT fall back to an implicit ordering. *(A guessed order is a silent
downgrade waiting to happen.)*

### Two-version coexistence — the decided answer

`[JAR2-COEX-01]` The system SHALL permit two loaded modules to contribute
`CellDescriptor`s for the same cell FQN with different `schemaVersion` values, and both
SHALL remain independently resolvable for the lifetime of both modules. *(53 §Model
"Multiple implementations of a logical cell coexist"; this is the incumbent/candidate
shadow window, `52`/G-32.)*

`[JAR2-COEX-02]` The registries SHALL resolve a `CellDescriptor` by
`(owningModule, fqn)`, and a `CellDescriptor` lookup for a live cell SHALL resolve
against the module that contributed the cell's own class. *(Fixes
`ContractRegistry.kt:37`'s unchecked `cellsByFqn[it.fqn] = it`, which is last-write-wins
today.)*

`[JAR2-COEX-03]` IF two loaded modules contribute `CellDescriptor`s for the same cell
FQN that differ in any field, THEN the registry SHALL retain both under their owning
modules and SHALL NOT overwrite either. *(Same defect; stated as the positive
obligation.)*

`[JAR2-COEX-04]` The system SHALL NOT permit two loaded modules to contribute
`ContractDescriptor`s for the same contract FQN with different `shapeVersion` values.
*(`ContractRegistry.register`'s own stated reason: "the wire decodes ids only, so a
silent repoint mis-decodes frames"; 53 §G-33 invariance line, `:189-199`.)*

`[JAR2-COEX-05]` IF a module contributes a `ContractDescriptor` whose `shapeVersion`
differs from a registered descriptor for the same FQN, THEN registration SHALL be
refused with a diagnostic naming the FQN, both `shapeVersion` values, and both owning
modules, and no part of that module SHALL be registered. *(Strengthens
`[JAR1-REG-05]`/`[JAR1-REG-01]` from an equality check on the whole descriptor to a
named, diagnosable version conflict.)*

`[JAR2-COEX-06]` The refusal in `[JAR2-COEX-04]` SHALL be documented as a permanent
design constraint of the ids-only wire, not a deferred capability. *(53: "A contract or
merge-semantics change is not a promotion — it is ordinary topology surgery",
`:196-199`. Recording this normatively is the response to bd's epic→feature edge
constraint noted under Dependencies.)*

### Migration admission — event-driven

`[JAR2-MIG-01]` WHEN `Promotion.promote` runs PRECHECK, it SHALL compare the incumbent's
and candidate's contract `shapeVersion` for the swap outlet in addition to the existing
structural `(portName, contractId)` check, and SHALL abort on inequality. *(53 §The
promotion swap step 1, `:115-122`; `[13-REBIND-02]`.)*

`[JAR2-MIG-02]` WHEN a candidate declares `StateMigrating`, `Promotion.promote` SHALL
pass a `PriorState` carrying the incumbent's snapshot, the incumbent's `schemaVersion`,
and its per-outlet `OutletWaveState`. *(93 I-27 §"Data shapes"; 53 §G-33 tier T1.)*

`[JAR2-MIG-03]` WHEN incumbent and candidate `schemaVersion` are equal and the candidate
is `Stateful`, the promotion SHALL take the T0 `restore(snapshot)` path and SHALL NOT
invoke a transform. *(53 §G-33 "T0 (restore) — snapshot schemas match".)*

`[JAR2-MIG-04]` WHEN incumbent and candidate `schemaVersion` differ, PRECHECK SHALL
resolve a chain of declared single-step transforms from the incumbent's version to the
candidate's, and SHALL abort the promotion — incumbent untouched, gate never red — if no
complete chain exists. *(53 §The promotion swap step 1: "Any failure aborts with the
incumbent untouched and zero traffic buffered".)*

`[JAR2-MIG-05]` WHEN a resolved chain is executed during COMMIT, each step SHALL be
applied to an off-live working state, and the candidate's live state SHALL be replaced
only once every step has completed. *(Core invariant: no partially-applied migration is
ever observable; 53 COMMIT is non-vetoing so a mid-chain fault must reach the existing
rollback path, `Evolution.kt:228-242`.)*

`[JAR2-MIG-06]` WHERE the candidate declares the hidden-state marker (state not fully
expressible in its invariant delta contract), PRECHECK SHALL refuse the promotion.
*(G-49 residual: "an explicit non-promotable declaration for hidden-state cells",
`53-evolution.md:255-256`; 93 I-27 §8.)*

`[JAR2-MIG-07]` WHEN a promotion is refused for any version reason, the diagnostic SHALL
name the incumbent version, the candidate version, and the specific missing or refused
step. *(A refusal a human cannot act on gets worked around, and the workaround is a
manual state edit.)*

### Migration execution — state-driven

`[JAR2-MIG-08]` WHILE a migration chain is executing inside the buffered swap window,
the incumbent SHALL remain retained, hot, and linked. *(53 §Rollback: "the incumbent is
retained hot with its links until COMMIT fully succeeds", `:144-147`; `[15-PROMOTE-01]`
context.)*

`[JAR2-MIG-09]` WHILE a migration chain is executing, inbound traffic SHALL remain
parked in the `Buffering` window in order, with its contexts, and SHALL be replayed on
green. *(`[15-PARK-01]`, `[13-NOLOSS-01]`; 53 §The promotion swap step 2/3.)*

`[JAR2-MIG-10]` WHEN a T0/T1 migration completes, the candidate SHALL adopt the
incumbent's `OutletWaveState` per outlet, continuing the same `sourceId` and counter.
*(`[22-SRC-01]`; 93 I-11/I-27 R6; already implemented at `Evolution.kt:198` — JAR2 must
not regress it.)*

### Unwanted behaviour — the destruction paths

This is the section JAR2 exists for. A migration that cannot run must **refuse**, not
partially apply; a rollback must restore observably-equivalent state or **refuse**; a
discarded state carrying an exclusive payload must **discharge** it.

`[JAR2-BAD-01]` IF a migration chain step throws, THEN the promotion SHALL abort with
`PromotionAborted("COMMIT", …)`, SHALL reverse every completed relink, SHALL re-green
the gate onto the retained incumbent, and SHALL leave the candidate's live state exactly
as it was before COMMIT began. *(53 §Rollback, `:144-150`; the existing catch block at
`Evolution.kt:228-242` is the mechanism.)*

`[JAR2-BAD-02]` IF a migration chain step throws, THEN the incumbent SHALL NOT be
despawned. *(RETIRE runs strictly after a successful COMMIT, `53-evolution.md:249-250`,
`Evolution.kt:244-247`; `[15-DESPAWN-01]`.)*

`[JAR2-BAD-03]` IF no transform exists for a gap in the version sequence (e.g. a v3
candidate over a v1 incumbent with no v1→v2 step declared), THEN the promotion SHALL be
refused at PRECHECK, and the candidate SHALL NOT be offered the v1 snapshot under any
tier. *(The T2 fallback is not a legal escape from a missing transform: 53 §G-33 makes
T2 sound only for source-idempotent cells, and `[15-PROMOTE-01]` makes that restriction
normative.)*

`[JAR2-BAD-04]` IF a candidate's `schemaVersion` is strictly lower than the incumbent's
and no reverse transform is declared, THEN the promotion SHALL be refused as a
downgrade. *(93 I-27 R4: the transform is directional; an implicit reverse is a guess.)*

`[JAR2-BAD-05]` IF a rollback cannot restore state observably equivalent to the
pre-promotion state — the retention horizon has passed, the checkpoint is absent, or the
journal suffix is truncated — THEN the rollback SHALL be refused with a diagnostic and
SHALL leave the current live state untouched. *(G-49 residual: "a retention window for
the retired incumbent's export snapshot with rollback-*after*-retire journal-reversal
semantics"; `[24-DUR-02]`. A best-effort rollback that half-restores is worse than
none.)*

`[JAR2-BAD-06]` IF a migration or rollback would discard a state value carrying an
`Owned` or `Leased` payload, THEN that payload SHALL be explicitly discharged, and SHALL
NOT be dropped, garbage-collected, or left to a finalizer. *(AGENTS.md core invariant;
`[12-EXCL-01]`; 93 I-27 R5 "Parked `Owned`/`Leased` payloads retain exclusivity across
the window … and are consumed exactly once on replay".)*

`[JAR2-BAD-07]` IF the T2 catch-up fallback discards the incumbent's snapshot and that
snapshot carries exclusive payloads, THEN they SHALL be discharged before the fresh
epoch is minted. *(Same invariant, applied to the tier that discards by design;
`Evolution.kt:199-210`.)*

`[JAR2-BAD-08]` IF a retention window expires while a `RollbackCheckpoint` still holds
exclusive payloads, THEN expiry SHALL discharge them explicitly and SHALL record the
discharge observably. *(Same invariant, applied to time-based disposal — the path
easiest to overlook because nobody is watching when it fires.)*

`[JAR2-BAD-09]` The system SHALL NOT permit a migration to run against a snapshot whose
`schemaVersion` is absent or unknown to the candidate; an unversioned snapshot SHALL be
treated as an unresolvable chain per `[JAR2-MIG-04]`. *(The pre-JAR2 status quo — an
untagged `Serializable` — must become inexpressible, not merely discouraged.)*

`[JAR2-BAD-10]` A refused migration SHALL leave the registries, the gate, the incumbent,
the candidate, and the journal in the state they held before `promote` was called.
*(53 §The promotion swap step 1; PRECHECK is "no side effects, freely abortable".)*

### Rollback and retention — event-driven and state-driven

`[JAR2-RB-01]` WHEN a promotion reaches RETIRE, the system SHALL retain the incumbent's
already-captured `exportState` snapshot, its `schemaVersion`, and its `OutletWaveState`
as a `RollbackCheckpoint` for a declared retention horizon. *(93 I-27 R9: "The single
`exportState` snapshot serves two consumers"; G-49 residual "retention window".)*

`[JAR2-RB-02]` The system SHALL NOT take a second snapshot for rollback purposes; the
checkpoint SHALL be the same capture `importFrom` consumed. *(93 I-27 R9 explicitly:
"composes with G-25 by sharing the snapshot, not by adding a second capture in the drain
window"; also the P2 fast-path argument.)*

`[JAR2-RB-03]` WHILE a `RollbackCheckpoint` is within its retention horizon, a post-RETIRE
rollback SHALL be admissible and SHALL execute as a fresh promotion in the reverse
direction, re-spawning the incumbent from the checkpoint as the reverse candidate.
*(53 §Rollback: "Rollback after a successful promotion is a fresh swap in the reverse
direction, identical protocol", `:148-150`.)*

`[JAR2-RB-04]` WHEN a post-RETIRE rollback runs, deltas the candidate emitted after
RETIRE SHALL be reversed through the invocation journal, and downstream SHALL converge
to a value consistent with the restored state. *(`[21-REBASE-01]`; 53 §Mechanical
decomposition, "Roll back — same swap, reversed; journaled invocations replay";
`[24-DUR-02]`.)*

`[JAR2-RB-05]` WHERE the promoted cell is volatile (`journalFor(cellRef) == null`), a
post-RETIRE rollback SHALL be refused, because no journal suffix exists to reverse.
*(`[24-DUR-01]`: a volatile cell is "never journaled, never replayed". Refusing is the
honest outcome; a snapshot-only restore would silently lose post-RETIRE deltas.)*

`[JAR2-RB-06]` WHEN a `RollbackCheckpoint` expires, the system SHALL record the
expiry observably and SHALL make subsequent rollback attempts refuse per
`[JAR2-BAD-05]`. *(An expired-but-silent checkpoint is indistinguishable from a present
one until the moment it matters.)*

`[JAR2-RB-07]` A `RollbackCheckpoint`'s retention horizon SHALL be configurable per
host and SHALL have an explicit default. *(G-49 residual names the horizon as the open
question; leaving it implicit re-opens the gap.)*

### Loader integration — event-driven and optional-feature

`[JAR2-MOD-01]` WHEN a module is loaded while another module with the same module id and
a different `ModuleVersion` is registered, the loader SHALL permit the load iff every
contract FQN the two share carries an equal `shapeVersion`, and SHALL refuse it
otherwise per `[JAR2-COEX-05]`. *(The load-time counterpart of `[JAR2-MIG-01]`;
consumes `[JAR1-REG-01]`'s validate-then-commit.)*

`[JAR2-MOD-02]` WHERE two versions of a module are loaded, `ModuleHandle` SHALL report
its parsed `ModuleVersion`, and the set of loaded handles SHALL be enumerable by module
id and version. *(Extends JAR1's `ModuleHandle` surface; WKB3 and JAR3 both read it.)*

`[JAR2-MOD-03]` WHEN a module is unloaded, its `CellDescriptor`s SHALL be removed under
its own provenance key, and the other version's SHALL remain resolvable.
*(`[JAR1-UNL-03]` applied to the cell half `[JAR2-COEX-02]` introduces.)*

`[JAR2-MOD-04]` IF an unload is requested for a module holding a live
`RollbackCheckpoint` that is still within its retention horizon, THEN the unload SHALL be
refused. *(A checkpoint whose classes have been unloaded cannot be restored;
`[JAR1-UNL-02]` refuses unload while cells are live, and a live checkpoint is a
deferred cell.)*

### Observability — ubiquitous

`[JAR2-OBS-01]` Every version-based refusal (registration, load, PRECHECK, downgrade,
rollback) SHALL be emitted through the host's existing observation seam, naming both
versions and the refusal reason. *(`[JAR1-SEC-04]`'s load-record obligation, extended to
version decisions; WKB3 renders exactly these.)*

`[JAR2-OBS-02]` A completed migration SHALL record the resolved chain (the ordered list
of version steps applied) observably. *(An unrecorded transform chain makes a
post-incident answer to "which transform ran?" unavailable.)*

### Honest non-requirements

Deliberately **not** requirements, because they cannot be verified honestly:

- *"Two versions of the same contract shall coexist."* Refused permanently by
  `[JAR2-COEX-04]`/`[JAR2-COEX-06]` — not deferred. The ids-only wire makes it a
  mis-decode, and 53's invariance line makes the operation that wants it not a promotion.
- *"A migration transform shall be correct."* Unverifiable in general. What is
  verifiable is 93 I-27 §8's third residual — a **generative harness** asserting that a
  T1 transform yields a downstream stream identical to the unswapped control across a
  representation change (generalizing `ShadowPromotionTest`'s v1 `Long` → v2 string
  case, `53-evolution.md:176-178`). B9 below is that harness. "Correct" is not claimed;
  "stream-equivalent to the control over N seeds" is.
- *"Rollback shall always be possible."* False whenever the horizon has passed or the
  cell is volatile. `[JAR2-BAD-05]` and `[JAR2-RB-05]` state the refusal instead.
- *"A hidden-state cell shall be migrated safely."* It cannot be; `[JAR2-MIG-06]`
  refuses it. Building a private snapshot channel for such cells is a distinct,
  unscheduled chunk (93 I-27 §8's last bullet).
- *"Coupled-flow windows during a migration shall complete."* That is **G-53**
  (`53-evolution.md:136-142`) and is explicitly out of scope. If a JAR2 scenario is
  found to depend on it, the honest resolution is an entry in
  `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md`, not a weakened scenario.

## Behaviour specifications (Given / When / Then)

Each scenario becomes one named test. Concord-corpus applicability is assessed per
scenario at the end.

### B1 — Version tags are generated, not derived

```
Given a cell class declaring snapshot schema version 3
  And a contract interface with four methods
When the module is compiled by the KSP ContractProcessor
Then the generated ContractModule's CellDescriptor carries schemaVersion == 3
  And its ContractDescriptor carries a shapeVersion
When one method is added to the contract and it is recompiled
Then shapeVersion differs from the previous build
  And every previously existing methodId still resolves via ContractRegistry.idsOf
```
The second half is the additive-evolution case 93 I-27 R3 depends on: the superset check
still passes while the shape version legitimately changes.
Covers `[JAR2-VER-01]`, `[JAR2-VER-02]`, `[JAR2-VER-03]`.

### B2 — Same-FQN contract collision is named, not coincidental

```
Given module A registered, contributing contract C with three methods
  And module B contributing a contract with the same FQN and four methods
When B is loaded
Then the load fails with a diagnostic naming C's FQN, both shapeVersions, and both
     module ids
  And nothing from B is registered
  And every descriptor A contributed is still resolvable
```
This is the same-FQN hash-collision guard G-49 asks for. Note it must fail with a
*version* diagnostic, not the generic `contractId collision` message
`ContractRegistry.kt:28` produces today.
Covers `[JAR2-COEX-04]`, `[JAR2-COEX-05]`, `[JAR2-MOD-01]`.

### B3 — Two implementation versions coexist without clobbering

```
Given module A@1.0 contributing CellDescriptor for cell FQN X with schemaVersion 1
  And module B@2.0 contributing CellDescriptor for the same FQN X with schemaVersion 2,
      an identical contract surface, and a different manifest
When both are loaded
Then both CellDescriptors are resolvable under their owning modules
  And a live cell spawned from A resolves to A's descriptor
  And a live cell spawned from B resolves to B's descriptor
When A is unloaded
Then B's descriptor still resolves and B's live cells are unaffected
```
Fails today against `cellsByFqn[it.fqn] = it` (`ContractRegistry.kt:37`) — the second
registration silently wins and A's live cell reads B's manifest.
Covers `[JAR2-COEX-01]`, `[JAR2-COEX-02]`, `[JAR2-COEX-03]`, `[JAR2-MOD-03]`.

### B4 — Migration failing halfway

```
Given an incumbent at schemaVersion 1 with live downstream subscribers and a
      non-empty state
  And a candidate at schemaVersion 3 declaring transforms v1→v2 and v2→v3,
      where v2→v3 throws
When Promotion.promote runs
Then PRECHECK passes (a complete chain exists) and the gate goes red
  And COMMIT fails with PromotionAborted("COMMIT", …)
  And every completed relink is reversed and the gate is green onto the incumbent
  And the incumbent is NOT despawned and its state is byte-identical to pre-promotion
  And the candidate's live state is byte-identical to its pre-COMMIT state
      (no v1→v2 result is left installed)
  And buffered inbound replays into the incumbent with nothing dropped and no dead-letter
  And downstream subscribers observe no glitch and no gap in the source's counter
```
The "candidate's live state is byte-identical" clause is the load-bearing one and the
reason `[JAR2-MIG-05]` requires an off-live working state. Covers `[JAR2-BAD-01]`,
`[JAR2-BAD-02]`, `[JAR2-MIG-05]`, `[JAR2-MIG-08]`, `[JAR2-MIG-09]`.

### B5 — Rollback after a partially-applied migration

```
Given the exact end state of B4 (a failed mid-chain migration, incumbent re-greened)
When the same promotion is retried with a fixed v2→v3 transform
Then the retry succeeds, and the state the candidate ends with is identical to the
     state a single clean run would have produced
When, separately, the failure is instead followed by a rollback request
Then the rollback is a no-op that reports "nothing to roll back — the promotion never
     committed", and refuses rather than manufacturing a reverse swap
```
The second arm is the trap: a failed in-window promotion has *already* rolled back, and
a second rollback on top of it would swap the incumbent out. Covers `[JAR2-BAD-01]`,
`[JAR2-BAD-10]`, `[JAR2-RB-03]`.

### B6 — A schemaVersion gap: v1 → v3 with no v2 transform

```
Given an incumbent at schemaVersion 1
  And a candidate at schemaVersion 3 declaring only a v2→v3 transform
When Promotion.promote runs
Then PRECHECK aborts with a diagnostic naming 1, 3, and the missing v1→v2 step
  And the gate never turns red
  And no inbound traffic was buffered
  And the candidate's importFrom was never called
  And the incumbent was never snapshotted
And the same holds when the candidate declares StateMigrating but no chain at all
And the T2 catch-up fallback is NOT taken as a substitute for the missing transform
```
The last two clauses are the ones that decide whether this epic is worth anything: the
attractive wrong implementation silently falls back to T2 and re-baselines downstream
from the candidate's shadow state, which for a non-source-idempotent cell double-counts.
Covers `[JAR2-MIG-04]`, `[JAR2-BAD-03]`, `[JAR2-BAD-10]`, `[JAR2-MIG-07]`.

### B7 — Downgrade attempt

```
Given an incumbent at schemaVersion 3
  And a candidate at schemaVersion 2 declaring no reverse transform
When Promotion.promote runs
Then PRECHECK aborts naming the direction (3 → 2) as a downgrade
  And the incumbent is untouched
When the candidate instead declares an explicit v3→v2 reverse transform
Then the promotion proceeds and the reverse transform runs
When a post-RETIRE rollback of an earlier 2→3 promotion is requested from a valid
     RollbackCheckpoint
Then the downgrade refusal does NOT apply — the checkpoint restores a state that
     provably existed
```
Covers `[JAR2-BAD-04]`, `[JAR2-RB-03]`.

### B8 — Post-RETIRE rollback, in and out of the horizon

```
Given a completed promotion from schemaVersion 1 to 2 over a journaled cell
  And a RollbackCheckpoint retained at RETIRE
  And N further deltas emitted by the candidate and observed downstream
When a rollback is requested within the retention horizon
Then the incumbent is re-spawned from the checkpoint as the reverse candidate
  And the post-RETIRE journal suffix is reversed
  And downstream converges to a fold consistent with the restored state
  And exactly one snapshot capture exists across the whole promotion+rollback sequence
When the horizon has expired and a rollback is requested
Then the rollback is refused with a diagnostic naming the expiry
  And the live state is untouched
And for a volatile cell (journalFor == null) the rollback is refused in both cases
```
The "exactly one snapshot capture" assertion is R9's shared-checkpoint rule, and it is
easy to violate invisibly. Covers `[JAR2-RB-01]`, `[JAR2-RB-02]`, `[JAR2-RB-03]`,
`[JAR2-RB-04]`, `[JAR2-RB-05]`, `[JAR2-BAD-05]`, `[JAR2-RB-06]`.

### B9 — Transform-correctness generative harness

```
Given a generated random input sequence and a graph containing a stateful cell
  And a control run with no promotion
  And an experimental run promoting v1 → v2 mid-stream via a declared transform
When both runs reach quiescence
Then the downstream delta stream of the experimental run equals the control's
  And the glitch-free frontier shows no straddling wave across the swap
  And the outlet's (sourceId, highWater) is continuous across the swap
Repeated over 100 seeds; a discovered failing seed is fixed, never replaced.
```
This is 93 I-27 §8's "`StateMigrating` transform correctness harness", generalizing
`ShadowPromotionTest`. Covers `[JAR2-MIG-10]`, and is the epic's honest substitute for
an unverifiable "transforms are correct" claim.

### B10 — Exclusive payloads across every discard path

```
Given a stateful cell whose snapshot delta carries an Owned payload
When a promotion takes the T2 fallback and discards the prior snapshot
Then the Owned payload is explicitly discharged and the discharge is observable
When instead a migration is refused at PRECHECK
Then no snapshot was taken, so nothing needs discharging (assert the snapshot count is 0)
When instead a RollbackCheckpoint holding an Owned payload reaches its horizon
Then expiry discharges it explicitly and records the discharge
And in no path is an exclusive payload dropped, finalized, or left to GC
```
Covers `[JAR2-BAD-06]`, `[JAR2-BAD-07]`, `[JAR2-BAD-08]`.

### B11 — Hidden-state cell refuses promotion

```
Given a cell whose recoverable state is not expressible in its outlet delta contract,
      declaring the non-promotable marker
When Promotion.promote is called with it as candidate or incumbent
Then PRECHECK refuses, naming the marker
  And the refusal happens whether or not a transform chain exists
```
Covers `[JAR2-MIG-06]`.

### B12 — Unversioned snapshot is inexpressible

```
Given a candidate whose importFrom is offered a PriorState with an unknown schemaVersion
When Promotion.promote runs
Then PRECHECK treats it as an unresolvable chain and refuses
  And no code path exists that hands a candidate a bare Serializable snapshot
      (asserted structurally: StateMigrating.importFrom takes PriorState only)
```
Covers `[JAR2-BAD-09]`, `[JAR2-MIG-02]`.

### B13 — Unload refused while a checkpoint is live

```
Given a promotion completed from module A@1.0's cell to module B@2.0's cell
  And a RollbackCheckpoint retained, holding A's snapshot
When unload of A is requested inside the horizon
Then the unload is refused, naming the live checkpoint
When the horizon expires and unload is requested again
Then the unload succeeds
```
Covers `[JAR2-MOD-04]`, and connects to `[JAR1-UNL-02]`.

### Concord corpus note

Most of JAR2 is **not** corpus material, for the same structural reason JAR1 gave:
dynamic loading and module versioning are *hosting* capabilities with no vocabulary in
`concord/schema/cell-catalog.md`, and minting script verbs for them is a gated schema
change (`concord/schema/*.md` are single-writer, schema-change-gated). B1–B3, B12 and
B13 are `:gen`/`:nature`/`:loader` tests.

Three scenarios are genuinely semantic and should be evaluated for corpus expression
during the epic, because they are claims about *dataflow*, not about jars:

- **B4** (migration fails halfway → no dropped delta, no dead-letter, downstream
  glitch-free) — expressible if the incumbent/candidate are ordinary catalog cells;
  `covers:` `[13-NOLOSS-01]` and `[22-GF-01]`.
- **B8** (post-RETIRE rollback → downstream converges to a fold consistent with the
  restored state) — this is `[21-REBASE-01]` almost verbatim, which is *already a gap
  row* in `doc/spec/CONCORDANCE.md` with a consolidated dispute entry at
  `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md:311-349`. If JAR2 can cover it, `covers: [21-REBASE-01]`
  and the dispute entry should be updated by the integration pass — **not** by this
  epic (AGENTS.md: do not edit plan/spec documents unless the task asks for doc
  maintenance).
- **B9** (transform-correctness generative harness) — the stream-equality property is
  corpus-shaped, but 100-seed generative runs are a `:kernel` test idiom, not a corpus
  idiom. Keep it in `:kernel`.

If any of the three cannot be expressed honestly through existing verbs, it goes in
`concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` — never substituted with a scenario that tests something
easier. `[15-PROMOTE-01]` already carries an ⚠ EARS-GAP marker in
`doc/spec/10-programming-model/15-lifecycle.md:56-57` (decided restriction vs landed
behavior); JAR2 must check whether its work closes that marker and, if it does, say so
in the final report rather than editing the spec.

## Scope boundaries

**In scope**: `shapeVersion` on `ContractDescriptor` and `schemaVersion` on
`CellDescriptor`, generated by KSP; `ModuleVersion` parsing/ordering in `:loader`;
provenance-keyed cell-descriptor registration (the `cellsByFqn` last-write-wins defect);
`PriorState` and the retyped `StateMigrating.importFrom`; declared migration chains with
PRECHECK resolution; downgrade and gap refusals; the hidden-state non-promotable
declaration; the `RollbackCheckpoint` retention window; post-RETIRE rollback with
journal reversal; exclusive-payload discharge on every discard path; the
transform-correctness generative harness.

**NOT in scope — JAR1** (`computenet-051`): the `:loader` module itself,
`ModuleClassLoader` isolation, the manifest/discovery contract, validate-then-commit
registration, `unregister`, the unload lifecycle, the `WireCodec` late-contribution
decision, the `Class.forName` site fixes. JAR2 **consumes these from `main`** and
re-solves none of them. If JAR1 has not landed, JAR2 does not start.

**NOT in scope — JAR3**: reading a `GraphSpec` out of a jar; the deploy/upgrade command;
diffing two deployed graphs; multi-module dependency resolution. JAR2 supplies the
version vocabulary and the migration/rollback mechanism JAR3's upgrade variant
orchestrates, and stops there.

**NOT in scope — WKB3**: any UI for version swapping. JAR2's `[JAR2-OBS-01/02]` produce
what WKB3 renders; WKB3 owns rendering it.

**NOT in scope — G-53** (`53-evolution.md:136-142`): coupled-flow (Symport/Antiport)
windows during a buffered swap. Explicitly excluded by the G-49 row itself: *"Coupled-flow
windows remain G-53."*

**NOT in scope — research-gated**: `GraphSpec` partial-apply atomicity (95 §R4,
`15-lifecycle.md:76-78`). JAR2 does not touch `applyRemote`.

**NOT in scope — out of lane**: contract migration or adapter synthesis (53: a contract
change is not a promotion); a private snapshot channel for hidden-state cells (refused,
not solved); replicated rolling promotion's version story
(`Promotion.promoteReplica`, `53-evolution.md:292-367`) beyond ensuring JAR2's PRECHECK
additions apply there consistently; wire-format version negotiation between peers
running different module versions.

7. **Exclusive-payload discharge across every discard path**
   (`[JAR2-BAD-06..08]`; B10.)
8. **Transform-correctness generative harness** (`[JAR2-MIG-10]`; B9.)

Features 1 and 3 are independent. 2 needs 1. 4 needs 1 and 2. 5 needs 4. 6 needs 5. 7
cuts across 5 and 6 and should be written *with* them, not after. 8 needs 5 and is the
gate on declaring the epic done.

---

## Verification

```bash
./gradlew :gen:test                      # descriptor emission — KSP output is contract
./gradlew :nature:test                   # provenance keying, shape-version refusal
./gradlew :loader:test                   # ModuleVersion, load gate, unload-vs-checkpoint
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.evolve.*'
./gradlew :kernel:test                   # journal reversal, retention, generative harness
./gradlew :wire:test                     # descriptor field additions must not move the wire
./gradlew :concord:test                  # driver's ContractRegistry.register usage undisturbed
./gradlew :demo:exchange:test            # composition exit gate
./gradlew test                           # repository-wide
```

Explicit non-regression:

- `ShadowPromotionTest` and `PromotionWaveStateTest` (the G-49 W3.5 verification named at
  `53-evolution.md:250-252`) pass with their **assertions unmodified**; a signature
  change to `importFrom` may edit their fixtures, never their claims.
- `ReplicatedPromotionTest` (`53-evolution.md:359-367`) passes: `promoteReplica`'s
  existing `NonIdempotentCatchUp` and same-ref refusals are untouched.
- `ManifestDriftTest` and the Inspector's `ObservationsCompletenessTest` pass — both walk
  `ContractRegistry.cells`, whose keying `[JAR2-COEX-02]` changes.
- A process with no dynamically loaded modules behaves observably as before.

Report exactly which tests ran; state plainly whether B9's harness found a failing seed
and what it was; and state whether `[15-PROMOTE-01]`'s ⚠ EARS-GAP marker
(`15-lifecycle.md:56-57`) is closed, narrowed, or untouched by this work.

---

## Risks / open questions

**R1 — The `importFrom` signature change is breaking.** `StateMigrating.importFrom(Serializable)`
→ `importFrom(PriorState)` breaks every implementor. There are few today, but
`ShadowPromotionTest`'s v1→v2 fixture is one of them and it is the *cited verification*
for G-33. A default-method bridge that keeps the old signature alive would defeat
`[JAR2-BAD-09]` (an unversioned snapshot must become inexpressible). **Decision needed
early**: break it cleanly, or accept a deprecation window with a hard removal in the
same epic. Prefer the clean break; a bridge that survives the epic is the gap re-opened.

**R2 — Where does the transform chain live?** Three candidate shapes: (a) methods on the
candidate declared via KSP annotations, (b) a `MigrationPath` object the candidate
exposes, (c) a registry of transforms keyed by `(cellFqn, fromVersion, toVersion)`.
(a) is most consistent with "generated descriptors are authoritative", (c) is the only
one that lets a *third* module supply a transform between two others' versions — which
JAR3's upgrade variant may want. Resolve in feature 4, before feature 5 starts, and
record the decision in the epic's notes.

**R3 — Retention horizon units.** Wall-clock is the obvious choice and the wrong one:
53 §"Judgment is declarative policy" measures the observation window "in observed
production waves and/or coverage stabilization — never wall-clock, never a barrier"
(`:41-47`). A checkpoint horizon measured in waves is consistent with that; measured in
seconds it introduces the first wall-clock dependency into the evolve path. **Open
question**: waves, journal segments, or an explicit `release()` call by the operator?
Argue it against 53 rather than defaulting to a `Duration`.

**R4 — Journal reversal is not currently a thing.** 53 §Mechanical decomposition's
"Roll back" row cites "journaled invocations replay" (24, 43 §5), and 93 I-27 R9 says
post-retire rollback "is exactly I-7's journal-restore (`Stateful.restore` + WAL
suffix)". But reversal-by-replay only reconstructs the *incumbent*; the candidate's
post-RETIRE emissions still reached downstream, and `[21-REBASE-01]` — the requirement
that makes downstream converge after a producer reverts — is itself an open gap row
with a `DISPUTES.md` entry. **This is the highest-risk item in the epic.** If
`[JAR2-RB-04]` cannot be verified honestly against the landed re-baseline behaviour, it
belongs in `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` and the epic must say so plainly rather than
asserting a convergence it cannot show.

**R5 — JAR1 dependency is real, not nominal.** JAR2's `[JAR2-COEX-02]` extends JAR1's
provenance model; `[JAR2-MOD-04]` extends JAR1's unload refusal; `[JAR2-MIG-01]`'s
cross-loader shape check is meaningless without `ModuleClassLoader`. If JAR1 lands
partially — in particular if `[JAR1-REG-08]` resolves to "refuse non-wire-capable
modules" rather than a rebuildable codec — JAR2 inherits that constraint and must not
quietly widen it.

**R6 — `shapeVersion` is a new field on a wire-adjacent descriptor.** `ContractDescriptor`
is not itself serialized over the wire (the wire carries ids only), but
`ManifestDriftTest` and the concord driver both read these tables. Additive defaulted
fields should be safe; verify rather than assume, and do not let `shapeVersion` leak
into a frame.

**R7 — Two versions of a cell, one `logicalId`.** `[JAR2-COEX-01]` says two
implementation versions coexist. During a shadow window they share a `logicalId`
(`IdentityBinding.NewInstanceOf`, `GraphDsl.kt:47`) and differ by `instanceId`. Any
consumer that keys placement, durability, or observation by `logicalId` alone will
conflate them. Sweep for `logicalId`-keyed lookups before feature 2, and note what is
found even if nothing needs changing.

# JAR2 — design notes

## Placement (decided)

No new Gradle module. JAR2 extends `:loader` (JAR1's) with a
`civictech.loader.version` package, and makes additive changes in `:nature`, `:gen`,
and `:kernel`.

```
nature/  ContractDescriptor.shapeVersion, CellDescriptor.schemaVersion,
         ContractRegistry provenance-keyed cellsByFqn + shape-version refusal
gen/     ContractProcessor emits both version fields
kernel/  cell/evolve/: PriorState, StateMigrating.importFrom(PriorState),
         MigrationPath, NonPromotable marker, RollbackCheckpoint
         cell/durability/: retention window + journal-reversal reader
loader/  civictech.loader.version: ModuleVersion, version-aware load gate
```

Rejected: a `:migrate` module. Every piece has an existing owner, and the registration
story JAR1 just consolidated in `:nature`/`:loader` should not be split across a third
place.

## Key source coordinates

| Thing | Path |

| In-window rollback (the catch block JAR2 must extend, not weaken) | `Evolution.kt:228-242` |
| RETIRE `despawn` — where the retention window is installed | `Evolution.kt:244-247` |
| `Promotion.promoteReplica` (PN-14 rolling form; PRECHECK additions must apply consistently) | `Evolution.kt:281+` |

## Shape sketch (indicative, not prescriptive)

```kotlin
// :nature — additive, defaulted, generated
data class ContractDescriptor(..., val shapeVersion: Long = 0L)
data class CellDescriptor(..., val schemaVersion: Int = 0)

// :kernel evolve — 93 I-27's decided shape
data class PriorState(
    val snapshot: Serializable,
    val schemaVersion: Int,
    val outletWaves: Map<String, OutletWaveState>,
)
interface StateMigrating { fun importFrom(prior: PriorState) }   // was importFrom(Serializable)

/** Declared, directional, single-step transforms. Resolution is PRECHECK's job. */
interface MigrationPath {
    val schemaVersion: Int
    fun steps(): List<MigrationStep>          // each (from, to)
}

/** Hidden state not expressible in the invariant delta contract — 93 I-27 §8. */
interface NonPromotable

class RollbackCheckpoint(
    val snapshot: Serializable,               // THE SAME capture importFrom consumed (R9)
    val schemaVersion: Int,
    val outletWaves: Map<String, OutletWaveState>,
    val horizon: RetentionHorizon,            // waves? journal segments? see R3
)

// :loader
data class ModuleVersion(...) : Comparable<ModuleVersion>
```

`:nature` registry change:

```kotlin
// today: cellsByFqn[it.fqn] = it            <- last write wins, silently
// after: cellsByFqn[ModuleScopedKey(owner, it.fqn)] = it, with FQN-only lookup
//        resolving through the requesting cell's own module
```

## The coexistence answer, in one table

| Two versions of… | Coexist? | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| the same **contract FQN**, equal `shapeVersion` | yes | `[JAR1-REG-06]` idempotent duplicate registration; both modules recorded as contributors |
| the same **contract FQN**, differing `shapeVersion` | **no, permanently** | `[JAR2-COEX-04/05/06]` — `contractId = hash(FQN)` on an ids-only wire; 53's invariance line makes the operation that wants it not a promotion |
| the same **cell implementation FQN** | **yes, and it is broken today** | `[JAR2-COEX-01/02/03]` — provenance-keyed `cellsByFqn`; this is the incumbent/candidate shadow window |
| the same **module id**, different `ModuleVersion` | yes, gated | `[JAR2-MOD-01]` — permitted iff shared contract FQNs agree on `shapeVersion` |

## Sequencing note

Feature 4 (`PriorState` + chains) carries **R1** (the breaking `importFrom` signature)
and **R2** (where transforms live). Both are decisions, not code, and both change what
features 5–8 build. Resolve them at the top of feature 4 and record them in the epic's
notes before feature 5 opens.

Feature 6 carries **R4**, the highest-risk item: post-RETIRE downstream convergence is
`[21-REBASE-01]`, which is itself an open gap with a `DISPUTES.md` entry. Budget for the
possibility that `[JAR2-RB-04]` ends as a dispute entry rather than a passing test — and
if it does, say so, do not soften the requirement.

Behaviour scenarios B1-B13 each exist as a named test citing its requirement ids. The two-version coexistence answer is realized in code, not prose: [JAR2-COEX-04/05/06] refuse divergent same-FQN contract surfaces with a named version diagnostic, and [JAR2-COEX-01/02/03] make two implementation versions of one cell FQN independently resolvable (fixing the last-write-wins cellsByFqn put at nature/src/main/kotlin/civictech/nature/ContractRegistry.kt:37). [JAR2-BAD-01..10] are the acceptance core: a migration that cannot run refuses at PRECHECK with the gate never red ([JAR2-BAD-03], [JAR2-MIG-04]); a mid-chain failure leaves no partially-applied state observable ([JAR2-BAD-01], [JAR2-MIG-05]); a rollback that cannot restore observably-equivalent state refuses ([JAR2-BAD-05], [JAR2-RB-05]); and every discard path discharges Owned/Leased payloads explicitly ([JAR2-BAD-06..08]) - a silent drop on any of these fails acceptance outright. title: ORA2 — Oracle coverage for the tagged/keyed family (OR-map, weighted)
description:
# ORA2 — Oracle coverage for the tagged/keyed family (OR-map, weighted)

Milestone-plan row (`computenet-milestone-plan.md` §1, Evidence lanes), verbatim:

> | ORA2 | Oracle coverage for tagged/keyed family (OR-map, weighted) | ORA1, KE1 core types | KE4-era work |

Filed as a **feature under ORA1** (`computenet-4ru`), not an epic: it builds no new
harness. Every mechanism it needs — the module, the generator, the differential runner,
the wave-prefix oracle, the shrinker, the pinned-seed corpus, the failure taxonomy — is
an ORA1 deliverable. ORA2 widens exactly one seam ORA1 was built to expose
(`OperatorCatalog.register(id, shape, kernel, model)`, `[ORA1-API-02]`/`[ORA1-API-03]`)
and adds one genuinely new *kind* of reference obligation: **convergence**, which the
batch oracle of ORA1 does not express.

---

## 1. Ambition / Why

ORA1's oracle answers one question: *does the incremental run of an acyclic operator
graph equal a batch recompute of the same script?* Its reference model is deliberately
**membership-only** — `[ORA1-MODEL-03]` forbids the model from reading tag identity, tag
counts, wave ids or any `SetDelta`/`TaggedMapDelta` internals, precisely so the oracle
stays independent of the tag algebra it checks. That is the right rule, and it is also
the reason ORA1 explicitly excludes the tagged/keyed convergence family in its scope
boundaries:

> **The tagged/keyed convergence family (OR-map, weighted sets).** That is **ORA2** […]
> ORA1 builds the *extension seam*; it does not model `OrMapCell`/`TaggedMapDelta`
> semantics.

The family it defers is where the interesting wrongness lives, for a structural reason.
For an OR-set, membership is decidable from the script alone: an element is live iff some
add is uncovered by an observed remove. For an **OR-map** the observable state is not
membership but *value*, and value is decided by the **dot order** — `[24-TMAP-03]`: "A
key's exposed value SHALL be the value of the live dot with the greatest
`(counter, sourceId)` order. No wall clock participates." A batch reference for
`OrMapCell` therefore *must* model dot minting and dot order. That is a different, and
strictly stronger, oracle obligation than ORA1's, and it is why ORA1 could not simply
widen its vocabulary.

Second, the family is the one where "the answer" is not a single value at all. A
replicated `OrMapCell` has one converged answer per *mesh*, reached by an arbitrary
gossip schedule, not one answer per *stream*. The property is `[42-REPL-04]` — "replicas
of one logical cell SHALL converge to equal folds at quiescence regardless of which
replica accepted each write" — and no amount of single-replica batch recompute checks it.
ORA2 introduces the **convergence oracle**: a batch reference over the *set of accepted
writes across all replicas*, checked against every replica's fold, and against the
delta-only twin.

What ORA2 unblocks, per the plan's own edges:

- **KE1 acceptance, completed.** The plan admits KE1 to the kernel lane at §4 rank 2
  explicitly with "ORA1 leverage", and lists ORA2 among KE1's consumers ("KE1 …
  Unblocks: AGO3, SOC1 keyed state, **ORA2**, BB-TPCH deletions, BB-YCSB"). The E1
  milestone's own acceptance clauses are *differential by construction* — E1.2's test
  clause is "any interleaving/duplication/reordering of a fixed dot set yields identical
  membership and per-key values … divergence control: the same schedule through
  `MapDelta`/`MapView` order-flips"; E1.5's is "outputs equal each other and a batch
  recompute over converged state on every seed; control: raw `MapCell` inputs under the
  same schedule diverge". Those are per-cell hand-rolled instances of exactly the engine
  ORA1 built. ORA2 is what stops E1.4–E1.6 re-hand-rolling them.
- **KE4-era work** (the plan's "Unblocks" column). E4's event-time waterline eviction is
  a *keyed* eviction over derived window keys; an eviction oracle is unwritable until the
  keyed reference model exists. ORA2 does not model eviction (that is KE4's own item) —
  it supplies the keyed half the eviction oracle will stand on.
- **BB-TPCH** deletions. §3's TPC-H row names "KE1 — tagged multiset deltas; RF2's
  deletions propagating through multi-join chains is the acceptance property" with "ORA1
  as cross-check". RF2 deletions through a tagged multiset are ORA2's vocabulary, not
  ORA1's.

### The honest state of the target surface (verified in the tree, 2026-08-08)

This matters because the plan's "OR-map, weighted" names two things at very different
maturities, and a feature that pretends otherwise will specify tests that cannot compile.

**Tagged map — largely landed.** `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/OrMapCell.kt`
exists and carries the four laws in its KDoc as `[24-TMAP-01]`…`[24-TMAP-04]`, matching
`doc/spec/20-dataflow-semantics/24-data-cells.md:330-345`. Its delta,
`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/delta/TaggedMapDelta.kt`, implements
`merge`/`liveDots`/`membership`/`value`/`keys`/`within` with a `DOT_ORDER` comparator, a
compact per-source wire grouping (`WireSourcePuts`/`WireSourceDels`/`WireKeyPuts`) and
`MergeablePayload`. `kernel/src/test/kotlin/civictech/cell/replication/OrMapConvergenceTest.kt`
is E1.3's convergence test. So E1.1–E1.3 are effectively in `main`.

**Tagged-map adopters — not landed.** There is no `UntagCell.kt` and no `TaggedMapView`
anywhere under `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/`; `OrMapCell` exposes
`membership()`/`value(key)`/`state()` but no `values(k)` multi-value read. Those are
E1.4 (embedded mergeable values) and E1.5 (`TaggedMapView` + `UntagCell` + join-family
adoption) and they are the "KE1 core types" edge in the plan's dependency column.

**Weighted (Z-set) family — not built at all.** There is no `WeightedSetDelta`,
`WeightedSetCell`, `TagsToWeightsCell` or `WeightsToTagsCell`. The family is
`doc/spec/90-roadmap/96-incremental-engines-plan.md` §E6, marked ⚠ PROPOSED, P3, and
described as "deliberately last (05 §priority): the tag↔weight boundary should be
informed by E1's OR-map and E3's GC work". That is why this feature is **P3** while its
sibling evidence chunks are P2, and why §4's weighted requirements are written as
**optional-feature (WHERE) EARS** that activate when E6 lands — not as work that blocks
the tagged/keyed half. ORA2 ships the tagged/keyed oracle unconditionally and the
weighted oracle **behind the existence of the cells**, honestly, rather than pretending
a reference model can precede its subject.

---

## 2. What we build

Four additions inside the existing `:oracle` module (`oracle/src/main/kotlin/civictech/oracle/`),
plus one new test source area. No new Gradle module, no new package convention.

### 2.1 Tagged/keyed reference model (`civictech.oracle.model`, extended)

A `DotModel` alongside ORA1's membership model: a pure fold from an op script to
`Map<K, V>` (values) and `Set<K>` (membership) computed through **modelled dots**. The
model mints its own dot per modelled `put`, from a modelled per-writer counter, and
resolves reads by the same `(counter, sourceId)` order the spec states — it does **not**
read `Timestamp`s out of the kernel's deltas. This is a deliberate, narrow, written-down
relaxation of `[ORA1-MODEL-03]` and it is the single largest design decision in this
feature (see §7 risk 1 and the design note).

### 2.2 Convergence oracle (`civictech.oracle.run`, extended)

`ConvergenceCheck`: given N replica handles of one `logicalId` and the global script
(each step tagged with the replica that accepted it), assert (a) every replica's fold
equals the model's converged answer, (b) all replicas equal each other, (c) the answer is
invariant under a re-run with a different gossip interleaving derived from the same seed.
This reuses ORA1's `RunOutcome`/`Mismatch`/failure-taxonomy types and its sweep/report
plumbing verbatim; it adds a failure kind, not a second runner.

### 2.3 Catalog registrations (`civictech.oracle.bind`, extended)

`OrMapCell`, `KeyedSetCell` (deepened past ORA1's membership-only coverage),
`MergeableGroupByCell`, `PnCounterCell` as keyed/tagged catalog entries, plus the E1.5
adopters (`UntagCell`, `TaggedMapView`) and the E6 weighted entries **guarded by
availability**, each registered as the ORA1-mandated (kernel factory, reference model)
pair so `[ORA1-API-02]`'s paired-registration failure keeps them honest.

### 2.4 Generator extensions (`civictech.oracle.gen`, extended)

Multi-writer scripts (ORA1's `[ORA1-GEN-*]` scripts are single-writer where the operator
is order-dependent, and `[ORA1-MODEL-09]` *rejects* multi-writer cases for those
operators). ORA2 adds: a writer dimension, per-writer observation state, a concurrency
knob (fraction of writes that are genuinely concurrent — issued without either writer
having observed the other), a replica-placement dimension, and a re-put/reset-remove
bias that targets `[24-TMAP-04]`'s reset-remove rule.

### 2.5 Tests

`oracle/src/test/kotlin/civictech/oracle/tagged/` — the tagged/keyed sweep, the
convergence sweep, the per-behaviour scenario tests of §5, the discrimination controls,
and the pinned-seed additions. Pinned seeds are appended to ORA1's existing
`PinnedSeeds`; they are never rotated (`[ORA1-REPRO-02]`).

## 3. How, using ComputeNet

### 3.1 Which ORA1 machinery is reused (not rebuilt)

| ORA1 deliverable | ORA2's use |
|---|---|
| `:oracle` module, `oracle/build.gradle.kts`, `settings.gradle.kts` include | unchanged; ORA2 adds packages inside it |
| `OperatorCatalog.register(id, shape, kernel, model)` (`[ORA1-API-02]`) | **the** extension point; every ORA2 cell arrives through it |
| shape rules picked up without generator edits (`[ORA1-API-03]`) | new keyed shapes register the same way |
| `DifferentialRunner.check(case)` + bring-your-own `check(buildGraph, script, reference, seed)` (`[ORA1-DIFF-11]`) | the convergence check is a caller of the second form |
| failure taxonomy: mismatch / dead letter / non-quiescence / model-evaluation (`[ORA1-DIFF-02]`,`-04`,`-07`,`-08`) | reused verbatim; ORA2 adds `DIVERGENCE` as a fifth kind |
| wave-prefix glitch-freedom oracle (`[ORA1-DIFF-06]`) | applies unchanged to tagged terminals |
| `forEachSeed` density sweep (`[ORA1-DIFF-03]`) | unchanged |
| `Shrinker` (`[ORA1-SHRINK-01..05]`) | extended with two reduction moves (drop a writer; drop a replica) |
| `PinnedSeeds` (`[ORA1-REPRO-01..03]`) | appended to |
| `[ORA1-HONEST-01/02]` honesty ledger | ORA2 files its own entries in the same place |

If ORA2 finds itself writing a second sweep loop, a second report format, or a second
shrinker, it has gone wrong.

### 3.2 The kernel surface under test (real types, real paths)

- `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/OrMapCell.kt` — `@CellBase interface OrMapApi<K,V>`
  with `inlet: Use<MapOps<K,V>>` (the **existing** `MapOps` contract; E1.2 deliberately
  minted no new contract) and `outlet: Subscribe<Propagate<TaggedMapDelta<K,V>>>`.
  Reads: `membership()`, `value(key)`, `state()`. Internals the model must *not* read:
  `puts`, `dels`, `dotSource`, `dotCounter`, `deadSources`, `liveDots`, `novelty`,
  `absorb`, `applyRemote`, `applyReBaseline`, `currentFrontier`.
- `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/delta/TaggedMapDelta.kt` — `merge`,
  `liveDots`, `membership`, `value`, `keys`, `within(interest, keyOf)`, `DOT_ORDER`
  (`compareBy(counter, sourceId)`), `MergeablePayload.mergeWith`.
- `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/KeyedSetCell.kt` — `KeyedSetOps.put/remove`;
  re-put ships retract+add atomically in one `SetDelta`. ORA1 covers it at membership
  level; ORA2 covers the **per-key atomicity** (never two live values, never zero) that
  `[24-TMAP-04]`'s analogue demands.
- `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/op/MergeableGroupByCell.kt` —
  `aggregates(): Map<K,A>`, grow/merge only, no retraction. The reference must encode the
  *absence* of retraction as the specified behaviour, not model a retracting group-by and
  call the difference a bug.
- `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/PnCounterCell.kt` and
  `delta/PnCounterDelta.kt` — per-source cumulative totals, pointwise-max merge; the
  existing second member of the replicable class beside the tagged set family.
- `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/op/TaggedSetOperator.kt` — the shared
  tag-state carrier (`emitOrAbsorb`, `page`, `snapshot`/`restore`) most set operators sit
  on; the seam that makes a keyed operator's reference model tractable.
- `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/delta/TagState.kt` — `applyReBaseline`,
  `deadSources`. ORA2 does **not** model re-baselining (that is a source-epoch concern,
  out of scope, §6) but must not be *broken* by it: generated cases contain no RESTART.
- `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/replication/Replication.kt` —
  `replicate(cell, host)`, `evict(...)`, `replicaFrontier(...)`; and
  `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/LocationRegistry.kt`'s `replicasOf(logicalId)`
  as the membership view. ORA2 builds **quiescent** meshes only; faults are CHA1/CHA3.
- `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/verify/ReplicaConvergence.kt` — `attach(replica)`,
  `converged()`, `state(ref)`, `states()`, with `liveRefs()` = `replicasOf(logicalId) ∩ folds.keys`.
  **This is the existing convergence invariant and ORA2's convergence check composes with
  it rather than replacing it**: `ReplicaConvergence` answers "do the replicas agree?";
  ORA2 answers "do they agree *on the right value*?" — the batch half `ReplicaConvergence`
  structurally cannot supply.
- `kernel/src/test/kotlin/civictech/cell/replication/OrMapConvergenceTest.kt`,
  `.../SetConvergenceTest`-family, `.../PnCounterReplicationTest.kt`,
  `.../ReplicatedSessionTest.kt` — the hand-rolled instances ORA2 subsumes or converts.

### 3.3 The dot model, precisely

For each modelled writer `w` the model keeps a counter and an observation set. A modelled
`put(k, v)` by `w`: mint `dot = (counter++, w)`; tombstone every dot `w` currently
observes live at `k`; record `(dot → v)` live. A modelled `remove(k)` by `w`: tombstone
exactly the dots `w` observes live at `k` (reset-remove, `[24-TMAP-04]`), no-op
otherwise. Merge = pointwise union of live and tombstoned dot sets. `membership(k)` = at
least one live dot (`[24-TMAP-02]`). `value(k)` = the value of the live dot maximal under
`(counter, sourceId)` (`[24-TMAP-03]`). Observation is advanced by explicit **script**
delivery events, never by reading kernel state — this is what keeps the model a second
implementation rather than a mirror.

The model's `sourceId` for writer `w` is a *modelled* identity that must be **order-
isomorphic** to the kernel's real `dotSource` for the corresponding cell, because
`DOT_ORDER` breaks counter ties by `sourceId`. The kernel derives it deterministically —
`UUID.nameUUIDFromBytes("or-map-tags:${ref.id}:${ref.instanceId}")` per E1.2 — so the
harness (not the model) supplies the mapping at case-construction time, and the case
generator is required to make ties observable rather than rare (`[ORA2-GEN-04]`).
