## 4. Functional requirements (EARS)

Ids are feature-scoped `[ORA2-GROUP-nn]`, mirroring `doc/spec/`'s `[NN-SLUG-nn]` shape
but namespaced so they can never collide with a normative id, with ORA1's ids, or with
CHA2/CHA3's. "The oracle" = the `:oracle` module; "the model", "the generator", "the
runner", "the shrinker", "the catalog" name ORA1's components as extended here. The
*Makes true* citation names the normative requirement each item makes checkable.

### 4.1 Ubiquitous — the tagged/keyed reference model

- `[ORA2-MODEL-01]` The model shall compute, from a complete multi-writer op script
  alone, the membership and per-key value of every modelled tagged-map terminal, without
  executing any kernel cell. *(makes `[24-TMAP-02]`, `[24-TMAP-03]` checkable)*
- `[ORA2-MODEL-02]` The model shall implement merge as pointwise union of live and
  tombstoned dot sets, and this union shall be commutative, associative and idempotent.
  *(`[24-TMAP-01]`)*
- `[ORA2-MODEL-03]` The model shall expose a key as present iff that key has at least one
  live dot. *(`[24-TMAP-02]`)*
- `[ORA2-MODEL-04]` The model shall expose a key's value as the value of the live dot
  maximal under `(counter, sourceId)`, and shall consult no wall clock and no arrival
  order in doing so. *(`[24-TMAP-03]`)*
- `[ORA2-MODEL-05]` The model shall treat `remove(k)` as reset-remove: it shall tombstone
  exactly the dots the removing writer observes live at `k` at that point in the script,
  and shall leave unobserved concurrent dots live. *(`[24-TMAP-04]`)*
- `[ORA2-MODEL-06]` The model shall advance a writer's observation set only from explicit
  delivery events in the script, and shall never read a kernel cell's state, deltas, or
  tag internals to do so. *(model independence; extends `[ORA1-MODEL-03]`)*
- `[ORA2-MODEL-07]` The model shall be a pure function of the script: two evaluations of
  the same script shall produce equal results and shall not mutate the script.
  *(mirrors `[ORA1-MODEL-11]`)*
- `[ORA2-MODEL-08]` The model shall reproduce `KeyedSetCell`'s per-key re-put atomicity:
  at every script prefix a key modelled as re-put shall have exactly one live element,
  never two and never zero. *(`[24-SET-01]`, `[24-SET-03]` at key granularity)*
- `[ORA2-MODEL-09]` The model shall reproduce `MergeableGroupByCell` as grow/merge-only
  with no retraction, and shall state that absence as the modelled specification rather
  than modelling a retracting group-by. *(`[24-OP-GROUPBY-01]`)*
- `[ORA2-MODEL-10]` The model shall reproduce `PnCounterCell` as per-source cumulative
  totals resolved by pointwise maximum. *(`[42-REPL-04]` for the counter member)*
- `[ORA2-MODEL-11]` The tagged/keyed model source set shall reference no type from
  `civictech.cell.data.op` and no concrete data-cell class, and this shall be enforced by
  the same import-scanning architecture test ORA1 installs for `[ORA1-MODEL-10]`.
- `[ORA2-MODEL-12]` Where the model must agree with the kernel on dot **order**, the
  writer-identity mapping shall be supplied by the harness at case-construction time and
  shall not be recovered by reading a kernel `Timestamp`.

### 4.2 Ubiquitous — the convergence oracle

- `[ORA2-CONV-01]` The convergence oracle shall accept a script whose every step names
  the replica that accepted it, and shall compute one converged reference answer for the
  whole script. *(`[42-REPL-04]`)*
- `[ORA2-CONV-02]` The convergence oracle shall compare every replica's fold against that
  one converged reference answer, and shall not merely compare replicas against each
  other. *(`[42-REPL-04]`; the gap `ReplicaConvergence.converged()` structurally leaves)*
- `[ORA2-CONV-03]` The convergence oracle shall report a replica-vs-replica disagreement
  and a replicas-agree-but-wrong result as distinct failure kinds.
- `[ORA2-CONV-04]` The convergence oracle shall assert that each replica's fold is
  reachable through that replica's own delta outlet stream, so a fold reconstructed from
  gossip alone is checked, not only the cell's internal state.

### 4.3 Event-driven

- `[ORA2-DIFF-01]` When a generated tagged/keyed case is executed, the runner shall fold
  every terminal, compare it to the model's result for the same script, and report any
  difference naming the seed, the terminal, the key set that differs, and for each
  differing key the expected and actual value. *(extends `[ORA1-DIFF-02]`)*
- `[ORA2-DIFF-02]` When two writers put the same key without either having observed the
  other, the runner shall assert that every replica exposes the single value the dot
  order selects, and that the losing dot remains live and reachable through the
  multi-value read where one exists. *(`[24-TMAP-03]`)*
- `[ORA2-DIFF-03]` When a writer removes a key concurrently with another writer's put of
  that key, the runner shall assert add-wins: the key remains present with the surviving
  unobserved dot's value. *(`[24-TMAP-02]`, `[24-TMAP-04]`)*
- `[ORA2-DIFF-04]` When the same tagged delta is delivered more than once by any path,
  the runner shall assert the terminal fold is unchanged by the repeat. *(`[24-TMAP-01]`)*
- `[ORA2-DIFF-05]` When a consumer links to a replica after deltas have already gossiped
  through the mesh, the runner shall assert the late consumer's fold equals an
  early-linked consumer's fold. *(`[42-REPL-05]`; mirrors `[ORA1-DIFF-05]`)*
- `[ORA2-DIFF-06]` When a sweep runs a seed range, it shall execute every seed and report
  failure density in the `forEachSeed` form. *(reuses `[ORA1-DIFF-03]`)*

### 4.4 State-driven

- `[ORA2-DIFF-07]` While a tagged/keyed case is being driven, every intermediate
  observation of a terminal shall equal the model's result for some prefix of the wave
  sequence, using ORA1's wave-prefix oracle unchanged. *(reuses `[ORA1-DIFF-06]`;
  `[22-GF-01]`)*
- `[ORA2-DIFF-08]` While a mesh is quiescent, the oracle shall require every replica of
  one logical id to expose equal membership and equal per-key values. *(`[42-REPL-04]`)*

### 4.5 Unwanted behaviour

- `[ORA2-DIFF-09]` If a replica's fold differs from the converged reference, then the
  runner shall report a divergence failure distinct from a single-stream mismatch, name
  the accepting replica of each differing key's winning dot, and shall not report the run
  as a value mismatch.
- `[ORA2-DIFF-10]` If any host emits a dead letter during a tagged/keyed run, then the
  runner shall report it as its own failure kind. *(reuses `[ORA1-DIFF-04]`)*
- `[ORA2-DIFF-11]` If the tagged model itself throws, then the runner shall report a
  model-evaluation failure, so a broken oracle is never read as a broken kernel.
  *(reuses `[ORA1-DIFF-08]`)*
- `[ORA2-DIFF-12]` If a generated case would place an untagged, arrival-order-dependent
  cell (`MapCell`/`MapDelta`, `ListCell`/`ListDelta`) under more than one writer, then
  the generator shall reject the case at generation time. *(reuses `[ORA1-MODEL-08]`,
  `[ORA1-MODEL-09]`; `[24-OP-MAP-01]`)*
- `[ORA2-GEN-06]` If the catalog names a tagged/keyed id with a kernel binding but no
  reference model, or the reverse, then registration shall fail loudly. *(reuses
  `[ORA1-API-02]`, `[ORA1-GEN-08]`)*
- `[ORA2-HONEST-03]` If a tagged/keyed behaviour cannot be checked honestly by a batch
  reference, then it shall be excluded from the vocabulary with a written reason and
  filed in `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` where it concerns a normative requirement — never
  modelled approximately so that a sweep passes. *(extends `[ORA1-HONEST-02]`)*
- `[ORA2-REPRO-02]` If a discovered failing seed would make the suite red, it shall not
  be removed, replaced, narrowed or reordered; the pinned corpus is append-only.
  *(`AGENTS.md` determinism invariant; reuses `[ORA1-REPRO-02]`)*

### 4.6 Optional feature — weighted (Z-set) family

These activate **only** when `96 §E6` lands. Until then each is satisfied by its stated
absence check, and the feature is complete without them.

- `[ORA2-WGT-01]` Where `WeightedSetDelta` exists in the kernel, the model shall
  reproduce it as element → signed count with merge by pointwise addition.
  *(`96 §E6.1`/`E6.2`)*
- `[ORA2-WGT-02]` Where `WeightedSetCell` exists, the runner shall assert that integrated
  weights after any interleaving of a fixed op multiset equal the batch sum, and that
  order of application does not change the integral. *(`96 §E6.2`)*
- `[ORA2-WGT-03]` Where `TagsToWeightsCell` exists, the model shall reproduce both modes
  — multiplicity (weight = count of live tags) and dist (0/1 membership) — and the runner
  shall assert the sign-change behaviour at the 0↔non-0 boundary. *(`96 §E6.3`)*
- `[ORA2-WGT-04]` Where `WeightsToTagsCell` exists, the runner shall assert that a
  `≤0 → >0` transition mints exactly one entry tag and a `>0 → ≤0` transition retracts it.
  *(`96 §E6.3`)*
- `[ORA2-WGT-05]` The oracle shall not gossip a `WeightedSetDelta` between replicas, and
  a generated case shall never place a weighted cell in a replicated mesh. *(96 §E6.1:
  raw weights on the wire are gossip-inadmissible; the borrowing rule "weights,
  arrangements and total orders live inside a replica; tags, lattices and vector
  frontiers cross replicas", `96` §How to read this plan)*
- `[ORA2-WGT-06]` If the weighted family is absent from the kernel, then the weighted
  suite shall be reported as **not applicable** with the reason recorded, and shall not be
  silently skipped, disabled, or replaced by a passing stub. *(honesty; `[ORA1-HONEST-02]`)*

### 4.7 Optional feature — E1.4/E1.5 adopters

- `[ORA2-ADOPT-01]` Where `UntagCell` exists, the runner shall assert that
  `OrMapCell → UntagCell → CombineLatestCell` on two peers produces outputs equal to each
  other and to a batch recompute over converged state, on every seed. *(`96 §E1.5`)*
- `[ORA2-ADOPT-02]` Where `UntagCell` exists, the suite shall include the E1.5 divergence
  control: the same schedule with raw `MapCell` inputs diverges on at least one seed.
- `[ORA2-ADOPT-03]` Where `OrMapCell` exposes an embedded-mergeable value mode
  (`V : MergeablePayload`), the model shall expose the `mergeWith`-folded value for
  concurrent live dots instead of the dot-order pick, and the suite shall include the
  E1.4 control that an LWW pick drops an increment. *(`96 §E1.4`)*
- `[ORA2-ADOPT-04]` Where `OrMapCell` exposes a multi-value read, the model shall
  reproduce it as the set of live dot values at the key. *(`96 §E1.4`)*

### 4.8 Complex

- `[ORA2-GEN-01]` Where multi-writer generation is enabled and the vocabulary contains
  only convergent cells, the generator shall emit scripts with more than one writer, each
  writer carrying its own observation state. *(precondition + trigger)*
- `[ORA2-GEN-02]` Where a concurrency ratio is configured, the generator shall issue that
  fraction of writes as genuinely concurrent — neither writer having observed the other's
  prior write to that key at issue time — and shall report the achieved ratio, so a
  configured-but-unrealised concurrency is visible rather than silently zero.
- `[ORA2-GEN-03]` Where replica placement is enabled, the generator shall instantiate more
  than one replica of a logical cell across more than one `ManagedHost` sharing one
  `LocationRegistry`, and shall gossip them through `Replication` with no injected fault.
- `[ORA2-GEN-04]` The generator shall produce, within any default sweep range, at least
  one case in which two live dots for one key share a counter and are separated only by
  `sourceId` order, and shall fail the sweep configuration if it cannot.
  *(`[24-TMAP-03]`'s tie-break is otherwise never exercised)*
- `[ORA2-GEN-05]` The generator shall bias scripts toward re-put and reset-remove at
  already-populated keys, so `[24-TMAP-04]` is exercised rather than incidentally reached.
- `[ORA2-GEN-07]` When the generator is invoked with a seed and config, it shall produce
  an identical case across JVM runs and machines. *(reuses `[ORA1-GEN-01]`)*

### 4.9 Discrimination — blocking

A green sweep without these is not evidence. Mirrors `[ORA1-DIFF-09]`/`[ORA1-DIFF-10]`.

- `[ORA2-CTL-01]` The suite shall include a divergence control in which the tagged map's
  reads are replaced by an arrival-order (untagged `MapDelta`/`MapView`) fold, and shall
  assert it **fails** on at least one seed of a fixed range. *(the E1.2 control, promoted
  into the oracle)*
- `[ORA2-CTL-02]` The suite shall include a mutation check in which the model's dot order
  is deliberately inverted, and shall assert the runner detects it and attributes it to
  the right terminal and key.
- `[ORA2-CTL-03]` The suite shall include a mutation check in which the model's
  reset-remove is replaced by a remove-all, and shall assert the runner detects it —
  proving the add-wins boundary is actually exercised.
- `[ORA2-CTL-04]` The suite shall include a convergence control in which one replica's
  gossip is not applied, and shall assert the convergence oracle reports divergence rather
  than passing.

### 4.10 Budget and reporting

- `[ORA2-PERF-01]` The default tagged/keyed sweep shall complete within the repository's
  normal per-module test budget on `./gradlew :oracle:test`. *(reuses `[ORA1-PERF-01]`)*
- `[ORA2-PERF-02]` Where a larger sweep is requested via the ORA1 Gradle property, the
  tagged/keyed sweep shall honour it without source changes. *(reuses `[ORA1-PERF-02]`)*
- `[ORA2-HONEST-01]` The module KDoc shall state that ORA2's model reads modelled dot
  order and is therefore *less* independent of the tag algebra than ORA1's membership-only
  model, and shall name `[ORA2-CTL-01..04]` as the compensating evidence.
- `[ORA2-HONEST-02]` The oracle shall record, per sweep, which optional families
  (weighted, E1.4/E1.5 adopters) were active and which were reported not-applicable.

## 5. Behaviour specifications

Each becomes one named test. `covers:` notes mark scenarios that belong in the concord
corpus; those are authored under `concord/corpus/` per `concord/schema/*.md` (single
writer, schema-change-gated) and are **not** part of `:oracle`. Where a scenario does not
belong in the corpus, the reason is stated.

**BS-1 — Concurrent same-key puts resolve by dot order, everywhere**
(`[ORA2-MODEL-04]`, `[ORA2-DIFF-02]`, `[ORA2-CONV-02]`)
*Given* a 3-replica `OrMapCell` mesh and a script in which writers A and B each
`put(k, ·)` without observing the other.
*When* the mesh reaches quiescence.
*Then* every replica exposes the same value for `k`, and that value is the one the model's
`(counter, sourceId)` order selects — not merely "some agreed value".
*Corpus candidate*: `covers: [24-TMAP-03]` — the concurrent-put resolution is
boundary-observable through `value(k)` and needs no fault verbs.

**BS-2 — The counter tie is broken by sourceId, and the tie is actually generated**
(`[ORA2-GEN-04]`, `[ORA2-MODEL-04]`, `[ORA2-MODEL-12]`)
*Given* a generated case in which two live dots at one key share a counter.
*When* the case runs.
*Then* the exposed value matches the model's `sourceId` tie-break. *And* if a default
sweep produces no such case, the sweep configuration fails rather than passing silently.
*Not a corpus scenario*: it asserts a property of the **generator**, not of the kernel.

**BS-3 — Add-wins under concurrent put/remove** (`[ORA2-MODEL-05]`, `[ORA2-DIFF-03]`)
*Given* writer A holding `k` live and writer B issuing `remove(k)` having observed A's
first dot only.
*When* A concurrently issues a second `put(k, v2)` that B has not observed, and the mesh
quiesces.
*Then* `k` is present at every replica with value `v2` — B's reset-remove tombstoned only
what it observed. *Corpus candidate*: `covers: [24-TMAP-02]`, `[24-TMAP-04]`.

**BS-4 — Reset-remove is not remove-all** (`[ORA2-MODEL-05]`, `[ORA2-CTL-03]`)
*Given* the same setup as BS-3 with the model's reset-remove replaced by a remove-all
mutant.
*When* the sweep runs. *Then* the runner **detects** the mutant and names the key.
*Not a corpus scenario*: it is a mutation check on the oracle itself.

**BS-5 — Duplicate delivery is absorbed** (`[ORA2-DIFF-04]`, `[ORA2-MODEL-02]`)
*Given* a tagged map replicated across a diamond so every delta arrives twice.
*When* the case runs over a seed range.
*Then* every terminal fold equals the model's answer on every seed, and the second arrival
of a delta produces no effective change. *Corpus candidate*: `covers: [24-TMAP-01]`.

**BS-6 — Late joiner equals early joiner** (`[ORA2-DIFF-05]`)
*Given* a mesh that has gossiped a substantial script.
*When* a second terminal links after a mid-script quiesce barrier and the run completes.
*Then* the late terminal's fold equals the early terminal's and equals the model's.
*Corpus candidate*: `covers: [42-REPL-05]`.

**BS-7 — Replicas agree but are wrong is a distinct verdict**
(`[ORA2-CONV-02]`, `[ORA2-CONV-03]`, `[ORA2-DIFF-09]`)
*Given* a mutated model of the kernel's dot order applied uniformly (so all replicas agree
with each other while disagreeing with the reference).
*When* the convergence oracle runs.
*Then* it reports `replicas-agree-but-wrong`, distinct from `replica-divergence` and from a
single-stream mismatch. *Not a corpus scenario*: it asserts the oracle's failure taxonomy,
not kernel behaviour.

**BS-8 — Missing gossip is caught** (`[ORA2-CTL-04]`)
*Given* a mesh in which one replica's outbound gossip is not applied at one peer.
*When* the convergence oracle runs.
*Then* it fails with a divergence, naming the two replicas and the differing keys — the
control that proves the convergence check can fail. *Not a corpus scenario*: the concord
scenario language has no fault verbs (CHA1 §6), and manufacturing one here would be a
schema change.

**BS-9 — Wave-prefix holds for tagged terminals** (`[ORA2-DIFF-07]`)
*Given* a tagged map feeding a glitch-free consumer through two paths.
*When* the case is driven. *Then* every intermediate observation equals the model's answer
for some wave prefix; no observation corresponds to a partially applied wave.
*Corpus candidate*: `covers: [22-GF-01]` for the tagged-map shape specifically.

**BS-10 — Keyed re-put is atomic at every prefix** (`[ORA2-MODEL-08]`)
*Given* a `KeyedSetCell` script that re-puts the same key repeatedly.
*When* every intermediate observation is taken.
*Then* the key has exactly one live element at every prefix — never two, never zero.
*Corpus candidate*: `covers: [24-SET-01]`.

**BS-11 — Mergeable group-by is grow-only, and that is the specification**
(`[ORA2-MODEL-09]`)
*Given* a script that removes elements feeding a `MergeableGroupByCell`.
*When* the case runs. *Then* the kernel's aggregate does not shrink, the model's does not
either, and the divergence between this and `GroupByCell`'s retracting behaviour is
asserted explicitly rather than left implicit. *Not a corpus scenario* unless a normative
id for the non-retracting rule exists; if none does, file the missing id in
`concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` rather than inventing one.

**BS-12 — PnCounter converges to the pointwise max** (`[ORA2-MODEL-10]`,
`[ORA2-CONV-01]`)
*Given* three replicas incrementing concurrently.
*When* the mesh quiesces. *Then* every replica's total equals the model's per-source
pointwise-max sum. *Corpus candidate*: `covers: [42-REPL-04]`.

**BS-13 — Arrival-order control fails** (`[ORA2-CTL-01]`)
*Given* a fixed seed range and the tagged reads replaced by an untagged
`MapDelta`/`MapView` fold.
*When* the sweep runs. *Then* at least one seed fails. An oracle that cannot fail is not
evidence. *Not a corpus scenario*: it is a control on the oracle.

**BS-14 — Multi-writer scripts are refused where the model is undefined**
(`[ORA2-DIFF-12]`)
*Given* a generator configuration naming `MapCell` with two writers.
*When* generation runs. *Then* the case is rejected at generation time with a message
naming the cell and the reason — not emitted with an undefined expected value.

**BS-15 — The weighted family is absent, and says so** (`[ORA2-WGT-06]`)
*Given* a kernel without `WeightedSetDelta`.
*When* the sweep runs. *Then* the weighted suite reports `not-applicable` with the reason,
the sweep report records it, and no stub test passes in its place.

**BS-16 — Weighted integration is order-invariant** (`[ORA2-WGT-01]`, `[ORA2-WGT-02]`)
*(activates with E6)* *Given* a fixed multiset of weighted ops. *When* applied in any
seeded permutation. *Then* the integrated weights equal the batch sum on every seed.
*Corpus candidate once E6.1's normative ids exist*; until then, no `covers:` id exists to
cite and the scenario stays in `:oracle`.

**BS-17 — Weights never gossip** (`[ORA2-WGT-05]`)
*Given* a generator configured with both the weighted vocabulary and replica placement.
*When* generation runs. *Then* no generated case places a weighted cell in a replicated
mesh, and the attempt to configure one fails loudly.

**BS-18 — Catalog pairing is enforced for the tagged family** (`[ORA2-GEN-06]`)
*Given* a registration of `OrMapCell`'s kernel factory with no reference model.
*When* the catalog is built. *Then* registration fails, naming the id.

**BS-19 — Pinned tagged seeds are append-only** (`[ORA2-REPRO-02]`)
*Given* a discovered failing tagged seed pinned in `PinnedSeeds`.
*When* a later change would make the suite red.
*Then* the seed is not removed, replaced or reordered; the failure is filed and, if it
concerns a normative requirement that cannot be checked honestly, recorded in
`concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md`.

---

## 6. Scope boundaries

Every exclusion follows a dependency edge in `computenet-milestone-plan.md` §1/§2 or an
ordering decision in §4/§5.

- **ORA1's engine.** Module, generator core, runner, wave-prefix oracle, shrinker core,
  pinned corpus and failure taxonomy are ORA1 deliverables. The plan's edge is
  `ORA2 depends on ORA1`; ORA2 must consume, not fork. Re-implementing any of them is a
  defect in this feature.
- **KE1 core types.** The plan's dependency column reads `ORA1, KE1 core types`. ORA2
  models what exists; it does **not** implement `UntagCell`, `TaggedMapView`,
  multi-value reads or embedded mergeable values. Those are `96 §E1.4/E1.5` and belong to
  the kernel lane (KE1). `[ORA2-ADOPT-01..04]` are optional-feature requirements that
  activate when they land — they are not a licence to build them here.
- **The weighted family itself.** `96 §E6` is ⚠ PROPOSED and unbuilt. ORA2 writes the
  oracle for it (§4.6), not the cells. E6 is deliberately last in the E-plan and this
  feature must not pull it forward.
- **Any kernel change at all.** ORA2 is evidence-lane and test-only, exactly as ORA1 is.
  A discovered defect yields a shrunk counterexample, a pinned seed and a findings entry;
  the fix is admitted to the kernel lane per plan §4/§6.
- **Faults.** Partition, reorder, duplicate-by-injection, crash, journal truncation and
  arbitrary-frontier restart are **CHA1**; membership churn is **CHA3**. ORA2 builds
  quiescent meshes and uses only topological duplication (a diamond) for BS-5. The
  composition of ORA2's generator with CHA1's fault injection is a later, separately
  scheduled join — and is the natural shape of the eventual OR-map churn oracle.
- **Source epochs, RESTART and re-baselining.** `TagState.applyReBaseline`/`deadSources`
  and `OrMapCell.applyReBaseline` are exercised by `21-REBASE-01` and adjudicated under
  D-C12; generated cases contain no RESTART.
- **Eviction and windowing.** `Windows` is key derivation only, as in ORA1. Waterline
  eviction is KE4 — which is what ORA2 *feeds*, not what it contains.
- **Cycles and fixpoints.** Generated graphs stay acyclic; recursion is KE5.
- **Tag/tombstone reclamation.** `96 §E3.7` compaction changes what a fold may forget; a
  reference model for a compacting cell needs E3.5's stability read first. Out of scope.
- **Concord.** ORA2 flags `covers:` candidates (§5) and stops. Authoring corpus scenarios
  is single-writer and schema-change-gated under `concord/schema/*.md`.
- **Performance.** BEN1 owns `:bench` and JMH. ORA2's only budget requirement is
  `[ORA2-PERF-01]`.

---

## 7. Suggested task decomposition

List only — **do not create these as beads from this description**; a later planning pass
owns that.

1. **Tagged/keyed catalog registrations + shape rules.** `OrMapCell`, `KeyedSetCell`
   (deepened), `MergeableGroupByCell`, `PnCounterCell` through
   `OperatorCatalog.register`; availability-guarded entries for the E1.4/E1.5 and E6
   families. Realizes `[ORA2-GEN-06]`, `[ORA2-WGT-06]`, `[ORA2-HONEST-02]`, BS-15, BS-18.
2. **The dot model.** Modelled dots, observation sets, reset-remove, merge, membership and
   value; the `KeyedSetCell` atomicity model; `MergeableGroupByCell` and `PnCounterCell`.
   Realizes `[ORA2-MODEL-01..12]`, BS-3, BS-10, BS-11, BS-12.
3. **Multi-writer / multi-replica generator dimensions.** Writer dimension, concurrency
   ratio with achieved-ratio reporting, replica placement, the counter-tie guarantee, the
   re-put/reset-remove bias, and the multi-writer rejection for untagged cells. Realizes
   `[ORA2-GEN-01..05]`, `[ORA2-GEN-07]`, `[ORA2-DIFF-12]`, BS-2, BS-14.
4. **Convergence oracle + divergence failure kind.** `ConvergenceCheck` over
   `Replication`/`replicasOf`, composed with `ReplicaConvergence`; the
   `replicas-agree-but-wrong` verdict; the outlet-stream fold. Realizes
   `[ORA2-CONV-01..04]`, `[ORA2-DIFF-08]`, `[ORA2-DIFF-09]`, BS-1, BS-6, BS-7.
5. **Controls and mutation evidence.** Arrival-order control, inverted dot order, remove-all
   reset-remove, missing gossip; plus the honesty KDoc. Realizes `[ORA2-CTL-01..04]`,
   `[ORA2-HONEST-01]`, BS-4, BS-8, BS-13.
6. **Shrinker moves, pinned seeds, and retiring the hand-rolled convergence folds.** Drop-a-writer
   and drop-a-replica reductions; appended pinned seeds; converting
   `OrMapConvergenceTest`, `PnCounterReplicationTest` and the `SetConvergenceTest` family
   to the shared engine where that does not weaken an existing assertion. Realizes
   `[ORA2-REPRO-02]`, `[ORA2-DIFF-01]`, `[ORA2-DIFF-04..06]`, BS-5, BS-9, BS-19.
7. **Weighted suite, behind availability.** `[ORA2-WGT-01..06]`, BS-16, BS-17 — scheduled
   only once `96 §E6.2` exists.

---

## 8. Verification

```bash
./gradlew :oracle:test                                                   # full module suite incl. ORA1's
./gradlew :oracle:test --tests 'civictech.oracle.tagged.TaggedSweepTest'
./gradlew :oracle:test --tests 'civictech.oracle.tagged.ConvergenceSweepTest'
./gradlew :oracle:test --tests 'civictech.oracle.tagged.TaggedControlsTest'   # BS-4, BS-8, BS-13 — blocking
./gradlew :oracle:test -Poracle.seeds=2000                               # extended sweep (on demand)
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.replication.OrMapConvergenceTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.replication.PnCounterReplicationTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test                                                   # converted call sites stay green
./gradlew :concord:test                                                  # unchanged — ORA2 authors no scenarios
./gradlew test                                                           # repository-wide gate
```

What constitutes proof:

- **Differential sweeps** over a seed range asserting incremental == batch on every tagged
  terminal, with density reported (`[ORA2-DIFF-06]`).
- **Convergence sweeps** asserting every replica equals the one converged reference
  (`[ORA2-CONV-02]`) — not replica-vs-replica agreement alone.
- **Discrimination evidence** (`[ORA2-CTL-01..04]`). A green sweep without these is not
  evidence and the feature is not delivered.
- **Named behaviour tests** for BS-1 … BS-19 (BS-16/BS-17 only when E6 exists).
- **The import-boundary architecture test** extended to the tagged model
  (`[ORA2-MODEL-11]`).
- The report must state which seed ranges ran, which optional families were active, and
  every excluded behaviour with its written reason (`[ORA2-HONEST-02]`,
  `[ORA2-HONEST-03]`).

No generated or build output in the diff. No edits to `doc/spec/`, `CONCORDANCE.md`,
`concord/corpus/*.yaml`, or plan documents.

---

## 9. Risks / open questions

1. **The model must read dot order, so it is less independent than ORA1's.**
   `[ORA1-MODEL-03]` bans tag internals precisely to keep the oracle honest; `[24-TMAP-03]`
   makes value a *function of* dot order, so ORA2 cannot obey that ban and still model
   `OrMapCell`. The chosen relaxation — model *its own* dots from the script, never read
   the kernel's (`[ORA2-MODEL-06]`, `[ORA2-MODEL-12]`) — preserves the second-implementation
   property but not the algebra-independence property. `[ORA2-HONEST-01]` requires saying
   so in the KDoc, and `[ORA2-CTL-02]` is the compensating evidence. **Do not** silently
   let the model read a kernel `Timestamp` "just for the tie-break": that collapses the
   oracle into a mirror.
2. **`sourceId` order-isomorphism is a real coupling.** The tie-break in `DOT_ORDER` is by
   `sourceId`, and the kernel derives it via `UUID.nameUUIDFromBytes("or-map-tags:…")`.
   The harness supplies the mapping; if a KE1 change alters the derivation, ORA2's ties
   silently stop matching. **Open question:** should the case builder assert the derivation
   at construction time (a checked-in expectation) so a derivation change fails loudly
   rather than producing wrong tie-breaks? Decide in task 2.
3. **Concurrency has to be *achieved*, not configured.** A naive generator emits scripts
   whose "concurrent" writes are in fact causally ordered by the delivery schedule, and the
   sweep then passes trivially. `[ORA2-GEN-02]`'s achieved-ratio reporting and
   `[ORA2-GEN-04]`'s tie guarantee exist because of this failure mode; treat a
   configured-100%/achieved-3% sweep as a red result, not a green one.
4. **KE1's shape may move.** E1.4/E1.5 are unbuilt, and the plan's dependency is on "KE1
   core types", not on a landed E1.6. If KE1 lands with a different adopter surface, the
   `[ORA2-ADOPT-*]` requirements need re-specification, not silent reinterpretation. The
   dependency edge is deliberately left **unwired** in the tracker until KE1 has an id.
5. **The weighted half may never activate under this feature.** E6 is P3 and last by
   design. `[ORA2-WGT-06]` is the honest guard: report not-applicable, do not stub. If E6
   slips indefinitely, the correct move is to split the weighted suite into its own item
   under KE-E6 rather than let it rot as an unmet clause here.
6. **Overlap with `ReplicaConvergence`.** The kernel already ships a convergence invariant
   with a departed-stream rule. ORA2 must compose with it, and must not duplicate its
   membership logic (`liveRefs()` = `replicasOf(id) ∩ folds.keys`) — particularly since
   CHA3 will extend exactly that path for churn. Coordinate the seam with CHA3 before
   writing task 4.
7. **Corpus pressure.** Several BS scenarios are honest `covers:` candidates
   (`[24-TMAP-01..04]`, `[42-REPL-04]`, `[42-REPL-05]`). Promoting them is a separate,
   schema-gated concord change and must not be smuggled in with this feature.
   `doc/spec/CONCORDANCE.md` is generated and must not be hand-edited.
8. **`MergeableGroupByCell`'s non-retraction may have no normative id.** If BS-11 finds
   none, the honest move is a `DISPUTES.md` entry naming the missing id — not inventing a
   `[24-*]` id, which is normative-id minting and requires explicit documentation-maintenance
   authorization.
design:
# ORA2 — design decisions and alternatives considered

## D1. A feature under ORA1, not an epic

ORA2 adds no harness. It registers cells through a seam ORA1 was explicitly built to
expose (`OperatorCatalog.register`, `[ORA1-API-02]`/`[ORA1-API-03]`), extends one model
package, adds one check to one runner, and appends to one pinned-seed list. The only
structurally new thing is the *convergence obligation* — and even that is a caller of
ORA1's bring-your-own entry point `[ORA1-DIFF-11]`, not a second runner. An epic would
imply an independent decomposition; the honest decomposition is §7's seven tasks inside
ORA1's module.

## D2. The model mints its own dots; it never reads a kernel `Timestamp`

`[24-TMAP-03]` makes the exposed value a function of dot order, so a purely
membership-derived reference (ORA1's `[ORA1-MODEL-03]`) cannot express `OrMapCell`. Two
options were considered:

- **(a) read the kernel's dots** and compute the expected value from them. Rejected: it
  makes the oracle a mirror. Any dot-minting or dot-ordering bug would be reproduced
  identically in the "reference" and the sweep would be green by construction.
- **(b) model dots independently from the script** and require only *order isomorphism*
  of writer identities. Chosen. The model is still a second implementation; only the
  writer→sourceId mapping crosses, and it crosses at case-construction time in the
  harness, not at evaluation time in the model (`[ORA2-MODEL-12]`).

The residual weakness — the model is no longer independent of the *tag algebra*, only of
the *implementation* — is stated in the KDoc (`[ORA2-HONEST-01]`) and answered with four
blocking controls (`[ORA2-CTL-01..04]`), one of which specifically inverts the model's dot
order (`[ORA2-CTL-02]`).

## D3. Convergence is a new failure kind, not a new runner

`ReplicaConvergence` (`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/verify/ReplicaConvergence.kt`)
already answers "do replicas agree?" — its `liveRefs()` intersects `replicasOf(logicalId)`
with attached folds, and it carries the G-45 departed-stream rule. What it cannot answer
is "do they agree on the *right* value", because it has no batch reference. ORA2 supplies
exactly that half and composes with the existing invariant. Consequently
`replicas-agree-but-wrong` and `replica-divergence` are two distinct verdicts
(`[ORA2-CONV-03]`, BS-7): collapsing them would hide the uniform-bug case, which is the
one a mesh cannot detect from the inside.

## D4. Concurrency must be measured, not declared

The dominant failure mode of a multi-writer generator is that the schedule causally
orders every "concurrent" write, so the interesting branch of `[24-TMAP-04]` is never
taken and the sweep passes for the wrong reason. Hence `[ORA2-GEN-02]` reports the
*achieved* concurrency ratio and `[ORA2-GEN-04]` makes the counter-tie case a
configuration requirement rather than a statistical hope. A sweep whose achieved ratio is
near zero is a red result.

## D5. The weighted family is specified, not built, and never faked

`96 §E6` is ⚠ PROPOSED, P3, and explicitly last in the E-plan ("the tag↔weight boundary
should be informed by E1's OR-map and E3's GC work"). No `WeightedSetDelta`,
`WeightedSetCell`, `TagsToWeightsCell` or `WeightsToTagsCell` exists in the tree today.
Three options:

- write the oracle now against types that do not exist — impossible;
- drop the weighted half from the plan row — dishonest, the row says "OR-map, weighted";
- **write it as optional-feature EARS gated on the cells' existence** (`[ORA2-WGT-01..06]`),
  with `[ORA2-WGT-06]` forbidding a silently-skipped or stubbed suite. Chosen.

`[ORA2-WGT-05]` additionally encodes the E-plan's borrowing rule — weights live inside a
replica, tags cross replicas — as a *generator* constraint, so a weighted cell can never
be placed in a gossip mesh even by accident.

## D6. Deliberately no faults

Partition/reorder/duplicate/crash/journal/restart is CHA1's rig; membership churn is
CHA3's harness. ORA2 stays quiescent and uses topological duplication (a diamond) for the
idempotence property. The composition — CHA1's fault plans driving ORA2's generated
tagged meshes — is the obvious next artifact, and it is deliberately left to a later
scheduled join so that a failure in either half is attributable.

## D7. Pinned seeds are append-only, always

`AGENTS.md`: "Do not replace a discovered failing seed with a friendlier seed."
`[ORA2-REPRO-02]` restates it for the tagged corpus. A tagged seed that goes red after a
KE1 change is a finding, and if the requirement it breaks cannot be checked honestly the
entry goes to `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` — never a softened scenario, never a rotated
seed.

## D8. Dependency wiring

Wired: **ORA2 → ORA1** (`computenet-4ru`), the plan's own edge.
Unwired, deliberately: **KE1** ("KE1 core types" in the plan's dependency column) — the
KE1 bead is being created in a parallel session and its id must not be guessed.
`[ORA2-ADOPT-01..04]` and much of §4.6 activate on that edge.

## D9. Scope: evidence lane, zero kernel edits

Same posture as ORA1. A discovered divergence produces a shrunk counterexample, a pinned
seed and a findings entry; the fix is admitted to the kernel lane per milestone plan §4/§6.
No `doc/spec/` edits, no `CONCORDANCE.md` edits (it is generated), no corpus authoring.
acceptance_criteria:
Accepted when every requirement id below is realized by a named test and the feature is verifiable via ./gradlew :oracle:test plus ./gradlew test.

REUSE (blocking): ORA2 adds no second sweep loop, report format, runner or shrinker. Every cell arrives through ORA1's OperatorCatalog.register seam ([ORA1-API-02], [ORA1-API-03]); the failure taxonomy, forEachSeed density sweep, wave-prefix oracle and PinnedSeeds are ORA1's, extended not forked. [ORA2-DIFF-06], [ORA2-DIFF-07], [ORA2-DIFF-10], [ORA2-DIFF-11], [ORA2-PERF-01], [ORA2-PERF-02].

TAGGED/KEYED MODEL: [ORA2-MODEL-01] through [ORA2-MODEL-12] — merge/membership/value/reset-remove modelled from the script alone; the model mints its own dots and never reads a kernel Timestamp; KeyedSetCell re-put atomicity, MergeableGroupByCell non-retraction and PnCounterCell pointwise-max modelled; the import-boundary architecture test extended (BS-3, BS-10, BS-11, BS-12).

CONVERGENCE ORACLE: [ORA2-CONV-01] through [ORA2-CONV-04] and [ORA2-DIFF-09] — every replica checked against ONE converged reference, not replica-vs-replica agreement; replicas-agree-but-wrong is a distinct verdict from replica-divergence; composes with cell.verify.ReplicaConvergence rather than duplicating it (BS-1, BS-6, BS-7).

GENERATOR: [ORA2-GEN-01] through [ORA2-GEN-07] and [ORA2-DIFF-12] — multi-writer scripts with per-writer observation state; ACHIEVED concurrency ratio reported, not merely configured; at least one counter-tie-broken-by-sourceId case per default sweep or the configuration fails; re-put/reset-remove bias; untagged order-dependent cells rejected under multiple writers (BS-2, BS-14).

DIFFERENTIAL RESULTS: [ORA2-DIFF-01] through [ORA2-DIFF-05], [ORA2-DIFF-08] — concurrent same-key puts, concurrent put/remove add-wins, duplicate absorption, late-joiner equality and quiescent replica equality all asserted against the model (BS-5, BS-9).

DISCRIMINATION (blocking — a green sweep without these is not evidence): [ORA2-CTL-01] [ORA2-CTL-02] [ORA2-CTL-03] [ORA2-CTL-04] — arrival-order control fails on a fixed seed range; inverted dot order detected and attributed; remove-all-instead-of-reset-remove detected; missing gossip reported as divergence (BS-4, BS-8, BS-13).

OPTIONAL FAMILIES, HONESTLY GATED: [ORA2-WGT-01] through [ORA2-WGT-06] and [ORA2-ADOPT-01] through [ORA2-ADOPT-04] — active only where the kernel types exist; an absent weighted family is reported not-applicable with its reason, never skipped, disabled or stubbed (BS-15, BS-16, BS-17).

HONESTY AND REGRESSION: [ORA2-HONEST-01] [ORA2-HONEST-02] [ORA2-HONEST-03] [ORA2-REPRO-02] [ORA2-GEN-06] — the reduced independence of the dot model is stated in the KDoc; per-sweep applicability recorded; unverifiable behaviour excluded with a written reason and filed in concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md; pinned seeds append-only, never rotated to make the suite green (BS-18, BS-19).

Green: ./gradlew :oracle:test, ./gradlew :kernel:test, ./gradlew :concord:test (unchanged), ./gradlew test. No kernel edits, no corpus authoring, no spec/plan/CONCORDANCE edits.

title: DSC3 — NAT traversal / relay
description:
# DSC3 — NAT traversal / relay

Lane: distribution. `computenet-milestone-plan.md` §1 (Distribution lanes), §5 rank 20 ("second
wave"). **Depends on: DSC2** (`computenet-aas`) — the DAG edge `DSC1 --> DSC2 --> DSC3`, and
transitively on DSC1 (`computenet-ssa`) via §5's *"DSC1 before DSC2/DSC3: identity before
discovery."*
Unblocks: **open-internet deployment** — the plan's "Unblocks" column names no chunk, because what
DSC3 unblocks is not another ticket but a *class of deployment*: peers that are not on the same LAN
and not behind a port-forward.

---

## 1. Ambition / Why

DSC2 answers *"who is out there and where do they say they are"*. It does not answer *"can I
actually open a socket to them"*, and on the real internet the answer is usually **no**. Every
ComputeNet peering that exists today is a TCP connect to a routable address:

```
is Wire.Listen -> WsTransport.listen(wire.wsPort, side)     // one side must be dialable
is Wire.Dial   -> WsTransport.connect(URI(wire.uri), side)  // demo/shopping/.../Main.kt:237-238
```

`WsTransport.awaitReachable` (`WsTransport.kt:79-89`) literally opens a raw `Socket(host, port)` and
retries until it succeeds. Behind consumer NAT, carrier-grade NAT, a corporate firewall, or a mobile
network, that socket never succeeds — not because of a bug, but because nothing on the path will
accept an unsolicited inbound connection. Two laptops in two homes can hold each other's verified
`PeerRecord`, agree on identity, and still never exchange a byte. **This is the exact point at which
ComputeNet stops being a LAN/manual-peering system, and it is the last structural blocker on the
deployment model the project's own niche implies** (P10, the civic-tech story: a neighbourhood
assembly whose participants go home and keep contributing).

Three consequences that are concrete, not aspirational:

- **The federated and decentralized product lanes assume open-internet reach.** SOC2 (federated:
  multi-peer, moderation membranes) and SOC3 (decentralized: open mesh) are LAN demos until an
  arbitrary pair of peers can connect. The plan does not draw `DSC3 --> SOC3` because SOC3 can be
  *demonstrated* on a LAN or on hosted VMs; it can only be *deployed* over DSC3.
- **"Rent a VPS with a public IP" is not the answer the architecture wants.** P4 (no global
  coordination) and P7 (local-first, open by default) are violated by degrees each time the only
  working deployment is "everyone connects to the one server". DSC3's job is to make the
  centralized element as small and as untrusted as possible — a byte forwarder that cannot read
  identity and cannot forge traffic — rather than a hub that holds the graph.
- **Every partial fix has already been absorbed elsewhere, so the remaining problem is exactly
  this one.** Identity is DSC1's (`:identity`, derived `PeerId`, authenticated hello). Finding a
  peer is DSC2's (`:discover`, signed `PeerRecord`, `PeerBook`). Parking, reconnect, catch-up and
  convergence across a dropped socket are already shipped (M10.3–M10.4, `WsConnection` backoff,
  `Peering.announceTo` re-announce, `[42-REPL-05]`). What is left, and only what is left, is
  **path establishment**.

**Why the relay, not the hole punch, is the deliverable.** The honest engineering position given
this codebase: the one shipped transport is **WebSocket over TCP** (`:wire`, `org.java-websocket`;
40/41 point 4 M5.5). Reliable NAT traversal in the field is a UDP technique — STUN-discovered
reflexive addresses plus simultaneous-open hole punching, as used by WebRTC/ICE and QUIC-based
meshes. TCP simultaneous-open works against a minority of NATs and not at all against symmetric NAT
or CGNAT. Therefore DSC3's primary mechanism is a **relay**: an untrusted, authenticated,
identity-blind byte forwarder that both peers can reach outbound, over which the *ordinary* DSC1
authenticated hello runs **end to end**. Direct-path optimization (a dialable peer preferring a
direct connection, reflexive-address learning, optional local port mapping) is a second, smaller
mechanism layered on top, and a UDP/QUIC transport with real ICE is explicitly a **separate future
epic**, not smuggled in here.

**The security property that makes a relay acceptable, and the one it cannot provide.** Because the
DSC1 hello runs end to end through the relay, the relay **cannot impersonate either peer** — it does
not hold either private key and cannot produce a valid nonce signature ([DSC1-HELLO-03..07]). It
can, however, **read every byte it forwards, drop them, delay them, reorder across peers, or splice
in bytes** — unless the two peers establish confidentiality and integrity *end to end through it*.
That is the single largest design decision in this epic, and §9 opens it explicitly: DSC3 either
brings an end-to-end encrypted channel between peers (a Noise-style handshake over the DSC1
keypairs, the smallest honest form), or it declares relay hops confidentiality-trusted — loudly,
configurably, and never by default silence. **This epic requires the decision to be explicit; it
forbids the silent third option of shipping a relay and not mentioning what it can see.**

## 2. What we build

### 2.1 Module: a new leaf module `relay/` (`:relay`)

**Decision: a new small leaf Gradle module `relay/`, not new code in `:kernel`, not folded into
`:discover`, not folded into `:wire`.** Registered in `settings.gradle.kts` beside `:wire`,
`:identity`, and `:discover`.

Dependency shape:

```
:identity -> :kernel                              (DSC1)
:discover -> :kernel, :identity                   (DSC2; MUST NOT depend on :wire)
:relay    -> :kernel, :identity, :wire, :discover (splices real frames; consumes PeerEndpoint)
:kernel   -> nothing new                          (MUST NOT depend on :relay)
```

Justification in the repository's own terms:

- **AGENTS.md: "Keep `kernel` transport-neutral. A new transport dependency belongs in a small
  transport module such as `wire`."** A relay is transport machinery in the strongest sense — it
  terminates and splices sockets. It has no business anywhere near `:kernel`; the kernel must not
  learn that a path can be indirect.
- **Not inside `:discover`.** `:discover` is deliberately transport-free — `[DSC2-NEU-02]` forbids
  it from depending on `:wire`, which is what lets `PeerBook` be tested with a fake dialer and no
  socket. A relay *must* depend on a transport (it splices WebSocket connections). Folding relay
  into `:discover` would destroy that property and force every discovery test to carry a transport.
- **Not inside `:wire`.** `:wire` is *"the one concrete transport"* (`doc/ARCHITECTURE.md` §1) and
  every demo depends on it. A relay is an **operated service** with a different lifecycle: it is a
  runnable process someone deploys, with its own resource limits, abuse surface, and configuration.
  Demos that never relay should not carry it.
- **Two artifacts, one module.** `:relay` contains both the *relay client* (path selection, relay
  session establishment, direct-path upgrade) and the *relay server* (a runnable forwarder). They
  share the framing and the admission vocabulary; splitting them across modules would duplicate it.
  If the server later needs to deploy without the client, splitting is a mechanical follow-up.
- **No new third-party dependency should be required.** The relay server can reuse `:wire`'s
  existing Java-WebSocket server. Reflexive-address learning, if built, is a small UDP or
  application-level echo, not a STUN library. Reject any dependency that arrives without a
  demonstrated gap — the `:wire` precedent is one dependency, deliberately chosen.

### 2.2 Surface

1. **`PathCandidate` and path selection.** Extends DSC2's `PeerEndpoint` vocabulary additively with
   a *kind*: `Direct(endpoint)` | `Relayed(relayEndpoint, peerId)`. `PeerRecord` (DSC2) already
   carries a list of endpoints inside its signed bytes ([DSC2-REC-02]) — a relay candidate is
   another entry, so **no new record format and no new signature scheme**. Path preference is
   deterministic and stated: direct before relayed, and a successful direct path supersedes an
   established relayed one.
2. **Relay session protocol (application-level, over the existing WebSocket).** A peer opens an
   ordinary connection to the relay and performs a *reservation*: it proves possession of its
   identity key (a nonce challenge, the DSC1 primitive reused) and asks the relay to accept
   connections addressed to its `PeerId`. A second peer connects to the same relay and requests a
   *circuit* to that `PeerId`. The relay then forwards bytes in both directions **without
   interpreting them**. From `WsTransport`'s point of view the socket is an ordinary peer socket:
   the hello, the announcements, the frames all run unchanged.
3. **End-to-end authentication through the relay — the non-negotiable property.** The DSC1
   authenticated hello runs between the two *peers*, not between peer and relay. The relay's own
   authentication is a separate, weaker relationship (the relay knows who reserved which id; it
   proves nothing about the traffic). `AuthLevel.Authenticated` on a relayed peering means exactly
   what it means on a direct one — that is the invariant that keeps in-process, direct-remote, and
   relayed-remote paths observationally identical.
4. **End-to-end confidentiality/integrity, or an explicit declared absence.** Two admissible
   outcomes, and the epic must ship one of them named in configuration and in the report:
   (a) an end-to-end encrypted channel between peers established over the DSC1 keypairs, so a relay
   forwards ciphertext; or (b) `RelayTrust.ConfidentialityTrusted` — the operator declares the relay
   trusted to read traffic, the system says so at startup, and the setting has no silent default.
   Option (b) alone is acceptable only as a first increment and only if (a) is filed as the
   follow-up. **What is forbidden is shipping a relay whose exposure is undocumented.**
5. **Relay server: admission, accounting, and limits.** A relay is an abuse magnet. It admits by
   reservation (identity-proved), applies per-identity limits on concurrent circuits, bandwidth, and
   reservation lifetime, and exposes counters. It holds no keys of its peers, stores no graph state,
   and persists nothing about the traffic it carries.
6. **Direct-path upgrade (optional feature, kept small).** When a peer learns a reflexive address
   that turns out to be dialable, or when one side is dialable and the other is not (the common
   asymmetric case, which needs *no* traversal at all — just the right dial direction), the system
   prefers the direct path and tears the circuit down without disturbing the peering's identity or
   its `LocationRegistry` state. **This is the case worth optimizing first: "one side is dialable"
   covers a large fraction of real deployments and requires no hole punching whatsoever.**
7. **Wire encoding.** Additive only. Relay framing is a property of the *connection to the relay*,
   not of `WireFrame`: the relay forwards opaque bytes and `WireCodec.VERSION` MUST NOT be bumped.
   New serializable types (reservation, circuit request, path candidate kind) register through the
   existing open polymorphic registry (`cell.wire.WireSerializers`, 40/41 point 1).

## 3. How, using ComputeNet

Real types and file paths a later agent starts from.

| Concern | Where it lives today |
|---|---|
| The dial that fails behind NAT | `WsTransport.connect(uri, side, backoff)` and its raw TCP probe `awaitReachable` (`wire/src/main/kotlin/civictech/wire/WsTransport.kt:72-89`) |
| Listener side (what a NATed peer cannot offer) | `WsTransport.listen(port, side)` → `WsListener` (`WsTransport.kt:50-56`, `:196-228`) |
| The session a relayed socket must reproduce exactly | `WsTransport.Session` — hello, ingress install, announcement hook, `onClose` unpublish (`WsTransport.kt:104-194`) |
| Reconnect/backoff semantics a circuit must not break | `WsConnection.onClose` reconnect thread (`WsTransport.kt:256-278`), `DEFAULT_RECONNECT_BACKOFF` (`:44`) |
| Peer identity + allowlist on a peering | `Peering.Side` / `Side.admits` (`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/wire/Peering.kt:115-124`) |
| Peer identity hull across reconnects (must survive a path switch) | `RegistryMirrorCell.peer` and its four-step happens-before KDoc (`Peering.kt:59-92`) |
| Disconnect ⇒ park, re-announce ⇒ replay (what a path switch rides on) | `LocationRegistry.unpublishRemotes(via)` (`Peering.kt:143-151`, `WsTransport.kt:146`, `:192`), `Peering.announceTo` catch-up (`Peering.kt:199-208`) |
| Derived identity, nonce challenge, sign/verify | `:identity` — **DSC1** (`computenet-ssa`); reused verbatim for relay reservation proofs |
| Signed endpoint candidates | `PeerRecord`/`PeerEndpoint` — **DSC2** (`computenet-aas` §2.2); relay candidates are additive entries in the already-signed list |
| Dial policy that must learn about paths, not addresses | `PeerBook` — **DSC2** (`[DSC2-DIAL-01..11]`) |
| Rejection observability | `ManagedHost.deadLetterOutlet`, `DeadLetters`, `WsTransport.Session.preHelloDrops` idiom (`WsTransport.kt:129-130`) |
| Deterministic harness | `testkit` `SimWorld`/`awaitUntil`; `Peering.loopback` (`Peering.kt:154`) as the socket-free twin |

**How a relayed peering comes up — the exact sequence, reusing existing seams:**

1. Peer A (NATed) opens an outbound WebSocket to relay R and **reserves** its `PeerId`, proving key
   possession with a nonce challenge (`:identity`, DSC1 primitive). The reservation is an ordinary
   outbound connection — the one thing NAT always permits.
2. A publishes a `PeerRecord` (DSC2) whose endpoint list now includes `Relayed(R, A)`. The list is
   inside the signed bytes ([DSC2-REC-02]), so the relay candidate is as unforgeable as any other.
3. Peer B discovers the record, verifies it ([DSC2-REC-04..05]), and `PeerBook` selects a path:
   direct candidates first, then relayed ([DSC3-PATH-*]).
4. B opens an outbound WebSocket to R and requests a **circuit** to A's `PeerId`. R matches it
   against A's reservation and, from then on, forwards bytes both ways without interpreting them.
5. `WsTransport.connect` runs against that circuit **unchanged**: the DSC1 hello exchange happens
   **between A and B**, end to end. R sees nonces and signatures it cannot produce. If either side
   fails verification the connection is refused at `Session.onText` before an ingress exists
   ([DSC1-HELLO-06..07]) — the relay has no way to make a failing hello pass.
6. From there it is today's system exactly: mirror bound, `announceTo` catch-up, `Remote` locations,
   parked traffic replays, `[42-REPL-05]` convergence.
7. If a direct path later proves usable, the peering re-establishes over it and the circuit closes.
   The path switch is a *reconnect*, which the system already handles: `unpublishRemotes(via)` parks
   senders, the re-hello re-announces, catch-up replays. **The peer's identity does not change
   across the switch** — `RegistryMirrorCell.peer` remains the hull, exactly as for an ordinary
   reconnect.

**Same observable semantics, in-process and remote ([41-LOC-01]) — the invariant this epic is most
able to break.** A relayed peering must be *observationally identical* to a direct one: same
delivered values, same wave/source/tag continuity, same ownership discipline, same dead-letter
accounting, same `AuthLevel`. Only cost differs (P2 tiers: direct call → queue hop → serialized
send → **serialized send through one extra forwarding hop**). Concretely, the things most likely to
silently diverge and which the tests must pin: per-link FIFO ordering across the extra hop; an
`Owned`/`Leased` payload in flight when a circuit dies (no path may silently drop an exclusive —
AGENTS.md core invariant); and `EdgeOpen`/`EdgeClose` topology frames ordered against data across a
path switch (40/41 §4, W3.2).

## 4. Functional requirements (EARS)

**Honesty note on upstream ids.** As established for DSC1 and re-verified here:
`doc/spec/40-distribution/43-security.md` carries **no `[43-*]` EARS ids at all** (its G-29 content
is prose), and `doc/spec/` contains **no normative text whatsoever on NAT traversal, relaying,
STUN/TURN, hole punching, or reachability** — grepping the whole spec tree returns nothing on the
subject, and `95-research-plan.md` has no R-entry for it (R7 covers identity strength only).
**So DSC3 cites no normative id that it makes true, because none exists.** What it makes true is the
milestone plan's DSC3 row and its "open-internet deployment" unblock.

Adjacent normative ids that MUST keep holding across the change — these are the real citations, and
they are the ones a relay is most likely to violate:

- **`[41-LOC-01]`** — linking behaves identically whether cells share a thread, a process, or
  nothing but a network; only cost differs. A relayed path is another cost tier, not another
  semantics.
- **`[42-REPL-05]`** — a consumer that links to a replica after deltas have flowed still converges;
  a path switch is exactly a late re-link.
- **`[42-REPL-06]`** — orderly departure semantics, which a circuit teardown must not counterfeit.
- **`[13-LINK-05]`** — link rejection reasons stay the defined set; "the relay dropped it" is not a
  new rejection reason visible to the graph.
- DSC1's **`[DSC1-HELLO-03..07]`**, **`[DSC1-HELLO-12]`**, **`[DSC1-OBS-01..05]`** and DSC2's
  **`[DSC2-ID-01..06]`**, **`[DSC2-REC-02]`**, **`[DSC2-DIAL-01]`** — consumed, never weakened.

A later agent may propose promoting stabilized `[DSC3-*]` requirements into
`doc/spec/40-distribution/` (alongside a DSC2-authored `44-discovery.md`) as `[44-*]`/`[45-*]` ids.
That is spec-maintenance work, **out of scope here**.

### 4.1 Path candidates and selection

- **[DSC3-PATH-01]** The system shall represent a way of reaching a peer as a path candidate that
  is either direct or relayed, and shall carry relayed candidates inside the same signed
  `PeerRecord` endpoint list DSC2 already defines ([DSC2-REC-02]).
- **[DSC3-PATH-02]** The system shall not define a peer name, handle, or address alias for relaying;
  a relayed candidate shall name the peer by the `PeerId` derived under DSC1 ([DSC2-ID-01]).
- **[DSC3-PATH-03]** When both direct and relayed candidates are available for a peer, the system
  shall attempt direct candidates before relayed candidates.
- **[DSC3-PATH-04]** The system shall maintain at most one live peering per `PeerId` across all
  path kinds ([DSC2-DIAL-01]).
- **[DSC3-PATH-05]** When a direct path becomes usable to a peer currently reached over a relay, the
  system shall establish the direct path and shall then close the circuit.
- **[DSC3-PATH-06]** When a path switch completes, the peer's `PeerId`, its mirrored `Remote`
  locations, and its topology attribution shall be the same as before the switch.
- **[DSC3-PATH-07]** If every candidate for a peer fails, then the system shall report the peer as
  unreachable with the per-candidate failure reasons and shall retry on a capped backoff.
- **[DSC3-PATH-08]** The system shall derive every path-selection timing decision from an injected
  clock and shall express path establishment through an injectable connector, so selection is
  testable without a socket.

### 4.2 Relay reservation and circuits

- **[DSC3-RLY-01]** Where a peer is configured to use a relay, the peer shall establish the
  connection to the relay as an outbound connection.
- **[DSC3-RLY-02]** When a peer reserves an identity at a relay, the peer shall prove possession of
  the private key corresponding to that `PeerId` by signing a relay-issued nonce.
- **[DSC3-RLY-03]** If a reservation request does not prove key possession for the claimed
  `PeerId`, then the relay shall refuse the reservation and shall record the refusal.
- **[DSC3-RLY-04]** The relay shall hold at most one active reservation per `PeerId`, and a later
  proved reservation shall supersede an earlier one rather than coexisting with it.
- **[DSC3-RLY-05]** When a circuit request names a `PeerId` with an active reservation, the relay
  shall forward bytes between the two connections in both directions.
- **[DSC3-RLY-06]** If a circuit request names a `PeerId` with no active reservation, then the relay
  shall refuse the circuit with a distinguishable reason and shall not hold the requester open
  indefinitely.
- **[DSC3-RLY-07]** The relay shall not parse, interpret, rewrite, or reorder the payload bytes of a
  circuit, and shall preserve their order and framing in each direction.
- **[DSC3-RLY-08]** The relay shall not require, request, or accept any private key material from
  any peer.
- **[DSC3-RLY-09]** The relay shall not persist circuit payload bytes to any durable store.
- **[DSC3-RLY-10]** When a reservation expires or its connection closes, the relay shall close every
  circuit that depended on it.
- **[DSC3-RLY-11]** The relay shall enforce configured per-identity limits on concurrent circuits,
  circuit lifetime, and forwarded bandwidth, and shall refuse over-limit requests with a
  distinguishable reason.
- **[DSC3-RLY-12]** The relay shall expose counters for reservations, circuits, refusals per reason,
  and bytes forwarded, and shall not include payload content in any log line.

### 4.3 End-to-end authentication through an untrusted relay

- **[DSC3-E2E-01]** The system shall perform the DSC1 authenticated hello between the two peers of a
  relayed peering, and shall not treat the relay as a party to it.
- **[DSC3-E2E-02]** While a peering is relayed, `currentPrincipal()` shall evaluate to the same
  `Principal` and `AuthLevel` it would evaluate to for the same two peers connected directly.
- **[DSC3-E2E-03]** If a relay substitutes, injects, or replays hello material, then the receiving
  peer shall refuse the connection before any ingress is installed and shall record the refusal
  ([DSC1-HELLO-06..07]).
- **[DSC3-E2E-04]** The system shall not raise a peer's `AuthLevel` on the strength of a relay's
  statement, a reservation, or a circuit.
- **[DSC3-E2E-05]** The system shall evaluate `Peering.Side.allow` on a relayed peering against the
  derived `PeerId` exactly as on a direct peering ([DSC1-HELLO-12]).
- **[DSC3-E2E-06]** If a relay tampers with, truncates, or injects bytes after the hello, then the
  receiving peer shall detect the resulting frame corruption, shall dead-letter it on the receiving
  host, and shall not apply it to any registry or cell state.
- **[DSC3-E2E-07]** The system shall state its relay confidentiality posture explicitly at startup —
  either that traffic is end-to-end encrypted between peers, or that the configured relay is trusted
  to observe traffic — and shall not adopt an observable-by-relay posture by silent default.
- **[DSC3-E2E-08]** Where end-to-end encryption between peers is enabled, the system shall establish
  it from the DSC1 identity keys, and a relay shall observe only ciphertext, connection timing, and
  volume.

### 4.4 Reachability and direct-path optimization

- **[DSC3-REACH-01]** Where one peer of a pair is directly dialable, the system shall establish the
  peering over the direct path in that direction without using a relay.
- **[DSC3-REACH-02]** Where a peer learns a reflexive (externally observed) address, it shall
  include it as an additional candidate in its signed `PeerRecord` rather than replacing its local
  candidates.
- **[DSC3-REACH-03]** The system shall not treat a reflexive address as authenticated information
  and shall verify it only by successfully establishing an authenticated peering over it.
- **[DSC3-REACH-04]** If a reflexive-address source is unavailable or returns inconsistent answers,
  then the system shall continue with its remaining candidates and shall not fail startup.
- **[DSC3-REACH-05]** Where local port mapping (for example UPnP-IGD or NAT-PMP) is enabled, it
  shall be disabled by default and shall require explicit configuration.
- **[DSC3-REACH-06]** The system shall not require inbound reachability for any peer in order to
  participate in a mesh.

### 4.5 Semantic equivalence across path kinds (the invariant most at risk)

- **[DSC3-EQV-01]** A relayed peering shall deliver the same values, in the same per-link order, as
  the same peering established directly ([41-LOC-01]).
- **[DSC3-EQV-02]** Wave, source, and tag continuity, and glitch-free completeness, shall hold
  across a relayed peering exactly as across a direct one.
- **[DSC3-EQV-03]** When a circuit fails mid-delivery, the system shall park senders and replay on
  reconnect exactly as it does for a direct socket failure, and shall not drop an `Owned` or
  `Leased` payload on any path, failure, teardown, or switch.
- **[DSC3-EQV-04]** Topology events (`EdgeOpen`/`EdgeClose`) shall retain their ordering against
  data frames across a relayed path and across a path switch.
- **[DSC3-EQV-05]** A path switch shall not produce duplicate `Remote` locations, duplicate
  announcements applied as new state, or a second peering for the same `PeerId`.
- **[DSC3-EQV-06]** The system shall not surface path kind to cell code, to `LinkRequest`, or to any
  `BoundaryPolicy` predicate.
- **[DSC3-EQV-07]** A relayed peering shall converge to the same state as a direct peering for a
  consumer that joins after deltas have already flowed ([42-REPL-05]).

### 4.6 Observability

- **[DSC3-OBS-01]** The system shall make the current path kind and relay endpoint for each peering
  available for read-only inspection.
- **[DSC3-OBS-02]** The system shall make every path-establishment failure observable with a
  machine-distinguishable reason among: unreachable, refused-at-hello, relay-unreachable,
  no-reservation, over-limit, circuit-closed, tampered.
- **[DSC3-OBS-03]** The system shall not silently discard any frame rejected on a relayed path.
- **[DSC3-OBS-04]** The system shall expose counters for circuits established, path switches, bytes
  relayed, and failures per reason.
- **[DSC3-OBS-05]** The system shall not include private key material, session secrets, or payload
  content in any log line, counter label, or dead-letter description.
- **[DSC3-OBS-06]** When the system runs with a confidentiality-trusted relay, it shall record that
  posture where an operator can read it, for the lifetime of the process.

### 4.7 Neutrality and compatibility

- **[DSC3-NEU-01]** The `:kernel` module shall not declare a dependency on `:relay`, and no kernel
  type shall gain a notion of path kind.
- **[DSC3-NEU-02]** The `:discover` module shall not declare a dependency on `:relay` or on `:wire`
  ([DSC2-NEU-02]).
- **[DSC3-NEU-03]** The system shall not increment `WireCodec.VERSION` for relaying.
- **[DSC3-NEU-04]** While no relay is configured, the system shall behave exactly as it does before
  this epic, for every existing demo and test.
- **[DSC3-NEU-05]** The relay server shall be startable and stoppable as an ordinary process without
  requiring any ComputeNet graph state, journal, or durable store.
- **[DSC3-NEU-06]** The path-selection logic shall be exercisable to completion with a test-supplied
  connector and clock, without binding a socket.

### 4.8 Explicitly non-verifiable — stated, not softened

Recorded up front, per AGENTS.md's honesty rule. These belong in `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` if a
corpus requirement is ever written against them, and must never be softened into a passing test.

- **[DSC3-NV-01]** **No single-host test can establish that NAT traversal works.** NAT behaviour is
  a property of specific middleboxes: endpoint-dependent vs. address-dependent mapping, symmetric
  NAT, CGNAT, hairpinning, firewall state timeouts, ISP filtering. A loopback or single-machine test
  proves the relay protocol, the path-selection policy, and the end-to-end hello; it proves nothing
  about traversal in the field. The honest claim is: *the relay path is verified as far as a single
  host can verify it; behaviour against real NATs is untested.* No requirement above may be worded
  so that a loopback test appears to satisfy "two peers behind NAT can connect".
- **[DSC3-NV-02]** **Direct-path success rate is unmeasurable here.** What fraction of real peer
  pairs get a direct path rather than a relay is a field statistic requiring deployment telemetry.
  Any number stated without that data is invention.
- **[DSC3-NV-03]** **A relay's non-observation cannot be proven, only structurally prevented.**
  Absent end-to-end encryption ([DSC3-E2E-08]), a relay reads everything, and no test on the peer
  side can detect that it did. `[DSC3-E2E-07]` requires the posture to be *declared*; declaring is
  not preventing.
- **[DSC3-NV-04]** **Traffic-analysis resistance is not attempted.** Even with end-to-end
  encryption, a relay observes who talks to whom, when, and how much — arguably the most sensitive
  metadata in a civic-tech deployment. DSC3 builds no padding, cover traffic, or mixing.
- **[DSC3-NV-05]** **Relay availability is a centralization the epic reduces but does not
  eliminate.** A peer whose only path is one relay is offline when that relay is. Multi-relay
  candidates ([DSC3-PATH-01]) help only if configured. DSC3 builds no relay discovery market, no
  incentive layer (ECO1's territory), and no automatic failover beyond retrying candidates.
- **[DSC3-NV-06]** **Denial of service against a relay is not solved.** `[DSC3-RLY-11]`'s
  per-identity limits are bypassed by minting fresh identities, which DSC1 `[DSC1-NV-02]` states is
  free. Costed identity is ECO1's (G-62 Sybil half). DSC3 must not claim abuse resistance.
