- **[SOC2-29]** (Optional-feature) WHERE the policy declares an attention ceiling or per-`Principal` rate for federated interest, a remote assertion above the ceiling SHALL be clamped rather than refused, and excess frames within a window SHALL be refused per `Principal` without penalizing any other `Principal`. *(cross-references [SEC1-14..15]; 30/34 decision 6 — "attention is a request, not an entitlement")*
- **[SOC2-30]** (Ubiquitous) A view assembled under a moderation policy SHALL report that content was withheld and under which rule class, and SHALL NOT present a moderated view as an unfiltered one. *(the application-visible half of SEC1's accounting; a silent hole is indistinguishable from data loss)*
- **[SOC2-31]** (Ubiquitous) A per-*person* moderation decision (mute/hide) SHALL be accounted with the same visibility as a boundary denial — a record, a counter, and a reported withheld-count — even though it is an ordinary dataflow filter rather than a `BoundaryPolicy` predicate. *(§2.4 last row)*
- **[SOC2-32]** (Ubiquitous) A moderation decision SHALL be local to the node that made it, and the epic SHALL NOT introduce a shared blocklist, a moderation vote, or any cross-node agreement on policy. *(P4; election-backed group governance is SOC3)*

### 4.5 Unwanted behaviour — the trust boundary

- **[SOC2-33]** (Unwanted behaviour) IF a message is moderated away at any seam, THEN it SHALL produce a typed denial record, increment the boundary's denial counter, and emit a sanitized dead letter — no moderation path SHALL drop a message without accounting. *(cross-references [SEC1-25]; SEC1 owns the mechanism, SOC2 owns being its consumer)*
- **[SOC2-34]** (Unwanted behaviour) IF a moderated-away crossing carries an `Owned` or `Leased` payload, THEN that payload SHALL be discharged exactly once — `Owned` frozen or consumed once, `Leased` released once — and a live exclusive handle SHALL NEVER reach the dead-letter fan-out. *(cross-references [SEC1-20], [SEC1-23], [SEC1-26]; standing repo invariant; spec 23 R8 / G-46)*
- **[SOC2-35]** (Unwanted behaviour) IF a moderation decision removes an input a downstream wave was waiting on, THEN the wave SHALL still reach completeness and the feed SHALL NOT hang. *(cross-references [SEC1-27]; I-18 edge-will-not-deliver)*
- **[SOC2-36]** (Unwanted behaviour) IF a moderation denial occurs mid-wave, THEN no observer SHALL see a reconvergence point combining pre- and post-denial values. *(cross-references [SEC1-28]; [22-GF-01..03]; if this cannot be asserted honestly on the landed frontier machinery it goes to DISPUTES.md — see §9)*
- **[SOC2-37]** (Unwanted behaviour) IF a peer floods interest assertions, THEN the node SHALL clamp and rate-limit them per `Principal` and SHALL continue serving every other peer, and no unauthenticated peer SHALL be able to raise this node's attention band above the configured floor. *(40/43 §"Attention is a request, not an entitlement"; cross-references [SEC1-14..15])*
- **[SOC2-38]** (Unwanted behaviour) IF a peer replays previously accepted gossip, THEN the node SHALL reject the replay on the per-source counter, SHALL NOT double-apply it, and SHALL converge to the same fold as if the replay had not occurred. *(93 I-28 — the counter defeats replay; tag idempotence; cross-references [SEC1-21..22], [DSC1-ANN-08])*
- **[SOC2-39]** (Unwanted behaviour) IF a peer emits deltas that fail integrity verification, THEN the node SHALL refuse them at ingress and SHALL recover by drop-and-reconverge, adding no ack, retry, version vector or second synchronization protocol. *(93 I-28; 42 §Integrity among untrusting replicas; cross-references [SEC1-22])*
- **[SOC2-40]** (Unwanted behaviour) IF a moderation policy is malformed or names an unregistered `ProjectionId`, THEN the node SHALL fail startup with a diagnostic naming the rule, and SHALL NOT start with the rule silently disabled. *(a silently-dropped moderation rule is a security failure that looks like success)*
- **[SOC2-41]** (Unwanted behaviour) IF a policy denial occurs, THEN it SHALL NOT be classified as a cell fault, SHALL NOT trigger supervision RESTART, and SHALL NOT mint or advance a wave. *(cross-references [SEC1-29])*

### 4.6 Findings and hygiene

- **[SOC2-42]** (Ubiquitous) The epic SHALL append its findings to `doc/demo-findings.md` citing G-ids, and SHALL NOT edit `91-gap-analysis.md` or `CONCORDANCE.md` directly. *(plan §6 standing hygiene)*
- **[SOC2-43]** (Unwanted behaviour) IF a required capability is missing from the kernel (multi-hop disclosure composition, capability revocation that tears down live links, management-plane authority across a bridge, per-person signing), THEN the epic SHALL record it as a finding citing G-54's residual / I-28 §8 and SHALL NOT implement it in-lane.
- **[SOC2-44]** (Ubiquitous) Every requirement above SHALL be covered by at least one named test or SHALL be explicitly listed as uncheckable with the reason.
- **[SOC2-45]** (Unwanted behaviour) IF a seed is discovered that fails a property, THEN that seed SHALL be retained and SHALL NOT be replaced with a passing seed. *(AGENTS.md core invariant)*

### 4.7 Explicitly non-verifiable — stated, not softened

These are named so that no weak test is written to appear to satisfy them. They belong in
`concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` if a corpus requirement is ever written against them.

- **[SOC2-NV-01]** SOC2 cannot demonstrate **moderation efficacy against a determined adversary**. Every property below is about *mechanism* — that a declared rule is enforced, accounted, and cannot be bypassed by the paths tested. Whether a policy achieves a social outcome, or whether an adversary can find an untested path, is not a testable claim and no requirement asserting it may be written.
- **[SOC2-NV-02]** SOC2 cannot bound **Sybil identity creation**. Minting a keypair is free (DSC1 [DSC1-NV-02]); a node can be flooded with fresh authenticated identities each within its own rate limit. Per-`Principal` budgets and identity-minting cost are ECO1 (G-62), consumed by SOC3.
- **[SOC2-NV-03]** SOC2 cannot verify **end-to-end authorship**. Signing is per emitting peer (93 I-28), so a relayed message's originating person is unverifiable without per-person keys, which SOC2 does not build. [SOC2-14]/[SOC2-15] make the limit visible rather than papering over it.
- **[SOC2-NV-04]** SOC2 cannot verify **multi-hop disclosure composition**. Whether `disclosure`/`integrity` compose across hops or must be re-declared at each membrane is open (I-28 §8). SOC2 adopts the safe default — re-declare at each membrane — and states it; it does not prove composition.
- **[SOC2-NV-05]** SOC2 cannot verify **revocation of already-disclosed content**. Once a peer has received state, removing it from an allowlist refuses future links but does not recall what it holds; capability revocation that tears down live links is G-54 residual.

---

## 5. Behaviour specifications (Given/When/Then)

Each scenario is intended to become one named test. `→ concord` marks scenarios that belong
in `concord/corpus/`; a `covers:` id is only legal if it exists in `doc/spec/` — where none
does, the entry goes to `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` instead, and the scenario lives as a
demo/kernel test.

### Happy paths

**BS-1 — Two nodes converge (`SocialFederationConvergenceTest`, `Peering.loopback` + seed sweep)** — [SOC2-17], [SOC2-18]
*Given* nodes A and B loaded from the same seed, joined by `Peering.loopback`, each with a
default (empty) moderation policy; *when* each applies a disjoint prefix of the SNB update
stream and the world runs to idle; *then* both nodes' replicated folds are equal, and the
result is independent of which node accepted each write.
→ concord, `covers: [42-REPL-04]`.

**BS-2 — Late joiner catches up (`SocialFederationConvergenceTest`)** — [SOC2-18]
*Given* A and B have gossiped for N updates; *when* node C joins the mesh; *then* C's fold
becomes indistinguishable from a node present from the start, with no separate sync protocol
invoked. → concord, `covers: [42-REPL-05]`.

**BS-3 — Interest scopes the wire (`SocialFederationInterestTest`)** — [SOC2-19], [SOC2-20]
*Given* viewer V on node A following exactly persons hosted on node B; *when* B's other
persons post; *then* those deltas never cross to A (asserted by counting frames at the
bridge, not by timing), and when V follows one of them, that person's *subsequent* messages
do cross. → concord, `covers: [42-INT-01]`.

**BS-4 — Authenticated federation (`SocialFederationIdentityTest`, `:wire`)** — [SOC2-08], [SOC2-09]
*Given* two nodes each with a DSC1 keypair and a policy containing a per-peer rule; *when*
they peer; *then* both admit at `AuthLevel.Authenticated`, each bound `PeerId` equals the
fingerprint of the other's public key, and starting either node with a per-peer rule and no
identity configured fails at startup rather than silently degrading.

**BS-5 — Redacted profile, catch-up and live alike (`SocialModerationDisclosureTest`)** — [SOC2-27]
*Given* a policy declaring `Project(ProjectionId("snb-public-profile"))` on the federated
profile exposure, with pre-existing state; *when* a remote peer links and then a live profile
update is emitted; *then* both the `onLinked` catch-up and the live delta arrive redacted by
the same transform, and no un-redacted field is observable on either path.
*(Cross-references [SEC1-17]; the same shape as SEC1 BS-8, here with real application content.)*

### Failure, recovery and adversarial paths

**BS-6 — A malicious peer forges attribution (`SocialFederationAdversaryTest`)** — [SOC2-11], [SOC2-12], [SOC2-14]
*Given* nodes A, B, M, where person P's home peer is B; *when* M emits a validly signed,
well-formed authored message attributed to P; *then* A refuses the attribution, emits exactly
one denial record naming M, B and P, increments the denial counter, applies nothing to P's
authored stream, and A's fold remains equal to B's.
**This is the scenario that distinguishes "the bytes verify" from "this peer may say this".**
It must not be omitted.

**BS-7 — Partition during a federated write (`SocialFederationPartitionTest`, seeded)** — [SOC2-21], [SOC2-22]
*Given* A and B mid-stream, with a viewer on A following persons on B; *when* the peering
partitions while both sides keep accepting writes, and the feed is read on A during the
partition; *then* A serves its own state, marks B's contribution stale with the frontier it
reached, and does **not** present it as current; *when* the partition heals; *then* parked
gossip replays, catch-up re-fires, and A and B converge with no operator action and no
duplicate application. *(Model on `demo/shopping`'s convergence tests and
`ReplicatedSessionTest`'s partition/heal shape.)*
→ concord candidate near `concord/corpus/42-replication`; bind `covers: [42-REPL-05]` only
if the scenario is honestly about catch-up, else DISPUTES.md.

**BS-8 — Replay and forged gossip (`SocialFederationAdversaryTest`)** — [SOC2-38], [SOC2-39]
*Given* an authenticated, signing peering; *when* a peer re-sends a previously accepted delta,
and separately sends a delta whose signature does not verify; *then* each is refused before
`deltaInlet` with a denial record naming the reason, no ack/retry/version-vector frame is
produced, the fold is unchanged by both, and a later valid signed delta is accepted and
converges. *(Cross-references [SEC1-21..22]; DSC1 [DSC1-ANN-06], [DSC1-ANN-08].)*

**BS-9 — Two peers disagree about moderation (`SocialModerationDisagreementTest`)** — [SOC2-24], [SOC2-30], [SOC2-32]
*Given* nodes A and B federating one forum, where A's policy hides content class X and B's
does not; *when* messages of class X and of other classes are posted on both nodes; *then*
A's and B's **replicated folds are equal**, their **presented feeds differ**, A's feed reports
a withheld count and the rule class that withheld it, B's reports none, and neither node
attempts to propagate its policy to the other.
**This scenario is the epic's thesis statement** — that policy divergence is not state
divergence — and it is the one most likely to be quietly weakened into "both feeds look
plausible". Assert both halves.

**BS-10 — Moderated-away exclusive payload (`SocialModerationOwnershipTest`)** — [SOC2-34]
*Given* a moderated exposure whose crossing carries an `Owned` payload (and a `Leased`
variant); *when* the policy denies the crossing; *then* the `Owned` is frozen exactly once,
a second `take()` raises use-after-move, the `Leased` is released exactly once and the pool's
outstanding-lease count returns to its pre-emission value, the denial record carries only the
`Frozen`/`Redacted` form, and no live exclusive handle reaches the dead-letter fan-out.
*(Cross-references [SEC1-20], [SEC1-23], [SEC1-26] — SEC1 fixes the mechanism; this scenario
is SOC2's proof that the fix holds through an application-shaped moderation path.)*

**BS-11 — Attention flood from one peer (`SocialFederationAdversaryTest`)** — [SOC2-29], [SOC2-37]
*Given* a policy with an attention `ceiling` and `ratePerWindow = k`; *when* peer M asserts
interest above the ceiling and sends `k+2` assertion frames in a window while honest peer B
sends `k`; *then* M's assertions are clamped to the ceiling (a clamp is **not** a denial and
produces no denial record — [SEC1-15]), M's excess frames are refused with two denial records,
every one of B's is delivered, and the node's dispatch band for unrelated work is unchanged.

**BS-12 — Moderation denial does not hang or tear the feed (`SocialModerationWaveTest`)** — [SOC2-35], [SOC2-36]
*Given* a feed whose assembly depends on two upstream edges, one crossing a moderated boundary;
*when* a delta on that edge is denied mid-wave; *then* the wave reaches completeness within a
bounded wait via the I-18 edge-will-not-deliver classification, the run does not hang, and a
reconvergent (diamond) read path never observes a mixed pre/post-denial combination.
**If the glitch-freedom half cannot be asserted honestly on the landed frontier machinery,
file it in `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` — do not replace it with a weaker assertion.**
*(This is SEC1 BS-13's hazard, reached through a real application topology; if SEC1 already
filed it as a dispute, SOC2 cites that entry rather than re-litigating it.)*

**BS-13 — Malformed policy fails loudly (`SocialModerationPolicyTest`)** — [SOC2-40]
*Given* a policy file naming an unregistered `ProjectionId` (and, as a second case, a rule
that cannot lower onto any seam); *when* the node starts; *then* startup fails with a
diagnostic naming the offending rule, and the node does not start with that rule disabled.

**BS-14 — Blocked peer cannot rehello under another name (`SocialFederationAdversaryTest`, `:wire`)** — [SOC2-08], [SOC2-09]
*Given* a policy blocking `Peer(M)` at admission, with `AuthLevel.Authenticated` required;
*when* M reconnects claiming a different allowlisted name while presenting its own key; *then*
the hello is refused before any ingress exists, the refusal is recorded with both ids, and no
frame from M reaches the registry. *(Depends on DSC1 [DSC1-HELLO-06], [DSC1-HELLO-12]; this
scenario is what makes the block real rather than nominal.)*

**BS-15 — Multi-JVM end-to-end (`SocialFederationJvmTest`, slow-tagged)** — [SOC2-04..06]
*Given* three nodes launched with `JvmPeer.launch` on `freePort()` ports, one listening and
two dialling, each with its own keystore and policy; *when* ops are posted over HTTP to each
node and one node is killed and restarted against its journal; *then* the surviving nodes
keep serving, the restarted node rejoins and converges, and `HttpProbe.await` observes the
converged feed on every node. *(Model on `demo/shopping`'s multi-JVM peering tests.)*

**BS-16 — Open default unchanged (`SocialFederationDefaultsTest`, regression guard)** — [SOC2-06]
*Given* a node started with no `--listen`, `--peer`, `--identity` or `--policy` flags; *when*
SOC1's whole test suite runs; *then* behaviour is indistinguishable from SOC1 — no boundary
predicate is evaluated, no per-message cost is added, and every SOC1 requirement still holds.
*(P7/P2; cross-references [SEC1-02..03].)*

---

## 6. Scope boundaries

**In scope**: multi-peer federation of the SOC1 graph, interest-scoped replication across the
wire, the moderation policy model and its lowering onto the three I-28 seams, application-visible
withholding, home-peer identity binding on DSC1's authenticated `PeerId`, the adversarial and
partition suites, and the findings all of that produces.

**Out of scope — belongs to a named other chunk (the plan's dependency edges):**

- **The boundary mechanism itself → SEC1** (`computenet-usd`). SOC2 declares policy; it does not
  build denial accounting, ownership discharge on denial, the wave/glitch behaviour of a denied
  edge, or the bridge binding of `BoundaryPolicy`. If SEC1 has not landed, SOC2 is blocked on it —
  it must not re-implement the seams. *(plan §1: `SEC1 → SOC2 moderation`.)*
- **Cryptographic identity → DSC1** (`computenet-ssa`). Keypairs, hello challenge/response,
  `AuthLevel.Authenticated`, signed announcements, key storage. SOC2 consumes them.
  *(plan §2: `DSC1 --> SOC2`.)*
- **The single-node graph, schema, generator, feed assembly → SOC1** (`computenet-07k`). SOC2
  extends; it does not redesign. *(plan §2: `SOC1 --> SOC2`.)*
- **Open mesh, discovery, election-backed groups, budget-bounded interest → SOC3.** No DSC2
  discovery (peers are configured), no MEM1 election or leader failover, no ECO1 budgets, no
  group governance state. *(plan §1: `SOC3 | SOC2, MEM1, DSC2, ECO1`.)*
- **NAT traversal / relay → DSC3.**
- **Per-Principal budgets, identity-minting cost, Sybil economics → ECO1** (G-62). SOC2 delivers
  the clamp and the rate limit it inherits from SEC1; it delivers no budget. *(plan §1:
  `ECO1 | DSC1, PLC2`.)*
- **Placement and spawn-redirection → PLC3** (G-61).
- **Leader/follower single-writer replication and election → MEM1/MEM2** (G-44/G-45). SOC2 uses
  mergeable state only.
- **The G-54 residual → filed, not built**: capability revocation tearing down live links,
  management-plane authority across a bridge, multi-hop disclosure composition, at-rest
  encryption ([SOC2-43], [SOC2-NV-04], [SOC2-NV-05]).
- **BB-SNB measurement, SNB BI queries, kernel ORDER BY/LIMIT, partitioning** — unchanged from
  SOC1's exclusions.
- **Spec and plan document edits.** Findings go to `doc/demo-findings.md` only ([SOC2-42]).

---

## 7. Suggested feature decomposition (list only — do not create these beads here)

1. **F1 — Federation skeleton and the allowlist decision.** `:wire`/`:identity` dependencies,
   `--listen`/`--peer`/`--identity` flags, `Peering.Side` + `WsTransport` wiring, loopback twin
   for tests, and the §2.2 decision taken in writing (escalate / facade / reduced scope).
   Covers [SOC2-01..06], [SOC2-16..18].
2. **F2 — Identity binding and attribution.** Home-peer field on `Person`, attribution check,
   attribution-strength surfacing, `AuthLevel.Authenticated` floor for per-peer rules.
   Covers [SOC2-08..15].
3. **F3 — Interest-scoped federated replication and the federated feed.** `Interest` promotion
   from demo-side filter to per-instance registered interest, follow/unfollow widening/narrowing,
   staleness marking, partition/heal. Covers [SOC2-19..24], [SOC2-07].
4. **F4 — The moderation policy model and its lowering.** Declarative policy artifact, the
   rule → seam lowering table, per-person filter layer, withheld-count surfacing, loud failure
   on malformed policy. Covers [SOC2-25..32], [SOC2-40].
5. **F5 — Adversarial and accounting suite.** Forged attribution, replay, bad signature, attention
   flood, blocked-peer rehello, moderated exclusive payload, denial-mid-wave, moderation
   disagreement, multi-JVM run, default-unchanged regression. Covers [SOC2-33..39], [SOC2-41],
   plus [SOC2-42..45] and the §4.7 non-verifiable statements in the final report.

---

## 8. Verification

```
./gradlew :demo:social:test
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.architecture.DemoSurfaceAllowlistTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.architecture.ArchitectureRatchetTest'
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.membrane.*'
./gradlew :wire:test
./gradlew :concord:test
./gradlew :demo:shopping:test
./gradlew :demo:exchange:test
./gradlew test
```

- Run `:demo:social:test` first and expand outward; `:demo:exchange:test` is the composition
  exit gate and must stay green.
- Multi-JVM (BS-15) is slow-tagged and excluded from the default gate, like SOC1's scale test;
  the convention plugin's 5-minute per-method timeout and 2g heap are hard ceilings.
- Determinism: every federated property must be checkable over `Peering.loopback` under
  `SimulationController`/`SimWorld` with `awaitUntil` ([SOC2-06]); a socket-only test is a
  weaker test and needs justification in its feature.
- Concord: add a scenario only with a legal `covers:` id — a dangling id fails
  `./gradlew :concord:check`. Regenerate `doc/spec/CONCORDANCE.md` with
  `./gradlew :concord:concordance` if and only if scenarios were added; never hand-edit it.
  Where no legal id exists (all of 40/43's moderation content), add a `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md`
  entry and say so in the report.
- Report exactly which tests ran, which requirement ids are covered, and which remain
  uncovered or explicitly uncheckable ([SOC2-44], §4.7).

---

## 9. Risks and open questions

1. **The demo-surface allowlist (§2.2) is the highest risk and it is structural, not
   incidental.** `civictech.cell.membrane` is not a demo-visible package. Resolve in F1 before
   any moderation code exists. Do not edit the guardrail to make the build pass.
2. **SEC1 must land first, and SOC2 must not paper over its absence.** Every denial requirement
   here ([SOC2-33..36], [SOC2-41]) cross-references a SEC1 requirement. If SEC1 has not shipped,
   SOC2's moderation is silent `return null` — which is exactly the state SEC1 exists to fix and
   which would make BS-10 pass vacuously. Check SEC1's landed state before writing F4/F5.
3. **DSC1 must land first for [SOC2-09] to mean anything.** Under `TransportVouched` only, a
   per-peer rule is keyed on a spoofable name. [SOC2-09] turns that into a startup failure rather
   than a silent weakness — but it also means SOC2 cannot demo per-peer moderation until DSC1 is in.
4. **Glitch-freedom across differing disclosure regimes** is genuinely open. SEC1 §9 risk 1 names
   it: a reconvergent graph where one arm is filtered and another is not can present a downstream
   cell with values from two disclosure regimes, and I-28 reasons only about a single crossing.
   A federated social feed is *full* of such diamonds. SOC2 must consume SEC1's decision, not make
   its own; if SEC1 filed it in DISPUTES.md, [SOC2-36] cites that entry.
5. **`readState` does not answer for remote refs.** The federated feed reads local replicas filled
   by interest-scoped gossip, not remote cells (§3). This makes freshness a first-class UI concern
   ([SOC2-21]) and is the design decision most likely to be "solved" by an unwanted synchronous
   cross-wire read. Do not add one.
6. **`supportsSince`/`supportsScope` coverage**, inherited from SOC1 risk 2, now bites across the
   wire: `KeyedSetCell.supportsScope = false`, `GroupByCell.supportsSince = false`. Which cell
   types can sit on a federated leg is an F3 design question, not an implementation detail.
7. **First-hop-only attribution ([SOC2-14], [SOC2-NV-03]) will feel wrong to a product reader.**
   It is the honest consequence of "signing is per emitting peer, never per logical cell". Per-person
   signing keys are a large, separate design (key custody, rotation, recovery, and a second identity
   tier) — file it, do not build it.
8. **Moderation efficacy is not testable ([SOC2-NV-01]).** Resist the pull to write a requirement
   like "the system SHALL prevent abusive content". Every moderation requirement here is about
   mechanism, accounting and visibility. A weak test that appears to satisfy an efficacy claim is
   worse than no test.
9. **Policy disagreement vs divergence (BS-9)** is easy to test wrongly. Assert equal *replicated
   folds* and different *presented views* in the same test; asserting only the second proves
   nothing, and asserting only the first misses the whole point of the epic.
design:
# SOC2 design notes

## Module

Extends the existing `demo/social/` (`:demo:social`) module from SOC1 — no new module.
`demo/social/build.gradle.kts` gains:

```kotlin
implementation(project(":wire"))      // as demo/shopping, demo/exchange
implementation(project(":identity"))  // DSC1's new leaf module
```

New package `civictech.demo.social.federation`. New flags on the existing `main`:
`--listen <port>`, `--peer <ws-uri>` (repeatable), `--identity <dir>`, `--policy <file>`.

## The guardrail that must be settled first

`kernel/src/test/kotlin/civictech/cell/architecture/DemoSurfaceAllowlistTest.kt:60-72`

```
demoCellPrefixes = { host, port, graph, data, observe, link, wire,
                     consistency, control, durability, replication }
```

`civictech.cell.membrane` (`BoundaryPolicy`, `CompositeCell`, `Exposure`, `SurfaceMode`) is
**absent**. Amendment policy in that file's KDoc: widening needs human approval + a note in
`doc/architecture-decisions.md`; "do not edit this file to make a build pass."

Three options, choose one in F1 with the tradeoff written down: (a) escalate the widening for
`:demo:social`; (b) build a narrow facade in an already-allowed package; (c) ship federation
without membranes and file the finding. (c) guts the epic.

## Topology sketch

```
node A                                            node B
 LocationRegistry / ManagedHost                     LocationRegistry / ManagedHost
 KeyedCells<Long>("snb-person") ──┐             ┌── KeyedCells<Long>("snb-person")
 KeyedCells<Long>("snb-forum")  ──┤             ├── KeyedCells<Long>("snb-forum")
                                  │             │
              FederationBoundary (CompositeCell + Exposure + BoundaryPolicy)
                                  │             │
   Peering.Side(registry, bridgeHost, peer = PeerId("ed25519:…"))
                                  └──── ws ─────┘
              Replication.replicate(cell, host)   // mergeable cells only
              LocationRegistry.setInterest(ref, Interest…)  // follows-as-interest
```

Feed on A = union over local replicas that interest-scoped gossip has filled, with SOC1's
per-instance `Map<CellRef, TagFrontier>` retention unchanged. `ManagedHost.readState` does
**not** answer for `Remote` refs — do not add a synchronous cross-wire read.

## Moderation policy → seam lowering

| SOC2 rule | Seam | Kernel mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| block peer | 1 admission | `Peering.Side.allow` / `allowPeers` |
| read-only peer on forum F | 2 link | `BoundaryPolicy.linkAuthority` |
| private forum | 3b disclosure | `disclosure = Deny` |
| redacted federated profile | 3b disclosure | `disclosure = Project(ProjectionId("snb-public-profile"))` |
| require signed gossip | 3c integrity | `integrity = RequireSigned` + `AuthLevel.Authenticated` |
| bound remote interest | 3a protocol | `protocolAuthority[ATTENTION]`: `minAuth`, `ceiling`, `ratePerWindow` |
| mute person P | — (not a seam) | local `SetCell<Long>` + `FilterCell` on the read path — a person is not a `Principal`; must still be accounted ([SOC2-31]) |

## Key types (all verified present)

| Concern | Type / file |
|---|---|
| Peering / allowlist / loopback | `civictech.cell.wire.Peering` — `Side(registry, bridgeHost, peer)`, `Side.admits`, `loopback(a,b)`, `hostIngress` (Peering.kt:115,123,154,168) |
| Bridge cells | `civictech.cell.wire.BridgeEgressCell`/`BridgeIngressCell` |
| Socket transport | `civictech.wire.WsTransport.listen/connect` (WsTransport.kt:50,72) |
| Gossip mesh | `civictech.cell.replication.Replication.replicate/evict` (Replication.kt:166,284) |
| Interest | `civictech.cell.link.Interest` + `LocationRegistry.setInterest/interestOf` |
| Boundary policy | `civictech.cell.membrane.BoundaryPolicy` / `CompositeCell` / `Exposure` — gated by §2.2 |
| Identity | DSC1 `:identity` — key-derived `PeerId`, authenticated hello |
| Denial accounting | SEC1's record + counter + sanitized dead letter; `DeadLetters.sanitizeForDeadLetter` |
| Tests | `civictech.testkit.SimWorld`, `awaitUntil`, `JvmPeer.launch/freePort`, `HttpProbe` |

## Sequencing

F1 (skeleton + guardrail decision) → F2 (identity binding) → F3 (interest-scoped federation)
→ F4 (moderation model) → F5 (adversarial suite). F4 is blocked on SEC1 actually having landed
its denial accounting; F2's `AuthLevel.Authenticated` floor is blocked on DSC1. Write BS-9
(moderation disagreement, equal folds + different views) and BS-10 (moderated exclusive payload)
first inside their features — both are invisible in the happy path.

## Standing constraints

- Kernel stays transport-neutral; nothing new lands in `:kernel` from this epic.
- Prefer additive wire encoding; no frame fork, no `WireCodec.VERSION` bump.
- Findings to `doc/demo-findings.md` only; never edit `91-gap-analysis.md` or `CONCORDANCE.md`.
- Do not replace a discovered failing seed with a friendlier one.
- Do not write a requirement asserting moderation efficacy or Sybil resistance — see §4.7.

Specifically: (1) module, topology and surface [SOC2-01..07], with [SOC2-03] (the civictech.cell.membrane demo-surface allowlist decision) resolved in writing before any moderation code is written and never by editing the guardrail; (2) identity [SOC2-08..15], including [SOC2-09] (per-peer rules require AuthLevel.Authenticated or startup fails) and [SOC2-11..12] (home-peer attribution refusal with an accounted denial); (3) replication and interest [SOC2-16..24], making [42-REPL-04], [42-REPL-05], [42-REPL-06] and [42-INT-01] true; (4) moderation policy content and lowering [SOC2-25..32], with [SOC2-30]/[SOC2-31] (withheld content is reported, never a silent hole) and [SOC2-32] (policy is local; no shared blocklist, no vote) treated as non-negotiable; (5) the trust-boundary unwanted-behaviour block [SOC2-33..41] — every moderated-away message accounted, every exclusive payload discharged exactly once, no hang, no glitch, no fault classification — each cross-referencing SEC1 ([SEC1-20], [SEC1-23], [SEC1-25..29]) rather than restating it; (6) findings and hygiene [SOC2-42..45]. Behaviour specs BS-1..BS-16 each exist as a named test, with BS-6 (forged attribution), BS-7 (partition during a federated write), BS-9 (moderation disagreement: equal replicated folds, different presented views), BS-10 (moderated-away Owned/Leased discharged exactly once) and BS-12 (denial mid-wave: completeness and glitch-freedom, or a DISPUTES.md entry — never a weakened scenario) all present. The §4.7 non-verifiable statements [SOC2-NV-01..05] (moderation efficacy, Sybil, end-to-end authorship, multi-hop disclosure composition, revocation of disclosed content) are stated in the final report as explicitly unverified rather than tested vacuously. Verification: ./gradlew :demo:social:test, :wire:test, :concord:test, :demo:exchange:test and repo-wide ./gradlew test green; DemoSurfaceAllowlistTest and ArchitectureRatchetTest pass without amendment, or a widening is escalated with human approval and a note in doc/architecture-decisions.md. Concord scenarios added only with a legal covers: id, otherwise a concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md entry. No spec or plan document edits; findings appended to doc/demo-findings.md only.
notes:
Milestone-plan source: computenet-milestone-plan.md §1 product row 'SOC2 | Federated: multi-peer, moderation membranes, real identity | SOC1, DSC1, SEC1 | SOC3'; §2 DAG (SOC1-->SOC2-->SOC3, DSC1-->SOC2, SEC1-->SOC2); §5 rank 20 second wave.

SCOPING CORRECTION that the plan row hides: the I-28 BoundaryPolicy seams already LANDED (W4.1/G-54 core) — vocabulary, three seams, ProjectionRegistry, SignedDelta, BoundaryPolicyTest/MediateProxyIntegrityTest. SEC1 (computenet-usd) fixes what is broken about them (every denial is a silent 'return null' that discharges no Owned/Leased and moves no counter, and the wire bridge does not consult a policy at all). SOC2 is therefore the first real CONSUMER of moderation policy: its requirements are about POLICY CONTENT and the MODERATION MODEL, and it cross-references SEC1's requirements ([SEC1-20], [SEC1-23], [SEC1-25..29]) rather than rebuilding the seam mechanism. Do not re-open I-28 candidates A (capabilities) or B (SecurityGateway) — both rejected. Do not re-add BoundaryPolicy.admission (deleted, remediation T03).

HIGHEST STRUCTURAL RISK, settle in F1 before writing moderation code: civictech.cell.membrane is NOT in DemoSurfaceAllowlistTest.demoCellPrefixes (allowed: host, port, graph, data, observe, link, wire, consistency, control, durability, replication). A demo cannot import BoundaryPolicy/CompositeCell/Exposure today. Options: escalate the widening with human approval + a doc/architecture-decisions.md note; build a facade in an allowed package; or ship reduced scope and file the finding. Never edit the guardrail to make the build pass.

SECOND DESIGN CONSTRAINT: ManagedHost.readState does not answer for Remote refs, so the federated feed reads LOCAL REPLICAS filled by interest-scoped gossip — this is 42's model (interest drives replication), not a workaround. Do not add a synchronous cross-wire read. Freshness becomes a first-class UI concern ([SOC2-21]).

40/43 carries NO normative EARS ids (only [41-LOC-01], [42-INT-01], [42-REPL-04..06] exist in doc/spec/40-distribution/). Moderation scenarios therefore have no legal covers: target; bind honestly or file in concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md, never onto a loosely-related id.

Module decision: EXTEND demo/social/ (:demo:social) from SOC1, adding :wire and DSC1's :identity — do not fork the SNB schema, generator, loader interface or feed assembly (BB-SNB depends on SOC1 being the single schema/workload host).

Explicitly unverifiable and named up front so no weak test appears to satisfy them: moderation efficacy against a determined adversary; Sybil resistance (minting is free until ECO1); end-to-end authorship (signing is per emitting peer, so relayed attribution is unverifiable without per-person keys); multi-hop disclosure composition (I-28 §8 open); revocation of already-disclosed content (G-54 residual).

Excluded by the plan's dependency edges: the boundary mechanism (SEC1), crypto identity (DSC1), the single-node graph (SOC1), open mesh/discovery/election/budgets (SOC3, MEM1, DSC2, ECO1), NAT traversal (DSC3), placement (PLC3), leader/follower election (MEM1/MEM2), and the G-54 residual.
UNWIRED DEPENDENCY EDGE (bd constraint, not a scoping choice): SOC2 depends on SEC1 (computenet-usd) per the milestone plan (§1 'SEC1 | ... | SOC2 moderation'; §2 DAG SEC1-->SOC2). bd refuses that edge because SEC1 is type=feature and an epic cannot be blocked by a non-epic ('epics can only block other epics, not tasks'). The dependency is therefore recorded NORMATIVELY here and in description §6: SOC2 MUST NOT start its moderation features (F4, F5) until SEC1 has landed its denial accounting and ownership discharge. Starting F4 against today's silent 'return null' denials would make BS-10 and every [SOC2-33..36] requirement pass vacuously. title: BEN2 — Macro workloads: graph shape × cardinality × host count sweeps; re-baseline cost under fan-out (G-43)
description:
# BEN2 — Macro workloads: graph shape × cardinality × host count sweeps; re-baseline cost under fan-out (G-43)

Lane: evidence (`lane:evidence`). Priority P3. Source: `computenet-milestone-plan.md`
§1 (evidence-lane row BEN2: *"Macro workloads: graph shape × cardinality × host count
sweeps; re-baseline cost under fan-out (G-43) | BEN1 | PLC1; journal-segmentation
trigger"*), §2 (DAG edge `BEN1 --> BEN2` and the dotted `BEN2 -.cost inputs.-> PLC1`),
§5 rank 13 (*"PLC1 → PLC2 — gated on BEN2's measured costs"*) and §5's deliberate
ordering note (*"**PLC1 gated on BEN2**: no simulating against fictional costs"*).

Depends on: **BEN1** (`computenet-x9e`) — the `:bench` module, the JMH wiring, the
`@Tag("bench")` gating convention, the result model, the dispersion gate, and
`doc/bench/findings.md`. BEN2 extends all six; it re-creates none of them.

Unblocks: **PLC1** (mesh simulator + cost model) and **PLC2** through it; the
**journal-segmentation trigger** under G-25 (*"journal segmentation — trigger: first
workload where one file hurts"*, `doc/spec/90-roadmap/91-gap-analysis.md` G-25 row).

---

## 1. Ambition / Why

**PLC1 is only as honest as this epic's numbers.** The milestone plan makes that a
standing rule rather than a preference: *"no simulating against fictional costs."* A
mesh simulator that guesses what a cross-host edge costs, what a re-baseline costs at
fan-out 256, or how state size scales with host count will produce a placement policy
that is internally consistent and externally false — and PLC2 will then encode that
falsehood as an economics engine, and PLC3 (`G-61` spawn-redirection enforcement) will
enforce it. BEN2 exists so that the first number PLC1 reads is a measured one.

That framing dictates the epic's centre of gravity. The sweeps are not the deliverable.
**The deliverable is a cost model export with a stated coverage envelope**, and the
sweeps are how it gets populated. Filing this epic with the export treated as a
by-product would reproduce exactly the failure mode the ordering note is guarding
against: a lane that produces a pile of tables nobody can consume, followed by a PLC1
that invents its own constants because the tables did not answer its question.

**Three concrete debts this epic pays.**

- **G-43's cost half.** `doc/spec/90-roadmap/91-gap-analysis.md` G-43 asks to *"bound
  the push-authoritative re-baseline (diff-against-last-acked / delta-since-generation)"*
  and names *"re-baseline cost under wide fan-out"* as an open item. The same gap
  marker is repeated verbatim in `doc/spec/30-execution-model/31-hosts.md:210`,
  `doc/spec/20-dataflow-semantics/24-data-cells.md:741`, and
  `doc/spec/40-distribution/42-replication.md:353`. "Bound" is a cost claim, and no cost
  has ever been measured. BEN1 measures the *fan-out scaling curve of ordinary delta
  propagation*; BEN2 measures the *re-baseline event itself* — the whole-state
  re-assertion that `ManagedHost.kt:845-864` triggers on a supervision RESTART — against
  that curve. Only the second number can say whether the current
  push-authoritative-always design needs the diff-against-last-acked bound G-43
  proposes, or whether it is cheap enough to leave alone. BEN2 measures and reports;
  **it does not implement the bound** (that is a kernel-lane change, out of scope, §4).
- **G-25's journal-segmentation trigger.** The gap row states the trigger literally as
  *"first workload where one file hurts"*. `FileJournal`
  (`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/durability/Journal.kt`) opens a fresh
  `FileOutputStream` and calls `fd.sync()` **per appended record**, and `replay()` reads
  the entire log into a `List<ByteArray>` in memory. Its own KDoc names the deferral:
  *"one file, fsync per append, whole-log replay in memory — segments, group commit, and
  streaming replay when a real workload's journal hurts."* A macro workload is the first
  thing in this repository capable of firing or retiring that trigger. BEN2 is the lane
  that gets to say so, with a number.
- **The multi-host measurement vacuum.** There is no N-host harness anywhere in the
  tree. `testkit`'s `SimWorld` (`testkit/src/main/kotlin/civictech/testkit/SimWorld.kt`)
  is single-host by construction (one `controller`, one `registry`, one `host`). The
  only N-peer composition in the repository is a `private class Peer` inside
  `kernel/src/test/kotlin/civictech/cell/durability/CrashRecoveryTest.kt:38-43`, hand-meshed
  three ways with `Peering.loopback`. `demo/shopping`'s peer addressing is derived from
  `listener`/`dialer` roles and does not generalize past two. "Host count" as a sweep
  dimension therefore requires building the substrate first.

**Why this is the epic that gates PLC1 rather than the one after it.** PLC1 needs
*placement* costs — what does it cost to put this cell on that host, and what does it
cost to route this edge across a host boundary. BEN1's per-operator throughput numbers
are single-host and answer none of that. The host-count dimension is the whole point.

---

## 2. What we build

### 2.1 Relationship to BEN1's `:bench` module — reuse vs. add

BEN2 adds **no new Gradle module**. Everything lands in `bench/`, created by BEN1.

**Reused unchanged (BEN2 must not fork, re-implement, or weaken any of these):**

| BEN1 asset | Where | How BEN2 uses it |
|---|---|---|
| The `:bench` module + build script | `bench/build.gradle.kts`, `settings.gradle.kts` | BEN2 adds `implementation(project(":wire"))` — see §2.2 — and nothing else |
| JMH plugin + pinned versions | `gradle/libs.versions.toml` | unchanged |
| `@Tag("bench")` gating convention | `buildSrc/src/main/kotlin/kotlin-jvm.gradle.kts` | BEN2's long sweeps are `@Tag("bench")`-tagged; multi-JVM sweeps additionally carry the existing `@Tag("multi-jvm")` |
| Result model (`RunEnvironment`, `BenchResult`, `Drive`) | `bench/src/main/kotlin/civictech/bench/Result.kt`, `Env.kt` | every BEN2 point is a `BenchResult`; the environment capture is not re-derived |
| Dispersion gate + `unreportable` rule | `bench/src/main/kotlin/civictech/bench/Dispersion.kt` (`[BEN1-24]`/`[BEN1-25]`) | applied per sweep point; a point that fails it is excluded from the export, not softened |
| SIM/REAL drive discipline, no-mixed-tables rule | `[BEN1-26]`/`[BEN1-27]` | extended, not relaxed — see the counts-vs-times split in §3.5 |
| Findings file + trigger vocabulary | `doc/bench/findings.md`, `[BEN1-30]`–`[BEN1-34]` | BEN2 appends; it does not start a second findings file |
| Package layout | `civictech.bench.micro`, `civictech.bench.suite.*` (BEN1 §9) | BEN2 occupies `civictech.bench.macro` and `civictech.bench.cost` |

**Added by BEN2:**

1. **`civictech.bench.macro.shape`** — a graph-shape generator emitting
   `civictech.cell.graph.GraphSpec` (`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/graph/GraphDsl.kt`).
   `GraphSpec` is `Serializable` and replayable onto another host via `applyTo` /
   `applyRemote`, which is exactly what a host-count sweep needs. Named shapes:
   *chain*, *fan-out tree*, *fan-in lattice*, *diamond* (the glitch-free-critical shape),
   *seeded random DAG*. Factory lambdas must capture nothing live — follow the static
   predicate-index pattern in
   `kernel/src/test/kotlin/civictech/cell/verify/GenerativeGraphTest.kt`.
2. **`civictech.bench.macro.mesh`** — an N-host harness. In-process and deterministic:
   one `LocationRegistry` + `ManagedHost` + bridge `ManagedHost` +
   `Peering.Side` + `Replication` per peer, each host taking its own
   `SimulationController.scheduler()`, meshed pairwise with
   `Peering.loopback(a, b)`. This generalizes `CrashRecoveryTest.kt:38-43` from a
   hand-meshed 3 to an N-parameterized topology, and supplies its own ref-minting
   scheme (the shopping demo's `listener`/`dialer` derivation does not generalize).
   **Where it should live is an open question (§9)**: promoting it into `:testkit`
   makes it reusable by kernel tests and the BB-* suites; keeping it in `:bench`
   keeps `:testkit`'s surface small. BEN2 must decide explicitly and record the
   decision, not drift into one.
3. **`civictech.bench.macro.rebaseline`** — the G-43 study: drive a supervision RESTART
   on a stateful source at controlled state cardinality and controlled outlet fan-out
   degree, and measure the re-assertion.
4. **`civictech.bench.macro.journal`** — journal-growth instrumentation for the G-25
   trigger: bytes appended per delta, file size over a run, `replay()` wall-time and
   peak retained size at recovery, `checkpoint()` cost.
5. **`civictech.bench.cost`** — **the cost model export**, its schema, its writer, its
   parser, and its coverage-envelope logic (§2.3). This is the epic's primary artifact.
6. **A cross-check over the real transport.** A small number of sweep points repeated
   over `:wire` (`wire/src/main/kotlin/civictech/wire/WsTransport.kt` — `listen`/`connect`)
   with `JvmPeer` (`testkit/src/main/kotlin/civictech/testkit/JvmPeer.kt`) forking real
   JVMs, so that the loopback mesh's message and byte counts can be validated against a
   socket rather than assumed equal to it.

### 2.2 Build-graph consequences

`:bench` gains `implementation(project(":wire"))` for item 6 above. That widens
`[BEN1-03]` ("project dependencies only on `:kernel` and `:testkit`") from two modules
to three; the widening is deliberate and must be recorded as an amendment in
`doc/bench/findings.md`, not made silently. `[BEN1-04]`'s converse — nothing may depend
on `:bench` — is untouched and still enforced.

Note also `kernel/src/test/kotlin/civictech/cell/architecture/ModuleInventoryTest.kt`:
every module in `settings.gradle.kts` must appear in `doc/ARCHITECTURE.md` §1. BEN1
already pays this; BEN2 must keep the row accurate if it changes `:bench`'s stated
dependencies.

### 2.3 The cost model export — the deliverable PLC1 consumes

This section is the epic's reason for existing and is specified as a first-class
artifact with its own requirements (`[BEN2-30]`–`[BEN2-46]`).

**The central design decision: separate structural counts from calibration times.**

A cost model built from wall-clock times alone is worthless to a simulator, because
every number is a property of the laptop that produced it. A cost model built from
counts alone cannot answer "is this placement faster". So the export carries two
layers:

- **Structural costs** — machine-independent, deterministic, re-derivable: messages
  sent, cross-host frames, bytes serialized through `WireCodec`, journal records
  appended, wave-completion steps. These come from **SIM drive**
  (`SimulationController`), are exactly reproducible for a given seed, and are the layer
  PLC1 should extrapolate over.
- **Calibration constants** — machine-dependent: nanoseconds per local delta dispatch,
  nanoseconds per cross-host frame encode/decode, nanoseconds per journal fsync, bytes
  retained per element. These come from **REAL drive**
  (`VirtualThreadScheduler`/`CoroutineScheduler`), carry full `RunEnvironment`
  provenance and a dispersion figure, and are the layer PLC1 multiplies by.

PLC1 then computes a predicted cost as `structural counts × calibration constants`, and
can state which half a given prediction is sensitive to. This is the only shape in
which the export can be honest about a machine it was not measured on.

**Envelope, not extrapolation.** Every sweep dimension the export covers is recorded
with its measured minimum and maximum. A consumer query outside the envelope is
**refused**, not extrapolated — the export refuses to answer rather than inventing a
number, which is the machine-readable form of "no simulating against fictional costs".

**Format.** A versioned, machine-readable document (kotlinx.serialization JSON, matching
repo style — see `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/wire/WireSerializers.kt`), written
to a stable path under `doc/bench/`, accompanied by a human-readable summary in
`doc/bench/findings.md`. Schema version is explicit so PLC1 can reject a version it does
not understand.

### 2.4 The sweep space

Four dimensions, crossed but **not exhaustively** (§9 risk: combinatorial explosion):

| Dimension | Values (indicative; final set is F-level work) |
|---|---|
| Graph shape | chain, fan-out tree, fan-in lattice, diamond, seeded random DAG |
| Cardinality | 10³ / 10⁴ / 10⁵ / 10⁶ elements; delta batch size 1 / 10 / 100 |
| Host count | 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 (in-process mesh); 2 and 3 additionally over `:wire` |
| Fan-out degree | 1, 4, 16, 64, 256 (continuing BEN1's `[BEN1-19]` degrees) |

Plus two orthogonal switches: **replication on/off** (`civictech.cell.replication.Replication`)
and **durability on/off** (`FileJournal` vs none). The requirement is that the sweep
*plan* is declared, recorded, and its omissions named — not that every cell of the cross
product is measured.

---

## 3. How, using ComputeNet

Every number is produced by driving real kernel entry points. No reimplemented
arithmetic, no mocked transport, no estimated constants.

### 3.1 Graph shapes → `GraphSpec`

`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/graph/GraphDsl.kt` supplies
`GraphSpec(steps)`, `SpawnStep`, `ConnectStep`, `InstanceSetStep`, `InstanceSpec`,
`CellFactory`, `graph(host) { ... }`, `GraphSpec.applyTo(host)` and
`GraphSpec.applyRemote(host): ApplyReport`. A shape generator produces a `GraphSpec`;
the mesh harness applies it across N hosts. Because `GraphSpec` is `Serializable`, the
same shape can be replayed identically on every host in the sweep — the property
`GenerativeGraphTest` already relies on.

Cell vocabulary drawn from `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/`
(`SetCell`, `MapCell`, `OrMapCell`, `KeyedSetCell`, `ListCell`, `CounterCell`,
`PnCounterCell`, `Aggregator`) and `data/op/` (`FilterCell`, `UnionSetCell`,
`IntersectSetCell`, `JoinSetCell`, `LookupJoinCell`, `SemiJoinCell`, `GroupByCell`,
`MergeableGroupByCell`, `CountCell`, `FlatMapSetCell`, `CombineLatestCell`,
`CoalescingCombineCell`, `PresenceCountCell`, `QuorumSetCell`, `TaggedSetOperator`).
`InstanceSpec.placement: String?` (`GraphDsl.kt:106`) is the only placement-typed field
in the kernel and is the natural hook a later PLC engine would drive — BEN2 records that
it exists and leaves it alone.

### 3.2 Host count → the N-peer mesh

Per peer, following `CrashRecoveryTest.kt:38-43`:

```
LocationRegistry()
ManagedHost(scheduler = controller.scheduler(), registry = ..., journal = ...)
ManagedHost(scheduler = controller.scheduler(), registry = ...)   // bridge host
Peering.Side(registry, bridgeHost, peer = PeerId(...))
Replication(registry)                                             // when replication is on
```

meshed with `Peering.loopback(sideA, sideB)`
(`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/wire/Peering.kt:154`), whose returned `Loopback`
also exposes `partition()` / `heal()` — available for a partitioned variant, though
partition behaviour itself is CHA1's lane, not BEN2's.

Cross-host frames go through `civictech.cell.wire.BridgeEgressCell` /
`BridgeIngressCell` and are encoded by
`civictech.cell.wire.WireCodec.encode/decode` (`WireFrame`), which is where **bytes on
the wire** are counted — the same encoding the journal uses, so one instrument serves
both. Routing is `LocationRegistry.deliver(invocation)`
(`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/LocationRegistry.kt:291`).

Real-socket cross-check: `WsTransport.listen(port, side)` / `WsTransport.connect(uri, side)`
in forked JVMs via `JvmPeer.launch` / `JvmPeer.freePort` / `JvmPeer.destroy`, tagged
`@Tag("multi-jvm")` so it lands in the existing `build-test-serial` lane's exclusion
scheme rather than in `build-test-fast`.

### 3.3 Re-baseline cost under fan-out — the G-43 measurement

The re-baseline path, precisely as it exists:

- `civictech.cell.host.ManagedHost.kt:845-864` — the supervision RESTART branch: bump
  the host-held generation (`generationOf(ref)`, `ManagedHost.kt:359`), deactivate, walk
  `PortRegistry.of(cell)` calling `FanOutlet.mintFreshEpoch()`
  (`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/port/FanOutlet.kt:233`) on every outlet to
  collect the superseded source ids, reactivate, restore the checkpoint, then — if the
  cell declares `civictech.cell.ReBaselineEmitting` — call
  `reBaseline(supersedes, supersede = true)`.
- `FanOutlet.reBaseline(supersedes, supersede, block)` (`FanOutlet.kt:245`) and
  `baselineTo(replyTo, frontier, block)` (`FanOutlet.kt:262`) emit it.
- `MessageContext.reBaseline: ReBaselineNotice(supersedes, supersede)`
  (`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/MessageContext.kt:53,85`) carries it, staged
  through `PendingReBaseline` (`MessageContext.kt:97`).
- Downstream, `civictech.cell.data.delta.TagState.applyReBaseline(delta, notice)`
  (`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/delta/TagState.kt:155`) drops the
  un-reasserted tags of superseded sources, union-merges, and fences the dead lanes.
- Fan-out width is the number of taps on the outlet: `FanOutlet.tap(port)` /
  `untap(portRef)` (`FanOutlet.kt:327,409`).
- The second re-baseline driver, for completeness:
  `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/evolve/Evolution.kt:196-208` (shadow promotion).

The measurement: for state cardinality × fan-out degree × host count, record the
re-baseline's **emitted message count, serialized bytes, downstream
`applyReBaseline` work, and wall time**, and state the observed growth law in each
dimension. The G-43 question the findings entry must answer in words: *is the
push-authoritative-always re-baseline bounded well enough at realistic fan-out that the
"diff-against-last-acked / delta-since-generation" bound G-43 proposes is not urgent, or
does it degrade badly enough to fire that work?* An entry that reports the numbers
without answering that question is incomplete, per `[BEN1-32]`.

Existing shape donors: `kernel/src/test/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/RestartReBaselineTest.kt`
(has a `private class Fixture` and drives the RESTART path),
`kernel/src/test/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/SupervisionTest.kt`, and concord scenario
`21-REBASE-01`.

### 3.4 Journal growth — the G-25 trigger

`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/durability/Journal.kt` — `interface Journal
{ append; replay; reset }`, `InMemoryJournal`, `FileJournal(file)`. Checkpointing is
`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/HostDurability.kt` —
`checkpoint(journal)` (:209) snapshots `Stateful` cells and the processed frontier then
`journal.reset(...)`; `recoverFrom(journal)` (:120) is checkpoint-restore plus tail
replay; `journalFrame(hostedInvocation)` (:189) is the `WireCodec` encoding of a record.
Host-level entry points: `ManagedHost.recoverFrom` (:672), `ManagedHost.checkpoint` (:678).
Journal minting for a realistic workload: `KeyedCells.hostJournal(dir)`
(`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/KeyedCells.kt`).

Measure: bytes per journaled record, total file size across a sustained macro run,
`replay()` wall time and peak retained bytes at recovery, and `checkpoint()` cost and
the size reduction it achieves. Then answer G-25's trigger in words — **does one file
hurt yet, at what workload, and by how much**.

### 3.5 SIM vs REAL, and the counts/times split

BEN1 already forbids mixing drives in one table (`[BEN1-26]`/`[BEN1-27]`). BEN2 leans
on that harder, because the two drives play different roles in the export:

- `civictech.cell.host.SimulationController` (`scheduler()`, `step()`, `runToIdle(budget)`)
  with one `scheduler()` per host gives a deterministic, seeded, machine-independent
  world. **This is where structural counts come from.** Wall-clock time measured under
  SIM is meaningless as a cost and must not enter the export as a calibration constant.
- `VirtualThreadScheduler` / `CoroutineScheduler`
  (`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/`) give real threads and real time.
  **This is where calibration constants come from.** Structural counts measured under
  REAL are valid but not reproducible seed-for-seed, so SIM is preferred for them.

Note both real schedulers currently `printStackTrace()` on uncaught loop exceptions
(`VirtualThreadScheduler.kt:33`, `CoroutineScheduler.kt:47` — the G-26 residual). A
sweep that silently swallows a scheduler failure into stderr would report a throughput
number for a broken run; the harness must fail the point instead (`[BEN2-27]`).

---

## 4. Scope boundaries

Boundaries follow the plan's dependency edges: BEN2 sits between `BEN1 --> BEN2` and
`BEN2 -.cost inputs.-> PLC1`, and touches the kernel lane only as a *reporter*.

**In scope**: the shape generator, the N-host mesh harness, the macro sweep suites, the
re-baseline study, the journal-growth study, the real-socket cross-check, the cost model
export with its schema/writer/parser/envelope, the consumer-shaped round-trip test, and
the BEN2 entries in `doc/bench/findings.md`.

**Explicitly NOT in scope:**

- **NOT PLC1.** No mesh simulator, no placement policy, no economics, no consumer of the
  export beyond the round-trip test of `[BEN2-45]`. BEN2 produces the input; PLC1 is the
  model. (Plan §1 distribution row: PLC1 depends on *"BEN1/BEN2 cost inputs"*.)
- **NOT the G-43 fix.** BEN2 measures re-baseline cost. It does **not** implement
  diff-against-last-acked, delta-since-generation, the per-cell push/pull direction
  policy, the supersede-vs-remove precedence rule, the poison-write escape, or the
  `deadLetter→requestState` recovery cell. Those are the G-43 *proposals* and belong to
  the kernel lane. BEN2 does not remove or weaken any G-43 marker in `doc/spec/`.
- **NOT the G-25 fix.** No journal segmentation, rotation, group commit, size cap, or
  streaming replay. BEN2 fires or retires the trigger with a number.
- **NOT KBLK.** No WAL-off/async host config, no batched ingress path, no
  deterministic-time drive hooks. If journal sync dominates a macro number, BEN2 reports
  it and names KBLK — inheriting `[BEN1-28]`/`[BEN1-29]` verbatim.
- **NOT any BB-\* suite.** No Nexmark, YCSB, TPC-H, LDBC SNB, Graphalytics, or TPC-C
  work. Those are separate chunks with their own kernel dependencies. BEN2's shapes are
  synthetic and parameterized, not standardized workloads.
- **NOT any kernel optimisation.** No change under `kernel/src/main` to make a sweep
  faster. A slow path found is a finding. (Inherits `[BEN1-35]`.)
- **NOT membership/partition semantics.** Partition, churn, and reconvergence belong to
  CHA1/CHA3 and MEM1/MEM2. `Loopback.partition()/heal()` may be *used* to set up a
  measurement; their correctness is not this epic's subject.
- **NOT a performance regression gate.** No CI threshold that fails on a number.
  (Inherits `[BEN1-38]`.)
- **NOT concord.** No `concord/corpus/` scenarios, no `CONCORDANCE.md` regeneration.
  See §7.
- **NOT gap-table edits.** `91-gap-analysis.md` and `CONCORDANCE.md` stay untouched;
  findings go to `doc/bench/findings.md` per milestone-plan §6.

requirement, it says so rather than restating it. **No requirement below asserts a
performance number**; every one is an obligation on the harness.

### Honesty note on verifiability

Four requirements above cannot be reduced to a pure pass/fail assertion and are called
out rather than softened:

- **`[BEN2-19]`** (omissions listed with reasons) and **`[BEN2-18]`** (sweep plan
  recorded) are document-completeness obligations. They are checkable by review, not by a
  test. Stating them as requirements is still worth it — an unlisted omission is the
  mechanism by which a sweep quietly becomes a cherry-pick.
- **`[BEN2-21]`**'s "stated tolerance" and **`[BEN2-43]`**'s "goodness-of-fit figure" both
  require a threshold chosen by judgement. Like BEN1's dispersion threshold, each must be
  derived from observation and stated; a tolerance widened until the cross-check passes is
  a violation in spirit and must be reported as such.
- **`[BEN2-26]`** (SIM determinism) is verifiable, but only by running each SIM point
  twice — which doubles sweep cost. The decision of whether to run the duplicate on every
  point or on a declared sample belongs to the implementing feature, and whichever is
  chosen must be stated in the findings entry.
- **`[BEN2-40]`**'s refusal is fully verifiable (`[BEN2-45]`'s consumer test asserts it);
  what is *not* mechanically verifiable is whether PLC1 later honours the refusal instead
  of working around it. That is PLC1's obligation to inherit, and this epic can only make
  the refusal loud.

## 6. Behaviour specifications (Given/When/Then)

Each should become a named test or, where marked *(observational)*, a reproducible
procedure recorded in `doc/bench/findings.md`. The unit tests among these run in
`:bench:test` and are fast — no sweep required.

**BS-1 — Shape generator emits replay-safe specs.**
Given a shape name and a seed;
When the generator produces a `GraphSpec`;
Then applying it to two independently constructed hosts yields structurally identical
graphs, and serializing then deserializing the spec produces an equal spec.
Covers `[BEN2-09]`, `[BEN2-10]`, `[BEN2-11]`.

**BS-2 — Mesh harness scales past two hosts.**
Given host count N ∈ {1, 2, 3, 5, 8};
When the mesh harness constructs N peers and meshes them pairwise via `Peering.loopback`;
Then every peer's `LocationRegistry` resolves every other peer's published refs, and a
delta injected at peer 0 is observable at peer N−1.
Covers `[BEN2-13]`, `[BEN2-14]`, `[BEN2-15]`.

**BS-3 — Boundary: host count 1 is a legal degenerate point.**
Given host count 1;
When the mesh harness is constructed;
Then it produces a working single-host world with zero cross-host frames, and the
resulting cost entry records cross-host edge cost as *not measured at this coordinate*
rather than zero.
Covers `[BEN2-13]`, `[BEN2-35]`, `[BEN2-39]`.

**BS-4 — Boundary: a host-count configuration that cannot be scheduled.**
Given a requested host count that the harness cannot construct — because the per-host
scheduler, thread, port or memory budget is exhausted, or because the machine cannot
fork that many JVMs for the `:wire` variant;
When the sweep reaches that coordinate;
Then the harness records the coordinate as **unschedulable** with the reason and the
observed limit, excludes it from the export, does not silently fall back to a smaller
host count, and continues the remaining sweep.
Covers `[BEN2-29]`, `[BEN2-41]`, `[BEN2-19]`.

**BS-5 — A sweep that fails to converge.**
Given a sweep point whose graph does not reach quiescence within its declared step budget
(`SimulationController.runToIdle(budget)` exhausting, or `awaitUntil` timing out under
REAL drive);
When the point completes;
Then it is recorded as **non-convergent** with its full coordinate tuple and the budget
it exhausted, is excluded from the export, appears in the findings entry, and the sweep
does not abort.
Covers `[BEN2-29]`, `[BEN2-41]`. This is the case where a macro benchmark is most likely
to be quietly wrong: a non-converged run still produces a throughput number.

**BS-6 — Failing seed is retained.**
Given a shape seed under which a sweep point fails an invariant or fails to converge;
When the suite is next modified;
Then that seed is still present in the suite's seed set and its failure is recorded.
Covers `[BEN2-12]`.

**BS-7 — SIM determinism check.**
Given a SIM-drive sweep point and a fixed seed;
When it is executed twice;
Then the structural counts are identical, and if they are not, the point is marked
non-deterministic and excluded from the export.
Covers `[BEN2-23]`, `[BEN2-26]`.

**BS-8 — Unwanted: SIM wall-clock cannot become a calibration constant.**
Given a `BenchResult` with `Drive = SIM` carrying a wall-clock value;
When the export writer is asked to admit it as a calibration constant;
Then it refuses.
Covers `[BEN2-25]`, `[BEN2-33]`. Fast unit test against the result model — no sweep.

**BS-9 — Unwanted: unreportable point cannot enter the export.**
Given points marked unreportable (dispersion), non-convergent, non-deterministic, and
failed;
When the export writer runs;
Then none of them appears in the export, and each appears in the findings entry with its
exclusion reason.
Covers `[BEN2-41]`, `[BEN2-29]`.

**BS-10 — Unwanted: dead letter fails the point.**
Given a sweep point during which a host emits on `deadLetterOutlet`;
When the point completes;
Then it is marked failed, the dead letter is recorded, and no cost entry is derived from
it.
Covers `[BEN2-28]`.

**BS-11 — Unwanted: scheduler exception fails the point.**
Given a REAL-drive point during which a scheduler loop throws;
When the point completes;
Then the point is marked failed rather than reported, notwithstanding that the kernel's
scheduler only prints the stack trace.
Covers `[BEN2-27]`. *(Requires the harness to install its own capture — the kernel is not
modified; see `[BEN2-51]`.)*

**BS-12 — Re-baseline cost under fan-out.**
Given a `ReBaselineEmitting` stateful source at cardinality C with fan-out degree D taps
on its `FanOutlet`, on a mesh of H hosts;
When a supervision RESTART drives `ManagedHost`'s RESTART branch — fresh epochs via
`mintFreshEpoch()`, checkpoint restore, then `reBaseline(supersedes, supersede = true)`;
Then the emitted message count, serialized bytes, downstream `TagState.applyReBaseline`
work and wall time are recorded per (C, D, H), and the findings entry states the observed
growth in each dimension.
Covers `[BEN2-36]`, `[BEN2-47]`. This is the G-43 measurement.

**BS-13 — Re-baseline across a host boundary.**
Given the same setup with the fan-out targets on *remote* hosts;
When the re-baseline is emitted;
Then cross-host frame count and `WireCodec` byte volume are recorded separately from the
local case, so the export can price a cross-host re-baseline edge distinctly.
Covers `[BEN2-35]`, `[BEN2-36]`.

**BS-14 — Journal growth and replay.**
Given a durable macro run against a `FileJournal`;
When the run completes and the host is recovered via `ManagedHost.recoverFrom`;
Then journal file size, bytes per record, `replay()` wall time and peak retained bytes
are recorded, `checkpoint()` cost and its size reduction are recorded, and the findings
entry answers G-25's "does one file hurt yet" with fires/retires/inconclusive.
Covers `[BEN2-37]`, `[BEN2-48]`.

**BS-15 — Unwanted: journal sync dominates.**
Given a macro throughput point on a durable host;
When journal sync accounts for the majority of wall time;
Then the finding reports the domination, names KBLK, and no WAL-off path is added.
Covers `[BEN2-49]`. *(Observational.)*

**BS-16 — Real-transport cross-check.**
Given a host-count point measured both on the in-process `Peering.loopback` mesh and over
`WsTransport` in JVMs forked by `JvmPeer`;
When both complete;
Then their message and byte counts are compared against a stated tolerance, and on
disagreement the loopback structural costs are marked transport-unvalidated in the export.
Covers `[BEN2-20]`, `[BEN2-21]`.

**BS-17 — Export round-trip.**
Given a populated export;
When it is written and re-parsed by `civictech.bench.cost`;
Then the parsed model equals the written one, including schema version, envelope, and
per-entry provenance.
Covers `[BEN2-30]`, `[BEN2-31]`, `[BEN2-34]`, `[BEN2-38]`, `[BEN2-42]`.

**BS-18 — Unwanted: unknown schema version is rejected.**
Given an export whose schema version is one the parser does not recognize;
When it is parsed;
Then the parser rejects it with an error naming the version, rather than reading the
entries it happens to understand.
Covers `[BEN2-32]`.

**BS-19 — A PLC1-shaped consumer.**
Given the export and a test consumer that mimics a mesh simulator;
When it asks for (a) the cost of an edge whose endpoints are co-located, (b) the cost of
an edge crossing a host boundary, (c) the residency cost of a cell of a given
cardinality, (d) the cost of a re-baseline at a given fan-out and host count, and (e) any
of the above at a coordinate outside the coverage envelope;
Then (a)–(d) return values with their provenance and dispersion attached, and (e) is
**refused** — the consumer receives an explicit out-of-envelope refusal and no number.
Covers `[BEN2-35]`, `[BEN2-36]`, `[BEN2-39]`, `[BEN2-40]`, `[BEN2-45]`. This is the
epic's contract with PLC1, expressed as a test.

**BS-20 — Growth law honesty.**
Given measured points over a dimension that do not fit the proposed law well;
When the export is generated;
Then it records the raw points and no law, rather than a law with an unstated poor fit;
and where a law *is* recorded, its fitted form, fitting points and goodness-of-fit figure
are all present.
Covers `[BEN2-43]`, `[BEN2-44]`.

**BS-21 — Sweep plan and omissions are recorded.**
Given a completed sweep;
When the findings entry is written;
Then it lists every dimension and value actually measured and every declared combination
not measured, each with a reason.
Covers `[BEN2-18]`, `[BEN2-19]`. *(Observational; review-checkable.)*

**BS-22 — Boundary: `:bench` stays a leaf.**
Given the resolved Gradle project graph after `:wire` is added;
When a test enumerates project dependencies;
Then `:bench` depends only on `:kernel`, `:testkit` and `:wire`, and no project depends
on `:bench`.
Covers `[BEN2-07]`, `[BEN2-08]`.

**BS-23 — Boundary: no kernel or spec edit.**
Given the epic's completed diff;
When it is inspected;
Then it contains no change under `kernel/src/main`, `concord/`, `inspect/src`, `demo/`,
`doc/spec/CONCORDANCE.md` or `doc/spec/90-roadmap/91-gap-analysis.md`, and every G-43 /
G-25 / G-42 marker in `doc/spec/` is byte-identical.
Covers `[BEN2-51]`, `[BEN2-53]`, `[BEN2-54]`.

### Concord

**No scenario in this epic belongs in `concord/corpus/`** — the same reasoning BEN1
recorded, and for the same reason. The corpus is the implementation-neutral arbiter of
*semantic* spec↔code agreement; a throughput figure, a byte count on a particular
machine, or a calibration constant is machine-dependent and not implementation-neutral,
and encoding one as a conformance scenario would make the corpus fail on a slow machine
— precisely the dishonesty `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` exists to prevent. This epic
therefore carries **no `covers:` ids**, adds no corpus files, and does not regenerate
`doc/spec/CONCORDANCE.md`. The *structural* counts are closer to implementation-neutral
than the times are, and a later agent may be tempted on that basis; the counts still
depend on scheduling and encoding choices that the corpus deliberately does not pin, so
the answer is still no. If someone believes otherwise, that belief is filed as a
question, not as a scenario.

6. **F6 — Re-baseline cost study (G-43).** `civictech.bench.macro.rebaseline`, local and
   cross-host. `[BEN2-36]`, `[BEN2-47]`, BS-12, BS-13.
7. **F7 — Journal-growth study (G-25).** `civictech.bench.macro.journal`.
   `[BEN2-37]`, `[BEN2-48]`, `[BEN2-49]`, BS-14, BS-15.
8. **F8 — Real-transport cross-check over `:wire`.** `[BEN2-06]`, `[BEN2-07]`,
   `[BEN2-20]`, `[BEN2-21]`, BS-16, BS-22.

Ordering: F1 and F2 are independent and parallel. F3 needs both. **F4 must land before
F5–F7** for the same reason BEN1 put its result model before its measurements: writing
the export's refusal rules after the numbers exist means the numbers get grandfathered
in, and the envelope becomes whatever was measured rather than a constraint on what may
be claimed. F5, F6, F7 are parallel once F4 lands. F8 is last — it validates the mesh's
counts, so it wants points to validate against.

---

## 8. Verification

```bash
./gradlew :bench:test                                    # fast unit tests: export round-trip,
                                                         # schema rejection, envelope refusal,
                                                         # consumer-shaped queries, drive rules
./gradlew :bench:test -PbenchOnly                        # the tagged macro sweeps (BEN1's gate)
./gradlew :bench:jmh                                     # JMH-shaped macro benchmarks; not a gate
./gradlew build check -PexcludeMultiJvm=true             # build-test-fast; must pass, no JMH fork,
                                                         # no @Tag("bench") execution
./gradlew build check -PmultiJvmOnly=true --max-workers=1 # build-test-serial; the :wire cross-check
                                                         # lands here if it is not bench-gated
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.architecture.ModuleInventoryTest'
./gradlew :concord:check && ./gradlew :concord:test      # must be unaffected
./gradlew test                                           # repository-wide gate; wall-clock must not
                                                         # materially increase
./gradlew build check --dry-run                          # task-graph proof that :bench:jmh is absent
git status --porcelain -uall -- doc '*/src'              # CI's untracked-files guard
```

Before declaring completion:

- `doc/bench/findings.md` contains BEN2 entries covering the sweep plan and omissions
  (`[BEN2-18]`/`[BEN2-19]`), the re-baseline study with its G-43 verdict (`[BEN2-47]`),
  the journal study with its G-25 verdict (`[BEN2-48]`), the `:wire` cross-check
  (`[BEN2-20]`/`[BEN2-21]`), and the `:wire` dependency amendment (`[BEN2-07]`).
- The cost model export exists at its stable path, parses through its own parser, and the
  consumer-shaped test of `[BEN2-45]` passes — including the out-of-envelope refusal.
- `git diff` shows no change under `kernel/src/main`, `concord/`, `inspect/src`, `demo/`,
  `doc/spec/CONCORDANCE.md` or `91-gap-analysis.md`, and no G-43/G-25/G-42 marker moved.

---

## 9. Risks / open questions

- **Combinatorial explosion.** Five shapes × four cardinalities × five host counts ×
  five fan-out degrees × replication × durability is 2000 points before batch sizes.
  A full cross product is not runnable and not wanted. Mitigation: `[BEN2-18]`/`[BEN2-19]`
  force the *plan* and its *omissions* to be explicit, which is the honest form of
  sampling. **Open**: the actual sampling strategy (one-factor-at-a-time around a
  declared baseline, versus a fractional design) — F5's decision, not this epic's.
- **Where the N-host mesh harness lives.** `:testkit` makes it reusable by kernel tests,
  CHA1/CHA3, and the BB-\* suites, at the cost of widening a module every test module
  depends on. `:bench` keeps it contained but guarantees the next lane copies it — which
  is how the repository ended up with `private class Peer` inside a durability test in
  the first place. **Open, and must be decided explicitly in F2**, not drifted into.
- **The 5-minute default JUnit method timeout.** `buildSrc/src/main/kotlin/kotlin-jvm.gradle.kts`
  sets `junit.jupiter.execution.timeout.testable.method.default = 5m` and
  `setForkEvery(80)` / `maxHeapSize = "2g"`. A 10⁶-element sweep on 8 hosts will exceed
  all three. Overriding them for the bench lane must not change them for any other module.
- **SIM structural counts may not equal socket structural counts.** The whole
  counts-based half of the export rests on the loopback mesh producing the same message
  and byte volumes as a real transport. `[BEN2-20]`/`[BEN2-21]` exist because that is an
  assumption, not a fact. **Open**: what tolerance is defensible, and whether a
  systematic offset (framing overhead, batching in `WsTransport`) should be modelled
  rather than tolerated.
- **The export will be quoted for years.** BEN1 already observed this happening —
  `BoundedRead.kt`'s KDoc cites V1C-BENCH numbers as load-bearing design justification.
  A cost model is worse: PLC1, PLC2, and eventually PLC3's enforcement hook all inherit
  it. `[BEN2-38]`/`[BEN2-39]`/`[BEN2-40]` are the mitigation, and the envelope refusal is
  the part that matters most.
- **Measuring a runtime that is still growing.** KE1, KE3, KE5, KBLK and KRD all change
  costs after they land. Any export is a snapshot. **Open**: whether the export should
  carry a "measured against kernel state X" marker beyond the harness SHA — a kernel
  commit SHA plus the set of landed E-milestones would let PLC1 detect staleness.
  Recommended; not required by any requirement above, and deliberately left as a question
  rather than half-specified.
- **Journal fsync may dominate everything.** `FileJournal` fsyncs per record. Every
  durable macro number may come back WAL-bound, making the *operator* dimension
  invisible. That is a legitimate result (it is exactly what fires G-25 and motivates
  KBLK), but it means the durability-on half of the sweep may produce one finding and
  little cost-model signal. Planned for, not prevented.
- **`Replication`'s gossip edges are invisible to the topology index.** Replication
  subscribes via `local.outlet.streamTo(sink)` rather than `ManagedHost.connect`, so
  mesh edges introduced by replication do not appear in `LocationRegistry.all()`. A
  structural cost model that counts edges from the topology index would undercount
  replicated traffic. The harness must count frames at the bridge, not edges at the
  registry.
- **PLC1 may not honour the envelope.** Nothing here can force it to. The refusal is
  loud (`[BEN2-40]`, BS-19), and the honesty note in §5 names this as the one obligation
  that passes to the consumer.
