# BEN2 — design notes

## Why this is an epic and not a feature under BEN1

The sizing rule says: file as a feature under `computenet-x9e` if this is really an
extension of BEN1's harness. It is not, on three counts.

1. **It crosses a seam BEN1 never touches.** BEN1 is explicitly single-host micro
   (its §4: *"BEN1 stops at single-host micro"*). BEN2's defining dimension is host
   count, and the substrate for that dimension **does not exist anywhere in the
   repository** — `SimWorld` is single-host, and the only N-peer composition is a
   `private class Peer` inside `kernel/src/test/kotlin/civictech/cell/durability/CrashRecoveryTest.kt:38`.
   Building an N-host measurement world, generalizing cell addressing past the
   two-peer `listener`/`dialer` scheme, and validating it against a real socket is
   substrate work, not a new benchmark in an existing harness.
2. **It has a deliverable with its own consumer contract.** The cost model export is
   an interface between two lanes, with a schema, a version, a coverage envelope, a
   refusal semantics, and a consumer-shaped acceptance test. Seventeen of the
   requirements (`[BEN2-30]`–`[BEN2-46]`) are about that artifact alone. BEN1 has no
   equivalent — its output is a findings document read by humans.
3. **It carries two gap triggers of its own** (G-43's cost bound, G-25's segmentation
   trigger), each requiring a designed measurement rather than a sweep parameter.

The eight-feature decomposition in §7 is a second signal: F1, F2, F4 are each
independently reviewable pieces of infrastructure, and F4 must precede F5–F7.

That said, BEN2 is *tightly* coupled to BEN1 and must not fork it. The description's
§2.1 table exists precisely to make the reuse boundary auditable — result model,
dispersion gate, drive rules, gating convention and findings file are BEN1's and stay
BEN1's.

## Concrete shape

```
bench/
  build.gradle.kts                       # + implementation(project(":wire"))   [BEN2-07]
  src/main/kotlin/civictech/bench/
    macro/shape/Shapes.kt                # chain | fanOutTree | fanInLattice | diamond | randomDag
    macro/shape/ShapeSpec.kt             # named shape + seed + cardinality -> GraphSpec
    macro/mesh/BenchMesh.kt              # N peers; per peer: LocationRegistry, ManagedHost,
                                         #   bridge ManagedHost, Peering.Side, Replication?
                                         # pairwise Peering.loopback; generalized ref minting
    macro/mesh/MeshRefs.kt               # host-count-independent CellRef derivation
    macro/SweepPoint.kt                  # the coordinate tuple           [BEN2-22]
    macro/PointOutcome.kt                # Ok | Unreportable | NonConvergent | NonDeterministic
                                         #   | Unschedulable | Failed     [BEN2-27..29], [BEN2-41]
    macro/Counters.kt                    # messages, cross-host frames, WireCodec bytes,
                                         #   journal records, sim steps   [BEN2-23]
    macro/rebaseline/ReBaselineProbe.kt  # RESTART-driven, C x D x H       [BEN2-36]
    macro/journal/JournalProbe.kt        # size, bytes/record, replay, checkpoint  [BEN2-37]
    cost/CostModel.kt                    # StructuralCost / CalibrationConstant / Envelope
    cost/CostSchema.kt                   # version constant + (de)serialization
    cost/CostWriter.kt                   # admission rules; refuses excluded points
    cost/CostQuery.kt                    # the PLC1-facing read API + envelope refusal
  src/jmh/kotlin/civictech/bench/macro/
    MacroSweepBenchmark.kt
    ReBaselineFanOutBenchmark.kt
  src/test/kotlin/civictech/bench/
    cost/CostRoundTripTest.kt            # BS-17, BS-18
    cost/CostEnvelopeTest.kt             # BS-8, BS-9, BS-19, BS-20
    macro/ShapeReplaySafetyTest.kt       # BS-1
    macro/MeshConstructionTest.kt        # BS-2, BS-3
    ProjectGraphTest.kt (BEN1's)         # extended for :wire — BS-22
doc/bench/
  findings.md                            # appended (BEN1's file)
  cost-model.json                        # the export                     [BEN2-30]
```

## The export's shape, concretely

The load-bearing decision is the two-layer split, so sketch it:

```kotlin
@Serializable
data class CostModel(
    val schemaVersion: Int,              // [BEN2-31], rejected if unknown [BEN2-32]
    val harnessSha: String,              // [BEN2-42]
    val envelope: Envelope,              // [BEN2-39]
    val structural: List<StructuralCost>,     // SIM-derived counts       [BEN2-33]
    val calibration: List<CalibrationConstant>, // REAL-derived per-unit  [BEN2-33]
    val laws: List<GrowthLaw>,           // fitted form + points + fit    [BEN2-43]
    val exclusions: List<ExcludedPoint>, // why a coordinate is absent    [BEN2-41]
)

@Serializable data class Coordinate(          // [BEN2-22], [BEN2-34]
    val shape: String, val shapeSeed: Long,
    val cardinality: Long, val batchSize: Int,
    val hostCount: Int, val fanOut: Int,
    val replication: Boolean, val durability: Boolean,
    val drive: Drive,                          // BEN1's enum
)

@Serializable data class StructuralCost(
    val at: Coordinate,
    val messages: Long, val crossHostFrames: Long, val wireBytes: Long,
    val journalRecords: Long, val simSteps: Long,
)

@Serializable data class CalibrationConstant(
    val name: String,                          // localDispatchNanos, crossHostFrameNanos,
                                               // journalFsyncNanos, retainedBytesPerElement, ...
    val value: Double, val unit: String,
    val dispersion: Double,                    // [BEN2-38], BEN1's figure
    val env: RunEnvironment,                   // BEN1's type, non-nullable fields
)
```

`CostQuery` is the PLC1-facing surface and the only thing that should be considered
public:

```kotlin
sealed interface CostAnswer {
    data class Priced(val value: Double, val unit: String,
                      val from: Provenance) : CostAnswer
    data class OutOfEnvelope(val dimension: String,
                             val requested: Any, val measured: ClosedRange<Double>) : CostAnswer
    data class NotMeasured(val reason: String) : CostAnswer
}

class CostQuery(model: CostModel) {
    fun coLocatedEdge(at: Coordinate): CostAnswer
    fun crossHostEdge(at: Coordinate): CostAnswer
    fun cellResidency(at: Coordinate): CostAnswer
    fun reBaseline(at: Coordinate): CostAnswer
}
```

Making `OutOfEnvelope` a *value* rather than an exception is deliberate: PLC1 must be
able to enumerate what it cannot price, so it can report its own coverage instead of
falling back to a guess. `NotMeasured` is separate from `OutOfEnvelope` because
"inside the envelope but this cell of the cross product was skipped" and "outside
everything we measured" call for different simulator behaviour.

## Structural-cost admission is the whole honesty mechanism

`CostWriter` should make the exclusion rules structural, exactly as BEN1 made its
result invariants structural:

- `CostWriter.admit(point: PointOutcome)` accepts only `PointOutcome.Ok`. Every other
  variant is routed to `exclusions` with its reason. There is no code path that turns a
  `NonConvergent` into a number.
- `CalibrationConstant` construction requires `Drive == REAL`. A SIM wall-clock cannot
  be constructed into one (`[BEN2-25]`, BS-8).
- `Envelope` is derived from the admitted points, never declared by hand — so it cannot
  be widened to cover a claim.
- `GrowthLaw` requires a goodness-of-fit value; there is no constructor without one
  (`[BEN2-44]`).

These are ordinary unit tests in `:bench:test`, sub-second, and they are what makes
this epic's honesty requirements enforceable rather than aspirational.

## The mesh harness, concretely

Per peer, generalizing `CrashRecoveryTest.kt:38-43`:

```kotlin
class BenchPeer(controller: SimulationController, index: Int, journal: Journal?) {
    val registry   = LocationRegistry()
    val host       = ManagedHost(scheduler = controller.scheduler(), registry = registry,
                                 journal = journal)
    val bridgeHost = ManagedHost(scheduler = controller.scheduler(), registry = registry)
    val side       = Peering.Side(registry, bridgeHost, peer = PeerId("bench-$index"))
    val replication: Replication? = ...
}

class BenchMesh(hostCount: Int, seed: Long, ...) {
    val peers: List<BenchPeer>
    // pairwise: for (i in indices) for (j in i+1 until n) Peering.loopback(peers[i].side, peers[j].side)
    fun runToIdle(budget: Int): Int   // controller.runToIdle
}
```

Ref minting must be a pure function of (logical name, peer index, host count) — not of a
`listener`/`dialer` role. `UUID.nameUUIDFromBytes("bench:$name@$index")` in the style of
`demo/shopping`'s `unionRef`, but index-based.

Full mesh at 8 hosts is 28 loopbacks; a star or ring variant is worth having as a
declared shape parameter, since PLC1 will care whether cost scales with *peers* or with
*edges*. Which topologies to measure is F2/F5's call; the harness should not hard-code
"full mesh".

## Counting frames at the bridge, not edges at the registry

`Replication` subscribes via `local.outlet.streamTo(sink)` rather than through
`ManagedHost`'s connect path, so replication traffic never appears in
`LocationRegistry.all()` / `localLinks()`. Any structural count derived from the topology
index would silently undercount replicated meshes — the exact failure that would make the
export wrong in the direction PLC1 cares about most.

Count at `civictech.cell.wire.BridgeEgressCell` / `BridgeIngressCell` and at
`WireCodec.encode` instead. `FanOutlet.targetMisses` is the only counter the port layer
currently exposes, so instrumentation must be harness-side (wrapping the bridge sink),
not kernel-side — `[BEN2-51]` forbids touching `kernel/src/main`.

## Driving the re-baseline

The cheapest reliable trigger is the supervision RESTART path already exercised by
`kernel/src/test/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/RestartReBaselineTest.kt`: install a
`SupervisionPolicy.RESTART`, make the cell throw once, and let
`ManagedHost.kt:845-864` do the epoch minting and `reBaseline(supersedes, true)` emission.
Fan-out width is set by the number of `FanOutlet.tap(...)` calls before the restart;
cardinality by pre-loading the source. The measured quantity is everything downstream of
the throw until quiescence.

`Evolution.kt:196-208` (shadow promotion) is a second re-baseline driver with a different
cost profile. Worth one comparison point; not worth a sweep dimension.

## What a later agent will be tempted to do, and must not

- **Extrapolate past the envelope** "because the curve is obviously linear" —
  `[BEN2-40]`. The envelope refusal is the epic's entire contribution to PLC1's honesty.
- **Implement G-43's bound** after measuring that it is needed — `[BEN2-52]`. Measuring
  that a bound is needed is the deliverable; the bound is kernel-lane work.
- **Add journal segmentation** after the G-25 trigger fires — `[BEN2-52]` again.
- **Turn the WAL off** to get a cleaner operator signal — that is KBLK, `[BEN2-49]`.
- **Swap a failing seed for a friendlier one** — `[BEN2-12]`, and a standing repository
  invariant.
- **Widen the tolerance** in `[BEN2-21]` until the socket cross-check agrees with the
  loopback mesh. If they disagree, the loopback costs get marked transport-unvalidated;
  that is the designed outcome, not a failure to be tuned away.
- **Start a BB-\* suite** "since the macro harness is there now" — `[BEN2-56]`. Each BB
  suite has its own kernel dependencies (KE1, KE4, KE5, KAGG-R, KRD, KBLK).
- **Add a concord scenario** for a structural count on the grounds that counts are
  machine-independent — see the description's Concord note.

## Ordering rationale, restated

F4 (the export) before F5–F7 (the sweeps) for the same reason BEN1 put F3 before F4–F6:
if the admission and envelope rules are written after the numbers exist, the numbers get
grandfathered in and the envelope becomes a description of what happened rather than a
constraint on what may be claimed. The export must be able to reject the first real
sweep.

description:
# PLC1 — Mesh simulator + cost model

Lane: distribution (`lane:distribution`). Priority P3. Rank 13 in
`computenet-milestone-plan.md` §5 (`PLC1 → PLC2`, "Gated on BEN2's measured costs").

**Depends on:** BEN1 (`computenet-x9e`, the `:bench` module and JMH harness) and **BEN2**
(macro workloads: graph shape × cardinality × host-count sweeps; re-baseline cost under
fan-out, G-43). BEN2 is the real gate and is being filed separately — it is listed here as an
**unwired dependency** and must be wired once its id exists.

**Unblocks:** PLC2 (offline placement/economics policy engine, G-61/G-62), and through it PLC3
and ECO1.

**Also an input (not a blocker):** V4-PILOT — inspector-v4 wave 10, merged `9dd03a8` — is the
distribution lane's *first merged evidence artifact*: the first same-logical-id replicated pilot
over a real socket, two JVMs, two inspectors. Its findings file is
`doc/demo-shopping-replica-pilot.md` (the milestone plan's §1 distribution note: "treat its
findings file as PLC/DSC input"). PLC1 consumes it as a **topology and shape** input — the first
real two-node replicated mesh the repo has ever observed — not as a cost source: it was not
instrumented to produce timings, and §4.2 below forbids treating an uninstrumented observation
as a cost.

---

## 1. Ambition / Why

**Placement and economics are entirely arguments about cost, and nobody has measured one.**

G-61's proposal (`doc/spec/90-roadmap/91-gap-analysis.md` row G-61, restated verbatim in
`doc/spec/30-execution-model/31-hosts.md:319`, `doc/spec/30-execution-model/32-concurrency-colors.md:53`
and `doc/spec/50-development-process/53-evolution.md:161`) asks for "a placement engine consuming
`CellDescriptor.color` and optional GraphSpec placement constraints to **co-host same-colored
chains**, replicate pure cells per color neighbourhood, and route multi-host replays … and a
placement/**cost policy bounding how much in-flight remote traffic a candidate co-location swap
may park** when membrane links span many peers".

G-62's proposal asks when to "**spawn a local replica vs subscribe remotely**", where replicas
live, "migration candidacy under persistent high attention with remote hotspots", and
"partition split/merge and bulk-rebalance triggering **by load/size/attention**".

Every italicised phrase is a comparison between two magnitudes. The specification already fixes
the *vocabulary* of those magnitudes normatively and refuses to fix their values:

> `[41-LOC-01]` … the graph SHALL compute the same observable result for a pipeline split across
> hosts as for its single-host twin. **Only cost differs (P2 tiers, 10/14): direct call → queue
> hop → serialized send.**
> — `doc/spec/40-distribution/41-location-transparency.md:9`

Three tiers, no numbers. `95-research-plan.md` §R5 is explicit about what is missing and in what
order: "**instrument fusion wins (co-hosted direct-call vs enqueue) to quantify what co-hosting is
worth**; prototype (1) with the simplest greedy policy on the existing telemetry; **defer (2)/(3)
until measured**." §R6 likewise: "start with (1) as a pure policy vocabulary (no enforcement) and
**measure what real workloads need**".

**Why the simulator, and not just more benchmarks.** BEN1/BEN2 measure the configurations you can
build. Placement decisions are about the configurations you have *not* built: a candidate
co-location swap, a replica spawned here instead of subscribed there, a repartition across a host
count that does not exist in the lab. The counterfactual is the product. A discrete-event mesh
simulator, driven by measured per-tier costs, is the cheapest honest way to compare candidates
before any of them is enforced by a kernel hook.

**Why the gate is a requirement, not a scheduling note.** The plan's deliberate ordering says
"**PLC1 gated on BEN2**: no simulating against fictional costs." Left as scheduling, that gate
decays: an implementer with a half-finished BEN2 types a plausible `remoteHopMicros = 50` to get a
green test, and from that moment the simulator produces guidance that is *indistinguishable in
shape* from calibrated guidance. PLC2 then consumes it as evidence, and PLC3 enforces the result
in the kernel. The fabrication is invisible three hops downstream, where it decides where cells
actually land.

So PLC1's central obligation is negative and structural: **the simulator must be unable to produce
guidance from unmeasured or fabricated cost inputs, and must record the provenance of every cost
scalar that entered a run.** A simulator that merely *discourages* fabricated costs has not
implemented this epic. This is also the honest reading of the repo's own rule (`AGENTS.md`): "A
requirement that cannot be checked honestly is filed in `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md`, never
weakened into a passing scenario."

**What PLC1 is not.** It is not a placement policy (PLC2), not an enforcement mechanism (PLC3),
not a benchmark harness (BEN1), not a runtime component of any kind. It never decides where a
cell lands; it makes candidate placements *comparable* and every comparison *auditable*.

---

## 2. What we build

### 2.1 Module: a new leaf module `sim/` (`:sim`) — offline, and deliberately outside `:kernel`

**Decision: a new leaf Gradle module `sim/`, registered in `settings.gradle.kts` next to `:wire`
and `:inspect`. No code lands in `kernel/`.**

Justification in the repository's own terms:

- **It is offline.** Nothing in `:sim` runs inside a host, spawns a cell, or serves a port. It
  reads recorded artefacts and writes a report. `AGENTS.md` — "Keep `kernel` transport-neutral … A
  new transport dependency belongs in a small transport module such as `wire`" — generalises: the
  kernel owns semantics; instruments live behind a module boundary. `:wire`, `:inspect`,
  `:concord` and (per BEN1) `:bench` are four existing precedents for exactly this shape.
- **Dependency direction.** `:sim → :kernel` and `:sim → :nature` (it reads `GraphSpec`,
  `InstanceSpec`, `Interest`, `CellDescriptor.color`, `Manifest` **as data**). `:kernel` **must
  not** depend on `:sim`; nor `:nature`, `:gen`, `:wire`. A kernel that transitively pulled a
  simulator would be a scope regression, and G-63 (the kernel SCC) is exactly the reason not to
  add another node to it for a tool.
- **No compile dependency on `:bench`.** This is a deliberate and load-bearing choice. Costs enter
  `:sim` as a **serialized measurement artefact** (a file BEN1/BEN2 emit), never as a
  cross-module function call. Three consequences, all wanted: the JMH tax stays in `:bench`; the
  artefact can carry provenance metadata that a Kotlin call cannot; and §4.2's refusal is
  enforceable because there is exactly *one* channel by which a cost can enter, and it is a
  channel that must carry provenance to parse at all.
- **Deterministic and dependency-light.** JDK-only plus whatever serialization `:bench` already
  emits. No simulation framework dependency; the event loop is a priority queue and a seeded RNG.

### 2.2 Surface

1. **`CostModel`** — the tiered vocabulary of `[41-LOC-01]` made numeric: `DIRECT_CALL`,
   `QUEUE_HOP`, `SERIALIZED_SEND` per-delivery costs, plus per-delta encode/decode cost, per-cell
   footprint, and per-host capacity. Nothing invented beyond what the spec's three tiers and
   BEN1's stated measurements (per-operator delta throughput, fan-out scaling, per-cell footprint)
   can populate.
2. **`CostScalar`** — a value that cannot exist without provenance: `(value, unit, provenance)`.
   There is no constructor that takes a bare number. This is the type-level half of §4.2.
3. **`CostProvenance`** — `(measurementId, benchmarkRunId, sourceArtifactDigest, gitCommit,
   hostProfile, capturedAt, sampleCount, dispersion)`. `SYNTHETIC` is a distinct, *labelled*
   provenance kind, permitted only in the explicitly-selected exploratory mode of §4.2.
3. **`CalibrationSet`** — the parsed BEN1/BEN2 artefact: which scalars it supplies, which it does
   not, and its own digest. A `CostModel` is *built from* a `CalibrationSet`; an unpopulated tier
   is a hole, never a default.
4. **`MeshTopology`** — hosts (with `HostColor` and capacity), link classes between them
   (co-located / same-JVM queue hop / socket), and the cell placement under evaluation, expressed
   over instance sets with `Interest` and the existing `InstanceSpec.placement` selector string.
5. **`MeshSimulator`** — a deterministic, seeded discrete-event simulation over a
   `(MeshTopology, Workload, CostModel)` triple.
6. **`SimulationResult`** — the run record of §4.4: inputs digest, seed, the complete set of cost
   provenances actually *consulted*, per-candidate aggregates, and the tool version.
7. **`SimulationRefusal`** — the typed refusal of §4.2, naming every missing or synthetic scalar.
   A refusal is a first-class returned outcome, not an exception swallowed by a caller.
8. **A Gradle entry point** (`./gradlew :sim:simulate -Pscenario=… -Pcalibration=…`) plus the
   `:sim:test` suite.

## 3. How, using ComputeNet

Real types PLC1 reads (all as data; `:sim` constructs none of them at runtime):

- **Colors.** `civictech.nature.Color` (`PURE`, `BLOCKING`, `SUSPENDING`) —
  `nature/src/main/kotlin/civictech/nature/ContractDescriptor.kt:107`; surfaced per cell as
  `CellDescriptor.color` (same file, `data class CellDescriptor`, line ~294). This is the *exact*
  input G-61's proposal names, and `32-concurrency-colors.md:51` is the SHOULD being costed:
  "Placement engines SHOULD co-host same-colored chains."
- **Host colors and the spawn-time colour rule.** `ManagedHost`'s constructor `color` and the
  validation in its `spawn` —
  `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/ManagedHost.kt:920-938` (`SuspendingCell` cannot
  spawn on a `BLOCKING` host, and vice-versa). A candidate placement that violates this is
  **infeasible**, not merely expensive; the simulator must model feasibility separately from cost.
- **The subtree quota walk.** `ManagedHost.kt:910-918` — the G-28 ancestor walk
  (`quota exceeded: host … allows N cells in its subtree (G-28)`). Same point: a capacity
  constraint the simulator must honour as feasibility.
- **Placement hints that already exist.**
  `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/graph/GraphDsl.kt` — `data class InstanceSpec(interest,
  instanceId, placement, journalId, frontierPolicy)`, whose KDoc records the exact state of the
  world PLC1/PLC2/PLC3 change: "`placement` — **host-selector hint (recorded, routed by the
  multi-host replay driver — 93 I-15, driver unbuilt)**". The simulator's topology vocabulary is
  built on that selector string so PLC2's output is expressible without inventing a second naming
  scheme.
- **Instance sets and interest.** `civictech.cell.link.Interest`
  (`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/link/Interest.kt`), `InstanceSetStep` / `InstanceSpec` /
  `InstanceCellFactory` and `InstanceSetStep.lower()` in the same `GraphDsl.kt`, and
  `civictech.cell.replication.InstanceSet` /`Replication.maybeLink`
  (`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/replication/`). `42-replication.md:139` `[42-INT-01]`
  fixes what an interest-scoped instance must hold; the simulator's link-formation model must
  agree with `maybeLink`'s overlap rule or its traffic estimates are fiction.
- **Graphs as data.** `GraphSpec` / `SpawnStep` / `ConnectStep` / `lowered()` —
  `GraphDsl.kt:232`. A recorded `GraphSpec` is the natural scenario input format; `:sim` reads it,
  never applies it.
- **Locality classes.** `LocationRegistry.Local(host)` vs `LocationRegistry.Remote(sink, peer)` —
  `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/LocationRegistry.kt`. These two constructors *are*
  the boundary between the second and third cost tiers of `[41-LOC-01]`, and the simulator's
  three-tier cost assignment must be defined against them rather than against a private notion of
  "remote".
  **KX interaction:** KX (`computenet-iyi`) extracts this class into registry + `InstanceIndex` +
  `DeliveryHold` (C-13). `:sim` must depend only on the *location* half — `location(ref)`,
  `Local`, `Remote`, `instancesOf` — which C-13's resolution keeps in the registry proper. PLC1
  must not reach into `interests`/`setInterest` or the repartition hold, which move.
- **The measured artefact.** BEN1 (`computenet-x9e`) creates `:bench` and its JMH harness; BEN2
  adds the macro sweeps (graph shape × cardinality × host count, and the G-43 fan-out
  re-baseline). PLC1 defines the *artefact schema* those two write into and owns the parser.
- **Evidence shape.** `doc/demo-shopping-replica-pilot.md` (V4-PILOT) — the two-JVM,
  same-logical-id replicated pilot over a real socket. PLC1's topology vocabulary must be able to
  express that mesh exactly (two hosts, one replicated logical cell, one socket link, two
  observers), because it is the only real multi-node shape the repo has evidence for.
- **Findings.** Per the plan's §6 standing hygiene, PLC1 writes to its own append-only
  `doc/placement/findings.md`, citing G-ids; it does not edit `91-gap-analysis.md` or
  `CONCORDANCE.md`.

## 4. Functional requirements (EARS)

Ids are epic-scoped `[PLC1-*]` and deliberately do not collide with normative spec ids, which
follow `[NN-SLUG-nn]`.

**Honesty note on upstream ids.** There are no `[3x-*]` or `[5x-*]` EARS ids for placement, and
none for economics: G-61 and G-62 exist as **prose gap entries** in
`doc/spec/90-roadmap/91-gap-analysis.md` and as ⚠ GAP blocks in `31-hosts.md:319`,
`32-concurrency-colors.md:53`, `53-evolution.md:161`, `42-replication.md:106` and
`43-security.md:143`, plus the research questions `95-research-plan.md` §R5/§R6 (verified by
grep). PLC1 therefore cannot cite "the G-61 requirement id it makes true". What each requirement
below cites is the specific normative *prose* obligation, the adjacent EARS id that must keep
holding, or the research-plan direction it realises. The adjacent normative ids in force here are
`[41-LOC-01]` (location transparency; source of the three cost tiers), `[42-INT-01]`
(interest-scoped holding), `[33-MOVE-01]` (migration equivalence) and `[42-REPL-04]` (replica
convergence).

Every requirement below is an obligation **on the simulator**. None asserts a performance
magnitude, a placement outcome, or that any particular placement is better than another —
asserting those would be exactly the fabrication this epic exists to prevent.

### 4.1 Cost inputs and provenance (ubiquitous / event-driven)

- **[PLC1-PROV-01]** The simulator shall represent every cost input as a value carrying, as an
  inseparable part of that value, the provenance record of the measurement that produced it.
  *(makes true: `95-research-plan.md` §R5 "defer (2)/(3) until measured"; the plan's "no
  simulating against fictional costs".)*
- **[PLC1-PROV-02]** The simulator shall provide no means of constructing a cost input from a bare
  numeric literal without an accompanying provenance record. *(same.)*
- **[PLC1-PROV-03]** A cost provenance record shall identify the measurement id, the originating
  benchmark run id, the digest of the source artefact, the source revision, the host profile, the
  capture timestamp, the sample count, and a dispersion measure. *(makes true: `95-research-plan.md`
  §R5 "instrument fusion wins … to quantify what co-hosting is worth" — an unattributed quantity
  cannot be re-derived.)*
- **[PLC1-PROV-04]** The simulator shall admit cost inputs from exactly one channel: a calibration
  artefact produced by the benchmark lane. *(makes true: the BEN1→BEN2→PLC1 dependency edge in
  `computenet-milestone-plan.md` §1/§2.)*
- **[PLC1-PROV-05]** When a calibration artefact is loaded, the simulator shall record that
  artefact's digest and shall reject any subsequent mutation of the loaded cost values.
- **[PLC1-PROV-06]** The simulator shall classify each cost tier it models against the three tiers
  `[41-LOC-01]` names — direct call, queue hop, serialized send — and shall define its assignment
  of a modelled delivery to a tier in terms of `LocationRegistry.Local` versus
  `LocationRegistry.Remote` and host identity. *(makes true: `[41-LOC-01]`.)*
- **[PLC1-PROV-07]** Where a calibration artefact supplies a value for a tier the simulator does
  not model, the simulator shall retain that value's provenance in the run record and shall report
  it as unconsumed rather than discarding it silently.

### 4.2 Refusal on unmeasured or fabricated costs (unwanted-behaviour / state-driven)

This is the section the epic exists for.

- **[PLC1-REF-01]** If any cost scalar required by the requested simulation is absent from the
  loaded calibration set, then the simulator shall refuse the run and shall not emit a
  `SimulationResult`. *(makes true: the plan's "PLC1 gated on BEN2: no simulating against
  fictional costs".)*
- **[PLC1-REF-02]** If a run is refused, then the refusal shall name every missing scalar
  individually, by the tier and quantity it belongs to. *(same; and `AGENTS.md`'s honesty rule.)*
- **[PLC1-REF-03]** If no calibration artefact has been loaded, then the simulator shall refuse
  every simulation request, including requests whose topology has a single host.
- **[PLC1-REF-04]** If a loaded calibration artefact fails digest verification, is malformed, or
  omits any required provenance field of `[PLC1-PROV-03]`, then the simulator shall refuse to load
  it, shall report the offending field and file, and shall not fall back to any default,
  previously loaded, or built-in cost value.
- **[PLC1-REF-05]** The simulator shall ship no default, built-in, or fallback numeric cost value
  for any tier or quantity. *(makes true: the plan's ordering note; without this, `[PLC1-REF-01]`
  is unenforceable.)*
- **[PLC1-REF-06]** Where an explicitly-selected exploratory mode permits synthetic cost values,
  the simulator shall mark every scalar so supplied with a synthetic provenance kind, shall mark
  the entire run record synthetic, and shall render that marking non-removable from any artefact
  the run produces. *(optional-feature form; makes true: `95-research-plan.md` §R5's
  "prototype … the simplest greedy policy" needs a sandbox, and the sandbox must be unable to
  masquerade as evidence.)*
- **[PLC1-REF-07]** While a run is marked synthetic, the simulator shall not emit comparative
  guidance between candidate placements, and shall emit only the raw per-candidate aggregates with
  the synthetic marking attached. *(state-driven; this is what "must refuse to produce guidance
  from fabricated cost inputs" means operationally.)*
- **[PLC1-REF-08]** If a calibration artefact's source revision is not an ancestor of, or equal
  to, the revision under simulation, then the simulator shall report the divergence in the run
  record and shall mark the run stale. *(makes true: G-43's re-baseline obligation — a cost curve
  measured against a different runtime is not evidence about this one.)*
- **[PLC1-REF-09]** If a cost scalar's recorded sample count or dispersion falls outside the
  configured admissibility bounds, then the simulator shall refuse the run and shall name the
  scalar and the bound violated. *(makes true: `95-research-plan.md` §R5's requirement that
  co-hosting's worth be *quantified*, not merely sampled once.)*
- **[PLC1-REF-10]** The simulator shall treat an observation that carries no timing instrumentation
  — including the V4-PILOT findings in `doc/demo-shopping-replica-pilot.md` — as a topology and
  shape input only, and shall not admit it as a cost source.

### 4.3 Reproducibility of a simulation run (ubiquitous / event-driven / unwanted)

- **[PLC1-RUN-01]** The simulator shall be deterministic: two runs given identical topology,
  workload, calibration artefact, seed, and tool version shall produce byte-identical run records
  apart from the wall-clock capture timestamp.
- **[PLC1-RUN-02]** The simulator shall derive every stochastic choice from a single explicit
  seed. *(mirrors the repo rule in `AGENTS.md`: "Preserve deterministic simulation/generative
  tests.")*
- **[PLC1-RUN-03]** When a run begins, the simulator shall record the seed, and when a seed is not
  supplied it shall generate one, record it, and report it.
- **[PLC1-RUN-04]** The simulator shall not consult wall-clock time, ambient system load, host
  thread counts, environment variables, or network state in any modelled quantity.
- **[PLC1-RUN-05]** If a run record is replayed against a calibration artefact whose digest differs
  from the one recorded, then the simulator shall refuse the replay rather than produce a
  differently-costed result under the same run id.
- **[PLC1-RUN-06]** If a discovered failing seed exposes a defect in the simulator, then that seed
  shall be retained as a regression input and shall not be replaced by a passing seed.
  *(`AGENTS.md`: "Do not replace a discovered failing seed with a friendlier seed.")*

### 4.4 What a result must record (ubiquitous)

- **[PLC1-RES-01]** A run record shall identify the tool version, the seed, the digest of every
  input artefact, and the digest of the topology and workload under simulation.
- **[PLC1-RES-02]** A run record shall enumerate the provenance of every cost scalar the run
  actually consulted, distinguished from those merely loaded.
- **[PLC1-RES-03]** A run record shall state, for each candidate placement evaluated, the modelled
  aggregates it produced and the feasibility verdict it received, with infeasibility attributed to
  the specific constraint violated.
- **[PLC1-RES-04]** A run record shall state every modelling assumption the simulator applied that
  is not derived from a measured scalar, as an enumerated list.
- **[PLC1-RES-05]** A run record shall be serializable to a stable textual form, and reloading a
  serialized run record shall yield an equal record.
- **[PLC1-RES-06]** A run record shall not contain a comparative recommendation between candidates
  unless every scalar it consulted has non-synthetic provenance. *(complex; consequence of
  `[PLC1-REF-06]`/`[PLC1-REF-07]`.)*
- **[PLC1-RES-07]** Where a run is stale per `[PLC1-REF-08]`, the run record shall carry the
  staleness marking and the two revisions involved.

### 4.5 Modelling fidelity — feasibility before cost (state-driven / unwanted)

- **[PLC1-MOD-01]** The simulator shall model a candidate placement as infeasible, rather than
  costly, when it places a cell on a host whose colour the kernel's spawn-time colour rule
  rejects. *(makes true: `32-concurrency-colors.md` §Colors and the rule implemented at
  `ManagedHost.kt:920-938`.)*
- **[PLC1-MOD-02]** The simulator shall model a candidate placement as infeasible when it would
  exceed any ancestor host's subtree quota. *(makes true: `31-hosts.md:296` G-28 subtree quota;
  implemented at `ManagedHost.kt:910-918`.)*
- **[PLC1-MOD-03]** The simulator shall form a modelled gossip link between two instances of one
  logical cell only where their declared interests overlap. *(makes true: `[42-INT-01]` and
  `42-replication.md` §Interest-scoped instance sets; implemented by
  `Replication.maybeLink`.)*
- **[PLC1-MOD-04]** The simulator shall filter each modelled emission to the target instance's
  interest before costing it. *(makes true: `[42-INT-01]` — "a delta a peer has no interest in
  never crosses"; costing an unfiltered emission would systematically overstate remote traffic.)*
- **[PLC1-MOD-05]** If the simulator's link-formation or filtering model diverges from the
  kernel's, then the divergence shall be recorded as a modelling assumption under `[PLC1-RES-04]`
  and reported, and shall not be silently absorbed into a cost.
- **[PLC1-MOD-06]** The simulator shall express a modelled mesh in terms of the existing
  `InstanceSpec.placement` host-selector vocabulary, and shall not introduce a second, parallel
  naming scheme for hosts. *(makes true: `GraphDsl.kt`'s `InstanceSpec` KDoc; PLC2's output must be
  expressible against the same seam that PLC3 will enforce.)*
- **[PLC1-MOD-07]** The simulator shall express the two-host, one-replicated-logical-cell,
  one-socket topology that V4-PILOT observed, without extension. *(makes true: the milestone
  plan's "treat its findings file as PLC/DSC input".)*

### 4.6 Boundary and neutrality (ubiquitous / unwanted)

- **[PLC1-BND-01]** The simulator shall not spawn a cell, start a host, open a socket, or apply a
  `GraphSpec`.
- **[PLC1-BND-02]** `:kernel` shall not depend on `:sim`, at compile time or at runtime.
- **[PLC1-BND-03]** The simulator shall consume `GraphSpec`, `InstanceSpec`, `Interest` and
  `CellDescriptor` as data and shall not require any change to their declarations.
- **[PLC1-BND-04]** If a change to `:sim` would require a change under `kernel/src/main`, then that
  change is out of scope for PLC1 and shall be reported rather than made. *(PLC3 is the only item
  in this arc that touches the kernel; see §6.)*
- **[PLC1-BND-05]** The simulator shall not write to `doc/spec/90-roadmap/91-gap-analysis.md` or
  `doc/spec/CONCORDANCE.md`; findings go to `doc/placement/findings.md`. *(makes true:
  `computenet-milestone-plan.md` §6 standing hygiene.)*

### 4.7 Explicitly non-verifiable — stated, not softened

`AGENTS.md`: a requirement that cannot be checked honestly is recorded, not weakened.

- **[PLC1-NV-01]** *Provenance truthfulness.* The simulator can verify that a provenance record is
  present, well-formed, internally consistent, and digest-matched against the artefact it came
  from. It **cannot** verify that the artefact's numbers were actually produced by the benchmark
  run they name — a sufficiently determined author can emit a well-formed artefact containing
  invented numbers from `:bench`. PLC1 closes the *casual* fabrication path (there is no literal
  constructor, no default, no second channel) and makes the *deliberate* one leave a signed-shaped
  audit trail with a named run id and revision. It does not close it. This limit shall be stated in
  the epic's final report and, if PLC2 is ever tempted to treat provenance as proof, filed in
  `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` rather than asserted.
- **[PLC1-NV-02]** *Simulator faithfulness.* No test in `:sim` can establish that the simulator's
  model of the runtime is *accurate* — only that it is deterministic, self-consistent, and
  agrees with the kernel's feasibility and interest rules. Accuracy is a validation activity
  against BEN2 measurements (see §7 F5), and its residual error is a reported quantity, never an
  asserted bound.
- **[PLC1-NV-03]** *Admissibility bounds.* `[PLC1-REF-09]`'s bounds are a configured policy, not a
  derived truth. PLC1 must state the chosen bounds and their justification; it must not claim they
  are correct.

## 5. Behaviour specifications (Given/When/Then)

Each becomes a named test in `:sim:test` unless stated otherwise.

### Happy paths

- **BS-01 — calibrated run is reproducible.** *Given* a calibration artefact covering every tier
  the topology needs, *when* the same topology, workload and seed are simulated twice, *then* the
  two run records are byte-identical apart from the capture timestamp. `[PLC1-RUN-01]`
- **BS-02 — provenance survives to the record.** *Given* a calibration artefact with three
  distinct measurement ids, *when* a run consults two of them, *then* the run record enumerates
  exactly those two as consulted and the third as loaded-but-unconsumed. `[PLC1-PROV-07]`,
  `[PLC1-RES-02]`
- **BS-03 — the pilot topology is expressible.** *Given* the two-host replicated shape recorded in
  `doc/demo-shopping-replica-pilot.md`, *when* it is expressed as a `MeshTopology`, *then* it
  parses and simulates without any extension to the topology vocabulary. `[PLC1-MOD-07]`
- **BS-04 — round-trip.** *Given* a run record, *when* it is serialized and reloaded, *then* the
  reloaded record equals the original. `[PLC1-RES-05]`

### Refusal and adversarial paths — the core of the epic

- **BS-05 — missing scalar refuses.** *Given* a calibration artefact lacking the serialized-send
  tier, *when* a two-host topology is simulated, *then* the simulator returns a refusal naming
  that tier and emits no `SimulationResult`. `[PLC1-REF-01]`, `[PLC1-REF-02]`
- **BS-06 — no calibration at all refuses, even single-host.** *Given* no calibration artefact,
  *when* a one-host topology is simulated, *then* the run is refused. `[PLC1-REF-03]`
- **BS-07 — no back door exists.** *Given* the public API of `:sim`, *when* it is enumerated,
  *then* no constructor, factory, builder, copy, or setter accepts a cost magnitude without a
  provenance record. Implemented as a reflective/architecture test in the style of
  `kernel/src/test/kotlin/civictech/cell/architecture/DemoSurfaceAllowlistTest.kt`.
  `[PLC1-PROV-02]`, `[PLC1-REF-05]`
- **BS-08 — no defaults exist.** *Given* a freshly constructed `CostModel` with no calibration,
  *when* any tier is queried, *then* the query yields an absence, never a number. `[PLC1-REF-05]`
- **BS-09 — tampered artefact refuses.** *Given* a calibration artefact whose recorded digest does
  not match its content, *when* it is loaded, *then* loading fails naming the file, and any
  previously loaded calibration is **not** used as a fallback. `[PLC1-REF-04]`
- **BS-10 — missing provenance field refuses.** *Given* an artefact omitting `sampleCount`, *when*
  it is loaded, *then* loading fails naming the missing field. `[PLC1-REF-04]`, `[PLC1-PROV-03]`
- **BS-11 — synthetic mode cannot produce guidance.** *Given* exploratory mode with a synthetic
  scalar, *when* two candidate placements are simulated, *then* the record contains both
  candidates' aggregates, carries the synthetic marking, and contains **no** comparative
  recommendation. `[PLC1-REF-06]`, `[PLC1-REF-07]`, `[PLC1-RES-06]`
- **BS-12 — the synthetic marking is not removable.** *Given* a synthetic run record, *when* it is
  serialized, reloaded, filtered, and merged with a non-synthetic record, *then* the synthetic
  marking is present in every derived artefact. `[PLC1-REF-06]`
- **BS-13 — stale calibration is marked.** *Given* a calibration artefact recorded at a revision
  that is not an ancestor of the revision under simulation, *when* a run executes, *then* the
  record is marked stale and names both revisions. `[PLC1-REF-08]`, `[PLC1-RES-07]`
- **BS-14 — thin sample refuses.** *Given* a scalar with a sample count below the configured
  bound, *when* a run requires it, *then* the run is refused naming the scalar and the bound.
  `[PLC1-REF-09]`
- **BS-15 — an uninstrumented findings file is not a cost source.** *Given* the V4-PILOT findings
  as input, *when* it is offered as a calibration artefact, *then* it is rejected as a cost source
  while remaining accepted as a topology input. `[PLC1-REF-10]`
- **BS-16 — replay against a different calibration refuses.** *Given* a run record, *when* it is
  replayed against a calibration artefact with a different digest, *then* the replay is refused.
  `[PLC1-RUN-05]`

### Fidelity and feasibility boundaries

- **BS-17 — colour infeasibility is not a cost.** *Given* a candidate placing a suspending cell on
  a blocking host, *when* it is evaluated, *then* the verdict is infeasible with the colour rule
  named, and no cost aggregate is reported for it. `[PLC1-MOD-01]`
- **BS-18 — quota infeasibility is not a cost.** *Given* a candidate exceeding an ancestor's
  subtree quota, *when* it is evaluated, *then* the verdict is infeasible naming the ancestor.
  `[PLC1-MOD-02]`
- **BS-19 — disjoint interests form no link.** *Given* two instances of one logical cell with
  disjoint hash-slot interests, *when* the mesh is simulated, *then* no gossip link is modelled
  between them and no cross-instance traffic is costed. This mirrors the kernel behaviour the
  concord scenario `concord/corpus/42-replication/42-INTEREST-01.yaml` already pins.
  `[PLC1-MOD-03]`
- **BS-20 — emissions are interest-filtered before costing.** *Given* two instances with partially
  overlapping interests, *when* deltas outside the overlap are emitted, *then* they contribute
  zero modelled remote cost. `[PLC1-MOD-04]`
- **BS-21 — determinism has no ambient inputs.** *Given* a fixed seed, *when* the same run
  executes under a deliberately perturbed environment (different available processors reported,
  different environment variables, different wall-clock), *then* the record is unchanged apart from
  the capture timestamp. `[PLC1-RUN-04]`
- **BS-22 — assumptions are enumerated.** *Given* any completed run, *when* the record is
  inspected, *then* every non-measured modelling assumption appears in an enumerated list.
  `[PLC1-RES-04]`

### Concord corpus impact — honest position

**None of BS-01..BS-22 belongs in `concord/corpus/`, and none should carry a `covers:` id.** Three
independent reasons, each sufficient:

1. Concord is the *implementation-neutral conformance suite for kernel semantics* — its scenarios
   describe what any ComputeNet implementation must do at runtime. `:sim` is an offline instrument;
   a second implementation of ComputeNet has no obligation to ship a simulator, so a `:sim`
   scenario is not a conformance statement.
2. `covers:` ids must be existing normative EARS ids (`concord/schema/provenance.md`; a dangling
   `covers:` fails `./gradlew :concord:check`). There are no `[3x-*]`/`[5x-*]` placement ids to
   cite, and PLC1 must not mint spec ids — `AGENTS.md` forbids editing plan/spec documents outside
   a documentation-maintenance task.
3. The corpus's schema has no vocabulary for cost, calibration, or provenance, and growing it "is
   a deliberate schema-change ticket between waves — not a corpus-authoring convenience"
   (`concord/schema/scenario.md`).

`BS-19` is the one scenario with a genuine kernel twin, and that twin **already exists** as
`42-INTEREST-01` (`covers: [42-INT-01]`). PLC1 should assert agreement with it, not duplicate it.

## 6. Scope boundaries

**Upstream (hard):**
- **BEN1** (`computenet-x9e`) creates `:bench` and the JMH harness. PLC1 does not create a
  benchmark harness and does not write JMH benchmarks.
- **BEN2** (unwired; being filed separately) supplies the macro sweeps and the G-43 fan-out
  re-baseline. **PLC1 may be implemented against BEN2's artefact schema, but no PLC1 guidance
  output is admissible until BEN2's measurements exist** — that is the plan's gate made
  operational by `[PLC1-REF-01]`/`[PLC1-REF-03]`. Implementers should expect to co-design the
  artefact schema with BEN2's owner.

**Downstream:** PLC2 (policy engine) consumes `SimulationResult` records. PLC1 emits no policy,
no recommendation ranking beyond raw comparable aggregates, and no decision.

**Explicitly out of scope:**
- Any change under `kernel/src/main` (`[PLC1-BND-04]`). PLC3 is the arc's only kernel item.
- Enforcement of anything, anywhere.
- The economic layer's *pricing* (G-62 / ECO1): identity-minting cost, per-`Principal` budgets,
  and Sybil economics belong to ECO1, which depends on DSC1 (`computenet-ssa`) and PLC2.
- Discovery and NAT (DSC2/DSC3), membrane disclosure (SEC1, `computenet-usd`).
- Editing `91-gap-analysis.md`, `CONCORDANCE.md`, or removing the G-61/G-62 gap markers. Marker
  removal happens when the gap is closed; PLC1 closes none of it.
- The multi-host `GraphSpec` replay driver itself (93 I-15) — PLC1 models it; PLC3/WKB-lane work
  builds it.

---

## 7. Suggested feature decomposition (list only — do not create these beads here)

- **F1 — `:sim` module skeleton.** New leaf module, `settings.gradle.kts` registration,
  `:sim → :kernel`/`:nature` only, empty test suite green, plus the architecture test asserting
  `:kernel` does not depend on `:sim`.
- **F2 — Cost vocabulary and provenance types.** `CostScalar`, `CostProvenance`, `CostModel`,
  `CalibrationSet`; the no-bare-literal API shape; `[PLC1-PROV-*]`, `[PLC1-REF-05]`.
- **F3 — Calibration artefact schema and loader.** Co-designed with BEN2; digest verification,
  field validation, staleness detection; `[PLC1-REF-04]`, `[PLC1-REF-08]`, `[PLC1-REF-09]`.
- **F4 — Refusal engine and synthetic mode.** The full `[PLC1-REF-*]` set including the
  non-removable synthetic marking; BS-05..BS-16.
- **F5 — Deterministic discrete-event core.** Seeded event loop, topology and workload model,
  feasibility rules (colour, quota, interest overlap, interest filtering); `[PLC1-RUN-*]`,
  `[PLC1-MOD-*]`.
- **F6 — Run record, serialization, and CLI.** `SimulationResult`, stable textual form, replay
  guard, `:sim:simulate` entry point; `[PLC1-RES-*]`.
- **F7 — V4-PILOT topology encoding and first findings.** Encode the pilot mesh; write
  `doc/placement/findings.md` with the shape observations and the enumerated modelling
  assumptions; `[PLC1-MOD-07]`, `[PLC1-RES-04]`.
- **F8 — Validation pass against BEN2 (runs after BEN2 lands).** Compare modelled aggregates with
  measured macro sweeps; report residual error as a quantity; do **not** assert a bound
  (`[PLC1-NV-02]`).

---

## 8. Verification

```bash
./gradlew :sim:test                                   # the epic's own suite (BS-01..BS-22)
./gradlew :sim:test --tests 'civictech.sim.RefusalTest'      # the §4.2 core
./gradlew :sim:test --tests 'civictech.sim.DeterminismTest'  # the §4.3 core
./gradlew :kernel:test                                # unchanged — PLC1 must not touch it
./gradlew :gen:test                                   # generator regressions surface here
./gradlew :concord:test                               # corpus scenario/covers counts unchanged
./gradlew :concord:concordance                        # CONCORDANCE.md must regenerate identically
./gradlew test                                        # repository-wide gate
```

Expected deltas: one new module and its tests; **zero** changes under `kernel/`, `nature/`,
`gen/`, `wire/`, `concord/`, `demo/`; `settings.gradle.kts` gains `include(":sim")`; a new
`doc/placement/findings.md`. No generated or build output in the diff.

---

## 9. Risks and open questions

1. **The BEN2 co-design risk (highest).** PLC1 owns the artefact *parser*; BEN2 owns the artefact
   *writer*. If they are designed independently the schema will be wrong on both sides. Mitigation:
   F3 is explicitly a joint feature; land the schema before either side's implementation, and
   accept that PLC1 may sit at F1–F2 until BEN2's shape is agreed. **This risk is the reason the
   plan gates PLC1 on BEN2 rather than merely ordering them.**
2. **Refusal ergonomics vs. refusal integrity.** A simulator that refuses everything is unusable
   during development; the escape hatch is `[PLC1-REF-06]`'s synthetic mode. The risk is that
   synthetic mode becomes the default path and the marking becomes noise. Mitigation: BS-11/BS-12
   test the *consequences* of the marking, not just its presence; and `[PLC1-RES-06]` makes the
   marking load-bearing rather than cosmetic.
3. **Model/kernel divergence.** `[PLC1-MOD-03]`/`[PLC1-MOD-04]` require the simulator's
   link-formation to agree with `Replication.maybeLink`. That agreement is asserted by
   construction today and will drift. Open question: should F5 derive the model from the kernel's
   own `Interest.overlaps` (a compile dependency on a kernel function, which is allowed) rather
   than reimplementing it? **Preference: yes, reuse** — `AGENTS.md` says "Search before adding a
   new abstraction."
4. **KX ordering.** KX (`computenet-iyi`) reshapes `LocationRegistry`. PLC1 reads only its
   location half, which C-13 keeps in place, but the import surface changes. Low risk; note it and
   re-check after KX merges.
5. **Which quantities BEN1 actually produces.** BEN1's stated measurements are per-operator delta
   throughput, fan-out scaling, and per-cell footprint. `[41-LOC-01]`'s three tiers are not
   literally those three quantities. Open question for F3: is the direct-call/queue-hop delta
   derivable from BEN1's fusion instrumentation (§R5's "instrument fusion wins") or does it need
   its own BEN1/BEN2 benchmark? **This should be resolved before F5, and the answer belongs in
   `doc/placement/findings.md`.**
6. **Discrete-event fidelity vs. effort.** A queueing-network approximation is far cheaper than a
   faithful event simulation and may be sufficient for the comparisons PLC2 needs. Open question
   for F5; whichever is chosen, `[PLC1-RES-04]` forces the choice into every run record.
7. **`[PLC1-NV-01]` is a real hole.** Provenance is an audit trail, not a proof. If PLC2 or a
   later reader starts treating a provenance record as evidence of measurement, that claim belongs
   in `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md`.

# PLC1 design notes

## Module decision (justified in description §2.1)

New leaf Gradle module `sim/` (`:sim`), registered in `settings.gradle.kts` beside `:wire` and
`:inspect`. **No code under `kernel/`.** Dependency direction `:sim → :kernel`, `:sim → :nature`;
`:kernel` must NOT depend on `:sim` (asserted by a test, not just convention). Deliberately **no
compile dependency on `:bench`**: costs enter as a serialized measurement artefact so that there is
exactly one channel by which a cost can enter the simulator, and that channel is one that must
carry provenance to parse at all. That single-channel property is what makes `[PLC1-REF-01]`
enforceable rather than aspirational.

## Seams that already exist and should be reused, not re-invented

- `civictech.nature.Color` / `CellDescriptor.color` —
  `nature/src/main/kotlin/civictech/nature/ContractDescriptor.kt:107` and `:294`.
- Spawn-time colour rule and G-28 subtree quota walk —
  `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/ManagedHost.kt:910-938`. These are *feasibility*
  constraints, not costs.
- `InstanceSpec(interest, instanceId, placement, journalId, frontierPolicy)` and
  `InstanceSetStep.lower()` — `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/graph/GraphDsl.kt`. The
  `placement` field is already "a host-selector hint (recorded, routed by the multi-host replay
  driver — 93 I-15, **driver unbuilt**)". Reuse this vocabulary; do not invent a second one.
- `civictech.cell.link.Interest` + `Replication.maybeLink` overlap rule — prefer calling the
  kernel's own `Interest` predicate over reimplementing overlap in `:sim`.
- `LocationRegistry.Local` / `Remote` — `kernel/.../host/LocationRegistry.kt`. These two are the
  boundary between `[41-LOC-01]`'s second and third cost tiers.
- `GraphSpec` / `lowered()` — `GraphDsl.kt:232`. Scenario input format; read, never applied.

## Ordering constraints that must not be broken

- **BEN1 → BEN2 → PLC1.** The plan's deliberate ordering: "PLC1 gated on BEN2: no simulating
  against fictional costs." F1–F2 may proceed before BEN2 exists; F3 must be co-designed with
  BEN2's artefact writer; no guidance output is admissible before BEN2's measurements exist.
- **PLC1 → PLC2 → PLC3.** PLC1 produces comparability, PLC2 produces policy, PLC3 enforces. Do not
  short-circuit: a PLC1 that emits a placement decision has taken PLC2's job, and a PLC1 that
  touches `spawnBound` has taken PLC3's.
- **Kernel lane (G-63) is not entered here.** PLC1 adds no node to the kernel SCC. Only PLC3 does.

## KX interaction

KX (`computenet-iyi`) splits `LocationRegistry` into registry + `InstanceIndex` + `DeliveryHold`
(C-13). PLC1 must import only the *location* half (`location`, `Local`, `Remote`, `instancesOf`),
which C-13's resolution keeps in the registry proper — not `interests`/`setInterest` or the
repartition hold, which move. Re-check imports after KX merges.

## Known-unverifiable claims (recorded up front, per AGENTS.md honesty rule)

- `[PLC1-NV-01]` Provenance is an audit trail, not proof of measurement. Well-formed artefacts
  containing invented numbers remain constructible from inside `:bench`. If a downstream consumer
  starts treating provenance as evidence, that belongs in `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md`.
- `[PLC1-NV-02]` No `:sim` test can establish model accuracy; F8 reports residual error against
  BEN2 and asserts no bound.
- `[PLC1-NV-03]` `[PLC1-REF-09]`'s admissibility bounds are configured policy, justified but not
  derived.

## Concord position

Nothing from this epic enters `concord/corpus/`. `:sim` is offline and not a conformance surface;
there are no `[3x-*]`/`[5x-*]` placement EARS ids to `covers:`; and the scenario schema has no
cost/provenance vocabulary (growing it is a gated schema-change ticket). BS-19 asserts agreement
with the existing `42-INTEREST-01` scenario rather than duplicating it.

## Deliberate non-goals restated for implementers

No policy, no ranking beyond raw comparable aggregates, no enforcement, no kernel change, no
pricing/budgets (ECO1), no discovery (DSC2/DSC3), no gap-marker removal, no spec or plan edits.
Findings go to a new append-only `doc/placement/findings.md` per the plan's §6 hygiene rule.
