# DSC2 design notes

## Why this is an epic and not a feature

Sizing rule check. DSC2 carries **four independent novel mechanisms**, each with its own failure
model, and none reducible to the others:

1. a self-authenticating signed record format with epochs, validity windows, and a canonical
   encoding (new serialization surface, new replay/supersession semantics);
2. an mDNS/DNS-SD network binding (new protocol, new dependency decision, new privacy posture,
   new class of malformed hostile input);
3. a rendezvous directory realized as a ComputeNet cell plus its client (new contract, new
   runnable process, new availability and trust story);
4. a dial policy that must hold "one peering per identity" under simultaneous dial, partition,
   reconnect, endpoint change, and an existing manual peering.

Plus a new Gradle module, an integration into two demo composition roots, and an equivalence proof
against the hand-wired path. That is weeks of work and multiple review boundaries — `epic` is
correct. Filing it as a feature would force the mDNS decision, the rendezvous trust model, and the
dial-race tie-break into one unreviewable diff.

## Module decision

New Gradle leaf module `discover/` (`:discover`), registered in `settings.gradle.kts` beside
`:wire` and `:identity`.

```
:identity  -> :kernel                    (DSC1: PeerId derivation, sign/verify, key store)
:discover  -> :kernel, :identity         (+ an mDNS dependency, see open question 1)
:wire      -> :kernel, :identity         (unchanged)
:kernel    -> nothing new                (MUST NOT depend on :discover)
:discover  -X-> :wire                    (forbidden; the dialer is an injected function)
```

The dial inversion is the load-bearing part: `PeerBook` takes `dial: (PeerEndpoint) -> AutoCloseable`
and the composition root passes `WsTransport::connect`. Consequences: `:discover` is testable with
no socket, a second transport reuses discovery unchanged, and transport selection stays where
`Peering.Side` is already constructed (`demo/shopping/.../Main.kt:234`).

## Seams that already exist and must be reused, not re-invented

| Need | Existing seam |
|---|---|
| Derive/verify a peer identity | `:identity` fingerprint + verifier — **DSC1**, `computenet-ssa` §2.2 |
| Sign/verify a record canonically | `:identity` canonical encoding — DSC1 `[DSC1-ANN-03]` |
| Allowlist | `Peering.Side.allow` / `Side.admits` (`kernel/.../wire/Peering.kt:115-124`) — one list, on derived ids |
| Dial | `WsTransport.connect(uri, side, backoff)` (`wire/.../WsTransport.kt:72`) |
| Retry-until-reachable idiom | `WsTransport.awaitReachable` (`WsTransport.kt:79-89`) |
| Backoff shape | `WsTransport.DEFAULT_RECONNECT_BACKOFF` (`WsTransport.kt:44`) |
| A management contract to model `PeerDirectory` on | `RegistryAnnounce` (`Peering.kt:25-37`) — `@Contract(management = true)`, push-only |
| App-defined wire types without kernel edits | `cell.wire.WireSerializers`, ServiceLoader (40/41 point 1) |
| Rejection observability | `ManagedHost.deadLetterOutlet`, `DeadLetters`, `Session.preHelloDrops` idiom |
| Deterministic multi-peer harness | `testkit` `SimWorld`/`awaitUntil`; `Peering.loopback` (`Peering.kt:154`) |

## The ordering constraint that must not be broken

Plan §5: **"DSC1 before DSC2/DSC3: identity before discovery."** Enforced in the requirement set,
not merely asserted: `[DSC2-ID-01..06]` make DSC1's derived `PeerId` the *only* naming scheme and
make a record a hint that grants no authority. A discovery source is untrusted by construction —
the record is self-authenticating, and the DSC1 authenticated hello is the final arbiter
(`[DSC1-HELLO-04..07]`). Any implementer tempted to add a "friendly name", a rendezvous-issued
handle, or a hostname-keyed cache is re-opening G-29 one layer up.

`RegistryMirrorCell.peer`'s four-step happens-before argument (`Peering.kt:59-92`) must survive
discovery-driven dials, including the simultaneous-dial case; re-derive it in KDoc if the sequence
changes.

## Upstream normative citation status (honest)

`doc/spec/40-distribution/43-security.md` has **no `[43-*]` EARS ids** (re-verified by grep), and
`doc/spec/` has **no normative discovery text at all** — no mDNS, no rendezvous, no bootstrap, no
peer discovery; `95-research-plan.md` has no R-entry for it either. DSC2 therefore cites no
normative id it makes true. Adjacent ids that must keep holding: `[41-LOC-01]`, `[42-REPL-05]`.
Promoting stabilized `[DSC2-*]` ids into a future `44-discovery.md` is spec-maintenance work,
explicitly out of scope.

## Known-unverifiable claims (recorded up front, per AGENTS.md honesty rule)

- Real-LAN mDNS behaviour (`[DSC2-NV-01]`) — a loopback test proves encoding and wiring only.
- Eclipse resistance (`[DSC2-NV-02]`) — signed records defeat forgery, never omission.
- Sybil bounds (`[DSC2-NV-03]`) — minting is still free; that cost is ECO1's.
- Reachability (`[DSC2-NV-04]`) — that is DSC3's whole subject.
- Advertisement metadata disclosure (`[DSC2-NV-05]`) — mitigated by off-by-default only.

These belong in `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` if and only if a corpus requirement is ever written
against them. They must never be softened into passing tests.

## Deliberate non-goals restated for implementers

Identity primitives (DSC1), reachability/NAT/relay (DSC3), membership/election/failure detection
(MEM1/MEM2), budgets and minting cost (ECO1), `BoundaryPolicy` and moderation (SEC1), DHT/gossip
peer exchange, `PeerId` type change, `WsTransport` reconnect-semantics rewrite, inspector UI.
acceptance_criteria: Requirement ids are defined in the description §4 (EARS) and scenarios in §5. Done when: (1) §4.1 [DSC2-REC-01..08] hold — self-signed PeerRecord, deterministic canonical encoding, signature-then-derivation verification before any field is used, validity window and epoch supersession; (2) §4.2 [DSC2-ID-01..06] hold — DSC1's derived PeerId is the ONLY naming scheme, no second allowlist or trust store, a record grants no AuthLevel, and a hello whose id differs from the advertised id closes the connection; (3) §4.3 [DSC2-MDNS-01..09] hold — advertise/browse/withdraw, both halves off by default, no multicast socket when disabled, malformed input discarded and counted, bounded candidate state, tolerant of no multicast interface; (4) §4.4 [DSC2-RDV-01..09] hold — registration over an ordinary authenticated peering, every served record re-verified by the receiver, rendezvous holds no signing authority, unavailability degrades to retained records plus LAN, multi-rendezvous union, replayed/withdrawn records lose to the higher epoch; (5) §4.5 [DSC2-DIAL-01..11] hold — at most one peering per PeerId across all sources, allowlist and self excluded, endpoint fallback and capped backoff, deterministic simultaneous-dial tie-break, re-dial after close, injected dialer and injected clock; (6) §4.6 [DSC2-OBS-01..06] hold — every discard observable with a machine-distinguishable reason, no silent drops, counters exposed, no key material or signature bytes in logs; (7) §4.7 [DSC2-NEU-01..07] hold — :kernel free of :discover, :discover free of :wire, WireCodec.VERSION unchanged, a discovered graph observationally indistinguishable from the hand-wired graph ([41-LOC-01]), unconfigured behaviour unchanged, PeerBook exercisable with no socket, no host scheduler thread used; # BB-TPCH — Incremental TPC-H (DBToaster framing: 22 queries maintained under RF1/RF2 streams)

Lane: benchmark-bridge (BB), `lane:benchmark`. Parent: BB umbrella epic (computenet-3xi).
Source: `computenet-milestone-plan.md` §1 (BB-TPCH row), §3 (Incremental TPC-H row of the
kernel-enablement matrix), §5 rank 10 (QRY1 "gets a finish line" here) and rank 19, §6 standing
hygiene.

Depends on: **ORA1** (computenet-4ru — the batch-oracle differential tester, wired as `related`
because beads will not let a feature be blocked by an epic).
Unwired deps (ids being minted by other agents): **QRY1** (Datalog/relational frontend,
non-recursive — carries most of the weight; 22 queries by hand is the alternative), **KE1**
(tagged multiset deltas; RF2 deletions are the acid test), **KAGG-R** (multi-column ordered top-K
over rows, count-distinct). Soft dep on **BEN1** for the `:bench` module.

---

## 1. Ambition / Why

TPC-H run *incrementally* — the DBToaster framing, where the 22 queries are **maintained** as
views under the refresh streams RF1 (new orders/lineitems) and RF2 (deletes) rather than executed
once over a static snapshot — is the sharpest available test of the single claim ComputeNet makes
about itself: that it is an incremental dataflow runtime whose operators are retraction-correct
through arbitrary depth.

Three properties make it the right instrument.

**It is a deletion benchmark disguised as a query benchmark.** RF1 is easy; every incremental
system handles inserts. RF2 deletes ~0.1% of orders and their lineitems, and those deletions must
propagate through multi-way join chains, through aggregates, through top-K orderings, and arrive
at the right answer. §3 of the milestone plan says it plainly: "RF2's deletions propagating
through multi-join chains **is the acceptance property**". Nothing else in the repository stresses
the retraction path at that depth. `Aggregator.kt`'s `Extremum`/`TopK` carry a full support
multiset precisely because "retraction of the current extremum must reshuffle without a re-scan" —
TPC-H Q2, Q10, Q18 and Q21 are what prove that comment true or false at scale.

**It has a real oracle, and we already have the oracle machinery.** TPC-H's queries have exact
defined answers, and ORA1 is a batch-oracle differential tester built over the operator algebra.
BB-TPCH is that tester pointed at a published, adversarially-designed workload instead of at
random graphs. Correctness-against-reference is therefore a hard requirement here, not an
aspiration.

**It is QRY1's finish line.** §5 rank 10 says QRY1 "starts once ORA1 is usable as oracle; BB-TPCH
gives it a finish line", and §1 says BB-TPCH "becomes QRY1's acceptance corpus". A relational
frontend with no external workload tends to grow toward whatever its author's tests demand.
Twenty-two queries written by someone else, that the frontend did not get to choose, is the
discipline. That is why this feature exists as a separate artifact rather than as tests inside
QRY1: the corpus must be able to *fail* QRY1.

Per §6, the product is findings. "Q21 cannot be expressed without correlated existential
subqueries and here is the missing surface" is a better outcome than a throughput chart.

---

## 2. What we build

### 2.1 In `:bench`

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `bench/src/main/kotlin/civictech/bench/tpch/TpchSchema.kt` | The eight tables (`Part`, `Supplier`, `PartSupp`, `Customer`, `Orders`, `Lineitem`, `Nation`, `Region`) as `Serializable` row types with the published column shapes. |
| `bench/src/main/kotlin/civictech/bench/tpch/TpchGenerator.kt` | Deterministic seeded dbgen-equivalent at small scale factors, plus the RF1 and RF2 refresh-stream generators. Fidelity to the published distributions is a requirement (`[BB-TPCH-01]`); byte-compatibility with `dbgen` is not. |
| `bench/src/main/kotlin/civictech/bench/tpch/queries/` | One entry per query, `Q01.kt` … `Q22.kt`. Each is either a QRY1 query expression or, where QRY1 is absent or the query is inexpressible, a hand-built graph or an explicit `not-expressible` record. |
| `bench/src/main/kotlin/civictech/bench/tpch/TpchReference.kt` | The oracle: a naive batch recompute of each query over the current logical table contents. Deliberately obviously-correct, no incremental cleverness, shares ORA1's comparison discipline. |
| `bench/src/main/kotlin/civictech/bench/tpch/RefreshStream.kt` | RF1/RF2 application against the ingress path, with per-refresh quiescence and comparison hooks. |
| `bench/src/main/kotlin/civictech/bench/tpch/TpchRun.kt` | Run protocol, record type, metadata capture, findings rendering. |
| `bench/src/jmh/kotlin/civictech/bench/tpch/` | `@Benchmark` bodies behind `:bench:jmh`. |
| `bench/src/test/kotlin/civictech/bench/tpch/` | Fast correctness tests at scale factor ≈ 0.001 — the *maintenance-correctness* suite, which is the part that must run in the default lane. |

### 2.2 Outside `:bench`

- `doc/bench/findings.md` — append-only lane findings; the only file outside `:bench` this feature
  writes.
- Nothing in `kernel/`, `gen/`, `wire/`, `concord/`, `demo/`, `doc/spec/`. In particular: when a
  query is inexpressible, the fix belongs in QRY1 or in a kernel chunk, filed as a finding — never
  patched from `bench/`.

### 2.3 Query coverage is staged, and partial coverage is a complete result

The 22 queries are not equally reachable. The feature's coverage ladder:

- **Tier 1** — selection/projection/aggregation and simple joins (Q1, Q3, Q5, Q6, Q10, Q12, Q14,
  Q19): expressible on today's operator family plus KE1.
- **Tier 2** — correlated subqueries, `EXISTS`/`NOT EXISTS`, nested aggregates (Q2, Q4, Q11, Q15,
  Q16, Q17, Q18, Q20, Q21, Q22): need QRY1's expression layer and KAGG-R's residuals
  (count-distinct, multi-column ordered top-K).
- **Tier 3** — anything that turns out to require recursion, windowing, or a surface no chunk owns:
  recorded as `not-expressible` with the missing surface named. **This is a deliverable, not a
  failure.**

---

## 3. How, using ComputeNet

### 3.1 Already in the kernel — DO NOT REBUILD

- **Retraction-aware aggregation.** `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/Aggregator.kt` —
  `Aggregators.count()`, `sumOf`, `avgOf`, `minOf`, `maxOf`, `topK(k, selector)`,
  `collectToSet()`. `minOf`/`maxOf`/`topK` already keep the **full support multiset**
  (`TreeMap<V, Int>`) so that retracting the current extremum reshuffles without a re-scan, and
  `TopK`'s KDoc already states that bounded-memory top-k is unsound under retractions. **Do not
  write an aggregate.** What is genuinely missing (count-distinct; multi-column ordered top-K over
  *rows* rather than a single selected value) is KAGG-R's job, not this feature's.
- **The join family.** `data/op/JoinSetCell.kt` (`joinSet`, `crossProduct`),
  `data/op/LookupJoinCell.kt`, `data/op/SemiJoinCell.kt`, `data/op/KeyedBinarySetJoin.kt`,
  `data/op/JoinLedger.kt`, and the outer-join builders in
  `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/graph/RelationalGraphs.kt` (`leftJoin`, `rightJoin`,
  `fullJoin`). Antijoin/semijoin are the `EXISTS`/`NOT EXISTS` substrate. **Do not write a join.**
- **Grouping.** `data/op/GroupByCell.kt` and `GroupByCell.global(...)`, plus
  `data/op/MergeableGroupByCell.kt` for the partitioned case. `[24-OP-GROUPBY-03]` already gives
  per-delta operator atomicity: all groups touched by one input delta emit as one `MapDelta` under
  that input's wave id.
- **Tagged multiset deltas.** `data/delta/TaggedMapDelta.kt`, `data/delta/TagState.kt`,
  `data/OrMapCell.kt`, `data/op/TaggedSetOperator.kt`. KE1 extends this class; BB-TPCH consumes it.
  **Do not write a multiset representation.**
- **Set algebra and graph assembly.** `graph/GraphDsl.kt`, `graph/SetAlgebraGraphs.kt`
  (`filter`/`count`/`intersect`/`union`), `graph/TypedRef.kt`; `data/op/FilterCell.kt`,
  `data/op/FlatMapSetCell.kt` + `mapSet`, `civictech/cell/MapperCell.kt`,
  `data/op/UnionSetCell.kt`, `data/op/IntersectSetCell.kt`, `data/op/CountCell.kt`.
- **Wave-scoped sealing.** `data/op/WaveGate.kt` and `[24-OP-SEMIJOIN-04]`'s opt-in per-wave seal.
  Relevant because `[24-OP-OUTERJOIN-02]` explicitly *permits* an observable transient overlap —
  which is why `[BB-TPCH-24]` below distinguishes a transient from a wrong answer.
- **The differential-testing discipline.** ORA1's batch-oracle tester is the pattern
  `TpchReference` follows; reuse its comparison and shrinking conventions rather than inventing a
  second dialect.
- **Drive and observation.** `testkit/.../SimWorld.kt` (`runToIdle`), `AwaitUntil.kt`,
  `host/SimulationController.kt`, `host/ManagedHost.kt`; `civictech/cell/observe/Observe.kt`,
  `observe/AlignedObserve.kt` (`observeAligned`).

### 3.2 What BB-TPCH legitimately adds

The schema, the generator (base data + RF1 + RF2), the 22 query definitions, the batch reference,
and the run/report protocol. If QRY1 is present, the query definitions are QRY1 expressions and
this feature writes almost no graph-assembly code at all — which is the intended end state.

---

## 4. Scope boundaries

- **Not a TPC-H audit.** No `QphH@Size`, no price/performance metric, no compliance claim, no
  refresh-function timing rules from the official spec's execution model. This is the DBToaster
  *incremental-view-maintenance* framing, and the record must say so.
- **No kernel/wire/gen/concord/demo/spec edits.** An inexpressible query or a missing operator
  surface is a finding or a pulled KAGG-R/KE1/QRY1 trigger — never solved in-lane.
- **No `concord/corpus/` scenarios.** Benchmark numbers are machine-dependent and therefore not
  implementation-neutral; BB-TPCH adds none. (The maintenance-correctness assertions live in
  `:bench`'s own test source set, where they can name machine-independent *equalities* without
  becoming conformance scenarios.)
- **No performance targets.** No requirement below asserts or accepts a number as a pass
  condition.
- **No recursive queries.** Anything requiring QRY2/KE5 is out; record it as `not-expressible`.
- **Large scale factors are optional.** Correctness at SF≈0.001–0.01 is the obligation;
  SF 1 and above is a measurement nicety and may be skipped without failing the feature.

---

## 5. Functional requirements (EARS)

### Ubiquitous

- **[BB-TPCH-01]** The harness shall implement the TPC-H schema, the 22 query definitions, and the
  RF1/RF2 refresh-function semantics as published, and shall name the specification revision it
  targets in every recorded run.
- **[BB-TPCH-02]** The harness shall state, in every recorded run, that it measures **incremental
  view maintenance** in the DBToaster framing and not TPC-H's audited execution model, and shall
  name no TPC-H compliance metric.
- **[BB-TPCH-03]** The harness shall reside entirely under `bench/`, and no module outside
  `:bench` shall depend on it.
- **[BB-TPCH-04]** The generator shall be deterministic: the same seed and scale factor shall
  produce identical base tables and identical RF1/RF2 streams on every run and every machine.
- **[BB-TPCH-05]** Each query shall be expressed either as a QRY1 query expression or, where QRY1
  is unavailable, as a graph assembled from existing kernel operator cells (§3.1); in neither case
  shall `:bench` reimplement an operator's semantics.
- **[BB-TPCH-06]** Every recorded run shall record: harness commit SHA; seed and scale factor;
  query id and tier; whether the query came from QRY1 or from hand assembly; refresh-stream length
  and RF1/RF2 ordering; JVM vendor and version; heap; machine CPU model, core count and OS;
  scheduler; durability mode; JMH parameters; and observed variance.
- **[BB-TPCH-07]** The harness shall report insert-driven (RF1) and delete-driven (RF2)
  maintenance cost separately for every query, and shall never present a blended figure.
- **[BB-TPCH-08]** The harness shall record, per query, the retained intermediate state — join
  ledger sizes, group counts, tag-state size — because state retained by view maintenance is a
  first-class result of an IVM benchmark.
- **[BB-TPCH-09]** The harness shall keep the maintenance-correctness tests at small scale inside
  the default `./gradlew test` lane, with all measurement behind BEN1's `@Tag("bench")` gate and
  `:bench:jmh`.
- **[BB-TPCH-10]** The harness shall publish a per-query coverage table stating, for each of the 22
  queries, its tier, its expression route, and its current status (`verified`, `blocked`,
  `not-expressible`).

### Event-driven

- **[BB-TPCH-11]** When a refresh (RF1 or RF2) has been applied and the graph reaches quiescence,
  the harness shall compare each maintained query's observed result against
  `TpchReference`'s batch recompute over the current logical table contents, and record the
  outcome.
- **[BB-TPCH-12]** When a maintained result differs from the reference answer after quiescence,
  the harness shall report the query as **failed**, shall record the differing rows, and shall
  record no maintenance-cost figure for that query.
- **[BB-TPCH-13]** When an RF2 deletion is applied, the harness shall verify that every derived row
  transitively depending on the deleted order or lineitem has been retracted from every maintained
  view that contained it, and shall record any surviving derived row as a failure.
- **[BB-TPCH-14]** When a query cannot be expressed on the surfaces available at run time, the
  harness shall record it as **not-expressible**, name the specific missing surface (operator,
  aggregate, or QRY1 expression form), and shall not substitute an approximation that changes the
  query's answer.
- **[BB-TPCH-15]** When a suite run hits a wall, the harness's operator shall write a dated entry
  to `doc/bench/findings.md` naming the wall either as a **candidate G-item** (gap-table column
  shape, id left `G-NN`) or as the **existing trigger it pulls**, and shall not close the wall in
  this lane.
- **[BB-TPCH-16]** When the full refresh stream has been applied, the harness shall additionally
  compare the final maintained state against a from-scratch batch computation over the final table
  contents, so that maintenance drift over a long stream is detected independently of per-refresh
  checks.

### State-driven

- **[BB-TPCH-17]** While QRY1 is unavailable, the harness shall express only Tier 1 queries by hand
  and shall record every Tier 2 query as **blocked**, naming QRY1 — hand-writing all 22 graphs is
  explicitly not this feature's plan.
- **[BB-TPCH-18]** While KE1's tagged multiset delta class is unavailable, the harness shall record
  every query whose correctness depends on multiset (bag) semantics as **blocked**, naming KE1,
  rather than silently running it under set semantics.
- **[BB-TPCH-19]** While KAGG-R's residuals (count-distinct, multi-column ordered top-K over rows)
  are unavailable, the harness shall record the queries requiring them as **blocked**, naming
  KAGG-R.
- **[BB-TPCH-20]** While a run is driven by `SimulationController` or `SimWorld.runToIdle`, the
  harness shall report no wall-clock latency figure and shall present maintenance cost as work per
  refresh, not as elapsed time.
- **[BB-TPCH-21]** While durability is enabled with synchronous WAL, the harness shall label
  refresh-application figures **WAL-bound**.

### Unwanted behaviour

- **[BB-TPCH-22]** If a maintained view's result matches the reference only after a full
  recomputation is triggered, then the harness shall record the run as **not incremental** and
  shall state which operator forced the recomputation.
- **[BB-TPCH-23]** If retained intermediate state grows monotonically across a refresh stream that
  applies equal numbers of inserts and deletes, then the harness shall record a state-reclamation
  finding naming the growing structure (join ledger, tag state, aggregate support multiset), and
  shall not treat the growth as an implementation detail.
- **[BB-TPCH-24]** If an observed difference from the reference answer is confined to a transient
  the spec explicitly permits — notably `[24-OP-OUTERJOIN-02]`'s permitted overlap of `(a, null)`
  and `(a, b)` — then the harness shall re-observe after quiescence before declaring failure, and
  shall record that a permitted transient was observed; if the difference survives quiescence,
  `[BB-TPCH-12]` applies unchanged.
- **[BB-TPCH-25]** If a floating-point aggregate would make the comparison order-sensitive, then
  the harness shall compare using the exact decimal semantics TPC-H specifies for that column, and
  shall not adopt a tolerance in order to pass.
- **[BB-TPCH-26]** If run-to-run variance exceeds the harness's declared threshold, then the run
  shall be marked **unreportable** and the variance recorded in place of a mean.
- **[BB-TPCH-27]** If a query's reference comparison is skipped, then the query's result shall be
  marked **unverified** and no downstream document shall cite it.
- **[BB-TPCH-28]** If a row type entering a query graph would carry an `Owned` or `Leased` payload,
  then graph construction shall fail, because a benchmark ingest path must never be one on which an
  exclusive can be dropped.
- **[BB-TPCH-29]** If findings would require editing `doc/spec/90-roadmap/91-gap-analysis.md` or
  `doc/spec/CONCORDANCE.md`, then the operator shall write to `doc/bench/findings.md` instead and
  leave both files untouched.
- **[BB-TPCH-30]** If a figure would be compared against a published DBToaster or other IVM result,
  then the record shall first state scale factor, semantics (set versus multiset), query coverage,
  and every deviation, and shall refuse the comparison if coverage differs materially.

### Optional feature

- **[BB-TPCH-31]** Where ORA1's differential tester is available, the harness shall run the TPC-H
  query graphs as ORA1 subjects with randomised refresh interleavings, and shall report any
  discovered failing seed **without replacing it with a friendlier seed**.
- **[BB-TPCH-32]** Where KBLK's bulk/benchmark host mode is available, the harness shall load base
  tables through the batched ingress path and shall record the load configuration separately from
  refresh figures.
- **[BB-TPCH-33]** Where a query has a published reference answer for a given scale factor and
  seed, the harness shall additionally check against that published answer and record the check as
  distinct from its own batch recompute.
- **[BB-TPCH-34]** Where the graph is partitioned across shards, the harness shall record per-shard
  and aggregate maintenance figures separately and shall state the key-range assignment.

### Complex

- **[BB-TPCH-35]** When RF2 deletes an order, while that order participates in a multi-way join
  chain feeding a top-K aggregate, the harness shall verify that the retraction reaches the top-K
  and that a previously-evicted value can re-enter the result, since `Aggregators.topK` keeps the
  full support precisely for this case.
- **[BB-TPCH-36]** When RF1 and RF2 are interleaved within one refresh batch, if the resulting
  wave ordering makes an intermediate observation inconsistent, then the harness shall compare only
  after quiescence and shall record that an intra-batch inconsistency was observed, naming the
  operator at which it appeared.
- **[BB-TPCH-37]** When a query is expressed through QRY1, if QRY1's plan differs from the hand
  assembly the harness would otherwise build, then the harness shall record both routes' results
  and shall report any disagreement as a QRY1 defect finding rather than adjusting either side.
- **[BB-TPCH-38]** When the coverage table reports fewer than 22 verified queries, the harness's
  result shall still be reportable, provided every unverified query carries a named cause per
  `[BB-TPCH-14]`, `[BB-TPCH-17]`, `[BB-TPCH-18]` or `[BB-TPCH-19]` — partial coverage with named
  causes is a complete outcome; partial coverage with silent omissions is not.

---

## 6. Behaviour specifications

**BS-1 — Generator and refresh-stream determinism (`[BB-TPCH-04]`)**
*Given* a seed and scale factor 0.001,
*when* base tables and RF1/RF2 streams are generated twice in-process and once in a fresh JVM,
*then* all three are element-wise identical, including refresh ordering.

**BS-2 — Q6 maintained equals batch (`[BB-TPCH-11]`)**
*Given* Q6 maintained over base tables at SF 0.001,
*when* an RF1 batch is applied and the graph quiesces,
*then* the maintained scalar equals `TpchReference.q6(currentTables)` exactly under TPC-H's decimal
semantics.

**BS-3 — RF2 deletion reaches every derived row (`[BB-TPCH-13]`)**
*Given* Q3 (a three-way join with a grouped sum) maintained over base tables,
*when* RF2 deletes an order that contributes to three result groups,
*then* after quiescence no derived row referencing the deleted order key remains in any maintained
view, and the group values equal the reference.

**BS-4 — Retraction re-enters a top-K (`[BB-TPCH-35]`)**
*Given* Q10-style top-K over revenue with `k = 20` and a 25-customer support,
*when* RF2 deletes the orders of the current rank-1 customer,
*then* rank 21 enters the result, the result equals the reference exactly, and no re-scan of the
base tables was required to produce it.

**BS-5 — Non-incremental maintenance is named (`[BB-TPCH-22]`)**
*Given* a query whose graph contains an operator that recomputes from full state on retraction,
*when* an RF2 batch is applied,
*then* the run record carries `incremental = false` and names the operator, and the finding is
written.

**BS-6 — Monotone state growth is a finding (`[BB-TPCH-23]`)**
*Given* a refresh stream applying 10 000 inserts and 10 000 deletes in alternation,
*when* the stream completes and the graph quiesces,
*then* the recorded retained state is compared against its value at the start, and any monotone
growth produces a dated `doc/bench/findings.md` entry naming the growing structure.

**BS-7 — Long-stream drift check (`[BB-TPCH-16]`)**
*Given* a maintained query and a refresh stream of 100 batches,
*when* the stream completes,
*then* the maintained result equals a from-scratch batch computation over the final tables, not
only the last per-batch comparison.

**BS-8 — Permitted transient is not a failure (`[BB-TPCH-24]`)**
*Given* a query containing an outer join and a refresh that briefly exposes `(a, null)` and
`(a, b)` together,
*when* the harness observes mid-wave and then after quiescence,
*then* the mid-wave difference is recorded as a permitted transient, the post-quiescence result
equals the reference, and the query is not marked failed.

**BS-9 — Inexpressible is recorded, not approximated (`[BB-TPCH-14]`, `[BB-TPCH-38]`)**
*Given* Q21 (correlated `EXISTS`/`NOT EXISTS` over lineitem) with no QRY1 expression form for it,
*when* the coverage table is produced,
*then* Q21 is `not-expressible` with the missing surface named, the run remains reportable, and no
approximate variant of Q21 appears in `bench/`.

**BS-10 — No tolerance for decimals (`[BB-TPCH-25]`)**
*Given* Q1's aggregated sums and averages,
*when* the comparison runs,
*then* it compares exact decimal values, and a deliberately-introduced 1-ULP difference causes a
failure rather than passing under a tolerance.

**BS-11 — Blocked beats set-semantics substitution (`[BB-TPCH-18]`)**
*Given* a tree without KE1's tagged multiset deltas and a query whose answer depends on duplicate
rows,
*when* the query is requested,
*then* it is recorded `blocked` naming KE1, and no set-semantics variant is run or reported.

**BS-12 — QRY1 disagreement is a QRY1 finding (`[BB-TPCH-37]`)**
*Given* Q5 expressed both through QRY1 and by hand assembly,
*when* both are maintained over the same refresh stream,
*then* any disagreement between them is recorded as a QRY1 defect finding, and neither route is
adjusted to match the other.

**BS-13 — Failing seed is kept (`[BB-TPCH-31]`)**
*Given* an ORA1 differential run that discovers a refresh interleaving producing a wrong answer,
*when* the finding is written,
*then* the seed is recorded verbatim and appears in a named regression test; no substitute seed is
introduced.

---

## 7. Suggested task decomposition (list only — do not create these beads)

1. `:bench` TPC-H schema package: the eight row types, `Serializable`, published column shapes.
2. Deterministic base-data generator at small scale factors; BS-1.
3. RF1/RF2 refresh-stream generator and the `RefreshStream` application protocol with per-refresh
   quiescence hooks.
4. `TpchReference` batch recompute for Tier 1 queries, under exact decimal semantics.
5. Run protocol and record type: full `[BB-TPCH-06]` metadata, coverage table,
   `verified`/`blocked`/`not-expressible`/`unreportable`/`unverified` states.
6. Tier 1 queries by hand (Q1, Q6 first; then Q3, Q5, Q10, Q12, Q14, Q19); BS-2, BS-3, BS-10.
7. RF2 deletion-propagation suite: transitive retraction check and the top-K re-entry case; BS-3,
   BS-4.
8. Retained-state accounting and the monotone-growth finding; BS-6.
9. Long-stream drift check; BS-7.
10. Permitted-transient handling; BS-8.
11. Once QRY1 lands: port Tier 1 to QRY1 expressions, add the dual-route disagreement check; BS-12.
12. Once QRY1 + KAGG-R land: Tier 2 queries; record the remainder as `not-expressible` with named
    surfaces; BS-9.
13. Once KE1 lands: multiset-semantics queries unblocked; BS-11 becomes a regression guard.
14. ORA1 integration: TPC-H graphs as differential subjects with randomised interleavings; BS-13.
15. JMH bodies for maintenance cost per refresh, RF1 and RF2 separately.
16. Coverage table + the first `doc/bench/findings.md` entry.

---

## 8. Verification

- `./gradlew :bench:test` — maintenance-correctness at SF≈0.001; must stay in the default lane.
- `./gradlew test` — repository-wide gate; wall-clock unchanged.
- `./gradlew :bench:jmh` — measurement only; never in `build`/`check`/`test`, never a required CI
  check.
- Diff review: only `bench/` and `doc/bench/findings.md`.
- Review that §3.1's "do not rebuild" list has no counterpart under `bench/` — no local aggregate,
  no local join, no local multiset representation.
- Review that the coverage table's `not-expressible` and `blocked` rows each name a specific
  surface, not a generality.

---

## 9. Risks and open questions

- **QRY1's arrival dominates the schedule.** Tier 2 is ten of the 22 queries and is essentially
  unreachable by hand within a sane budget. `[BB-TPCH-17]` makes "Tier 1 only, Tier 2 blocked on
  QRY1" a complete outcome, but it means the feature may sit at ~8/22 coverage for a long time.
- **Bag versus set semantics is not a detail.** TPC-H is defined over multisets. ComputeNet's
  landed families are set- and tagged-set-shaped; the weighted (Z-set) family is E6, which is not a
  dependency here. `[BB-TPCH-18]` refuses the silent substitution, but the open question is whether
  a meaningful subset of TPC-H is answerable *correctly* before E6 rather than E1.
- **Decimal semantics.** TPC-H specifies exact decimal arithmetic; `Aggregators.sumOf` is
  deliberately `Long`-based ("float sums are order-sensitive") and `avgOf` returns `Double`.
  Reconciling that with `[BB-TPCH-25]`'s no-tolerance rule may itself surface a missing
  fixed-decimal aggregate — a likely early finding.
- **The oracle's cost.** A naive recompute after every refresh is quadratic-ish over a long stream.
  Mitigation: compare after every refresh at small scale, and only per-batch plus a final drift
  check (`[BB-TPCH-16]`) at larger scale.
- **State reclamation may be the real result.** `[BB-TPCH-23]`'s monotone-growth check touches
  G-42 (tag/tombstone reclamation) territory. If join ledgers and tag state grow under a
  balanced insert/delete stream, that finding matters more than any maintenance-cost number this
  feature produces.

Behaviour specs BS-1..BS-13 exist as named tests. Coverage table published per [BB-TPCH-10]. No diff outside bench/ and doc/bench/findings.md; no concord/corpus/ scenario added; no requirement asserts a performance number.

title: BB-YCSB — YCSB: point read/write/scan throughput under tunable mixes (thin adapter over keyed cells + bounded read)
description:
# BB-YCSB — YCSB (point read/write/scan throughput under tunable mixes)

Lane: benchmark-bridge (BB), `lane:benchmark`. Parent: BB umbrella epic (computenet-3xi).
Source: `computenet-milestone-plan.md` §1 (BB-YCSB row), §3 (YCSB row of the kernel-enablement
matrix), §5 rank 16, §6 standing hygiene.

Unwired deps (ids being minted by other agents — wire when they exist): **KRD** (the
request/response bounded-read primitive, generalised from inspector-v4's V1C-KERNEL), **KE1**
(OR-map / tagged-map convergence class — multi-writer keyed state), **KBLK** (bulk/benchmark host
mode — the load phase), **KAGG-R** (ordered key-range scan check, needed only by workload E).
Soft dep on **BEN1** for the `:bench` module and its gating convention.

---

## 1. Ambition / Why

YCSB is the cheapest possible answer to a question that will be asked of ComputeNet constantly and
which it currently cannot answer at all: *what does a point read cost, and what does a point write
cost?* Every other suite in the BB lane measures a composite — a query graph, a join chain, an
iterative analytic. YCSB measures the two primitives underneath all of them, under a mix the
caller controls. §1 of the milestone plan sizes it accurately: "**thin adapter over keyed cells +
the bounded-read primitive**". Almost all of its value comes from the fact that it is thin.

The strategic reason to run it is that ComputeNet's read path is *new*. Until inspector-v4's
V1C-KERNEL, the only state read was `snapshotOf`, whose cost was never characterised — and
`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/BoundedRead.kt`'s own KDoc currently cites measurement
numbers that the tree cannot re-derive (that is one of BEN1's stated motivations). YCSB is the
workload that turns the bounded read from a mechanism with an anecdote attached into a mechanism
with a curve attached, across the read/write/scan mixes the storage literature actually uses
(A 50/50, B 95/5, C read-only, D latest-read, E short scans, F read-modify-write).

The second reason is that YCSB is an honest *negative* instrument as much as a positive one.
ComputeNet is not a key-value store and should not pretend to be one. Workload F
(read-modify-write) sits exactly on the seam that BB-TPCC's negative-result study identifies:
there is no abort, no isolation, and `[21-PULL-03]` says a walk is "verifiable, not isolated".
Running F and reporting precisely *what it means* on this model — rather than quietly redefining
it into something achievable — is a lane finding worth more than the throughput number beside it.

Third: **ordered scan is the one genuinely new operator surface** across all six suites (§3). YCSB
workload E is what forces the question, and KAGG-R is the small chunk that answers it. Filing this
feature makes that pull visible and attributed.

---

## 2. What we build

### 2.1 In `:bench`

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `bench/src/main/kotlin/civictech/bench/ycsb/YcsbRecord.kt` | The YCSB record model: a key plus F fields of L bytes, `Serializable`, matching the published field/record shape. |
| `bench/src/main/kotlin/civictech/bench/ycsb/YcsbGenerator.kt` | Deterministic seeded key/operation generator with the published distributions: uniform, Zipfian (with the constant the spec fixes), latest, and the scan-length distribution for workload E. |
| `bench/src/main/kotlin/civictech/bench/ycsb/YcsbWorkloads.kt` | Workloads A–F as declared mixes, expressed as data, not code branches. |
| `bench/src/main/kotlin/civictech/bench/ycsb/YcsbAdapter.kt` | The adapter: `read`, `insert`, `update`, `scan`, `readModifyWrite` mapped onto keyed cells and the bounded-read primitive. This is the artifact the plan calls "thin"; if it stops being thin, that is a finding. |
| `bench/src/main/kotlin/civictech/bench/ycsb/YcsbReference.kt` | An in-memory `TreeMap`-backed model of the same operations, used as the correctness oracle for every mix. |
| `bench/src/main/kotlin/civictech/bench/ycsb/YcsbRun.kt` | Load phase, run phase, quiescence, record emission with `[BB-YCSB-06]`'s metadata. |
| `bench/src/jmh/kotlin/civictech/bench/ycsb/` | `@Benchmark` bodies; behind `:bench:jmh`, not in `build`/`check`/`test`. |
| `bench/src/test/kotlin/civictech/bench/ycsb/` | Fast correctness tests at tiny record counts. |

### 2.2 Outside `:bench`

- `doc/bench/findings.md` — append-only lane findings. The only file outside `:bench` this
  feature writes.
- Nothing in `kernel/`, `gen/`, `wire/`, `concord/`, `demo/`, `doc/spec/`.

### 2.3 What "adapter" means here, precisely

The YCSB client interface is `read(table, key, fields)`, `scan(table, startkey, count, fields)`,
`update`, `insert`, `delete`. The adapter's job is to bind those six verbs to ComputeNet
mechanisms **and to state, for each, the semantic it actually delivers** — not the semantic YCSB
assumes. That mapping table (§3.3) is a deliverable in its own right and is what makes the numbers
interpretable.

---

## 3. How, using ComputeNet

### 3.1 Already in the kernel — DO NOT REBUILD

- **The bounded read.** `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/BoundedRead.kt` —
  `interface BoundedStateful : Stateful` with `readBounded(request: StateRead): StatePage`, plus
  `StateRead`, `StatePage`, `StateReadResult`, and `ExclusiveEntry` (with
  `ExclusiveEntry.isExclusive(value)` recognising `Owned`/`Leased`). Cursoring and budget
  exhaustion live in `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/BoundedWalk.kt`
  (`exhausted(bytes, byteBudget)`). The wave-neutrality, cursor-cost and provenance properties
  already have kernel tests: `kernel/src/test/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/BoundedReadWaveNeutralityTest.kt`,
  `BoundedReadCursorCostTest.kt`, `BoundedReadProvenanceTest.kt`. **Do not write a read path.**
- **Request/response over ports.** `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/protocol/StateRequestProtocol.kt`
  — a `StateRequest` rides a `PORT_PROTOCOL` frame; the scatter-gather router fans it to shards
  (PN-5/FU-1). `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/partition/RoutedCommand.kt` is one leg.
- **Keyed state and keyed instantiation.**
  `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/KeyedSetCell.kt` (`KeyedSetApi.put/remove`,
  `KeyedSetStateEntry(key, element, tag)`), `data/MapCell.kt`, `data/OrMapCell.kt` (the KE1
  convergence class), and `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/KeyedCells.kt`
  (`getOrSpawn(key)`, `recover()`, `keys()`, `hostJournal(journalDir)`). **Do not write a keyed
  index.**
- **Partitioning and scatter-gather.** `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/partition/` —
  `Partitioned`, `PartitionedCell`, `PartitionedShardSet` (the scatter-gather board of per-shard
  live key ranges; `[24-PART-03]` disjoint ranges ⇒ conflict-free union), `ShardCell` (its live
  key range). **Do not write a sharding scheme.** Note `BoundedRead.kt`'s own KDoc caveat about
  reads "across a scatter-gather boundary (where the answering instance may change)".
- **Delta vocabulary.** `data/delta/MapDelta.kt`, `TaggedMapDelta.kt`, `SetDelta.kt`,
  `TagState.kt`. Tag-map growth is the prime suspect for dominating any keyed number (BEN1 says so
  explicitly) — measure it, don't re-derive it.
- **Durability.** `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/durability/` and `host/HostDurability.kt`
  are the WAL seam KBLK configures. The load phase runs against these, not around them.
- **Drive and observation.** `testkit/.../SimWorld.kt` (`runToIdle`), `AwaitUntil.kt`,
  `host/SimulationController.kt`, `host/ManagedHost.kt` with `VirtualThreadScheduler` /
  `CoroutineScheduler`; `civictech/cell/observe/Observe.kt` and `observe/AlignedObserve.kt`.

### 3.2 What BB-YCSB legitimately adds

The generator, the workload mixes, the six-verb adapter, the `TreeMap` reference model, and the
run/report protocol. Nothing else.

### 3.3 The verb-mapping table (a required deliverable, sketched)

| YCSB verb | ComputeNet mechanism | Semantic actually delivered |
|---|---|---|
| `insert` | keyed put through `KeyedCells.getOrSpawn` / `KeyedSetApi.put` | effective-only emission; no abort |
| `update` | same, as a tagged-map write under KE1 | last-writer-by-tag convergence, **not** linearizable overwrite |
| `read` | `readBounded(StateRead)` via KRD | bounded, wave-neutral, **not isolated** (`[21-PULL-02]`, `[21-PULL-03]`) |
| `scan(start, count)` | ordered key-range read over the keyed family | **the new surface** — KAGG-R's range-scan check; may not exist yet |
| `delete` | keyed remove (tombstone/tag semantics) | convergence by supersession, tag-state cost is real |
| `readModifyWrite` (F) | bounded read then keyed write | **no atomicity, no isolation, no abort** — must be reported as such, never as RMW |

---

## 4. Scope boundaries

- **Not a key-value store claim.** This feature measures ComputeNet under a KV-shaped workload. It
  must not be read, or written, as an assertion that ComputeNet is a competitive KV store.
- **No kernel/wire/gen/concord/demo/spec edits.** A missing capability (ordered scan being the
  likely one) is a finding or a pulled KAGG-R trigger, not an in-lane implementation.
- **No `concord/corpus/` scenarios.** Benchmark numbers are machine-dependent and therefore not
  implementation-neutral; BB-YCSB adds none.
- **No performance targets.** No requirement below asserts or accepts a number as a pass
  condition.
- **No distribution sweep.** Multi-host/replicated YCSB is out of scope for this feature; the
  single-host adapter and its findings come first.
- **No YCSB client-JVM integration.** Reimplementing the workload generator inside `:bench` is
  cheaper and more deterministic than driving the upstream Java client; the obligation is fidelity
  to the *specification*, not reuse of the *code* (`[BB-YCSB-01]`).

---

## 5. Functional requirements (EARS)

### Ubiquitous

- **[BB-YCSB-01]** The harness shall implement the YCSB core workload specification — record and
  field shape, the operation mixes of workloads A through F, and the published key and
  scan-length distributions — and shall name the specification revision it targets in every
  recorded run.
- **[BB-YCSB-02]** The harness shall reside entirely under `bench/`, and no module outside
  `:bench` shall depend on it.
- **[BB-YCSB-03]** The generator shall be deterministic: the same seed, record count and workload
  shall produce an identical operation sequence on every run and every machine, including the
  Zipfian key order.
- **[BB-YCSB-04]** The adapter shall bind YCSB's verbs to existing kernel mechanisms (§3.1) and
  shall not implement storage, indexing, ordering, or paging of its own.
- **[BB-YCSB-05]** The harness shall publish, as a required part of its output, the verb-mapping
  table of §3.3 stating for each YCSB verb the ComputeNet mechanism used and the semantic actually
  delivered.
- **[BB-YCSB-06]** Every recorded run shall record: harness commit SHA; seed, record count, field
  count and field length; workload id and its mix; key distribution; JVM vendor and version; heap;
  machine CPU model, core count and OS; scheduler; durability mode; load-phase configuration; JMH
  parameters; and observed variance.
- **[BB-YCSB-07]** The harness shall report read, write and scan figures separately and shall
  never present a single blended operations-per-second figure as the result of a mixed workload.
- **[BB-YCSB-08]** The harness shall record retained tag-state size and per-key memory footprint
  alongside every run, because keyed-family state growth is a first-class result.
- **[BB-YCSB-09]** The harness shall keep its `:bench` test source set inside the default
  `./gradlew test` lane, with measurement behind BEN1's `@Tag("bench")` gate and `:bench:jmh`.

### Event-driven

- **[BB-YCSB-10]** When the run phase reaches quiescence, the harness shall compare the full keyed
  state against `YcsbReference`'s `TreeMap` model of the same operation sequence and record the
  comparison outcome.
- **[BB-YCSB-11]** When the observed state differs from the reference model, the harness shall
  report the run as **failed** and shall record no throughput figure for it.
- **[BB-YCSB-12]** When a scan is issued, the harness shall verify that the returned keys are in
  ascending key order, are contiguous within the requested range, and match the reference model's
  slice for the same start key and count.
- **[BB-YCSB-13]** When a bounded read exhausts its byte budget mid-page, the harness shall follow
  the cursor to completion and shall count the number of pages required, so that paging cost is
  visible rather than amortised away.
- **[BB-YCSB-14]** When a suite run hits a wall, the harness's operator shall write a dated entry
  to `doc/bench/findings.md` naming the wall either as a **candidate G-item** (in the gap table's
  column shape, id left `G-NN`) or as the **existing trigger it pulls**, and shall not close the
  wall in this lane.
- **[BB-YCSB-15]** When the load phase completes, the harness shall record load-phase duration and
  configuration separately from run-phase figures, and shall never fold load cost into a run-phase
  number.

### State-driven

- **[BB-YCSB-16]** While KRD's public request/response bounded-read primitive is unavailable, the
  harness shall implement no substitute read path and shall record every read-bearing workload as
  **blocked**, naming KRD.
- **[BB-YCSB-17]** While an ordered key-range scan primitive is unavailable, the harness shall
  record workload E as **not-expressible**, naming the missing range-scan surface and the KAGG-R
  chunk that owns it, and shall not emulate the scan by reading the whole keyspace and sorting in
  `:bench`.
- **[BB-YCSB-18]** While KE1's tagged-map convergence class is unavailable, the harness shall
  restrict write workloads to a single writer per key and shall label all write figures
  **single-writer only**.
- **[BB-YCSB-19]** While durability is enabled with synchronous WAL, the harness shall label every
  write and load figure **WAL-bound** and shall state that the figure measures the durability
  path.
- **[BB-YCSB-20]** While a run is driven by `SimulationController` or `SimWorld.runToIdle`, the
  harness shall report no wall-clock latency figure.

### Unwanted behaviour

- **[BB-YCSB-21]** If the adapter would need to hold state of its own — an index, a sorted view, a
  cache — in order to serve a YCSB verb, then that need shall be recorded as a finding naming the
  missing kernel surface, and the adapter shall not silently acquire the state.
- **[BB-YCSB-22]** If workload F (read-modify-write) is run, then the harness shall report it as
  **read-then-write without isolation, atomicity or abort**, shall cite `[21-PULL-02]`,
  `[21-PULL-03]` and the absence of an abort verb, and shall not present the result as a
  read-modify-write throughput.
- **[BB-YCSB-23]** If concurrent writers to the same key produce a state that the reference model
  cannot predict deterministically, then the harness shall compare against the *convergence*
  property (all replicas/readers agree after quiescence) rather than against a specific value, and
  shall say which comparison it performed.
- **[BB-YCSB-24]** If a read is served across a scatter-gather boundary where the answering
  instance may change mid-walk, then the harness shall record the read as **smeared** and shall
  not count it toward a consistency claim.
- **[BB-YCSB-25]** If run-to-run variance exceeds the harness's declared threshold, then the run
  shall be marked **unreportable** and the variance recorded in place of a mean.
- **[BB-YCSB-26]** If a run's reference comparison is skipped, then the run shall be marked
  **unverified** and no downstream document shall cite its number.
- **[BB-YCSB-27]** If a benchmark record would carry an `Owned` or `Leased` payload, then graph
  construction shall fail, because a benchmark ingest path must never be one on which an exclusive
  can be dropped; `ExclusiveEntry.isExclusive` is the available check.
- **[BB-YCSB-28]** If the findings would require editing `doc/spec/90-roadmap/91-gap-analysis.md`
  or `doc/spec/CONCORDANCE.md`, then the operator shall write to `doc/bench/findings.md` instead
  and leave both files untouched.
- **[BB-YCSB-29]** If a figure would be compared against a published YCSB result for a database,
  then the record shall first state that ComputeNet offers no isolation level and no abort, and
  shall refuse the comparison if the cited system's figure depends on either.

### Optional feature

- **[BB-YCSB-30]** Where KBLK's bulk/benchmark host mode is available, the harness shall run the
  load phase through the batched ingress path with WAL off or asynchronous, and shall record which
  mode produced the load figure.
- **[BB-YCSB-31]** Where the keyed state is partitioned across shards, the harness shall report
  per-shard and aggregate figures separately and shall state the shard count and key-range
  assignment.
- **[BB-YCSB-32]** Where a latency-capable acknowledgement path (the KE2 ack slice) is available,
  the harness shall report write-to-visible latency percentiles; where it is not, sink-observed
  latency may be reported and shall be labelled **sink-observed, not acked**.
- **[BB-YCSB-33]** Where journal recovery is exercised, the harness shall verify via
  `KeyedCells.recover()` that the post-recovery keyed state equals the reference model, and shall
  record recovery duration as a separate figure.

### Complex

- **[BB-YCSB-34]** When workload D (read-latest) is run, while the key distribution is the latest
  distribution rather than Zipfian, the harness shall verify that the read path observes the most
  recent write for a key after quiescence, and if it does not, shall record the staleness window
  observed rather than declaring a failure — the model provides convergence, not immediacy.
- **[BB-YCSB-35]** When a scan crosses a shard boundary, if the scatter-gather union of shard key
  ranges is not disjoint at the moment of the read, then the harness shall record the scan as
  **cross-shard-arbitrary** and shall cite the spec's "across shards there is no joint cut", and
  shall not count the result as a correctness failure.
- **[BB-YCSB-36]** When a run is executed with more than one writer per key, while KE1 is
  available, the harness shall verify convergence to the tagged-map's decided value and shall
  additionally record the tag-state growth attributable to the multi-writer configuration.
- **[BB-YCSB-37]** When the adapter's verb-mapping table changes, if any row's "semantic actually
  delivered" column changes, then previously recorded findings entries citing that row shall be
  superseded by a new dated entry rather than edited in place — `doc/bench/findings.md` is
  append-only.

---

## 6. Behaviour specifications

**BS-1 — Zipfian determinism (`[BB-YCSB-03]`)**
*Given* a seed, record count and workload B,
*when* the operation sequence is generated twice in-process and once in a fresh JVM,
*then* all three sequences are element-wise identical, including key selection order.

**BS-2 — Workload C matches the reference (`[BB-YCSB-10]`)**
*Given* a loaded keyspace of 10 000 records and workload C (read-only),
*when* the run phase completes and the graph reaches quiescence,
*then* every read result equals the reference model's value for that key, and the run record
carries `verified = true`.

**BS-3 — Scan order and contiguity (`[BB-YCSB-12]`)**
*Given* a keyspace with 1 000 records and a scan from a key at position 400 with count 50,
*when* the scan returns,
*then* the returned keys are strictly ascending, contiguous in the reference model's ordering, and
exactly 50 in number (or fewer only at the keyspace end, which the record states).

**BS-4 — Missing scan surface is a finding, not an emulation (`[BB-YCSB-17]`, `[BB-YCSB-21]`)**
*Given* a tree in which no ordered key-range scan exists,
*when* workload E is requested,
*then* the harness records `not-expressible` naming the missing range-scan surface and KAGG-R,
writes a dated `doc/bench/findings.md` entry, and the `bench/` tree contains no sorted-index or
whole-keyspace-sort implementation.

**BS-5 — Paging cost is counted (`[BB-YCSB-13]`)**
*Given* a `StateRead` whose byte budget forces at least three pages,
*when* the read is followed to completion,
*then* the record carries the page count and total bytes, and the union of the pages equals the
single-page result obtained with an unbounded budget.

**BS-6 — Workload F is reported honestly (`[BB-YCSB-22]`)**
*Given* workload F,
*when* the run record is produced,
*then* it is labelled read-then-write without isolation, atomicity or abort; it cites
`[21-PULL-02]`/`[21-PULL-03]`; and no field of the record is named or typed as a
read-modify-write throughput.

**BS-7 — Load cost is never folded in (`[BB-YCSB-15]`)**
*Given* a run whose load phase inserts 1 000 000 records,
*when* the record is produced,
*then* load duration appears in its own field and the run-phase throughput is computed over an
interval that provably excludes the load phase.

**BS-8 — Recovery equals the model (`[BB-YCSB-33]`)**
*Given* a run with journalling enabled and a crash injected after the run phase,
*when* `KeyedCells.recover()` completes on restart,
*then* the recovered keyed state equals the reference model, and recovery duration is recorded
separately.

**BS-9 — Multi-writer convergence, not equality (`[BB-YCSB-23]`, `[BB-YCSB-36]`)**
*Given* two writers updating the same key concurrently with KE1 present,
*when* the graph quiesces,
*then* all readers observe the same value, the record states that a convergence comparison (not a
value comparison) was performed, and tag-state growth is recorded.

**BS-10 — Smeared cross-shard read is labelled (`[BB-YCSB-24]`, `[BB-YCSB-35]`)**
*Given* a scan spanning two shards while a repartition flip is in progress,
*when* the scan returns,
*then* the result is labelled cross-shard-arbitrary/smeared, is not counted as a correctness
failure, and the record cites the absence of a joint cut across shards.

**BS-11 — Exclusive payload refused (`[BB-YCSB-27]`)**
*Given* a record type wrapping an `Owned<ByteArray>` field,
*when* the adapter constructs the graph,
*then* construction fails naming the exclusive payload rule, and no host is started.

**BS-12 — Blocked beats improvised (`[BB-YCSB-16]`)**
*Given* a tree without KRD's public bounded-read primitive,
*when* any read-bearing workload is requested,
*then* the harness records `blocked` naming KRD, and the `bench/` tree contains no alternative read
path.

---

## 7. Suggested task decomposition (list only — do not create these beads)

1. `:bench` YCSB package skeleton, record/field model, workload declarations A–F as data.
2. Deterministic generator: uniform, Zipfian (published constant), latest, scan-length; BS-1.
3. `YcsbReference` `TreeMap` model + the comparison protocol (`verified` / `failed` /
   `unverified`).
4. Run protocol and record type: load phase separate from run phase, full `[BB-YCSB-06]` metadata,
   `unreportable`/`blocked`/`not-expressible` states.
5. Adapter — write path first (insert/update/delete over `KeyedCells` + keyed cells), single-writer
   until KE1.
6. Load-phase measurement, with and without KBLK's bulk mode; BS-7.
7. Adapter — read path over KRD's bounded read; page-following and page-count accounting; BS-5,
   BS-2.
8. Workloads A, B, C, D end to end; per-verb figures per `[BB-YCSB-07]`; BS-2, and the D staleness
   observation of `[BB-YCSB-34]`.
9. Workload E: the ordered-scan probe. Either it runs (BS-3) or it produces the KAGG-R finding
   (BS-4). Both outcomes are complete.
10. Workload F: the honest-reporting path and its finding; BS-6.
11. The verb-mapping table as a published deliverable (`[BB-YCSB-05]`), and the first
    `doc/bench/findings.md` entry.
12. Multi-writer convergence once KE1 lands; BS-9, `[BB-YCSB-36]`.
13. Optional: journal-recovery variant (BS-8), partitioned variant (`[BB-YCSB-31]`, BS-10),
    latency percentiles once the KE2 ack slice exists.

---

## 8. Verification

- `./gradlew :bench:test` — reference-model comparison, determinism, scan-order and paging tests.
- `./gradlew test` — repository-wide gate; wall-clock must be unchanged.
- `./gradlew :bench:jmh` — measurement, never in `build`/`check`/`test`, never a required CI check.
- Diff review: only `bench/` and `doc/bench/findings.md`.
- Review that §3.1's "do not rebuild" list has no counterpart under `bench/` — particularly no
  index, no sorted view, no cache (`[BB-YCSB-21]`).

---

## 9. Risks and open questions

- **The scan question may simply be open.** KAGG-R's own description is "verify … an ordered key
  range scan for keyed families; implement only what's missing". BB-YCSB may run before that
  verdict exists. `[BB-YCSB-17]` makes "workload E is blocked" a complete and legitimate outcome,
  but it does mean the feature can close with one of six workloads unrun.
- **Semantic mismatch is the headline, not a footnote.** YCSB assumes a store with
  read-your-writes and single-value semantics. ComputeNet offers convergence. There is a real risk
  that a well-meaning implementer tunes the adapter until the reference comparison passes, thereby
  hiding the interesting result. `[BB-YCSB-05]`, `[BB-YCSB-22]` and `[BB-YCSB-23]` exist to make
  the mismatch a deliverable rather than a bug to be papered over.
- **Tag-state cost may dominate everything.** BEN1 flags tag-map growth as "a prime suspect for
  dominating any set-shaped number". If it does, the YCSB numbers describe tag bookkeeping rather
  than the read/write path — which is itself a high-value finding (G-42 reclamation territory) and
  should be filed as one.
- **Zipfian constant and record shape.** Different YCSB revisions and ports differ. `[BB-YCSB-01]`
  requires naming the revision; whether the chosen one is the one the systems we'd like to compare
  against used is an open question.
- **Adapter thinness is an assertion, not a guarantee.** The plan calls it thin. If it turns out
  fat, `[BB-YCSB-21]` converts that discovery into a finding — but a fat adapter also means the
  numbers measure the adapter.
acceptance_criteria: Closes on [BB-YCSB-01..15] and [BB-YCSB-19..29] and [BB-YCSB-34], [BB-YCSB-37] for every workload that is expressible; on [BB-YCSB-16..18] recorded as blocked/not-expressible/single-writer for every workload that is not; and on [BB-YCSB-30..33], [BB-YCSB-35..36] where their optional gates landed. Behaviour specs BS-1..BS-12 exist as named tests. Verb-mapping table published per [BB-YCSB-05]. No diff outside bench/ and doc/bench/findings.md; no concord/corpus/ scenario added; no requirement asserts a performance number.

Soft dep on BEN1 (computenet-x9e) for the :bench module; wired as 'related' because beads will not let a feature be blocked by an epic.
