title: BB-NEX — Nexmark (auction stream, Q1-Q8+): continuous-query throughput/latency, KE4's acceptance suite
description:
# BB-NEX — Nexmark (auction stream, Q1–Q8+)

Lane: benchmark-bridge (BB), `lane:benchmark`. Parent: BB umbrella epic (computenet-3xi).
Source: `computenet-milestone-plan.md` §1 (BB-NEX row), §3 (Nexmark row of the
kernel-enablement matrix), §5 rank 7 (the **Q1–Q3 slice**) and rank 19 (the rest), §6
standing hygiene.

Depends on: **BEN1** (`:bench` module, JMH harness, `@Tag("bench")` gating) — wired.
Unwired deps (ids being minted by other agents): **KE4** (event-time waterline eviction —
the only kernel blocker for the windowed queries), **KBLK** (bulk/benchmark mode, for honest
throughput), **KE2** ack slice (optional, for end-to-end latency percentiles).

---

## 1. Ambition / Why

Nexmark is the suite the incremental-dataflow field actually publishes against. DBSP/Feldera,
Flink, Beam, Timely/Differential and Materialize all carry Nexmark numbers, which makes it the
only benchmark in the BB lane that yields a *comparative* statement rather than a self-relative
one. Every other suite tells us how ComputeNet behaves; Nexmark tells us where ComputeNet sits.

That comparative value is why it ranks 7 in §5 despite ranking 19 as a whole. §5's justification
is precise: the Q1–Q3 slice (map, filter, equi-join) is **runnable today on existing operators**,
so it "establishes the harness, generator, and comparability baseline while KE4 queues". The
expensive, blocking part of a benchmark is almost never the queries — it is the generator, the
run protocol, the reference-answer machinery and the reporting discipline. Building all of that
against three queries that need no kernel work, and then adding queries as kernel chunks land,
converts BB-NEX from a single blocked lump into a standing instrument.

The second reason this suite matters is that it is **the acceptance suite for KE4**. §3 of the
plan states the dependency in one direction only: watermark-driven eviction is "literally the
deferred trigger named in `Windows`' KDoc", and BB-NEX is what pulls it. The KDoc in
`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/Windows.kt` says it outright — "Windows never close:
late elements are ordinary adds and retractions flow (view semantics). Watermark-driven eviction
is deferred with trigger (24)." BB-NEX's windowed queries are that trigger arriving with a
concrete, published workload attached rather than as an abstract worry about state growth.

Per §6, the lane's actual product is findings. A BB-NEX run that discovers unbounded group
retention under Q5 has produced its deliverable even if it never prints a throughput number.

---

## 2. What we build

### 2.1 In `:bench` (everything, unless listed in §2.2)

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `bench/src/main/kotlin/civictech/bench/nexmark/NexmarkGenerator.kt` | Deterministic, seeded Person/Auction/Bid event generator matching the published Nexmark event model and skew parameters. |
| `bench/src/main/kotlin/civictech/bench/nexmark/NexmarkEvents.kt` | The three event records + the derived row types the query graphs consume; `Serializable`, since graph-spec capture and journals require it. |
| `bench/src/main/kotlin/civictech/bench/nexmark/queries/` | One builder per query (`Q1.kt` … `Q8.kt`), each assembling a graph out of *existing* kernel operator cells. |
| `bench/src/main/kotlin/civictech/bench/nexmark/NexmarkReference.kt` | Batch recompute reference answer over an event prefix — the correctness oracle. Naive, obviously-correct, no incremental cleverness. |
| `bench/src/main/kotlin/civictech/bench/nexmark/NexmarkRun.kt` | Run protocol: build graph, load, drive, quiesce, read sink, compare, emit a record with the full run metadata of `[BB-NEX-05]`. |
| `bench/src/jmh/kotlin/civictech/bench/nexmark/` | `@Benchmark` bodies. Not wired into `build`/`check`/`test`. |
| `bench/src/test/kotlin/civictech/bench/nexmark/` | Fast correctness tests: tiny scale factor, reference comparison, generator determinism. These run in the default build and must stay sub-second. |

### 2.2 Outside `:bench`

- `doc/bench/findings.md` — append-only lane findings (created by BB-TPCC if it lands first;
  otherwise created here). The **only** file outside `:bench` this feature writes.
- Nothing in `kernel/`, `gen/`, `wire/`, `concord/`, `demo/`, or `doc/spec/`. If a query needs
  kernel behaviour that does not exist, that is a finding, not an edit.

### 2.3 The Q1–Q3 slice as a separately-schedulable increment

Per §5 rank 7, the feature carries an explicit internal boundary. **Increment A (Q1–Q3)** is
complete and shippable on its own: generator, run protocol, reference harness, reporting
discipline, and the three queries that need no kernel work. **Increment B (windowed and
ordered queries)** is gated on KE4 and KBLK and adds queries only — it must add no new harness
machinery, and if it needs to, that is a design defect in Increment A.

---

## 3. How, using ComputeNet

### 3.1 Already in the kernel — DO NOT REBUILD

An agent implementing this feature must read these before writing a line of query code. §3 of the
milestone plan names them specifically as the "what already exists that I might have rebuilt by
mistake" column.

- **Windowing is already solved as key derivation.**
  `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/Windows.kt` — `Windows.tumbling(size)` returns an
  event-time → window-start function; `Windows.sliding(size, slide)` returns event-time → list of
  window starts. Both are named `Serializable` classes so they survive graph-spec capture. There
  is **no wall clock** (P1): event time is an explicit attribute of the element. Tumbling is a
  composite group key; sliding is per-element expansion through
  `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/op/FlatMapSetCell.kt` followed by a group-by. **Do
  not write a window operator.**
- **Grouping and aggregation.** `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/op/GroupByCell.kt`
  (and `GroupByCell.global(...)`), with `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/Aggregator.kt`
  supplying retraction-aware `count()`, `sumOf`, `avgOf`, `minOf`, `maxOf`, `topK(k, selector)`
  and `collectToSet()`. `minOf`/`maxOf`/`topK` are already the retraction-correct TreeMap
  support-multiset implementations that Q5 and Q7 need. **Do not write a top-k.**
- **Joins.** `data/op/JoinSetCell.kt` (`joinSet`, `crossProduct`), `LookupJoinCell.kt`,
  `SemiJoinCell.kt`, `KeyedBinarySetJoin.kt`, `JoinLedger.kt`, plus the outer-join builders in
  `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/graph/RelationalGraphs.kt`
  (`leftJoin`/`rightJoin`/`fullJoin`). Q3 (auction ⋈ person) and Q8 are equi-joins over this
  family.
- **Map / filter / flat-map.** `data/op/FilterCell.kt`, `FlatMapSetCell.kt` (+ the `mapSet(f)`
  helper), `civictech/cell/MapperCell.kt`. Q1 (currency conversion) and Q2 (filter) are these.
- **Set algebra and graph assembly.** `graph/GraphDsl.kt`, `graph/SetAlgebraGraphs.kt`
  (`filter`/`count`/`intersect`/`union` on `CellHandle`), `graph/TypedRef.kt`.
- **Deterministic drive and quiescence.** `testkit/src/main/kotlin/civictech/testkit/SimWorld.kt`
  (`runToIdle`), `testkit/.../AwaitUntil.kt`, and
  `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/SimulationController.kt`. Real-threads runs go
  through `host/ManagedHost.kt` with `VirtualThreadScheduler` or `CoroutineScheduler`.
- **Observation.** `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/observe/Observe.kt` and
  `observe/AlignedObserve.kt` (`observeAligned { … }` → `AlignedCompositeCell`) are the sink-read
  seam. Reading a sink is an observation, not a new outlet.
- **Watermark substrate already exists in part.** `data/Watermark.kt` (`WatermarkCell`,
  `advance(source, thru)`, `watermark(source)`, `close()`, `suspend()`/`resume()`) and
  `data/delta/WatermarkDelta.kt` landed as E3.2. KE4 builds the *waterline/eviction* consumer on
  top; BB-NEX must not build a parallel one.

### 3.2 What BB-NEX legitimately adds

Only three things: (a) the event generator, (b) per-query graph assembly out of the cells above,
(c) the reference-answer recompute and the run/report protocol. Anything else is scope creep and
should surface as a finding instead.

### 3.3 Query-by-query kernel status (the schedule, in one table)

| Query | Shape | Runnable today? | Gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 currency conversion | map | **yes** | — (Increment A) |
| Q2 selection | filter | **yes** | — (Increment A) |
| Q3 local item suggestion | equi-join auction ⋈ person, + filter | **yes** | — (Increment A) |
| Q4 average price per category | join + nested aggregate | yes, verify retraction path | Increment A stretch |
| Q5 hot items | sliding window + count + max-by | no | **KE4** (state bound), `Windows.sliding` + `topK` exist |
| Q6 average selling price per seller | per-key bounded history | partial | KE4 for the bound |
| Q7 highest bid per window | tumbling window + max | no | **KE4** |
| Q8 monitor new users | tumbling-window join | no | **KE4** |

---

## 4. Scope boundaries

- **No kernel, wire, gen, concord, demo or spec edits.** A missing capability is written to
  `doc/bench/findings.md` as a candidate G-item or a pulled trigger; it is never solved in-lane.
- **No `concord/corpus/` scenarios.** Benchmark numbers are machine-dependent and therefore not
  implementation-neutral; the concord corpus is an implementation-neutral conformance suite.
  BB-NEX adds zero scenarios to it. (Correctness-vs-reference assertions live in `:bench`'s own
  test source set.)
- **No performance targets.** This feature specifies the *instrument and its obligations*. No
  requirement in §5 asserts, implies, or accepts a throughput or latency number as a pass
  condition.
- **No optimisation of the runtime.** If a run is slow, the output is a number and a finding, not
  a patch to `kernel/`.
- **Nexmark only.** Streaming-adjacent suites (Yahoo Streaming Benchmark, linear road) are out.
- Increment B does not begin before KE4 has merged into `main`; the plan's §4 tension (MEM1 ↔ KE4
  swap) is the orchestrator's decision, not this feature's.

---

## 5. Functional requirements (EARS)

Ids are namespaced `BB-NEX-nn`, mirroring `doc/spec/`'s `[NN-SLUG-nn]` shape without colliding
with it. "The harness" means the BB-NEX code and run protocol in `:bench` taken together.

### Ubiquitous

- **[BB-NEX-01]** The harness shall implement the Nexmark event schema (Person, Auction, Bid) and
  query semantics as defined by the published Nexmark specification, and shall name the exact
  specification revision it targets in every recorded run.
- **[BB-NEX-02]** The harness shall reside entirely under `bench/`, and no module outside `:bench`
  shall depend on it.
- **[BB-NEX-03]** The generator shall be deterministic: the same seed, scale factor and event
  count shall produce an identical event sequence on every run and every machine.
- **[BB-NEX-04]** Each query graph shall be assembled from existing kernel operator cells and
  graph builders (§3.1) driven through the real link/port path, and shall not reimplement any
  operator's semantics inside `:bench`.
- **[BB-NEX-05]** Every recorded run shall record: harness commit SHA; generator seed, scale
  factor and event count; query id; JVM vendor and version; heap settings; machine CPU model,
  core count and OS; which scheduler drove it (`SimulationController` versus
  `VirtualThreadScheduler`/`CoroutineScheduler`); durability mode; JMH mode, forks, warmup and
  measurement iterations; and the observed variance.
- **[BB-NEX-06]** Every recorded run shall state, explicitly and per query, every deviation from
  published Nexmark semantics that was required to express the query on ComputeNet, together with
  its justification.
- **[BB-NEX-07]** The harness shall express each query's result as a sink observation obtained
  through `civictech.cell.observe`, and shall not read cell internals to produce a result.
- **[BB-NEX-08]** The harness shall keep the `:bench` test source set fast enough to remain in the
  default `./gradlew test` lane, with all long-running work behind BEN1's `@Tag("bench")` gate and
  the separate `:bench:jmh` task.
- **[BB-NEX-09]** The Q1–Q3 slice shall be independently completable and reportable without any
  unlanded kernel dependency, and shall carry the generator, run protocol, reference harness and
  reporting discipline in full.
- **[BB-NEX-10]** The harness shall record insert-direction and retraction-direction behaviour
  separately for every query whose graph contains a retraction-aware operator, because retraction
  is where incremental engines differ and an insert-only figure would be misleading.

### Event-driven

- **[BB-NEX-11]** When a query graph reaches quiescence over a generated event prefix, the harness
  shall compare the observed sink contents against the reference answer computed by
  `NexmarkReference` over the same prefix, and shall record the comparison outcome.
- **[BB-NEX-12]** When the observed sink contents differ from the reference answer, the harness
  shall report the run as **failed** and shall record no throughput or latency figure for it.
- **[BB-NEX-13]** When a suite run hits a wall — a query that cannot be expressed, a state bound
  that cannot be held, a semantic that cannot be preserved — the harness's operator shall write a
  dated entry to `doc/bench/findings.md` naming the wall either as a **candidate G-item** (in the
  gap table's column shape, id left as `G-NN` unassigned) or as the **existing trigger it pulls**,
  and shall not attempt to close the wall in this lane.
- **[BB-NEX-14]** When a query requires windowing, the harness shall obtain window assignment from
  `Windows.tumbling` or `Windows.sliding` as a key derivation over an explicit event-time
  attribute, and shall not introduce a window operator, a wall clock, or a timer.
- **[BB-NEX-15]** When a late event arrives for a window whose group has already produced output,
  the harness shall apply it as an ordinary add and shall verify that retraction flow carries the
  sink to the reference answer.
- **[BB-NEX-16]** When a run completes, the harness shall record the peak retained group count and
  peak retained tag-state size alongside the run, so that state growth is visible independently of
  throughput.
- **[BB-NEX-17]** When the harness is run at two different scale factors, it shall report both, so
  that a single-point number is never the only evidence offered.

### State-driven

- **[BB-NEX-18]** While KE4 (waterline eviction) has not landed, the harness shall label every
  windowed query result **unbounded-state** and shall report its retained-state growth curve as a
  first-class result rather than a footnote.
- **[BB-NEX-19]** While a run is driven by `SimulationController` or `SimWorld.runToIdle`, the
  harness shall report no wall-clock latency figure, because simulated drive answers a throughput
  and correctness question, not a latency one.
- **[BB-NEX-20]** While durability is enabled with synchronous WAL, the harness shall label every
  throughput figure **WAL-bound** and shall state that the figure measures the durability path,
  not the operator path.
- **[BB-NEX-21]** While Increment B's kernel gate (KE4) is unlanded, the harness shall still
  execute the windowed queries at a scale small enough to complete, in order to produce the
  state-growth finding — the absence of the eviction primitive is a result, not a reason to skip
  the query.

### Unwanted behaviour

- **[BB-NEX-22]** If event generation is on the measured path and generation cost is a
  non-negligible fraction of the measured interval, then the harness shall mark the run
  **unreportable** and shall state generation cost as the reason.
- **[BB-NEX-23]** If a query cannot be expressed on the operator set available at run time, then
  the harness shall record it as **not-expressible**, name the specific missing capability, and
  shall not substitute an approximation that changes the query's semantics.
- **[BB-NEX-24]** If run-to-run variance exceeds the threshold the harness declares for the run
  mode, then the harness shall mark the run **unreportable** and shall record the observed
  variance rather than a mean.
- **[BB-NEX-25]** If a run's reference comparison is skipped for any reason, then the harness
  shall mark the run **unverified** and no downstream document shall cite its number.
- **[BB-NEX-26]** If a result would be compared against a published third-party Nexmark figure,
  then the harness's record shall first state every configuration difference known to affect
  comparability (scale factor, semantics deviations per `[BB-NEX-06]`, durability mode, hardware),
  and shall refuse the comparison if any deviation is material.
- **[BB-NEX-27]** If an exclusive payload (`Owned`/`Leased`) would enter a benchmark graph, then
  the harness shall reject the graph at construction time, because benchmark ingest must not
  become a path on which an exclusive can be dropped.
- **[BB-NEX-28]** If the harness's own findings would require a change to
  `doc/spec/90-roadmap/91-gap-analysis.md` or `doc/spec/CONCORDANCE.md`, then the harness's
  operator shall write to `doc/bench/findings.md` instead and shall leave both files untouched.

### Optional feature

- **[BB-NEX-29]** Where the KE2 sink-side ack slice is available, the harness shall measure
  end-to-end write-to-visible latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) and shall record the ack semantics
  the measurement relies on.
- **[BB-NEX-30]** Where the KE2 ack slice is not available, the harness may use sink-side
  observation as a latency stopgap, and shall label every such figure **sink-observed, not
  acked**.
- **[BB-NEX-31]** Where KBLK (bulk/benchmark host mode) is available, the harness shall offer a
  run mode with WAL off or asynchronous and the batched ingress path enabled, and shall record
  which mode produced each figure.
- **[BB-NEX-32]** Where KE4 has landed, the harness shall additionally report, for each windowed
  query, the retained-state bound achieved under waterline eviction and the count of elements
  dropped as late.

### Complex

- **[BB-NEX-33]** When a windowed query is run, while KE4's eviction is enabled and a late element
  arrives beyond the waterline, the harness shall record the element as dropped-late, shall verify
  the sink still equals the reference answer computed **under the same lateness policy**, and
  shall report both the drop count and the policy — a reference answer computed without the policy
  is not a valid oracle.
- **[BB-NEX-34]** When a run is executed on a real-threads `ManagedHost`, while fan-out on any
  outlet exceeds the degree BEN1's fan-out curve covers, the harness shall cite the BEN1 curve for
  that degree in its record, or shall state that the degree is uncovered by existing measurement.
- **[BB-NEX-35]** When a query's result differs from the reference answer, if the difference is
  confined to a transient permitted by the spec (for example an outer-join transient), then the
  harness shall re-observe after quiescence before declaring failure, and shall record that a
  transient was observed; if the difference survives quiescence, `[BB-NEX-12]` applies unchanged.
- **[BB-NEX-36]** When Increment B adds a query, if that query requires new harness machinery
  rather than only new graph assembly, then the harness's operator shall record the requirement as
  a defect in Increment A's design before implementing it.

---

## 6. Behaviour specifications

Each is specific enough to become a named test in
`bench/src/test/kotlin/civictech/bench/nexmark/`.

**BS-1 — Generator determinism (`[BB-NEX-03]`)**
*Given* a seed `S`, scale factor `F` and event count `N`,
*when* the generator is run twice in the same JVM and once in a fresh JVM,
*then* all three event sequences are element-wise identical, including the interleaving of
Person/Auction/Bid and every skewed field.

**BS-2 — Q3 equals its reference answer (`[BB-NEX-11]`)**
*Given* a Q3 graph built from `joinSet` + `FilterCell` and a 10 000-event prefix,
*when* the graph is driven to quiescence with `SimWorld.runToIdle`,
*then* the observed sink set equals `NexmarkReference.q3(prefix)` exactly, with no ordering
assumption imposed on set-shaped results.

**BS-3 — Retraction direction is measured, not assumed (`[BB-NEX-10]`)**
*Given* a Q4 graph containing a retraction-aware aggregate,
*when* a prefix is applied and then a suffix of retractions removing half the auctions is applied,
*then* the sink equals the reference answer over the reduced input, and the run record carries a
separate retraction-direction figure.

**BS-4 — A wall becomes a finding, not a fix (`[BB-NEX-13]`, `[BB-NEX-28]`)**
*Given* a Q7 run whose retained group count grows without bound,
*when* the run terminates on the harness's state ceiling,
*then* the run is recorded as a state-bound wall, a dated entry naming the pulled KE4 trigger
appears in `doc/bench/findings.md`, and the diff contains no change to `kernel/`,
`91-gap-analysis.md` or `CONCORDANCE.md`.

**BS-5 — Late element without eviction converges (`[BB-NEX-15]`, `[BB-NEX-18]`)**
*Given* a tumbling-window Q7 graph with KE4 absent,
*when* an event with an event time inside an already-emitted window is applied after that window
has produced output,
*then* the sink converges to the reference answer that includes the late element, and the run is
labelled unbounded-state.

**BS-6 — Late element with eviction is dropped and declared (`[BB-NEX-33]`)**
*Given* the same graph with waterline eviction enabled and the waterline advanced past the
window,
*when* the late event is applied,
*then* the element is counted as dropped-late, the sink equals the reference answer computed under
the same lateness policy, and the record states the policy.

**BS-7 — Unreportable beats optimistic (`[BB-NEX-22]`, `[BB-NEX-24]`)**
*Given* a run configured so that generation happens inside the measured interval,
*when* the run completes,
*then* the harness emits an `unreportable` record naming generation cost, and emits no throughput
number in any field a report could read.

**BS-8 — Reference skipped means unverified (`[BB-NEX-25]`)**
*Given* a run mode that disables reference comparison for speed,
*when* the run completes,
*then* the record carries `verified = false` and any attempt to render it into a findings entry
fails a harness-side check.

**BS-9 — Exclusive payloads are refused at construction (`[BB-NEX-27]`)**
*Given* a query graph whose element type is `Owned<Bid>`,
*when* the graph is constructed,
*then* construction fails with a message naming the exclusive payload rule, and no host is
started.

**BS-10 — Simulated drive reports no latency (`[BB-NEX-19]`)**
*Given* a run driven by `SimulationController`,
*when* the record is produced,
*then* every latency field is absent (not zero, not null-with-a-default), and the record states
the scheduler used.

**BS-11 — Q1–Q3 slice stands alone (`[BB-NEX-09]`)**
*Given* a tree in which no KE4, KE2 or KBLK code exists,
*when* the Increment A test suite is run,
*then* it passes in full, produces reference-verified results for Q1, Q2 and Q3, and no test is
skipped for a missing kernel capability.

**BS-12 — No window operator was written (`[BB-NEX-14]`)**
*Given* the BB-NEX source tree,
*when* it is inspected for window assignment,
*then* every window key is derived through `Windows.tumbling`/`Windows.sliding` and there is no
`:bench`-local class implementing window assignment, timers, or wall-clock reads.

---

## 7. Suggested task decomposition (list only — do not create these beads)

Increment A (no kernel gate):

1. `:bench` Nexmark package skeleton + event model (`NexmarkEvents.kt`), `Serializable`, with the
   targeted specification revision recorded in one place.
2. Deterministic seeded generator with the published skew parameters; determinism test (BS-1).
3. Run protocol + record type: metadata capture per `[BB-NEX-05]`, `unreportable`/`unverified`
   states, findings-entry rendering with the `[BB-NEX-25]` guard.
4. `NexmarkReference` batch recompute for Q1–Q4.
5. Q1 and Q2 graphs (`mapSet`, `FilterCell`) + reference tests.
6. Q3 graph (`joinSet` + filter) + reference test (BS-2); retraction-direction coverage (BS-3).
7. JMH bodies for Q1–Q3 in `bench/src/jmh/kotlin`, behind `:bench:jmh`.
8. First findings entry: the Q1–Q3 comparability baseline, with every `[BB-NEX-06]` deviation
   enumerated.
9. Q4 as an Increment A stretch, if its retraction path is clean.

Increment B (gated on KE4; KBLK improves fidelity):

10. Q5 / Q7 / Q8 graphs over `Windows.sliding`/`tumbling` + `GroupByCell` + `Aggregators.topK`.
11. State-growth measurement and the unbounded-state finding (BS-4, BS-5) — runnable *before* KE4
    lands, and the reason `[BB-NEX-21]` exists.
12. Post-KE4: waterline-eviction bound, dropped-late accounting, policy-matched reference (BS-6).
13. KBLK run mode and the WAL-bound/bulk-mode comparison.
14. Optional: KE2-acked latency percentiles, or the labelled sink-observed stopgap.

---

## 8. Verification

- `./gradlew :bench:test` — reference-comparison and determinism tests; must stay in the default
  lane and sub-second-ish per BEN1's convention.
- `./gradlew test` — the repository-wide gate; its wall-clock must be unchanged by this feature.
- `./gradlew :bench:jmh` — the measurement run, never part of `build`/`check`/`test` and never a
  required CI check.
- Manual review that the diff touches only `bench/` and `doc/bench/findings.md`.
- Manual review that §3.1's "do not rebuild" list has no counterpart implementation in `bench/`.

---

## 9. Risks and open questions

- **Reference-answer cost.** A naive recompute over a large prefix may be slower than the run it
  verifies. Mitigation: verify at small scale, measure at large scale, and record which prefix was
  verified (`[BB-NEX-25]` makes the unverified case explicit rather than silent).
- **Semantic deviation creep.** Nexmark's queries assume SQL-ish bag semantics; ComputeNet's
  operator family is set/tagged-multiset shaped. `[BB-NEX-06]` forces each deviation to be stated,
  but an accumulation of individually-defensible deviations can quietly destroy comparability.
  Open question: is there a deviation budget beyond which the suite stops claiming comparability?
- **KE4's shape is not yet fixed.** `[BB-NEX-33]`'s policy-matched oracle assumes the eviction
  policy is observable to the harness. If KE4 lands with an opaque policy, that is itself a
  finding.
- **Which Nexmark revision.** The Beam and Flink variants differ from the original Nexmark paper
  in query numbering and definitions. `[BB-NEX-01]` requires picking one; the choice determines
  which published figures are comparable at all.
- **Machine noise.** Numbers from shared CI runners are regression smell only, never findings
  material (BEN1 §6 already states this); BB-NEX inherits that rule and `[BB-NEX-24]` is its
  enforcement.
acceptance_criteria: Increment A closes on [BB-NEX-01..14], [BB-NEX-19], [BB-NEX-22..28], [BB-NEX-35] with Q1-Q3 reference-verified. Increment B closes on [BB-NEX-15..18], [BB-NEX-21], [BB-NEX-32..34] plus [BB-NEX-29..31] where their optional gates landed. Behaviour specs BS-1..BS-12 exist as named tests. No diff outside bench/ and doc/bench/findings.md; no concord/corpus/ scenario added; no requirement asserts a performance number.
notes: Filed from computenet-milestone-plan.md sections 1 (BB-NEX row), 3 (Nexmark row of the kernel-enablement matrix), 5 rank 7 (Q1-Q3 slice) and rank 19, 6 (standing hygiene). Wired dep: BEN1 (computenet-x9e). UNWIRED deps, being created by other agents - wire when their ids exist: KE4 (event-time waterline eviction; the only kernel blocker for windowed queries), KBLK (bulk/benchmark host mode; throughput fidelity), KE2 ack slice (optional; end-to-end latency percentiles). The Q1-Q3 slice (Increment A) is separately schedulable and has NO unlanded kernel dependency - that is section 5 rank 7's whole point.

title: BB — Benchmark bridge (standardized suites as acceptance corpora)
description:
# BB — Benchmark bridge

Umbrella epic for the standardized-suite lane (BB-*) defined in §1 and §3 of
`computenet-milestone-plan.md`.

## Ambition / Why

Each BB suite doubles as the acceptance corpus for its kernel or product parent. The
lane's actual product is **findings, not numbers**: per §6 of the milestone plan, every
suite run that hits a wall names the wall as a candidate G-item or pulls an existing
trigger. The numbers are a side effect.

The plan's §3 conclusion is what makes this a coherent epic rather than six unrelated
benchmarks: across all six suites the net new kernel surface is **KE1, KE4, KE5** (already
planned), plus two small chunks (KAGG-R, KBLK) and one generalization (KRD). The benchmark
ambition adds almost no kernel scope — it adds *pull* to scope that was already queued.
This epic exists to keep that pull visible and attributed.

## Children

Requirements live in the child features. This epic adds no EARS ids of its own.

Currently parented:

1. **BB-TPCC — TPC-C bridge document.** Doc-only, no dependencies, runnable now.
   Deliberately a negative-result study: what ComputeNet lacks to be an interactive
   multi-key transactional system, and whether it should want to be. Its real product is an
   EARS specification sketch of the missing primitive (interactive cross-cell transactions
   with abort), from which a future G-item can be written.

Expected future children, each firing when its parents land (do not create speculatively):

2. **BB-NEX** — Nexmark. Q1–Q3 runnable on today's operators once BEN1's harness exists;
   windowed queries need KE4; honest throughput needs KBLK.
3. **BB-YCSB** — needs KRD (via V1C-KERNEL) + KE1 + KBLK; ordered scan needs KAGG-R.
4. **BB-TPCH** — incremental TPC-H; needs QRY1 + KE1 + KAGG-R, with ORA1 as cross-check.
5. **BB-SNB** — hosted by SOC1's artifact; needs KRD + KAGG-R; BI adds KE5.
6. **BB-GRA** — Graphalytics; needs KE5 + KBLK.

## Findings this epic owns

Discovered while specifying BB-TPCC; they constrain the whole lane:

- **There is no abort verb anywhere in `doc/spec/20-*` or `40-*`.** Emission is
  effective-only; RESTART is specified as "restore + re-baseline, never a bare local
  rollback". The missing primitive is not a coverage gap — the model has no vocabulary
  for it.
- **`93` Candidate C (cross-host 2PC) was already considered and not adopted.** Any
  proposal in this lane is re-opening a settled question and must say why.
- **`demo/exchange` does not prove atomicity** despite being the composition probe — it
  proves convergence of a partitioned `GroupBy(sum)`. Do not cite it as evidence of
  transactional behaviour.
- **`QuorumSetCell` is a presence-count threshold fold, not a voting protocol** — the
  "coordinator-cell over quorum cells" candidate has less existing substrate than the
  plan's phrasing suggests.

## Scope boundaries

- This epic is an organizing parent. It builds nothing itself.
- No suite may quietly grow kernel scope. A wall is filed as a finding or a candidate
  G-item; it is not solved in-lane.
- Per §6: findings go to the lane's own append-only findings file. Never edit
  `91-gap-analysis.md` or `CONCORDANCE.md` directly.
- Benchmark numbers are machine-dependent and therefore not implementation-neutral: BB
  suites do not add `concord/corpus/` scenarios.

## Exit criteria

Per-child. This epic closes when every child that has been scheduled has closed and the
lane's findings file records, for each suite run, either a clean result or the named wall.

# TTD1 — Time-travel core: journal reader, offline reconstruction, run diffing

Lane: product. Source: `computenet-milestone-plan.md` §1 product row TTD1, §2 DAG (`TTD1 --> TTD2`),
§5 rank 12 — *"high demo value, low urgency"*. Depends on: nothing. Unblocks: **TTD2** (scrubbing UI
in the inspector, which also needs WKB1 — already delivered by inspector-v4 waves 1–6).

---

## 1. Ambition / Why

A ComputeNet run is already fully described on disk for every durable cell: `ManagedHost` appends
**every accepted invocation as a wire frame** to its per-cell journal before staging it
(`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/ManagedHost.kt:606,639`), plus checkpoint blobs and
`Effectful` processed-frontier advances (`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/HostDurability.kt`).
Today exactly one thing can read that file: a live `ManagedHost` recovering itself. The journal is a
recovery artifact and nothing else.

That is a waste of the best debugging asset the system has. Dataflow bugs are *history* bugs: a view
converged to the wrong fold, a wave released torn, a retraction resurrected a removed element, an
`Effectful` sink fired twice. The question a developer actually has is never "what does the state
look like now" — the inspector already answers that (WKB1) — it is **"what did this cell look like
three waves before it went wrong, and what did the previous run do differently there?"**

TTD1 makes the journal a *first-class readable history*:

1. **A journal reader.** Open a `Journal` (file or in-memory) without a host and get a typed,
   ordered, indexed record stream: frames with their `(cellRef, portName)`, wave coordinate
   `(sourceId, counter)`, and args; checkpoints with the cells they restore; frontier advances with
   the inlet they belong to. Structural reading must work even when the application's `@Contract`
   descriptors are absent — `WireCodec.decode` needs `ContractRegistry`, the raw `WireFrame` JSON
   does not.
2. **Offline state reconstruction.** Rebuild the graph off-process and drive the journal prefix up
   to an arbitrary wave/frontier cut, producing the `Stateful` snapshot every reconstructible cell
   held at that point. Not an approximation of recovery — *the recovery path itself*, stopped early.
3. **Run diffing.** Two journals of two runs of the same graph (a good run and a bad one, a
   pre-change run and a post-change one) aligned by wave coordinate, with the first divergence
   located and reported: which cell, which wave, which record, what the two states were.
4. **A CLI.** `inspect`, `reconstruct`, `diff` as commands over journal directories, so the whole
   thing is usable in a terminal on a crash artifact from CI before any UI exists.

**What TTD2 needs from this, specifically.** TTD2 is a scrubber: a timeline the user drags, with the
inspector's existing graph/cell/state panes re-rendering at the scrubbed position. That needs, from
TTD1: (a) an *enumerable, addressable* timeline — a stable ordered list of positions with wave
coordinates and human-meaningful labels; (b) `stateAt(position)` cheap enough to call repeatedly
while dragging, which means checkpoint-anchored replay and a reusable cursor, not a fresh
full-journal replay per frame; (c) state rendered in a shape the inspector's existing `CellState` /
`ValueEncoder` DTOs (`inspect/src/main/kotlin/civictech/inspect/Dto.kt`, `ValueEncoder.kt`) can
serve without a second encoding vocabulary; and (d) an explicit *fidelity* answer per cell, so the
scrubber can grey out what it cannot honestly show instead of drawing a plausible lie. TTD1 owns all
four; TTD2 owns only routes and UI.

**The honesty boundary is the point of the epic, not a caveat.** Un-suppressed replay through the
ordinary decode path is sound exactly for the replay-stable idempotent vocabulary the spec names
(`doc/spec/20-dataflow-semantics/24-data-cells.md` §Durability spectrum, "Boundary of the landed
mechanism", 93 I-7): ref-derived tags and PN slots, idempotent merges, anti-entropy dedup. Outside
it — wall-clock/random logic, spontaneously-emitting sources, `Effectful` sinks (C-9/G-59) — a
reconstruction is not the run. A debugger that silently shows a plausible-but-wrong past is worse
than no debugger. Every reconstructed value TTD1 emits carries a fidelity verdict, and a cell it
cannot faithfully reconstruct is reported as such and never given a value.

---

## 2. What we build

### Module

A **new leaf Gradle module `timetravel/` (`:timetravel`)**, added to `settings.gradle.kts` beside
`:inspect`, with `implementation(project(":kernel"))`, `implementation(libs.kotlinx.serialization)`
(the journal frame encoding is kotlinx JSON), `testImplementation(project(":testkit"))`. Package
`civictech.timetravel`.

Justification (fuller argument in the design field):
- **Not `:kernel`** — the kernel is the runtime; a journal *analysis* tool with a CLI entry point,
  a diff model and a report format is not runtime surface, and `AGENTS.md` warns against growing
  the kernel SCC.
- **Not `:inspect`** — `:inspect` is a read-only view of a *live host process* and depends on
  `:demo:shell` for its HTTP/SSE transport. Time travel is headless and offline; forcing it through
  `:inspect` would drag an HTTP server into a CLI and invert the TTD2 dependency. TTD2 later adds
  `:inspect -> :timetravel`, which is the right direction.
- **Not `:testkit`** — this is a product deliverable, not test scaffolding.
- **Leaf** — nothing depends on it yet; `:kernel` must not gain a dependency on it, ever.

### Surface

1. **`JournalReader`** — opens a `Journal` (or a journal file path) and yields an ordered
   `List<JournalRecord>` / `Sequence<JournalRecord>` with 0-based indices matching
   `HostDurability.recoverFrom`'s own record numbering (so a `RecoveryIncomplete.recordIndex` from a
   real crash names the same record the reader shows). `JournalRecord` is a sealed hierarchy:
   `FrameRecord` (cellRef, portName, type, wave coordinate, contract/method ids, decoded args when
   descriptors are present, raw JSON otherwise), `CheckpointRecord` (the cell refs it restores, and
   whether each snapshot deserialized), `FrontierRecord` (cellRef, portName, `(sourceId, counter)`),
   `UnknownRecord` (unrecognized leading type byte), `TornRecord` (a truncated trailing record).
2. **`RunTimeline`** — the addressable position model: records folded into positions carrying wave
   coordinate `(sourceId, counter)`, record index, the cells touched, and checkpoint anchors. This
   is what TTD2's scrubber indexes.
3. **`Reconstructor`** — `stateAt(position): Reconstruction`. Rebuilds the graph from a
   caller-supplied `GraphSpec` (or an app-supplied graph-building lambda), spawns onto a private
   `ManagedHost` driven by a `SimulationController`, and replays the journal *prefix* up to the
   position via the real `HostDurability.recoverFrom` path — see §3. Returns per cell: the
   `Stateful.snapshot()` blob, a rendered value view, and a `Fidelity` verdict.
4. **`Fidelity`** — per-cell verdict: `FAITHFUL`, `DEGRADED(reasons)`, `UNRECONSTRUCTIBLE(reasons)`,
   with machine-readable reasons (`EFFECTFUL_CELL`, `VOLATILE_CELL`, `NO_DESCRIPTOR`,
   `NONDETERMINISTIC_SOURCE`, `CHECKPOINT_UNDESERIALIZABLE`, `JOURNAL_TORN`, `GRAPH_MISMATCH`,
   `WIRE_VERSION_MISMATCH`, `COMPACTED_AWAY`).
5. **`RunDiff`** — aligns two `RunTimeline`s and reports `RunDiffReport`: aligned prefix length,
   first divergent position, divergence class (record-level: a frame present in one run and not the
   other, different args, different wave ordering; state-level: same position, different
   reconstructed state), and per-cell state deltas at the divergence. Output as a stable
   `@Serializable` DTO with a JSON encoder and a human text renderer.
6. **CLI `civictech.timetravel.Main`** — `timetravel inspect <journal>`, `timetravel reconstruct
   <journal> --at <position> [--graph <spec>]`, `timetravel diff <journalA> <journalB>`; `--json`
   for machine output on all three. Exit codes distinguish "ran, no divergence", "ran, divergence
   found", and "could not read".

---

## 3. How, using ComputeNet

Every step below is anchored in code that exists today. Nothing here invents a parallel durability
model, and nothing changes the journal format.

**The record framing is already fully determined and must be read, not redefined.**
`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/durability/Journal.kt` defines `Journal` (`append`, `replay`,
`reset`), `InMemoryJournal`, and `FileJournal` — length-prefixed records in one append-only file
(`writeInt(size)` then bytes), fsync per append, `reset` writing a temp file and atomically renaming
(checkpoint compaction), and a torn trailing record silently dropped on replay.
`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/HostDurability.kt` owns the record *types*: a leading
byte `1` = frame (`WireCodec.encode(HostedPortInvocation)` — kotlinx JSON `WireFrame`), `2` =
checkpoint (Java-serialized `CheckpointRecord(state: Map<CellRef, Serializable>, frontier:
Map<Pair<CellRef,String>, Map<UUID,Long>>)`), `3` = frontier (Java-serialized `FrontierRecord(cellRef,
portName, timestamp)`). Those three constants and the two payload records are currently `private` /
file-private in `HostDurability.kt`; TTD1's **only** permitted kernel change is the minimal
visibility/accessor work needed to read them from `:timetravel` without copy-pasting the framing —
prefer a small `internal`→`public` read-side accessor or a dedicated read-only decoder placed in
`civictech.cell.durability`, over duplicating the byte layout in a second module where it can drift.

**Wave / frontier coordinates come from `MessageContext`.**
`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/MessageContext.kt:16` — `Timestamp(sourceId: UUID, counter:
Long)`; `:50` — `MessageContext(timestamp, sourcePort, reBaseline, baseline: TagFrontier?, hop)`.
A frame's wave coordinate is `frame.context?.timestamp`; a *root* frame driven externally carries no
context at all (`HostDurability.baselined` documents exactly this), so the timeline must handle
context-free frames as positions addressed by record index alone. Wave order is per-source counter
order — the invariant `WaveFrontier`
(`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/consistency/WaveFrontier.kt`) already folds against. A
"frontier cut" position is therefore a `Map<UUID, Long>` (the same shape as `TagFrontier.perSource`),
and the journal prefix for that cut is every record whose context timestamp is at or behind it, in
journal order.

**Reconstruction reuses the recovery path; it does not reimplement it.** `ManagedHost.recoverFrom`
(`ManagedHost.kt:672`) delegates to `HostDurability.recoverFrom`, which replays checkpoint restores,
frontier restores, and frames re-entering the ordinary intake inside one `ReplayScope`, stamped as
catch-up baselines (`replayAsBaseline = true`, PN-2). TTD1 constructs a `ManagedHost` with a
`SimulationController` scheduler (`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/SimulationController.kt`
— the same deterministic driver `CrashRecoveryTest` uses), applies the caller's `GraphSpec`
(`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/graph/GraphDsl.kt` — `GraphSpec(steps)`, `applyTo`), then
calls `recoverFrom` against an `InMemoryJournal` seeded with the *prefix* of the real journal's
records, and drives to idle. State is read via `Stateful.snapshot()`. That is exactly the sequence
`[24-DUR-02]` mandates ("rebuild the graph, then `recoverFrom` restores the latest checkpoint's
`Stateful` snapshots and replays the frame tail"), and it is why reconstruction inherits recovery's
correctness for free: any divergence between reconstruction and recovery is a bug in one of them,
not a modelling choice.

**The graph is not in the journal — this is a hard, spec-stated constraint.**
`doc/spec/20-dataflow-semantics/24-data-cells.md` §Durability spectrum states plainly that the
shipped journal "appends every intake frame (management included) and does not journal topology at
all — the graph is rebuilt out-of-band before `recoverFrom`". So a reconstruction *requires* a graph
source, supplied by the caller: a `GraphSpec`, or an app-level structure log (the pattern
`demo/agora/src/main/kotlin/civictech/agora/AgoraService.kt:84,111` already uses — a `graph.jsonl`
replayed before `recoverFrom`, wired in `AgoraApp.kt:39`). TTD1 accepts both and **refuses to guess**
when neither is available.

**Descriptors gate arg decoding.** `WireCodec.decode`
(`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/wire/WireCodec.kt:262`) checks `frame.version == VERSION`
(currently 2) and requires `ContractRegistry.method(contractId, methodId)` to resolve — absent the
application's KSP-generated descriptors, decode throws. The reader's structural layer parses the
`WireFrame` JSON directly (cellRef, portName, type, context, contract/method ids, raw args) and
works without them; the hydration layer uses `WireCodec.decode` and is only available when the app's
classes are on the classpath. Reconstruction needs hydration; `inspect` and record-level `diff` do
not.

**Per-cell journals are the norm, not the exception.** `journalFor: (CellRef) -> Journal?` (CP-C1,
`ManagedHost.kt:86`) means a journal holds only its own cells' records (`[24-DUR-03]`) and a
`null` selector makes a cell volatile — never journaled, never replayed (`[24-DUR-01]`). A volatile
cell has no history and must be reported `UNRECONSTRUCTIBLE(VOLATILE_CELL)`, not silently omitted.
A journal *directory* may therefore hold several journals; the CLI takes a directory and reads each.

**`Effectful` and C-9.** `Effectful` is the marker at
`kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/evolve/Evolution.kt:22`. G-59 (which closes C-9) gives each
`Effectful` inlet a durable processed-frontier — the last applied `(sourceId, counter)` per
`(cellRef, portName)` — consulted by both replay and live delivery, so an invocation at or behind it
is dropped as already-acted rather than re-driving the sink (`[24-DUR-05]`;
`doc/spec/30-execution-model/31-hosts.md:101,245`; `doc/spec/90-roadmap/91-gap-analysis.md:18`). For
TTD1 this cuts two ways and both must be honoured: the frontier records are *readable history* (they
tell the reader which effects were actually applied, which is genuinely useful in a debugger), and
they are *not* a licence to re-execute an effectful cell offline. TTD1 reconstructs the *state* of
`Effectful` cells at best `DEGRADED` and never fires their effects — offline reconstruction runs with
their effect inlets suppressed, and says so.

---

## 4. Scope boundaries

**In scope:** reading journals; reconstructing state offline at an arbitrary position; diffing two
runs; a CLI; the fidelity model; the minimal kernel visibility change needed to read the record
framing without duplicating it.

**Explicitly NOT in scope:**

- **The scrubbing UI — that is TTD2.** No `:inspect` routes, no `inspect/ui` changes, no SSE. TTD1
  must leave a Kotlin API TTD2 can wrap; it must not pre-build TTD2's HTTP contract.
- **Effect replay semantics — that is C-9 / G-59 / KFX territory.** TTD1 does not change how the
  processed-frontier is written, consulted, or recovered; it only *reads* frontier records and
  refuses to re-fire effects.
- **Journal format changes.** No new record types, no version bump, no segmentation or rotation
  (that residual is trigger-gated in `doc/spec/20-dataflow-semantics/24-data-cells.md` and in
  `FileJournal`'s own ponytail note), no group commit, no streaming-replay rewrite of `FileJournal`.
  If TTD1 wants a thing the format cannot express, it files a finding — it does not extend the
  format.
- **Journaling topology.** 93 I-7's decided classification (journal `PORT_API` data plus topology
  events) still diverges from the landed tee. Closing that divergence would make TTD1 much nicer and
  is precisely why it is out of scope here: it is a kernel-lane durability change with its own
  spec argument. TTD1 takes the graph from the caller and files the pain as a finding.
- **Live-run capture, tracing, or a new event log.** TTD1 reads what durability already writes.
- **Non-deterministic and effectful re-execution.** Not attempted, not approximated — reported.
- **Writing to journals.** Absolutely not: no `append`, no `reset`, no compaction, no repair of a
  torn file.
- **Distributed/multi-host run reconstruction.** One host's journals per run. Cross-host causal
  alignment is a later chunk if the demo demands it.

---

## 5. Functional requirements (EARS)

Ids are epic-scoped (`[TTD1-nn]`) and deliberately do **not** collide with normative
`doc/spec/` ids (`[NN-SLUG-nn]`). Where a requirement makes an existing normative requirement true,
the spec id is cited in parentheses. "The reader" = `:timetravel`'s journal-reading layer; "the
reconstructor" = its offline state-reconstruction layer; "the differ" = its run-diffing layer; "the
CLI" = its command-line entry point; "the module" = `:timetravel` as a whole.

### A. Reading a journal

- `[TTD1-01]` The reader shall present a journal's records in journal order, 0-based, using the same
  record indices `HostDurability.recoverFrom` reports in `RecoveryIncomplete.recordIndex`. (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD1-02]` The reader shall classify each record by its leading type byte into frame, checkpoint,
  or frontier, matching `HostDurability`'s `RECORD_FRAME`/`RECORD_CHECKPOINT`/`RECORD_FRONTIER`
  encoding. (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD1-03]` The reader shall expose, for every frame record, the `cellRef`, `portName`,
  `HostedPortInvocation.Type`, contract id, method id, and the `MessageContext` when the frame carries
  one — parsed from the `WireFrame` JSON without requiring the application's `ContractRegistry`
  descriptors. (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD1-04]` Where the application's `@Contract` descriptors are on the classpath, the reader shall
  additionally expose each frame's decoded method name and arguments via `WireCodec.decode`.
  (Optional feature)
- `[TTD1-05]` If a frame's contract/method ids do not resolve in `ContractRegistry`, then the reader
  shall present that frame at structural fidelity, mark it `NO_DESCRIPTOR`, and continue reading
  subsequent records. (Unwanted behaviour)
- `[TTD1-06]` If a frame's `version` field differs from `WireCodec.VERSION`, then the reader shall
  report `WIRE_VERSION_MISMATCH` naming both versions and shall not decode that frame's arguments.
  (Unwanted behaviour)
- `[TTD1-07]` The reader shall expose, for every checkpoint record, the set of `CellRef`s whose
  `Stateful` snapshots it carries and the `(cellRef, portName) -> (sourceId -> counter)`
  processed-frontier map it carries. (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD1-08]` If a checkpoint record's payload cannot be deserialized, then the reader shall report
  `CHECKPOINT_UNDESERIALIZABLE` with the record index and shall continue reading subsequent records.
  (Unwanted behaviour)
- `[TTD1-09]` The reader shall expose, for every frontier record, its `cellRef`, `portName`, and
  `(sourceId, counter)`. (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD1-10]` If a record carries an unrecognized leading type byte, then the reader shall emit an
  `UnknownRecord` for it, carrying the byte and the record index, and shall continue. (Unwanted behaviour)
- `[TTD1-11]` If a journal file ends in a truncated record (a length prefix with fewer bytes
  following, or a partial length prefix), then the reader shall report the truncation with the index
  of the last intact record, present every intact record before it, and mark the run `JOURNAL_TORN`.
  (Unwanted behaviour)
- `[TTD1-12]` The reader shall never write to, truncate, rename, or lock a journal file, and shall
  open journal files read-only. (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD1-13]` Where a journal directory contains multiple journal files (the per-cell `journalFor`
  tee, CP-C1), the reader shall read each independently and attribute every record to its own
  journal. (Optional feature; makes `[24-DUR-03]` observable)
- `[TTD1-14]` While a journal is being read, the module shall not construct any host, scheduler, or
  cell — reading is a pure decode. (State-driven)

### B. The timeline / positions

- `[TTD1-15]` The reader shall derive a `RunTimeline` of addressable positions, each carrying its
  record index, its wave coordinate `(sourceId, counter)` when the record carries a
  `MessageContext`, and the `CellRef`s the record touches. (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD1-16]` The timeline shall order positions by journal order, which for waved frames is
  per-source counter order — the ordering `WaveFrontier` folds against. (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD1-17]` Where a frame carries no `MessageContext` (an externally-driven root frame), the
  timeline shall address it by record index alone and shall not synthesize a wave coordinate for it.
  (Optional feature)
- `[TTD1-18]` The timeline shall accept a position expressed either as a record index or as a
  per-source frontier cut (`Map<UUID, Long>`, the `TagFrontier.perSource` shape) and shall resolve a
  frontier cut to the longest journal prefix whose waved frames are all at or behind that cut.
  (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD1-19]` The timeline shall identify every checkpoint position as a reconstruction anchor.
  (Ubiquitous)

### C. Offline reconstruction

- `[TTD1-20]` When asked to reconstruct at a position, the reconstructor shall rebuild the graph from
  the caller-supplied graph source, then invoke the kernel's own `recoverFrom` over the journal prefix
  for that position — it shall not reimplement checkpoint restore or frame replay. (Event-driven;
  makes `[24-DUR-02]` true offline)
- `[TTD1-21]` The reconstructor shall drive reconstruction on a deterministic scheduler
  (`SimulationController`) and shall drive to idle before reading state. (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD1-22]` The reconstructor shall report, for each cell in the rebuilt graph, that cell's
  `Stateful.snapshot()` at the requested position together with a `Fidelity` verdict. (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD1-23]` If no graph source is supplied, then the reconstructor shall refuse to reconstruct and
  shall report that the journal carries no topology (the graph is rebuilt out-of-band —
  `doc/spec/20-dataflow-semantics/24-data-cells.md` §Durability spectrum). (Unwanted behaviour)
- `[TTD1-24]` If the supplied graph does not contain a `CellRef` the journal holds records for, then
  the reconstructor shall report `GRAPH_MISMATCH` naming that ref and shall not silently drop its
  records. (Unwanted behaviour)
- `[TTD1-25]` The reconstructor shall reconstruct a cell that is not `Stateful` as
  `UNRECONSTRUCTIBLE(NOT_STATEFUL)` rather than reporting an empty state. (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD1-26]` While reconstructing, the module shall suppress every `Effectful` cell's effect inlet,
  such that no externally visible side effect is caused by a reconstruction. (State-driven; respects
  the C-9/G-59 boundary)
- `[TTD1-27]` The reconstructor shall mark every `Effectful` cell's reconstructed state at most
  `DEGRADED(EFFECTFUL_CELL)`. (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD1-28]` The reconstructor shall mark a cell whose journal selector was `null` (volatile,
  `[24-DUR-01]`) as `UNRECONSTRUCTIBLE(VOLATILE_CELL)` when that is determinable from the graph
  source, and shall never present a value for it. (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD1-29]` Where a checkpoint anchor precedes the requested position, the reconstructor shall
  replay from the latest such anchor rather than from record 0. (Optional feature)
- `[TTD1-30]` When reconstructing successive positions from the same journal and graph, the
  reconstructor shall support advancing an existing reconstruction forward without rebuilding the
  graph, provided the new position is at or after the current one. (Event-driven; this is TTD2's
  scrub-drag requirement)
- `[TTD1-31]` If the requested position is before the current position of an advancing
  reconstruction, then the reconstructor shall restart from the nearest preceding anchor rather than
  rewinding state in place. (Unwanted behaviour)
- `[TTD1-32]` If `recoverFrom` throws `RecoveryIncomplete` during a reconstruction, then the
  reconstructor shall report the failing record index and total, shall mark every cell's fidelity at
  most `DEGRADED(RECOVERY_INCOMPLETE)`, and shall not present the partial replay as a complete
  reconstruction. (Unwanted behaviour)

### D. Fidelity and honesty

- `[TTD1-33]` The module shall attach a `Fidelity` verdict of `FAITHFUL`, `DEGRADED(reasons)`, or
  `UNRECONSTRUCTIBLE(reasons)` to every reconstructed cell state it emits. (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD1-34]` **If a cell's state cannot be faithfully reconstructed for any reason, then the module
  shall report `UNRECONSTRUCTIBLE` with machine-readable reasons and shall emit no value for that
  cell — it shall never present a plausible-but-unverified state as the run's actual past.**
  (Unwanted behaviour — the epic's central honesty requirement)
- `[TTD1-35]` The module shall mark `FAITHFUL` only a cell whose reconstruction stayed inside the
  replay-stable idempotent vocabulary the spec names — ref-derived tags and PN slots, tag counter as
  snapshot state, idempotent merges (`[24-DUR-04]`; `doc/spec/20-dataflow-semantics/24-data-cells.md`
  "Boundary of the landed mechanism"). (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD1-36]` If the journal was torn, contained an unknown record, or contained an undeserializable
  checkpoint at or before the requested position, then every cell's fidelity at that position shall be
  at most `DEGRADED`. (Unwanted behaviour)
- `[TTD1-37]` The module shall carry a run-level fidelity verdict that is no better than the worst
  per-cell verdict it reports. (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD1-38]` Where the module cannot determine whether a cell is deterministic, it shall report
  `DEGRADED(UNKNOWN_DETERMINISM)` rather than defaulting to `FAITHFUL`. (Optional feature; the
  conservative default is mandatory)

### E. Run diffing

- `[TTD1-39]` The differ shall accept two `RunTimeline`s and report an aligned prefix length and, when
  the runs diverge, the first divergent position in each. (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD1-40]` The differ shall align positions by wave coordinate `(sourceId, counter)` and
  `(cellRef, portName)` where both are present, and by record index only where they are not.
  (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD1-41]` The differ shall classify a divergence as one of: record present in one run only,
  same-position records with different frames, same-position frames with different arguments,
  different per-source wave ordering, or same-position reconstructions with different state.
  (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD1-42]` When both runs are reconstructible and diverge, the differ shall report the
  per-cell state difference at the first divergent position. (Event-driven)
- `[TTD1-43]` If the two runs' source ids differ entirely (different `sourceId` UUIDs on every
  frame), then the differ shall report that the runs are not wave-alignable and shall fall back to
  record-index alignment, saying so explicitly. (Unwanted behaviour)
- `[TTD1-44]` If either run is `UNRECONSTRUCTIBLE`, then the differ shall still report the
  record-level diff and shall report the state-level diff as unavailable with the reason.
  (Unwanted behaviour)
- `[TTD1-45]` The differ shall emit a `RunDiffReport` as a stable `@Serializable` DTO with both a
  JSON and a human-readable text rendering, such that the JSON form is diffable and assertable in
  tests. (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD1-46]` The differ shall be deterministic: two runs of the differ over the same pair of
  journals shall produce byte-identical JSON reports. (Ubiquitous)

### F. CLI and safety

- `[TTD1-47]` The CLI shall provide `inspect`, `reconstruct`, and `diff` commands over journal file
  or directory paths. (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD1-48]` The CLI shall support `--json` on every command, emitting the same DTOs the Kotlin API
  returns. (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD1-49]` The CLI shall exit `0` when it ran and found no divergence, `1` when it ran and found a
  divergence, and `2` when it could not read or reconstruct — distinguishable without parsing output.
  (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD1-50]` If a path passed to the CLI is not a readable journal, then the CLI shall report the
  path and the reason and shall exit `2`. (Unwanted behaviour)
- `[TTD1-51]` The module shall not open a network socket, bind a port, or serve HTTP. (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD1-52]` The module shall not modify the journal format, add a record type, or change
  `WireCodec.VERSION`. (Ubiquitous)
- `[TTD1-53]` `:kernel` shall not depend on `:timetravel`. (Ubiquitous)

**Verifiability note.** `[TTD1-35]` and `[TTD1-38]` are the two requirements whose honest check is
hardest: "did this cell stay inside the replay-stable vocabulary" is not decidable in general from a
`Cell` instance. They are checkable in the concrete form the module will implement — a positive
allow-list of kernel cell types known replay-stable (the `civictech.cell.data` family and its
operator algebra, per `[24-DUR-04]` and `CrashRecoveryTest`), everything else `DEGRADED` — and that
allow-list is itself testable. If a later agent finds it cannot check them honestly even in that
form, it files the fact in `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` (for any corpus-facing part) or as a bead —
it does not weaken the requirement into "the module shall attempt to assess fidelity".

---

## 6. Behaviour specifications

Each scenario should become a named test in `timetravel/src/test/kotlin/civictech/timetravel/`.
Corpus placement is called out where it applies.

### BS-1 — Reconstruct at an arbitrary wave, mid-run (happy path)
**Given** a durable single-host graph (a `SetCell` source feeding a union feeding a view) driven
under `SimulationController` with a fixed seed, journaled to an `InMemoryJournal`, with N adds
applied and the host driven to idle
**When** the journal is read and the view's state is reconstructed offline at the position of the
k-th add (0 < k < N), from a `GraphSpec` describing the same graph
**Then** the reconstructed view state equals the state the live run held immediately after the k-th
add (captured during the live run for comparison), and every cell reports `FAITHFUL`.
*Test:* `ReconstructAtWaveTest`. Covers `[TTD1-15]`, `[TTD1-18]`, `[TTD1-20]`, `[TTD1-22]`,
`[TTD1-33]`, `[TTD1-35]`.

### BS-2 — Reconstruct at a per-source frontier cut, multi-source
**Given** the same graph driven by two independent sources emitting interleaved waves, so the journal
holds frames from two `sourceId`s
**When** reconstruction is requested at the frontier cut `{sourceA: 3, sourceB: 1}`
**Then** the reconstruction includes every waved frame at or behind that cut and no frame beyond it
in either source, and the resulting view equals the batch fold of exactly those adds.
*Test:* `FrontierCutReconstructionTest`. Covers `[TTD1-16]`, `[TTD1-18]`.

### BS-3 — Reconstruction is the recovery path, not a lookalike
**Given** a journal from a run that crashed mid-burst (the `CrashRecoveryTest` shape)
**When** the same journal is (a) recovered by a live `ManagedHost.recoverFrom` and (b) reconstructed
offline at the final position
**Then** the two `Stateful.snapshot()` outputs are equal for every cell.
*Test:* `ReconstructionMatchesRecoveryTest`. Covers `[TTD1-20]`. **This is the epic's anchor
property** — it is what makes reconstruction trustworthy without a second correctness argument.

### BS-4 — Checkpoint anchor is used, and a snapshot-plus-tail journal reconstructs
**Given** a journal that has been checkpointed (`HostDurability.checkpoint` reset it to a single
checkpoint record) and then appended to with further frames
**When** reconstruction is requested at a position after the checkpoint
**Then** the reconstruction restores from the checkpoint and replays only the tail, and the result
equals a reconstruction of the same logical history from an uncompacted journal.
*Test:* `CheckpointAnchoredReconstructionTest`. Covers `[TTD1-19]`, `[TTD1-29]`. Corpus-adjacent:
`concord/corpus/15-durability/DUR-SNAPTAIL-01.yaml` already covers the kernel half.

### BS-5 — Truncated / partially-written journal
**Given** a `FileJournal` whose file has been truncated mid-record (both variants: a partial length
prefix, and a full length prefix with fewer payload bytes than declared)
**When** the reader opens it
**Then** every intact record before the tear is presented with its index, the tear is reported with
the index of the last intact record, the run is marked `JOURNAL_TORN`, no exception escapes, and a
reconstruction at any position is at most `DEGRADED`.
*Test:* `TornJournalTest`. Covers `[TTD1-11]`, `[TTD1-36]`.

### BS-6 — Unknown record type and undeserializable checkpoint
**Given** a journal into which a record with leading byte `9` and a checkpoint record with a
corrupted payload have been injected
**When** the reader opens it
**Then** the unknown record is reported as `UnknownRecord(9, index)`, the checkpoint is reported
`CHECKPOINT_UNDESERIALIZABLE(index)`, reading continues past both, and neither causes a silent skip.
*Test:* `MalformedRecordTest`. Covers `[TTD1-08]`, `[TTD1-10]`.

### BS-7 — A journal containing an effectful cell fires nothing and says so
**Given** a durable graph containing an `Effectful` sink whose every applied invocation increments an
externally observed counter, journaled together with its processed-frontier records (the
`DUR-REPLAY-01` / `EffectfulRecoveryTest` shape)
**When** the run is reconstructed offline at its final position
**Then** the external counter is **unchanged** (no effect fired), the sink's state is reported at
most `DEGRADED(EFFECTFUL_CELL)`, and the reader still surfaces the frontier records showing which
`(sourceId, counter)` pairs the live run actually applied.
*Test:* `EffectfulReconstructionSuppressedTest`. Covers `[TTD1-09]`, `[TTD1-26]`, `[TTD1-27]`. The
kernel-side requirement it respects is `[24-DUR-05]`, already covered in
`concord/corpus/15-durability/DUR-REPLAY-01.yaml` (`covers: [24-DUR-01, 24-DUR-02, 24-DUR-05]`) —
**TTD1 adds no corpus scenario for it**; the corpus covers normative spec ids, and `[TTD1-nn]` ids
are epic-scoped, so a `covers: [TTD1-27]` would be a dangling id that fails `:concord:check`.

### BS-8 — Unreconstructible cell is named, never guessed
**Given** a graph where one cell's `journalFor` selector returned `null` (volatile) and another cell
is not `Stateful`
**When** a reconstruction is requested
**Then** the volatile cell reports `UNRECONSTRUCTIBLE(VOLATILE_CELL)`, the non-stateful cell reports
`UNRECONSTRUCTIBLE(NOT_STATEFUL)`, **neither carries a value field**, the run-level verdict is
`UNRECONSTRUCTIBLE`, and the reconstructible cells still report their own faithful states.
*Test:* `UnreconstructibleIsNamedTest`. Covers `[TTD1-25]`, `[TTD1-28]`, `[TTD1-34]`, `[TTD1-37]`.

### BS-9 — No graph source: refuse, don't infer
**Given** a journal and no `GraphSpec` and no structure log
**When** a reconstruction is requested
**Then** the reconstructor refuses, reporting that the journal carries no topology, and the CLI exits
`2`; `inspect` and record-level `diff` on the same journal still succeed.
*Test:* `NoGraphSourceRefusalTest`. Covers `[TTD1-23]`, `[TTD1-49]`, `[TTD1-50]`.

### BS-10 — Graph mismatch
**Given** a journal holding records for cell `X` and a `GraphSpec` that does not spawn `X`
**When** a reconstruction is requested
**Then** `GRAPH_MISMATCH(X)` is reported, `X`'s records are not silently discarded, and the run
verdict is at most `DEGRADED`.
*Test:* `GraphMismatchTest`. Covers `[TTD1-24]`.

### BS-11 — Diffing two runs that diverge
**Given** two journals from the same graph and the same seed, where run B applied one extra add at
wave `(sourceA, 4)` and otherwise identical input
**When** the two runs are diffed
**Then** the report names an aligned prefix ending at `(sourceA, 3)`, a first divergence at
`(sourceA, 4)` classified as "record present in run B only", and — since both runs reconstruct — the
per-cell state difference at that position, and the JSON report is byte-identical across repeated
runs.
*Test:* `RunDiffDivergenceTest`. Covers `[TTD1-39]`, `[TTD1-41]`, `[TTD1-42]`, `[TTD1-45]`,
`[TTD1-46]`.

### BS-12 — Diffing two runs that agree
**Given** two journals produced by two runs of the same seeded graph
**When** they are diffed
**Then** the report shows a full aligned prefix, no divergence, and the CLI exits `0`.
*Test:* `RunDiffIdenticalTest`. Covers `[TTD1-39]`, `[TTD1-49]`.

### BS-13 — Runs with disjoint source ids are not wave-alignable
**Given** two journals from two runs whose sources minted different `sourceId` UUIDs (the ordinary
case for two independent process starts)
**When** they are diffed
**Then** the report says explicitly that the runs are not wave-alignable, falls back to record-index
alignment, and does not present the index alignment as a wave alignment.
*Test:* `UnalignableRunsTest`. Covers `[TTD1-43]`.

### BS-14 — Scrub-forward reuses the reconstruction
**Given** a reconstruction advanced to position p
**When** positions p+1, p+2, … are requested in order, then a position before p is requested
**Then** the forward requests advance the existing reconstruction without rebuilding the graph, the
backward request restarts from the nearest preceding checkpoint anchor, and every position's state
equals a from-scratch reconstruction at that position.
*Test:* `ScrubCursorTest`. Covers `[TTD1-30]`, `[TTD1-31]`.

### BS-15 — Read-only, offline, no side effects
**Given** a journal file with a recorded size, mtime, and content hash
**When** every reader, reconstructor, differ, and CLI command is run against it
**Then** size, mtime, and hash are unchanged, no port is bound, and no host outlives the call.
*Test:* `ReadOnlyOfflineTest`. Covers `[TTD1-12]`, `[TTD1-14]`, `[TTD1-51]`.

---

## 7. Suggested feature decomposition

1. **`:timetravel` module skeleton + journal reader** — Gradle wiring, the minimal kernel read-side
   accessor for the record framing, `JournalRecord` model, structural and hydrated decode.
   (`[TTD1-01]`–`[TTD1-14]`; BS-5, BS-6, BS-15)
2. **Timeline and position model** — `RunTimeline`, record-index and frontier-cut addressing,
   checkpoint anchors. (`[TTD1-15]`–`[TTD1-19]`; BS-2)
3. **Offline reconstruction over the recovery path** — graph source, `SimulationController`-driven
   host, prefix replay via `recoverFrom`, snapshot extraction, scrub cursor.
   (`[TTD1-20]`–`[TTD1-32]`; BS-1, BS-3, BS-4, BS-9, BS-10, BS-14)
4. **Fidelity model** — verdicts, reasons, the replay-stable allow-list, effect suppression, the
   run-level roll-up. (`[TTD1-26]`–`[TTD1-28]`, `[TTD1-33]`–`[TTD1-38]`; BS-7, BS-8)
5. **Run diffing** — alignment, divergence classification, `RunDiffReport` DTO + JSON/text renderers.
   (`[TTD1-39]`–`[TTD1-46]`; BS-11, BS-12, BS-13)
6. **CLI + a demo-journal walkthrough** — `inspect`/`reconstruct`/`diff`, exit codes, and one
   end-to-end run against a real demo journal (`demo/agora`'s `--journal <dir>`, which already writes
   `host.journal` beside an app-level `graph.jsonl` structure log). (`[TTD1-47]`–`[TTD1-53]`)

---

## 8. Verification

- `./gradlew :timetravel:test` — every BS-n scenario above as a named test.
- `./gradlew :kernel:test` — mandatory, because feature 1 touches kernel visibility. In particular
  `kernel/src/test/kotlin/civictech/cell/durability/` (`CrashRecoveryTest`, `RecoveryAccountingTest`,
  `EffectfulRecoveryTest`, `DurableGlitchFreeReplayTest`, `MixedDurabilityTest`) and
  `kernel/src/test/kotlin/civictech/cell/host/{KeyedCellsRecoveryTest,TwoWriterDurabilityTest}.kt`
  must be untouched and green — TTD1 changes no recovery behaviour.
- `./gradlew :concord:test` — must stay green with **no new corpus scenarios and no edits to
  `doc/spec/CONCORDANCE.md`**. TTD1 adds no normative requirement id, so it adds no `covers:`.
- `./gradlew :demo:agora:test` — the one demo with a real `FileJournal` + structure log
  (`AgoraApp.kt:30,39`); its `DurabilityTest` must stay green, and feature 6's walkthrough uses its
  journal shape.
- `./gradlew test` — the repository-wide gate.
- Determinism: the diff-report byte-identity check (`[TTD1-46]`) and the seeded reconstruction tests
  must not be re-seeded to pass. A discovered failing seed stays.
- Findings: anything TTD1 hits that the journal format cannot express (topology absence, segmentation
  pain, per-cell journal discovery, cross-host alignment) is written as a finding citing the relevant
  G-id, per `AGENTS.md` and the milestone plan's §6 hygiene — never as a spec or gap-table edit.

---

## 9. Risks / open questions

1. **The journal has no topology — this is the biggest design risk.** `[24-DUR-02]` and the spec's
   own note make the graph an out-of-band artifact. Every reconstruction therefore needs a caller
   -supplied graph, which makes the CLI's "point it at a crash artifact" story weaker than it sounds:
   without a `GraphSpec` or a structure log, only `inspect` and record-level `diff` work.
   **Open question:** should feature 6 standardize the agora-style `graph.jsonl` structure log as a
   `:timetravel`-readable convention, or stay agnostic and take a `GraphSpec` from the caller? The
   recommendation is *stay agnostic, read agora's format as one adapter*, and file the standardization
   ask as a finding — journaling topology is 93 I-7's decided-but-unlanded classification and belongs
   to the kernel lane, not here.
2. **Non-deterministic and effectful cells.** Wall-clock, random, spontaneously-emitting sources, and
   `Effectful` sinks are outside the replay-stable boundary (93 I-7, C-9/G-59). The fidelity model is
   the mitigation, but the allow-list approach (`[TTD1-35]`) will mark some genuinely faithful
   application cells `DEGRADED`. That is the correct direction to err, and it is worth stating in the
   CLI output so users are not confused by a pessimistic verdict.
3. **Journal truncation and segmentation.** `FileJournal` is deliberately one file with an fsync per
   append and whole-log in-memory replay; segmentation/rotation is an explicitly trigger-gated
   residual. A long-running demo's journal may not fit comfortably in memory, and the reader inherits
   that. **Open question:** does the reader need streaming/`Sequence` reading from day one, or is
   whole-log reading acceptable until a real journal hurts? Recommendation: design the API around a
   `Sequence` so a later streaming implementation is not an API break, implement it over the existing
   whole-log `replay()` initially.
4. **Journal format stability.** `WireCodec.VERSION` is 2 and `decode` hard-fails on a mismatch; the
   record type bytes are file-private constants in `HostDurability.kt`. A reader in a second module
   is a *second consumer of an unversioned internal framing*, and it will drift if the framing is
   duplicated. Hence `[TTD1-52]` and the design's insistence on a shared read-side accessor rather
   than a copied byte layout. **Open question:** is a small `civictech.cell.durability` read-only
   decoder in `:kernel` (public, used by both) the cleanest seam? Recommendation: yes — it keeps one
   definition of the framing and leaves `:timetravel` free of byte-level knowledge.
5. **Memory cost of reconstruction.** Each reconstruction spawns a real graph on a real
   `ManagedHost`. A scrubbing UI dragging across a long timeline could create many. `[TTD1-30]`'s
   forward-advancing cursor is the mitigation; the backward case (`[TTD1-31]`) still pays a restart
   from the nearest anchor, which for a journal with no checkpoints means from record 0. **Open
   question:** is a periodic in-memory anchor (snapshot the reconstruction every k positions, in the
   reader's own memory, never written to the journal) worth building in TTD1 or deferred to TTD2 when
   the scrubber's real interaction cost is measurable? Recommendation: defer, measure, file a finding.
6. **Per-cell journal discovery.** CP-C1 means a run may have many journals with no manifest naming
   them or mapping them to cells. The CLI reads a directory, but the cell↔journal mapping only comes
   out of the records themselves. Acceptable for TTD1; worth a finding.
7. **Cross-host runs.** A distributed run's history is spread across hosts with no shared clock.
   Explicitly out of scope, but the demo value of time travel is highest exactly there — expect this
   to come back as a TTD3-shaped ask.
