## Functional requirements (EARS)

Ids are scoped to this epic (`[WIR1-*]`) so they never collide with normative spec
ids under `doc/spec/`; the style mirrors `concord/schema/provenance.md` §1. Related
normative material: `[41-LOC-01]` (`doc/spec/40-distribution/41-location-transparency.md:9`),
spec 41 points 1 and 4 (frame-level prose, deliberately id-less), G-35
(`doc/spec/90-roadmap/91-gap-analysis.md:36`,
`doc/spec/10-programming-model/12-ports.md:223`,
`doc/spec/30-execution-model/34-scheduling.md:63`), and ⚠ CONFLICT C-13
(`doc/spec/40-distribution/41-location-transparency.md:~190`).

### Group A — obligations on the corpus artifact

`[WIR1-C01]` The corpus SHALL consist of plain-text UTF-8 JSON files under version
control, readable with a JSON parser alone, requiring no JVM, Kotlin, or Gradle
toolchain.

`[WIR1-C02]` Each vector SHALL be one self-describing document carrying at minimum:
a stable `id`, a `title`, a `category`, a `covers` list, the `codecVersion` it was
generated against, a `decoded` value in the neutral grammar, and either an `encoded`
block (`utf8` and `base64` of the same bytes) or an `expect.reject` classification.

`[WIR1-C03]` Vector ids SHALL be immutable once assigned and SHALL NOT be reused
after deprecation (mirroring `concord/schema/provenance.md` §1).

`[WIR1-C04]` The corpus SHALL contain at least one positive vector for each
`HostedPortInvocation.Type` variant: `PORT_MANAGEMENT`, `PORT_API`, `PORT_PROTOCOL`.

`[WIR1-C05]` The corpus SHALL contain at least one positive vector for each
polymorphic subclass registered in `WireCodec`'s `SerializersModule`, and for each
arm of the `Interest` polymorphic hierarchy.

`[WIR1-C06]` For each additive-optional `WireFrame` field (`context`, `protocolId`,
`protocolMessage`, `edge`, `routingEpoch`, `natures`), the corpus SHALL contain both
a vector in which the field is present and a vector in which it is absent.

`[WIR1-C07]` The corpus SHALL contain handshake vectors pinning the exact `HELLO`
text with a peer name and without a peer name, and SHALL state which WebSocket
message kind (text vs binary) carries each.

`[WIR1-C08]` The corpus SHALL contain negative vectors covering, at minimum:
malformed JSON, truncated bytes, invalid UTF-8, unknown `type` enum name, unknown
polymorphic discriminator, missing required field, unknown contract/method ids,
`PORT_PROTOCOL` missing `protocolId`, `PORT_PROTOCOL` missing `edge`, a wire
`version` below current, a wire `version` above current, and a `Leased` payload
offered at encode — each with an expected rejection classification.

`[WIR1-C09]` Every identity-bearing field in a vector (`CellRef`, `PortRef`, edge
id, `Timestamp`, any UUID) SHALL be pinned to a literal constant, such that encoding
a vector is a pure function of the vector.

`[WIR1-C10]` While the wire format is unchanged, the `encoded` bytes of an existing
vector SHALL NOT be edited; new behaviour is expressed by appending new vectors.

`[WIR1-C11]` If a vector's bytes cannot be produced deterministically — unordered
map or set iteration, floating-point text formatting, locale- or
platform-dependent rendering — then the corpus SHALL either pin the ordering and
literal rendering explicitly in the vector, or record the vector in
`wire/corpus/NONDETERMINISM.md` with the reason and the tolerated variation; it
SHALL NOT silently normalize.

`[WIR1-C12]` The corpus SHALL carry a machine-readable `manifest.json` enumerating
every vector with its id, category, and file path, so a harness can discover
vectors without relying on directory-walking conventions.

`[WIR1-C13]` The corpus SHALL carry a prose companion (`README.md`) sufficient to
implement a conforming encoder/decoder without reading Kotlin, covering: transport
framing (text hello, binary frames), the JSON options in force
(`useArrayPolymorphism`, `allowStructuredMapKeys`, `encodeDefaults = false` and its
omission consequences), the envelope field list, the version rule, and the
`PORT_PROTOCOL` edge/natures rules.

`[WIR1-C14]` The corpus SHALL carry an authoring contract (`SCHEMA.md`) defining the
vector document schema and the neutral `decoded` grammar; changing that grammar
SHALL be a deliberate schema-change ticket, not a corpus-authoring convenience
(mirroring `concord/schema/scenario.md`'s seam rule).

`[WIR1-C15]` The corpus SHALL NOT contain vectors for payload types contributed by
applications through `civictech.cell.wire.WireSerializers`; it covers
kernel-registered types only, and `README.md` SHALL document the extension point.

`[WIR1-C16]` Where a vector pins behaviour that the specification does not require
and that a future spec change may legitimately alter (for example the strict
version-equality check of `[WIR1-I04]`, or the write-disabled/read-tolerated
`routingEpoch`), the vector SHALL say so in its `notes`, so a later reader can
distinguish "pinned because normative" from "pinned because current".

### Group B — obligations on any conforming implementation

Written implementation-neutrally: "a conforming implementation" means any
encoder/decoder claiming to speak the ComputeNet wire, of which the JVM
`WireCodec` + `WsTransport` pair is the first instance and WIR2's non-JVM peer is
intended to be the second.

`[WIR1-I01]` For every positive vector, a conforming implementation SHALL encode
the vector's `decoded` value to a byte sequence equal to the vector's `encoded`
bytes.

`[WIR1-I02]` For every positive vector, a conforming implementation SHALL decode
the vector's `encoded` bytes to a value equal to the vector's `decoded` value.

`[WIR1-I03]` A conforming implementation SHALL satisfy `decode(encode(v)) == v` for
every positive vector's `decoded` value.

`[WIR1-I04]` If a decoded frame's `version` field differs from the implementation's
own wire version, then the implementation SHALL reject the frame with an
unsupported-version error and SHALL NOT partially apply it. *(Honesty note: this is
the whole of "version negotiation" today —
`check(frame.version == VERSION)` in `WireCodec.decode`. There is no negotiation
handshake, no range, no downgrade. The requirement states the observable rule rather
than inventing a mechanism; a real negotiation is G-35 follow-up and a spec change,
explicitly out of WIR1's scope.)*

`[WIR1-I05]` When a decoded frame carries an envelope field the implementation does
not recognise, the implementation SHALL ignore that field and decode the remainder
successfully. *(This is the additive-compatibility contract `natures` and
`routingEpoch` were landed under.)*

`[WIR1-I06]` If a non-`PORT_PROTOCOL` frame names a contract id / method id pair for
which no local descriptor exists, then the implementation SHALL reject the frame
with an error naming both ids, and SHALL NOT deliver a partially reconstructed
invocation.

`[WIR1-I07]` If the received bytes are truncated, not well-formed JSON, or not valid
UTF-8, then the implementation SHALL reject them and SHALL NOT deliver any part of
the frame.

`[WIR1-I08]` If a polymorphic payload carries a discriminator the implementation
does not know, then the implementation SHALL reject the frame rather than silently
substituting a value or dropping the argument.

`[WIR1-I09]` If a frame's `type` names a frame kind the implementation does not
know, then the implementation SHALL reject the frame.

`[WIR1-I10]` Where `PORT_PROTOCOL` is supported, a `PORT_PROTOCOL` frame SHALL carry
both a `protocolId` and an `edge`; if either is absent, then the implementation
SHALL reject the frame.

`[WIR1-I11]` Where `PORT_PROTOCOL` and nature typing are supported, an absent or
empty `natures` field SHALL be interpreted as the default nature vector, and an
unrecognised nature axis SHALL be ignored rather than causing rejection.

`[WIR1-I12]` When a peer connection opens, each side SHALL send exactly one text
handshake message as its first message on that connection, of the form
`HELLO <mirror-ref-uuid>` optionally followed by a space and the local peer name.

`[WIR1-I13]` While no admitted handshake has been received on a connection, the
implementation SHALL NOT deliver inbound binary frames into the graph, and SHALL
count each such dropped frame.

`[WIR1-I14]` If the handshake names a peer that boundary admission refuses, then the
implementation SHALL close the connection before accepting any announcement or
frame from it.

`[WIR1-I15]` When a second handshake arrives on an existing session (a reconnect
re-hello), the implementation SHALL supersede the previous announcement hook rather
than accumulating hooks.

`[WIR1-I16]` If an outbound invocation carries a lease-scoped payload, then the
implementation SHALL refuse to encode it. *(Spec 23 corollary: a lease on a remote
pool is meaningless.)*

`[WIR1-I17]` When an outbound invocation carries exclusively-owned payloads, the
implementation SHALL consume each such payload exactly once as part of encoding
(move-by-serialize), and SHALL NOT leave a live sender-side reference.

`[WIR1-I18]` The encoded bytes SHALL NOT contain class names, method names, package
names, or any other reflection artifact — identity travels as ids and pinned
discriminators only.

`[WIR1-I19]` A conforming implementation SHALL omit every envelope field that equals
its default, such that a value-identical frame produced by two conforming
implementations is byte-identical.

**Honesty ledger for this section.** Two things WIR1 *cannot* check and must not
pretend to: (a) conformance of any non-JVM implementation — WIR1 only checks the
JVM one plus corpus self-consistency; the second-implementation claim is WIR2's
deliverable. (b) Whether a bridged link negotiates identically to a local one —
that is ⚠ CONFLICT C-13, owned by CP-A2, and spec 41 already states it "is not part
of this id's checkable surface". No `[WIR1-*]` requirement should be written to
imply otherwise. If a later agent finds a requirement here that cannot be checked
honestly, the correct move is to record it in `wire/corpus/NONDETERMINISM.md` (or
`concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` if it touches an EARS id), never to weaken it into a
passing check.

## Behaviour specifications

Each scenario is specific enough to become one named test. Concord placement is
noted per group; the short answer is **none of these belong in `concord/corpus/`**,
because `concord/schema/provenance.md` explicitly excludes protocol frames from the
L0 conformance surface, and adding a frame/byte vocabulary to the scenario schema
would contradict concord's implementation-neutrality thesis. The one
wire-adjacent behaviour that *is* boundary-observable — a cross-host pipeline
equalling its single-host twin — already exists as `concord/corpus/41-location/
41-SPLIT-01.yaml` with `covers: [41-LOC-01]`, and needs nothing from WIR1. If WIR2
later wants a peer-level behavioural scenario, that is the `covers:` id it would
carry.

### B1 — Round-trip and byte identity, per frame type

**B1.1 PORT_API frame with a `SetDelta<String>` payload**
- *Given* vector `WV-PORT-API-SETDELTA-01` with pinned `cellRef`, `portName`,
  contract/method ids and one add-delta
- *When* the implementation encodes the vector's `decoded` value
- *Then* the bytes equal the vector's `encoded.utf8` exactly, byte-for-byte
  — `[WIR1-I01]`

**B1.2 PORT_API frame decode**
- *Given* the same vector's `encoded.base64`
- *When* the implementation decodes it
- *Then* the reconstructed invocation's cell ref, port name, method name, and
  argument values equal the `decoded` block — `[WIR1-I02]`

**B1.3 PORT_MANAGEMENT frame** — as B1.1/B1.2 for a management-API invocation
(`linkTo`-class), asserting the `type` discriminator is the only structural
difference — `[WIR1-C04]`, `[WIR1-I01]`

**B1.4 PORT_PROTOCOL frame with an `EdgeOpen` message**
- *Given* vector `WV-PORT-PROTOCOL-EDGEOPEN-01` carrying `protocolId`, a full
  `edge` (id, fromRef/fromCell/fromPortName, toRef/toCell/toPortName), and a
  non-empty `natures`
- *When* encoded and decoded
- *Then* bytes match exactly and the decoded edge reconstructs both `PortAddress`
  pairs and the nature vector — `[WIR1-I01]`, `[WIR1-I10]`, `[WIR1-I11]`

**B1.5 Every registered payload type** — a parameterized run over
`payloads/*.json`, one case per registered discriminator, each asserting exact
bytes and value equality — `[WIR1-C05]`, `[WIR1-I01]`–`[WIR1-I03]`

**B1.6 Default omission**
- *Given* two vectors identical except that one sets `natures` to the empty list
  explicitly and one omits it
- *Then* both encode to the same bytes, and neither contains the substring
  `"natures"` — `[WIR1-I19]`, `[WIR1-C06]`

**B1.7 No reflection artifacts**
- *Given* any positive vector
- *Then* its `encoded.utf8` contains no `civictech.` package fragment, no `java.`
  fragment, and no Kotlin class simple name that is not a pinned `@SerialName`
  — `[WIR1-I18]`

**B1.8 Coverage lint**
- *Given* the live `SerializersModule` registration list
- *When* the driver enumerates it and compares against `manifest.json`
- *Then* a registration with no vector fails the build with the missing
  discriminator named — `[WIR1-C05]`, `[WIR1-C12]`

**B1.9 Generator check mode**
- *Given* the corpus and the current encoder
- *When* `:wire:wireVectors` runs in check mode
- *Then* every regenerated `encoded` block equals the committed one; a difference
  fails with a diff and the message that the encoder changed — `[WIR1-C10]`

### B2 — Handshake and version

**B2.1 Hello with peer name**
- *Given* a session whose side declares peer name `alpha` and mirror ref
  `<pinned uuid>`
- *When* the connection opens
- *Then* the first outbound message is a **text** message equal to
  `HELLO <pinned uuid> alpha` — `[WIR1-I12]`, `[WIR1-C07]`

**B2.2 Hello without peer name** — same, minus the trailing name and its separator
— `[WIR1-I12]`

**B2.3 Binary frame before hello**
- *Given* an open connection on which no admitted hello has arrived
- *When* a valid binary frame arrives
- *Then* nothing is delivered into the graph and the pre-hello drop counter
  increments by one — `[WIR1-I13]` (existing coverage:
  `wire/src/test/kotlin/civictech/wire/WsTransportPreHelloDropTest.kt`)

**B2.4 Refused peer**
- *Given* a listener with an allowlist not containing `mallory`
- *When* `HELLO <uuid> mallory` arrives
- *Then* the connection closes and no announcement hook and no ingress are
  installed — `[WIR1-I14]` (existing coverage: `WsPeerIdentityTest`,
  `kernel/.../TrustBoundaryTest.kt`)

**B2.5 Re-hello supersedes**
- *Given* a client session that has already handshaken
- *When* a second hello arrives after a reconnect
- *Then* the previous announcer is closed and exactly one announcement hook remains
  — `[WIR1-I15]` (adjacent: `WsReconnectSmokeTest`, `ChainOnReannounceTest`)

**B2.6 Version below current**
- *Given* a vector whose frame carries `"version": 1`
- *When* decoded by an implementation whose version is 2
- *Then* it is rejected with an unsupported-version error naming `1`, and nothing is
  delivered — `[WIR1-I04]`, `[WIR1-C08]`

**B2.7 Version above current** — same with `"version": 99`. Together B2.6/B2.7 pin
that the check is equality, not a floor or a range — `[WIR1-I04]`

**B2.8 Unknown envelope field**
- *Given* a v2 frame carrying an extra field the implementation does not know
- *When* decoded
- *Then* it decodes successfully and the unknown field is ignored — `[WIR1-I05]`

**B2.9 routingEpoch read-tolerated, write-disabled**
- *Given* a legacy vector carrying a non-null `routingEpoch`
- *Then* it decodes successfully; *and* encoding the equivalent current value
  produces bytes with no `routingEpoch` field — `[WIR1-I05]`, `[WIR1-C16]`

### B3 — Malformed, unknown, truncated

**B3.1 Malformed JSON**
- *Given* `negative/WV-NEG-MALFORMED-01` whose bytes are `{"version":2,`
- *When* decoded
- *Then* rejection is classified `malformed`, and no invocation is delivered
  — `[WIR1-I07]`

**B3.2 Truncated frame**
- *Given* a valid vector's bytes cut at 60% of their length
- *When* decoded
- *Then* rejection is classified `truncated`/`malformed`, with no partial delivery
  and no state mutation on the receiving side — `[WIR1-I07]`

**B3.3 Invalid UTF-8** — bytes containing a lone continuation byte reject before
any parse — `[WIR1-I07]`

**B3.4 Unknown frame type**
- *Given* a frame whose `type` is `"PORT_TELEPATHY"`
- *Then* decoding rejects, classified `unknown-frame-type` — `[WIR1-I09]`

**B3.5 Unknown payload discriminator**
- *Given* an args array containing `["QuantumDelta", {...}]`
- *Then* decoding rejects; the argument is neither dropped nor null-substituted
  — `[WIR1-I08]`

**B3.6 Unknown contract/method ids**
- *Given* a well-formed frame with ids no local descriptor knows
- *Then* decoding rejects with both ids in the message — `[WIR1-I06]` (existing
  coverage to extend: `WireCodecTest."unknown ids are rejected at decode"`)

**B3.7 PORT_PROTOCOL missing protocolId** — reject, classified
`missing-required-field` — `[WIR1-I10]`

**B3.8 PORT_PROTOCOL missing edge** — reject, same classification — `[WIR1-I10]`

**B3.9 Leased payload at encode**
- *Given* an invocation whose args include a lease-scoped payload
- *When* offered to the bridge egress
- *Then* encoding is refused before any bytes are produced — `[WIR1-I16]`

**B3.10 Owned payload consumed once**
- *Given* an invocation carrying an exclusively-owned payload
- *When* it is encoded
- *Then* the payload is consumed exactly once and a second consume fails
  — `[WIR1-I17]` (adjacent: `kernel/src/test/kotlin/civictech/cell/wire/
  OwnershipTest.kt`)

**B3.11 Nondeterminism guard**
- *Given* a vector whose value contains a multi-entry map or a `Double`
- *When* encoded 100 times in one process and once in a fresh JVM
- *Then* all 101 byte sequences are identical, or the vector is listed in
  `NONDETERMINISM.md` with its reason — `[WIR1-C11]`

---

## Suggested feature decomposition

1. **Corpus foundation** — `wire/corpus/` layout, `SCHEMA.md` (vector document +
   neutral `decoded` grammar), `README.md` (the prose wire companion),
   `manifest.json`, `NONDETERMINISM.md`. Satisfies `[WIR1-C01]`–`[WIR1-C03]`,
   `[WIR1-C12]`–`[WIR1-C15]`.
2. **JVM driver and generator** — the `:wire` test-source driver, the
   `:wire:wireVectors` task in write/check modes, and the registration-coverage
   lint. Satisfies `[WIR1-I01]`–`[WIR1-I03]`, `[WIR1-C10]`, and B1.8/B1.9.
3. **Envelope and payload vectors** — `PORT_API` and `PORT_MANAGEMENT` frames plus
   one vector per registered polymorphic subclass and per `Interest` arm.
   Satisfies `[WIR1-C04]`–`[WIR1-C05]`, B1.1–B1.3, B1.5, B1.7.
4. **PORT_PROTOCOL, edge, and additive-field vectors** — protocol messages,
   `WireEdge`, sparse `natures`, `routingEpoch`, present/absent pairs. Satisfies
   `[WIR1-C06]`, `[WIR1-I05]`, `[WIR1-I10]`–`[WIR1-I11]`, B1.4, B1.6, B2.8–B2.9.
5. **Handshake and version vectors** — `HELLO` forms, pre-hello drop, allowlist
   refusal, re-hello, version below/above. Satisfies `[WIR1-C07]`,
   `[WIR1-I04]`, `[WIR1-I12]`–`[WIR1-I15]`, B2.1–B2.7.
6. **Negative-vector suite and ownership boundary** — malformed, truncated,
   invalid UTF-8, unknown type/discriminator/ids, missing required fields, leased
   refusal, owned consume-once, plus the determinism guard. Satisfies
   `[WIR1-C08]`–`[WIR1-C09]`, `[WIR1-C11]`, `[WIR1-I06]`–`[WIR1-I09]`,
   `[WIR1-I16]`–`[WIR1-I18]`, B3.1–B3.11.

---

## Verification

```bash
./gradlew :wire:test                                    # the corpus driver's home
./gradlew :wire:wireVectors                             # generator in check mode; must be clean
./gradlew :kernel:test --tests 'civictech.cell.wire.*'  # existing codec/bridge tests still green
./gradlew :concord:test -Pconcord.profiles=core         # concord unchanged (no scenarios added)
./gradlew test                                          # repository-wide gate
```

Expected end state: `:wire:test` runs one case per corpus vector (parameterized, so
adding a vector adds a case with no Kotlin edit); the coverage lint fails on an
un-vectored registration; the generator check fails on any byte change; and
`git diff` shows no change under `kernel/src/main/` or `wire/src/main/` — WIR1 is a
test-and-data epic, and a production-source diff is itself a review signal that the
scope boundary was crossed.

---

## Risks / open questions

**Maintenance cost when the protocol legitimately changes.** The central risk. A
corpus that is painful to update gets bypassed with a blanket regeneration, which
restores exactly the drift blindness it was built to remove. Mitigations built into
the design: `decoded` is hand-authored and `encoded` is generated, so a legitimate
change is one reviewed `--write` run; the check-mode failure message names the
remedy explicitly; and `[WIR1-C16]` marks which vectors pin *current* rather than
*normative* behaviour so a reviewer can tell an intended change from a regression.
Open question for the implementing agent: should a regeneration diff require a
`covers:`-style justification line in the vector, or is the PR review sufficient?

**Determinism of encodings.** Real and unresolved until measured. Three specific
hazards: (a) `MapDelta`/`TaggedMapDelta`/`SetDelta` iteration order — kotlinx
serializes collections in iteration order, so a `HashMap`-backed delta may encode
differently across runs or JDK versions; `TaggedMapDeltaSerializer` "groups dots by
sourceId", which helps but must be verified. (b) `Double` — kotlinx uses the JDK's
shortest-round-trip formatting; stable in practice on one JVM, unverified across
implementations, and `1.0` vs `1` is exactly the kind of difference a TS peer will
hit. (c) UUID rendering case. `[WIR1-C09]`/`[WIR1-C11]` and scenario B3.11 exist to
force this into the open early: the first feature to author a map vector should run
the determinism guard before authoring the rest.

**Vectors could ossify a bug.** The corpus pins today's behaviour, including
behaviour nobody would design on purpose — the strict version equality check, the
absence of real negotiation, `routingEpoch`'s asymmetry, and the C-13 bridged-link
handshake bypass. That is the correct choice for WIR1 (pin, don't redesign), but it
means the corpus is *not* a specification of what the wire should be. `[WIR1-C16]`'s
`notes` requirement is the mitigation; the deeper answer is WIR2, whose independent
implementer will find the places where the corpus documents an accident.

**Scale of the payload catalogue.** Roughly 30 registered discriminators plus 7
`Interest` arms plus additive-field pairs plus negatives — on the order of 60–90
vectors. Large enough that hand-authoring every `decoded` block is the epic's real
cost. Open question: should feature 3 generate skeleton `decoded` blocks from the
registration list and have a human fill in values, rather than authoring from
scratch?

**Handshake vectors are not pure data.** Frame vectors are a pure function
(bytes ↔ value); handshake behaviour (pre-hello drop counting, allowlist close,
re-hello supersession) is stateful session behaviour that a corpus can describe but
not fully encode. Feature 5 should expect a split: the `HELLO` *text* is a vector;
the session *behaviour* is a conventional test in `:wire` that cites the
`[WIR1-I12]`–`[WIR1-I15]` ids. Say so rather than pretending the corpus covers it.

**Interaction with `WireSerializers`.** `[WIR1-C15]` excludes app-contributed
types, but the ServiceLoader module is folded into the codec at construction and
`plus` fails fast on collision. Open question: should the driver assert the
kernel-only module in isolation, or accept whatever the test classpath contributes?
Isolating is more honest and should be the default.
design:
# WIR1 — design notes

## D1. Why not `concord/`

`concord/schema/provenance.md` §1 "checkable through the SPI" rule states that
statements about **protocol frames** stay normative prose *without* EARS ids —
they are "implementation guidance, not conformance surface". Concord's thesis is
that a second implementation with a completely different wire format could pass
the whole corpus. A byte-level vector corpus asserts the opposite kind of fact.
Filing it as concord scenarios would require growing the L1 scenario schema with a
frame/byte vocabulary — a schema-change ticket that would damage concord's own
seam rule (`concord/schema/scenario.md` preamble).

Corroborating evidence: `doc/spec/40-distribution/41-location-transparency.md`
carries exactly one EARS id (`[41-LOC-01]`) and says its negotiation-parity half
"is not part of this id's checkable surface".

**Decision:** `wire/corpus/` (data) + a driver in `wire/src/test/kotlin/civictech/
wire/vector/`. `:wire` already depends on `:kernel`, so the driver reaches
`WireCodec`. A non-JVM reader needs only a JSON parser and `wire/corpus/README.md`.
The corpus borrows concord's *shape* — neutral artifact, thin driver, id scheme,
coverage lint, honesty ledger — without living inside it.

Rejected alternative: a top-level `wirespec/` module. Buys a separate publication
story we do not need, at the cost of a fourth place to look for wire semantics.
Revisit only if WIR2 shows that a language-neutral consumer needs a published
package rather than a repo path.

## D2. Hand-authored `decoded`, generated `encoded`

The vector's decoded value is the human-owned half; the bytes are derived. This
keeps authoring cheap and makes a byte change reviewable as a diff. The generator
runs in check mode by default (a byte difference fails) and in `--write` mode only
as a deliberate, reviewed act. Blanket regeneration is the failure mode to design
against — see the maintenance risk in the description.

## D3. Neutral `decoded` grammar

`{"type": "<pinned @SerialName>", "fields": {...}}` trees. No Kotlin type names, no
FQNs, no JVM descriptors — those are precisely what spec 41 point 1 removed from
the bytes (P9), and re-introducing them in the corpus would make the artifact
JVM-shaped again. Identity fields are literal pinned constants (`[WIR1-C09]`) so
encoding a vector is a pure function.

## D4. Coverage lint is the anti-drift mechanism

Golden vectors catch changes to *existing* encodings. They cannot catch a *new*
registered payload type shipping with no vector. The lint that enumerates
`WireCodec`'s live `SerializersModule` registrations and diffs against
`manifest.json` is what closes that hole, and it is the single highest-value piece
of the epic. It is also the only part of the driver that is legitimately
JVM-specific — WIR2's driver will not have it, and should not be expected to.

## D5. What the JSON options force us to pin

From `WireCodec.kt`:
- `useArrayPolymorphism = true` ⇒ `["<SerialName>", value]`.
- `allowStructuredMapKeys = true` ⇒ polymorphic map keys as `[k, v]` arrays.
- kotlinx default `encodeDefaults = false` ⇒ defaulted fields are omitted. This is
  the mechanism CP-G2 used to add `natures` with no version bump, and `[WIR1-I19]`
  turns it into a requirement so two conforming encoders are byte-identical.
- Frames are UTF-8 JSON text bytes sent as **binary** WebSocket messages; the
  handshake is a **text** message. Any peer that confuses the two fails at hello.

## D6. Version: state the truth, do not invent negotiation

`WireCodec.decode` does `check(frame.version == VERSION)`. That is the entirety of
version handling. `[WIR1-I04]` states the observable rule (strict equality reject,
no partial application) and the description flags it as pinned-because-current, not
pinned-because-normative. Writing a richer negotiation requirement here would be
unverifiable prose and would quietly expand WIR1 into G-35 follow-up work.

## D7. Handshake vectors are a hybrid

The `HELLO` *string* is data and belongs in the corpus. Pre-hello drop counting,
allowlist close, and re-hello supersession are stateful session behaviours that
belong in ordinary `:wire` tests citing `[WIR1-I12]`–`[WIR1-I15]`. Feature 5 must
not force the latter into vector files.

## D8. Determinism is a first-task risk, not a last-task risk

Map/set iteration order, `Double` text formatting, and UUID case are the three
concrete hazards. Scenario B3.11 (encode 100× in-process + once in a fresh JVM)
should run against the *first* map-bearing vector authored, before the payload
catalogue is written — if encodings are not stable, the corpus format needs a
tolerated-variation escape hatch (`NONDETERMINISM.md`) before 60 vectors exist,
not after.

## D9. Explicit non-goals worth restating at review time

No production-source diff under `kernel/src/main/` or `wire/src/main/`. No
`@SerialName` changes, no version bump, no CBOR, no TLS/compression/keepalive. C-13
(bridged links bypass `handshake()`) stays open and owned by CP-A2. Real G-35
capability negotiation stays open. Application `WireSerializers` contributions stay
out of the corpus.

## D10. Sizing

~30 registered discriminators + 7 `Interest` arms + additive-field pairs +
~12 negatives ⇒ 60–90 vectors. The driver is small (~200 lines); the cost is
authoring `decoded` blocks. Consider generating skeletons from the registration
list in feature 3 and filling values by hand.

Implementation obligations [WIR1-I01]-[WIR1-I19] verified against the JVM codec+transport by the corpus driver, with scenarios B1.1-B1.9, B2.1-B2.9 and B3.1-B3.11 each landing as a named test. title: BB-TPCC — TPC-C bridge document (negative-result study: interactive cross-cell transactions with abort)
description:
# BB-TPCC — TPC-C bridge document (deliberate negative-result study)

Lane: benchmark-bridge (BB). Source: `computenet-milestone-plan.md` §1 (BB-TPCC row),
§3 (TPC-C row of the kernel-enablement matrix), §5 rank 19, §6 standing hygiene.
Priority P3, unblocked (doc-only, no dependencies), explicitly flagged in the plan as
"a good agent-idle writing task".

**This epic produces a document, not code.** Every child feature and task under it is
research, analysis, and writing. Nothing in `kernel/`, `wire/`, `gen/`, `concord/`,
`demo/`, or `doc/spec/` may be modified.

---

## 1. Ambition / Why

Five of the six BB suites end in a number. This one deliberately ends in a *negative
result*, and that is the whole point.

"Can ComputeNet do OLTP?" is currently an unanswered question that costs the project
something every time it is asked: it invites speculative kernel scope, it makes the
benchmark story look evasive ("we ran the five suites we could run"), and it leaves an
unnamed hole in the middle of the distribution model where a reader expects to find
either a primitive or a refusal. The plan's own framing (§3): *"None buildable today:
the missing primitive is interactive cross-cell transactions with abort."*

A negative result is a real deliverable because it converts that vague question into
exactly one of two durable artifacts:

1. **A named candidate G-item** — a precise statement of the missing coordination
   primitive, in the shape `91-gap-analysis.md` uses, with a specification sketch
   strong enough that a future integration pass can adopt it (or a future research
   entry can gate it) without redoing the analysis; or
2. **A documented out-of-scope-by-design decision** — the honest alternative, grounded
   in the spec's own stated principles (P4 "no global coordination", P2 "no per-message
   cost", `42-replication.md` §Principles "**No global consensus**", `53-evolution.md`'s
   "a whole-composite atomic transaction would be the distributed barrier P4 forbids",
   `14-invocations.md`'s "transactions are not the framework's core (dataflow is)").

Either outcome is a win. What is *not* acceptable is a document that surveys TPC-C,
observes that it is hard, and declines to decide. §6 of the plan states the lane's
product directly: *"every suite run that hits a wall names the wall as a candidate
G-item or pulls an existing trigger — that's the lane's actual product; the numbers are
a side effect."* This epic is that sentence with the numbers removed.

There is a second, quieter value. The spec already contains three unbuilt placeholders
that all point at the same hole — the "explicit coordinator cell" escape hatch
(`22-consistency.md` §Topology versioning, rule S5), the JoinBarrier proposal under
⚠ G-39, and R3's coupling-abort-with-compensating-release (`95-research-plan.md`). They
have never been examined together against a single concrete workload. TPC-C is the
cheapest workload that forces all three into the same frame.

---

## 2. What we build

### 2.1 Output paths (exact)

| Path | Status | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `doc/bench/bb-tpcc-bridge.md` | **new file, the deliverable** | The bridge document, sections per §2.2 |
| `doc/bench/findings.md` | **new file or append-only add** | One dated lane-findings entry: the decision reached, the candidate G-item id-less statement, and pointers into the bridge doc. Per plan §6, lanes write findings here and cite G-ids; they never edit the gap table. |

`doc/bench/` is the benchmark-bridge lane's findings directory (the lane whose module
name in BEN1 is `:bench`). If it does not exist, create it; that directory creation is
the only filesystem change beyond the two files above.

### 2.2 Required sections of `doc/bench/bb-tpcc-bridge.md`

1. **Status header and scope disclaimer** — matching the house style of
   `doc/spec/90-roadmap/*.md` headers (`> **Status**: …`, `> **Sources**: …`,
   `> **Implementation**: none`). It must say in the header that this is an analysis
   artifact of the BB lane, not normative spec, and that it proposes nothing built.
2. **What TPC-C actually measures** — the five transactions (New-Order, Payment,
   Order-Status, Delivery, Stock-Level), their mix, the warehouse/district/customer/
   stock schema, and the two properties the benchmark is really about: multi-row
   read-modify-write under a *declared abort path* (New-Order's 1% rollback) and
   the consistency conditions the spec's own §3.3 imposes. tpmC and the pricing
   metric are named and then set aside as out of scope.
3. **What ComputeNet's model guarantees today** — grounded, cited inventory (see §3).
4. **Transaction-by-transaction walk** — for each of the five, what mechanism covers
   it and what specifically does not. Behaviour specifications (§5) live here.
5. **The gap, stated precisely** — EARS specification sketch of the missing primitive
   (§4 group B). This is the section a future G-item or research entry is cut from.
6. **Candidate evaluation** — coordinator-cell-over-quorum-cells, evaluated concretely
   against what exists, versus out-of-scope-by-design. Both must be argued, not one.
7. **Decision** — one of the two, stated in one paragraph, with its consequences: if
   candidate G-item, the proposed row text and the section(s) it would be cited from;
   if out-of-scope-by-design, the sentence that should eventually appear in the spec
   and *who* would put it there (the periodic integration pass, per plan §6).
8. **What this document does not do** — the boundary, restated for the reader.

### 2.3 The decision the document must reach

The document is not done until §7 states, unambiguously and in its own voice, one of:

- **(A) Candidate G-item.** The missing primitive is real, worth naming, and the
  document supplies its EARS sketch, its interaction constraints, and a proposed
  gap-table row in `91-gap-analysis.md`'s exact column shape
  (`| G-NN | <gap> | <resolution/proposal> | <where> |`) rendered *inside the bridge
  document as a quoted proposal*, with the id left as `G-NN (unassigned)` because only
  the integration pass mints ids.
- **(B) Out of scope by design.** Interactive cross-cell transactions with abort are
  refused on principle; the document states which principles refuse them, what
  ComputeNet offers instead for each TPC-C transaction (and where that is genuinely
  weaker), and what a user who needs TPC-C should do (use a database; ComputeNet
  consumes its CDC stream — see the CON1 connector chunk).

A hybrid is permitted and may be the honest answer — e.g. (B) for the general primitive
plus (A) for a strictly narrower sub-gap such as *bounded multi-cell all-or-nothing
within a single host and a single wave*. If the answer is a hybrid, both halves must be
stated with the full rigour of their respective shapes.

---

## 3. How, using ComputeNet

The document's argument must be built from the real model, not from a general critique
of dataflow systems. The grounding below is the research already done for this epic;
the implementing agent must verify each citation by reading the cited file, and must
correct anything that has drifted.

### 3.1 What the model gives (verified, with citations)

- **Waves are per-source, not global.** `MessageContext(timestamp, sourcePort)` with
  `Timestamp(sourceId, counter)`; a source is "one outlet during one emission epoch of
  one instance" (`doc/spec/20-dataflow-semantics/22-consistency.md` §Source identity).
  Origination mints, reactive emission carries transparently. A wave id is *not* a
  transaction id.
- **Glitch-freedom is per-cell and opt-in**: `[22-GF-01]` (no mixing pre-wave and
  post-wave inputs), `[22-GF-02]` (composed fork-joins), `[22-GF-03]` (identical
  condition across a host boundary). Non-declaring cells process eagerly.
- **Per-delta operator atomicity**: `[24-OP-GROUPBY-03]` — all groups touched by one
  input delta emit as one `MapDelta` under that input's wave id. Atomicity's unit is
  *one input delta*, never a set of independent writes.
- **Cross-source alignment is explicitly refused**: `[22-SRC-01]` gives cross-source
  joins "convergence … not simultaneity, unless an explicit coordinator cell is
  inserted"; `[22-LIVE-01]` forbids over-alignment across independent sources.
- **Read-side alignment exists and is the strongest multi-view guarantee**:
  `[22-OBS-01]`/`[22-OBS-02]` (internal consistency against *some* per-source vector
  frontier), plus 22's own §Acceptance benchmark: the balanced-transfer suite. Note
  precisely what that benchmark tests — *observation* of balanced transfers, not
  atomic *execution* of them. This distinction is the spine of the document.
- **Replication is CRDT gossip, opt-in, consensus-free**: `[42-REPL-04..06]`;
  membership "is never a consensus" (93 I-3), "no view number, quorum, or barrier (P4)".
  Single-writer replication (42 §Single-writer replication, decided 93 I-25, unbuilt)
  is primary-backup log-shipping with a `LeaderMark(id, epoch, leaderRef)` max-epoch
  fold — "not a vote" — and an explicitly lossy failure window; ack-from-k "explicitly
  not adopted".
- **Partitioning is disjoint interest**: `[42-INT-01]`, `[24-PART-01..05]`, notably
  `[24-PART-03]` (disjoint ranges ⇒ conflict-free union) and `[24-PART-04]`
  (repartition = Buffering + catch-up + atomic routing-table flip + `routingEpoch` bump).
  "Disjointness *is* the merge-safety proof."
- **Cross-shard reads are explicitly arbitrary**: scatter-gather pull (PN-5) is
  "per-shard-consistent, cross-shard-arbitrary"; "Across shards there is no joint cut".
- **Ownership has a hold-like mechanism that is not a transaction**:
  `doc/spec/20-dataflow-semantics/23-ownership.md` — `Owned`/`Leased` with the SPSC link
  rule; on saturation refusal (93 I-12) "the owner-of-record remains the sender's link —
  ownership has not transferred", sender parks, `take()` fires once at replay. R6/R7/R8:
  RESTART never re-consumes an `Owned`; SUSPEND parks once, replays once; dead-letter
  move-by-serializes `Owned` and releases `Leased`. Note that this chapter carries **no**
  `[NN-SLUG-nn]` ids — cite it by section name.
- **Bounded reads do not isolate**: `[21-PULL-02]` (a bounded read emits nothing and
  advances no wave), `[21-PULL-03]` (a walk is verifiable, not isolated); 21 §Bounded
  state read rejects snapshot isolation on P2 grounds and calls a concurrent walk a
  "smeared" read. This is the read half of every TPC-C transaction.

### 3.2 What the model does not give (the hole)

There is **no abort**. The document must state this as its central finding and support
it exhaustively: nowhere in `doc/spec/20-*` or `doc/spec/40-*` is there a verb for
undoing an emitted delta. The admissible dispositions of an in-flight delta are buffer,
park, absorb-ack, dead-letter, degrade, or retract-as-data — never undo. Supporting
text: 21 §Push rule 2 (emission is effective-only); 23 §SPSC corollaries ("Drop is
forbidden for exclusive payloads — park, or the visible dead-letter boundary");
22 §Completeness over silent or stuck edges (WAIT / DEGRADE / RE-SCOPE — "abandon the
lost contribution loudly", i.e. degrade, never undo); 21 §RESTART re-baselines
("RESTART is *restore + re-baseline*, never a bare local rollback") with `[21-REBASE-01]`
and `[24-TAG-02]` making it convergence-by-supersession.

There is also no multi-cell atomic commit, no tentative hold on data payloads (the
ownership park is backpressure, not prepare), no write quorum, and an explicitly
arbitrary cross-shard cut. Transients are *permitted* rather than prevented —
`[24-OP-OUTERJOIN-02]` allows an observable transient overlap of `(a, null)` and `(a, b)`;
`[24-OP-SEMIJOIN-04]`'s per-wave seal is opt-in and "the default stays ungated".

The two places in the spec where such a primitive would go are both unbuilt placeholders,
and the document must name both: the **"explicit coordinator cell"** escape hatch
(22 §Topology versioning, rule S5) and the **JoinBarrier** proposal under ⚠ G-39
(repeated in 21, 22, 41). A third, adjacent: **R3 — Coupling liveness (G-53)** in
`95-research-plan.md`, whose direction (1) is "membrane-scoped deadline with
*compensating release*: on expiry the held side is released to its port with a
`CouplingAborted` notice on the metadata plane (no loss, explicit degrade)". That is the
closest thing in the corpus to an abort, and the document must say exactly how far it
falls short of a transaction abort (it releases *one held side of one coupling*; it does
not reverse committed downstream effects).

### 3.3 The five transactions, walked

For each, the document names the covering mechanism *or* the specific missing guarantee.
This is the analysis the implementing agent performs; the sketch below is the starting
hypothesis, to be confirmed or corrected against the code and spec.

- **Stock-Level** (read-only, 2 tables, one district): plausibly the *only* one that is
  near-covered today. Bounded read (`[21-PULL-01..03]`, and KRD/V1C-KERNEL's wave-neutral
  `snapshotOf` successor) plus a keyed family read. The gap is not atomicity but
  *isolation*: TPC-C §2.8 allows this one to run at a reduced isolation level, and
  ComputeNet's "smeared" walk may or may not satisfy even that. The document must check
  the actual TPC-C isolation requirement per transaction rather than asserting it.
- **Order-Status** (read-only, customer + latest order + lines): read-side alignment
  question. `[22-OBS-01/02]` gives a per-source vector frontier; the customer cell and
  the order-line cells are different sources, so the read is internally consistent
  against *some* frontier — which may be exactly what TPC-C wants, or not. Decide, cite,
  and say which.
- **Payment** (update warehouse + district + customer YTD, insert history): a
  three-cell read-modify-write with a derived write. If all three are keyed entries of
  one partitioned family under a single ingress delta, `[24-OP-GROUPBY-03]` and
  `[24-PART-03]` may cover it — the SNB row of plan §3 makes exactly this conjecture
  for a different suite ("verify a single ingress delta fanning to person+edge cells
  lands in one wave (likely already holds — verify, don't build)"). The document must
  actually verify it for Payment's shape and report the result. Where the three live on
  different hosts, PN-5's "no joint cut" applies and it does not hold.
- **New-Order** (5–15 line items across warehouse/district/stock/order tables, plus the
  **1% deliberate rollback** on an invalid item): the load-bearing case. Two independent
  gaps: (i) multi-key read-modify-write with a *conditional* outcome that depends on
  reading all lines before writing any, and (ii) an abort that must unwind the
  district's next-order-id increment and every stock decrement already applied. There is
  no mechanism for (ii). This transaction is why the answer is a gap and not a workaround.
- **Delivery** (deferred, batched, 10 districts, each a multi-row update): the one TPC-C
  transaction whose *deferred* execution mode is a natural fit for a dataflow model. The
  document should say so plainly — it is the strongest "ComputeNet is a different shape,
  not a worse one" data point — while noting that per-district atomicity is still
  required.

### 3.4 Evaluating "coordinator-cell over quorum cells", concretely

The plan names this candidate; the document must evaluate it against the code that
actually exists, not against an imagined kernel.

What exists (verify these paths, they were confirmed for this epic):

- `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/op/QuorumSetCell.kt` — a threshold fold
  over a dynamic `SetDelta<E>` fan-in, where `threshold(liveSources: Int)` selects
  union / intersection / majority / k-of-n / all-but-one. **Read what it actually is**:
  it is a *presence-counting set operator* — "the elements whose presence count (distinct
  live source links asserting them) meets threshold" — with `AdvertisedLedger` tag
  discipline shared with `IntersectSetCell`, and a baseline-admits-regardless rule
  (`[24-REPLAY-01]`). It is not a voting protocol, has no proposal/promise/accept phases,
  no ballot numbers, and no notion of a decided value that cannot later change: an
  element can leave the quorum when a source retracts or a link closes.
- `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/consistency/ReplicaQuorum.kt` and
  `WaveFrontier.kt` — read-settlement quorum (PN-7 `ReplicaFrontier.completeAt`: a wave
  is replica-complete when every covering, interest-admitting member has delivered it).
  Again: settlement of a *read*, not agreement on a *write*.
- `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/op/PresenceCountCell.kt`,
  `CoalescingCombineCell.kt`, `Emit.kt`, and the absorb-ack machinery
  (`kernel/src/test/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/op/OperatorAbsorbAckTest.kt`).
- `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/replication/SingleWriterReplication.kt` and
  `Replication.kt`; `kernel/src/test/kotlin/civictech/cell/consistency/ReplicaQuorumTest.kt`,
  `.../durability/DurableQuorumReplayTest.kt`, `.../data/QuorumSetCellTest.kt`.
- `demo/exchange/` — the composition probe. **This is the sharpest evidence in the
  repo and the document should use it.** Despite its name, `demo/exchange/src/main/kotlin/
  civictech/demo/exchange/Main.kt` implements no matching engine and no trade
  settlement: it is region-keyed orders in per-peer writer `SetCell`s, gossiped to the
  counterpart over the wire, folded through a region-partitioned `GroupBy(sum)` behind a
  glitch-free board. `demo/exchange/src/test/kotlin/civictech/demo/exchange/
  ExchangeCompositionExitTest.kt` asserts, over 100 seeds and through a repartition, a
  shard migration, a peer partition/recover, and a late joiner, that both peers' boards
  equal a batch group-by over the converged order set. That is the repo's toughest
  property gate — and it is a *convergent aggregation* property, not an atomicity one.
  The most OLTP-sounding artifact in the tree turns out to prove convergence, not
  transactions. Say that.

The evaluation must therefore answer, explicitly:

1. Could a coordinator cell built from `QuorumSetCell` + a glitch-free frontier
   implement two-phase commit over a set of participant cells today? Walk the protocol:
   where does PREPARE live, what carries a vote, what makes a decision durable across the
   coordinator's own crash, and what un-does a participant's already-emitted delta if the
   decision is ABORT. Name the first step that has no mechanism.
2. What would participants have to gain that they do not have — tentative/uncommitted
   state visible to nobody, a hold on `Owned` payloads that is neither park nor transfer,
   and an emission that is retractable rather than effective-only.
3. Does the promotion machinery's two-phase swap (`53-evolution.md`:
   "pre-validated two-phase swap transaction with a non-vetoing commit and a retained
   incumbent", PRECHECK/PREPARE/COMMIT/RETIRE + ROLLBACK) generalize? Answer expected to
   be no, and the document must say why in the spec's own words: it is a *code-version
   swap of one cell*, membrane-local, and 53 already states that "a whole-composite
   atomic transaction would be the distributed barrier P4 forbids". Also note
   `93-feature-interactions.md`'s Candidate C — "Cross-host atomic multi-link two-phase
   commit" — considered and **not adopted**. The document must engage with why it was
   rejected before proposing anything adjacent to it.
4. What does the primitive cost when it is *not* used? P2 forbids per-message cost. If
   the primitive is opt-in per link/cell like glitch-freedom is, that is the design's
   only viable shape, and the document should say so.

### Group B — EARS specification sketch of the missing primitive

This group is the epic's real intellectual product. It states what *interactive
cross-cell transactions with abort* would have to guarantee **inside ComputeNet's
model** — not in the abstract. It is written as a specification sketch so that, if the
decision is (A), a future G-item or `95-research-plan.md` entry can be cut directly from
it; if the decision is (B), it is the precise thing being refused, which is what makes
the refusal honest.

The document reproduces this group, refined by the analysis, in its §5. The
requirements below are the starting text; the implementing agent may strengthen,
split, or correct them, but may not delete one without stating why in the document.

Naming: call the hypothetical primitive a **transaction scope** with a **coordinator**
and **participant cells**, to avoid implying either the promotion machinery's
two-phase swap or classical 2PC.

**Structure and identity**

- `[BB-TPCC-20]` The runtime shall assign every transaction scope an identity distinct
  from a wave `Timestamp`, because a wave is per-source and per-outlet-epoch
  (`22-consistency.md` §Source identity) and a transaction spans independent sources.
- `[BB-TPCC-21]` The runtime shall make transaction-scope membership explicit at
  formation — a transaction shall name its participant cells, and shall not acquire
  participants implicitly by propagation reach.
- `[BB-TPCC-22]` Where a transaction scope is not declared on a link or cell, the
  runtime shall impose no per-message cost on that link or cell (P2; the same opt-in
  discipline glitch-freedom uses, `[22-GF-01]`).

**Atomicity across cells**

- `[BB-TPCC-23]` While a transaction scope is open, the runtime shall not expose any
  participant's transaction-local state to a non-participant reader.
- `[BB-TPCC-24]` When a transaction scope commits, the runtime shall make every
  participant's state change observable such that no observer sees a proper non-empty
  subset of them — the multi-cell generalization of `[22-GF-01]`, and the guarantee
  `[22-SRC-01]` explicitly declines to provide today.
- `[BB-TPCC-25]` When a transaction scope commits, each participant shall emit its
  resulting deltas downstream, and the document shall state whether those emissions
  carry the transaction identity, a shared wave id, or each participant's own wave id —
  this is an open design point and shall be recorded as one, not silently resolved.
- `[BB-TPCC-26]` If a downstream cell is glitch-free and subscribes to more than one
  participant of the same transaction scope, then the runtime shall deliver that
  transaction's contributions as a single frontier-complete unit, or shall state that
  the composition is refused at link time.

**Abort**

- `[BB-TPCC-27]` The runtime shall provide an abort disposition for a transaction scope
  that leaves no participant's state changed and no participant's delta observable
  downstream — a capability that does not exist today, since emission is effective-only
  (`21-propagation.md` §Push rule 2).
- `[BB-TPCC-28]` When a transaction scope aborts, the runtime shall not emit downstream
  retractions as the mechanism of undo unless the document explicitly adopts
  retract-as-data as the semantics, in which case it shall state that observers may
  transiently see the aborted effect and shall state whether that is acceptable for
  TPC-C's declared rollback.
- `[BB-TPCC-29]` When a transaction scope aborts, the runtime shall release every
  `Leased` payload it holds and shall discharge every `Owned` payload exactly once,
  never silently dropping one (`23-ownership.md` §Taps, the discharging-sink rule; the
  invariant C-11 currently violates in `Shadow.spawn`).
- `[BB-TPCC-30]` If a transaction scope aborts after a participant has consumed an
  `Owned` payload, then the runtime shall state the payload's disposition explicitly —
  returned to the sender as owner-of-record (the 93 I-12 park shape), dead-lettered
  (R8), or declared unabortable-once-consumed. The document shall pick one and justify
  it; "unspecified" is not an acceptable answer here, because G-46 already records that
  exclusives "have no defined story off the happy path".
- `[BB-TPCC-31]` The runtime shall bound the time a transaction scope may remain open,
  and if that bound is exceeded, then the scope shall abort with a visible notice on the
  metadata plane rather than stalling participants indefinitely (the shape R3 proposes
  for coupling liveness: "released to its port with a `CouplingAborted` notice … no
  loss, explicit degrade").

**Interaction with waves, glitch-freedom, and replication**

- `[BB-TPCC-32]` While a transaction scope is open, the runtime shall not block waves
  from independent sources that touch no participant, because a global propagation lock
  is rejected (`22-consistency.md` §Local glitch-freedom: they "serialize the whole
  graph").
- `[BB-TPCC-33]` If two open transaction scopes name an overlapping participant set,
  then the runtime shall define their interleaving — the document shall state whether
  the model serializes them, refuses the second at formation, or admits both and defines
  the merge; an undefined answer here is a correctness hole, not a deferral.
- `[BB-TPCC-34]` Where participants are replicas of a `Replicable` cell, the runtime
  shall state how a transaction commit relates to CRDT convergence, given that
  `[42-REPL-04]` requires equal folds at quiescence regardless of which replica accepted
  each write — a commit that decides an outcome is in tension with a merge that cannot
  be decided, and the document shall name the tension rather than paper over it.
- `[BB-TPCC-35]` Where participants are shards of a partitioned family, the runtime
  shall state whether disjoint interest (`[24-PART-03]`) makes the transaction trivially
  safe (all keys in one shard) and what changes when the participant set spans shards,
  where PN-5 today gives "no joint cut".
- `[BB-TPCC-36]` The runtime shall state whether a transaction scope may span hosts, and
  if it may, then the document shall confront `42-replication.md` §Principles
  ("**No global consensus**") and P4 directly and shall say whether the primitive is a
  violation of a stated principle or an admitted exception to it.

**Failure during commit**

- `[BB-TPCC-37]` If the coordinator fails after any participant has committed and before
  all have, then the runtime shall define a recovery that terminates — the document
  shall state where the decision is durable (journal, `[24-DUR-01..05]`), who reads it
  on recovery, and how a participant that never learns the decision is resolved.
- `[BB-TPCC-38]` If a participant fails while a transaction scope is open, then the
  runtime shall abort the scope or shall define a substitute participant, and shall
  state which — noting that RESTART today is "restore + re-baseline, never a bare local
  rollback" (`[21-REBASE-01]`) and therefore does not by itself abort anything.
- `[BB-TPCC-39]` When a transaction's commit decision is replayed from a journal during
  recovery, the runtime shall not re-drive `Effectful` participants, consistent with the
  processed-frontier rule (`[24-DUR-04]`, C-9, G-59).
- `[BB-TPCC-40]` If the primitive cannot satisfy `[BB-TPCC-37]` without a mechanism the
  project has already refused, then the document shall record that as the decisive
  argument for out-of-scope-by-design rather than proposing the refused mechanism under
  a new name.

## 5. Behaviour specifications

Given/When/Then scenarios drawn from the five TPC-C transactions. **These are analysis
scenarios, not tests.** No `concord` scenario, no JUnit test, and no corpus YAML is
produced by this epic; the bridge document must say so where it presents them.

Each scenario is annotated with a verdict — `COVERED` (today's model satisfies it, with
the mechanism named), `PARTIAL` (satisfied under a stated restriction, e.g. single host
or single shard), or `MISSING` (with the exact guarantee that is absent). The verdicts
below are the starting hypotheses to be confirmed or corrected by the analysis; a
corrected verdict is a *result*, not a failure.

**S1 — New-Order, happy path (multi-key read-modify-write)**
Given a warehouse cell, a district cell, and ten stock cells holding current quantities;
When a new order arrives naming ten items;
Then the district's next-order-id increments exactly once, each stock quantity decrements
exactly once, and no observer sees the order as placed while any stock decrement is
outstanding.
Hypothesis: `PARTIAL` — plausible within one host, one shard, one ingress delta via
`[24-OP-GROUPBY-03]` + `[24-PART-03]` + a glitch-free downstream `[22-GF-01]`; `MISSING`
across shards or hosts, where PN-5 gives "no joint cut" and `[22-SRC-01]` gives
convergence rather than simultaneity. The analysis must determine which by construction.

**S2 — New-Order, the 1% rollback (the load-bearing scenario)**
Given the same setup;
When the tenth item is an invalid item id, and the transaction must roll back;
Then the district's next-order-id increment is undone, every stock decrement already
applied is undone, and no downstream observer ever sees the partial order.
Hypothesis: `MISSING`. No abort exists (§3.2). Retract-as-data can restore the *values*
but not the invariant "never observed" — `[24-OP-OUTERJOIN-02]` establishes that
transients are permitted, and an eager (non-glitch-free) downstream will have seen them.
The document must decide whether "restores the value but was transiently visible"
satisfies TPC-C's rollback requirement. It should read the TPC-C specification's own
wording before deciding, and if it cannot, say so per `[BB-TPCC-19]`.

**S3 — Payment (three-cell derived update)**
Given warehouse, district, and customer YTD balances and a history table;
When a payment is applied;
Then all four changes are visible together and the history row references the same
amounts.
Hypothesis: `PARTIAL`, same axis as S1. The plan's SNB row makes the sibling conjecture
("verify a single ingress delta fanning to person+edge cells lands in one wave (likely
already holds — verify, don't build)"). This epic's job is to *verify* it for Payment's
shape, in the kernel and its tests, and report the finding — including the negative
finding if it does not hold.

**S4 — Order-Status (read-only, cross-source)**
Given a customer cell and the order-line cells of that customer's latest order;
When the status is read;
Then the returned lines all belong to the same order and reflect one coherent moment.
Hypothesis: `COVERED` or `PARTIAL` via `[22-OBS-01]`/`[22-OBS-02]` (internally consistent
against *some* per-source vector frontier) plus the bounded read (`[21-PULL-02/03]`,
KRD). The catch is `[21-PULL-03]`'s "smeared" read: a walk is verifiable, not isolated.
The analysis must state whether "some frontier" is the same as "one coherent moment" for
this transaction's declared isolation requirement.

**S5 — Delivery (deferred, batched, ten districts)**
Given ten districts each with an oldest undelivered order;
When the delivery batch runs;
Then each district's order is marked delivered and the customer's balance updated, per
district atomically, and the batch may complete asynchronously.
Hypothesis: the **best fit** in the whole benchmark — a deferred batch is what a dataflow
model does natively, and the per-district scope is a single-key scope if districts are
the partition key (`[24-PART-03]`). Verdict likely `PARTIAL`→`COVERED`. This scenario is
the document's main positive result and should be presented as one.

**S6 — Stock-Level (read-only, reduced isolation)**
Given a district's last 20 orders and the stock cells of their items;
When the count of low-stock items is computed;
Then a count consistent with a recent state is returned.
Hypothesis: `COVERED`, modulo the actual isolation requirement TPC-C states for this
transaction. Bounded read plus a keyed-family scan (the KAGG-R range-scan surface named
in plan §3's YCSB row).

**S7 — Concurrent New-Orders on the same district (the interleaving case)**
Given two New-Order transactions arriving concurrently for the same district;
When both increment the district's next-order-id;
Then two distinct order ids are produced and no order id is reused.
Hypothesis: `COVERED` for the counter itself if the district is single-writer or a
partition owner (`[24-PART-03]`, 42 §Single-writer replication) — a per-key single writer
is a real strength and should be credited; `MISSING` for the joint case where the
increment must be atomic *with* the stock decrements, which is `[BB-TPCC-33]`'s
overlapping-participant question.

**S8 — Crash during a New-Order (durability of a partial transaction)**
Given a New-Order in progress with some stock decrements applied;
When the host crashes and recovers from its journal;
Then the transaction is either wholly applied or wholly absent.
Hypothesis: `MISSING`. `[24-DUR-01..05]` give per-cell journals and replay-stable
identity; there is no cross-cell commit record and no distributed log (§3.1). This is the
scenario behind `[BB-TPCC-37]`.

   section (bridge doc section 3) and a correction list per `[BB-TPCC-18]`. Read-only.
2. **F2 — TPC-C characterization.** Bridge doc section 2: the five transactions, the
   schema, the declared rollback, the per-transaction isolation requirements, and what
   the benchmark is actually asserting. Sets aside tpmC per `[BB-TPCC-17]`.
3. **F3 — Transaction walk and behaviour specifications.** Bridge doc section 4:
   scenarios S1–S8 with confirmed verdicts and named missing guarantees. Depends on
   F1+F2. This feature includes the actual verification work behind S3's conjecture.
4. **F4 — Gap specification sketch (EARS) and candidate evaluation.** Bridge doc
   sections 5 and 6: refine and reproduce group B (`[BB-TPCC-20..40]`); evaluate
   coordinator-cell-over-quorum-cells against `QuorumSetCell`/`ReplicaQuorum`/
   `demo/exchange`, the promotion two-phase swap, and rejected Candidate C.
5. **F5 — Decision, assembly, and lane findings.** Bridge doc sections 1, 7, 8; the
   decision per `[BB-TPCC-06]`; the quoted candidate row per `[BB-TPCC-07]`; the
   `doc/bench/findings.md` entry per `[BB-TPCC-16]`; and a boundary audit confirming
   `git status` shows exactly the two intended files.

---

## 8. Verification

The deliverable is reviewable and done when:

- Every group-A requirement `[BB-TPCC-01]` … `[BB-TPCC-19]` is satisfied by the produced
  document, checkable by reading it.
- Group B `[BB-TPCC-20]` … `[BB-TPCC-40]` appears in the bridge document's §5, refined,
  with every deletion justified in the text.
- Every scenario S1–S8 carries a verdict of `COVERED`, `PARTIAL`, or `MISSING` with a
  named mechanism or a named missing guarantee — no scenario left unannotated.
- A stated decision exists (§2.3) and does not read as a deferral.
- Citations resolve: every `[NN-SLUG-nn]` id quoted appears in the file it is attributed
  to; every repository path exists.
- `git status` shows changes confined to `doc/bench/bb-tpcc-bridge.md` and
  `doc/bench/findings.md`. No `doc/spec/` file, no `concord/` file, no source file.
- No test suite needs to run, and none was added — but if any command was run to verify
  a claim about the code (e.g. reading a test to confirm S3), the document names it.

Honesty clause: if a requirement above cannot be checked honestly against the produced
document, the reviewing agent says so in the review rather than marking it satisfied.
The same applies inside the document: `[BB-TPCC-19]` exists so that an unverifiable
assertion is labelled, not laundered.

---

## 9. Risks / open questions

- **The dominant risk: designing the primitive instead of specifying the gap.** Group B
  is a *specification sketch of what would have to be true*, deliberately written in the
  hypothetical. It is one short step from there to a protocol design, a message format,
  or a `CoordinatorCell` sketch — and that step is out of scope, would duplicate the
  already-rejected Candidate C, and would produce an unreviewable artifact. If the
  writing starts to feel like design, the correct move is to record the design question
  as an open point (`[BB-TPCC-25]`, `[BB-TPCC-33]`, `[BB-TPCC-36]` are already written
  that way) and stop.
- **The opposite failure: a survey that decides nothing.** `[BB-TPCC-06]` exists to
  prevent it. "It depends" is not a decision; a hybrid with both halves fully stated is.
- **Motivated reasoning toward (B).** Out-of-scope-by-design is the comfortable answer
  and the project's principles lean that way. The document must argue (A) properly
  before rejecting it, and must credit what the model *does* give (S5, S7's per-key
  single writer) so the negative result is credible rather than defensive.
- **Stale grounding.** §3's citations were gathered for this epic and the kernel lane
  moves. F1 exists because of this; `[BB-TPCC-18]` is its escape hatch.
- **Open question — how much TPC-C detail is enough?** The document needs the
  transactions' shapes and the declared rollback, not the full specification. If the
  agent cannot access the TPC-C specification text, it must say which claims rest on
  secondary knowledge (`[BB-TPCC-19]`), particularly the per-transaction isolation
  requirements that S4 and S6 turn on.
- **Open question — is `doc/bench/` the right lane directory?** Plan §6 says
  `doc/<lane>/findings.md`; no lane directory exists in `doc/` yet, so this epic
  establishes the convention for the BB lane. If a later integration pass prefers
  another name, that is a rename, not a rework.
- **Open question — does the narrow sub-gap (single-host, single-wave, bounded multi-cell
  all-or-nothing) deserve its own candidate G-item even if the general primitive is
  refused?** S1/S3's `PARTIAL` verdicts are where this gets decided, and it is the most
  likely genuinely useful outcome of the whole exercise.

# BB-TPCC — design notes for the implementing agents

## Why the document is shaped as an argument, not a survey

The failure mode of a "can X do OLTP?" document is a feature matrix with shrugs in the
cells. The structure imposed by the epic avoids that in three ways:

1. **Grounding first (F1).** Every claim about ComputeNet must resolve to a requirement
   id, a spec section, or a file path. This forbids the generic-dataflow-critique
   register, which is where these documents usually go wrong.
2. **Scenarios with verdicts (F3).** Every TPC-C scenario ends in `COVERED` / `PARTIAL` /
   `MISSING` plus a named mechanism or a named missing guarantee. A cell with a shrug in
   it fails review.
3. **A forced decision (F5).** §2.3 of the description permits a hybrid but not a
   deferral.

## Reading order for the implementing agent

1. `AGENTS.md` (authority order; "Start every task here"), `doc/ARCHITECTURE.md` §2, §7.
2. `doc/spec/20-dataflow-semantics/22-consistency.md` in full — it is the single most
   load-bearing file. Pay particular attention to §Source identity: emission epochs,
   §Local glitch-freedom, §Topology versioning (rule S5, the "explicit coordinator cell"
   escape hatch), §Completeness over silent or stuck edges (WAIT/DEGRADE/RE-SCOPE),
   §The observation frontier, and §Acceptance benchmark: the balanced-transfer suite.
   The last one is the document's rhetorical pivot: the spec's own money-transfer
   benchmark tests *observation*, not *execution*.
3. `21-propagation.md` §Push, §Bounded state read, §RESTART re-baselines.
4. `23-ownership.md` in full — note it carries **no** `[NN-SLUG-nn]` ids, so cite by
   section. §The four contracts, §The SPSC link rule, §Recovery and dead letters (R6/R7/R8),
   §Taps (the discharging-sink rule).
5. `24-data-cells.md` — `[24-OP-GROUPBY-03]`, `[24-PART-01..05]`, `[24-DUR-01..05]`,
   `[24-OP-OUTERJOIN-02]`, `[24-OP-SEMIJOIN-04]`, `[24-TAG-02]`, `[24-REPLAY-01]`.
6. `40-distribution/42-replication.md` — §Principles, §Single-writer replication,
   §Interest-scoped instance sets, `[42-REPL-04..06]`, `[42-INT-01]`, PN-5, PN-7.
   `41-location-transparency.md` — `[41-LOC-01]`, C-13.
7. `doc/spec/90-roadmap/91-gap-analysis.md` — for the **row shape** (four columns:
   `| ID | Gap | Resolution/proposal | Where |`, the `Where` column carrying
   `chapter/section` pairs like `20/24`, `40/42`) and for G-39, G-44, G-46, G-53, G-59.
   Highest currently-minted id is G-67; the proposed row therefore reads
   `G-NN (unassigned)`, never `G-68`.
8. `doc/spec/90-roadmap/95-research-plan.md` — for the **entry shape** (Question /
   Blocks / Directions, ranked by preference / Actions) and specifically R1 (leader
   election, where "classical consensus is explicitly *not* preferred (P4: no global
   coordination; P10: niche)"), R3 (coupling liveness, the compensating-release abort),
   R4 (compensating rollback of partial promotion).
9. `doc/spec/90-roadmap/93-feature-interactions.md` — Candidate C (cross-host atomic
   multi-link two-phase commit, **not adopted**), I-3, I-12, I-25.
10. `doc/spec/50-development-process/53-evolution.md` — the two-phase swap and the
    "whole-composite atomic transaction would be the distributed barrier P4 forbids" line.
11. Code: `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/op/QuorumSetCell.kt`,
    `.../consistency/ReplicaQuorum.kt`, `.../consistency/WaveFrontier.kt`,
    `.../replication/SingleWriterReplication.kt`;
    `demo/exchange/src/main/kotlin/civictech/demo/exchange/Main.kt` and
    `demo/exchange/src/test/kotlin/civictech/demo/exchange/ExchangeCompositionExitTest.kt`.

## Which of the two shapes the deliverable takes

The description requires a decision, and the decision determines which house shape the
proposal is rendered in *inside* the bridge document:

- Decision (A), a **candidate G-item** → render a `91-gap-analysis.md` table row, quoted.
  Suited to a *narrow, decidable* gap (e.g. bounded single-host multi-cell all-or-nothing).
- Decision (A'), a **research entry** → render a `95-research-plan.md` §R-entry, quoted,
  with Question / Blocks / Directions / Actions. Suited to a gap whose *solution shape is
  genuinely open* — which is the likelier fit for the full cross-host primitive, given
  that R1 already records classical consensus as not preferred. The implementing agent
  should treat this as a live third option and pick the shape that matches the honesty
  of the finding; §2.3's requirement is a *decision*, and "this is research-gated, here
  is the entry" is a decision.
- Decision (B), **out-of-scope-by-design** → render the sentence that a future
  integration pass would add to `42-replication.md` §Principles or
  `93-feature-interactions.md`, quoted, plus the per-transaction "what we offer instead".

In all three cases the rendering is *quoted text inside `doc/bench/bb-tpcc-bridge.md`*.
No spec file is touched. This is the single hardest boundary in the epic and the review
should check it first (`git status`).

## Anti-patterns to refuse explicitly

- **Writing a 2PC design.** If a paragraph starts specifying message rounds, ballot
  numbers, or a coordinator state machine, it has left scope. The right output is a
  Group-B EARS requirement plus an open-question marker.
- **Redefining the problem until it's solved.** "TPC-C is really just eventual
  consistency if you squint" is not a negative result, it is an evasion. The 1% rollback
  (S2) is the load-bearing case and cannot be squinted away.
- **Treating retract-as-data as an abort.** It restores values; it does not restore
  never-having-been-observed. `[24-OP-OUTERJOIN-02]` establishes that transients are
  permitted and observable. The document must state this distinction crisply — it is
  probably the single most valuable sentence in the deliverable.
- **Confusing `QuorumSetCell` with a quorum protocol.** It is a presence-count threshold
  over live source links; membership can leave the quorum when a source retracts. Read
  the source before writing about it.
- **Confusing PN-7 read settlement with a write quorum.** `ReplicaFrontier.completeAt`
  settles a *read*.
- **Crediting `demo/exchange` with transactional behaviour** because of its name. It is
  region-keyed orders → union → partitioned `GroupBy(sum)` → glitch-free board. Its
  exit test asserts convergence against a batch group-by, not atomicity.

## Verification approach

There is no test to run. Review is by reading, against the group-A ids. The one place
where actual repository verification is required is S3/S1's conjecture — whether a
single ingress delta fanning to several keyed cells lands in one wave. That is checkable
by reading `[24-OP-GROUPBY-03]`, the partitioned-shard tests
(`kernel/src/test/kotlin/civictech/cell/...` partitioned/shard tests and
`demo/exchange`'s exit test), and the `GroupByCell`/`MergeableGroupByCell` sources. The
document must report what it found, including a negative finding.

## Sizing

Roughly one focused session per feature; F3 and F4 are the substantial ones. The whole
epic is a writing task with a research front-end, explicitly flagged in the milestone
plan (§5 rank 19) as agent-idle work — it can be interleaved with anything, blocks
nothing, and is blocked by nothing.
acceptance_criteria: Group A requirements [BB-TPCC-01]..[BB-TPCC-19] all satisfied by doc/bench/bb-tpcc-bridge.md, checkable by reading it. Scenarios S1-S8 each annotated COVERED/PARTIAL/MISSING with a named mechanism or a named missing guarantee ([BB-TPCC-14]). A single decision stated per [BB-TPCC-06] and rendered in house shape per [BB-TPCC-07] or [BB-TPCC-09], quoted inside the bridge document only. Candidate evaluation satisfies [BB-TPCC-10], [BB-TPCC-11], [BB-TPCC-12], [BB-TPCC-13]. Lane findings entry added per [BB-TPCC-16].
