title: FRM1 — TLA+ model of wave completeness + glitch-freedom (G-38/G-39/G-40)
description:
# FRM1 — TLA+ model of wave completeness + glitch-freedom (G-38/G-39/G-40)

Lane: evidence (test/model-only). Source: `computenet-milestone-plan.md` §1 evidence row FRM1,
§2 DAG (`FRM1 -.spec input.-> KE3`, `FRM1 -.spec input.-> KE2`), §5 rank 11 — *"before KE3's spec
ticket is written"*. Depends on: nothing. Unblocks (soft, spec-input): the E2/E3 spec tickets
(96 §E2.1, §E3.1) that KE2 and KE3 will be written from.

---

## 1. Ambition / Why

ComputeNet's wave machinery has grown by accretion of *decided* rules — per-source waves (G-20),
in-band `EdgeOpen`/`EdgeClose` floors (G-39, 93 I-13), watermark advance by delta | `Progress`
absorb-ack | later wave (G-40, 93 I-18), catch-up-as-baseline (G-38, 93 I-24), cross-replica
covering quorums (PN-7), the R13 creation fence, the FU-2 converged-membership barrier. Each was
argued in prose and then defended by seeded tests. Seeded tests are the right instrument for
*implementation* defects; they are the wrong instrument for the question KE2 and KE3 are about to
answer, which is a **quantified** one:

> Is the completeness predicate *sound* (no release of a torn wave) and *live* (no wave stuck
> forever) over **all** interleavings of a topology that opens and closes edges, over arms that
> absorb, suspend, restart with fresh epochs, and arrive as replicas — or are the three advance
> mechanisms merely sufficient for the schedules our seeds happen to explore?

A 200-seed diamond test samples the schedule space. A model checker exhausts a small one. The
distinction matters most exactly where the spec is already nervous in writing: the G-39 proposal
asks for *"a liveness proof (an upstream cut must not strand a waiting join)"* in so many words,
and the G-40 residual asks to *"calibrate the backstop deadline against frontier depth"* — neither
is a thing a test can establish, both are things a bounded exhaustive check can.

**What the model buys, concretely, before KE2/KE3 are written:**

1. **A liveness answer for the G-39 cut.** `EdgeClose` "drops the link from all in-flight waves,
   unblocking any wave waiting on it" is asserted, never proved. The interesting case is a *chain*:
   a cut two hops upstream of a waiting join, where the intermediate cell is absorbing. Does the
   floor/ack/close machinery reach the join at all, given that all metadata-plane notices are
   single-hop (G-36)? A liveness property either holds or hands us a counterexample trace that is
   itself the KE3 ticket's motivating example.
2. **Whether the three advance mechanisms are complete.** G-40's core claim — delta ∨ `Progress`
   ∨ later-wave retires every arm — is a *closure* claim over a state machine. Model checking it
   with the absorb-ack rule disabled must produce the documented slotfinder stall; with it enabled
   it must produce nothing. That pair is the honest form of "the mechanism works".
3. **The vector-frontier guarantee stated once, precisely, before code.** [22-OBS-01] currently
   says "correct output for some per-source vector frontier of this replica's inputs" and cites a
   research essay. KE2 (E2 aligned sink) will implement whatever that sentence means. A TLA+
   definition of the batch-equivalence relation makes the sentence executable: the aligned sink's
   emission must equal the batch recompute over the frontier prefix. That definition is a
   deliverable KE2's spec ticket can cite verbatim.
4. **The R13/FU-2 hold-vs-release asymmetry, checked rather than argued.** PN-7 shrank the quorum
   to the covering subset, which introduced a *premature release* hazard closed by two separate
   conservative holds (the creation fence, the membership barrier). Those are precisely the shape
   of thing that is fine in every test you thought to write and wrong in the interleaving you
   didn't. KE3 inherits this substrate; it should inherit it checked.
5. **A cheap probe of the interactions we have only reasoned about**: floors × cycles × merge tags
   (named unresolved in G-39), baselines arriving mid-wave (G-38's mid-wave late join), and
   fresh-epoch `ReBaseline` succession recomputing a live completeness set (93 I-22).

**What is worth proving rather than testing** (the selection rule for §4): properties that quantify
over *all* schedules or *all* topologies of a bounded shape, and properties whose failure mode is a
permanent stall or a silent premature release rather than a wrong value. Properties about
throughput, allocation, encoding, or any single concrete run stay in tests where they belong.

**What this is not.** It is not a proof of the implementation. TLA+ checks a model; the model is a
hand-written abstraction, and the gap between it and `WaveFrontier.kt` is real and permanent (see
§8 Risks). The mitigation is not a refinement proof — that is disproportionate here — but a
*named, reviewed abstraction map* (§5) plus the discipline that every property the model checks
either already has a concord scenario or gets one filed as a follow-up.

---

## 2. What we build

### 2.1 Location and build integration

**New top-level directory `formal/`. Not a Gradle module.**

```
formal/
  README.md                  # what is modelled, what is not, how to run, how to read a trace
  ABSTRACTION.md             # the model↔kernel map of §5, reviewed as the epic's main artifact
  specs/
    Waves.tla                # core state machine: sources, epochs, FIFO links, edge markers
    Frontier.tla             # the WaveFrontier completeness fold (EXTENDS Waves)
    GlitchFree.tla           # diamond / nested-diamond safety + liveness properties
    Aligned.tla              # multi-view vector-frontier alignment ([22-OBS-01/02])
    ReplicaFrontier.tla      # delivered-watermark lattice, covering quorum, R13, FU-2, stability
  models/
    MCFrontierSmall.cfg      # + MCFrontierSmall.tla instance file per config
    MCFrontierCut.cfg
    MCAligned.cfg
    MCReplica.cfg
    MCStability.cfg
  controls/
    <one .cfg per control>   # deliberately broken constants/overrides that MUST fail
  check.sh                   # pinned tla2tools runner; runs every model + every control
  tools/
    tla2tools.sha256         # pinned release asset + checksum (no Maven coordinate exists)
```

**Justification for "not a Gradle module".** The precedent is explicit and twice-used in this
repo: `inspect/ui/` and `demo/agora/ui/` are deliberately npm-only and "not wired into Gradle"
(ARCHITECTURE §1, §5). The same reasoning applies harder here.

- The toolchain is `tla2tools.jar` (TLC) — distributed as a **GitHub release asset**, not as a
  Maven coordinate under any stable group id. Wiring it into Gradle means either vendoring a jar
  into the repo or adding a bespoke download task to `buildSrc` — a non-Kotlin toolchain inside
  the build graph that every `./gradlew test` would then carry.
- Nothing in `formal/` produces or consumes a classpath artifact. It imports no ComputeNet type
  and is imported by none. A Gradle module would exist purely to own a shell-out.
- `:concord`'s neutrality ratchet (`NeutralityGateTest`) shows the repo's taste here: the
  specification layer is kept structurally unable to reach into `civictech.cell.*`. `formal/` is
  the same layer one level more abstract; it should be *incapable* of coupling, not merely
  disciplined about it.

**How it runs.**

```bash
formal/check.sh                    # every model + every control; the CI entry point
formal/check.sh MCFrontierSmall    # one model
formal/check.sh --controls         # controls only
```

`check.sh` resolves a **pinned** `tla2tools.jar` (version + SHA-256 in `formal/tools/`), verifies
the checksum, runs `java -XX:+UseParallelGC -cp tla2tools.jar tlc2.TLC -workers auto -deadlock`
per config, and exits non-zero if any model reports a violation **or** if any control reports
success. Java 21 is already the repo toolchain, so there is no new runtime dependency.

**CI.** One new job `formal-check` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, structurally mirroring
`ui-test`/`agora-ui-test` (independent job, own timeout, no Gradle): checkout → setup-java 21 →
cache the pinned jar → `formal/check.sh`. It must be added to the branch-ruleset required checks
(AGENTS.md §Branches) in the same PR that introduces it, or it is decorative. Wall-clock budget is
a hard design constraint: the default configs must finish **under 10 minutes total** on a GitHub
runner. Any configuration exceeding that is split into a `formal/models/deep/` set run behind a
manual/`workflow_dispatch` gate and recorded in `README.md` with its last-run date and result —
never silently dropped.

### 2.2 TLA+, not Alloy

**Decision: TLA+ with TLC. Alloy is not adopted.**

- The load-bearing properties are **temporal**: *eventually* released, watermarks *always*
  monotone, stability *never* runs ahead of the true global frontier. These are TLA+'s native
  subject; expressing "eventually, under weak fairness of the delivery action" in Alloy's
  relational bounded-trace idiom is possible but adversarial.
- The subject is a **state machine with an evolving relation** (links open and close, epochs
  succeed, membership grows). TLA+ actions model that directly.
- Fairness is first-class. The G-39 liveness question is *precisely* a fairness question: which
  actions must be assumed to eventually fire for a waiting join to release. TLA+ makes the
  assumption explicit and reviewable; that assumption set is itself a deliverable for KE3.
- The counterexample is a **trace** — a schedule — which maps directly onto a `SimWorld` seed a
  later ticket can transcribe into a failing kernel test.

Alloy's strength — enumerating all *structures* of a bounded size — would suit one adjacent
question (which graph topologies are well-formed under cycle-head/damping-witness admission). That
question belongs to G-19/`LinkAdmission`, not to this epic. Recorded in `README.md` as considered
and declined; **out of scope** (§6).

Apalache is *optionally* used for one thing only: checking a candidate inductive invariant on the
watermark lattice, where TLC's state enumeration is weakest. It is not a required tool and must not
become one — if it is used, the result is recorded in `findings.md`, and the CI gate stays TLC.

### 2.3 The modules

| Module | Models | Kernel counterpart |
|---|---|---|
| `Waves.tla` | Sources as `(sourceId, epoch)` outlets with monotone counters; per-link FIFO channels; `EdgeOpen`/`EdgeClose` markers in-band on the link's own channel; per-source floors computed at marker processing; baseline-marked deltas; `ReBaseline` supersession | `MessageContext`/`Timestamp`, `FanOutlet` stamping, `Protocols`/`EdgeOpen`/`EdgeClose`, `MessageContext.baseline` |
| `Frontier.tla` | The completeness fold: per-edge per-source watermark map; advance by delta, by `Progress(thru)`, by later wave (`max`); the completeness predicate; release in per-source counter order; `Stall` with WAIT/DEGRADE/RE-SCOPE; suspended-edge set | `consistency/WaveFrontier.kt` |
| `GlitchFree.tla` | Diamond and nested-diamond topologies with absorbing intermediates; the no-torn-wave property; the batch-recompute reference function | `consistency/GlitchFree.kt`, `GlitchFreeDiamondTest` |
| `Aligned.tla` | N named views over a shared frontier; one composite published per settled wave; per-source vector frontier; batch-equivalence relation | `observe/AlignedCompositeCell`, `observeAligned` |
| `ReplicaFrontier.tla` | Delivered-watermark rows `slot → source → thru`, pointwise-max merge; covering-subset quorum by interest; R13 creation fence; FU-2 membership barrier via the gossiped `members` set; `closed`; causal stability as pointwise min; a mock reclaimer | `data/WatermarkCell.kt`, `consistency/ReplicaQuorum.kt`, `ReplicaFrontier` |

---

## 3. Functional requirements (EARS)

Two levels, deliberately kept apart. **`[FRM1-D-nn]`** are requirements on the *deliverable* — the
model artifact and its checking harness. **`[FRM1-P-nn]`** are the *properties the model asserts
about ComputeNet's semantics*; each cites the spec requirement id or gap it formalizes. Ids are
epic-scoped and never collide with normative `doc/spec/` ids (`[NN-SLUG-nn]`).

### 3.1 Deliverable requirements — the model artifact and harness

- **[FRM1-D-01]** (Ubiquitous) The formal model shall live under `formal/` and shall not be a
  Gradle module, shall not appear in `settings.gradle.kts`, and shall not be reachable from any
  Gradle task's inputs.
- **[FRM1-D-02]** (Ubiquitous) The model shall be written in TLA+ and checkable by TLC from a
  pinned `tla2tools.jar` release identified by version and SHA-256 in `formal/tools/`.

### 3.2 Modelled properties — what the model asserts about ComputeNet

Each cites the spec id or gap it formalizes. "Safety" ⇒ TLA+ invariant; "Liveness" ⇒ temporal
property under stated fairness.

**Core completeness and glitch-freedom** (formalizes [22-GF-01], [22-GF-02], [22-LIVE-01]; G-40)

- **[FRM1-P-01]** (Ubiquitous, safety) The model shall assert that a glitch-free cell never
  releases a wave whose input set mixes contributions from different waves of the same source —
  the no-torn-wave invariant of [22-GF-01].
- **[FRM1-P-02]** (Ubiquitous, safety) The model shall assert that every released wave `(s,t)` had,
  at release, `watermark(e,s) ≥ t` for every OPEN, non-suspended inlink `e` with `floor(e,s) < t`
  — completeness soundness, the predicate of 20/22 §Completeness over silent or stuck edges.
- **[FRM1-P-03]** (Ubiquitous, safety) The model shall assert that per-edge per-source watermarks
  are monotone non-decreasing under every action (G-40's `max` fold).
- **[FRM1-P-04]** (State-driven, safety) While waves from one source are being released, the model
  shall assert they are released in strictly increasing counter order on each inlet.
- **[FRM1-P-05]** (Event-driven, liveness) When a source emits a waved delta and every downstream
  cell eventually acts (weak fairness on delivery, absorb-ack, and quiescence actions), the model
  shall assert the wave is eventually either released or explicitly resolved by `EdgeClose` or
  RE-SCOPE — no wave is stuck forever. This is the G-40 liveness claim.
- **[FRM1-P-06]** (Event-driven, liveness) When an operator's waved input yields no effective
  output, the model shall assert a `Progress(sourceId, thru)` absorb-ack is emitted on the outlet's
  real links, riding that exact wave — the emitting-side obligation of the absorb-ack rule.
- **[FRM1-P-07]** (Unwanted, liveness) If the absorb-ack action is disabled, then the model shall
  exhibit a reachable state in which a wave is permanently unreleased — the documented slotfinder
  stall, the control that proves the rule is load-bearing.
- **[FRM1-P-08]** (Ubiquitous, safety) The model shall assert that an independent silent source
  never blocks the release of waves from another source ([22-LIVE-01]; over-alignment across
  independent sources is forbidden).

**Topology versioning and cuts** (formalizes G-39; 93 I-13/I-14)

- **[FRM1-P-09]** (Event-driven, safety) When a consumer processes an `EdgeOpen` marker, the model
  shall assert every arrival on that edge at or below the computed per-source floor is discarded as
  pre-join and never admitted to a completeness set.
- **[FRM1-P-10]** (Event-driven, liveness) When an `EdgeClose` is processed for an edge a wave is
  waiting on, the model shall assert that wave is unblocked in a bounded number of steps.
- **[FRM1-P-11]** (Event-driven, liveness) When an upstream link is cut two or more hops above a
  waiting join, with an absorbing intermediate cell, the model shall assert the join is not
  stranded — the liveness proof G-39 asks for verbatim. **Honest caveat:** given G-36 (all
  metadata-plane notices are single-hop), this property is expected to *fail* as the spec currently
  stands; the deliverable is the counterexample and its disposition, not a green run. It is
  therefore checked in `models/`, not asserted as a passing gate, and its status is recorded per
  [FRM1-D-14].
- **[FRM1-P-12]** (Event-driven, safety) When an outlet starts a fresh emission epoch, the model
  shall assert no `(sourceId, counter)` pair is ever reused across epochs or instances (93 I-14
  rules S1/S2).
- **[FRM1-P-13]** (Event-driven, safety) When a fresh-epoch succession of a live lane occurs, the
  model shall assert a `ReBaseline` supersession notice naming the superseded source ids precedes
  any delivery under the new epoch, and that consumers recompute their per-source completeness set
  on it (93 I-11/I-22; C-12).
- **[FRM1-P-14]** (Ubiquitous, safety) The model shall assert a preserved-epoch instance swap emits
  no edge event and is invisible to downstream completeness (93 I-11).

**Baselines and catch-up** (formalizes G-38; 93 I-24; [22-REC-01])

- **[FRM1-P-15]** (Ubiquitous, safety) The model shall assert a baseline-marked delta is never
  admitted to any wave-completeness set and never advances a watermark.
- **[FRM1-P-16]** (Event-driven, safety) When a consumer installs a baseline mid-stream, the model
  shall assert that glitch-freedom resumes at the first wave complete over the post-install
  topology, and that no output between install and that wave claims wave alignment.
- **[FRM1-P-17]** (Unwanted, safety) If a baseline were admitted to a completeness set, then the
  model shall exhibit a torn release — the control proving the exclusion rule is load-bearing.

**Vector-frontier observation** (formalizes [22-OBS-01], [22-OBS-02]; KE2/E2 input)

- **[FRM1-P-18]** (Ubiquitous, safety) The model shall assert every published composite equals the
  batch recompute over some per-source vector frontier of the inputs — internal consistency stated
  as a checkable equivalence, [22-OBS-01].
- **[FRM1-P-19]** (State-driven, safety) While a composite is being assembled for wave `(s,t)`, the
  model shall assert it is published only after every contributing named view has settled every
  wave at or below the shared frontier ([22-OBS-02]).
- **[FRM1-P-20]** (Ubiquitous, safety) The model shall assert per-name view identity is preserved
  through assembly — two views emitting an identical delta remain distinguishable ([22-OBS-02],
  `observeAll` blocker 1).
- **[FRM1-P-21]** (Unwanted, safety) If assembly is point-consistent per view rather than
  frontier-aligned, then the model shall exhibit a composite mixing waves — the `CompositeSink`
  control.
- **[FRM1-P-22]** (Optional-feature, safety) Where frontier-gated emission is enabled for a
  non-monotone operator (antijoin membership flip, outer-join null extension), the model shall
  assert no enter-then-exit pair for the same element is observable within one wave, and no
  null-extended row is retracted by the wave that produced it (96 §E2.4).

**Cross-replica settlement and stability** (formalizes G-39/G-40 residuals, G-42; PN-7, R13, FU-2;
KE3/E3 input)

- **[FRM1-P-23]** (Ubiquitous, safety) The model shall assert the delivered-watermark row merge is
  a join-semilattice — commutative, associative, idempotent, monotone under pointwise max.
- **[FRM1-P-24]** (Ubiquitous, safety) The model shall assert no local settlement read runs ahead
  of the true global delivered frontier (the Naiad safety analog, 96 §E3.1 point 2).
- **[FRM1-P-25]** (State-driven, safety) While instance interests are disjoint, the model shall
  assert a keyed wave settles on the covering subset only, and a non-covering member never holds it
  (PN-7 F2).
- **[FRM1-P-26]** (Event-driven, safety) When a covering member joins with no row for a source, the
  model shall assert the wave is **held**, not released — the R13 creation fence.
- **[FRM1-P-27]** (Event-driven, safety) When a covering member has announced itself on the
  watermark companion but is absent from the local `instancesOf` view, the model shall assert every
  keyed wave is held until membership converges (FU-2 barrier).
- **[FRM1-P-28]** (Unwanted, safety) If the creation fence or the membership barrier is disabled,
  then the model shall exhibit a premature release — a torn cross-replica read.
- **[FRM1-P-29]** (State-driven, liveness) While the membership set is converged and every live
  member heartbeats, the model shall assert every held keyed wave is eventually released — the hold
  is a latency bound, not a wedge (FU-2 §Boundaries).
- **[FRM1-P-30]** (Ubiquitous, safety) The model shall assert the causal-stability frontier
  (pointwise min over open rows) is monotone and never exceeds any member's delivered watermark
  (96 §E3.5 invariants i–ii).
- **[FRM1-P-31]** (Ubiquitous, safety) The model shall assert a reclaimer discarding tombstones at
  or below the stability frontier never causes a removed element to be resurrected by a later
  merge (the G-42 GC safety property).
- **[FRM1-P-32]** (Unwanted, safety) If reclamation is triggered at the merely *locally* delivered
  frontier rather than the stability frontier, then the model shall exhibit a resurrection — the
  control proving stability, not delivery, is the correct trigger (96 §E3.5).
- **[FRM1-P-33]** (Event-driven, safety) When a member departs cleanly by closing its row, the
  model shall assert stability advances past it; and when a member vanishes without closing, the
  model shall assert stability freezes and is surfaced, never silently unfrozen (96 §E3.6).

**Cycles** (formalizes 93 I-5; bounded)

- **[FRM1-P-34]** (Event-driven, safety) When a declared cycle head re-originates at the
  feedback→emission transition, the model shall assert no `(sourceId, counter)` traverses any cell
  twice, so per-wave buffering applies to loops unchanged.
- **[FRM1-P-35]** (Ubiquitous, safety) The model shall assert feedback inlets never join wave
  completeness.

**Explicit non-properties** (per [FRM1-D-13]) — stated here so no later reader mistakes their
absence for an oversight: no property about wall-clock backstop deadlines (the model has no clock;
G-40's "calibrate the backstop deadline against frontier depth" is answered only as a *structural
depth* bound, not a duration); no property about the DEGRADE correctness contract's *observability*
(how a downstream distinguishes a degraded emission is undecided in spec — the model checks
DEGRADE's frontier-shrinking effect only, and the observability half is filed as an open question,
§8); no property about Byzantine or permanently-partitioned members (96 §E3.6 residual).

## 4. Behaviour specifications

Each is a model-checking obligation: the configuration, the property, and the counterexample shape
that falsifies it. Concord linkage is noted where the property has an executable sibling; a noted
`covers:` id means the concord scenario exercises the same rule on the implementation — the model
generalizes it over schedules, it does not replace it.

### BS-1 — Diamond, no torn wave
*Given* a source `A` fanning to `B` and `C`, both feeding glitch-free join `D`, all edges open,
*when* TLC explores every interleaving of delivery on the two arms for `WaveBound = 3` waves,
*then* [FRM1-P-01] and [FRM1-P-02] hold at every state.
**Config**: `MCFrontierSmall` — 1 source, 2 arms, 3 waves, no absorption.
**Counterexample shape**: a state where `D` has released wave `t` with arm `B` at `t` and arm `C`
at `t−1`.
**Concord**: `covers: 22-GF-DIAMOND-01`; nested variant `22-GF-NESTED-01` (checked as
`MCFrontierSmall` with a 2-level chain).

### BS-2 — Absorbing arm, wave still releases
*Given* the diamond of BS-1 with `C` a filter that drops the final wave, *when* the filter absorbs
and emits `Progress(s, t)` per the absorb-ack rule, *then* `D` releases wave `t` without waiting
for a subsequent write — [FRM1-P-05], [FRM1-P-06].
**Config**: `MCFrontierSmall` with `AbsorbAck = TRUE`.
**Counterexample shape**: a terminal state (deadlock) with a buffered wave at `D` and no enabled
action — TLC's `-deadlock` check is the detector.
**Concord**: `covers: 22-LIVE-01` (silent-source sibling).

### BS-3 — Control: absorb-ack disabled ⇒ permanent stall
*Given* BS-2's configuration, *when* the absorb-ack action is disabled, *then* TLC **must** report
a violation of [FRM1-P-05] — [FRM1-P-07].
**Config**: `controls/MCNoAbsorbAck.cfg`. A clean run here fails the harness ([FRM1-D-05]).
**Counterexample shape**: exactly the documented slotfinder stall — the trace is the expected
output, and its absence is the defect.

### BS-4 — Silent independent source
*Given* two independent sources into a `k=1` fan-in join, *when* one source never emits, *then*
waves from the live source are released — [FRM1-P-08].
**Config**: `MCFrontierSmall` with `Sources = {s1, s2}`, `EmitFrom = {s1}`.
**Counterexample shape**: a wave from `s1` never released because `s2`'s edge is treated as
expected.
**Concord**: `covers: 22-LIVE-01`.

### BS-5 — Mid-stream `EdgeOpen`, floor discards pre-join arrivals
*Given* a join with one open arm and one arm opened after waves 1–2 have flushed, *when* the new
arm's producer emits waves 1–3, *then* waves at or below the computed floor are discarded as
pre-join and wave 3 completes over the post-install topology — [FRM1-P-09], [FRM1-P-16].
**Config**: `MCFrontierCut` with `OpenLate = TRUE`.
**Counterexample shape**: a pre-join arrival admitted to a completeness set, producing either a
torn release or a permanently unsatisfiable expectation.

### BS-6 — `EdgeClose` unblocks a waiting wave
*Given* a join waiting on arm `C` for wave `t`, *when* `C`'s link is closed, *then* the wave
releases within a bounded number of steps — [FRM1-P-10].
**Config**: `MCFrontierCut`.
**Counterexample shape**: `EdgeClose` processed and the wave still buffered in the terminal state.

### BS-7 — Upstream cut two hops above a waiting join (the G-39 liveness question)
*Given* `A → M → D` where `M` is absorbing and `D` is also fed by `B`, *when* the link `A → M` is
cut while `D` waits on the `M` arm for wave `t`, *then* [FRM1-P-11] asks whether `D` is eventually
unblocked.
**Config**: `MCFrontierCut` with `ChainDepth = 2`.
**Expected outcome**: a **counterexample**, given G-36's single-hop restriction on metadata-plane
notices. The deliverable for this scenario is the trace, its minimal configuration, and a
`doc/formal/findings.md` entry naming G-39 and G-36 — *not* a passing check ([FRM1-D-14]). If it
unexpectedly passes, the reason must be explained in `ABSTRACTION.md` (most likely the model is
over-generous about marker propagation, which is itself a finding).

### BS-8 — Fresh-epoch restart is announced, not silent
*Given* a live source lane feeding a glitch-free join, *when* the source cell restarts under
supervision and mints a fresh epoch, *then* a `ReBaseline` naming the superseded ids precedes any
delivery under the new epoch and the consumer recomputes its completeness set — [FRM1-P-12],
[FRM1-P-13].
**Config**: `MCFrontierCut` with `Restarts = 1`.
**Counterexample shape**: a wave under the new epoch admitted while the join still expects the
superseded source, stalling forever; or a `(sourceId, counter)` reused across the epoch boundary.
**Concord**: `covers: 22-SOURCE-ID-01`, `21-REBASE-01`.

### BS-9 — Baseline excluded from completeness
*Given* a consumer receiving a catch-up state-as-delta on link install, *when* the baseline is
installed, *then* it advances no watermark and joins no completeness set — [FRM1-P-15].
Paired control `controls/MCBaselineCounted.cfg`: admitting it produces a torn release
— [FRM1-P-17].
**Counterexample shape** (control, expected): the join releases a wave whose expectation was
satisfied by a baseline that represents no single wave — G-38's original unsatisfiable-as-written
observation, reproduced mechanically.

### BS-10 — Aligned composite equals a batch recompute over a vector frontier
*Given* 3 named views over 2 sources feeding one aligned composite, *when* every interleaving is
explored for `WaveBound = 3`, *then* every published composite equals the batch recompute over some
per-source vector frontier — [FRM1-P-18], [FRM1-P-19], [FRM1-P-20].
**Config**: `MCAligned`.
**Counterexample shape**: a published composite matching no vector frontier — i.e. view `v1` at
`(s1,2)` and `v2` at `(s1,1)`, the exact failure the balanced-transfer suite hunts for at runtime.
**Concord**: no scenario today — file as a scenario-gap candidate per [FRM1-D-12].
**Control** `controls/MCPointConsistent.cfg`: point-consistent assembly violates it — [FRM1-P-21].

### BS-11 — Non-monotone emission gating
*Given* an antijoin whose membership flips twice within one wave, *when* `emitOnFrontier` is
enabled, *then* the net effect is emitted once and no enter/exit pair is observable within the wave
— [FRM1-P-22]. Ungated is the control (flicker expected).
**Config**: `MCAligned` with `Gated ∈ {TRUE, FALSE}`.

### BS-12 — Watermark lattice laws
*Given* rows gossiped over a mesh with duplication, reorder, and partition/heal, *when* every merge
order is explored, *then* the merge is commutative, associative, idempotent, and monotone, and all
members converge — [FRM1-P-23].
**Config**: `MCReplica` — 3 slots, 2 sources, `ThruBound = 2`.
**Counterexample shape**: two members with divergent rows at quiescence, or a row that decreases.
**Control**: a signed-delta (Naiad-verbatim) accumulator double-counts under redelivery — the
documented reject in 96 §E3.2.

### BS-13 — Covering quorum under disjoint interest
*Given* a 2-slot × 2-copy instance set with disjoint interests, *when* a keyed wave touching one
slice is settled, *then* only the covering subset is quorum — [FRM1-P-25]. Control: quantifying
over all members never releases (the pre-PN-7 F2 stall).
**Config**: `MCReplica` with `Interests` disjoint.
**Concord**: sibling of `ShardedReplicaFrontierTest`; no corpus scenario — gap candidate.

### BS-14 — R13 fence and FU-2 barrier hold, never release early
*Given* a settled mesh, *when* a covering member joins with no row (R13) or announces on the
companion before appearing in `instancesOf` (FU-2), *then* every keyed wave is **held** —
[FRM1-P-26], [FRM1-P-27] — and released once convergence completes — [FRM1-P-29].
**Config**: `MCReplica` with `Join = TRUE`.
**Counterexample shape**: a keyed wave released in a state where an unaccounted covering member
exists — a torn cross-replica read.
**Control** `controls/MCNoFence.cfg` and `controls/MCNoBarrier.cfg`: both must produce that
premature release — [FRM1-P-28].

### BS-15 — Stability frontier and GC safety
*Given* the mesh of BS-12 with a mock reclaimer, *when* tombstones at or below the stability
frontier are discarded, *then* no later merge resurrects a removed element — [FRM1-P-30],
[FRM1-P-31]. Control: reclaiming at the locally delivered frontier resurrects — [FRM1-P-32].
**Config**: `MCStability`.
**Counterexample shape**: a converged state where an element removed before reclamation is present
on some member.

### BS-16 — Departure
*Given* a 3-member mesh, *when* a member closes its row, *then* stability advances past it; *when*
a member vanishes without closing, *then* stability freezes and the freeze is observable —
[FRM1-P-33]. Control: a silent unfreeze must be unreachable.
**Config**: `MCStability` with `Departures = {clean, unclean}`.

### BS-17 — Cycle head wave uniqueness
*Given* a declared cycle head with a feedback inlet, *when* the loop iterates to the bound, *then*
no `(sourceId, counter)` traverses any cell twice and feedback inlets never join completeness —
[FRM1-P-34], [FRM1-P-35].
**Config**: `MCFrontierCut` with `Cycle = TRUE`, `IterBound = 3`.
**Concord**: chapter-34 corpus is the runtime sibling.

### BS-18 — Harness teeth
*Given* the full `formal/check.sh` run, *when* any control in `formal/controls/` passes cleanly,
*then* the harness exits non-zero — [FRM1-D-05]. This is the meta-scenario a reviewer runs by
deliberately "fixing" a control and confirming CI goes red.

## 5. How, using ComputeNet — the abstraction map

This is the content of `formal/ABSTRACTION.md` and the epic's most reviewable artifact. Every model
name binds to a real concept and a real path; each row also states what is abstracted away.

| Model constant/variable/action | ComputeNet concept | Where it lives | Abstracted away |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Sources` (set of `[id, epoch]`) | outlet emission epoch — a source is *one outlet during one epoch of one instance*, never the logical cell (93 I-14 Rule S5) | `cell.MessageContext`, `Timestamp(sourceId, counter)`; minting in `cell.port.FanOutlet` | UUID collision-freedom is assumed, not modelled |
| `counter` | the per-outlet monotone wave counter | `Timestamp.counter` | 64-bit overflow |
| `Cells`, `Edges` | cells and links, with `LinkRole` restricted to `Consume` (only Consume links count toward frontiers) | `cell.link.Link`, `LinkRole`; `ManagedHost.connect` | `Observe` taps (never gate a wave), link policies, nature reconciliation |
| `channel[e]` (sequence) | per-link FIFO — the property that makes wave completion monotone per source | spec 30/31; `ManagedHost` dispatch, `HostedPortInvocation` | attention bands, intake saturation, park/coalesce — the model assumes only FIFO per link |
| `Deliver(e)` action | one invocation dequeued and handled | `AttentionScheduler` per-cell FIFO; `SimulationController` for determinism | band selection between cells (irrelevant to per-source FIFO) |
| `EdgeOpen(e)` / `EdgeClose(e)` | in-band markers on the affected link's own FIFO (93 I-13) | `cell.protocol.EdgeOpen`/`EdgeClose`, `TopologyOrderProtocol`; bridged as `PORT_PROTOCOL` frames | the wire encoding — bridged and local are one model (spec's own location-transparency claim, [22-GF-03]) |
| `floor[e][s]` | the consumer-computed per-source flushed high-water at marker processing | `WaveFrontier` floors | representation/compaction horizon (an open G-39 question the model can *probe* but not decide) |
| `watermark[e][s]` | per-edge per-source settled counter, advanced by delta ∨ `Progress` ∨ later wave | `WaveFrontier` | none material |
| `Progress(s, thru)` | the absorb-ack, emitted when a waved input yields no effective output | `cell.control.Progress`, `cell.control.absorbAck`, `emitOrAbsorb` in `civictech.cell.data.op` | which operator absorbed — the model has one generic absorbing cell |
| `Stall(reason, recoverable)` + `WAIT`/`DEGRADE`/`RE-SCOPE` | typed stall markers and per-edge policy | `cell.control.StallNotice`, `GlitchFreeCell.WaveMode` | DEGRADE's *observability* contract (undecided; see §3.2 non-properties) |
| `Complete(s,t)` | every OPEN, non-suspended inlink with `floor(s) < t` has `watermark(s) ≥ t` | `WaveFrontier`'s completeness test | — |
| `baseline` flag on a delta | `MessageContext.baseline: TagFrontier?` — catch-up and journal replay (G-38, [22-REC-01]) | `cell.MessageContext`; `GlitchFreeCell`'s baseline branch; `ManagedHost.recoverFrom`'s `ReplayScope` | the tag frontier's *content* — the model needs only the marked/unmarked bit |
| `ReBaseline(supersededIds)` | fresh-epoch succession notice (93 I-22) | `cell.ReBaselineNotice`; supervision RESTART path in `ManagedHost` | — |
| `views[name]` + `Composite` | named inlets of the aligned sink, one composite per settled wave | `cell.observe.AlignedCompositeCell`, `ManagedHost.observeAligned` | the fold's payload type — deltas are opaque tokens with a batch-recompute reference function |
| `rows[slot][source]` + `Merge` | delivered-watermark lattice, pointwise max | `cell.data.WatermarkCell`, `WatermarkDelta` | gossip transport; the model merges nondeterministically, which is stronger |
| `closed`, `members` | grow-only departure and membership sets | `WatermarkDelta.closed`, `announceMember()` | — |
| `interest[slot]`, `CoveringSubset(key)` | interest-scoped covering quorum (PN-7) | `cell.link.Interest`/`Scoped`; `ReplicaFrontier.completeAt(source, counter, key)`; `LocationRegistry.instancesOf` | the key space — a small enumerated `Keys` set |
| `fence`, `barrier` | R13 creation fence, FU-2 converged-membership barrier | `Replication.replicaFrontier(creationFence, membershipBarrier)`, `cell.consistency.ReplicaQuorum` | — |
| `stable` | pointwise min over open rows = causal stability | `stableFrontier(logicalId)` (96 §E3.5) | — |
| `CycleHead`, `feedback[e]` | cycle-head re-origination; feedback inlets absorb into loop state (93 I-5) | `cell.port.FeedbackInlet`, `CycleHead`; `LinkAdmission` | `hop` divergence guard (a liveness backstop, not part of the wave join key) |

**Dispatch classes and ownership** are deliberately *not* in the model (§6): `Owned`/`Leased`
discipline is an accounting property of failure paths, orthogonal to wave completeness, and adding
it would multiply the state space for no property gained.

---

## 6. Scope boundaries

**This epic delivers a model and its checking harness. Nothing else.**

- **Not implementing KE2 or KE3.** No kernel code. `WaveFrontier`, `AlignedCompositeCell`,
  `WatermarkCell`, `ReplicaQuorum` are *read* and mapped, never modified. The E2/E3 spec tickets
  are written by KE2/KE3 later, citing this model's findings — the milestone-plan edge is
  `spec input`, dotted, soft.
- **Not replacing concord.** Concord is the executable specification *of the implementation*: it
  binds requirement ids to scenarios a driver runs against real kernel code. The model is
  **upstream** of that — it checks whether the *rules themselves* are sound and live, over
  schedules no scenario enumerates, before any implementation exists to check. The relationship is
  one-directional: a model counterexample becomes a candidate concord scenario or a `DISPUTES.md`
  entry; a concord failure is never "answered" by the model. No corpus YAML, no `covers:` id, no
  `CONCORDANCE.md` regeneration is part of this epic ([FRM1-D-17]) — a scenario the model motivates
  is filed as a follow-up bead for the owning lane.
- **Not editing the spec.** G-38/G-39/G-40 rows in `91-gap-analysis.md`, the 20/22 chapter, and
  `93-feature-interactions.md` are *inputs*. Findings go to `doc/formal/findings.md` (milestone-plan
  §6: every lane writes its own append-only findings file; the periodic integration pass is the
  only writer of the gap table).
- **Not modelled** (each an explicit non-goal, not an oversight):
  - **Durability and journal replay mechanics** — beyond the single fact that replay is a baseline
    ([22-REC-01]). Journal segmentation, checkpoint atomicity, `Effectful` processed-frontier
    dedup: out.
  - **Ownership and exclusive payloads** — `Owned`/`Leased` consume/release/discharge accounting.
    Orthogonal; belongs to a different model if ever.
  - **Wire format and encoding** — `WireCodec`, frame types, `routingEpoch`, HELLO. The model
    assumes location transparency ([22-GF-03]) rather than proving it; a bridged edge and a local
    edge are the same model object. That assumption is itself recorded in `ABSTRACTION.md` as a
    limitation.
  - **Scheduling, attention, backpressure** — bands, `IntakeControl`, `ParkQueue`, quotas. The
    model assumes only per-link FIFO.
  - **Replication *convergence*** — CRDT merge correctness for `SetCell`/`OrMapCell` payloads. The
    watermark lattice is modelled; the data lattices are not (they have their own harnesses).
  - **Fixpoint semantics / G-19** — cycles are modelled only for wave *uniqueness* ([FRM1-P-34]),
    never for convergence or quiescence thresholds.
  - **Membership election and failure detection** (G-44/G-45, MEM1/MEM2) — the model takes
    membership as a given set with join/depart actions.
  - **Byzantine members, permanent partition** (96 §E3.6 residual), wall-clock deadlines, and
    performance of any kind.
  - **Alloy** — considered and declined (§2.2). The structural-topology question it would suit
    belongs to G-19/`LinkAdmission`.
  - **Refinement proof from model to Kotlin.** Disproportionate. The abstraction map plus the
    control/counterexample discipline is the honest substitute, and §8 names the residual risk.

---

## 7. Suggested feature decomposition

1. **FRM1-F1 — `formal/` scaffold, pinned TLC runner, CI gate, controls harness.**
   Satisfies [FRM1-D-01]–[FRM1-D-06], [FRM1-D-08], [FRM1-D-10], BS-18. Lands with one trivial
   model and one trivial control so the teeth exist before any real property does.
2. **FRM1-F2 — `Waves.tla`: the core state machine + `ABSTRACTION.md`.**
   Sources/epochs, FIFO channels, edge markers, floors, baselines, `ReBaseline`. Satisfies
   [FRM1-P-09], [FRM1-P-12]–[FRM1-P-17], [FRM1-D-11]; BS-5, BS-8, BS-9.
3. **FRM1-F3 — `Frontier.tla` + `GlitchFree.tla`: completeness, absorb-acks, cuts.**
   The epic's centre of gravity. Satisfies [FRM1-P-01]–[FRM1-P-08], [FRM1-P-10], [FRM1-P-11];
   BS-1, BS-2, BS-3, BS-4, BS-6, BS-7.
4. **FRM1-F4 — `Aligned.tla`: vector-frontier observation (KE2 input).**
   Satisfies [FRM1-P-18]–[FRM1-P-22]; BS-10, BS-11.
5. **FRM1-F5 — `ReplicaFrontier.tla`: delivered watermarks, covering quorum, stability (KE3 input).**
   Satisfies [FRM1-P-23]–[FRM1-P-33]; BS-12–BS-16.
6. **FRM1-F6 — Cycles + findings write-up and handoff.**
   [FRM1-P-34], [FRM1-P-35]; BS-17. Then `doc/formal/findings.md` per [FRM1-D-14]/[FRM1-D-15], the
   scenario-gap list per [FRM1-D-12], and follow-up beads for anything the model defeats.

F1 → F2 → F3; F4 and F5 both depend on F3 (they reuse the frontier fold) and are mutually
independent; F6 last.

---

## 8. Verification — how a reviewer confirms this is real

**That the model matches the spec:**

1. Read `ABSTRACTION.md` row by row against §5's table and open each cited kernel path. Every
   model action must name a real concept; every abstraction must be stated, not implied.
2. For each `[FRM1-P-nn]`, open the cited spec section and confirm the TLA+ formula says the same
   thing. The high-value spot checks: `Complete(s,t)` against 20/22 §Completeness over silent or
   stuck edges (the `floor(s) < t` guard is easy to get subtly wrong); the baseline exclusion
   against 20/22 §Pull/late-join; `CoveringSubset` against 20/22 §Interest-scoped settlement.
3. Confirm the §3.2 non-properties list is honest — that nothing on it was quietly demoted from a
   property to a comment ([FRM1-D-13]).

**That checking actually runs:**

4. `formal/check.sh` locally: every model passes, every control fails, exit code 0.
5. Break a control on purpose (make it pass) and confirm `check.sh` exits non-zero — BS-18.
6. Break an invariant on purpose (weaken `Complete`) and confirm the corresponding model reports a
   violation with a readable trace.
7. Confirm `formal-check` is in the CI workflow **and** in the branch ruleset's required checks —
   a job that isn't required is a job that can go red unnoticed ([FRM1-D-10]).
8. Check the reported wall-clock against [FRM1-D-08]; confirm anything over budget is in
   `models/deep/` with a dated result line, not silently deleted ([FRM1-D-09]).
9. Confirm TLC reports non-trivial state counts and no `Assumption` short-circuit — a model that
   explores 40 states is checking its own bounds, not ComputeNet.

**That the output is usable by KE2/KE3:**

10. `doc/formal/findings.md` exists, cites G-ids, and — critically — records BS-7's expected
    counterexample with its minimal configuration. A green run everywhere is *suspicious*, not
    reassuring: the epic's most valuable single output is the G-39 cut trace.
11. Confirm no file under `kernel/`, `doc/spec/`, or `concord/corpus/` changed except a permitted
    `DISPUTES.md` append ([FRM1-D-17]) — `git diff --stat` against the base.

---

## 9. Risks and open questions

- **State-space blowup.** The dominant risk. Mitigation is bound discipline: 1–2 sources, 2–3
  arms, ≤3 waves, ≤3 replica slots, symmetry sets where TLC allows, and separate small models per
  property family rather than one grand unified spec. If a config cannot fit the 10-minute budget
  it moves to `models/deep/` ([FRM1-D-09]) — never quietly shrunk until it passes.
- **Model-vs-implementation drift.** Real and unfixable at this budget. `WaveFrontier.kt` will
  change under KE2/KE3 and the model will not follow automatically. Disposition: the model is
  dated evidence about the *rules as specified at a commit*, and `ABSTRACTION.md` records that
  commit. It is not a regression gate on kernel behavior — concord is. Open question for the
  reviewer: should the CI job be *required* (drift then breaks builds) or *advisory*? This epic
  proposes required, on the argument that a model nobody must keep green is a model nobody keeps.
- **A model that proves nothing.** The failure mode where every property passes because the model
  is too generous (e.g. metadata notices propagate multi-hop where the real system is single-hop
  per G-36). Mitigation: the control-must-fail discipline ([FRM1-D-05], [FRM1-D-07]) and the
  explicit expectation that BS-7 *fails*.
- **Ownership and maintenance.** Nobody in this repo currently writes TLA+. Open question: is
  `formal/` maintained by whoever touches wave semantics next (i.e. KE2/KE3's implementer inherits
  it), or is it a dated artifact that goes stale by design? This epic recommends the former and
  requires `README.md` to state the answer explicitly, whichever is chosen.
- **BS-7 may reveal that a decided rule is unsound.** If the G-39 cut cannot be made live without
  hop-by-hop metadata propagation (G-36), that is a scope discovery affecting KE3, not a bug in
  this epic. Disposition per [FRM1-D-15]: findings file plus a follow-up bead; no spec edit here.
- **Backstop deadlines are unmodellable.** G-40 asks to "calibrate the backstop deadline against
  frontier depth". A model with no clock can answer only the structural half (frontier depth).
  Stated as a non-property (§3.2) rather than faked with a step counter dressed up as time.
- **DEGRADE's correctness contract is undecided in spec**, so the model can check its
  frontier-shrinking effect but not "how downstream distinguishes a degraded emission". Open
  question forwarded to KE2/KE3 rather than invented here.
design:
# FRM1 — design notes

## Deliverable shape (decided)

`formal/` — a new **top-level, non-Gradle** directory, on the `inspect/ui` / `demo/agora/ui`
precedent ("npm-only and deliberately not wired into Gradle", ARCHITECTURE §1).

Why not a Gradle module:
- `tla2tools.jar` (TLC) ships as a GitHub release asset, with no stable Maven coordinate. Wiring it
  in means vendoring a jar or adding a download task to `buildSrc` — a non-Kotlin toolchain inside
  the build graph that every `./gradlew test` then carries.
- The directory produces and consumes no classpath artifact. It imports no `civictech.*` type and
  is imported by none. A module would exist only to own a shell-out.
- The repo's taste (`NeutralityGateTest` on `:concord`) is to make specification layers
  *structurally* unable to reach into `civictech.cell.*`. `formal/` is that layer one level more
  abstract; it should be incapable of coupling, not merely disciplined.

Run: `formal/check.sh [model|--controls]`. Pinned jar + SHA-256 in `formal/tools/`. Java 21 is
already the repo toolchain.

CI: one new `formal-check` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, structurally mirroring
`ui-test`/`agora-ui-test` (independent job, own timeout, no Gradle), added to the branch ruleset's
required checks in the same PR. Budget: default models under 10 minutes on a GitHub runner;
anything slower moves to `formal/models/deep/`, out of the gate, with a dated result line in
`README.md`.

## TLA+ vs Alloy (decided: TLA+/TLC)

The properties are temporal (eventual release, monotone watermarks, stability never ahead of the
true frontier) over a state machine with an evolving relation (edges open/close, epochs succeed,
membership grows), and the central G-39 question *is* a fairness question. TLA+ makes the fairness
assumptions explicit and reviewable — and that assumption set is itself an output for KE3. TLC
counterexamples are traces, i.e. schedules, which transcribe directly into `SimWorld` seeds.

Alloy would suit "enumerate all well-formed topologies of bounded size", which is a G-19 /
`LinkAdmission` question, not this one. Declined, recorded in `formal/README.md`.

Apalache: optional, for one candidate inductive invariant on the watermark lattice. Never the CI
gate; result recorded in `README.md`.

## Relationship to `:concord` (one-directional, upstream)

Concord binds requirement ids to scenarios a driver runs against **real kernel code** — it checks
the implementation. The model checks whether the **rules** are sound and live across schedules no
scenario enumerates, and it can do so before an implementation exists. So:

- model counterexample → `doc/formal/findings.md` entry → candidate concord scenario (filed as a
  follow-up bead for the owning lane) or a `concord/corpus/DISPUTES.md` entry;
- concord failure → never "answered" by the model.

This epic writes no corpus YAML, claims no `covers:` id, and does not regenerate
`doc/spec/CONCORDANCE.md`. Existing siblings worth naming in `ABSTRACTION.md`: `22-GF-DIAMOND-01`,
`22-GF-NESTED-01`, `22-LIVE-01`, `22-SOURCE-ID-01`, `22-WAVE-FANIN-01`, `21-REBASE-01`.

## Module layering

`Waves.tla` (core state machine) ← `Frontier.tla` (completeness fold) ← {`GlitchFree.tla`,
`Aligned.tla`, `ReplicaFrontier.tla`}. One `MC*.tla` + `.cfg` instance per configuration; every
property paired with a control config that MUST fail.

Bounds discipline: 1–2 sources, 2–3 arms, ≤3 waves, ≤3 replica slots, ≤3 loop iterations, symmetry
sets where TLC permits. Separate small models per property family — no grand unified spec.

## Kernel reading list for the implementer

- `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/consistency/WaveFrontier.kt` (418 lines — the completeness
  fold, floors, watermarks, `Progress`, `Stall`, replica-fed edges)
- `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/consistency/GlitchFree.kt`
- `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/consistency/ReplicaQuorum.kt`
- `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/data/Watermark.kt`
- `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/observe/` (`AlignedCompositeCell`, `CompositeSink`)
- `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/control/` (`Progress`, `StallNotice`, `absorbAck`)
- `kernel/src/main/kotlin/civictech/cell/protocol/` (`EdgeOpen`/`EdgeClose`, `TopologyOrderProtocol`)

## Spec reading list

- `doc/spec/20-dataflow-semantics/22-consistency.md` — in full; it is the model's source text
  (MessageContext, source epochs, glitch-freedom, completeness over silent/stuck edges, the
  observation frontier, topology versioning, bridged frontier, recovery-as-baseline,
  interest-scoped settlement, converged-membership barrier)
- `doc/spec/20-dataflow-semantics/21-propagation.md` §Catch-up is a baseline (G-38)
- `doc/spec/90-roadmap/91-gap-analysis.md` rows G-38, G-39, G-40, G-42, G-36
- `doc/spec/90-roadmap/93-feature-interactions.md` I-5, I-11, I-13, I-14, I-18, I-22, I-24
- `doc/spec/90-roadmap/96-incremental-engines-plan.md` §E2 (E2.1–E2.5) and §E3 (E3.1–E3.7) — the
  milestones KE2/KE3 will implement; the model must target these, not today's code alone

## Sequencing note

Milestone-plan §5 ranks FRM1 at 11, explicitly *"before KE3's spec ticket is written"*. The
kernel-lane order (§4) puts KE3 fifth. F1–F3 are the part that must precede KE3's spec ticket; F4
(KE2 input) and F5 (KE3 input) are the direct spec-input deliverables. If the lane is time-boxed,
F1→F3→F5 is the minimum that discharges the milestone-plan edge.

## Explicit prohibitions for the implementing agent

No kernel code. No `doc/spec/` edits. No corpus YAML, no `CONCORDANCE.md` regeneration. Findings go
to a new `doc/formal/findings.md` only (milestone-plan §6). A model counterexample that defeats a
decided rule is a finding plus a follow-up bead — never a spec edit and never a softened property.
